Okay enough with the silly stuff. Let's get into the gritty details.
The story is set before and after the events of the first Hotline Miami game but is mainly set after. Unlike the first game where you play 2 characters, the game is based on more than 6 different characters:
The Fans, The Writer, The Soldier, The Detective, the Pig Butcher and many more.
If you played the last few levels of the first game, this game is a lot similar to that imo. There are less masks in this game but are more distinct than the last one.
For example, the Fans have 4 masks, one has a dodge roll, one can kill people by punching them but can't use weapons and there's one where you can play 2 characters (one with a chainsaw and one with a gun).
There is a slight problem with the camera but it's a very minor complaint.
Plus it's very hard so yeah.
The music is one of the biggest strong points of the game, I enjoyed killing everyone to the 80s-esque techno music. If you're a fan of techno music, I highly reccommend that you buy the Hotline Miami 2 OST (and the first one as well).
There is tons of replayability in this game where you can get achievements, try out new masks in levels that you played before. You can try and get the biggest highscore or you can get all the achievement in the game. Either way, you'll be playing this game over and over again.
If you're a fan of the Hotline Miami series, I highly recommend that you check out this game. If you like mindless violence with a bit of difficulty, then I would recommend this too.

I have been putting this a side for a sale as I have been uming and ahing over whether I should buy this or not. I finally decided to buy the game cheap as it looked promising despite many people saying the controls weren't the best. I was prepared for the bad controls but not for the disappointment this game is.
This game seems to be very unpolished as the controls were very slow to respond particularly when aiming. The game suffered from poor level design and character animations; adding to the frustration of controlling the character. The triggers in levels were often too soon to kill you or killed you for random reasons.

There were many glitches and technical problems which increased the frustration tenfold, some were funny, some a minor annoyance and others were almost game breaking. For example, whenever the game was saving it would lag out for a few seconds. A more serious problem was when there was a running level near the end of the game and the character randomly just fell through the ground and died. The character animations could not only be annoying when controlling the characters, but they also looked quite ugly and unpolished as there was no transitions between animations and sometimes the character would just teleport.
The plotline was almost non-existent and of what story there was it was uncreative and cliché. This was emphasised by character development and voice acting; which both were as predictable as they were cheesy. We learn almost nothing about the characters including the protagonist, we only see some major plotline at the end of the game and as I said before it was uncreative.
There were a few positives to note such as; the environments as they fit well with the atmosphere of a post-apocalyptic setting. The artwork for the cutscenes was fairly nice because of the sketchy, grungy art style which I thought fit well, though some may take the art style to be lazy. Some mechanics that were introduced were good but could have been executed better. For example the enemies coming from the background and into the foreground, so you could see them approaching. The music was okay but, it isn't really anything worth mentioning and most of the time just seemed to get lost.
Overall this game is just bad; there are more bad points than good points to mention. The game is very difficult to get into and hard to enjoy because of constant frustration. Please do not buy this game as it is a waste of time and money. If you really must buy this game, get it super cheap in a sale.

A beautifull but awfully short (3-4 hours to beat the story) platformer which kind of reminds me the classic Prince Of Persia, kind of "easy" for the new generation players.
Good platforms (Although no particular "hard" spots to climb/jump), nice combat system in which more than two zombies are a problem (Unless you have a gun, and better save bullets) and usually is better just run away, interesting story (With an ending not too good) and stunning visuals (although the game doesn't seems to have anti aliasing) with a great atmosphere.
And of course you have your secrets and the hidden stuff if you want to 100% the game.
Maybe the game is just 3-4 hours long because its formula can't be more expanded (You have some guns, and can run/jump, there's no new items, no new tools), maybe is budget's fault, but in the end, all that's left is a nicely done game which will end way too early.
So, better wait for sales to get it.

This game brings a new edge to the zombie apocalypse genre. As a platform game it is very rich in detail and deep in story. I would compare it to the likes of Trine but of course with a more realistic feel.
Although the puzzles in the game are not that difficult, it keeps you entertained by occasionally requiring the use of one of your abilities, like shouting to get attention from zombies, to get past particular parts. Some parts are fast paced where you don't stop to kill zombies whereas others are take it slow and search to find the secrets of each stage. Which are sometimes interestingly hidden. This brings back memories of the old platform games from the 90s.
The controls are simple and not overly complex which gets you into the game very fast. You really only need your movement and action keys of swinging an axe or interacting with an object. Though of course you can shoot the different guns and slingshots that you get and as previously mentioned get the attention of people through the shout key. The stamina bar is a nice addition and adds to the realism of the game that swinging an axe at zombies does make you tired! So you have to be careful not to overdo it and back off as required.
I played this with keyboard and mouse but you can play with the controller also, and I think it would make an excellant relax on the sofa game.
A highly recommended game from me all around.

Deadlight is actaully quite fun to play. You die a lot because of unpredictable traps and platforming remenicnet of Prince of Persia (1989) but sometimes it succeeds just right to let you escape on the first try from an unexpected enemy.
And when the platforming and haning does work it is a joy. You feel like a badass for outrunning and outsmarting zombies and jumping from building to building, not stoping because that would get your but chewed off.
There are however three things that this game does makes me cringe over: The gunplay, the writing (oh god the writing!) and the use key.
First a word on the melee: It's ineffective and difficult and I am totally ok with that. I'm no superman or machine that can rip trough enemies like paper. The main character (if you want to call him that) is a normal man who can swing an axe a few times and the need a beather. It serves the atmosphere of the game that you actaully have to run more than fight.
The guns however are donwright clumsy: aiming is slow and if you are in a tight situation and start pointing the gun in the wrong direction you are pretty much doomed and unlike the melee it feels unnessecearly punishing for the tiniest mistake. The perfect aim also make guns way too powerful concidering that the protagonist is pretty much a novice with handguns. It diminishes the feeling of panic that the melee has.
Then there is the writing: riddeld with clihés, sterotypes, tropes and right out lazyness, it is the weakest side of the game. The main character has one note that he keeps playing toughout and the one woman in the game is frustratingly typecasted as weak, a damsel in distress and the sexy one destined to be saved. She is also almost♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ The ending of the game is also so baffling it hurts to think about. I guess there is a lot of material in the diary, but for a short game pressing for urgency in the plot, I could not be bothered.

I really, really, really, really want to like this game, I want to get into the the way I did with the first installment of Hotline Miami, but thus far, Wrong Number is, well, nearly bad. The story, such as it is, is of poor quality, and seems to flirt with about three different tones, and has only tenuous ties to the first game, while totally abandoning its atmosphere. Each time you enter a level, you KNOW who you are, and roughly why you're about to murder an entire building full of people; a major departure from the original Hotline Miami. The level design is poor in comparison to the first game as well, trading tight, claustrophobic apartments and offices filled with goons, for huge sprawling areas filled to bursting with gun-toting thugs. While Hotline Miami did have its share of levels similar to those found in Wrong Number, they were the exception rather than the rule. Similarly, the music is poor in comparison, and is far more accessable and repetitive.
Overall, I dont think I can honestly reccommend this game. It really is a great example of how thankful we should be for the Hotline Miami we all got to start with, and it really does prove the old addage that lightning never strikes the same place twice.

'Far Cry 3' is a very enjoyable open-world sandbox first-person shooter. Right off the bat, I was free to explore one of the two islands. I spent the first 16 hours of the game exploring, activating radio towers (the only time to date I actually enjoyed first-person platforming), hunting animals and relics, crafting bigger wallets and ammo bags, and -- the best part of the game -- liberating outposts. Given the dynamic game environment, each of my encounter or scenarios with enemies varied, and this made 'Far Cry 3' unpredictable and replayable.
It wasn't until my 24th hour that I moved on with the story missions, which feature exciting set pieces and action. Just when I thought I've got the rhythm of the game down, the game granted me access to the second island. This second island features a different terrain, providing new challenges in liberating outposts and making me rethink my tactics. It's also full of nooks and cranies and secrets waiting to be discovered, just like on the first island.
One of my very few gripes about 'Far Cry 3', however, was the boss battles. Like some of the contemporary action games I've played, boss battles were reduced to quick time events. This diminished the tension of the conflicts and made me feel more like an observer, resulting in rather unsatisfying gameplay. One particular boss battle was particularly disappointing because his character was already under developed; battling him by pressing a few buttons on cue made the experience even more underwhelming. This made me miss grand boss battles like those found in games like 'Crysis'
Despite my annoyance about boss battles, 'Far Cry 3' remained entertaining and fresh as I approached my 50th hour into the game. The game has surprisingly much to offer. 'Far Cry 3' gets a very enthusiastic thumbs-up from me.

Deadlight? Dead-right! What an expectantly, thrilling little game. Solid story and engaging story with exciting game play accompanied by eerie & chilling soundtrack. This game is a sterling way to break up the genre and immerse yourself into a good storyline with atop-notch visual experience. Scenery, backdrops and models are of the highest quality and will keep you spellbound from start to finish.
Admittedly, the story has been done before and feels like a repeat at times, but that will not be enough to distract you from the overall experience and wanting to progress. For the money, this game is worth every cent & offers a ‘nightmare mode’ once completed to test your application and patience. The main story has about 3-4 hours gameplay. I recommend finding the secrets and diary pages to spread the game out a little bit and fully engross yourself into the story.
The developers really nailed the zombie survival, post-apocalyptic feel for the game. You get a decent amount of ammo but are encouraged to find alternative ways to deal with zombies as well retaining your stamina. The game would have got an extra point if there had more weapons and more uses for the sling (i.e. distracting enemies)
Deadlight deserves an 8.5/10 – Visual aspect of the game is just ace and is really something to marvel as you move into each area. A real sense of tension is created in each scene as you’re made to think on your toes and work out situations quickly. I would recommend this game to anyone. It’s a classy addition to the genre and a breath of fresh air in my video game lungs.

In a genre that seems to be oversaturated by mediocre games and bogged down by tropes, Contagion stands out as somthing that is very focused on quality not quantity.
The zombies in Contagion hail from the slow moving, bullet sponge zombies from the classic movies, not the sprinting cannon fodder from games like Left 4 Dead, it's going to take a perfect headshot in order to kill. Ammo is scarce and the hoard is plentiful, this leads to some very fun, very tense moments in multiplayer. The players aren't immune to the virus either, all it takes is one bite and you're going to turn after a short while.
Gunplay is very satisfying, you can unload, discard, and manage the guns in your limited inventory in order to conserve ammo. Gun power is a tad irrelevant given that bullets only work if they hit the head, so there is less squabbling over power weapons and more focus on ammo conservation.
As a Zombie you are able to call the hoard to a location with a zombie roar, in addition you move faster and can track down the human players. It's very fun to coordinate and attempt to take down the survivors. A well coordinated zombie assult can be extremly fun for both the zombies and the survivors.
To sum it up, Contagion is fun with friends, the focus on survival and old school shambling zombies is refreshing, and workshop support will add more fun content in the future. It's worth the 20 dollars.

Edit 10/9/15 After coming back to this on a whime my opinon has vastly improved of the game, many of my points still stand however. I now recommend it just be aware of the problems i've highlighted.
I have not fully finished the game due to technical issues, although i have played enough to have a good idea on what to expect.
Deadlight is a zombie survival platformer. The story elements are good and it strays away from the generic dull story's of many zombie themed titles. There are enough plot twists to keep it interesting as well. Music certainly does its job, but it isn't anything special it does however add a lot to the game. Voice acting is pretty basic with several characters sounding somewhat annoying. The game is fully linear with no choices, the only side paths you may encounter will be small rooms or areas with little collectable, secrets and lore. These side areas are the only real reason to replay this game. However the platforming is just too much of an issue; there are several areas such as climbing over a fence require pressing multiple directions and buttons, this is not very pleasant to do when escaping instant death in one of the later stages. There are several areas in which you have to escape something chasing you that will instantly kill you, these can be dull at best and irritating at worst. The game also tends to freeze for about 20 seconds (still present two years later) or so when you attempt to pause, couple this with frequent audio playing to late or just not playing at all and this can really sour the experience. I have also had the game completly crash with the pause menu freezing.
Oddly enough the audio rarely works for me in cutscenes, It only worked in one cutscene.

I have really enjoyed Call of Duty since 3 came out (played 2 after I played 3 and enjoyed it too), with the exception of World at War and now Ghosts. So I am not going to come out and say that it's the same game every year, as if that is even true. Different guns, different killstreaks, different maps, I'd even go as far to say a whole different playstyle needs to be adapted. It changes enough year to year. That being said, this game is a huge letdown. The campaign was probably the biggest leap they made, which is sad because as everyone knows, CoD is a multiplayer game first. They introduced new campaign elements that atleast kept me entertained for the 5 hours it takes to get through. By no means is it a stellar story, but it is an improvement over previous Call of Duty campaigns.
Multiplayer is unplayable. Literally. You cannot find a game on PC. I've played this on Xbox 360 and PS4 and find matches pretty easily but it appears that the PC audience is absent from this installment. If you are looking for a fun FPS to play on Steam with your friends, I would advise you to look elsewhere. There are a total of maybe 1,000 players online during peak hours, and of those players more than half play Team Deathmatch. If you want any variety of gameplay like an objective, you can go to hell. Aside from all of that, the class customization is over the top. In CoD4 (arguably the best of the series), you get a Primary, a Secondary, 3 perks, a lethal and tactical grenade, and that was it. Short and sweet. In Ghosts, Jesus ♥♥♥♥ing Christ. A primary, a seconday, two attachment slots for each, camo for each, lethals, tacticals, 17 ♥♥♥♥♥ons of perks, 90 different killstreaks to choose from. What's next, can I choose the camo on my ♥♥♥♥ing frag grenades? It's overwhelming, it's not fun. I feel like to compete in this game you have to sit and heavily think about your loadout and it is supposed to be a casual shooter game. They took the appeal of the simplistic shooter style of CoD4 and said ♥♥♥♥ it, you wanted a peanut butter and jelly sandwich as a snack? Here's a 5-course meal prepared by the Emperor's gourmet. It's overkill.
Squads mode isn't even worth touching. Why the hell is this in the game? Just do a Basic Training mode like Black Ops and be done with it. I don't wanna pit this pathetic AI system against itself. I guess I can't bash it too much since that is what I had to play most of the time, since I cannot find a damn multiplayer match to jump into.
Extinction. We get it, you want to re-create a fun game mode like Nazi Zombies. Try again, I guess. I can't hate on them for trying to do something new and fun like this but it was poorly executed. Maybe it's different now, I only played the first "episode" of it on the PS4.
Activision, get your♥♥♥♥♥♥together. Stop dishing out money on stupid ♥♥♥♥ing live action advertisements with big name actors, start using the money to make more quality games. You do not need ads, you already have a succesful franchise, people will play it and YouTubers will promote it for you given that it is a quality game.

Hard to believe the team that made the renowned Zombie Panic: Source mod for Half Life 2 also made this disaster. Contagion tries to combine co-op and versus simultaneously, which on paper sounds great but is executed horribly. With player zombies zig-zagging and crouch spamming to dodge bullets combined with the abhorrent net code, versus is a chore. Sadly co-op gets old fairly fast as well.

I have yet to play much of Contagion, what I have played is extremely interesting and fun. The gameplay and mechanics are things I've felt would make for an amazing zombie game, and to see it utilized cements my belief. The only headshots kill is a wonderful and perfect mechanic to a zombie game and it plays well. Graphcally speaking it looks great. The atmosphere is also phenomenal. Its dark and terrifying. Perfect for a zombie survival game. Though there are a few issues.
Firstly is the amount of RAM required to run this game. 4 gigs is kind of ridiculous to me. I only have 3 gigs and no other game has required that much RAM, though, I may be making more of a deal out of it than it is. Secondly is the light mechanic. Upon certain surfaces it creates a weird glare like deal along the screen and is mildly blinding. Kind of a pain to me, and I havent found a way to fix it.
All in all though this is a great game at an ASTOUNDING price, and if you have the RAM, unlike me, you shouldnt have to many issues if any at all. I would highly recommend it to all gamers with a love for zombies. Buy, Install, and ENJOY my friends.

I just finished Deadlight in about 6 hours... which was about 3 too many.
To start with the one positive, the visual effect is very neat. Running on a 2d plane with a full 3d world behind you looks amazing, as is the way enemies come out of the background.
But everything else is just sub-par and unfun. The controls are unresponsive, lagging a second behind your input. Nothing ever feels quite accurate, and you'll die at some platforming section 5 times in a row, then suddenly clear it with no apparent difference in technique. Most unforgivable is that every other room has some instant-death trap that you'll never see coming, making it a trial-and-error game of reloading.
Puzzles require absolutely no thought, and amount to pushing buttons when prompted and shooting at obvious targets. Platforming sections never evolve or try anything new, making the last half of the game practically identical to the first.
The writing is also exceptionally weak. Cliche story with bad guys who are bad... just because? And of course zombies who are zombies, just because zombies. The game purportedly takes place in 1980s Seattle, but the game world looks nothing like the city (hint: Seattle isn't 99% flat, unlike this dull landcape) and the setting is never relevant in any way, except someone once mentions the Space Needle. Characters repeatedly mention "The Stadium," as if the writers couldn't even bother to Google the name of an actual stadium in '80s Seattle. Then we get to the last chapter, where we meet up with Generic Annoying Female who does nothing but scream and whine, and require your help over platforms (because that's a fun mechanic, right?) Then it all ends with a "twist" that you'd have to be blind to not see coming.

Deadlight takes a different approach to the zombie genre. With it's more or less 'flight over fight' playstyle, it forces the player to flee when the numbers of the deemed "shadows" exceed that that of more than two. I personally found it to be a very enjoyable twist in the series, opposed to games such as Left 4 Dead that give you the option to fight whilst keeping a steady movement pace, Deadlight encourages the player to keep moving at all times, only slowing them down with numerous puzzles and sequences of contraptions concieved by survivors.
However, beyond the hordes of undead and traps that could massacare Randall in a blink of an eye, the real threat lies within the game's controls. Unresponsive, clunky sequences result in a very unenjoyable experience at several points of the game that make you just want to walk away from the computer. Several stages of the game feature fast-paced parkour over fences and under obstacles, but fail to properly display the full potential of such a mechanic due to Randall prefering to hang onto a ledge whilst
or hordes of undead threaten to rip you limb from limb.
Overall the game has a very fun premise but falls short of something that could have been an amazing experience for the player to enjoy for hours on end.
7/10.

Movies, fans, etc., are being sprung up with plenty more murders and other chaotic♥♥♥♥♥♥are going out. If you haven't played the last Hotline Miami, I won't go much farther. The game is fun, especially with friends and large groups of online players. (Online players are admittedly harder to come by as the community is usually low if not dead.) However, the game could use work, too. But at the end of the day, I think the game is worthwhile. I'll provide some deetz:
--Panic mode is a blast: you start off with all your survivor friends, and one of you is randomly infected, making it only a matter of time before one turns or sees their friends turn, ensuing in hilarious chaos. But the fun in every mode does not end when you turn into a zombie; rather, as a zombie you now have to hunt down your friends, with a pack of zombies at your disposal depending on the mode you play in.
--Hunted mode is a thrill: you are alone in an environment full of zombies, and every survivor wants you dead for your gear, all the while every sound you make--even opening doors, reloading your weapon, and mere footsteps--can notify nearby enemies where you are.
--Extraction mode is likewise thrilling: you and your friends must find and protect bot-survivors in various locations and hold out the zombie swarms bursting through every possible enterance untill you can get the bot-survivor to safety.
--Escape mode is great too: follow the tasks generated for you and make it though a large maze-like map with your friends alive. However, after about two or three runs in Escape mode, it does get a little boring. But, hell, for every escape map, I first try to play it through alone and it always scares the crap out of me.
--Of all the zombie games I've played, this is among the better ones. I always ended up coming back to it for some fun. But to keep this game going at all, they need to continue expanding the number of enviroments and modes, maybe even increase the number of players allowed in a game (8, or even 16, is pretty small given the size of the maps), and recruit more players--also perhaps by not charging $20 for it.

On the surface, the visuals are gorgeous.  The environments are a clear example of the power of Unreal Engine crossed with the skills of the artists who worked on this game.  The lighting was superb and the texture quality was just right for the game's distant camera.  Even the character animations were clearly top notch motion capture.  The player had smooth transitions for nearly every action he could take from climbing a ladder to an attempted dead-stop after a sprint that causes him to slip as he reaches for something to hold onto.  It's all very striking, but in there lies part of the problem.
Games like Super Meat Boy are built on one simple principle, the player is always right.  The visual fluidity of the character's actions come second only to the player's input.  This allows a platforming character to land seemingly impossible jumps in a predictable manor.  The main character in Deadlight suffers from the fact that animations trump input.  The player will often walk right off a ledge or miss a jump because the physics could not line up with the player input.  Even at a rock solid 60 frames per second, the character always seemed to take 1 step too many before a long jump or just after.  This, mixed with Super Meat Boy-like brutal jumps, lead to more frustration than enjoyment.  Some jump "puzzles" came down to a simple battle of attrition where I would have to jump over spikes or traps repeatedly until the physics finally did what I wanted them to do.  I can recall several times where I restarted at least 30 times over to pass an unreasonable jump puzzle, only to be trolled on the next screen by a pit or more spikes or yet another trap - forced to do it all again.  This game could have been better if it just got out of it's own way.
Speaking of getting in it's own way; let's talk about the writing for a moment.  This crappy review is like Shakespeare compared to the complete mess that is the writing of this game.  The one-note main protagonist makes me want to jump into a pit of "Shadows" every time he opens his mouth.  (note: "Shadow" is a zombie in this game... yeah I know, don't get me started).  The character is constantly tossing out cheesy "damn dirty apes" type of comments and stating the obvious like, "that's gun fire" after a weapon fire can be heard and, "that's a car crash!" after screeching tires come to a stop with a sudden crash.  Thanks Captain Obvious, I'll call you if I need someone to tell me what it sounds like when I take a♥♥♥♥♥♥next time.  The story is as flat as the characters and it plays out like something that a 5 year-old wrote in French, then Google translated it Swahili and then to English.  Sadly, this would have been a much better game if it was completely void of conversation.
Deadlight is a game filled with promise, but it does little to reach that promise.  With loose jump mechanics and terrible writing, this game falls apart in more ways than I'd like to admit.  The zombie theme and gloomy but gorgeous visuals seem too good for what ultimately turned out to be a heaping mess of misplaced good intentions.

Deadlight is brilliant. Picked it up on the xbox when it came out and again on steam during the sale.
The game presents itself so well for such a simple design of side-scrolling. There is a lot of interaction with the environment and the backgrounds offer a lot of involvement with gameplay. Zombies lie waiting, feasting on a fallen survivor and when you make your move past the group, they will come into your plane and chase you down until you can trick them into falling into a crevasse. The attention to detail is highly impressive, too. When you wade through low, muddy waters, you will see your feet kicking up piles of mud. Everything about the game has some bit of detail to it.
If you're on the fence about Deadlight, I can highly recommend the game. It is worth more than a blank check, let a lone $3 on sale. Buy this game. You will not be disappointed. I would not be surprised if developer Tequila Works sees huge success in coming years from only Deadlight. Any fan of zombie games will have a blast with the game. Bravo, Tequila Works.

Contagion applies the Zombie rules set out by George A. Romero. Playing Contagion brings you closer to staring in one of Romero's Dead series. With these slow(er) moving Zombies they can seem to the player at first as sitting ducks while idle, however they are numerous whereas ammo isn't. It doesn't take much to become overcome by the walking dead as they are relentless. Sometimes stealth is required, teamwork, maybe its a new use for a wrench? A gun shot carefully aimed at the brain, it has to be the safer method.
But did you think of the noise it made, now nearby Zombies have been alerted to its sound and hence your whereabouts, its time to run or fight! Play in co-op, alone as a hunter in pvp up against human survivors, AI and human Zombies as death in Contagion isn't the end, just your new stumbling beginning.
Contagion at this time of writing has 3 game modes
*Hunted (PVP)
*Excape (objective)
*Extraction (Holdout)
*New FREE DLC to add more maps and modes in the pipeline
*SDK for user made content including maps. (check out the forums for current projects)
*Currently they are 5 offical maps, 2 free addon maps. (28/04/14)
*The game uses Brainboxes not to be mistaken as headshots for one shot kills.
*Zombie AI is realisticly zombie like, stumbling and farting like they should. (OK I lied about the farting)
*Aim down gun sights for careful placement of high speed bullet between the eyes.
*Great weight to characters movements.
*George A. Romero: Zombie rules applies. Big +ve.

This is (or was) a fun World War II multi-player shooter, where you queue for your battle and find yourself capturing resource points or command locations to win the game.
You can play infantry, anti-tank, airman, sniper, paratrooper or tanker - drive numerous vehicles and even ride a bicycle into battle.
Graphically it's very nice. The servers seem fast enough, and the maps aren't too bad.
That's the 'Heroes' side of it.   The 'Generals' side has you commanding units on a battle-map to ultimately win a war. When you move a unit into a battle-area, that unit becomes available to the real-life players... so if you move a tank squad into Arnhem, then players who have tanker characters will be playing your unit's individual tanks.
Initially I loved the game. There was a lot to do - though levelling your character could be a bit of a grind if you didn't want to pay RealLifeMoney(tm) - but there were plenty of tank battles, lots of opportunities for snipers, paratroopers and aircraft.
Being an infrantryman in a pitched battle full of dogfighting, tank combat, and ducking sniper fire was damn exciting.  Being in a BF-109 dropping bombs on Hellcats and running like hell from P38-Lightnings was also great fun.
Now, however... I suspect the number of players has bottomed out.  I haven't been able to get into an aircraft for over a month (I used to queue for a minute or two. Now I'm giving up after 45.)  and the tank games are few and far between.  There are too many people getting cheap kill just driving jeeps around (jeep physics are broken) and friendlies on AA guns will STILL insist on shooting down friendly paratrooper aircraft.
In short... I did love it, but now I don't.   Really, given that you spend most of your time playing infantry, with no real opportunity to do much else, there are better games out there. Planetside2 for starters.
Still Heroes and Generals is free, so it certainly isn't going to hurt to take a look... but unless things change, the situation for tankers and airmen is pretty grim.

Okay. So first of all, I just wanna say that Far Cry 3 runs really well on optimized Intel HD graphics drivers! I've got Intel HD 5500 and I can run this game on medium - high settings without it overheating my CPU. Now, that says something!
Now, to the game review.. This, I will say, is one of the best open world games I've ever played! If you're looking for a game that challenges you and intrigues you constantly with its AMAZING storyline, this is the game for you. Yea, some of the missions are hard and I won't lie, I've probably died over 100 times in total, but every time was worth it, because that's all about the challenge and becoming a better player. This game has really expanded my gameplay as a gamer and I don't regret buying it.
PROS:
. Open world
. Fun Missions
. Exploration + Time to do so
. Fun side missions (unlocked with UPlay)
. Amazing storyline (really drives the game)
. Great graphics (on low end graphic cards)
Fun gameplay overall!
CONS:
. Open world gameplay isn't too expansive
(You can't interact with the Isanders unless it's part of a mission and you can't eat, drink, sleep. Ya know.. Just little things  that would make it more realistic. I love open world games that feature these things, but sadly, this game does not.)
. First Person driving is difficult.
(Now this is one thing that  I absolutely HATE about the game. The driving. I find driving on boats to be much easier than driving cars or dirt bikes. I've gotten better at it, but for the most part, I usually try to avoid driving as much as possible in the game. I either cut through paths or just drive to a certain point and walk from there. It's horrible..)
. Having to constantly avoid getting attacked by the pirates!
Tip: There's a workaround once you unlock something called "fast travel". It helps me escape situations I've lost control over so I don't lose the things I've found and my LIFE lol. Play and find out ;)
. Speaking of losing things, the game has an odd save system where you can't save during missions, so it saves it for you at each checkpoint reached. It can be annoying, so when given the chance to explore, I do, because that is the only time you can save your progress.
Tip: SAVE AS MUCH AS POSSIBLE!
Other than those four things, there's nothing really wrong with the game. As far as ratings go, I would give this game an 8/10. Kudos to the developers! :)

There isn't a more watered down, money-grabbing catastrophe of a shooter out there that brings you closer to curb stomping your PC than the next installment of Call of Duty.  There hasn't been a solid game in over 7 years and at this rate you can expect the same quality in the future. The graphics along with the animations are almost a decade old now. The knowledge that deep down you're online experience is at the mercy of some loser's porn-addled laptop playing from a college dorm is enough to stop playing within the first 5 minutes.  And given you play longer than that you might just get lucky enough to experience the framerate drops which can be more or less just as unreliable as the connection. The weapons are redundant and feel more like toys than well designed killing machines. The killstreaks and perks are agravating and unsatisfying no matter what end you find yourself on.  There are very and I mean VERY few redeeming qualities of today's Call of Duty.  If you were fortunate enough to enjoy some of the first entries of the series I'd strongly recommend re-installing some of those for your Call of Duty fix and for the love of the gaming industry stop putting money into the pockets of these developers.

Who am I to say this? I've been playing Call of Duty since it came out day 1 vanilla. I've been in the franchise, excluding console only titles since then, and MW3, BO2 was enough for me to turn around and say I'm done with the CoD title. I purchased this for myself when it reached Summer Sales 50% off. I'm no longer interested in the MP aspect of the game, beause lets be honest, it hasn't required skill in a long time. A fast-reaction time and high rate-of-fire weapon is all that is required. You naysayers will sit there and say to me, get skill. I say to you, I have skill, and today's CoD was too easy for me, to the point that any time the clan I was in, and I, would join a match, we were called hackers and the enemy team would abandon the match. Moving on, because this is a SP review.
Do you remember back when you were 10 years old, and you and your best mate would play pretend soldier on a weekend? Remember how you came up with that pretend mission? That is Ghosts SP. Written by a 10 year old, and pitched to the execs in a paragraph or less; *spoilers ahead*
Two brothers, a father. Father is an elite unit 'Ghost' commander. America is attacked (again) from space. Big wall is put up across America, to prevent South America who have allied with Russia from invading. Fast forward a decade, brothers are in the army defending the wall, with their Father general of their unit. Wall is penetrated and the army camp is raided. Father goes missing, brothers trying to find him, get rescued by Ghosts. Turns out father is a ghost all along (shocked face). Brothers now tag along with ghosts to earn getting into the unit. People die, you dont really care, cliche 10 year old phrases of the army are spoken often. You've got to kill the equivalent Makarov. Yada yada yada.
You probably already know how it all ends. So let's put the atrocious storyline aside for a moment. Gameplay, same as every other CoD really. AI, same as every other CoD really, only the harder you go, the quicker reaction AI aimbot is. So it isn't difficult in the sense of smart AI, it's just difficult because you need a faster reaction time than the AI. I have a fast reaction time, but some of the times I was killed by AI literally were prefires on corners where their LoS and positioning had no idea. Moving on.
Soundtrack? Nope. No Hans Zimmer or anything dramatic to even speak of. Graphics, shiny yes, but this was overdue for CoD for sometime, and the only reason it has happened now is because consoles got a new generation. What else is there, weapon variety, in SP, not really. Kept seeing the same 10 weapons or so with different variations throughout the entire map.
In summary, if you want to focus on the typical MP experience CoD offers, go for it. But you're a bloody sheep buying last years title with a new name. If you're like me and were buying it for SP, don't bother until it's on sale or budget binned. I wouldn't pay more than $10 for this experience.
CoD used to have really decent SP, MW and MW2 showed that. What the hell happened Activision? Try invested those millions of dollars from DLC into improving your product in the future, because I'm glad I didn't buy this until it was on sale, and I won't be purchasing anything further unless your SP investment improves.

This game... oh this game. Well let me start off with what I actually like about this game. Shooting zombies and the guns can be slightly satisfying, the game looks great, and killing another player as a zombie has a lot of satisfaction to it. Also the atmosphere is amazing, the way it sounds and looks is fantastic and it can be immersive at times. However that does not save this game because this game is awful! Let me break it down Contagion Prides it's self on being a unique realistic zombie game with an ever changing environment for a different experience every time you play. First off this game is not unique the fact it's a zombie game makes it already a "been there done that" experience, and also I can't quite prove it but for some reason this game reminds me of Left 4 Dead whether it's the fact that the first game mode involves you trying to escape the place your in and get to safety like every L4D campaign. The second involves trying to survive against zombies to wait for an extraction like the ending level of every chapter in L4D. Lastly the PVP combat that involves one team as zombies and the other as survivors (see why I get this hunch) also there is the fact that they have all these "unique" (and totally not cardboard as hell) Characters Like L4D's Louis, Zoe, Bill, Francis, Nick, Elise, Coach, and Rochelle. Only thing is at least I can remember there names unlike a single character in this whole damn game.
But I’m not done yet let’s talk about those three game modes mentioned up above shall we. First is escape which features two maps which I’m not even going to complain about the lack of levels because for one the levels are supposed to change every time you play them so you get a lot of replay value out of a single level, and second I don't want more levels because jest one of them is unbearable! The best way to describe this game mode is boring its sooooo boring. You get all these objectives on your little I phone (that won't get dated or anything like that) but the objectives vary from walk over there like an idiot now walk over there like an idiot and now look for something like an idiot. But don't worry about getting lost... because you will. The game has this little meters number that tells you how far you are from your objective (which by the way is incredibly annoying it should have been a map like in the extraction game mode) to help prevent getting lost. So I hope you like looking at your I phone because that’s all you'll be doing as you walk around the boring city or the boring prison, and you will get sooooo board walking and walking and WALKING! that’s all you do there are zombies walking around that are annoying as hell to deal with because you have to hit them in the head but the hit box is so messed up that you'll end up hitting them in the head and they'll jest keep on coming. In the end though I could not even finish the damn escape mode I was so damn board. Also multiplayer is not better here because in a good zombie coop game like L4D you can't split up and rush to the end because the special infected will kill you forcing you to work as a team. Here there’s nothing like that so there’s nothing stopping other team mates from running up a head and completing the story while you wonder the streets aimlessly.
Also this game brags about how realistic it is yeah that’s why there’s lots of random guns and ammo in the stupidest places. Like a sub machine gun on the couch in an apartment because yeah that’s what I do with my illegal firearms. I just leave them on the table when I have to go out to the store, or better yet how there’s all this ammo in the stupidest places that are also in these perfect little boxes. Like I found ammo in a dinner booth because yeah I’d jest leave my ammo in a dinner in the zombie apocalypse because who needs guns. No really who needs them when melee weapons instant kill zombies 8/10 times, don’t use ammo, and don’t attract zombies making them supper over powered. Don’t worry though it’s not like this game is hard or anything like that the only reason I died was because they spawn so many zombies that you can’t kill them all because you’ll run out of ammo. Speaking of spawning I hope you like infinitely spawning enemies that spawn every were way to much so that you’ll constantly being followed by zombies unless your on easy.
The other two game modes are not any better either extraction is IMPOSSIBLE not because the zombies kill you or anything sensible like that ohhh no its because the survivor died. You see the reason it's impossible is because well the second…THE SECOND you get to the house you have to defend. Before you even get in the damn door the zombies start coming giving you no time to search the house, find were the survivor(s) are standing, and barricade the doors. Also yes the survivor(s) are jest stupid NPCs that jest stand there they don't have a gun, they don't run from zombies or at least away form them, they will however truck straight into a crowd of zeds, and you can't tell them to do anything so instead of getting them to a safer place like the attic you have to hold out were he is standing which is usually on the first floor next to a damn window that zombies easily get through and kill him.

Deadlight is a thing of beauty, to the naked eye at least.
Presentation: 9.5/10 - The games great mixture of colours is visually stunning. All the pitch black cadavers lining the empty, cold, and harsh streets while the sun shines down brightly and creates glare on your screen is simply a sight that should be seen. How they mix the pitch black bodies with the bright surroundings around them is simply put; amazing. I must also mention the soundtrack. The music fits the mood rather well, and helps immerse you in the world.
Gameplay: 6.0/10 - Although the idea was original, especially for a zombie game, Deadlight fails in many areas. It's basically a simple, linear, clunky, and slippery platformer. All the surfaces you jump on feel slipper and the controls are clunky and sometimes have a bit of a delay. The game is also very linear, in the sense that there are no real, "secret," areas and you just end up following the cookie trail that the game gives you. You also get some weapons in the game like a revolver or axe, but they aren't anything unique. For the long ranged weapons it's a simple point and shoot, which is basically the same for the axe or any other physical weapon. Simple, but not too clean.
Plot: 6.5/10 - Other than some great story telling, the plot ends up being a little too cliched for me. As I said, they tell the story in a great way, but the actual story isn't that great. They also did a good job at making you feel for the protagonist, Randall Wayne, but once again the main premise feels old.
Overall: 7.0/10 - Good.

Actually a good game for free (or two games)
I thought I needed to write the post about the game.
It is a good game and it is free, without the need to pay for it.
Yes, you get a small advantage if you buy premium. You get the chance to have another badge which gives you an edge. But you still need to cap, hit enemies and avoid getting hit. (Reto also needs to get some funds)
You get many good matches (Heroes) where you sometimes actually get in teams that play as teams and many bad games where you are not sure what your team mates are doing. Or worse you know what they are doing (tree faeries everywhere). But remember everone have their own agenda about what they need or want. If you want to get better with grenades you nead to use explosives.
But the strange part is that you can still enjoy games even if you or your squad needs ”to do everything by yourselves”. You also get more experience points, gold and warfunds if you ”have to do” a good performance.

Hotline Miami 2 is closer to the last levels of the first game (Biker) than the rest of Hotline Miami (Jacket and all his masks), and thus feels like a direct continuation rather than just a new coat of paint. This opinion might seem a bit obtuse now, but I will explain later on why it is an important distinction.
So, why is it a continuation rather than a new take?
Well, at first, the difficulty is brutal right off the bat. This game is aimed at people who already played Hotline Miami 1 and are familiar with the concept of its ultra-violent twitch gameplay associated with tight level design forcing the players to plan their route according to the situations.
And then, the playable characters are mostly forced, just like Biker was, and they have an equally narrow skillset. Biker had a hatchet and three knives to throw but could not pick up weapons? Tony from Hotline Miami 2 has his insta-kill fists but is unable to pick up weapons.
The game moved on from the freedom of choice offered in the majority of Hotline Miami 1, and forces a more controlled experience. This idea goes further, as a lot of levels are designed so tightly that the chaotic action of Hotline Miami 1 has been replaced by puzzles with barely more than one way to solve them.
Moreover, the gameplay is overall less rough around the edges, with more solid surfaces that block bullets, and most especially a seemingly slower speed, I feel more like I have to anticipate every movement rather than play on the fly and let my instincts and skills take over. More 'slow', less 'flow'.
So here I come to the point that I made at the start: Hotline Miami 2 feels like a more controlled experience as a direct continuation to the Biker levels, rather than the early levels with their chaotic sandbox design that allowed for a much wider variety of approaches.
However, enough Hotline Miami 2 levels are not so tight and can offer variety, and  a lot of missions offer a choice between different characters or weapons. So the game still does a good job at offering variety. My observation is just that the variety feels forced, rather than the sweet spot and perfect flow that I felt Hotline Miami 1 achieved.
Hotline Miami 2 is more polished that the first one. Way more polished. The levels, atmosphere, sounds/music and storylines have all been crafted with great attention to details and take the player on several journeys that make this sequel well worth playing. The game definitively feels fresh and ambitious rather than 'more of the same', and its controlled chaos makes the first Hotline Miami still relevant with its less polished but more chaotic and free ultra-violence.

Don't let the cheesey, ugly, and arguably derivative intro trailer fool you - Contagion is in my opinion, the definitive multiplayer zombie game. It's true that it's a bit rough around the edges, and that it definitely needs it's on going development, but there is A LOT of fun to be had here. Especially in the "hunted" multi-player mode. In it, up to 8 or 10 surivors are let loose in a large open area (My favorite is the massive and urban "Barlow Square" which comes complete with explorable multi-leveled buildings, subways, and movie theaters that can be raided for supplies, or reinforced for a last stand) before squaring off in a death match. What seperates this from your run of the mill FPS zombie death match is that not only is ammo limmited, but every shot attracts waves of the undead.
Spy a player characte running across the street? Take aim, but beware... if you miss he'll simply duck into cover, while any zombies in the immediate area make a b-line toward your position.
The zombies also add an interesting dimension to combat. On multiple occasions have I found myself in a stand off with an opponent with superior fire power, but his back to a wall. My strategy is to fire a bunch in the air to attract the hordes and scamper off before he can figure out what's happening. "PLAYER WAS KILLED" is so satisfying to see knowing that you attracted the zombies that devoured him as you scurry away through fire escapes and broken windows.
If you're like me, games like Left 4 Dead and Dead Island don't truly feel like zombie games. They've got the look, but they lack the thrill of Running through alleyways with your friends, trying to make every shot count while making decisions on the fly (should we try running here? Or There? What if that leads to a dead end?)
Every now and then you and a friend find youselves behind a set of doors while being pursued by a horded of zombies. You  two enter a room, quickly shut the door and nail it shut with a nail gun. There's a shotgun in the room with 6 rounds in it. Your friend happens to have a few more shells that he found but had no use for. He presses "J" to toss them to you just as the zombies start pounding at your barricade. "We'll alternate fire" The doors smash open. It's a glorious last stand.
Oh, now for the negatives...
the game is buggy. like I said earlier, it's rough around the edges. most of the level designs are really unintuitive and take a long time to learn your way around. Some might just be TOO big. I think some of the mechanics could use a bit of tweaking to really balance things a bit, but nothing game breaking.
Oh, the sound design is fantastic.
All in all, the zombie apocalypse by it's nature is going to be a bit unbalanced and dirty... just like Contagion is... still, there's something that just brings us all back to it. I definitely reccommend.

As of right now, having played for a relatively short while in the grand scheme of things, I think a TL;DR review is in order.
I am a competent FPS player, and have been for many years. I am a huge fan of milsims, the ARMA series, Red Orchestra etc. Run and gun FPS games along the lines of Planetside 2, which I've plowed far too many hours into and the Battlefield series. This game plays like none of the above while trying to cater to the entirety of the player base.
I am currently level 4, close to level 5 in the game, which doesn't sound like much given my play time but some heavy grind is to be expected.
Level 1-2 was great, I felt immersed in the grit and grime, massive infantry battles played out between regular troopers, with the occassional support jeep or gun car, or my first ever battle featuring a tank on either side, it felt great to see the pieces falling in place.
THEN came level 3, which throws you immediately into the regular pool of players, now many of these people buy weapons/upgrades or are FAR past your level and time investment. Snipers are rife and it is not uncommon to spend time on the same maps just one level previous you were scoring 10-15 kills or scoring a 5 k/d to be picking the scattered remnants of your brain up from the forest, the road or the barn- every- single- spawn.
Overwhelmingly I have died more to enemy sniper tryhards than I have random tank barrages (Which are also an issue) and it seems everyone and their grandmother is laying in the bushes with a scoped rifle, headshotting you as you leave your spawn from several hundred meters away.
TL;DR?
Map design needs work to prevent spawn camping and some maps feel one sided based purely on your sides spawn locale - Realistic and immersive this aint'
Team balancing is abysmally bad - 15 germans versus 9 Americans or vice versa
Role balancing is terrible - 3 german tanks to 1 american tank and ten enemy snipers at all times.
Weapons - Some are clearly OP, which despite my wish for a 'realistic' WW2 experience, will need to be fixed
I WANT to like this game, hell I want to love it. I'm far from a casual tryhard that wants things handed to me, I love the grind, I love the work, I love the satisfaction of dropping an enemy, I love the sheer enormity of what they are trying to achieve but right now? Well right now it's the bloody stump at the end of your wrist after you cooked that MK2 for too long.
Level 1-2 I'd easily rate a 7/10 with hopes as I leveled for this to grow along with the scope of battles.
Level 3 Took a dump right in my mouth and told me it was humble pie.

Far Cry 3 is an open world action-adventure first-person shooter video game developed by Ubisoft Montreal in conjunction with Ubisoft Massive, Red Storm Entertainment, Ubisoft Shanghai, and Ubisoft Reflections, published by Ubisoft for Microsoft Windows.
The main story is about a couple of age 20 something American tourists, holidaying in a tropical island in Thailand but caught up in a whole load of trouble when they got kidnapped by a savage terrorist group. You play as one of the survivors Jason and through your actions, beat the bad guys and win the day.
The open world feel of this game is brilliant. It is a joy to traverse in large open world lush tropical jungles, exploring little nooks and crannies and seeing wild animals roam about doing their thing. I like how the game has some very interesting mechanics that are tied to the world exploring.
For example, you can craft bags and equipments from salvaged wild animal hides. Yes hunting is actually possible in this game, and extremely useful. You can also explore the various radio towers across the tropical island to unlock them which you will get better weapons for free. It even tries its best to immerse you by using tattoos that you brand on your skin as indicator of skills that you learn in-game.
The game also lets you have it your way on how to approach a mission. Do you want to go in all stealthy and ninja-like? Run in guns blazing? Both styles are equally viable.
That said, the negatives for this game, at least for me are focused mostly on the story elements itself. The protagonist Jason, is a typical American teenager with no prior military training of any sorts. It is kindda hard to believe that a soft-spoken guy who has never handled firearms before would suddenly go all Rambo and suddenly be proficient in all sorts of exotic weaponry and even a master of stealth kills.
I also didn't like how a very important villian Vaas whom you meet at the beginning of the game is just simply shoved away halfway thru the game for a much lesser developed final boss. Really was a wasted opportunity as Vaas was such a good villian. I don't understand why they set out to create such an interesting character then suddenly cast him aside midway thru the story.
Also, while the crafting is fun, eventually you will craft every bag in the game, and never have to hunt wild animals again. Its abit of a shame because it was fun to actually explore, and hunt them. To have the whole process of hunting suddenly come to a halt because you are unable to craft better bags is abit of a shame. I wished the bags had some kind of durability mechanic so we could continue hunting to be able to patch / repair them or something.
Overall Rating: 8.0 / 10

If I say
is derivative, you'll probably immediately jump to the conclusion that it's because it's another goddamned game with zombies in it. Which it is, but that's not where it is at its most derivative. Sure, the zombie apocalypse has been done to (un)death to the point where me complaining about how it's become a cliche is a cliche in and of itself. And the relentless grime of the ruins of Seattle mixed with more bucolic but violated suburbs will definitely remind one of "The Walking Dead" and the countless source materials that inspired it. The much more interesting source material copied by
, however, is actually something as far removed from the grit and greyness of current zombie fiction as can be imagined - the whimsical, magical and thoroughly player-punishing original
.
Luckily there's no clock and there's no having to go back to the beginning upon death. But
serves as a resurrection of a style of play mostly left abandoned after the early successes of
,
and that lineage. Your avatar, Randall Wayne, moves with a surprising, loping grace - at times an unbelievable grace as the former park ranger wall-jumps, but honestly, this isn't a game that really cares that much about plot. Oh, there is a plot - Randall struggles with nightmares as he attempts to rescue both his family and a band of survivors in the remains of ruin-porn Seattle - but that comes secondary to the platforming. This isn't the bouncy platforming of Mario - there's a human desperation in Randall's movements even as you navigate set-pieces that seem wholly illogical except through the magic of platform game logic.
The game will kill you. Be ready for that. The platforming requires thought, to the point that the game is, in some ways, a puzzle game. That said, enough trial and error (and repeated painful deaths for Mr. Wayne) will usually allow you to figure out the correct series of moves needed to get through a tricky spot, and the game is incredibly generous with checkpoints, meaning that you won't have to repeat tough challenges over and over again.
In terms of plot and atmosphere,
is the child of children of the 1980s. The nod to the older games this one is based on carries through to its time setting, though you'd be forgiven for not noticing in some ways - the time period doesn't really affect the plot except for some window dressing, though the visual window dressing is often nicely detailed. The scriptwriting is fairly hackneyed and the voice acting is, bluntly, bad. Whether this is a facet of the game designers not working in English as a first langague, I don't know - but whoever did the localization in that case will be mentioned in my next year's Festivus grievances. Though in some ways, the wooden dialogue and petrified delivery could be seen as an unintentional nod to Hollywood's most gloriously brain-dead era.
I recommend
for people who enjoy games with a deep, unified sense of style, and for people who fondly remember old classics like
. It may not have the magic of that game (or even the recent re-releases of that chestnut on PSN and XBL) but it will definitely satisfy a certain itch. If you never played those old games, if you want a conquerable trial-and-error platformer where running is almost always a better option than standing your ground, pull the trigger on this one. It's not perfect, but it'll be a nice, flawed gem in the collection of the right player.

As of right now, having played for a relatively short while in the grand scheme of things, I think a TL;DR review is in order.
I am a competent FPS player, and have been for many years. I am a huge fan of milsims, the ARMA series, Red Orchestra etc. Run and gun FPS games along the lines of Planetside 2, which I've plowed far too many hours into and the Battlefield series. This game plays like none of the above while trying to cater to the entirety of the player base.
I am currently level 4, close to level 5 in the game, which doesn't sound like much given my play time but some heavy grind is to be expected.
Level 1-2 was great, I felt immersed in the grit and grime, massive infantry battles played out between regular troopers, with the occassional support jeep or gun car, or my first ever battle featuring a tank on either side, it felt great to see the pieces falling in place.
THEN came level 3, which throws you immediately into the regular pool of players, now many of these people buy weapons/upgrades or are FAR past your level and time investment. Snipers are rife and it is not uncommon to spend time on the same maps just one level previous you were scoring 10-15 kills or scoring a 5 k/d to be picking the scattered remnants of your brain up from the forest, the road or the barn- every- single- spawn.
Overwhelmingly I have died more to enemy sniper tryhards than I have random tank barrages (Which are also an issue) and it seems everyone and their grandmother is laying in the bushes with a scoped rifle, headshotting you as you leave your spawn from several hundred meters away.
TL;DR?
Map design needs work to prevent spawn camping and some maps feel one sided based purely on your sides spawn locale - Realistic and immersive this aint'
Team balancing is abysmally bad - 15 germans versus 9 Americans or vice versa
Role balancing is terrible - 3 german tanks to 1 american tank and ten enemy snipers at all times.
Weapons - Some are clearly OP, which despite my wish for a 'realistic' WW2 experience, will need to be fixed
I WANT to like this game, hell I want to love it. I'm far from a casual tryhard that wants things handed to me, I love the grind, I love the work, I love the satisfaction of dropping an enemy, I love the sheer enormity of what they are trying to achieve but right now? Well right now it's the bloody stump at the end of your wrist after you cooked that MK2 for too long.
Level 1-2 I'd easily rate a 7/10 with hopes as I leveled for this to grow along with the scope of battles.
Level 3 Took a dump right in my mouth and told me it was humble pie.

My Review for "Murder Simulator 2: Electric Boogaloo"
The Good:
-You want more Hotline? You got it, ALOT OF IT.
-A soundtrack thats so good, i have it on cassette.
-The same addicting gameplay, but with new twists with the awesome new masks...Mark's?...too much fun.
-A confusing yet compelling story.
-Why play the game over when you can MAKE YOU OWN LEVELS!
-Because there's also a Hard Mode for the masochistic completionist in all of us.
The MEH:
-My R key broke...
-May need eye surgery after extended play sessions.
-Some irritating item clipping bugs that force you to restart a level.
Overall: If you liked the first one, you're already playing this. However, if you've never played Hotline Miami before, you should absolutely give this a shot, but be warned, if you're easily agitated...many keyboards will be broken.

Skip to the bottom for a quick overview of this review.
Gameplay: Amazing so far. It plays very similarly to the first, just with many more masks to choose from. This is a very tense game. Running around the map trying to get the highest combo possible is some of the most intense action I've played in a long time. The basic premise is your character starts normally slightly outside the map, and you must move into the building and try to kill all the enemies on the floor. There are many weapons, however many of them have been imported from the first game and tweaked a bit. This game is hard. So very hard... My major complaint is the size of the levels. Many of the levels have an insane amount of windows and enemies, which discourages a fast and frantic play style. You will have to take these levels a lot slower. Thus far it seems a lot more difficult that the first, and I've only played the first act! If you were a fan the original then you will feel right at home. 8/10
Sound/Music: Oh my god the music is great! Many of the tracks are just as good, if not better than the tracks for the original. They are very electronica based, and set the mood of the game perfectly. Best soundtrack of the year yet. As for the other sounds, they are very similar to the original. There do their job, and I never thought any of the sounds were out of place. 10/10
Graphics: Beautiful! Very stylistic, just like the original. The gore is just as awesome as it was the first time around. The environments seem more detailed this time. Lots of the props can be interacted with, like when you walk into a coat rack it spins around. All the character models are unique and all the masks look fantastic. Another small addition that is great is that whenever the game is paused, it is stylized to look like what old VHS tapes looked like when they were paused. 10/10
Story: Thus far it is interesting. It is a lot less abstract. It is told by around five different perspectives, and jumps around frequently. It is set after the events of the original, with most of it dealing with the aftermath of Jacket's killings. I am interested to see where it goes, but I'd say this is the least important aspect of the game. 8/10
Editor: I will do an update once it is released.
Summary: This is the perfect sequel. It is similar enough to the original, but different enough to justify it's price. It's only 15 dollars, thats a steal! Everything has been improved, and will likely only get better once the editor is realised. Game of the year so far!
Pros:
+Stylized graphics
+Soundtrack!
+New masks
+Story
Neutral:
*Huge levels
Cons:
-No editor yet (Coming out soon)
I would recommend this to any fans of the original, as well as anyone who loves fast paced, insanely hard games.
Overall Score: 9/10
Recommended purchase price: Full price

From the makers of the hit mod "Zombie Panic: Source" comes "Basically the Same Thing but with Friendly Fire and Getting Lost in Maps that are Way Too Large and a Price Tag"
Do you find yourself craving a team-based zombie survival game where your teammates will shoot you right when you spawn just to get your pistol? That's right, friendly fire is enabled- and encouraged -to the MAX! It's great when games reward you for betraying your teammates, I wonder why Left 4 Dead didn't do the same thing? At least they're not attacking you for your melee weapons. I would never want to give up my fire axe with a full 3 second swing delay. It's just too valuable against these agile zombies! Good thing they removed the need for stamina conseravtion, right?
Are you sick of your favorite game putting you close to the action? Well don't worry about that, *when* you die, you will respawn safely on the other side of the map from where you were! No more of that pesky gameplay, why not cool off in between lives with a brisk 7 minute shamble to the action? Once you get there, be sure to speak to the friendly one-hit kill associate to be dropped bak where you started to esperience the incredibly wide and vast map all over again. And don't worry about your computer not being able to handle such an absolutley ENORMOUS map, they've taken the liberty of using like 5 or 6 houses so you don't have to load too many prefabricated buildings. The bset part is, to make sure you *really* get he most out of your walk, they've taken it upon themselves to not include immediatley-visible landmarks. It's a scavenger hunt for the gameplay!
Just in case this is all a bit overwhelming, the devs have simplified the gameplay for you. No more team selection, who has time to make that kind of decision? You'll always spawn as survivor instead of being allowed to start on the zombie team whether you want to or not. How convenient! Gone are the days of looking for your objective, having your mysterious survivor friends text your objectives and send GPS waypoints to you is all the rage! Don't worry though, there's no navigational aid for the zombies. You have to listen for the sounds of gunfire. But just to make sure that isn't too esasy, they've gone ahead and made the echo as ambiguous as possible. Plus, byt the time you get to where you think you heard the ginfire, they'll be on the other side of the map! The fun chase never ends!
If any of these bullet points interest you, then shove Contagion into your library today!

Contagion is a zombie survival horror. Although it's already sounding really dull and unoriginal it's far from it. Contagion offers you three differen't game modes. Firstly, Hunted: A pvp mode, Extraction: A mode where you escort AI survivors to safety and finally Escape: A mode where you complete objectives throughout the map which eventually lead to your escape! Besides from these game modes the game has difficulty levels. Easy, normal, hard and insane. Zombies are a headshot only kill and can even have their legs blown off (via shotgun or explosive) It's great at creating tension among the players when your're getting swarmed by zombies, you're low on ammo and your buddy behind you has just gained a taste for brains. Yes, contagion features a infection system where when you are struck by a zombie you have a chance of getting infected. (Chances get higher with higher difficulty) When this happens you have a certain ammount of time before you completely turn. Within this time you can be a hero, tell you teammates you're infected and either be shot by fellow teammates or go out in a bang. Or, you could not tell them and hide behind them and when you turn pounce of your former friends. With escape the map changes paths. Making you take a differen't path than before. Creating a fresh experience each time you play. Overall Contagion is a game where you can have large ammounts of fun with friends or without.

This game is definitely something. Before I bought the game it didn't look all that interesting to me. Based on screenshots and description it looked to me like a less polished Oblivion or something, but upon pressing the play button for the first time my opinion faded. The Singleplayer gameplay is a lot like a game of Risk, only there are NPCs that move around the map and do various things. Most often these NPCs are lords of the various kingdoms, some of which you will partake in battles with. The combat is NOT like Risk, and no names come to mind of similar combat systems in other games. During combat you play as your character, often times lined up with your troops. You and your men are on the opposite side of the field as the enemy, go figure, and the two sides must do battle the way war used to be: line up your armies and smash them into each other. Individual one-on-one combat during a battle is very enjoyable: you can swing in multiple (self-chosen) directions, same with blocking, and the damage seems farely realistic compared to combat in games like Skyrim, for example. This means that slashing with (or getting slashed by) a sword actually DOES damage, even if your character isn't well-spec'd in swordplay. Overall this game is very enjoyable, replayable, and moddable, so go git 'em Tiger.

Short but fun.  Similar to Braid or Limbo, this is clearly a game where you are expected to fail frequently, but the game does not make you wait long to try again.
Gameplay is fairly tight, and limited resources drive a number of fight-or-flight decisions.  While Randall can hold his own against a handful of enemies, he will quickly find himself overwhelmed if he fails to keep moving.
The real draw for this game, however, is the short and effective storyline.  I encourage you to read the diary pages that Randall keeps with him.  He has some with him at the start of the game, while others are found along his journey.  They will add a lot of context to the interactions he has with other characters, and make the ending more meaningful.

Contagion at first glance might seem like Left 4 Dead, but when you get into it, it's actually very different from the L4D series. Rather than a linear map, or run and gun game play, Contagion features an open map level design, and conserving resources such as ammo is key to your success. The game can get hectic with 8 player multiplayer and will involve some discovery by the player to progress through the game. It still has a few rough edges here and there, but overall it's a pretty enjoyable experience.
Pros:
- Open world environments
- Co-op or PvP game modes
- Interesting player to zombie game mechanics
- procedurally generated objectives and item placement
Cons:
- Open world can leave players lost at times
- A few bugs and quirks that still need ironing out
- Zombie game play lack luster after a couple of tries

First of, There is a MAJOR pay to win factor in this game. When i first played with training matches, i was hapily strolling along with my Gewer when suddenly, *BOO* a level one with a Degtyarev. On the earlier levels i got destroyed, though after a while, i got a good gun and pwned the enemy team. But note, I said after a while. To get good guns you have to grind to the MAX, guns cost a lot of credits and badges can be hard to level up (PS if you are leveling up a gun badge, you can just shoot in the air to level them up). Another issue with this game is the unfairness in weapons. I find that even though Germany ussually wins the war, The US guns are so much stronger than the German guns (except the MG42, though which no one uses)
Everything costs so damn many god damn credits. I get rekt by tanks alot because i down't want to use money on my bazooka or antitank magnet mines or sticky bombs.
Another anoying thing about this game are the tanks and planes, especially the planes. The amount of times i've spawned in my jeep and got instantly blown up by a tank or plane are uncountable, tanks arent that bad though is i can spawn in my bike and easily beat the turret traverse. But planes are a whole different thing. Constant bombing whenever i am infantry. On my last game i played with planes there were five german planes in the sky. FIVE. Each with more than two bombs (there is a badge that allows that) and constantly bombing. Also coming to fround level just to shoot me in my bike. There is no escaping the planes, which makes those matches frustrating and painful. ANd those damn stupid snipers make my head want to explode
The grinding in this game is painful, I earn about 3500 credits a match which is rather basic, but the good guns, which take me about a day to get cost roughly 150,000 credits. That is about 42 matches. which may not seem long, but while i was grinding on holiday it took me two days (not 48 hours, two days with breaks) to finally get the gun i wanted. But the annoying thing is that you cant test out the guns in a firing range or something like that. So i spent a while farming 120,000 for my B.A.R (Which i am trying to learn to use as i dont want to waste my money) too find out that i hate it because of the weapon sway. It took me four days to grind for that, including ribbon time (granted leveling up the garand ribbon is longer than smg ribbon which takes about a day with breaks).
So why do i reccomend this game you may ask? Because its fun. Me and my friend play often (it's more fun with a friend) and we quite often win. The firefights are very fun (note some of the guns are historically inacurate), the classes are fun, the matches are long though not tedious, the battlefields are bery big and are sprawling with enemies, and the game is challenging. So even though the game is frustrating at some points, it's fun. But only if you are willing to grind through hours.
