Well, now that its out of beta, I can finally review this. Long story short, the quality of Contagion could be graphed in a similar manner to the heartbeat of a dieing man; it started going up and down slowly, then more quickly, then it just flatlined and died. Id love to talk about the specific kind of fun I had with some versions of the game during the beta phase, but Ive got to review it for what it is NOW.
Anyway, Contagion is a zombie shooter with three "unique" modes. Extraction, where you have to assist a bunch of slow and poorly coded AI civilians to safe zones, Escape, which is basically Left For Dead with far, far less polish, and Hunted, where players try to kill eachother and be the last man standing. Extraction and Escape were always and still are largely broken, with completion requiring immense luck and foreknowledge of the map layout respectively. Hunted, what was once the game's only saving grace, has been reduced from its former glory to being a shadow of its old self, mainly due to extreme nerfs in movement speed that the devs really could never reconcile: Humans are essentially faster than normal zombies, but when players control zombies that becomes problematic, so they made humans slower, which just means the game is painfully slow to play.
As someone who bought this game on sale near the begining of its life on Steam, I can safely say that it has failed to deliver on the majority of its promise, and is generally not worth playing, and consequently not worth buying. This one's going right into the "Buyer's Remorse" folder.

"Beautiful" is not a word I think most people would use to describe anything related to the zombie genre, but it is very appropriate description for this game.  The backdrops in this sidescrolling platformer made me want to stop and look around more but we all know that is never a good idea when zombies are lurking about.  I didn't find the puzzles overly complicated and I believe that may have been by design so the pacing of the story would not be interrupted by long delays solving them.  I used an XBOX controller when playing, so I can't speak to how intuitive the keyboard controls feel, but this game was designed for the controller and it felt good to hold one in my hand again after so many hours at the keyboard and mouse.  I had a few sound issues during the cell shaded cut scenes where my sound cut out completely, but I could usually infer what was being said by the graphic novel style presentation the designers used.  All things considered, if your looking for a good atmospheric zombie tale without all the blood and gore that usually accompanies the genre, you'll like Deadlight and have fun playing it.  I'd give it an 8/10 with the sound issues, 9/10 without them.

This game is definitely something. Before I bought the game it didn't look all that interesting to me. Based on screenshots and description it looked to me like a less polished Oblivion or something, but upon pressing the play button for the first time my opinion faded. The Singleplayer gameplay is a lot like a game of Risk, only there are NPCs that move around the map and do various things. Most often these NPCs are lords of the various kingdoms, some of which you will partake in battles with. The combat is NOT like Risk, and no names come to mind of similar combat systems in other games. During combat you play as your character, often times lined up with your troops. You and your men are on the opposite side of the field as the enemy, go figure, and the two sides must do battle the way war used to be: line up your armies and smash them into each other. Individual one-on-one combat during a battle is very enjoyable: you can swing in multiple (self-chosen) directions, same with blocking, and the damage seems farely realistic compared to combat in games like Skyrim, for example. This means that slashing with (or getting slashed by) a sword actually DOES damage, even if your character isn't well-spec'd in swordplay. Overall this game is very enjoyable, replayable, and moddable, so go git 'em Tiger.

Ooo-wee. Far Cry 3. What a rollercoaster this game was.
Let's start with the good--which is a lot. A huge range of weapons, customizable talent trees, exciting and realistic (at least more realistic in comparison to other FPS games) combat, colorful characters, and a vast environment to explore and destroy to your liking.
The guns are great, the environment is great, the stealth vs run'n'gun option, the story is pretty solid, minus a few characters and plotholes here and there but a few splotches don't stop this game from shining. The levels are detailed and so much fun to look around and explore. Also the in-game color commentary by another character is interesting and almost 3rd wall breaking but it does serve a purpose to keep you entertained and to let you know you and your friends aren't alone on this island.
What's better than fighting a bunch of pirates on a tropical island? Fighting crocodiles, sharks, and cassowaries at the same time! That's one thing this game did right above other FPS's--wildlife. A lot of shooters neglect animals in their games, and I can't imagine why--it adds a whole level of excitement and detail, especially with the "challenges" (it's easy to kill a pack of leopards with a rocket launcher, but try it with a simple bow and arrow? Much more satisfying).
So with a beautiful island full of danger that only you and your trusty explosive arrows and and automatic rifles can solve, populated with colorful and interesting characters along the way, what's wrong with the game?
Well, anything but the main story is ridiculously repetitive. But it does it at least in a different way. For example, to hold ammo, you need to craft bigger ammo pouches. I can't remember the exact animals you need to skin to make said pouches but for example it's like "4 deer skins for level 1 ammo pouch, 2 tiger skins for level 2," etc. And the same goes for every other pouch you need to upgrade. The same goes for all the collectibles and trophies. It just becomes a tiring grindfest.
And another issue is that it seems like they wasted all their creativity making 3 or 4 really interesting characters and then just copy+pasting the rest. I couldn't even tell you what Jason's girlfriend looked like, or what her name was, but I still remember Vaas and will never forget him. And I specifically recall saving one of my friend's from human traffickers and the first thing he says when he sees me after I rescue him? "Nice tats, man!" Nice. Tattoos. Like, what? Did they drug him before he was going to be sold? Like, no concern for the situation at hand, just nice ink on my arms.
And the story is almost a bit forced. Seems like there are a handful of times where I had the option to escape with my friends, or at the very least send my friends away for help while I could have stayed and dealt with the situation at hand since apparently a college party bro suddenly becomes a trained killer and skilled combat tactician almost overnight. Though the game does put in a bit of effort to "train" you through a quest or two.
Despite its shortcomings with a few 2D characters, repetitive grinds, and somewhat silly story, the game is still really solid, story is still somewhat engaging, and there are equal interesting and fantastic characters as there are cardboard ones. Overall a fun game and great adventure and I enjoyed my experience with it for the most part.

I wont waste your time with dramatic statements, so here is a list of the pros and cons of this game. This is not a complete list.
Pros
- Excellent and engaging combat system, if you want to kill someone you must time your attack well and make sure you actually hit them. Horseback combat is great and satisfying giving you the ability to charge into combat.
- Tactics and stategies are a required element in battle and that does include charging head first into the fray. Battles are great fun with alot of creative ways to fight the enemy depending on your units.
- Unit variety is immense. From tough armoured spearmen, to crazy vikings. Nobles knights to horse archers this game has a great variety of units to spice up your army.
- Awesome seiges make taking and holding castles and cities intense and frantic.
- Large campaign map, go to various cities, castles and villages with 6 different kingdoms waring and plotting against eachother for dominance.
- Feudal system brings the kingdoms to life and offers a decent level of intrigue with the various lords and Kings.
- Be your own king, when your a strong enough you are able to forge your own kingdom. However the consequences of this are significant and is something the game punishes you for doing unprepared.
- Character customisation allows you to play the combat the way you like.
- Excellent value for money, a slow burning game but one that is engaging throughout.
- Fantastic mod supports, diplomacy mod is essential in my opinion.
- Tough but fair, if your unprepared then you will lose hard. If you decide to leave the city on your own then dont be surprised when a group of bandits kidnap you.
- Solid and intense multiplayer
- Armies feel organic as they evolve from raw recruits to veterns.
- Are you the noble and honorable commander or the ruthless general that pillages cities. You decide.
Cons (Some of them are subjective)
- Dated graphics, but this does mean you can run it on a potato.
- Due to the nature of the game it can get somewhat tedious as you build up your strength to claim independance.
- Despite its open world feel, you do feel like your are being pushed down the whole conquering army route. There is no option to be a rich merchant and buy your way to power or any other subtle ways, this is not Crusader Kings 2. This game is about being the conqueror.
- When ruling you govern nobles rather than your people. You feel as if your just courting favours from the nobility rather than enforcing the right to rule or setting policies. Diplomacy mod does have some elements of governing but it is just reduced to slide bars.
- For a game focusing on the medieval era the intrigue offered is passable but not deviously machiavellian as one would like. Sure you can marry for favour or support a rival claim, but no assassinations or great conspiracies. Alot of the intrigue offered is simple to do and is rather dull.
In summery a great, intense game if your want a conquering simulator which is slow burning and a great value for money, if your more interested in the intrigue and politics of the middle ages then get Crusader Kings 2 instead.

Here is the most honest review I can come up with:
HnG is a very fun game, the ambiance and gritty feeling of WW2 is conveyed well in this game.  To most WW2 die hard fanatics, the arcade style of this game may not fit the bill for you.  It can be very unrealistic at times and many of the weapons + vehicles operate on levels that are historically innaccurate.  For an FPS, the game takes getting used to as things feel like they are clunky and slow at first.  Some of the gun sights can be hard to get used to and there is alot of overcorrecting and sway handling to take account for on most guns to get good shots.
I primarily play as a Tanker.  The tanks are awesome and provide a very interesting mode of play.  Sticking your head out of the tank to get a good view of your surroundings can be risky as you can be sniped out of your tank and have it stolen.
There are snipers everywhere in this game, so running in open field is pretty much a death sentence for any unit.  The sniper rifle is very easy to attain, even on infantry and you can easily get spawn camped by snipers.  Like actual war, flanking and cover is huge in this game.
If your just starting out without any gold, the game can be very frustrating.  You may end up being sniper bait until you can afford something better, which takes time and grind.  Or wallet warrioring.  There is a huge convenience to buying gold, but everything can be achieved without it.  The best bang for your buck is the veteran memberships, which can also be bought with in-game credits.
After the Young update, the grind has exponentially increased, but the game has become more balanced and with more options.  I will take the grind model over "rent-a-guns" like other cash shop FPS games.  While the game is hard, you can do decently well with starter gear and the first tier SMG to become decently competitive its not that hard to obtain.
Dropping a few bucks into a decent gun and/or vehicle can completely change your exprience.  I don't recommend buying the ribbons you need to unlock things outright, the boosters are a much better option.  Ribbons level relatively fast to unlock weapons, badges, and vehicles until the midway point.  So you can get decent stuff fairly early, but amazing stuff takes time.
You can also do fairly well with almost nothing.  One one map I scored 48 kills with just the combat knife because I had no gear to weight me down and I was moving like a ninja.
There are still some problems with game balance, but it is improving.
PROS:
-Great atmosphere and feeling once you get the controls down
-Many dynamic ways to play by having your soldiers take specific roles such as infantry or tank pilot
-Maps are well designed and a good size, although I'm hoping for larger full scale maps with all unit types
-The strategy aspect of the game is expensive to get into but looks interesting
CONS:
-Game balance.  While fun HnG is far from balanced, especially with the US being far superior with their weapons and vehicles to the Germans.  In staged battles the US Chaffe light tank is pretty much a medium tank with a light tank label.  You can pretty much blow away every enemy tank uncontested with its 75mm turrent when the highest calibur that the german light tank turrets go is 35mm.  Also the STUG tank hunter on the german side has no machine gun and the gunner seat is open, allowing your co-pilot to get sniped.  The US hellcat equivalent has an enclosed gunner, built in machine gun, and better manuverability.  Also as a tanker, regular infantry and mines/sticky bombs are overpowered.  People regularly kamikaze themselves on you using motocycles and mines.  The tanker has very little defense against this.
-Progression system: Repairs are expensive and sometimes you are forced into half completed battles that award you with less credits that it costs to refill your ammo.  Grinding to get what you want can take a long long time without spending gold in the cash shop.
-Armor system.  The armor system in the game is broken at the moment and doesnt work right, shells don't reflect right and I've been killed by 2 shots by an enemy tank on my Tiger II - the most armored tank in the game - even when the shells hit the front and most heavily armored section of my vehicle.  It's pretty much just rolling dice right now.
-Snipers all over.  I think the overabundance of snipers ruined the game, snipers should be limited to recon and the scoped rifle on infantry needs to go.  This was improved by limited the scope on infantry sniper rifles to lower zooms, but still poses an issue.
VERDICT:
The game definitely feels like BETA.  It's a fun as hell beta but it does have some balance issues and needs some polish.
I feel that HnG has the potential to be a really great WW2 game.  I think some adjustments (especially on the german side), and polish of certain game systems is needed.
Overall, I do think that the game has matured enough for me to change my review.  I definitely recommend trying it out.  I also do think the devs are good folks and do want to see this game succeed.

First of all, I bought Contagion when it was in its Early Alpha stages and couldn't really play a lot of it since there weren't a lot of players and servers. But now, I found out that the game is finally released and I'm not disapointed. At first I wanted to get this game because it reminded me of The Walking Dead TV show (Which I say about a lot of zombie games but they are not as they seem to me at first) but it's not like that at all except for the "Only headhsots kill" rule. Now since the release a lot has changed: New and modified weapon slots which make it easier to find weapons, new zombie "Roar" feature which lures more zombies to the survivors to make them suffer even more, achievments, trading cards, modes and an improved intro and menu. The level section is easy to choose from, the only problem is that there still aren't many servers to play on, but if you do find one, the experience is great. The levels are never the same and the keyitems are always scattered in different locations and some pathways are closed in one playthrough but in the other they aren't. The only negative aspects I can find in this game for now are the way too overpowered human controlled zombies and the zombie spawn points. They don't die to a single headshot, no, they take an entire magazine to the face to die. They are just normal zombies to blend into the crowd and not some special infected like in Left 4 Dead, so they should have lower health and better spawn points. They can kill a human in about 2 hits and once you respawn you need to find the survivors at the other end of a totally confusing map!
All in all Contagion is fun zombie game and I'd recommend it to anyone who likes zombie survival games which they can play with friends.

Deadlight is not worth playing. The platforming is incompetent, the combat is a buggy disaster, and the story is a transparent, mewling mess.
The premise is your standard biteception fare: zombies take over, survivors come down with a case of interminable douchiness, world goes to hell. You play a fellow named Randall Wayne, some random sod searching for his family months after the end of civilization. The story rarely meets anything resembling coherence, constantly pushing the boundaries of plausibility. Gentle helicopter crashes? Check. Man outrunning a hail of bullets? Check. Insane scientist calling the zombie plague the heaven we've all been awaiting? Check. You'll have predicted the outcome of the story before you finish the first area of the game, but the game doesn't miss an opportunity to hammer you with every trope it can find before you finally reach the punchline. It doesn't even have a consistent presentation: the story is told largely through comic-book-noir cutscenes, which clash amusingly with the gameplay's generic realistic-3D look.
On the gameplay side, Deadlight is basically a 2D platformer with 3D backgrounds used to the worst possible effect. You'll often be left wondering whether items are in the foreground or background -- sometimes you'll jump at something which isn't there, and other times you'll bounce off an object you thought was out of reach. The platforming itself fails to offer challenge in any sense beyond the omnipresent bugs. You will rarely have more than 1 route, there are basically no puzzles to solve, and the game never pressures you to make tough maneuvers. You'll fall to your death repeatedly, however, because the game sometimes just forgets to grab ledges or just won't turn around without running halfway across the screen. The controls are generally unresponsive and unwieldy. The game actively prevents meeting that platforming zen by pulling you to a complete stop any time you do anything. Catch a climbing line midair? You'll be watching a 3-second animation while Randall grabs onto it, then come to a complete stop and slowly crawl from one side of the line to the other. Sometimes, Randall will teleport about because the game can't even decide where you are. He will hang from invisible ledges or be unable to jump. If you fall the wrong place, you can get completely stuck and have to restart the scene entirely.
Combat, however, is a whole 'nother level. Zombies attack from the background, so you never know when you can hit them and when you can't. Sometimes, they'll even fall back from the foreground into the background, and you're left swinging at nothing until it re-emerges on top of Randall and immediately grapples. The meeting of Randall and zombie is never remotely clean, often leaving Randall struggling with air and a zombie flailing wildly behind him. Using anything but the heavy axe attack is pointless because Randall will otherwise teleport through enemies, failing to hit them, or push enemies from the ground back onto their feet. The most joy you'll get out of it is laughing at the utter absurdity of it.
To summarize, Deadlight is not worth the time to play, let alone the cash. The combat is poor, the platforming is poor, the story is poor, the presentation is dodgy, and it's just not fun.

Here is the most honest review I can come up with:
HnG is a very fun game, the ambiance and gritty feeling of WW2 is conveyed well in this game.  To most WW2 die hard fanatics, the arcade style of this game may not fit the bill for you.  It can be very unrealistic at times and many of the weapons + vehicles operate on levels that are historically innaccurate.  For an FPS, the game takes getting used to as things feel like they are clunky and slow at first.  Some of the gun sights can be hard to get used to and there is alot of overcorrecting and sway handling to take account for on most guns to get good shots.
I primarily play as a Tanker.  The tanks are awesome and provide a very interesting mode of play.  Sticking your head out of the tank to get a good view of your surroundings can be risky as you can be sniped out of your tank and have it stolen.
There are snipers everywhere in this game, so running in open field is pretty much a death sentence for any unit.  The sniper rifle is very easy to attain, even on infantry and you can easily get spawn camped by snipers.  Like actual war, flanking and cover is huge in this game.
If your just starting out without any gold, the game can be very frustrating.  You may end up being sniper bait until you can afford something better, which takes time and grind.  Or wallet warrioring.  There is a huge convenience to buying gold, but everything can be achieved without it.  The best bang for your buck is the veteran memberships, which can also be bought with in-game credits.
After the Young update, the grind has exponentially increased, but the game has become more balanced and with more options.  I will take the grind model over "rent-a-guns" like other cash shop FPS games.  While the game is hard, you can do decently well with starter gear and the first tier SMG to become decently competitive its not that hard to obtain.
Dropping a few bucks into a decent gun and/or vehicle can completely change your exprience.  I don't recommend buying the ribbons you need to unlock things outright, the boosters are a much better option.  Ribbons level relatively fast to unlock weapons, badges, and vehicles until the midway point.  So you can get decent stuff fairly early, but amazing stuff takes time.
You can also do fairly well with almost nothing.  One one map I scored 48 kills with just the combat knife because I had no gear to weight me down and I was moving like a ninja.
There are still some problems with game balance, but it is improving.
PROS:
-Great atmosphere and feeling once you get the controls down
-Many dynamic ways to play by having your soldiers take specific roles such as infantry or tank pilot
-Maps are well designed and a good size, although I'm hoping for larger full scale maps with all unit types
-The strategy aspect of the game is expensive to get into but looks interesting
CONS:
-Game balance.  While fun HnG is far from balanced, especially with the US being far superior with their weapons and vehicles to the Germans.  In staged battles the US Chaffe light tank is pretty much a medium tank with a light tank label.  You can pretty much blow away every enemy tank uncontested with its 75mm turrent when the highest calibur that the german light tank turrets go is 35mm.  Also the STUG tank hunter on the german side has no machine gun and the gunner seat is open, allowing your co-pilot to get sniped.  The US hellcat equivalent has an enclosed gunner, built in machine gun, and better manuverability.  Also as a tanker, regular infantry and mines/sticky bombs are overpowered.  People regularly kamikaze themselves on you using motocycles and mines.  The tanker has very little defense against this.
-Progression system: Repairs are expensive and sometimes you are forced into half completed battles that award you with less credits that it costs to refill your ammo.  Grinding to get what you want can take a long long time without spending gold in the cash shop.
-Armor system.  The armor system in the game is broken at the moment and doesnt work right, shells don't reflect right and I've been killed by 2 shots by an enemy tank on my Tiger II - the most armored tank in the game - even when the shells hit the front and most heavily armored section of my vehicle.  It's pretty much just rolling dice right now.
-Snipers all over.  I think the overabundance of snipers ruined the game, snipers should be limited to recon and the scoped rifle on infantry needs to go.  This was improved by limited the scope on infantry sniper rifles to lower zooms, but still poses an issue.
VERDICT:
The game definitely feels like BETA.  It's a fun as hell beta but it does have some balance issues and needs some polish.
I feel that HnG has the potential to be a really great WW2 game.  I think some adjustments (especially on the german side), and polish of certain game systems is needed.
Overall, I do think that the game has matured enough for me to change my review.  I definitely recommend trying it out.  I also do think the devs are good folks and do want to see this game succeed.

8/10. Good, a few irritating flaws and pretty short but it's fun and comes with feels.
However, if you're allergic about color filters (desaturation for example, if you're the kind of people willing to mod it out of every single game you can) or dark stuff (half the screen is black, the other half is brown), you should avoid this game. It's not exactly colorful, and that's alright because the theme isn't exactly carebears or mario, but then people remove desaturation in Dead Island (another game where it fits the theme) or play with ridiculously high gamma settings on Rust (another game where darkness is a pretty important part of the gameplay and the atmosphere).
Enough ranting, more about the game. It's pretty short, 4 hours if you're enjoying your time (and/or try to get all of those collectibles), but closer to 2 hours if you run through (note: running through is encouraged here, because non-armed combat sucks and guess what, no ammo for half the game!), but it has its moments (mainly the parts about running from "shadows" (2dark4u zombies) in the town).
Graphically, it looks alright but it's hard to tell how anything looks like in this game. There are a few bad parts though, at some point you encounter a redhead and her hair is the only half-colorful thing of the entire screen. Even her face is black.
Sounds are good, music is fine.
Gameplay isn't the best point of the game though, controls sometimes feels sloppy (played the game with an Xbox 360 Controller) and there's some latency on many actions (like GTA IV, where turning around takes half a second because of animations, or old french games featured on JDG). Guns aren't used much, but they are satisfying at cutting heads. But melee combat is really bad, if a zombie is attacking you you get some sort of QTE/button mashing contest to free yourself in which every zombie around you is free to kick your♥♥♥♥♥ Including the latency before your character finally gets the ability to push back the zombies.
All in all, a fun game but not the best platformer you could get and its artstyle may hurt some people's sensitive eyeballs.

I wasn't sure what to expect, since the Call of Duty series has been such a polarizing IP, often described as representing the worst of modern gaming: superficial yearly updates, lots of locked DLC content, nickel and diming you to get new vanity items, etc.  I also hadn't played a COD game in about 5 years, so I was a bit hesitant when I picked this up.  Fed up with EA and their Origin software, the fact that COD doesn't force you to use a propietary DRM tool is a huge plus.  The single player campaign was fun, while short as some have noted.  The action is fast paced, though sometimes it does feel way too "on-rails."
Graphically this game is quite nice, and the levels can be quite atmospheric.  I play on "ultra" settings, and there are some very beautiful set pieces during the single player campaign.  This isn't a graphical revolution like Crysis was back in the day, but it's a good looking game if you have the hardware.  I only recently got this game, though, so I didn't experience any of the pre-patch problems people complain about.  It's been very reliable.
The multiplayer is what most people play, and I was very happy to see the addition of the Squads feature, which is perfect for a casual player like myself.  Basically, by using bots to fill in your squad, it allows you to have an online or offline experience that feels like playing against all human opponents.  Regular multiplayer is decent, though as always it's a crapshoot as to how good/idiotic/rude your fellow gamers will be.  The game modes are fun (love kill confirmed), and the ability to build up your stats/guns/gear etc is pretty much par for the course, and the gun selection is pretty good.

Another game that I can't give a straight Yes or No recommendation for. I will go with Yes, but I ultimately grew frustrated with this game and didn't quite finish it.
Graphics in this game are outstanding. The backgrounds are detailed and atmospheric. The use of shadows is great also, especially the way the characters are all silhouettes.
Deadlight has a solid story in a tired genre with good voice acting even if the main character is a bit of a cliche tough guy.
As I proceeded through the game I had a lot of fun with the puzzles. There are times when you have no weapons and have to find ways to defeat traps/puzzles by using the zombies instead of fighting them, which is interesting.
There isn't really a lot of combat if you're looking for an action game. You will spend most of your time evading or running from enemies. Weapon selection is limited and at times non-existent. I thought it worked well for this game, since the game design doesn't require you to fight that often.
Deadlight is full of Steam achievements, some of which are obtained just by reaching checkpoints, so it regularly rewards you with a sense of accomplishment.
On the downside, the game can be frustrating. There's a lot of trial and error. Sometimes the color scheme of the game can make it difficult to discern certain objects. I fell through floors I thought were there a few times. On the plus side, checkpoints are very frequent, so you can afford some trial and error. Save points are frequent too, but if you quit the game, be prepared to repeat a few checkpoints, which is really no big deal.
Here's the MAJOR problem. This game is a port from XBOX Arcade, so it was designed with a 360 controller in mind. The conversion to keyboard and mouse is not pleasant. I eventually just gave up after COMPLETELY failing to outrun a helicopter through an obstacle course about 25 times. It requires fast reflexes and precision timing that I just couldn't manage on a keyboard (but maybe you could). You need to sprint away from the copter, then basically stop and inch your way up to fences, because if you hit jump while moving you will just bounce off the fence. Fence climbing in general is frustrating. Sometimes it would just take too long for the character to interact with the fence to get away from the helicopter in time. If you ARE using a 360 controller it may work better for you. I tried a PS2-style Logitech PC controller but couldn't remap the pre-configured 360 controller commands. Even my L1, L2, R1, R2 buttons weren't doing the same as the 360 buttons.
I was disappointed that I ultimately put this game down (at least until I get a 360 controller I guess), because I really liked the puzzles, graphics, and atmosphere.

The script writers nailed this story down to a 'T', and if it wasn't for the fascinating grip of the story this game would be average at best.
I seriously think out of all video games Hollywood should definately consider making this game into a movie. I highly praise the work put into this game. The characters are interesting, well-voiced, and very unique.
And not only is the story in this game super, but the missions are amazing also. Some missions involve you high on drugs, killing drug barons, and even fighting yourself to unleash the inner warrior.
Far cry 3 is an FPS like no other. It's skill tree is good, and collecting animal skins for better equipment make it worthwhile to go and hunt animals. I cannot say many bad things about this game. It's vast islands make it enjoyable to explore when the sun is shining, and the game makes you feel you're actually on a tropical island.
Overall - This game gave me an experience like no other game has. It's now on my list of great games!

Yet another game I purchased after seeing it on YouTube.  I enjoy Zombie themed and/or post apocalyptic themed games, despite the recent over usage of such.   I also enjoy a good 2d platformer.  So this game was right up my alley.

Let me start off by saying some of the gripes in other reviews or forum threads are warranted.  There are some technical issues at times with Deadlight, and a few control issues, but nothing too jarring in my opinion.

The graphics are decent enough, with a typical post apocalypse art style.  It works well in this game.  The game is fairly straight forward, easing you into the controls and such as you play.  The story, is your typical zombie story, but with a rather unexpected twist at the end, at least for me.   It's nothing to write home about, but it works ok for the game.

The experience is short, which in my opinion might be a positive for this one.  Seeing how the story plays out I can easily tell that dragging this game on would not be a plus but rather a negative.

My main gripes with this game are the controls.  They are you standard 2d scroller type controls, but there are a few instances where they will betray you, and cause you to die.  There are a few specific areas in this game where the controls frustrated me to no end because they just would not do what you tell them to, and in a timed area where one mistake gets you killed.   You do have the option to use a gamepad, which I did, so I cannot comment on the Keyboard controls.

Aside from that I really enjoyed my quick romp through this one and even played it a second time to attempt to gather some achievements.

Though there are some issues with zombie pathing and balancing, the value you're getting at $20 is excellent considering there is Workshop support coming soon and that the devs are commited to bringing releasing free DLCs with new guns, characters, maps and even game modes.
Should you get it? if you like a challenge and prefer realistic gameplay, definitely.
- excellent gun mechanics with realistic ballistics, penetration, recoil and decent weapon sounds
- atmospheric
- varied game modes (pvp, coop and survival)
- solid replayability on the escape maps (you actually get completely different endings, paths, objectives and loot spawn locations, unlike L4D2 that just makes loot random and the odd door here and there)
- challenging (you can die quite easily if you're not paying attention)
- good bullet detection in pvp and not a lot of lag either
- several characters to choose from
- good graphics (still the Source Engine, but the lighting is very good indoor and the weapon models are very detailed)
- a good variety of weapon types (
)
- weapon animations are very well made
- devs are easy to reach to and helpful
- official modding support (SDK)
- upcoming Steam Workshop integration
- upcoming free DLC
- frequent updates
- melee play feels clunky (still a lot better than DayZ though, but less fluid than Dead Island)
- pathing issues with zombies (has improved a bit since the alpha, but there are still issues, especially with doors)
- escape objectives are not very clear and can lead to a lot of head scratching at times
- due to the dynamic nature of the escape maps, balancing is hit or miss at times (you can either get quicly swarmed, not find enough ammo or end up with a riot zombie that blocks you and that you can't kill quickly enough)
- no option to control the volume level of the characters
- graphics are inconsistent in outdoor areas (some areas are detailed others not so much)
- few zombie models and only three zombie "types" (slow, fast and armored)
- fairly limited number of maps
- zombie animations can get stuck when in "roam mode" where you see the zombie continue to try and walk when he has an obstacle in front of him (happens a lot less since the last updates)
- crossbow bolts sometimes can't be retrieved (not sure if feature or bug :) )
- zombie clipping can occur (especially near closed doors that have to be activated by a switch)
- learning curve can be steep as there is no dedicated tutorial (this has improved since they've added tooltips post-release)
Personally, I've followed Contagion since their kickstarter and jumped aboard fairly soon after they got on steam and had the chance to see them build upon the game, adding new content, fixing bugs and improving the experience.
The dev team is comprised mostly of the people that worked on the excellent Zombie Panic Source mod for HL2 and while the production value of this game is very high compared to some other indie titles, they are a small team with a limited budget.
Arguably, for $20, Left 4 Dead 2 offers a ton of content and replayability in a solid experience; so does Dead Island and State of Decay.
Also, for $10 more, there is DayZ, which is pretty much an MMO in terms of what you can do in the game world, the huge scope, vast arsenal, customizing and rich PVP experience.
However, I feel like it's unfair to compare Contagion to similar zombie games like Left 4 Dead, Dead Island or State of Decay that cost millions to make.
I believe that if we continue to show them our support they will also continue to add content to the game, fix bugs and perhaps even come with new game modes or features, similar to what they did for ZPS.
As of 10.05.2014, they've released several updates, an official modding SDK, have revamped the zombie sounds and have promised to release a new escape map, free DLC with new characters, new guns and a new game mode, as well as Steam Workshop integration.

It's hard to say when Zombies caught the hearts and imagination of the world but recently the love for this style of monster has swept up TV, Movies, and Games.  Whether it be the Walking Dead, Left for Dead, Evil Dead (remake), Zombies seem to be here to stay.  Although Deadlight portrays this oversaturated market it does it in quite a different way.  First off, it's beautiful especially for a side scroller and adds some great side scrolling, puzzle, action platformer qualities that I lean towards in a game.   If you're a fan of zombie games, story telling, and more underground games then Deadlight won't dissapoint.
With that being said, Deadlight isn't all sunshine and roses.  First off, it's only about 3 hours of gameplay to complete and get over 1/2 of the achievements.   Now, this obviously doesn't take away from that fact that the game is fun, has a unique ending, and some cool cut scenes but it does leave you wanting more.  It feels short and not just short but lets hurry up production and get something out the door short.  The story here could be one that had an impact such as Infamous (which the cut scenes and narration reminds me of, although not nearly done as well), Last of Us, or something of that ilk.  Unfortunately Tequila Works kept it short and to the point which really takes away of the possible story rich, cinematic, potential they had in this game.
I bought this game over the Steam summer sale for 7.50$ and couldn't be happier but if you are looking for a longer game, with a deeper story, and aren't a huge side scroller or Indie fan, I'd say hold off on the 15$ and wait for a Steam Sale purchase.  If you dig this style, this story line, and want to have a fun experience then pull the trigger and give Deadlight a play through.

This review is to tell you a little about the game as I have played it.
(So I play with a small group of friends. We started playing only a little while ago so we still have much to learn.)
First off for those that are about to hit download be warned... this is "pay to win". You can have tons of fun even if you never drop a penny on this game tho. Very good gameplay for a "free" game.
Now a little bit of a warning. If you do play with riends be warned that some classes (like tankcrews) can only group with those of the same kind (tankcrews with tankcrews, ect,ect...) so make a choice with your friends to have more fun. You can switch back to the base class at anytime but it will always cost credits to switch classes, even if you have been that class before.
In a sense it is best to try to find something you like early on and try to stick to it and build up credits (you get credits after every match). I myself found that I like to stick with SMG's and cars to help out the team so I spend most my credits in that area. Tho my friends are more long distance players so the spend credits to Semi automatic and bolt action guns.
Now to talk about how you will end up spending those credits... You need ammo right? well in this game you will end up spending credits to refill your supplys or repairing any cars, tanks, or planes you own. You can also "edit" your guns with upgrades and differant ammo types so you will always have something to want in this game.
So how do you get these upgrades you may wonder... Well this game uses the badges system. There is always something to get EXP for in this game. From capping bases, getting kills with a type of weapon or driving teammates to places to just walking... it is a thing...
Metals are given to you at some points that act as "buffs". I don't really want to go into this one since it is kind of one of those things that will be understandable in under 10 seconds when you get one.
So where do I stand on this game you my ask? Well let me leave this as the last note in this review... My friend and I were in my car heading to a base that was defended by a tank.... so we bum rushed the tank head on and jumped out last second and both shot it with rockets point blank and killed them. Soon after we had to hop in a bike and huff it it the next base while we sang a song for the poor tank driver we just killed.
10/10 will be driving that car into another tank again.

New review since the game just released from the Early Access stage. Immediately had to reset to dafault keys and it seems to be an okay game. It's more serious than L4D as the game has no specialized zombies like a tank or witch, just traditional zombies. Players can also play as zombies after dying as a human, so it has a bit of Zombie Panic and No More Room in Hell mixed in together. Considering part of the Zombie Panic team also worked on No More Room in Hell, this game really does resemble a bit of both. The game offers a fair amount of modes, objective mode is fairly complicated and easy to get lost in. Extraction mode I didn't particularly like since you're acting as rescuers. A bit strange of a goal especially when the NPC's follow you around like clueless morons with no survival skills. That's the job of the military usually, to rescue survivors, not you because you're too busy trying to survive on your own. You'd think the NPC survivors would also be trying to save their own hide. So it offers a new gameplay mechanic that Nmrih and Zombie Panic doesn't offer, but it's not the best mechanic either. Cellphone replaces the compass function you'd normally have in Nmrih and unlike Nmrih the players can still play after dying so a bit of Zombie Panic.
The good news is the game is less spatially disorientating than what it was in the past, so I give it a thumbs up for improving the camera movements of the game. The zombie running animation with the claws running out furiously could use some work, but aside from that, overall it's a mediocre game. I suggest buying this cheap and not at the full price ($19.99) it is currently at. You can have more fun with the free Zombie Panic and No More Room in Hell mods.

This game is quite amazing. I've never seen something quite like it. Its an open world sandbox for medeviel politics and combat. Wondering around growing your forces, going to tournaments, causing intrigue with the local lords, raiding villages, fighting in wars. Those are the kinds of things you primarily do. Its surprisingly much more satisfying than Rome Total War, where you start to dread entering battles. Clobbering through enemies never really gets old, although infantry to infantry combat could stand some improvement (the game is built around riding on a horse, as per the name). Think of it as Dynasty Warriors Total War with a faint hint of Crusader Kings.
There's a lot of different approaches in playstyle, army composition, etc. So while I imagine there's a lot of replay value in the full game (seems like it would take quite a long time to become king or have your faction take over the world), you'll probably want to play it again to take another approach.
All in all, its easy to get into, and doesn't seem to get boring, even though I played the demo for about double my steam time a few years ago.

I'd give Contagion a 8/10.
Contagion is officially released, and it has come a long way from even a few months ago and has gained a lot of polish.  Extraction mode is a ton of fun to play, heading from house to house and holding out against waves of zombies until it's time to make a break for the extraction point, civilians in tow.  The escape mode (which is similar to L4D where you make your way to an extraction point across the map) has some issues, (if you start mid game you start at the beginning of the map, alone.)  and could use a GPS map like the extraction mode has, as a group that is not familiar with the map can easily lose their way.  Hunt mode is Deathmatch with zombies spread all over the map, and has the cool and unique function of letting you use your phone to call other survivors phones to locate them audibly.  Guns are very deadly so it only takes 1 or 2 shots to put them down once you locate them.  Melee weapons have a satisfying heft to them and are great to silently take out small groups of zombies without bringing the hordes down on you.
Overall this game is totally fun if you enjoy the zombie genre and you will learn quick to go for the headshot if you want to put  a zombie down!
There are some servers that have some lag issues but all in all my experience with latency has been pretty good, and since this runs off the source engine, it doesn't take a mondo computer to run, but still looks pretty good on the lowest settings.
Map design and ambience are very well done, though once again you NEED to learn the map as there are a lot of little side paths that dead end and will get you killed if you run down one with a horde at your back!

A really nice game - Great story line, graphics and use of environment.
The levels are well planned and do not become repetative which I find side-scrollers can become very fast.
The characters in the game are also well thought out and have a good depth of back story which adds largely to the game world.
Game play is generally good and fluent. The fast-paced paths work well and the player is required to work when running through the environments however there are some snag which which got me pretty frustrated.
There are several cons:
As mentioned above, the fast-paced stages are let down by snagging which become frustrating when in a chase.
Example: running from a chopper and the player gets keeps volting the same fence instead of dismounting.
A few of the controls do not make sense & feels like the Keyboard controls were shoehorned in after being designed for a gane pad.
Example: you have to hold shift and somehow hit control at the same time to roll.
The melee weapons are vitually useless. You can not tactically kill a hord if you are using a melee - believe me, I tried.
The pick-up-item is far to slow for the pace of the game. Many occations I have stopped to pick something up and by the time I have been given control of my character again, I am dead.
The above cons are not big deals. I do think using a game pad would stop the repeated volting on fences - it would also solve my issue with the control issue. The melee part only really became aparent a few times in the game where I was forced to fight.
Overall a good game. I would play through with a controller next time.

This is a review for the multiplayer of Call of Duty: Ghosts, as the game is so poorly optimized I'm not even going to begin to attempt the singleplayer (and we all know we don't play Call of Duty for its story). I am a Call of Duty fan. I have been a fan since Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare, but this game may be the game that stops me from purchasing another Call of Duty. This game's PC version was poorly executed, and if this is the treatment I expect to get with future titles, you can forget it Activision. To start with, I have a fairly nice machine. I can run Skyrim on the highest graphical settings with HD graphical mods with excellent FPS, but I have to run Call of Duty: Ghosts at a medium setting because of how utterly poorly optimized this game is. Graphics are not everything, but they are an important part and in this respect Call of Duty fails. It's "revolutionary graphics" looks pretty much the same as other titles in the franchise. On to the gameplay (when the game decides to let your machine play), it's not bad. It's a pretty decent ARCADE SHOOTER. This game is not in any way meant to be realistic, and if you come into the franchise on that assumption you are wrong. The upgrading and leveling system is pretty nice, but nothing spectacular. The game hardly improves from it's predecessors. Not the mention, Activision insists on its horrible "Hardened Editions" or DLC models. This game is just another cash grab, and I feel ashamed that I have given so much money to these people. Do not purchase this title for the PC.

Deadlight leaves me with mixed feelings. Overall I enjoyed the game and appreciated its artistic style and interesting levels, the design reminded me of Flashback, Prince of Persia and Rick Dangerous soaked in healthy dose of The Walking Dead. The agility of Randall suited the ruined post apocalyptic world and gave the sense that he was a survivor long before we joined him. However there were some points where control response let Randell down, for example trying to hack a Shadow to death or pulling at shelving to block a door. There were a number of times I felt frustrated as Randall died purely because my frantic key presses didn't register in Randall's synapsis and he just stood there serving himself up as fresh zombie meat.
The game is very unforgiving and perhaps should be when set in the Deadlight world. Death in some parts of the game is frequent and at times felt a little unfair. I become frustrated at the load times between death and respawn and felt this was unneccessary and broke the flow of the gameplay. Also the amount of ground lost caused me slight annoyance and  I felt that the check points could be reworked to improve the flow. For instance when I have to sit through an automatic scene and listen to some speech then pick up the gun over and over... Yeah, that gets dull quick.
The story was a little generic given the satuation of the Zombie genre but it successfully joined the segments of the game together. Voice acting was a little weak but certainly forgivable.
As frustrated as I got at times, Deadlight kept drawing me back in and left me wanting to see more. I felt it ended well with a good opening for a sequel and one I will look forward too if it is on the cards. As negative as I may come across here, I still recommend Deadlight. Even with all it's annoyances it still succeeded in being fun. I'd give it 65-70%.

GAMEPLAY: Know this: the game's difficulty progression is based on setting up obstacles to be increasingly difficult to pass solely based on the game's clunky controls. It becomes evident 2/3 through that it is a design choice, and that the challenge is intended to come from enduring dozens of seemingly needless deaths to a chorus of "WHAT THE HELL? I DIDN'T WANT TO DO THAT!". There are context-sensitive abilities (such as breaking through doorways) that solve puzzles and progress scenes. Unfortunately, they are not as sensitive as one would hope. Instead, they seem to be always on. Running toward any solid wall causes the player to attempt to ram it like a door. Because it is a wall, the player bounces off for a stun animation for a brief moment. These sorts of abilities are all well and good except for a few action sequences that require perfectly executing a series of moves to get through a section without stalling out because the game thought you were trying to do something else. I'm probably not describing it well, because that sounds like exactly the kind of thing that makes a 2D platformer good! In execution, with this particular game, it comes off as confused and clunky.
PLOT: The plot is similar in style and structure to low budget horror movies, which is exactly what it's going for. The protagonist isn't very sympathetic, but it would be far too generous to call him complex. He and the rest of the cast are simple caricatures of genre tropes. As a result, they don't carry much emotional weight when the plot asks them to, but it is probably wrong to assume that anyone expects the plot to be the driving force in this game. I will say that if you reach the end and felt like the task was a chore, the ending will be especially unrewarding.
STYLE: The depth of the 2.5D set pieces is actually well done and helps give life to the world you are moving through. The player character is backlit almost the entire time, making him indistinguishable from the undead enemies, called "shadows" (there is an obvious meaning behind this, but at least it's something). The game is very brown, but I suppose that is to be expected for the genre. There are a few brief moments of vibrant color that are a welcome reprieve.

**Very Fun and Engaging Game, But with a catch**
Let me begin by saying that This game is like BattleField 1943 on steroids!
Having only played a couple of WW2 FPS's (World At War and BF1943) this game is the closest to what I'm looking for in a WW2 game. And it's FREE!
I've always wanted to play a WW2 game that takes advantage of the very diverse selection of vehicles that WW2 really offered and this game definately meets my expectations in that category but I see room for more.
For the Too Long Didn't Read, here is my takedown:
+++THE PRO:
+Wide Selection Of Vehicles
-each team's equivilent of a Jeep, Tank, AAGun, ect is modified slightly (They look significantly different, IDK about tanks, but the AAguns have different sights for both teams and they shoot differently)
+Maps are diverse and can be fun (I will talk about the cons later)
+Two different types of game types (War and staged battles that don't effect the war)
-This makes the matches very intense because you can be fighting a battles that can turn the tide of the War
+A satifactory selection of game modes (Defense, Attack, Skirmish)
+Each battle you have a limited number of resources (for vehicles) and spawn tickets. This makes it exciting because your surival matters for the team. BUT there is a bad part about it that I will get into later concerning this with generals.
***The CON
+As a F2P there is A LOT OF GRINDING
+There is quite a bit of a camping problem
-The map designs don't help with this (Sometimes unless you go the VERY LONG way around, you are left in the open)
Not a fair distribution of cover
-A lot of sniping and camping
-Frequent spawn camping. My observation is a lot of this comes from the US team. The Devs need to fix this
+Spawn spots are poorly placed. Many times when an objective is being captured (or enemy close by) and you choose to spawn at that point, they place you very far away with a very open field you have to run through, and the enemy is ready to just pick you off.
+I am getting more certian every time that some snipers are using bots.
+Tank can be overpowered.
+Depending on how well the generals are on your team, you can have a good match or a very unfaif match. (Generals purchase vehicles and attack squads for your battle) So if you have a bad general then your team will just have jeeps while the enemy has jeeps, tanks, and planes. (THIS IS BY FAR THE WORST PART OF THE GAME, a close 2nd is camping)
+Small selection of guns, but wide range of equipment overall.
-Takes a long time to unlock good equipment and A VERY LONG TIME FOR GUNS.
-One gun I unlocked (2nd gun I unlocked I believe) will take a almost a month to be able to purchase with in game currency, that is, if I only save and not spend on any equipment or vehicles.
As a BETA Free2Play game, this game has a lot of potential.
If they addressed camping, fixed spawns, balanced vehicles, then this game would be purchase worthy.
Also if they get rid of the grinding and the other common F2P catches like making generals so important (Which requires a lot of grinding or a payment), I would rather buy this game for $15 ($25 if they add more content to make the gameplay more diverse)
Overall, give it a try. But DO NOT become one of those bad players that camps.

This game (in my opinion) is fun as in most game modes; extraction and escape, a lot of teamwork is needed and sharing is vital.
Pros:
- I dont have the best graphics card but with settings at low it still gives a good look to the game and in return gives decent performance (but it may not be the same on even less advanced PCs)
- the zombies are like the typical resident evil-slow-but-dangerous-in-numbers kind of zombies (which is how I prefer zombies)
- You can be a zombie and kill other live players (like in zombie panic source)
- it is based off the zombie panic source engine so if you like that mod then this is somewhat similar.
- zombie AI is clever as they will move to flank
Cons:
- the player zombies are very OP (seriously I have taken out six people with one zombie before)
- there are about a couple maps (3-4 but this does depend on the game mode you are playing aswell, NMRIH has custom maps so there are plenty more)
- NPC zombies can be found in buggy areas.

Overall I find this game very fun and a good challenge especially when I am using only a melee weapon, a lot of work has been put into this game as I will usually play periodically and there is usually a fair bit new content and the menu has been restyled and looks really cool. I think this game deserves plenty of credit for its features and hard work, and since I am a hardcore zombie gamer my natural instincts got me this game so I do recommend this game to any fans of the genre. Much better than WarZ or whatever it is called now, then again Herpes is better then that game

You guys really should have stick to the Zombie Panic Source format. But no you had to make it co-op, you had to make it only 8 players per server, you had to make it "realistic".
What were you thinking in the developing process? That you guys actually have the experiences to make a "realistic" zombie game? no you don't! So why try for this half♥♥♥♥♥attempt at making a half♥♥♥♥♥"No more room in hell" experience.
Zombie Panic was great because:
1. 32 players a server = Lot's of social experience. Team base game. More dynamic social encounter
2. I have features that other zombie games doesn't. Such as "pushing furnitures to make barricade". People get creative with this, and it's greatly differentiate an experienced players to non-experienced.
3. Huge escape map. Contagion maps are linear and predictable. You guys might did a better job at "decorating" them, but too bad when it's come to interactiveness it as stale as a wallpaper. Nothing is movable in Contagion, everything is a stiff as a rock, even chairs.
And let's talk about the Zombie AI, it's a good idea for a new features....but it shouldn't be the reason why you replace 32 player base with it. I get it, I have more zombies to shoot at now, but in no way it can replace encounter I get with a human zombie player. And the AI, they aren't smart, they just walk toward you until you put a bullet in their head...there's no challenge to it, just a mean for you to waste ammo. At least in NMRH, ammo is limited and melee is challenging.
In conclusion, if you still have the budget...revamp the game...make it Zombie Panic Source 2. Otherwise, this is a dead game and it won't be an undead one.

I never purchased a Ubisoft game before, so I really didn't know much about this Uplay tool everyone complains about.  Now that I've gone through this myself, I have to admit that it's the worse gaming requirement I've ever come across.  There's absolutely no reason for this when you legally purchase games through a service like Steam.  I had to make a general comment on Uplay before going through my negative experience with this game on my PC.
Onto the game .. it started off horribly.  First the game is out of sync between video and audio.  It recommended "high" settings (not ultra mind you), but the frame rate kept shooting down and the audio was out of sync.  I found switching this to "medium" seemed to get the video/audio back in sync.  Okay solved that snafu and back into the game.  So I'm going through the first part of the game where you sneak around with your brother.  Come to a map and game tells me to pick it up with letter E.  Keep pressing E on my keyboard but nothing's happening.  Really?!!  So with the help of the web (not the game), found I had to keep the letter E pressed down.  Would be nice if the game tutorial told you this.  You can just tell while playing that it wasn't ported well from console to PC.
Okay moving on .. my soldier in-game brother dies and find my character is a sissy :(  Now I have to make a run for it.  Running for awhile, eventually go through this cavern by ducking and come out the other side and then this guy drops on top of me with a knife.  Game tells me to press Space Bar.  No matter how I press it (here and there, holding it down (worked before with "E")), I die each time.  Grrrrrr :(  So check the web again to find there's an on-going issue back to the beginning of the PC version and Ubisoft never fixes it.  So I now have to bind my space bar to another key not already bound (I chose G since it wasn't used and close to my movement keys).  Finally killed the knife guy and moved on.
At the very beginning, I chose to play this game on the easiest of settings.  I'm not really into challenges after working hard each day; I basically just want to run around and shoot bad guys "in game of course".  However, even on the easiest setting, I'm constantly needing to shoot up with health needles just to survive.  Finally get to a point where I'm able to roam around freely and then get ambushed by komodo dragons.  When I shoot them, then here comes the baddies to finish me off.  If you get past that, then you have to constantly buy ammo (I always ran out),  and obtain all of these leaves and pelts to store more stuff.  It doesn't feel as much as a first person shooter as it feels like a survival game.
This will be the first and last Ubisoft game I purchase.  I requested a refund from Steam and don't think I'll have a problem there.  Steam itself is great, but Ubisoft should be ashamed of themselves.  However, I'm glad a lot of people have had a great experience with this game and wish them the best.  I just can't recommend it to someone myself based on my experience of the game.

This game is plagued by horrible design choices regarding gameplay mechanics and on top of the fact that the game is a pretty obvious (though relatively tolerable) console port, with sub-par voice acting for some characters. It touches on the post-apocalypse of an infested world overrun by zombies ("shadows" as they call them in this game) and although the zombies present a relatively difficult challenge, the difficult combat feels more like a design flaw than actual difficulty (for example, Dark Souls combat against AI). Beyond that, the story itself is relatively interesting, and both the graphics and art style are a breath of fresh air in my opinion, though it's not something visually stunning or unseen before; it certainly has its own charm. I quite enjoyed the comic-book style cinematic, as well as the overall presentation of the game.
The gameplay can be broken down into two or three parts; platforming, combat, secret finding.
Platforming in this game is okay, but I've had better. Essentially, the platforming is plagued by unresponsive controls, where you'll keep flipping to the left and right side of a fence, or maybe jump vertically instead of off a wall. Furthermore, the feel of parkour elements in this game make you wonder why your character is unable to vault over an obstacle with relative ease, instead he partakes in the, "jump, climb up, stand on object, jump off" sequence, which can really break the flow of action during a chase scene. Another part of this is the unclear explanation of some sequences, in that you're never quite sure what you're supposed to do on a first try. For example, boxes in your path that appear to be in the background are actually in your way, and you'll trip over them if you try to sprint, sprint jump or even dive roll over them. The only way to pass the boxes without falling over (which is typically a fatal mistake) is to run at normal pace, and perform a normal jump. In a chase sequence, most players would be sprinting, so sprint jump is the common reaction to an obstacle; design flaws such as these are what plagues the game and more often than not, these flaws made me almost rage-quit the game a few times just because the ways of overcoming an obstacle was unclear (until you did trial and error a few times; the amount of times you did this stacks up by the end of the game).
Combat in this game is relatively unresponsive as well. The only time your character seems to react to being hit is when a zombie grabs you via a script (bite sequence, push to ground, etc) where you can shove them off with a single mouse click. It takes far too long to kill a zombie with melee, unless you get a lucky hit; though it emphasises the fact that you're not a fighter and you should be avoiding zombies anyway. But the inability to jump past a zombie (I believe normal-jump works, but it's not reliable) on a side-scrolling game means that in majority of the cases, you're gonna have to get down and dirty with some zombie brains on your hands. Another poor design flaw, is the fact that you can't stop interacting with objects; therefore if a zombie is near you and say there are maybe two or three just behind, it's game over. Reloading checkpoints is also a pain as you have to pass a load screen, as well as a deathcam that lasted more than a few bearable seconds. At first the loading was tolerable, but after the many trial and errors, it became unbearable.
Secrets in this game aren't really secrets at all. They're so easily found. On top of that, a lot of the story-building sequences and items just don't appear that interesting what so ever. I've tried reading the main character's journal, but got thrown off by the relatively bad handwriting (though it's a good roleplay / story thing!) as well as the easily summed up items (for example, picking up a picture gives you a one sentence summary of what it's about.) You also start to wonder what the relevance of things are, when you pick up an ID card that says "This is the ID card of *insert name here*" for the 20th time.
I haven't finished this game, but my inner drive to finish all my games will get the better of me.
In summary, for the low low price of $3 during the steam sale, get this game for a spin. Is it worth the original $15 price tag? I think not.

How do I describe the awesomeness that is Mount and Blade: Warband? Let me start with how you start the game. Mount and Blade begins with you not just creating his/her appearance and stats, but also a backstory. Now, you can choose to follow it or not, but this simple little menu screen is the first little string in a large rope that pulled me into the world of Calradia. You'll find yourself cursing your enemies like a knight of the middle ages, and gaining a twisted smile while you watch enemies fall before your blade. You can choose to pledge your sword to a king, live as a travelling Adventurer, or even invade a castle and begin your own Kingdom. However, none of these are simple tasks to accomplish. The personality of each of the Royal NPCs in the game varies, and their opinion of you, your kingdom, and even those companions you hold in your company will change and effect how they feel about you. A complex political system contours and twists your path through Mount and Blade, so no two characters will ever experience exactly the same path to glory and power. With nearly endless replayability, Mount and Blade Warband is a steal during a sale, and, while I'd say it's so good it's worth buying for the full $20 it currently costs, I'd say wait for a sale. Mount and Blade unfortunately has a few bugs and glitches, as most open world sandbox-style games do. I have experienced many Graphical Glitches throughout my playthroughs, but none that couldn't be fixed through a quick alt+tab. Mount and Blade is also not a shiny game, the Graphics were a bit behind for it's time, but I ensure you if you can dig beneath skin-deep beauty, you'll find a shining diamond within Mount and Blade.
TL;DR/Final Rating
Pros; Fantastic game, great atmosphere, lots of replayability.
Cons; Graphical Glitches, Poor Graphics, a few bugs.
Rating: 8.7/10. A fantastic game and series, with a ton of potential. I hope to see a new installment soon, and I'll see you all on the fields of Calradia!

The Far Cry games are very much the Final Fantasy of first-person shooters - each game within these series plays very similarly but are almost completely unconnected to one another, they've both spawned multiple sequels and broken out into spin-offs, and you're unlikely to find a universal answer when asking which game is everyone's favourite. I basically like this entry in the series, but for all its efforts, it still falls far short in taking the throne as best of the Far Cry games.
Here you'll play as Jason Brody, an adventuring party dude turned captive turned escapee turned murdering, rampaging sociopath who slaughters his way across a couple of islands as he rescues his friends and overthrows a villainous regime. It's the feel-good story of the year! By which I mean it's total, utter toss. It could have been a typical, lazy, straightforward story about finding the bad guy and getting the girl then living happily ever after, but almost counterintuitively, the fact that they tried to do something more with it actually only made it worse than if they hadn't tried at all. The problem is the writing. It's f*cking awful. Painfully so. Between the dialogue, characters and their actions, even the goddamn journal entries, every instance only serves to grate against the player rather than ingratiate you into the world. I honestly struggle to think of a single likable character in the game. From the island's inhabitants to the "helpful" NPCs to your best friends and even the very guy you play as, pretty much every single human being in this game is an *sshole. Like, a massive one. The kind that smells really bad and is surrounded by thick, curly hairs and has little speckles of brown all around it. Everyone around you is either going to be trying to kill you, will betray you, or mean well but only be an annoying c*ck instead. Ev-er-y-one!
The main antagonists of the story are Vaas, a deeply unhinged leader of a large and merciless band of pirates, and his boss, Hoyt, the equally deranged slave trader and mastermind behind all the brutality being forced upon the islands he has taken over. The developer seems to have taken great inspiration from Heath Ledger's Joker and try to make these characters deep and complex threats who toy with their victims, but I never really felt it. My problem with it is the fact there are so few interactions with these people, they're really talked about more than they're actually seen. And when we do see them, pretty much every interaction with them comes in the form of a cutscene rather than any kind of meaningful gameplay. This really diminished their intimidation for me. Like... we almost had to take the game's word that they were vile, evil people since we didn't get to see any real examples of that. Had Vaas been given an opportunity to be a bad*ss and we could have seen him leading an insane, nihilistic charge into some enemy forces and win, or if we'd fought him several times, maybe then I could have bought it. But, instead, the greatest threat from him is that he might bore you to death as he talks and yells his way through a handful of cutscenes at you. It just didn't work for me. I mean, I've ripped men's throats out with my knife, set dozens on fire with flamethrowers and Molotovs, and massacred countless men and animals with a huge array of weapons and vehicles. Believe me, Vaas is not the worst example of humanity in this game. Granted, Hoyt is given a little more presence and chances to be villainous, but it still doesn't leave much impact. But you'll be pleased to know there is some gameplay here, which is far more successful at gripping the player.
It's an open world, first-person shooter, so you pretty much already know the score by now. Buy, find or earn some weapons, customise them as you see fit, then use them to kill, kill, kill your way through a few dozen hour's worth of missions and exploration. There are basically three different things you can choose to pursue to pass the time in this game, either run around searching for a dizzying wealth of largely meaningless collectibles (this is a Ubisoft game, after all), clear out enemy outposts which reduce hostile presence in the immediate area, or just play through the story missions and see where those take you. The story stuff is OK, I guess. Go to location A, kill target X or destroy objective Y, then get away to safety. Either that or go on a handful of drug trips as you "discover yourself" and unlock the warrior within. I found these sequences to be pretty slow and plodding, though, or just a chore to play through. But maybe that's just me and others will enjoy some of the more abstract visuals and break from the more standard killing simulator the rest of the missions are.
I think most will agree, though, that the real fun to be had here is in the outposts. These are camps scattered all throughout the islands and guarded by several enemies which vary type from outpost to outpost. Most will have basic grunts patrolling, while others may have snipers keeping watch or flamers stomping around the grounds or dogs sniffing you out. How you approach these is entirely up to you. If you want to rock up with a grenade launcher and crater the place, go for it. Maybe you want to try incinerating the camp and picking off the stragglers amid all the panic and confusion. Handy with a silenced sniper rifle? Go pop some heads, son. Or perhaps you're the kind of tasty b*stard that likes to sneak into the heart of the lair and knife everyone in the back one by one without anyone ever knowing what hit them. It's yours for the taking, however you want to take it. It does pay to be sneaky, as liberating an outpost without being discovered will net you 1500 XP, while simply taking it by brute force will only earn you 500. But there's really no shortage of XP being handed out in the game (I maxed out mine and unlocked every ability long before the end of the game), so you shouldn't worry about that too much.
There are some online options, too, like PvP multiplayer or some specially made co-op missions, but, yeah... just do yourself a favour and don't bother with them. I only played an hour or two of the multiplayer, and really tried getting into it, but it's nothing special. And the co-op missions are a bloody mess. They're little more than going to an area and holding it down and fending off waves of spawning enemies until the game decides to let you move on to the next location and do it again. It would be a passable distraction were it not so riddled with bugs (that on several occasions made it impossible for me to continue) or lousy matchmaking or options in general. I wouldn't dare to call them lazy, but I would say they feel tacked on, like they were made at a time when they felt they needed to have these features as a bullet point on the back of the box to sell copies and make people feel like they'd gotten their money's worth and not sell their discs after tha main campaign. But there's no shortage of online FPSs to play, either competitively or cooperatively, and unless you had no other option, I don't know why you'd stick with this. Though, that said, some people are, as the games still seemed to be very active and populated with plenty of players. F*ck knows why.
While, yes, I do pretty much recommend this, at the same time, as seems to be the increasing trend with Ubi games, they've taken 10 or 15 hour's worth of a good, fun idea, then stretched it out to dozens of hours, where every hour stretched beyond its point starts to wear you down rather than entertain, and TONS of niggling interface issues and bugs and crashes keep kicking you down. But in certain doses, spread over a large period of time, this is a fun, solid shooter. Though, for my money, FC2 is still the peak of the series and a better place to get your shooty, stabby kicks.

The graphics are lacking entirely, nothing at all to be desired (except the camos which are near impossible to buy unless you grind many hours away or pay a good sum for them). The game looks worse than Cod World at War, which should be the base for all fps games to hit now-a-days, if not better. This wouldn't be a huge fault if the rest of the game was actually good.

It doesn't encourage team play unless you're playing with friends, which btw, does not use the convience of steam's friendslist if that's a drawback for anyone, I can deal with it though. The squad leader is based on the highest level "character" rather player, so if you switch from a character you've been sniping with to a tank destroyer soldier you've played less, you lose that squad commander perk (if it was ever one, for you only get three commands, "rally", "Attack", "Defend").
Sniping in this game is horrid, if you're not sniping, you're being sniped, as there are no downsides to sniping in this game. Longshots get more xp, no punishments for spawn camping, no punishments for going completely outside the actual battlefield to snipe from so far away, someone would have to spend 10 minutes finding them, kill them, then get back into the actual action.
