Any advancment to nearly any objective is impossible.
Few Extra Gripes:
Lack of variety with filler in worlds.
Lack of any tactics required to play this game.
Not enough Stamina with small loadouts.
Animations are nothing to be desired.
Trailers on storefront are nothing like the game they are made for.

Now that we got that out of the way, what makes this game awesome, is that it is probably the best feudal era simulation there is right now. The combat, once you get over the steep mountain that is the learning curve, is fantastic. Competing in a tournament is a blast as you joust, fight in a huge melee, throw javelins at each other, etc. Siege battles are insane and really force you to learn the system as you can't just charge in and win. You will die if you think this is Skyrim. Land battles can be gigantic and epic with 100s of soldiers crashing into each other in a huge wave up close and personal.
The simulation parts, such as running a kingdom, or participating in one, are just as great. They're a bit odd at first, but once you learn how the system works, it's all downhill from there. Becoming a lord in an army, or playing the mercenary, or becoming a ruler of your own kingdom is exhilerating and challenging. Conquering the land is incredibly hard to do as the current powers that be don't like weak upstarts and will crush you if you're not equally politically savvy and bloodthirsty. You'll want to do this, too, once you realize how useless having a King/Queen really is when YOU could be calling the shots. The first time I lead a kingdom into battle, it didn't stop for years as I cut huge portions of land for myself.
Is this my favorite game of all time? No. Why? Because I think that M&B 2 whenever it comes out will be.

Unfortunantly, in a world where pressing the wrong button a fraction of a second too late ends in instant death, he only knows how to jump when his right foot is forward. Hitting space when his left foot is forward requires him to take a second step, usually off of an edge and into some painful looking death.
It feels like the game must complete his current animation before starting another one. In a game where you are required to complete complex freerunning sections, this is gamebreaking for me. I was glad to see this game see the 'light' of day on STEAM. They're a couple of things that Deadlight does 'Dead' on, and they aren't word puns.
The side scrolling platform gameplay is refreshing, especially for a zombie apocalypse game in an over-saturated zombie game world. It does have moments where you will accidentally do something you might not have meant to, since some controls are keyed for multiple actions. In the worst of these situations, it could result in Randy's death (That's the guy you see in all the screenshots by the way. He's not very personable but somewhere deep down; he's a soft teddy bear who likes a cuddle now and then). Fortunately checkpoints are given out like candy and these deaths are minor setbacks.
The other thing Tequila Works did right, besides having a snazzy studio name that incorporates alcohol with game development, is having genuine moments of tension in their game. Certain moments are an all-out rush to get from point A to point B without getting eaten alive in the process. And the not so subtle ability to full sprint tackle a zombie to the ground in an attempt to get past them when you are unarmed is nice in a zombie setting.
I can't say I believe the voice actors should receive any awards for outstanding performances in a video game. In fact, if I had to choose a solitary fault with Deadlight, voice acting would be it. Just having little word bubbles would have been better, perhaps destructive to the art direction but better than having to listen to the dialogue where you could clearly tell the actors just wanted to get it done and see their paychecks.
Though $15 may be a bit steep, I would say you could justify $10 or less. If you've been living on STEAM you've come to realize that Valve does Steam Sales about as much as EA publishes an unfinished game so just be patient if you truly must. Though Deadlight is worth a look and a play through or two won't leave you feeling 'Dead' and empty inside...

Zombies might be all the rage these days, but Deadlight quickly became one of my favourite platformers in recent times. The game handles its story well and the artwork is post-apocalyptically beautiful. There are some very nice puzzle elements, with classic hidden parts throughout the levels for those into exploration.
For the mosty part, the puzzles and mechanics work well, there are, however, a couple of scenes that are frustrating not due to difficulty, but to control issues (it is always possible these may have been fixed in a bug release by the time you read this).

Deadlight is a flawed game that has some frustrations you'll have to overcome to win. Some sections, particularly in the later part of the game, are frustrating trial-and-error affairs. The story is also rather plain and predictable. But it's not a bad game, it has some pretty fluid mechanics and some rather smart level design often, with a few cool collectibles in little minigames you can collect and diary pages that are interesting enough. The environments look pretty, the music is nice... It feels like it holds itself back, though its hard to explain. But I don't regret playing it, I did in fact enjoy it. Catch it on a sale, and if the idea of a 2D Zombie game is interesting to you, I'll recommend it. But it has its rough patches of frustrations, some glitches, and sometimes feeling not very inspired.

This game is not just awesome - it is one of the greatest gaming experiences I've ever had the opportunity to enjoy. I mean it! The last time I enjoyed myself so much and was so very immersed in a world was when I played "The Guild".
Some reasons why "Mount & Blade: Warband" is THE game for you, my friend!
a) Roleplay elements not just for your main character with level-ups and many different skills, as well as equipment such as boots, chest armor, weapons, helmets - but also for each of the heroes (you did not misunderstand me, my friend, indeed each of your followers can be equiped and customized with their very own gear!) you recruit from the taverns, furthermore including many different and differing quests to earn renown, honor and, of course, some money? Check!
b) Real-time strategy in oppulent fights - either first person or third person, as you like it, Sir or Madam - in which you can order your troops around, swing your sword, chop with your axe, use your lance, throw some daggers, use your bow from the horseback or simply snipe with a crossbow? Check!
c) Turn-based travels over a grand, interactive map with vivid (although, in terms of graphics, slightly outdated) details, wandering troops you can intercept, aid, join, etc.? Check!
d) A great number of vastly different units, differing from nation to nation, which you can upgrade about three to four times each? Check!
e) A rich number of armors, weapons, goods and even horses - each with their own stats and value? Check!
f) Trading, politics, becoming the chief of villages, castles and even cities, meanwhile owning a brewery in each town to make some coin? Check!
If you were looking for a game that supplies you with everything you could ever want from a sandbox game (and manages to do all of that in a most satisfying way!), vastly outclassing the possibilities of an Elder Scrolls (although I love this series), you are in for the grandest treat you have ever experienced, I promise you that!
Give it a try, and if you like RPGs like the Elder Scrolls, games like The Guild or Anno, and strategy titles such as Total War, you won't stop playing this remarkable piece of creativity! :-)))

How do I describe the awesomeness that is Mount and Blade: Warband? Let me start with how you start the game. Mount and Blade begins with you not just creating his/her appearance and stats, but also a backstory. Now, you can choose to follow it or not, but this simple little menu screen is the first little string in a large rope that pulled me into the world of Calradia. You'll find yourself cursing your enemies like a knight of the middle ages, and gaining a twisted smile while you watch enemies fall before your blade. You can choose to pledge your sword to a king, live as a travelling Adventurer, or even invade a castle and begin your own Kingdom. However, none of these are simple tasks to accomplish. The personality of each of the Royal NPCs in the game varies, and their opinion of you, your kingdom, and even those companions you hold in your company will change and effect how they feel about you. A complex political system contours and twists your path through Mount and Blade, so no two characters will ever experience exactly the same path to glory and power. With nearly endless replayability, Mount and Blade Warband is a steal during a sale, and, while I'd say it's so good it's worth buying for the full $20 it currently costs, I'd say wait for a sale. Mount and Blade unfortunately has a few bugs and glitches, as most open world sandbox-style games do. I have experienced many Graphical Glitches throughout my playthroughs, but none that couldn't be fixed through a quick alt+tab. Mount and Blade is also not a shiny game, the Graphics were a bit behind for it's time, but I ensure you if you can dig beneath skin-deep beauty, you'll find a shining diamond within Mount and Blade.
TL;DR/Final Rating
Pros; Fantastic game, great atmosphere, lots of replayability.
Cons; Graphical Glitches, Poor Graphics, a few bugs.
Rating: 8.7/10. A fantastic game and series, with a ton of potential. I hope to see a new installment soon, and I'll see you all on the fields of Calradia!

You are Randall, a badass survivor looking for his family: a man who seemingly knows pain and loss in a 1980's zombie apocalypse. Deadlight holds itself as a puzzle platformer, with Assassin’s Creed jumps and traps galore. Think Prince of Persia meets The Walking Dead, and throw in a few traps for fun. Although the game is pretty short, taking me around 5 hours to beat; it makes up for it in ingenuity and atmosphere.
The story is touching, Randall – you – is searching for his wife and daughter amidst the chaos of the end times. The real enemy beyond the zombies is a group of renegades who call themselves “The New Law”. They are a sadistic group who take delight in torturing and killing innocent survivors. Separated from his survivor group at the beginning, Randall’s journey will introduce him to The New Law but he will still meet a few new friends on the way.
1980’s Seattle is really a beautiful setting (besides the dead people and destruction). The HUD is very non-intrusive with only a small health and stamina bar, leaving plenty of screen space for the visual delights. The background looks amazing: varying between dark gritty cityscapes, dark gritty warehouses, or even a dark gritty sewer. Okay, there’s not a lot of variety in setting, but it’s so pretty you won’t even care. The environment can be shiny and heavy with rain, or even have a crumbling building in the background, all-in-all the effects employed are beautiful.
The lighting can come from lonely street lamps or neon lights: giving the zombies a Christmassy glow. This isn’t the zombie game where you’re a one man killing machine; these zombies will tear you apart if you get more than two at once, so you really want to run away. The sounds of these shambling “Shadows” (as the game calls them) is quite unnerving. You never know if a dead body you pass may climb up and greet you. The music isn’t too intrusive, but makes use of classic horror “creepy ambiance” sounds: a DUN DUN at a surprise, a constant hum to build suspense in an area, or just some soft music to add a somber mood. Speaking of ambiance, the almost constant downpour in Rain City adds a serious tone to the usual jubilance of constantly fighting for survival against hordes of the undead. Our protagonist’s gravelly, serious voice guides us through this desolate world and feels comforting, always calm in the face of tragedy.
The gameplay and controls typically feels pretty solid, the controls being standard for keyboard controls, with the option for a USB Xbox controller. The aiming is tight and straightforward, and the platforming is what you’re used to with Assassin’s Creed or Prince of Persia. A large problem is when trying to jump vertically, sometimes Randall won’t grab the ledge unless in the exact right spot or he’ll just jump forward into a puddle of electricity or horde of zombies.
When backed into a corner, Randall can fend off the horde with a fire axe or a few different guns discovered throughout the story. The first gun you get is a revolver, and it takes Randall into a flashback to his first time with a gun and learning to shoot, giving a tutorial without it feeling like a classroom lecture, quite refreshing. Later on, you unlock a shotgun and an assault rifle, both useful for clearing a pesky zombie horde when running isn’t an option.
Overall, Deadlight is a great story driven game -- If relatively short -- and offers an interesting perspective on the zombie apocalypse, running away taking priority to fighting, and with the climbing and jumping elements. Where Deadlight really shines is the environment. The broken city and serious tones give the setting the perfect mood to combine with danger and a feeling of loss. A game as colorful as it is lighthearted, I definitely recommend spending $15 -- or less if you wait for a Steam sale -- to experience this game, whether for the compelling story or the amazing atmosphere.

What did we have so far? Braid,Limbo, Trine, Bionic Commando, and perhaps a few others I failed to mention.
The game takes place in 1986 during the world zombie outbreak.
This game has it all, zombies, an intensive narrative, more or less realistic combat, shortage of ammo, expansive and realistic environments, human conflict, back story, gore, puzzles. Once you beat the game you get the Nightmare mode unlocked, wherein you have to beat each of the three long acts (each with 4-5 scenes) without dying. Once you do so you unlock the alternate ending. This achievement is so hard that I haven't seen anyone on the net post the alternate ending yet.
One level I would take out is the one in the sewers, it was quite a torture I might say. Everything else looks great: detailed ambiance levels, the physics, the animation, the chase scenes, the cliffhangers, being outnumbered, using environment to kill foes, outstanding soundtrack. There are plenty of Easter eggs: such as three handheld video games, miscellaneous items, pieces that help complete the story as well as ID of famous serial killers and such. The game itself is also pretty long, around 5-6 hours..
Anyways, short review.

Soundtrack is non existent, unless you get in a car and can't turn off the goddamn radio, but I don't mind it much.
Story: great! until the end...
**spoilers**
So after rescuing your 6 friends from the pirates who have been trying to kill you, they are all kidnapped by the people who you've been helping the whole time. Intense! Then when you go to free them, you're given the option to save them and leave the island...or kill them. I think ubisoft had a good idea here, they were trying to make it "difficult to decide" kind of like how telltale games does (and they're very good at) but this was poorly executed. The protagonist's mind starts to become like the island, very primal and rather evil, willing to kill anyone who stands in his way, and then is given the ultimatum! But...the player doesn't get very immersed in this because we're friends with obligations, friendships, and morals. I chose the good ending, and the evil ending and both of them are very dissatisfying. One has you save your friends and then you leave to go back to your life, with a 2-sentence momologue from the protagonist, and the other has you killed by the chief of the tribe after impregnating her (yes there's a sex scene.)
The end!
**End of spoilers.**

Deadlight is a thing of beauty, to the naked eye at least.
Presentation: 9.5/10 - The games great mixture of colours is visually stunning. All the pitch black cadavers lining the empty, cold, and harsh streets while the sun shines down brightly and creates glare on your screen is simply a sight that should be seen. How they mix the pitch black bodies with the bright surroundings around them is simply put; amazing. I must also mention the soundtrack. The music fits the mood rather well, and helps immerse you in the world.
Gameplay: 6.0/10 - Although the idea was original, especially for a zombie game, Deadlight fails in many areas. It's basically a simple, linear, clunky, and slippery platformer. All the surfaces you jump on feel slipper and the controls are clunky and sometimes have a bit of a delay. The game is also very linear, in the sense that there are no real, "secret," areas and you just end up following the cookie trail that the game gives you. You also get some weapons in the game like a revolver or axe, but they aren't anything unique. For the long ranged weapons it's a simple point and shoot, which is basically the same for the axe or any other physical weapon. Simple, but not too clean.
Plot: 6.5/10 - Other than some great story telling, the plot ends up being a little too cliched for me. As I said, they tell the story in a great way, but the actual story isn't that great. They also did a good job at making you feel for the protagonist, Randall Wayne, but once again the main premise feels old.
Overall: 7.0/10 - Good.

Deadlight is an undeniably nice looking short game, the 2.5D perspective really allows it to shine (or should I say darken) in the right areas in terms of visuals and the lighting effects are pretty enough to keep a consistent downpour like tone to the whole of the game and if you think that a game can solely be carried on its visual aspects then buy away my friend! On that note the tone is consistent  in being a survival game that you rarely feel like you can go in guns blazing at the zombies and fleeing from them feels like actually surviving rather than avoiding an encounter – bullets are scarce, and zombies often like to gang up on you and use your tasty human buttocks for their next meal. It is also nice in the fact that the game tries to make you survive in other aspects such as traversing the landscape as well.
Yet my problem with Deadlight is that it suffers in most other areas of the game, it’s like the developers wanted to create a moody cinematic (with all the comic-style cut scenes) got the tone and the colour pallet out and forgot how everything else works in a video game. The game suffers from an incurable case of “End Level Abomination” syndrome in which the last few levels we’re more frustrating than fun and the subtlety and the plot are comparable to a drunken stage actor in his last ever performance with him to give what is supposed to be details to a small sub plot to the audience but instead vomits it all over the stage and narrative whenever he’s supposed to be on cue. That combined with voice acting that sounded like it was supposed to be ironic than actually engaging. Platforming can be awkward at times with the main character’s movement  feeling like you’re moving a partially brick man with small springs attached, sometimes fighting zombies is unbelievably frustrating but I guess that may have been the point?
The game doesn’t add any new mechanics to the survival genre other than showing that a zombie apocalypse game can be carried by aspects other than zombies namely the environment that it’s in but all in all Deadlight feels like it was “my first zombie apocalypse” in that it’s got a good tone down but the application at times feels shoddy or unbalanced. If Deadlight were to enter a break dancing battle with all the other survival horror games out there, it’d come in the flashiest tracksuit but as soon as it goes to break it down ends up fumbling together some mediocre moves that he learnt off the TV. Not saying that Deadlight is exactly a bad game it’s not buggy or anything from what I played but it just felt like it didn’t have enough experience behind it.
Verdicts:
+ Stunning visuals
+ Good survival concept and aspects
+ Isn’t buggy or glitchy
- Voice Acting needs work
- Platforming and Action sections can be frustrating
- Last few levels we're annoying

One of the most pretentious and joyless games I've played in a long while. So predictable, cliche, corny and full of uninspired design decissions that it's just painfull.
It all felt like some kind of attempt at mixing every bland and overused gaming feature from the last several years with evenly bland, overdramaticised and predictable plot. As if the zombie apocalypse setting wasn't sickening enough on its own, the graphics are like every single pseudo-artistic indie physics platformer since Limbo, the cut-scenes try way too hard to copy Ashley Wood's motion comics, the story is a poor man's The Walking Dead mixed with Resident Evil, and our bland protagonist is forced to have some obvious hurrdurr grimdark past he has to atone for (because "teh drama").
And keeping with gaming tradition of having an obligatory sewer level Deadlight has a full sewer CHAPTER, together with cheap deaths, frustrating controls and mandatory physics puzzles...
Took 4 hours to beat, yet felt like forever. Avoid.

Deadlight is a pseudo-3D puzzler / action / platformer that takes place in a somewhat cliché setting. The world has been ripped apart by a zombie-apocalypse and you are one of very few survivors, trying to track down your wife and daughter. As plots go, it’s not something that hasn’t been done before and it has been done better. Part of the story you can even take or leave, as you will find pages of your own diary that, against all logic and reason, are scattered throughout the levels. There is an obligatory twist ending that is clumsily handled, more groan-inducing than profound or surprising. There is a voice-over narration by the character you play and the writing is corny and on-the-nose, though the voice is appropriately gruff. I have to assume the character was doing voice-over work for action-movie trailers before the end of the world came along. In between the bits where you are in control, there are cut-scenes in gritty graphic novel style that show events that would be hard to capture using the faux 3D playing field. The style in which these are drawn, comes suspiciously close to the style used for the The Walking Dead comics and game.
In case the semi-3D needs clarification; it means you are running through an environment that looks 3D, but you can only follow a straight line through it, running along the screen from one side to the other. As you enter buildings, the sides disappear to show you what’s inside. Being caught in 2D plane doesn’t really help your immersion as you are sometimes looking at the background thinking ‘Well, can’t he just go through there?’ or ‘That object I can’t get to in the back would really come in handy right now’. You just have to accept you can only work within the narrowly predetermined options offered by the game. Most of the time, there is only one way to proceed.
Deadlight makes up for most of its shortcomings by looking and sounding very good, creating a dark, interesting atmosphere. The slower parts of the soundtrack are beautifully sad and during the action bits, the music turns frenetic and helps to speed up your pulse. However, the mood can’t quite compensate for trial-and-error gameplay, clumsy save-points and controls that aren’t quite as tight as the game wants them to be. A few times, the game will spring something deadly on you so fast that there is no way to not get killed the first time you pass through. During sections where speed is of the essence, you will find yourself repeatedly dying because your alter-ego won’t drop himself from a wall at the exact moment you tell him to. He is also a bit particular when standing under a ladder; he may jump straight up and grab it as intended or take a big jump sideways if slightly misplaced. And then when you die (unfairly) you may find yourself in the room/section before the one you died in, meaning you have to replay a bit you got right the first time. It may be an attempt to stretch the playtime (which is still not that long) but it spoils the mix of challenge and enjoyment a bit, adding too much frustration to the recipe.
After you finish the story, Nightmare Mode is unlocked, which apparently does away with the save-points altogether and would have you do a full playthrough without dying. For the life of me I can’t imagine why anyone would subject themselves to that, especially given the sticky controls, but I am sure someone has already posted the video of them succeeding.  All in all, Deadlight makes for an interesting palate cleanser in between larger, more complex games and I would recommend it if you find it for a bargain price. Just be prepared to find yourself cursing at your monitor from time to time.

When "Deadlight" was first announced, I thought that the concept looked interesting: the art style, the "parkour" Tequila Works promoted, the story... and then it came out on the Xbox 360 and received fairly mediocre reviews. The PC port however appeared to solve all the problems the console version boasted, from the bugs to the clunky controls. I can assure you, after having played both the Xbox and the PC versions, that the PC port is better. However, the port available to buy on Steam still suffers from a lot of problems, problems that detracted from the game and caused me to quit the game in anger several times. "Deadlight" is one of those games that looked fantastic on paper but failed to deliver what most expect from not just a zombie game, but an action/adventure game too.
Gameplay - 2/5 stars - The bugs, the performance, the controls, the cutscenes... they angered me to the point where completing the game seemed like a chore. The parkour is fun, I'll give the game that, but the combat is way too easy due to plentiful ammo. The controls were also extremely clunky. I suggest that you change the key bindings the second you boot up the game, for some keys are in the most awkward of places.
Story - 3/5 stars - The voice acting (in some cases) is really well done and the story arc, though cliche, is made interesting due to the collectibles scattered throughout the game. I find the lead-up to the infection in zombie games to be the most interesting part, and the fact that "Deadlight" is set in the mid-1980s helps create a unique backstory to the zombie outbreak.
Sound - 2/5 stars - Not much to say here. The music was atmospheric though it starts to loop and it can get annoying when you have to retry a section over and over due to the previously mentioned controls. Just generally mediocre I'd say.
Graphics - 4/5 stars - The game's art direction is cool and refreshing. I'd love to see more games harness this kind of art direction, just like how I wish more games harnessed cell-shading. Despite the visual style, the graphics are great (when they aren't being crippled by glitches and frame-rate drops).
Price - 4/5 stars - For $14.99, you get around 4 hours of gameplay, excluding hunting for collectibles. Not too shabby, and the deal get's even sweeter if you can pick this game up during a sale. There is some replay value too.
Overall - 3/5 - Honestly, "Deadlight" can be worth the $15 if you're accustomed to technical issues. At the end of the day, I recommended this game to some friends and I'd recommend it to you too. It may sound like I loathe the game, but I think the game was actually okay. It's just that though: "okay." Perhaps "Deadlight 2" will solve all the problems presented in "Deadlight," if Tequila Works develops a sequal that is.

1. I hate that each update dumbs the game down to nothing more than a 'Red Vs. Blue' shoot 'em up that even the most mindless of FPS player would find too simple.
2. I hate that the devs cater to people who complain en mass over something they don't like (getting sniped) and implement something totally stupid to counter it (tracer rounds that can be seen clearly even in the day time)
3. I hate that good suggestions (medics, better flight models, proper tank physics, realistic damage to tank tracks, plane cockpit view, different uniforms as you go up in rank, deployable bipods, tank cupola view and so on) have been seemingly neglected.
4. I hate that rather than fix something or make it the best they can (e.g. Tanks) the devs just introduce more of said broken item.
5. I hate that after 3 years+ of development we still have one campaign, guns sound like they are firing paintballs, tanks flip when running into bicycles and come to a complete stop when hitting a simple wooden fence and much more.
6. I hate that maps are so big and empty with no ambiance, no destruction and nothing that makes me remotely think I'm in a war.
7. I hate the new weight system and how totally absurd it is (a grease gun weighing as much as a Thompson, a scoped Kar 98 weighing less than a regular Kar 98)
8. I hate that it took them so long to bring back paratroopers, and have essentially made them useless by giving them only 6 equipment slots, barely enough to equip anything. Even though paratroopers in WW2 were fitter and carried almost triple the equipment of a regular soldier.
9. I hate that the FG42 is listed as an LMG and has the same weight as an MG42 when it is comparable in size and weight to a modern assault rifle.
10. I hate that veteran has been essentially shoved down our throats by removing a weapon and badge slot, even though they have other ways of gaining income (especially a $99 pack on steam unlocking everything).
11. I hate that the devs seem to have no clear direction and won't admit it, even though we can all see it.
12. I hate that Team killers and griefers are not getting banned. People are getting random banned.
13. I hate that when I fielded my assault team and they got routed, I got database connection error.
Basically I have to stay away from the general tab to play the fps game. What a joke.
14. Most of all, I hate that the devs don't see that they are essentially running their own game into the ground by not respecting the community, or heeding their feedback. Long time players are leaving in droves because of it and how each update brings the game further away from what they hoped it would be. Short time players (who they are now catering too) will eventually leave after they've wallet warriored their way to boredom and see that the game is essentially in a stalemate.

Contagion is a great game and considering it is just at beta stage the developers have done an amazing job on this. It has a good range of weapons to choose from, the're not over powered, great map size's and designs. They really brought back the REAL survival zombie game with Contagion it took the modern shoot em up, mini gun packing, grenade throwing, action hero and took away all his fire power. It threw him in a dark, dank room filled with fires, smoke, locked doors and of course, zombies. It has all the elements of a true masterpiece and i dare say could be the zombie survival equal to the all time great series the Elder Scrolls. Though they are two different genre's the Elder Scrolls was and still is THE number one RPG/Free roam game for the last 14 years and I firmly believe Contagion is the start of a new multiple year stacking horror game and I will gladly explain why I say this.
What is a horror game? It is a simulation of a scary event in which we are cast as the main person of interest. Contagion does this extremely well, if you play the single player mode you are utterly alone and have only a low powered pistol with only about 3-4 mags. This creates a sense of helplessness and isolation.
What is a survival game? It is a simulation of a survival event which you must use your knowledge to survive. Contagion does this well, you have to use your judgement on what to use and when to use it as you are limited as to what you can carry. Once again this creates a sense of helplessness and lack of self confidence as you doubt your own ability to survive carrying only one or two guns which in turn breeds anxiety.
In short these two elements alone and how Contagion molded them to its self makes you feel truly alone. You worry about exploring further and quickly panic when surrounded or cant decide on what to take with you and what to leave behind. These are not all the elements it poses but the roots which all zombie and horror survival games in general thrive on. Take these away and you dont have a survival horror game, you have another Left 4 Dead where you have half a million guns with even more ammo taking on mutated and one foot shot kill zombies who you massacre in seconds, just taking on 3 - 4 is tricky enough in Contagion and even more so in a small space.
I would truly recommend this game as it will get many awards and forge a legendary status for its self. But, I will not say it is 100% perfect as all things can be improved in some way. Excluding glitches and bugs (I exclude these because it isn't working game play based, which is the area I am targeting) the ammo is abundant and decreases the self doubt and overall fear factor. It reminded me of dead space 1, dead space had an amazing fear factor at the start but as I got to much ammo and guns to carry it turned from a horror survival into an action sci-fi which actually made it boring because I wasn't scared anymore. This did happen at the end of a match I was playing, I had maxed out ammo on three guns and to be honest I wasn't scared or even worried anymore. In face i was actually wasting ammo to try make it more worrying but of course I found another few box's just around the next corner. This is a massive factor as its the guns that take away the fear, remove the fear killer, you force the player to feel more fear. All they need to do is make ammo more scarce and force you become paranoid about even using a gun in case you run out, especially if the player is the spray and pray type. It takes either one well placed, time consuming head shot to kill a zombie, or ten plus body shots, you can only carry about one hundred sixty five 9mm rounds. So that's sixteen dead zombies and seventeen if you include using five rounds then beating it to death. Regardless its only about 5% - 10% of a maps total zombie count, not good enough to keep you alive without lots of bullets. So in short, less bullets equals only head shot killers have bullets throughout the map and still have a hard time keeping any rounds spare, increasing the level of fear felt in the game.
Other than this it just needs more maps and mode applicable to those maps but that's it, its an epic game in almost all areas and a 9/10 for me. Would be a 10/10 if it had more maps and less ammo.

This Review is written in Japanese and English. Sorry about my poor English.
まず何より先に言っておきたいのですが、このゲームはアメリカ軍がドイツ軍より有利な条件になっています。ですが最終的にはドイツ軍側の武器も充実してきます。ドイツ側プレイヤーに求められるのは忍耐です。たとえ経験豊富なFPSプレイヤーであっても、兵士が育ちきるまでは、ドイツ側はアメリカ兵に倒されまくる事を覚悟しましょう。
All what I'd like to say is " US weapons of fresh soldiers are stronger than German ones in this game". Of course, German weapon can be strong in the end. GERMAN PLAYERS MUST BE PATIENT. Until your trooper trained enough, you will be killed so many times even if you are experienced in First-person shooter. Don't worry about the "Kill-Death Ratio". In this game, tankers usually make 30kill-0death score or more. Anyway, if you want to play on Axis side, please remember these disadvantages as follows.
第一に、歩兵装備の優位性です。ドイツ軍のG43ライフルは威力や反動の面でアメリカ軍のM1ガーランドに劣っています。また、ドイツ兵が最初に購入できるようになるMP34サブマシンガンは装弾数が20発しかないため、アメリカ兵のM3グリースガンやM1トンプソンと撃ち合う際に苦しい思いをすること請け合いです。サブマシンガンで戦果を挙げてリボンをLv UPさせればMP40を購入できるようになりますが、かなり高価(MG34や38t戦車よりも値段が高い)ですし、M1トンプソンの火力や連射性能にはどうしても負けてしまいます。
First, US infantry equipments are superior than German's ones. The damage and recoil of G43 rifle(German beginning rifle) are inferior than M1 Garand(American). If you want to keep using this rifle for long time, you should improve these status by installing weapon mods. After that, this rifle will be able to defeat Uncle Sam with only twice body-hits in close to middle range. MP34 Submachine gun has only 20 rounds while M3 Greese gun has 30 rounds. This gap suffer German players. Of course, you can purchase MP40 Submachine gun when you earn enough EXPs of SMG ribbon.However, its Fire Power and Rate of Fire is still worse than M1 Thompson. In addition, the biggest problem is ...... MP40 is so expensive. Its price is higher than MG34 and even light tanks !!
第二に、戦車の性能の差です。「ドイツ戦車といえばWW2最強だろ！」と考える人は少なくないと思われますが、少なくともこのゲームではドイツ戦車乗りは茨の道を歩かされることは間違いないと言えるでしょう。というのもこのゲーム、ドイツ戦車兵はまず1号戦車からスタートするのですが、敵として遭遇(マッチング)する相手は、皆この戦車よりも強力です。M24チャーフィどころか、M5スチュアート相手にも勝機はほぼありません。具体的に言うと、高価なAPCR弾を奴らの背面に打ち込んでも、まったく砲弾が貫通してくれずにノーダメージとなります。M2A2軽戦車が相手ならまだ勝ち目はありますが、向こうは12.7mm機関銃を装備しているのに対し、こちらは7.92mm機関銃しかないので相変わらず苦しいです。歩兵やジープを撃ってはクレジットやリボン経験値を稼ぎ、38t戦車を手に入れるまでは、ひたすら苦労することでしょう。ティーガーやティーガー2は確かに強力なのですが、そもそも投入できる戦場が絶対的に少ないです。なおドイツ重戦車の仮想敵はM26パーシングです。
Secondly, the difference of the quality of Tanks is serious. Excepting Russian, most people may believe "German tanks are best in WW 2 !!". Although it might be true, in this game, German tank soldiers must walk thorny path. Pz.I light tank(German beginning tank) is the worst tank, and it will be just a coffin in Tank battle.This tank bring only a pair of 7.92mm machine gun while American M2A2 LT has 12.7mm machine gun. For example, however when you shoot APCR(better penetration and more expensive ammo) against the back armor of M5 Stuart or M24 chaffee, it can NEVER penetrate(shoot out) their armor, even THEY ARE LIGHT TANKS!! In case, against M4 sherman or M26 persing? Needless to answer...... So, if you want to train German tanker, I recommand you to avoid tank battle with Pz.I. Attack only enemy infantry and non-armored vehicles, and gain EXPs of Light tank ribbon to buy 38t tank. It is the best light tank in German, and it can kill American light tank from its front. German Heavy tanks are actually good, but there are only a few opportunity to cast them in standard battle.
とまあ、こんな感じにドイツ側はかなりマゾい戦いを強いられますが、兵士が育って武器や車両が揃ってくれば、段々と楽しくなってきます。最初のうちは、1ゲームがすぐ終わるSkirmishルールの戦場でクレジットを稼ぐのが良いでしょう。
Like this, german player will fight under disadvantages. But, after getting well-trained soldier and purchase enough weapons, you will feel this game fun. While you are new player, you should join only "Skirmish" battle, and earn EXPs and Credits. Skirmish mode battle takes less time thans "Assault" mode battle.
また、これは米独両軍の新兵に気をつけて欲しいのですが、雇用したての歩兵は対戦車兵器を全く持っていませんし、買えません。もちろん、初期装備の手榴弾は対人用途にしか使えず、装甲車両には全くダメージが入らないため、先述の1号戦車にさえも遠距離から一方的に虐殺されかねないです。更にこのゲームの対戦車兵器は威力が弱く、紙装甲で有名なM18ヘルキャット相手ですら、パンツァーファウストを3発は直撃させないと撃破できません。対戦車手榴弾もあるのですが、これは戦車破壊リボンのレベルがかなり上がっていないと購入できず、敵戦車に肉薄するリスクを要するにも関わらず、戦車を一撃で撃破できるRed Orchestraシリーズの対戦車手榴弾とは違い、このゲームの対戦車手榴弾は、軽戦車を撃破するのにすら2～3個の使用を必要とされます。やはり敵戦車を撃破するには、こちらも戦車を出して対抗するのが1番安全なように思えます。
Finally, I need to tell an important thing to both US and German new players. The fresh soldier has no Anti-tank weapons, and they cannot buy them yet. Your Anti-human grenades cause quite NO damage against armor targets. It means, you can easily be slaughtered by even Pz.I light tank!! And, compared with "Red Orchestra" series, the damage of Anti-tank weapons is weaker and weaker. For exapmle. you will need 3 direct hit of Panzerfaust to kill M18 hellcat(even this tank-destroyer has only 13~25mm of armor). If you use Anti-tank grenade(this is so risky), it also needs twice or more. Using Panzerschreck or M1A1 Bazooka is more damage than Panzeraust, and much safer than Anti-tank grenade. But their prices are so expensive. After consuming all 50 rounds, you need to supply them at the same prices of buying new ones. As the result, when you get suffered by enemy tanks and you want to eliminate them, you should cast a tank, like enemy does.

Deadlight held a lot of promise for me. I love platformers and a decent amount of infection-driven post-apocalyptic fiction, and visually, it looked great. I was hoping it would give me a nice solid gameplay experience with an interesting story, but unfortunately, that's not what it held.
While Deadlight is visually appealing, and has a pretty good soundtrack, I was pretty disappointed in it overall. This disappointment ultimately comes down to two simple but pretty massive faults: the controls were unreliable, even with an Xinput controller, leading to the player character behaving unpredictably and getting killed; and the story was lackluster, derivative, predictable, and uninspiring.
While quite a bit of the game can be enjoyable thanks to its atmosphere, I found much of the game frustrating. I should preface this by saying that I am a very big fan of punishingly difficult games, including platformers, so long as they are well-designed and far. The trouble I found, however, is that this game did not feel intentionally difficult, but rather became frustratingly difficult through design oversights and poor controls. It felt like almost every time I died, it was something beyond my control or something without any warning. As an example, there are some pretty infuriating sequences in this game where you have to run away from things that kill you instantly, and they put up obstacles that your character climbs over really slowly no matter what you do. This doesn't appear to be used to build the tension in any way, and appears to be completely unintentional, but it results in the player dying even when they've been doing very well in maintaining their stride up until that point. It makes it feel like the game is killing you because it's not well designed, not because you made a mistake, which really kills the experience.
If the story was worth it, then I'd be a bit more forgiving of control issues. Unfortunately, the story isn't anything memorable, and the big twists are very predictable right from the beginning. There's not much character development, which is probably a byproduct of having a short game that tries to do too much. It's an okay story, but it feels more akin to reading mass market fiction, giving a fleeting sense of enjoyment that you won't really care too much about upon reaching its conclusion.

Far Cry 3 at first seems like a simple game in which you play as acharacter who learns to fight while rescuing his friends from pirate on a large open world island. But then you start to get into the story a little bit more, and you start to notice something at one point. Something in the character, Jason (who you play as), that doesn't seem right, but matches what your actions have been to this point. Far Cry 3 not only draws you into Jason and puts you in his head, but does so in such a subtle way, that nearing the end of the story, you are able to feel the emotion Jason does through quicktime events that are nothing but a simple button press for the player, but for Jason... It could be something as harsh as killing an innocent man... or much worse.

Inevitably this game will be compared up against Left 4 Dead 2. This is understandable but not entirely fair to the game although there are certainly many similarities. In a market already oversaturated with zombie-games left, right and center what is there to recommend? What is there to make this stand out? Honestly I can't answer that since I haven't played most of the other games out there. What I can tell you though is why I like it.
First of all it has atmosphere in spades. The graphics do a lot to help with this and by that I don't necessarily mean visual fidelity but the overall style. Where L4D is a little lighter on the horror and as a result tend to be a brighter game this is darker and more - dare I call it - "realistic". When I say dark I mean litteral darkness and your flashlight is designed in such a way that it isn't a magic lamp that illuminates everything and make things instantly better. You'll have to see it to know what I mean but I can tell you that facing off against a gang of zombies in a dark room can get very tense despite your flashlight.
The pace is also very different. It's slower and less arcade than other similar FPS zombie games. Zombies move slower and though they can "run" (more like walking fast) there are no sprinters. It builds more on the premise that even a few zombies become a serious threat if you let them come up close. Headshots are the name of the game and ammo/weapons are meant to be scarce. Melee is an option but don't expect to wade through even a few zombies with your sledgehammer. Zombies take multiple hits to go down, swings are slower than you might think... oh and they use precious stamina that you also need to sprint.
I could go on but I hope the above has already given you a sense of whether this is something for you or not. You can read about the different game modes elsewhere but in brief there's one PvP mode (hunting others on maps filled with zombies) and two co-op modes. And when I say co-op I do mean co-op: don't expect to get far or have an easy time without some serious teamwork!
Bottom-line: don't let comparisons to other games (such as L4D1-2) influence your decision. Both this game and L4D2 are among my favorite zombie co-op shooters and I love each for their way of doing things.

Contagion isn't a game that "has potential". It already GOT Alot of Potential. It is not just  another mindless action zombie game like most FPS games with zombies have or DayZ wannabe. One of the things is that this game does not try to be another DayZ or another FPS game with zombies mode. It is also not as sosphisticated and complex that games that try to copy those games.
It has 3 simple objectives. Gather ammo and weapons. Fortify, and survive. They can expand on weapons and game modes, but because the game does not have a huge open world (Just good big maps), it isn't so hard to get confused.

While there are dozens of zombie fps games out there these days. Few actually have a "creep" factor to them like Contagion does. I honestly felt like there was going to be a horde just wobbling around  every corner ready to set their dead eyes on me as a tastey lunch! Some of them move slowely, some of them move quickly like the "freshly dead" even if they look far from fresh. The creepiness is the biggest factor for me hands down. Not to mention the fact you HAVE TO SHOOT THEM IN THE HEAD to put them down perminately! Shooting off their other extremeities will slow them down but why not go for the one secure shot?! To put it all together this is most definetly one of the best zombie fps games i have ever had the pleasure to play. It may still be in early access but to me it doesn't even feel like it. I even rented my own game server for this game! Play it, you will love it!

Deadlight tries to be an Eversion-like, pixel precise, edge-jumping platformer, but has the movement mechanics of Out of this World or Flashback, with none of the polish.
An astronomical number of cheap deaths and hours of frustrating trial and error gameplay will have you screaming at your monitor. "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥T!" you'll say, as the door you just barreled through throws you into a horde of zombies, and the game's hit detection decides to crap out on you. "♥♥♥♥!" you'll scream, as the game pulls the rug out from under you for the hundredth time, changing up an established mechanic yet again, for no reason other than to throw another "curveball" at you.
Poor voice acting, a rough script, and a nonsensical and painfully cliched plotline full of gaping logic holes strip the game of any remaining worth it might have had.
It looks pretty though. Shame about the whole "gameplay" part.
If you're looking for something along the lines of Out of This World, Flashback, or Prince of Persia, look elsewhere. I would recommend Oddworld: Abe's Oddysee and Oddworld: Abe's Exoddus, which are available in a bundle for $5 even when there isn't a sale going on, and even less when there is.

Deadlight reintroduces us to a vintage and tragic world. Vintage as based on old-school Side-scrolling and Tragic as based on the end of the human race. This near 3D side scrolling ZOMBIE infested nightmare will bring you to the edge of your wits as you play as an unlikely common Survivalist named Randall Wayne. You set out to find your missing family and along the way will meet various and random Survivors both friend and foe. In the ruined city you’ll need to run along from platform to platform avoiding or killing the walking dead better known as Shadows. These shadows and not your garden variety group of ZOMBIES. They will not infect you, they will not taunt you; they will merely KILL you. This adventure offers a side order of hunting for hidden clues and objects and the opportunity to increase health and stamina. Each scene is re-playable so you can go back and search for missing items. Your weapons are limited and unique for the situation. This has been a lot of fun to play and left me wanting more.

Gameplay -
Here's the big one. the game is a slog, but an enjoyable one. It nevers feels like you're doing the same thing over and over again. There is plenty of amazing moments in game which brake up any monotony. And If it ever get's boring, you can always swap to a tank crewman, fighter pilot, paratrooper or sniper for a fee.
Speaking of fees, Heroes and Generals is has a surprisingly good moto for them, "Give you really, really big ones, but few." The Kar 98k for Germany costs about 70,000 in-game credits and you only get about 1,500 per game. But you can always pick up a sniper rifle in game, or michine gun or tank (you can't keep them but you can use it until you die).
There are 5 different units you can be. Everyone starts as an Infantryman who can use rifles, machineguns, sub-machine guns, anti-tank weapons, grenades, and mines. Tank crew (the next unlock) can use submachine guns but start with a light tank (of which there are three you can purchase for only 2 billion dollars a piece!), medium tank, heavy tank or tank destroyer. Next is fighter pilot. they get a plane on spawn  and start with a pistol. Then paratroopers, with their rifles and sub-machine guns. Finally Recon, who are snipers. They get pistols and scoped rifles. Each class has distinctive vehicles and weapons can cross classes.
Joining a server is easy and cntrols are simple. Fighting a battle is interesting depending on your point of view. If playing as an infintry, prepare to get anhaliated. Snipers can pick you off from a million kms, tanks will plast you and fighter pilots will strafe and bomb you. tanks are invulnerable except to exceptally rare anti-tank weapons and tanks. Games are capture a series of flags till you get enough points to win.

A lot of people think this is a good game. It's not.
First off, you only have access to a few weapons, certainly not more than 20. This isn't weapon types, or weapons that you can buy different models of. Just 20 weapons, period. And they're terribly easy to get. Within 1 hour of starting the game, I had access to the assault rifle I used for literally THE REST OF THE GAME. The combat is also pretty stupid since you face the exact same enemies over and over and over again. All in all, combat gets repetitive enough that you actually hope no enemies show up. IN AN FPS.
You gain xp (?) from getting to checkpoints in the story which unlocks skills periodically. They're not impressive and are mostly useless, and I'm confident you could beat the entire game without ever looking at the skill tree. As an example, there's a skill that lets you assassinate an enemy from below by climbing onto the ledge they're stanging on. It sounds badass, but the opportunity to do this comes up only like twice in the whole game.
To be fair, the visuals and exploration system are the highlights of this game. There's nothing quite like going to the highest point in the map and jumping off with a hang glider. You can also explore caves and abandoned Japanese bunkers to find relics and other crap that gives you the history of the island. All that stuff is marked on your map though, so there's no real exploration going on.
Finally, this game has NO replay value at all. It's totally linear except for the ending cutscene (you can choose one of two endings, both of which are anticlimactic). Apart from that, you have no choices to make and no way to influence the story. If you were dumb enough to play this game again, you would have to do all the same stuff you did the first time around, just to get to one alternate 30-second cutscene.
You'd be better off buying skyrim, which has crazy replay value, and watching the cutscenes from far cry on youtube. That would give you the full experience of this game without costing a cent.

They don't feel too "gamey", but more like real places gone to Hell because of the Apocalypse.

This might be one of my favorite games of all time.
There is no game out there other than this one that gives me supreme feeling of awesomeness that I get leading a charge of heavy cavalry into and through a pack of swordsman or archers, lancing the first man and the pulling a sword and hacking down a few more as we ride through the ranks, only to form up on the far side and comeback doing the same again, then watching the enemy army crumble, turn and run, only to be ridden down and slaughtered.
Such strong feelings of joyful if brutal slaughter are match by the horror of leading that same charge only into rocky terrain, and seeing the bristle of pikes too late, realizing you've ridden your expensive and experience horseman into to a death trap.  Lucky, you can get off your horse, pull out that two handed claymore and just go to town, but getting out alive might still be a challenge.
As an indy game, there are some odd flaws in the game.  Sieges are strange, there are no options to chose/build siege equipment other than defined by the map, which are either a single ladder, a single rolling tower or occasional ...2 ladders.  Why i would assault a castle or tower with hundreds of men and one ladder is beyond sense.  But you know what?  It doesn't bother me that much, because it's just so much fun anyway.
So while some of the game mechanics don't make sense (You're immortal, as are you're named companions) the pure epic funnies of the battles is absolutely worth all the quirky game mechanics that make the campaign work.

As of 3/10/2014, Contagion in Early Access.
Contagion is a wonderful concept. It's fun with friends, a blast really.
However, it can get dull as it does have a repetitive nature.
They did a hell of a job making areas really dark, keeping you on your toes.
Zombies can climb, crawl, jump.
If you become a zombie, you can pretty much hire nearby NPC zombies to follow you and make up your own horde to ambush the living. As the spiritual successor to Zombie Panic! Source, once again you can do some lunging and running.
As a human, you have stamina that does dwindle if you run around, but if you slow down you will quickly regain it.
They recently added a new map, but it is for the hunted gamemode. Pretty much that's a PVP free for all. On the plus side, if you become a zombie in this game, you don't have "specials", so you can blend in easily and really startle the living players.
All in all, this game is progressing nicely, but needs to continue to grow, as the community within the game seems small -- then again, it doesn't help that most servers have an 8 player maximum slot. Would be interesting to see twice that.
I personally feel that this game should have some kind of a quick tutorial on player controls to make a new player feel welcome and give an understanding about Contagion.

The main game mode is called escape and sees up to 8 players try to work their way through a map full of zombies to escape a situation. The puzzles are pretty basic and usually involve finding an item to open a door or barrier. Each time you play the game the route changes, keys change location, different doors are unlockable/open, one game saw the team using vents to get around the map instead of taking the stairs. The zombies are easy enough to kill but a lack of ammo and limit to the number of things you can hold means that you often resort to using risky melee weapons. The limits on holding 5 things at once mean that through the game you do things such as swap a key for machine gun with no ammo(in the hope you will find ammo) only to find that the armory later in the game is locked..
Deathmatch sees up to 8 players battling it out on medium sized maps filled with zombies. While not strong the zombies are a great addition to the fight. The match is slow paced and it can be quite hard to find other human players, following a hoard who can smell human blood is a great way to track people down. Other ways to find humans include following flashlights, which works great when you see a small flash in the front room of the house next door or following gunshots. Gunshots is a great idea by the developers because at some point human players find themselves cornered in a loft with a zombie they need to take out; unfortunately, unless you have 5.1 sound its unlikely to help locate people that much.
I should point out the game is beta, so there is plenty of time for things to change. I don’t know how being a zombie can be more fun while not making them too powerful for humans. While it takes a while to hunt a human player down in escape mode, this stops the humans getting overran by 5 zombie players. I should also note that while being a zombie was a tad boring, playing as a human was really fun. It was also really tense, death actually meant something to the player and kept you on your toes.
I’m giving this 4.5 stars because I’m knowingly taking part in a beta. Perhaps I would give it 3.5 if this was the finished product, but it’s not. Reviewing games at this stage in their life is perhaps a little unfair, but I think its good giving games trying something new and following the kickstarter/green light/beta business models as much coverage as possible.

Deadlight is one of those games that charms no end with the attention to detail, the graphical backdrops and the dialogue. Yet in the same instance is perhaps one of THE most frustrating games to play - due to its input methods.
First off, I would strongly recommend using a 360 pad for this game. But if not, be prepared to repeat and repeat certain sections of the game, time and again. The crux of all these problems are the key combo presses. You can crouch. But to roll requires you to be running. When you're actually moving, stop for any reason and you loose momentum - meaning you cannot roll. Yep - roll through that little opening ahead of you. Oh look, you've just died again because a trap has impaled you.
Added to that is the fact that it appears the devs have lined up sequences where you can JUST about complete them before your imminent death. Trial and error get ultimately frustrating, but the overall quality of the game pulls you through.

While modern games today depend on "particle physics" and "SMAA", Mount and Blade focuses on scale and freedom.
There's not many graphics options for mount and blade.  Frankly, I'm surprised that it's even got an option for Antroscopic Filtering, and that the highest setting isn't 4.  However, it's able to run on DX7. If you want a scale, DirectX 8 came out on Windows 98.  For even more comparison, M&B:W could probably run on just about any computer from the year 2003 on.
However, if it's decent graphics you want, you can easily add in SweetFX or ENB to make the game look purrty.
However, Mount and Blade allows you to seige castles the proper way, and teaches you a thing or two about conquering kingdoms.  It also teaches you to not get cocky, and always overestimate your opponent, even if it's just a group of looters.
The combat system in M&B:W is a little clunky on occasion, but once you get the hang of it, it'll become second nature.  There are several combat skills to learn, such as One-handed, Throwing, Polearm, and Crossbows.  Horse combat plays a large part, and unless you have specific troops to take on horses, you'll need to outnumber the enemy by a large margin if you're going to win.  Thankfully, recruiting and upgrading your army is quite simple, compounded by the fact that you can lead them into battle yourself and give them orders in real time, from horseback or on foot.
The mods for this game are quite astounding.  There is a popular mod known as "A Clash of Kings" that is set in the Game of Thrones universe, as well as numerous Lord of the Rings mods, and even a Star Wars mod for the original M&B.
Of the mods that I use, I am partial to Light and Darkness, a more story-oriented mod for M&B:W that adds a lot of neat features, such as sprint, an in-game battle area map, and a true enemy faction.
I also play "Gekokujo", a mod set in fuedal Japan(with an accurate map of glorious Nippon), and "The Sword and the Axe", a mod set during high medieval Scandanavia(not sure on how accurate map is).  In additon, there are also mods set in Colonial 'Murica, the Crusades, and Ancient Rome.
And that's not even the multiplayer.  If you want multiplayer, you better prepare yourself for 200-man battles.  Battles in which, if you're commander knows what he's doing, can feel very much like a battle that would have happened in history with very real losses and gains.
Basically, it's "Medieval warrior/economic simulator 1206".

I'm writing this short review approximately 1 month from proposed release date, so the game is still officially in 'early beta'.
As a huge fan of co-op FPS (borderlands, etc) and especially zombie titles (dead island, L4D, etc) I'm very excited about this game.  Overall the game is quite polished already, but there are a few quirks (overused character models, texture clipping, etc) that spoil the immersion a little.
There is limited content (I would suggest that 'escape' mode seems to be the main campaign/mode of the game but there is only one map), and there are some bits missing like zombie-climbing animations, voice acting etc but all of these seem on track for the full release.
If the game follows through with its full release it has the potential to be a truly awesome game. Left 4 Dead comparisons are discouraged but unavoidable, and I for one (as a L4D fanatic) am looking forward to this. It sits somewhere between L4D and 'no more room in hell' (a slightly slower, more realistic zombie survival co-op game than L4D).
Keep an eye out for the full release due some time around April 2014.

Hi, Tacfap6 here!
Short version--- amazing rollercoaster of laughing/swearing, owning/getting pwnt, great teamwork/wanting to choke out teammates, action packed chaos that I love / hate every second of.  You will have moments of great triumph and terrible anger.  Great weapons, great maps, cool vehicles, difficult but rewarding gameplay.  I highly recommend this game.
Longer version---
FYI: I have not paid a single cent for anything in this game.  Once you learn the maps and weapons, you will be a force to reckon with.  But if you want shortcuts to get that gun or that tank then by all means do it.  Vetern membership seems to be worth it for sure.  However, I have reaced the recon branch with no money, so yeah you can grind there...it takes time...but you will be the among the top players in each round because you are awesome and you know to capture and defend, what gun suites your styles, and what role you play in the battle, and how to work with your team to win.
1. This is an Early Access Game and the Dev Team is doing great.
2. This is a difficult game starting out for either team.  You start with a semi auto rifle, acceptable at mid and close range.  Aim for the face.  Get to the capture point.  Defend the objectives.  The game considers bullet drop, bullet stability, range, movement, etc, so aim for the face and chest to maximize damage.  Get to the capture point!  Seriosly, capping a point and defending it gets you xp, money, and victory these are things you need.   Read the guides and keep your chin up!
3. Maps.  The full size maps are great battles and are well balanced.  The Devs have blended the pitfalls and benifits of urban warfare and rural warfare in each.  The terrain can provide you cover, a choke point, or set an ambush....but remember it works both ways.  There are many buildings you can enter which can allow you to regroup, pick off someone, avoid death from above (bombs), or wait for an enemy to pass and then hit them from behind.. use them but watch out for gernades.  There are fields, roadways, and open areas you will wish you can run faster to get past.  Spots to hide your tank or provide overwatch as a recon sniper... Just remember, if you lose all the objective points you will lose, and if you lose your spawning points, your entire squad will have to leave the game unless there are reinforcement squads available.  Tactics.
4.  Gameplay, there is something for everyone and if you get tired of that something, there are other somethings to try.  In the FPS section of the game, you can fight as a regular infantryman, drive a tank, fly a plane, be a paratrooper, or be a sniper.  Each has its pros and cons and each contributes to the battle and the overall war in a major way.  Within the primary infantry roles, you can be a lightning fast, in your face, devistating at close quarters force or you can be a steadily advancing, hard hitting, accurate, and tactical unit.  There are needs for both, weapons for both, and when you work together, it is beautiful.   Being a paratrooper is amazing
Teamwork is essential and you will find out quick if yours is not working together.
5.  There is a decent upgrade system to the player, the weapons, and the vehicles.  Player upgrades are known as badges, which are unlocked by certain tasks such as stealing vehicles or defending points.  Badges themselves are ranked and have different upgrades at lower ranks than high.  So a badge might allow you to reload a little faster or sprint a little longer, there are many and you will be able to use one that fits your role and style of gameplay.
Weapon upgrades include ammunition, triggers, sights, barrels, springs, etc that manipulate stability, range, damage, ROF etc.  Vehicle upgrades include support boxes, ammo types, etc.  So if your tank cant penitrate that panzer's armor, keep at it and ugrade your shells.
6.  Graphics.  I think the graphics are just right for this game.  Not picturesque, but that lets it be less demanding on your system enabling smoother gameplay, and not cartoonish or childish. The models of the weapons and vehicles are wondeful.  There are foggy and low light conditions too.
7.  The introduction of staged battles has helped the balancing of each round.  If one side is outnumbered, a 'deploy queue' is enacted on the larger side.  So if it is 15 v 19, the team with 19 will not beable to spawn all 19 at one time.  A few of them will need to die before the others can spawn again.  It might take 10 seconds it might take 60, but it will eases the steam roller effect.  The regular war battles can be a different story hahaha
---Suggestions for future updates--- more large maps please.   If waiting in the deploy queue for more than, say 40 seconds, it would be nice to not have to experience the typical extend spawn times, especially for paras, such as 'traveling to location' delay and 'picking up equipment'  I understand the purpose but it is frustraiting :)   more light transportation vehicles.  and keep being a great dev team!

Buy? Maybe. It's a linear, zombie survival platformer, with an emphasis on staying on the move and managing the stamina used from running and climbing. You control Randall Wayne in the late 1980s, trying to find his way back to his family back at the "Safe Point" in Seattle. This is hardly an action platformer; you'll run out of stamina trying to kill zombies and you can only take three hits, so it's always better to run. When you do get a gun, it's not for long. The game is mostly about moving to the right, avoiding zombies, dealing with mild hindrance puzzles, and escaping certain death via traps or gunfire via sprinting and platforming. The Rat section is particularly annoying as you encounter traps you don't expect or aren't completely sure what the game wants. It isn't really that hard, and only about 15-30 mins of the game, but I got irritated and was glad to get out of there. I played this because I read it was short and figured I could knock it out of my backlog, but after about 2-3 hours, I felt like I had enough and put it down. The game isn't really BAD, I just felt like I had enough and I think I'm tiring of pretentious zombie dramas. (maybe pretentious isn't the right word, but I become less interested in story based gaming as of late). Watch some videos and if the idea of zombie survival 2D platforming (versus zombie action like Dead Island or Resident Evil) appeals to you, you'll probably enjoy it.

I played the game for a short while and overall I liked it to the point where its a little bit better than Left 4 Dead. 10/10
Unlike other zombie games that try to imitate Left 4 Dead this one tries to stick to simple normal zombies and a great atmosphere that is complimented by some good graphics and the best flashlight effect I've seen in a game.
Difficulty is more or less dependant on how many people you have playing with you so if you want to have a challenge go solo but thats not very recommended as some areas of the game has 10-20+ zombies rushing you and I had trouble managing them with me and 1 other guy without having to funnel them into a hallway.

Imagine an updated Zombie Master (you played that one, right? remember the Winchester level?) has developed a mutagenic virus and injected it into a really bad RPG and you've got CONTAGION.
Though there are several map modes none of them really contain any new ideas. There are also only a very small handful of maps. One map mode has you running around looking for clues to get through the level which sounds fun and would smack of left4dead if your companions had any reason whatsoever to want to have you around. Anyone who knows the level already can more or less just ignore everyone else and complete all the objectives leaving new players to wonder how the game is actually played without huge amounts of trial and error or reading guides. It does not teach itself well and the targets can be very obscure.
That the map system consists of a PDA showing very little information does not help to soften the "alone in a crowd" feeling when the team has already completed several objectives and you spawn at the start wondering where to go or being blocked off from the team by crowds of zombies. Your entry to the level is hardly ever soft.
The choice of key mappings also leaves much to be desired. It is very easy to accidentally drop your weapon if you are used to the controls from other common games. Add to this the fact that targeting and picking up or interacting with things requires the utmost precision and you've got one hell of a headache.
Contagion has an interesting concept - which was already very successfully done by left4dead - and adds nothing new to the genre. It could easily be said that it goes back a few steps. This has the feeling and polish level of one of those FPS mods that sits in small-team development-hell for years with almost nothing getting done on it.
The graphics are indeed quite passable. The Christmas/snow level has quite a nice feel to it reminiscent of neighborhood charm of several of the similar half-life community maps from long ago.
Again, nothing new.
4/10.

WARNING: THIS REVIEW REFLECTS MY PERSONAL EXPERIENCE DURING THE EARLY ACCESS BUILD 4259
IT IS IN NO WAY A FULL PRODUCT REVIEW AND IT WILL BE UPDATED IN THE FUTURE AS THE GAME EVOLVES
Contagion is in many ways the ultimate co-op zombie apocalypse experience. You have many game modes, you have many weapons to grab, tools to use, there is a variety of zombies, it's graphically superior to many other games, and it's a challenge to anybody who wants to play a zombie game and doesn't want to be bothered by a-holes ruining the games, like they do in other zombie games I could mention (but I won't, you already know of which I'm talking about).
You shoot the zombies to the brain and the brain explodes, you see the bullet coming out of their head exactly where it should, and it's awesome. You need to take care and not waste your ammo because there's few and it's a valuable and scarce resource; same goes with medkits.
There are currently three game modes, one in which you must escape a facility carrying on a number of tasks, another where you need to evacuate a neighbourhood before it gets overwhelmed (and you must hold position barricading and such) and a game called "hunt" made for PVP combat. The first two are cooperative, although there is friendly fire so look where you shoot. The last one is a free for all deathmatch; the last man standing wins.
Although there are few maps at the time, you can see they are very detailed and won't get bored so easily as there is also a script which randomizes each game making it feel fresh, changing everything from weapon spawns to open hallways and houses.
All in all and even though it's early access this game is a gem and if you're into zombie shooters you should give it a test drive because it may be just what you were looking for.

As you can probably tell by my gamelist I am not one for shooters. Especially WWII shooters that have frankly done to death during my lifetime. We've gone from one shooter to another for so long that it's gone from dull to stale to tasting of bile... which has resulted in my largely abandoning the shooter genre for the past half a decade or so.
This game may be changing that.
What amounted to an amusing 'lets see what this is about' has proven to be an addicting experience that is making me relearn all those skills lost in a half decade of strategy and role-playing games.
Well enough hyperbole; Heroes&Generals is at its core two different games: a shooter and an RTS. So far I've not had a chance to get into the RTS aspect of the game, but the shooter is solid and I've enjoyed taking commands from other players who ARE playing this as an RTS. The experience is interesting to say the least, and once I made it out of the noob pen and got to play with more experienced folks that don't just charge at machine guns head on the experience went from 'kinda fun' to 'really fun'. This is one of those games where you don't necessarily have to be the best shot to be useful and everyone can feel like they're contributing even if their K/D ratio is skewed one way or another.
Add to the superb shooter aspect the ability to man vehicles, airplanes and such and you've got vast battles that can shift quickly, depending on where the general chooses to spend resources and sacrifice land for gain.
In short? Try it. The game's still in Beta, but it's creators have shown serious dedication and the upcoming features (such as a new faction, the Soviet Union!) are truly interesting.

Deadlight is a side scrolling puzzle and survival game with zombies in it. Yes a puzzle game with zombies in it, there are some jumping challenges and some well disguised puzzles but the zombies are a moving challenge as you must follow that tradition to go right the zombies will chase you no matter where you go so you have to use your own brain.
To me a side-scrolling zombie survival game is new, what got my attention was the look of it all. First off the main character is completely black, a silhouette while the background, zombies and other characters are in full color but there are still shadows everywhere so it fits. As you go through the game the camera doesnt just follow you, it locks in place. If your in a building you aren’t the center of attention, the building is. You can see every floor and every zombie whether they were playing dead on the ground near your feet or deep in the background.
The background is amazing, definitely not a simple still image, from looking at the background you can make sense of what you are doing, why you are going through the window in the foreground, why you aren’t running towards those zombies in the background who are heading towards you as they join the foreground, it is alive and shouldn’t be ignored.
I liked the puzzle element of playing with the zombies, they created a whole lot of tension to the game as you diddn’t always have a suitable amount of ammo to fight them all. Pistols and shotguns are there and I found myself having to use them at least 50% of the time which is a shame because I had much more fun trying to avoid the zombies than shooting them. Because it is a side scroller shooting a zombie was very easy. I never felt scared of the zombies or bandits. I could see through an entire building so there wasn’t much fear in the game, there was much more suspense than your average zombie game but thanks to some very generic action it never really delivered.
Overall I found it to be a great experience, too short for my taste but it has been so long since I have played a side scrolling game that I am proud to see what a mature themed side-scroller can do. If you like Zombie games and also like to use your brain then I highly suggest you try this out. If you expect great action and a good story then you’ll be disappointed.

Anyone interested in buying this: hold off until the developers lay out some sort of roadmap, or put out an update with a decent amount of new content and fixes.

This is a game that's really lovely to play at first, but quickly exceeds NES Battletoads for difficulty due *ENTIRELY* to the controls requiring too much micro-management of your actions. The helicopter chase sequence is where I gave up playing because I didn't buy this for a spasmodic twitch-fest but for an adventure game w/ occasional moments of high tension.
As an adventure game, it's excellent...
