My first impressions aren't great.  I've found the movement jerky, the leaning-while-strafing annoying, the hit-recognition terrible, and the "find-the-mission-item-to-proceed" and general inventory implementation a bit frustrating.
It seems like the movement was coded to represent someone constantly out-of-breath, always struggling to take the next step.  It's almost like the character is shuffling like a zombie from the get-go.  Running just makes the effect even more pronounced.  Also, when you strafe left or right, the game adds a leaning effect to your movement.  Maybe it's an attempt to progress the state of game movement, but instead, it just feels awkward.  I would guess that most users expect left/right to act the same as forward/backward as far as camera-bob is concerned.  In this case, the leaning seems to add a touch of lag to left/right movement.  Why couldn't they just add additional buttons to provide the ability lean left/right rather than mix it with the default strafing buttons?
In the most recent patch, it's stated that hit-box computations were tweaked, but I found myself missing at point-blank range all of the time.  Multiple times, I found myself emptying an entire clip into a zombies face with zero effect, only to take damage once the clip was empty.
My complaint with the mission item revolves around the first 'find-the-key' objective.  The devs stated that they simplified the act of finding the key, but I still wasted a half-hour of no zombie-killing doing laps trying to find the elusive key.  After 6 laps around the open parts of the level, I was bored, totally removed from the action, assuming that the item just didn't exist.  I finally looked it up in the Steam community threads to get a slight hint about it being at eye-level hanging from some sort of rack.  When a game totally removes you from the action to find an item, I would consider it poor quest implementation.
My last complaint is about inventory.  Reading through the community discussions, my complaint certainly isn't unique.  I mean, really?!?!  You have to discard one of your four weapons to hold a single key?!?!  Does a key really weigh as much as a shotgun or assault rifle?  In no reasonable way should I have to throw a gun on the floor to carry a single key across a level.  Additionally, it's recommended to keep the key to try on different doors, so I feel forced to continually waste 1 of the 4 item slots on said single key *just in case* there's a second door somewhere that could possible be unlocked by it.
Maybe I'll try the game when it's no longer in 'Early Access' and provide a different view of the game.  Until then, I cannot recommend this game to the causual gamer thinking that this game is in an entertaining, playable form.

Brilliant game. 2D zombie apocalypse platformer with 3D graphics, like a Prince of Persia survival horror. Really detailed environments that are fun to work through & a pleasure to explore, and just to look at.
Despite what some reviews might say, the "frustrating" parts they complain about are very short and only take a a handful of attempts. I almost skipped this great game because of those stupid reviews, until a friend and a Steam sale made me take another look.
Some people also complain about the controls. They must not be playing the game with a gamepad. Plug a 360 pad in and the controls are perfect. This isn't a mouse & keyboard game, and everyone has a 360 pad these days, don't they? If not, the wired ones are cheap and the standard for PC games these days.
As with lots of PC games, I had some problems that seemed to be due to alt-tabbing when it was full-screen. It seemed to pause for a long time once and crashed another time when coming back to the game. (Maybe also due to having two monitors.) Switching it to windowed mode cured all of that and it has been stable for several hours of further play. Its windowed mode is also very good, as it positions the window so the play area is all on screen, not pushed off slightly due to window borders/titlebars. Finally a game that does windowed mode right! And the option is right in the menus, no ini file editing or command-line arguments were required.
Go get it.

First the good parts:
If you like the WW2 scenario, have a look. You'll find many iconic weapons, tanks and even planes. They are nicely animated, in general the graphics are good for a free2play. The weapon behaviour is consistent and most weapons are balanced well, with a few exceptions.
You can reach all the different classes and even get a few gold ( in-game currency) for the first game of the day, if you are willing to invest time. So no weapons or vehicles are restricted to people who pay hard money, only optical stuff like skins.
And here are my reasons for the the thumbs down:
H&G is a typical grinding-style game. That's not inherently bad, just so you know what's coming: lot's of hard, somewhat monotone farming awaits you. It's a matter of personal taste, I guess.
But this game is not your typical shooter. Team effort is an important factor but sadly also the most frustrating part, at least if you play to win. If you start with random allies you'll soon notice that a few inconsiderate people can waste all your teams effort in a flash. The frustration increases when you use your credits in form of expensive weapons like the panzerschreck f.e. or use tanks and planes.
This brings me to my next point: Unless you pay for a veteran status, you might find yourself ending up with nearly no credit gain if you use said expensive weapons, vehicles or gun modifications. Those repair-costs hurt even more when you lose games because of inexperienced or even just lazy people who refuse to do their part or just randomly waste precious spawns.
You can use weapons without mods and thus farm credits but be prepared to face opponents that will have superior arms, which is quite the disadvantage and again, can be quite vexing.
I personally feel that some maps are unbalanced, and in general defending seems to be more easy than attacking. The individual rounds vary in length, many are quite long, at least half an hour and can be very repetitive and tedious. Especially some maps will be a one-sided slaughter and you'll be grateful when it's over regardless of the result.
Regarding my opening phrase:
Sadly this game sports cheaters and hackers resulting in frequent ban-waves. Reto has reduced their numbers quite a bit but I have heard reports of innocent people being banned along with the filth.
Also, you might want to learn their TOS by heart because they know just one punishment for miscreants, no matter how small the offense: permanent ban. So if you don't want to lose everything at the drop of a hat, be very careful.
This game CAN be fun, but you'll need either money or tons of free time and shouldn't be afraid of frustration.

It was pretty great when I started playing, everyone is basically on the same level and with the same class so there's nothing that is excessively "unfair".  The game only really starts when you get to level three though which is corporal rank for the US.  From here you can start to specialise in specific roles, tanker, pilot, paratrooper you know.  This is also the point where I started to like the game a lot less.
You're thrown into a game filled with more experienced players who have unlocked snipers and such.  You've basically got to choose between your semi-auto rifle or your ♥♥♥♥♥♥ machine gun.  Either way, you're vastly outclassed by every other player on the map.
As with what everyone else has said, this game is kind of pay to win but not quite.  It's more like, pay to not waste your time.  There is an in-game currency which rewards you with money everytime you participate in a battle, of course, everything costs a ton with in-game currency.  If you're not up to experiencing grinding for money then you can just buy it with coins, the games real-world money currency.
It doesn't end there though, you'll also need to unlock specific ribbons to use specific things.  Want to ride a motorbike?  Well you better drive the car until you've unlocked a specific ribbon 7 times.  There's a way to get around this though, their real world currency system.
Overall I think the game is pretty fun.  That is until you're put on the stage with pilots, snipers and tankers...then you're just there with your M1 Gerand and the grenades you paid in-game money for thinking....well, ♥♥♥♥.

The game is pretty fun and does have a lot of potential. But since it's still in early access, the amount of content isn't that huge, there's only 3 modes and 3 maps out (at least I've only seen those in populated servers). And there definitely has to be some tweaking in terms of gameplay mechanics. For example in one game mode the last one standing against zombies is the winner, so you'd expect that the game will have some tense situations when it's either kill the zombies together or kill the other player so that you'll be one step closer to being the last one standing and thus the winner of the round. But unfortunately it's pretty easy to just get away with killing every human player you see, and that's definitely a con. It makes it more of a deathmatch mode with zombies just roaming around.
The graphics and sounds are just as they should be and I've got nothing to complain about those.
I'd still recommend the game if you'll get it cheap. After a couple of months the game might be drastically different and better with more content. I've played the game for only 4 hours, but feel like I've seen everything there is to offer at this point.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.
Eat.

I'm not sure if I'll continue playing. Obviously I'm bad at it, but I don't feel it's entirely my fault.
You need exceptionally good eyes in this games. Enemies are not distinguished in any way, you get an occassional "enemy spotted", but it's basically telling you "there's an enemy that-a-way". No way to know if he's on the other side of the street or across the country.
The IDEA is GREAT. Most of the game feels good, but it's the details that ruin it. The basic rifle you get is slow, so you need to make every hit count - which means close-quarter combat is useless (I tried shooting without aiming at an enemy standing perhaps 5 meters away from me - missing, of course).
Switching to another weapon (if you have one, you start with rifle and grenade) means waiting for about a second until you can actually fire.
(BTW, grenades aren't something you use impromptu - it takes about a second at least to draw and throw them. So they're useless if you get surprised by a gang of enemies.)
The worst thing, however, is that you have no situational awareness. You hear "pop pop pop" all the time, knowing there's gunfire. But who or what? No idea.
I'm not sure how you're supposed to know where the enemies are, except for lying on the ground still, waiting for movement. Which is hard to do if you want to reach another location.
Sure, there are footsteps and you hear reload - vehicles aren't silent either. But no way to say if it's just your own guys or the enemies.
(Your own team has blue names above them - but when you're close together, it's hard to see the top of the character without missing everything else.)
Then there's hit points - I'm not sure, but I guess you have 2, maybe 3 hitpoints. Meaning that 3 hits at most kill you.
First hit - you realize there's an enemy, you start turning into his direction. Second hit, you're either dead or close to. Until you finished turning and started looking for the enemy, you're dead.
You might call all that "realistic" - and I admit I wouldn't know how it is in real life. But I do know that in real life my vision works differently than what a game portraits - and sounds are different as well.
We may not have enemy radar in real life, but I would think that situational awareness is somewhat better than displayed in this game.

Pros:
1) Great fps game for people that like strategy games. If you like any fast paced fps you may not like this game because most games after training missions are 30 minutes and in that time period you may not get more then 5 kills.
2) Many classes to chose from and once you play with the same class for a long time they are quite rewarding.
3) Weapons feel real. By that I mean that every weapon in the game is♥♥♥♥♥♥ It feels like you are in ww1/2.
4) Driving meachanics are pretty good.
5) Combat is very good (not including melee).
Cons:
1) To get the "nicest" classes you need to play for a long time. Once you pay to get the class you want (in game money) if you decide you don't want it anymore, you need to buy back into the infantry class to then level up again. The infantry class is the main class so if you want to get recon (sniper class) you will play infantry a long time.
2) Items in the game are very expensive so if you dont play a long time or spend money to get things (which is in euro) you won'te get much. Most guns are over 60 000 in game credits. By playing at least 8 hours and having mostly positive kdr, you csan get that much money, but it is very long.
3) You die a lot. If you are a new player, going 2/20 will be good. Going up agaisnt tanks, snipers, planes as an infintry will be challenging but, I did have a lot of fun going with explosives to blow up tanks.
4) A lot of camping/Spawn killing. Because of the sizes of the maps, you can have planes and tanks. But usually 5-10 min into the game all the tanks are in position and it is quite the camping match. Each team grills marshmallows.
5) Melee weapons. When snipers and tanks can get you easily 500 meters away, melee weapons are useless. If they didnt take space then it wouldn't be too bad, but most take 1-2 slots that sould be used for something much more usefull like mines or a pistol.
Verdict: Great game if you play with friends, very time consuming if you want things in the game, but its a game that you can easily pickup and play when ever

I was a huge fan of Far Cry 2, because it was one of very few games that I have ever played where I literally enjoyed every single second of the experience. There were no menus to go to for inventory, no menu to open for a map (map was just pulled out of the pocket; in-game): everything was integrated into the game, it was beautiful! This complete lack of need to enter a menu provided incredible level of immersion. The game also gave one complete freedom to explore on one's own terms. All of this was ruined in Far Cry 3, which is why I am not recommending it today. Here is a list of reasons:
1. Game seems a half-arsed port from a console version. You will notice it when trying to get around menus.
2. Lack of options. For example, you cannot turn off the minimap. I hate the minimap in all games and is the first thing I turn off. Instead you have this map that is constantly nagging at you, point you which way to go, and thus indirectly curbing your freedom.
3. Menus, menus, menus. For inventory, for crafting, for skills... kills the immersion.
4. Story is inferior to its predecessor.
5. The camera feature is cool, but because it marks all your opponents instantly and automatically, the combat becomes very silly. You are able to predict where all your enemies are at all times, because you can see their markers through walls. That's just ridiculous. Oh yeah, no option to turn this off, so if you just want to use a camera to zoom in and take a closer look at a far away camp without marking tagets, you are at a loss...
6. Having to gather plants for crafting is cool, but provides to be a boring mechanic, because the plans are shown on the map and you have to put ZERO effort into actually trying to locate the plant. They are just there, and everywhere.
7.  As a result of all this, I just found the game literally boring. Found myself just "grinding" to complete it, just to complete it, not out of enjoyment.
On the account of all this, I would advise against buying this game, and would instead suggest you get Far Cry 2, if you are a hardcore gamer and are looking for a challenging, immersive gameplay.
On the bright side: it is pretty! This may sound silly, but I also enjoyed the shade of green in FC2 WAY better than what they used in FC3, and seeing how this whole game is green, it really becomes a huge factor. That aside, it is still gorgeous, although landsace features did not stick out in my mind as much as those in FC2. Sky is amazing, sunsets are to die for, and a multitude of unique locations makes this game a definite eye candy.

If you're even remotely interested in swords, bows and sieges this game is a must.
In brief, you're thrown into a world filled with warring factions and then more or less left to do what you like. There are a couple of starting missions and if you're new to the game I'd recommend doing them as it's a good way to get to grips with the basics. After that though ... up to you.
You could raise an army of knights and start your own kingdom. You could become a bandit, attacking trade caravans on route to the cities. You might just want to play as a trader, always on the lookout for the best deals. There aren't many games that offer you this much freedom and it lends the game absolutely masses of replay value.
Be aware that the learning curve is pretty steep. This isn't a game where you can single handedly demolish an army, if you end up surrounded and alone you'll probably suffer. In addition it can take some time to get your head around the numerous gameplay elements such as managing your troops, finding allies, keeping up morale and so on. I promise you though that once you've got a rough idea of what you're doing you'll be hooked.
This game is still in Early Access so don't expect the full package, but you're still going to have a lot of fun with the current content already in the game, so enjoy :D

This game...has taken so much of my life...but I give it all gladly, for there are few games that are so satisfying.
This game is very difficult starting out, with unique gameplay and controls of an astounding complexity. With practice, however, I have mastered every aspect of it; I've won tournaments at level one; I've raided fortresses at the head of the charge, decimating my foes before my fellows reach me to provide support; I've seduced noblewomen; I've lead rebellions; I've even lived the simple merchant life.
My loyalty lies with Swadia, as their knights are unmatched in battle prowess, however I choose not align myself publicly with any kingdom until I've gained the strength to lead my own.
The ability to build an army from the ground up is marvelous; you have the power to hand-pick each unit, as well as placement on the battlefield. For the more experienced players, you can issue commands to individual groups to completely decimate the enemy. For new players, I recommend simply building an army of Swadian Knights and trampling the enemy like dogs.
In addition to a marvelous single player, this game has a multiplayer aspect that puts many games to shame; some of the most impressive battles can be experienced surrounded by friends as you strategize and compete against others. And if that's not enough, this game has a very open stance towards modding. The modding community has put together some very impressive additions that can make even the most experienced player fall in love with the game all over again.
If you want a game that brings a powerful sense of satisfaction, then look no further.

Ok so you have to take this game for what it is, free with in game purchases. Its not going to be perfect and the devs most likely will not listen to what most of us have to say. So saying that here are my thoughts.
Pros- Its free! what can you say, its a decent game thats completely free. Yeah it takes alot of grind to obtain some of the better weapons/vehicles but its still free. The game play is fun, frustrating at times, but fun. Most of the classes are really interesting and unique. Tanks crewman is one of my favorites and keeps things interesting, you could be destroying tanks left and right chopping down some unlucky infantry and then blamo! Enemy tank out flanked you.
Cons-Sniper class is way to easy and people take way to much advantage. if they tweeked it a bit and made it a bit of a challange it would be in the pro section. Issues with joining games with friends and getting split into another squad for some odd reason more and more. AA guns need to be really tweeked, your better off trying to shoot a dive bomber out of the sky with your rifle then use those useless things. The chartoonish nature of your character sliding by a doorway, minor issues with graphics that could be improved.
Overall this game is very good for a free one. I would for sure recommend it to anyone. Its going to continue to have issues, but hey we all know this. Its not going to be perfect.

Seriously one of the best games I have ever played, I must have racked up 200 hours on the vanilla campaign alone. Not many games you can say that about!
The game revolves around your hero and their quest to unite the factions of Calradia under one banner. This can be your banner, or your chosen factions.
The game mechanics are fun and immersive, you manage your army and the world in real time through a birds eye view of the map, comparable to Crusader Kings 2 except you control the movements of your warband and can interact with the map. You then switch into third person when you enter a town, or enter a battle. As well as the mechanics the game takes advantage of addictive RPG elements, making levelling your character both fun and rewarding, especially when you start taking your own castles and having liege lords. I could talk all day about the ins and outs of the game, but what's really important are the giant battles. The game allows you to be right in the thick of battle with an army of men you recruited from the ground up. Just last night I led an army of 500 men against 1300, the battle raged for over an hour before I went back to my castle victorious and drank wine from the skulls of my enemies while banging my wife. (Disclaimer: To have a similar experience you must be willing to use your imagination somewhat)
Then there are the mods, these add so much to the experience, giving you different maps, new troops, more quests, better diplomacy, you name it. There's even a complete overhaul that throws you into Westeros and turns the game into a Game of Thrones simulator. While the mods add a hell of a lot to the game they do not take away from that je ne sais quoi that keeps you coming back for more.
Next there is the multiplayer, the learning curve on multiplayer can be a little difficult if you go straight from the single player, but that's because human enemies are slightly smarter than the ai, slightly being the operative word in most cases. The multiplayer is at it's best when there are 100 human players besieging another 100 players in a giant castle. The large scale of it makes you feel epic, and means there is never a dull moment.
Long story short, buy this game and become king of Calradia. Then become Emperor of Rome. Then maybe king of Britain.
The graphics may not always be great, and I would like a better UI and statistics but other than that this game is great. I love gathering a huge army and just go on a rampage, Game of Thrones style!

The obvious caveats apply when dealing with any Ubisoft game. Yes, you have to climb towers to unlock bits of the map. Yes, there are infinite bits of unspecific stuff scattered about the map that you are encouraged but in no way obligated to collect. Yes, the narrative mostly builds itself around one completely amazing character performance and then falls apart when that character isn't onscreen.
Similarly, the obvious technical caveats apply as well. This is, after all, a game being published on PC by Ubisoft, and Ubisoft doesn't know how to make video games. So pop-in is common, character models vibrate and glitch around for no apparent reason, the graphical options are bare-minimum at best. For example, you can't disable motion blur without turning off post FX completely unless you go in to muck about with the game files, so I hope you looking at your shooters through dirty glasses. Optimization is generally crap, as we would expect from the publisher behind Uplay. Even with most of the graphical options dropped from ultra to high, and the resolution dropped to sub-1080p, I still couldn't get the game up to a consistent 60 fps, and I've got a 960 in my rig. I dread to think what the average customer is going through with this one.
Even once I'd gotten the game in a workable state, the technical issues still reared their ugly head from time to time. Friendly AI seems like it took a few blows to the head as a young child. At one point, I was running cross-country and stumbled upon a group of friendly villagers having a shootout with local pirates. Always hungry for action, I leapt into the fray and we quickly won the skirmish. One of the friendly villagers then called me over, and when I hit the "interact" prompt, he decisively and confidently turned around, walked five steps in the opposite direction, and started peeing on the ground while repeating "this is all me, all me" to nobody in particular. Villagers have a mechanic where they put their hands up or run away when you point guns at them, but this reaction doesn't seem to have any relation to how far away from them I am when I point the gun or whether they have line-of-sight on me. At one point I managed to pull agro from a group of friendlies because I aimed at them from the top of a cliff while they were looking in the opposite direction. Normally, these kinds of inane AI glitches wouldn't bother me, but then you get into one of the innumerable escort missions and find yourself getting yelled at because your current client won't stop sprinting directly into enemy machine gun fire.
And yet, I still love it. Warts and all, I still found myself drawn back to it every time I got frustrated and stopped. When you're alone and working through enemy strongholds, there's nothing more satisfying than expertly picking off an entire squad of bad guys with a series of well-timed headshots. Even when my plans for taking out a base go completely south and I find myself sprinting from cover to cover jamming myself with hypodermic needles in between smacking away the resident pit bull and swearing at the stupid thing, I was still having crazy amounts of fun. A well-structured skill tree and sensibly-implemented XP system mean that you get to figure out a combat style over the course of the game and upgrade the skills you want to complement that style. And while it doesn't usually amount to much more than the choice between "stealth killing everything" and "decidedly non-stealth-killing everything", it's still incredibly rewarding and lets you feel like you're getting a shooter tailored to your play style. So overall, while it's not anything close to perfect, it at least does everything it needs to, and that's really all I ask for from a game.

Not sure what to think of it. First: It's not an MMO. The store description is misleading. It's a middle-scaled matchmaking-based session shooter bearing similarities to Red Orchestra (difficult gun handling and enemy spotting, some overarching war theatre strategy aspects I haven't understood yet) and Battlefield (vehicles). It isn't necessarily providing the same depth and technical polish, but it's looking and feeling good enough to have some solid fun with it.
However, one must carefully watch if this is going to be "pay2win" or not. You seemingly can unlock and earn most that is purchaseable by playing/grinding too, however this is the case in practically all F2P games these days, so this is not a valid argument against P2W. If any P2W games exist they must be something like H&G or at least close to it.
Because at this point already I believe seeing paying players having advantages over me. They can carry more guns, they can switch them in the middle of the combat and they have them available more consistently than me. "Stock" players can only carry 1 firearm and 1 explosive equipment to which they are forced to stick with while the match is lasting (severly limiting their adaptibility) and explosives (even fragmentation grenades) need to be restocked after too many uses with the free currency you earn by playing or by using the premium currency you can buy with real-life money.
What put me off more right now is that premium players get access to better/new gear and vehicles more quickly. If you join a session and have your team consisting mostly of infantry (because they are free players, or because they are newbies or whatever), and the other team is using several tanks you'll soon understand the frustration that can come of it. You can pick up guns from dead people, and you can pick up a (well, one) Panzerfaust from your spawn location, but these pickups temporarily replace your one and only firearm to fight infantry with. On your way to finding a tank to blow up with it you will literally pray not to stumble into some hostile infantry because switching back to your own firearm makes your character automatically drop the replacement pickup (or, in the case of the Panzerfaust, simply vanish). Even if you make it through and get close to a tank your one and only Panzerfaust may not kill it. You would then have to head back to your spawn to pick up a new one - something no one will ever do because the way can be long and your sprinting bar is tiny by default. Or you do the poor man's decision and let someone kill you or suicide (which is greeted by a spawn delay penalty or by a spawn queue because for some reason the game won't allow too many people be on the battlefield at the same time, which is highly silly because this game is dealing with standard team numbers of something like 16 vs 16). All of this effectively cripples the efforts of stock players to fight tanks (and makes them want to pay too - that sure is the calculation the devs made here). Thus far any match I joined where one team had none or less tanks than the other was lost quickly and very one-sided. I myself purchased me a bazooka with the free currency, but then I must watch not to waste it's ammo because restocking it seems costly. Furthermore: My bazooka is only usable when I am playing on the US team - gear for either side must be purchased and restocked seperately which in turn may make people want to stick to "their" faction and lead to general imbalances and team biases wherever possible as well as to tensions between the community on some overarching level.
And these hickups are just relating to infantry vs infantry vs tanks. I bet there will be more annoyances of the likes when you'll be facing enemies in aircrafts. Annoyances to get rid off properly only when you will be paying with your wallet or spending half your life grinding your way somehow through, so I fear.
If you can overlook these obvious P2W aspects and have the luck to find sessions where there is mostly infantry fighting you can have some fun with this game. However I would recommend this only to people who not already own "proper" titles such as Red Orchestra or Battlefield. If you own the latter games you will hardly see anything new or appealing in "Heroes & Generals" maybe except for more excessive leveling and gear unlocks/mods (stuff that almost comes naturally with F2P titles). But even lovers of that may be better off with less obvious P2W titles such as Blacklight: Retribution if it needn't be WW2 one seeks.

The obvious caveats apply when dealing with any Ubisoft game. Yes, you have to climb towers to unlock bits of the map. Yes, there are infinite bits of unspecific stuff scattered about the map that you are encouraged but in no way obligated to collect. Yes, the narrative mostly builds itself around one completely amazing character performance and then falls apart when that character isn't onscreen.
Similarly, the obvious technical caveats apply as well. This is, after all, a game being published on PC by Ubisoft, and Ubisoft doesn't know how to make video games. So pop-in is common, character models vibrate and glitch around for no apparent reason, the graphical options are bare-minimum at best. For example, you can't disable motion blur without turning off post FX completely unless you go in to muck about with the game files, so I hope you looking at your shooters through dirty glasses. Optimization is generally crap, as we would expect from the publisher behind Uplay. Even with most of the graphical options dropped from ultra to high, and the resolution dropped to sub-1080p, I still couldn't get the game up to a consistent 60 fps, and I've got a 960 in my rig. I dread to think what the average customer is going through with this one.
Even once I'd gotten the game in a workable state, the technical issues still reared their ugly head from time to time. Friendly AI seems like it took a few blows to the head as a young child. At one point, I was running cross-country and stumbled upon a group of friendly villagers having a shootout with local pirates. Always hungry for action, I leapt into the fray and we quickly won the skirmish. One of the friendly villagers then called me over, and when I hit the "interact" prompt, he decisively and confidently turned around, walked five steps in the opposite direction, and started peeing on the ground while repeating "this is all me, all me" to nobody in particular. Villagers have a mechanic where they put their hands up or run away when you point guns at them, but this reaction doesn't seem to have any relation to how far away from them I am when I point the gun or whether they have line-of-sight on me. At one point I managed to pull agro from a group of friendlies because I aimed at them from the top of a cliff while they were looking in the opposite direction. Normally, these kinds of inane AI glitches wouldn't bother me, but then you get into one of the innumerable escort missions and find yourself getting yelled at because your current client won't stop sprinting directly into enemy machine gun fire.
And yet, I still love it. Warts and all, I still found myself drawn back to it every time I got frustrated and stopped. When you're alone and working through enemy strongholds, there's nothing more satisfying than expertly picking off an entire squad of bad guys with a series of well-timed headshots. Even when my plans for taking out a base go completely south and I find myself sprinting from cover to cover jamming myself with hypodermic needles in between smacking away the resident pit bull and swearing at the stupid thing, I was still having crazy amounts of fun. A well-structured skill tree and sensibly-implemented XP system mean that you get to figure out a combat style over the course of the game and upgrade the skills you want to complement that style. And while it doesn't usually amount to much more than the choice between "stealth killing everything" and "decidedly non-stealth-killing everything", it's still incredibly rewarding and lets you feel like you're getting a shooter tailored to your play style. So overall, while it's not anything close to perfect, it at least does everything it needs to, and that's really all I ask for from a game.

Ok. After playing this game for some months now I am going to recommend this game despite the many negative reviews and publicity it got. If you are true Call of Duty fan I would recommend this game to players. Now looking at the system requirements I would STRONGLY ADVISED that you pay attention to the RECOMMENDED SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS if you want the best gameplay experience. Let's face it you cannot expect to run a "NexGen Game" on "LastGen" hardware: it just would not work. Now let's look at the pros and cons of this game.
Pros.
1. Solid Single Campaign. Good Storyline.
2. Various game modes to play in multiplayer.
3. Various customization on guns, loadouts, characters etc.
4. New gameplay mechanic in multiplayer for example  fewer shots to kill your opponents online.
5. New game modes added such as SafeGuard, Squads & Extinction which is really fun.
6. A lot Of Downloadable Content  especially for Season Pass holders allowing for more longevity of the game.
7. Stellar Graphics providing that you meet the below Recommended system requirements.
8. A Clan mode feature which is a Call of Duty first. Ideally for competitive players.
Cons.
1. The system requirements can be a huge barrier to most PC owners seeing that they may not have the budget to meet those system requirements.
2. An Unoptimized game. Based on the COD community it is said that people who have average to high end systems they reported that their game was giving problems on max settings.
3. Hackers still exists in this game. Probably one of main reasons why the community doesn't have much players. Which leads to point...
4. Hard to find players on all game modes. You find players on TDM, Domination, Kill Confirm and S & D
5. Surprisely this game doesn't have a "Ping indicator" like its predecessors.
I know a lot of people might disagree with this recommendation but I am personally having fun with this game especially the DLC and its customization. I personally believe that this game is a great game and it would have been better if weren't for hackers destroying the COD community gameplay experience.

Mount and Blade: Warband has to be one of my favorite Role Playing Games. You start out with making your character. At the character creation screen you can choose what your father did and then what you did as a child, then teenage years. All those things have an impact on your stats. For example a "Game Poacher" may start with higher Bow proficiencies.
After the character creation you are dropped into the world and well, your adventure begins. After you do the first quest you are free to roam Calradia. The goal in this game is for one faction to control Calradia. You may either join a Kings Army where you may later on become the "Marshall" and have the commanding role in that empires military campaigns or... the more challenging route. You may start your own faction.
While traveling around Calradia you may find "Compainions" in the taverns of the major cities. They may help you in combat and if you make your own faction you may assign them as your "Vassal" and give them a fief (Castle, City, or Village). As your vassal they will mass their own armies and fight your factions enemies automatically.
Lastly I wanted to cover the battles. Your troops are able to be commanded by you, the player. You may have them hold a position, charge, advance ten paces, etc. The Enemy AI are adaptable on higher difficulties leading to varying tactics.
So, the decision is yours. Will you forge a mighty empire? Or join one. The choice is yours in Mount and Blade: Warband.

3/18/2016 updated review.
Revisited the game one year later. Some improvements were made. A few of my previous cons such as spawn camping and no exp for neutralizing were addressed.
PROS
1. good hit detection
2. Decent player base. I havent seen anywhere near the usual level of toxicity present in other fps games.
3. Free to play. Pay to advance quicker but not pay to win.
4. Environmental effects like fog or glare.
CONS
1. Tanks can sit waaaaay back from combat and snipe you out with 0 way to do anything about it. These players will sit on the edge of their base or the edge of the map and destroy you across the map. Tank drivers can also instantly exit tank and mow you down while your setting an AT mine or nade.
2. There is a lot of grinding to unlock anything in this game. Don't expect to install it and be able to play in the style of your choosing. It takes many many hours to become a sniper or a pilot or a tank crew.
3. Spawning. You can't do it on teammates. Only at base or the very rare mobile spawn vehicle. Bike to capture point, get killed on way because they know exactly where your team is attacking from, repeat. It can be tedious.
4. No experience for assists or spotting.
5. Devs are very slow to make impactful updates. They push new content instead of prioritizing current flaws. After nearly two years game is still Early Access. It's clear the game won't evolve significantly from its current state.
6. War game mode queues can be very long.
7. Few maps in place. They get stale quickly.
Subscription benefit system in place. This game is probably worth about $15 but if u spent that in their shop you'd come away with so little. And of course your subscription benefits would expire as soon as you stopped dishing out the mullah every month.
Would be nice to pay a flat amount to enjoy permanent subscription benefits.

Quick and Snobby Review: Deadlight (PC)
So, on a whim, I decided to download Deadlight because it was on sale via Steam. All I can say is wow! Great atmosphere, intriguing storyline, great visual (very Limbo-esque), and great blend of several game play types. Even when you finally get weapons, you'll want to use your know how and lure enemies into traps and avoid confrontations. This game is about survival, not kill counts.
This game has puzzles, to action, to platforming, all set in a metroidvania style side scrolling motif, and boy is it fantastic. There is no overall map and you don't get a ton of items, but the fixed camera is there and some areas really open up.
Deadlight was originally an XBLA game and was ported to PC without any major hiccups (some slowdown during loading sequences that should not happen on even a moderate PC, but would on a console, for example). The keyboard controls could have been tweaked a little more, but overall a great experience at a great price.
I would give it a solid 8/10...
Pros: Visuals, Varied Blend of Gameplay, Intriguing Story
Cons: Wonky Controls (Occasionally), Performance Issues (Loading)

This game is very difficult starting out, with unique gameplay and controls of an astounding complexity. With practice, however, I have mastered every aspect of it; I've won tournaments at level one; I've raided fortresses at the head of the charge, decimating my foes before my fellows reach me to provide support; I've seduced noblewomen; I've lead rebellions; I've even lived the simple merchant life.

In addition to a marvelous single player, this game has a multiplayer aspect that puts many games to shame; some of the most impressive battles can be experienced surrounded by friends as you strategize and compete against others. And if that's not enough, this game has a very open stance towards modding. The modding community has put together some very impressive additions that can make even the most experienced player fall in love with the game all over again.
If you want a game that brings a powerful sense of satisfaction, then look no further.

Mount and Blade: Warband has to be one of my favorite Role Playing Games. You start out with making your character. At the character creation screen you can choose what your father did and then what you did as a child, then teenage years. All those things have an impact on your stats. For example a "Game Poacher" may start with higher Bow proficiencies.
After the character creation you are dropped into the world and well, your adventure begins. After you do the first quest you are free to roam Calradia. The goal in this game is for one faction to control Calradia. You may either join a Kings Army where you may later on become the "Marshall" and have the commanding role in that empires military campaigns or... the more challenging route. You may start your own faction.
While traveling around Calradia you may find "Compainions" in the taverns of the major cities. They may help you in combat and if you make your own faction you may assign them as your "Vassal" and give them a fief (Castle, City, or Village). As your vassal they will mass their own armies and fight your factions enemies automatically.
Lastly I wanted to cover the battles. Your troops are able to be commanded by you, the player. You may have them hold a position, charge, advance ten paces, etc. The Enemy AI are adaptable on higher difficulties leading to varying tactics.
So, the decision is yours. Will you forge a mighty empire? Or join one. The choice is yours in Mount and Blade: Warband.

Pros: The game is absolutely beautiful graphics-wise, and alot of fun... when it works.
Cons: This game has been out for over 3 years now and yet Ubisoft has still not fixed the glaring technical issues. First off, you must have the game installed to the same drive as Uplay. This is frustrating, as I keep all of my games on their own drive and do not like installing them to my main C drive with other programs. At first, you would have no idea that this is an issue as the game starts up fine, but it will not load the first level without crashing to the desktop if you do this.
Once you do get the game to start up, you will likely be faced with some of the most horrific stuttering you will ever see in a video game. My PC's specs annihilate the requirements for this game (4790k@4.4Ghz and R9 390) but yet I still cannot run the game without huge stuttering issues, even at the lowest settings. I can go from running the game at 100fps to 0fps in an endless cycle. There are countless pages and forums online with people with similar issues and yet Ubisoft has not done a thing. It's a shame, as what little time I have spent on the game at the time of this review, has been really fun. This is a high-budget game from a company with more than enough money to ensure that the game is in working condition for the millions of buyers. We shouldn't have to spend hours browsing forums just to find a way to get it to run. It just SHOULD from the start.
UPDATE: after reading through forums for a few hours, I finally found a solution that worked for me. Go into Radeon Settings (Crimson) and make a profile for Far Cry 3. Set Target Frame Rate Control to 60fps and force V Sync. This seems to stop the stutter for the most part, but I'm not sure why since the game completely ignores these settings and runs uncapped at around 90-140 fps for me. I will not be changing my rating of the game to positive though, due to having to waste hours of my time to get the game up and running. That said, it is a really fun open-world, first-person, action-adventure game and I'm enjoying it so far.

For starters, I have played Far Cry 3 trough once on Xbox 360, but bought it on sale and re-played it + played the DLC material (which I havent played before). Thats why I have around 40h played of story mode.
Far Cry 3 is an open world FPS, with fair amount of weapons, weapon customizations, vehicles and enemies. AI is kinda ok, gives good challenge even on normal difficulty. Dark sense of humor and characters are the salt in this game, all of em are cool and interesting which gives this game a nice first play experience. For example, Vaas, the baddie, has been said to be one of the best bad guys in gaming history. Jason Brody, the guy who you are, is also well done. Its interesting to see how he changes troughout the game, starting from wussy richboy and ending to badass jungle soldier.
After you have played trough tutorial, its all about open world and advancing the story when you feel like it. Game itself kind of forces you to start by crafting larger backbags, wallets, weapon holsters and so on because your first bags are too small for any normal human being. This is done by hunting different animals for their leather. Its not nerve wrecking at all, all animals are marked on the map so its easy to find the right zone where to hunt.
After you have done that its all about capturing outposts and radio towers. Outposts give you fast travel location and some side quests. They are also fun places to challenge yourself to be best god damn ninja in those tropical islands. Radio towers make area of map visible and make 1-2 weapons free per tower unlocked.
It should be noted that FC3 is well made, running in the jungle, or swimming in the pacific ocean really feels and looks neat and realistic. This game has also nice sneaking moments + its somehow awarding when you hit enemy from 150m with a f**king bow.
Biggest failure in Far Cry 3 is giving weapons for free. This makes the game so much easier because you dont have to grind money for weapons. All you have to do is to go to the radio towers, climb up there and reveal area. Most of these towers dont have enemies near them and if there actually are enemies, its mostly 2-4 of em.
Another bad side is the replayability. FC3 is so story driven that after playing it trough, you wont even think about it for 1-2 years. Dont get me wrong, story is good and interesting BUT after you know what is going to happend, you really dont wanna go trough the trouble again. Atleast thats how I see it.
Third con is the weird "bugs". Sometimes enemy baddies spot dead body even trough walls or see where they shouldnt see. This annoys a bit but its kind of rare so it doesnt really ruin your gaming experience.
Far Cry 3 to those who enjoy story driven single player games with littlebit of RPG aspect in the mix. Far Cry 3 is a good game and worth your time even when it gets easy. Its also quite fun for the first playtrough, with its dark comedy. For example you get to burn weed fields with a flamethrower which... well.. you know what happends when weed burns.

even do so much as consider purchasing another Call of Duty title on PC developed by Infinity Ward. Some games as well as previous Call of Duty titles are meant to be more user friendly and developed around  lower end systems to pass on on graphical fidelity and instead aim for a more mechanics driven experience. Call of Duty Ghosts delivers neither of those two and instead falls on its stupid masked face.
Upon launch of the game back in 2013, it was a poor excuse for a console port to PC. No FoV options, pitiful graphics while consuming obscene amounts of system horsepower while running terribly, ridiculous system requirements (seriously, you need 50GB of my disk space for this rubbish?), gun play that feels "meh" at best, and God awful multiplayer level design.
I'll admit, there are some interesting aspects. It's nice to see the "Pick 10" system still
in place, but not nearly as well designed as Treyarch's version. Certain weapons coming with integrated attachments is a neat thing, albeit with a rather narrow selection of weapons to choose from. Though this doesn't help that the aforementioned gun play is rather boring, and no gun I ever tried had significant
to it to make me feel as if I am using more than some dinky airsoft gun from a corner store.
All that sounds bad for the most part, I know. But you know what sounds worse? The actual game. Call of Duty Ghosts has no doubt, the absolute
sound design in any shooter I have ever played. It's absolutely pathetic. Half the guns seem to sound the same, and I wouldn't mind that if they at least had some depth to the sound. But every gun sounds like you put a rock in a tin can and shook it around! In fact, that would sound BETTER than half the guns in this abysmal game.
You know what else is bad? The level design for multiplayer. I don't know what they were thinking with the pacing of the maps, but I'm pretty sure their minds were obscured by a bit of LSD. The flow of combat in the maps is terrible, and movement feels sluggish and boring. Back in MW2, the movement speed was perfect for the map size and the maps were the right size to begin with. But now we're constantly being given tiny maps compared to what used to be the norm, and to make sure you can't do a lap of them in five seconds you now move painfully slow. Not to mention the maps are organized in a way that makes as much logical sense as using molasses as libricant in your car's engine. And I hope you don't mind respawning within 15 meters of an enemy at all times thanks to the awful spawning system.
Now, the Extinction mode. I'll admit, it looks kinda cool. One of the better co-op experiences done by Infinity Ward for sure, and for the Call of Duty franchise it's certainly something new. But is it a good new? Eh... I'll leave that up to the individual to decide. If I'm going into a co-op shooting gallery, aliens aren't high up on my list of preferred bullet pin cushions. Though I'll award a few pity points for trying to do something with this game in at least one category.
On the subject of the Single Player... I'll admit, I didn't touch it. Let's face it, year after year, people buy into Call of Duty for the multiplayer. If I want a lush and deep single player game, I'll look to a game that is designed around the concept of a blissful single player experience. Knowing how this game is though, I can imagine that the campaign was rather lackluster at best if not a poor excuse for a tacked on side game mode for when you ragequit the online multiplayer. And Squads? I'm just gonna ignore that... It falls within the realm of the online multiplayer, and that mode is a joke in just about every regard.
So in conclusion; this game is not worth your time or your dollars, euros, rubles, or freaking Dogecoins if you somehow managed to obtain this game using them. The game runs poorly, simple features that should have been present at launch were not to be seen, the game looks like a dated console port that has way too much brown in the colour pallete, the multiplayer is the worst experience to date, the sound in game is nearly gag worthy,
while taking up FIFTY GIGABYTES of your monthly internet bandwidth and 50GB of space on your hard drive. It's a waste of space, a waste of time, and a waste of money. Want a good PvP shooter experience? Go buy Titanfall! If you don't want to use Origin's service (I don't blame you there), and you still want to go buy something... Go buy six copies of Goat Simulator and gift five of them to your friends. They will love you for it. Otherwise, avoid this game like the bubonic plague.

For starters, I have played Far Cry 3 trough once on Xbox 360, but bought it on sale and re-played it + played the DLC material (which I havent played before). Thats why I have around 40h played of story mode.
Far Cry 3 is an open world FPS, with fair amount of weapons, weapon customizations, vehicles and enemies. AI is kinda ok, gives good challenge even on normal difficulty. Dark sense of humor and characters are the salt in this game, all of em are cool and interesting which gives this game a nice first play experience. For example, Vaas, the baddie, has been said to be one of the best bad guys in gaming history. Jason Brody, the guy who you are, is also well done. Its interesting to see how he changes troughout the game, starting from wussy richboy and ending to badass jungle soldier.
After you have played trough tutorial, its all about open world and advancing the story when you feel like it. Game itself kind of forces you to start by crafting larger backbags, wallets, weapon holsters and so on because your first bags are too small for any normal human being. This is done by hunting different animals for their leather. Its not nerve wrecking at all, all animals are marked on the map so its easy to find the right zone where to hunt.
After you have done that its all about capturing outposts and radio towers. Outposts give you fast travel location and some side quests. They are also fun places to challenge yourself to be best god damn ninja in those tropical islands. Radio towers make area of map visible and make 1-2 weapons free per tower unlocked.
It should be noted that FC3 is well made, running in the jungle, or swimming in the pacific ocean really feels and looks neat and realistic. This game has also nice sneaking moments + its somehow awarding when you hit enemy from 150m with a f**king bow.
Biggest failure in Far Cry 3 is giving weapons for free. This makes the game so much easier because you dont have to grind money for weapons. All you have to do is to go to the radio towers, climb up there and reveal area. Most of these towers dont have enemies near them and if there actually are enemies, its mostly 2-4 of em.
Another bad side is the replayability. FC3 is so story driven that after playing it trough, you wont even think about it for 1-2 years. Dont get me wrong, story is good and interesting BUT after you know what is going to happend, you really dont wanna go trough the trouble again. Atleast thats how I see it.
Third con is the weird "bugs". Sometimes enemy baddies spot dead body even trough walls or see where they shouldnt see. This annoys a bit but its kind of rare so it doesnt really ruin your gaming experience.
Far Cry 3 to those who enjoy story driven single player games with littlebit of RPG aspect in the mix. Far Cry 3 is a good game and worth your time even when it gets easy. Its also quite fun for the first playtrough, with its dark comedy. For example you get to burn weed fields with a flamethrower which... well.. you know what happends when weed burns.

The fact that I can do stunts with a fc3 boat over a waterfall, by default press E to single handedly turn over the boat 180 degrees is a good pleasure. Lisa as a girlfriend with not much active features is a let down. Where's the black tour guide in most of my adventures? The fact that we have to climb radar tower everytime to gain strategic advantage is a bad let down as it tested my fear of heights to the limits I even give out girlish screams as I fall now. I rate it 3/7
There are reasons to complain, but not enough to overshadow the fun to be had.

Far Cry 3 is maybe one of those games that really would put anyone in the protagonist's feelings. It is an open world game that makes you think throughout any kind of missions such as stealth, dinamic or other ways of dominating outposts and the entire island.
Unlike Far Cry 2, Far Cry 3 is more into the first game made from the Far Cry series, in the way that the action is based on a dangerous, hostile island and the protagonist has to make his way to get away from it. The storyline is as thrilling as it can be, stuck on a place you do not know, pirates, enemies, predators, all sorts of plants that you have to collect so you can survive, an insane journey.
The main character has little battle and combat experience, so he has to learn how to survive from scratch, little supplies, he is going to be helped by many people who will soon become his buddies/friends. During the game, you have to gain the "tatau", which is their way of calling "tattoos". They are essential from the beginning of the game to the very end; they are the symbols of a whole, representing the skills you have to gain in order to finish Far Cry 3.
One more interesting fact is introducing the bow. The protagonist can finally use the bow and customize it in the way the player wants to, paint it, use different arrows etc.
Last but not least, there are lost loots, lost letters, relics, radio towers to activate (to free new guns) and other things that need you to be discovered, in the game, you can play games such as poker, throwing knives, car races, in order to gain or lose (in bad luck :/) money.
I have played this game for more than 30 hours, and I can say i have not finished even half of it (the storyline is excellent). The missions, outposts, helping people in need, searching for artifacts and so on is just amazing for any of us to try.
I would definitely recommend this game to anyone who is willing to try it :)

This is my first review of a game on Steam but felt that I had to write something about it.
Generally FC3 gets mostly positive reviews and for the life of me I can't understand why. It's a heavily over cliched trawl through the same tasks over and over e.g. activate tower,  capture outpost, do side quests and look for relics & lost letters, next tower, capture outpost etc.
Some reviewers have spoken about the open world play. What open world play? Once you have a map area cleared what is there left to do? Stand in a field and take a pop shot at animals?
What irks me most though is this game has absolutely no originalty and there was just a sense of boredom playing it, the terrain doesn't even change for example. The devs have a chance of creating an open world full of possibilities and they just deliver a linear story which isn't immersive or fun in any way.
If you're looking to buy this, even on a sale then don't bother. Do yourself a favour and get Just Cause 2 or 3. Similar story line and similar environment bu JC2 is great fun. Come on, who doesn't like hijacking a helicopter, taking it to the nearest base/oil rig/etc and just going to town on it. It's good fun.
Far Cry 3 Cons:
* Boring unbelievable story. How does 1 tourist take over a series of islands that a whole army of tribal warriors couldn't?
* Main character (Jason Brody) could do with a slap
* Monotonous terrain
* Keystrokes take an age to activate e.g. hold q to heal, by the time that kicks in you're dead
* The local animals are just a hinderance e.g. in the middle of a fire fight, a tiger comes in and kills you
* Repetitious game play
* Not enough modes of transport
Pros:
* Can't think of any

Heroes & Generals Review as of 08/08/17:
Okay, ive been playing this for almost 4 years now, having started in september 2013, and i must admit this game has been a rollercoaster ride of ups and downs.
The game started of as great, balanced and very fun back in 2013 where we still had only 2 factions: USA vs Germany.
Every aspect of the game was balanced; be it war, infantry, tanks, planes, etc... and i played around 100hrs at that time.
Sometime later, the russia update hit h&g... brutally. URSS was brutally overpowered in every aspect and signed the start of a long history of inbalance in the game that persists to this day. Soviet infantry weapons were better in every aspect to US and GE counterparts, their tanks were inpenetrable and and 2 shot their enemies who 3 shot them, their plane was faster and more armed, etc... Also, the grind was greatly increased through low rewards and high repair costs...
I stopped playing the game due to this.
In the course of 2016, the devs launched many new updates aimed at reducing this inbalance as well as significantly reducing the grind. New tanks and planes were introduced, all faction weapons were balanced, the game became fun again.
In the course of 2017, they have fixed vital gameplay issues such as vehicule physics, spawn protection and Weapon/ vehicule balance through all factions and announced incoming updates that will fix the games 3 main current problems, namely; 1) Broken RTS War system in disfavor of Germany, 2) Broken Armor vs Infantry system in disfavor of Armor, 3) Broken specialised class limit system in disfavor of Germany in heavy fighter planes and USA in fighter planes matches.
Also, 2 new maps and 3 new planes are in the final tests and will be released shortly.
Personally, i think the game is on the right path right now, and is very much playable. I have a constant K/D of 1.30 and can make roughly 40,000 credits per hour if i need cash, simply by playing as pilot, and all aspects are fun to play. I own 10 toons, of level 6 to 15, each owning fully modded end game weapons and vehicules, as well as 2 assault teams for the RTS.
This game is NOT P2W, the grind is very generous, the community is rather friendly and always ready to help new players.
The gameplay is fluid, i rarely have bugs, dev feedback seems to be increasing with biweekly dev streams which is good!
On this note, i give to to current state of the game a 7/10, leaving alot of room for much needed improvement, and dearly hope the devs stay on the path of improving this game that has huge potential.
Ive so far invested 10€ into the game to show my support and hope they keep heading in the right direction with this game.
To all players interested in starting the game, go for it, dont trust the reviews of rage quitters and fps kids with no sense of strategy.

"Lost potential" best sums up this game.
If you were looking at this and thinking that the big strategy map idea sounded really good, you're not going to be able to do that in game for quite some time as it's level gated; until you hit the right level, you're only a soldier on the ground. For the first three levels, you're also restricted to playing a limited pool of maps which are not a part of the current war scenario. I can understand why they've done that, they don't want fresh-faced new players to get demolished so they match them with other new players but getting the recquired levels to advance is a serious grind. If you don't mind playing the same maps and not affecting the war scenario for the first five(ish) hours of gameplay then that may not be a problem for you.
Whilst there's no direct pay to win, the in-game store is ridiculous. It's going to be a long, long time before you'll be able to afford something new and fancy unless you put real money into this. Due to not many being able to afford upgrades, vehicles or new weapons with just the in-game currency alone, purchasing things with real money can put you at a real advantage. You can still be outplayed but there's some definite tipping of the scales.
Player movement is pretty horrible. It constantly feels like you're trying to walk whilst waist-deep in syrup with an excitable (and potentially drowning) child on each leg.
Yes it's still in early access and everything is subject to change but these problems are going to take a long time to get fixed if they end up being fixed at all. Overall, it's an ok game for an hour or two but it's nothing more than a quick time waster. Don't expect to get dragged deeply into this.

Far Cry 3 is an open world action-adventure first-person shooter video game developed by Ubisoft Montreal in conjunction with Ubisoft Massive, Red Storm Entertainment, Ubisoft Shanghai, and Ubisoft Reflections, published by Ubisoft for Microsoft Windows, Xbox 360, and PlayStation 3. The game was released on November 29, 2012 in Australia, November 30 in Europe, and December 4 in North America. A stand-alone expansion titled Far Cry 3: Blood Dragon was released on April 30, 2013.
Far Cry 3 is set on a tropical island between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. After a vacation goes awry, protagonist Jason Brody must save his friends, who have been kidnapped by pirates and escape from the island and its unhinged inhabitants.
The third installment in the Far Cry series, Far Cry 3 was critically acclaimed upon release, with reviewers praising its world design, open-ended gameplay and story, while the game's multiplayer mode was criticized. Following the game's success, Ubisoft announced a successor, Far Cry 4.

Heroes and Generals is a great game, and I highly recommend it, especially to those who enjoy RTS/MOBAs. Unlike CoD and Battlefield, H&G is heavily strategy-based and teamwork is key to any victory. A decent variety of weapons allows for interesting gameplay, but it can take a while to earn the credits to buy multiple advanced weapons. One feature I think is rather well-designed is the mulitple-soldier system: instead of having one playable character with many loadouts, you can create several soldiers with independant XP/items, but share credits. While it might be a bit of a grind to get to where you want to go, H&G is not noticeably Pay 2 Win in-game, especially considering the ease with which one can kill an enemy and appropriate their weaponry. Even though purchases are heavily integrated into the shop, 10-year-olds with their mom's credit cards and a Scoped M1903A1 with 1-hit kill mods are most often just a detriment to their team and easily defeated by those who put the time in to learn the game.
TL;DR: 8/10

It takes a while to invest yourself into the game, but you can lose hours into it building your own army, participating in Tournaments, ransacking the villages of enemy kingdoms and attending the occasional feast (Or if you side with Swadia, go to a feast every single day).
The gameplay is great, having directional controls with the mouse to use your weapon takes time to get used to, but it also gives the game a higher skill ceiling and feels great to master.
The only problem is that the game is relentless if you fall in battle, and even more so when you lose your army. Hopefully in the new game there will be more of an ability to direct your armies in battle, but otherwise, it is well worth your time.
Also, if you are into multiplayer, you will be happy to know that Mount and Blade has a thriving multiplayer community of dedicated fans, and the Napoleonic Wars expansion is also quite popular too.

Far Cry 3 is a sum of many ubisoft games, they have taken many features from their other IPs and successfully combined it with the tropical setting of far cry 1 the end result is a brilliant open world fps that is exciting to play till the end.
There is coop and competetive multiplayer in FC3, the PvP is decent fun you level up fairly quickly and have battle cries and can customize a lot, you can spend a decent amount of hours in it before getting bored, the PvE is really fleshed out and the characters are well written and is objective based you will have better luck finding a game in the competitive mp rather than the coop mp.
The single player is a very diverse,really fleshed out levels and thoroughly exciting until the end. The best part i loved about FC3 was that it rewarded stealth play example if you take out an outpost you get 500 xp take out the outpost but without triggering the alarm and you get 550 xp and if you take out the outpost without being detected you get 1500 xp. This is the reason why i almost always used stealth to take out outposts and you can do the same in most of the missions. The wildlife makes it feel like a real world where you can skin animals and sell it for cash or use for crafting, the herbivores will run away scared of you the carnivores will actively attack you and try to kill you, you can also set animals like bears,tigers and lions on the enemies by luring the animal to them or by shooting the caged animals which is a lot of fun.
Traversing through FC3 is a blast you can use the outposts you captured as fast travel, the cars are decent to use the water vehicles are very fun to use espically the jetski, the most fun you can have traveling is when you ziplines and the glider, later during the late game you will have access to wingsuit and paracute which makes traveling from one point to the other even more exhillariting and fun to do. FC3 is a looker it looks really good and the vistas change from region to region some of the segments are breathtaking, the level of detail if you can run it on very high/ultra is mindblowing, the lighting the shadows and the particle effects are really well done, the facial animation doesnt look that well but it is a 4 year old game now so cant complain too much. The jungle truly comes alive as the meshes of the trees grass and plants make it feel really life-like.
I feel FC3's villian characters are really interesting with backstories and are well developed especially Vaas whose voice actor really brings the character to life but the hero characters espcially the main hero J.Brody is not intersting nor convincing the character will blurt out stupid puns and make fun or everything and sometimes acts all serious making him feel like a man-child. The story is simple and the game has two endings, i only wish they made the "bad" ending somewhat better but i guess then it wouldnt be the bad ending but overall the story is servicable and the characters for the most part are good.
There is a lot to do in FC3 from unlocking towers to view segments of the maps, free outposts to fast travel and access new items, complete side quests in which you are required to eliminate enmies or animals using speific wepons, looting is very fun and the game actively encourages you to do so the chalice ones are hard to do and fun since it makes you explore, apart from these you have races,gambling,knives throws, etc, so yeah a lot to do. FC3 tropical setting really helps the mood of the game and the nigh and day cycle really bring out the jungle vibe. The game doesnt have too many  bugs or glitches, i did run into a few popups and stutters but mostly its looks good and runs well. The problem sometimes occues in mp when uplay decided to disconnect you automatically during game and its quite annoying but thanfully thats just on the mp side of the things.
You can crafy syringes to enhance your abilites and skin animals to upgrade carrrying ammo, extra guns and special bows.There are also some dlc missions which are quite good if you have them, blowing stuff up feels really rewarding and the enemy AI is really nice, they will try to flank you into the open they actively use grandes to make you go into open areas to kill you easily.The tagging system in FC3 really makes the stealth aspect very intriguing as you can tag the enemies observe their pattern to quitely assassinate them or set animals on them. The takedown feature is probably the best feature ive seen in video games reason being the variety of takedown you can perform, from the simplet takedown to chain,gunslinger,death from above/below, heavy and grande, each does something differnet and feels really satisfying.
Lastly the audio is really crispy and on point, some of the soundtracks are spot on the one instance where you light a weed farm on fire with flamethrower has skillrex's ft. damien marely make it bun dem is brilliant and become my faveourite track, you can hear the hissle of snakes and the roars of the tigers from a distance giving you audio feedback as how to approach your immediate surronding.
Overall an excellent open world game by ubisoft and truly back to the Far Cry roots and a step in the right direction since i considered FC2 a failure, FC3 is a game anyone can easily love and sink hours into you can spend anywhere between 20-40 hours doing all kinds of things, I completed all outposts and towers and many of the missions and still wanted to play for an hour or so coz travelling with the wingsuit was so darn fun.Easily recommeded to anyone at any price point.

Mount & Blade: Warband is my second most played game so I thought it was appropriate that I make a review.
Mount & Blade as a series is good but I would argue that Warband is the best. Warband captures a unique playstyle in which your AI units are not commpletely helpless. In a lot of other bot reliant games, I see that you always have to clean up after your bots and they can't really do anything on their own. In Warband, I could easily stroll around in the back of the map while my soldiers win for me. Even though I do not play so much as I used to, this is a game I play for the relaxing factor of single player.
After playing a fair bit of single player, I moved on to multiplayer. Warband has one of the most brutal transitions from single to multiplayer that I have ever experienced. Single player is quite tame compared to multiplayer and you will die over and over unless you adapt to multiplayer. Albeit it is very difficult and only a few can master multiplayer, I still find it quite rewarding..

It runs pretty rough on my rig. I work for a computer company. I use my rig to virtualize entire small business environments with ease. I can play pretty much any game, including BF4 on ultra settings. I have up-to-date drivers. Really, I would comfortably say I'm well above average in knowing how to configure a computer to run a video game. That being said, I know when something is poorly optimized. This game is not optimized for AMD hardware. If you have a higher-end intel chip, and a really decent graphics card, then you should be fine. This is dissapointing, as the game isn't all that impressive graphically, so it goes to show that the dev's simply aren't interested in providing a better experience across all platforms. AMD does everything I want it to at a fraction of the price, and the only time performance is poor, is in games where dev's won't take the time to better optimize their games for a wider range of hardware.
So, my experience will be vastly different than someone who can play the game without issues. When the game was performaning well, I found it to be underwhelming in almost all categories. I found myself going back to BF3, BFBC2, and Insurgency. If you can snag it on sale for 15 bucks, the campiagn may be worth it if you can get it to run properly.

After a catastrophic worldwide event, the city of Seattle has been overtaken by the infected—shadows in the game, zombies to the rest of us—and you set out in search of your family as one of the few remaining survivors. If you've played The Walking Dead, then you're no doubt familiar with this very scenario.
Deadlight is a sidescrolling, survival horror platformer with plenty of zombies coming after your brains.  Armed with a hatchet and gun, you'll run, jump, climb, push crates, take the occasional zombie's head off, push more crates, and do it all over again.  Extremely simple, completely linear, demands minimal skill from the player and is very generous with checkpoints.
The game is laid out as brief stages where your completion time and collectibles found are recorded.  You may replay them at any time from the main menu to aim for 100% and better times on the leaderboards.  Cutscenes and voice acting are so cringeworthy you'll want to skip them, but the environments look great and set the scene properly.  Deadlight takes around four hours to 100%, supports gamepad, and won't impress you but is worth playing through for something quick and mindless.
If you're already thinking about buying this just do it. =)
