Ok so this is going to be a very long review.
Let me start with the positive points:
-great gameplay
-great concepts
-awesome graphics
- innovative mechanisms ( phone , boltcutters etc)
This game has a very high potential to become one of the best zombie games out there, but as I said it : POTENTIAL.
For the moment being, this game has a nice surface but a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ core.
Contagion looks fantastic but the lacking features which are a must have for such a COOP heavy game are pretty scare in my opinion.
Here are the negative points to explain my view:
- questionable hit boxes ( often times shooting with a gun to the direct head of a zombie is sometimes more random than skill)
- not enough ammo
- no "tutorial" or easy level to get  new people started
- randomized maps
- not many maps ( it's normal for a beta I guess)
- no "through the wall" zombie vision
Alright, let's start with the ammo problem and combine it with the randomized maps.
The ammo on the maps is WAY too little for the amount of players.
Since this game is in a beta stage and a lot of new people are currently joining in, it's very very hard to coordinate around the maps, even harder to search ammo while watching ones♥♥♥♥♥not to be bitten from behind.
The randomized map constructions are a nice thing, no doubt, but applying that one a map so little and complicated to manoveur like the one with the jail is a shot in ones own foot.
It makes the map impossible to get around with and the lack of ammo makes players explore the map even more, which often leads to people splitting completly up and everyone being alone , thus ending up eaten in 3 mins without even getting to first objectives.
The maps which exist are for most part easy on the surface,such as the neighbourhood one, but on the other hand a labirinth ( the jail). It would have been nice to develop a basic survival or objective map which is easy to find the objectives with and not too hard to navigate without a map and decent common sense. ( the umbrella map from ZPS for example)
As for the hitboxes, it may be only me , but considering I have a pretty decent ping and FPS, I don't think I can blame my aim for not hitting the heads since I am a long yeared FPS - Gamer.
The zombies not having a "through the wall" vision like in L4D is not something neccessary, but it would help zombies find the survivors easier since zombies don't have it any easier to navigate the maps than the survivors.
The shooting sounds of the guns are unreliable to the distance and location and thus don't really help THAT much.
It would be nice to let the zombies have a 5 meter range through the wall vision or something similar.
Alright, this is my review so far.
I am ready to accept change and fixes, but for the moment, I have a rather negative experience with this game.

I bought this game because I saw an LP of it and really enjoyed what I'd seen.
So, Mount & Blade: Warband is an open-world medieval sandbox role-playing game.  You name your character, select your backstory, and select your starting location, and you get dropped into the world and can do pretty much whatever you want.  Do you want to become a vassal in one of the existing kingdoms?  How about start your own kingdom?  Find a claimant to a kingdom's throne and help them rise to power?  Or how about being a trader, or bandit?  You can do any of those.
The graphics are a bit dated, yes, but it's a blessing in disguise.  Since the graphics are less demanding, there can be a ton of stuff happening on screen while you're in battle.  Once you build your army up, battles can be very large, so much so that there's actually an option to limit their size.  All of this means that the game will run smoothly regardless of how beefy your computer is.
Combat can take a bit of getting used to, but the weapon variety and combat system combined allows for a variety of different ways to fight.  Once you get the hang of things you can slice guys up or fill them full of arrows all day every day.
The only true downside is that the beginning of the game can be a bit rough.  If you don't play your cards right you can end up in an endless cycle of losing battles, being taken prisoner, having your money and supplies stolen, and not really having enough money, equipment, or allies to continue.  I would recommend buying land in a city to open up a factory of one or another variety as quickly as possible.  This will get you a steady stream of income, and then you can follow suit in other cities and eventually money becomes way less of an issue.  Participating in tournaments and placing bets on yourself can also net you some extra money.
Mount & Blade: Warband is an excellent game, and is definitely worth the money.

I give this game an 8/10. (Single-player only; I have not touched multi-player.)
I disliked Far Cry 2 because it was repetitive and seemed like an exercise in futility--with entire enemy camps respawning in what seemed like no time. I stopped playing about 6 hours into Far Cry 2. But I read good reviews of Far Cry 3, bought it cheap a while back, and just recently played it. For a while, I thought it might be just more of the same.
But I can tell you the exact moment I discovered I was having a hell-of-a-time playing Far Cry 3. for some reason, I had started liberating camps one by one from the pirates, usually by stealth with the sniper rifle, but sometimes by brute force. I came to this one small camp with about six guards fairly tightly bunched up in the yard. I stealthed up a ladder to the top of a building to take out the lone sniper that was covering the camp. How to take out the rest of the pirates? I noticed that there was a caged tiger in the camp. I could use that to even the odds a little against the other pirates, so I shot open the cage. Even if it killed one or two of them, that would make my job easier. I watched from my hiding place as the angry tiger took out one of the pirates. Then two. Then--holy crap--it took out a third as they were shooting at it. Then a fourth. That tiger managed to kill all the remaining pirates and liberate the camp for me! And lucky for me, he couldn't climb the ladder to my safe little hiding place. As I turned to watch the incoming Rakyat, to see if they would mop up that tiger for me--I felt myself being mauled in the back by an angry, wounded tiger! Unbeknownst to me there was, on the other side, a happy tiger STAIRWAY up to the top of the building I was perched upon. With only a shred of health left, I quickly turned and shot the tiger with the few remaining bullets in my clip. Lol. I will never forget that moment.
So yeah, I fully enjoyed this game. Some high points were doing hunter quests to craft better bags, some of the intense combat set pieces, tomb-raider-esque puzzle solving, and, of course, sniping enemy camps. Stand-out performance by Michael Mando as Vaas. Negatives: The inventory system is crap. And towards the end I felt like I was accumulating lots of money with nothing really to buy. The story was totally implausible, and I despised the whiny rich white kid protagonist and his whiny rich white kid friends. Ugh. The Citra ending is pretty much what this kid deserves.
Doubt I will be buying another Far Cry game since it looks like it's become a money grab with more-of-the-same. But I admit I enjoyed playing Far Cry 3.

I was gonna try to explain what Warband is, but you could probably figure it out faster by watching a video or two on the combat, and a video or two on the overland map and item managements.
Chances are, if you're looking at Reviews, you're wondering if the game is worth it for what it does and what price tag is on it.
The answer, as easily reflected by my (low, as a result of offline play) play time, is yes. The game is highly addictive, and you quickly learn to make your own goals for yourself within the world of Kalradia. I often found myself saying "Ok, now I'll do this thing so I'm at a good point and get off here for a bit." repeatedly until three more hours had passed.
And even if you somehow grow bored or are disappointed with a facet of the base game, the modding community is ambitious, and can easily breathe as much life into the game as you want to pull out of it.
Mount & Blade: Warband receives a full 9.5/10 in my book.

This 2.5D platformer gives off the impression of suspense, horror, puzzles and quick reflexes that's packed in one neat little package. The game forces trial or error, which forces you to learn through dying. This game does well in rendering the game 3D but playing out as a platformer, you'd see zombies crawling towards you from the background as you dash to the streets or running across roof tops as the city is burning down. The gameplay has quirky and clunky control so you wouldn't feel too fluid controlling Randall, you'd find yourself dying from judging too quickly the distance between jumps or sometimes for no apparent reason. The music fits well with the gameplay, the story seems solid and the voice acting is above average. The game is about six hours for most people.
Pro(s)
- Graphics is great
- Music fits mood
- Alternative ending
- Zombies
Con(s)
- Clunky control
- Random death
- Nightmare mode is stupidly hard (beat game in one sitting without dying)
Score: 7/10

You won't find the COD gang here, that's for sure. This game takes a complete, well-rounded, player to be good at. The fighting is intense, to say the least. Every weapon, whether it's a sword, axe, mace, staff, bow, knife or crossbow, is incredibly unique in how it's used. The fighting mechanics are better than any game I've seen thus far. That, of course, is my personal opinion. But how can you go wrong with a game where you actually need to take your sword, and hold it in the area that you are being swung at in order to block? Very few games are able to pull that off correctly. This one does.
Even on top of the nearly perfect combat/multiplayer system, there is an open-world, medieval, RPG to be played.
There are areas that a definitely left for improvement, but they achieve this without making terrible errors. For these reasons, it is one of my top three favorite games of all time. And I cannot wait for the sequal to arrive: Bannerlord.

My hours should show you my feelings about the game. But I'll expand:
Negative points:
- Weird glitches get annoying sometimes. I've had this problem where sometimes, completely randomly, my weapon will disappear for a second and then immediately come back. You can't fire during this time. That's one of a number of glitches, although small, that
- The hardest difficulty isn't that difficult. I ended up using the Gun Realism mod so the enemies actually hit you with the same damage as you hit them with. It actually makes being faced with a car-mounted machine gun a challenge if you're not armed with an RPG.
Amazing points:
- Excellent gunplay. It's what I base my ratings of other games' gumplay off of. It's great fun and even more with the Gun Realism mod.
- Good story. I don't play games for the story, but FC3's story was pretty good. I don't get the complaints about the fact that Jason acts like he's never fired a gun before in a mission after arriving with an LMG and a grenade launcher. It's a game and unless you wanted to be stuck doing stealth or something for the first few hours of the game that's what you've got to deal with.
- For a game from 2012, it doesn't feel that dated. Probably not an issue for many, but for me it would be.
Get it while it's on sale. It's so worth $7.48. Heck, I'd go to say that it's worth $29.99. Or the original $80 I paid at the start.

The story of this game is very very good. Right from the first mission, you start to sympathise with the main character. You basically develop from an innocent youngster into a survival machine. As the player you really do want to complete the missions and try to save Jasons friends. This makes the game very addicting and makes you want to play through the campaign quickly. However, there are many side objectives that are worth doing and give rewards that make the missions a bit easier (by getting access to more guns cheaply).
After only a couple of hours playing the game, I'm already hooked. I might just buy the other Far Cry games out there, because they definitely seem worth it.
Update after finishing the game:
The story started out really strong, dipping in the middle. This might have to do with my playstyle rather than the story however. I decided to do a lot of the side game stuff, like capturing outposts, upgrading my bags, etc. This isn't completely useless though. Capturing outposts 'captures' areas and you will be less likely to run into enemies. Upgrading bags is obvious, but takes quite a bit of time.
Things get really spicy when you meet Citra. This chick looks amazing and her model looks pretty sick. The character development during these quests is really good. The combat gets a little repetitive, but that's with any shooter I suppose.
The most annoying quests were with Buck (who likes to ♥♥♥♥ xD), so I guess the voice actor and writers did their job well on that part.
Just like the strong start, the ending is pretty strong too.
Overall, I'd still recommend the game. If you like to do the stuff like outposts, do it while you're in the area for the main questline, instead of hoarding and doing them all together. Otherwise, doing just the main questline is pretty good too.
8/10

Deadlight is an amazing little game that could've used a little more polish. Let me explain: the game plays like a platformer. It's all 2.5D by the way, so everything is in 3D, but the gameplay itself is restricted to a 2D plane.
Now, the graphics are nothing short of amazing. It's some of the best art I've ever seen. It's bloody brilliant.
The voice acting is alright. Some of the characters could've used a little more emotion at times. It's a place filled with zombies, damn it, so act like it !
The story will keep you interested until the end, which most of us will reach in 3-5 hours, depending on if you're collecting and searching everything.
So, so far it's all good. But near the end you'll be dying an awful lot. And not the good, challenging-kind of dying, but the occasionally-unresponsive-controls-kind of dying. There's one scene I must have done literally about 20 times. It. Was/Is. Infuriating.
But despite this flaw I would still highly recommend it to all zombie fans out there.
[Rating: 82/100]

Second of my apocalyptic double tonight is 'Deadlight'
A 80's style and setting, old school platformer very similar to the original Prince of Persia and Another World/Flashback and the more modern Limbo.
So we have a side scrolling 2D platformer set in a very serious very bleak setting. It paints a grim zombie infested world with a direct nod to George Romero's earlier dead trilogy. There's no comedy here. And the sheer level of detail in the gorgeous visuals really really hit home the hopelesness of it all. The backgrounds are beautifully drawn and animated. The soundtrack and ambient effects are top notch too. A really fantastic atmophere it all creates.
Some nice collectibles to be found also. And there a full set of making of videos and early artwork. Lots of 80's stuff and an explanation of why the game was set in the 80's :) Worth looking through it if you buy the game.
I totally recommend it!
PS all of the achievements are named after hit songs from the 80's :)

Heroes & Generals is what World War II Online should have been. I wish they hadn't gone with a micro-transaction model though. It ruins the experience for the rest of the players who want to earn their way.

This is a great game. The Heroes side runs similarly to Battlefield, where you and your team (up to 20 on each side) of infantry, paratroopers, tank crews, fighter pilots, and recon fight for control of map objectives. The Generals side runs like an RTS game where you purchase Assault Teams which are made up of inf, para, armor, planes, etc and you send them around the map of Europe to fight for your faction (atm only US for Allies and Germany for Axis). This is a very fun concept because the Assault teams which the Generals are sending around to different battles directly effect the Heroes side of the game, such as the number of spawns each team has and which types of soldiers are avilable. The game is still in Beta so there are still some bugs to be fixed (mainly hit-detection and vehicle physics imo) but the game is still a lot of fun! It can be frustrating to fight a battle which you will certainly lose (example you have 22 inf spawns and they have 300 and also have tanks) howeve sometimes halfway through the battle a friendly General sends you paratroopers and recon and more infantry spawns and you end up winning the match. Overall, I recommend the game because its free to play (devs do try really really hard to get you to buy gold, and I must admit a Veteran membership is worth it if you want to level up twice as fast) and because its in Beta it should only be getting better! GO USA!

An utter disgrace to the PC and Call of Duty community. Previous to Call of Duty: Ghosts, I was a huge fan of the Call of Duty series. Black Ops 2 was, in my opinion, the best Call of Duty in a long time. I was excited to see how Infinity Ward would raise the bar even higher. Not only did Infinity Ward not raise the bar, they completely tripped and slammed their head against it like that poor disabled boy you felt sorry for in primary school. At first glance during the weeks until release, the game looked promising, but I soon discovered otherwise after installing the game, which took over an hour to do, over 4 physical discs, and 60GBs of my precious hard drive space. Call of Duty: Ghosts is a poorly optimised utter piece of garbage. It shouldn't even be classified as a game. The game suffers from constant FPS drops and stutter, even at low graphics settings. I bumped the graphics as high as possible, regardless of FPS, to see how the game looked at it's best. Even at the highest graphics settings, this game looks like someone had used shutterstock images ripped straight from Google Images. Due to the fact that I was using an SLI configuration for my PC, the game decided that it should constantly annoy me by flickering many essential textures, such as the sights on my gun. After complaining about this issue to activision support, they informed me that they would release a patch shortly, which never happened. Whether or not that issue has been fixed at the time of writing this review, I wouldn't know, as I even refuse to update a game this poor in quality. Another fun fact about the patches is that they take up even MORE space, and barely fix anything. Infinity Ward didn't even bother putting a simple feature like a field of view changer, which is essential for PC gamers. The only way to change the FOV is to download an unofficial mod, which Infinity Ward will ban you for using. Even when disregarding the technical issues with this game, it is still a terrible game. Campaign is stale and boring, and multiplayer on the PC version only has an average of 2000 players, most of which camp in corners and use IEDs instead of their guns. Extinction mode isn't bad, but gets boring really fast. I even spotted an Xbox One button icon in one of the menus whilst playing Extinction mode, which is proof that Infinity Ward never even bothered to make a decent port of the game. All they did was make the Xbox One version of the game playable with a mouse and keyboard.
In closing, Infinity Ward and Activision have slapped together THE WORST CALL OF DUTY GAME EVER KNOWN TO MAN, charged their customers large amounts of money for a product equivelant to that of the matter that falls out from a dog's behind, and overhyped the innocent Call of Duty community with promises that they couldn't even keep, such as dedicated servers, HD graphics and ongoing support.
If you are a Call of Duty fan, DO NOT BUY THIS GAME. Instead, wait for Treyarch (the one true Call of Duty developer) to clean up Infinity Ward's mess when they release their next Call of Duty title.

This game is sweet. A lot of other people are bashing the game because of the pay 2 win and grind, but check this out:
You will be able to unlock almost every class of soldier and also a good majority of the guns and special upgrades in around 100 hours of gameplay.
As far as I'm concerned, I wouldn't want to pay because moving up the ranks is really fun. You can be a tank driver pretty quick as it's the first class you can unlock. It's true that you have to pay for ammo and also for rockets, etc. But even with paying for all that, you're still looking at around 100 hours to unlock most of what you want.
The real secret to this game is sound. If you use headphones or a surround sound system, you don't need great guns to win. You just need to drive real crazy (so the snipers can't hit you) and listen for guys around outside and anticipate them entering while you capture objectives. I've made easily over 100 melee kills and you HARDLY EVER see anyone use melee weapons so you just have to know how much sound you're making and also you need to know when to fight inside and when you go outdoors. Grenades and melee are VASTLY under-used in this game. You need to get used to switching weapons and being very tactical - this is not Call of Duty. This is the game that people play who don't like people who play Call of Duty.
I would say this is DEFINITELY the best free to play game out there.
Some people in their reviews forget that these people who make this game have to feed themselves and their families. I might spend some money for this game JUST TO SUPPORT THE DEVS, but I actually do not need to spend any money at all.
I would say about 80% of games I am in the top 10 (out of 15-18) and I would say I am top of the board about 20% of the time. I have been playing FPS games for about 20 years, but I would not really consider myself THAT good. I'm just REALLY REALLY aggressive. If you like to be terrifically aggressive then you will not need to spend any money.

I've been playing FPS games my whole life and this game reminds me a lot of the ORIGINAL Battlefield 1942. It's basically exactly the same game. Like Operation Flashpoint. You can crouch, go prone, drive planes, drive APCs, drive tanks, etc.
You have to be quiet, stay out of sniper fire, drive like a psycho and dodge tanks - people always make a big deal out of tanks but you seriously can just drive around them most of the time.
The people who play this game are generally clueless. Don't expect ANY coordination or help from anyone. Expect them to be lost in the woods for the sniper that killed them 20 minutes ago while all your points are being captured and you are being crushed by tanks and snipers.

Okay first off good game. Has potential and is fun. It's not perfect though so here for your INFORMED decision is the pros and cons.
Pros:
1. Easy UI - controls are simple and the interfaces are straight forward. You will easily slip into how the game works if you've played ANY shooter before.
2. Realistic combat - You're not a walking fridge and you are not shooting rocket propelled bullets (out side of rocket launchers). Combat is challanging because of this but also rewarding giving you a feeling of true joy when you survive a bullet and making you THINK before attacking.
3. LARGE MAPS, while the intro maps aren't that big most of the maps are giant and make use of the diverse roles players can take.
4. Role Diversity. - So rarely do classes actually make a difference. Here they do. Tank operators play differently then pilots, soldiers function differently from scouts, ect. They all have ACTUAL ups and downs.
5. Proper Vehicle playing. - With the exception of early light tanks and light vehicles most heavy vehicles require more the one person to operate all the guns. Medium and heavy tanks require multiple players operating them to man every gun on them. A feature usually over complicated OR just left out in other games.
6. Easy match making.
7. Balancing Money spending items. - While you can buy your way to higher ranks quickly they balanced it by locking in those classes. If you BUY your rank in a tank operator or a pilot that character can NOT switch jobs. Only players who worked and earned their ranks can switch jobs on a character.
Cons:
1. Slow lvling - While the first few levels come fairly easily ranking up soon becomes SLOW and sluggish. However not to the point that you will overly suffer.
2. No rank memory - If you transfer a soldier the ranking xp doesn't save it seems. So don't transfer too often. That is a major annoyance.
3. Over-Priced Item Mall - While almost everything in the game item wise (and all core aspects of characters) can be reached without spending money it is quite a bit slowed.
4. Redundant missions - Yup there's not that big of a map diversity at the moment and only a few kind of engagement types so it gets a bit repetative.
At the end of the day the game is fun and you don't have to drop cash to actually play it. It's worth trying if nothing else.

Graphics: 3/5
Not the prettiest game out there but:
Gameplay: 4/5
Made up for with some fantastic gameplay. The first Tier 1 missions can feel like a slog at first as they get a bit redundant, but once you get to the bigger maps, it's much more interesting. i will say the map diversity is limited; you never get the feel for different locations in europe with the same 4 or so maps that are recycled. These are big maps, though, and the experience can be very different depending on the disposition of forces. Weapons are well balanced and realistic for the most part (although the damage system is quite forgiving). Gameplay can be very rewarding, especially when mixed unit types come into play. Players are rewarded with points and credits for teamwork, particularly so when it comes to actually capturing objectives.
Interface: 2/5
It's extremely difficult to communicate and team up with your friends. There are a lot of limitations; for example, you can't modify your loadout or mix and match unit types in a squad (I cant team up with my infantry friends when I run a tank). It also stinks that you cant pull your guy out of a match once you're in. Matches can run as long as a half hour so it can be irritating if you are trying to join up with friends.
P2W: 5/5
This game is by no means pay to win. If you don't mind a bit of grinding, you can unlock and mod great weapons and vehicles without dropping dough (I frequently top the charts and have yet to spend a dime) and be perfectly competitive.
Overall:
4/5
This is a solid game for a free-to-play; if you are a WWII/FPS fan, I definitely recommend checking it out.
A word to the developers:
Please improve the menu interface. This is by far the worst part of the game. Add some more diverse map locales, like north africa for instance, a dense urban setting, or a beach invasion (a la Battlefield 1942 style). Let me choose if I want to skirmish or fight control point battles. Keep up the good work!
Disclaimer: I have never played the strategic portion of this game; this review is strictly with regards to the "Heroes" portion.

I loved this game. It's one of the few games that played well on my underpowered laptop.
You recruit soldiers to fight for you and use that group to take over towns, cities and fight other lords. The big thing you have to worry about is going against a powerful lord and having your group of hundreds of soldiers completely wiped out in one battle, losing hours of recruitment in the process. The gameplay can get a little tedious outside of the battles. A lot of fetch this-escort that quests for extra cash, but the game does have an economy system where you can invest in industries to earn money.
I think the biggest strength of this game is its multiplayer. Imagine battles of 30-50 people fighting with swords and bows. I have countless memories of storming castle walls using siege ladders with a dozen teammates, only for all of us to be mowed down by the 3-4 guys at the top with polearms.  It's a huge amount of fun. But the game is four years old, so there are only a few vanilla servers left with a sizable population.
But I'd definitely recommend this game. It's a huge amount of fun.

First of all, i would like to address my time spent with this game. I do not own the game on this account. I just happened to have a friend who bought one, who let me try it out. All of this was before steam family sharing. Otherwise, i spent about 6 hrs with the singleplayer and 20 hrs in multiplayer.
Now to the game itself. Call of Duty Ghosts is the 10th game in the franchise, released in november 2013.
One thing i want to mention is of the game's requirements. They ask too much, yet don't really make it look better than Battlefield for example, which clearly shows that no effort was put into optimization of the game.
The game is of very poor quality and optimization wasn't the only victim. The sounds aren't all that great too.
That surely isn't the way a game that makes billions of dollars a year should be. I actually don't even remember the guns in COD sounding that bad.
The campaign lasted 4 hours, and it was one of the worst plots i ever seen.
The main enemy in this game are not muslims or russians, but latinos. In this game, all of the Latin America is united under one nation. They launch a secret attack on US, where they hijack a satellite of some sort that is armed with missiles. All the major cities are practically bombarded, sending US to the stone age.
The game starts 10 years later and surprisingly, USA is still fighting. Their cities are now just craters. All the major factories are probably destroyed too. How is there still resistance? How do they get their ammunition? Where do they repair any damage done to their armored vehicles? The setting is supposed to be post apocalyptic for USA, but none of what you are looking at makes it feel that way.
The whole story revolves around US resistance - guerrilla warfare, but like i said, it never feels that way. Games like homefront for example, actually worked hard on showing those elements.
The story is simply awful, and it's because of garbage like that COD isn't taken seriously anymore. Other than that it's your typical linear shooter.
Unlike the previous installment - Black Ops 2, the game doesn't provide you with branching stories, or allows to customize loadouts for your missions or even use perks in singleplayer.
The only good thing was probably the mission variety. There were a few well done levels, like the underwater level, the car chase on ice, the skyscraper level.
As for multiplayer, it was
. Here is why.
First of all, no one was playing at release on pc. As i said, it had very irrational game requirements, which might have swayed a lot of the crowd from their game.
But here is the real reason why you will experience lag. When looking for a match, the game will have a max ping value of 800. Overall, since COD is usually played in 6v6, you are not gonna find a lot of free slots. Usually, from most multiplayer games that i played, the server autokicks after you reach 300.
To fix that you actually need to go to the config files and change the value to something smaller. Even so, i doubt you are gonna have a pleasant experience. The game also doesn't even have a ping indicator.
If we put this aside, we get another broken COD experience. In multiplayer all that matters is balance and content. The factors that can affect the balance are the maps, the spawns, and the damage dealt from guns/killstreaks.
Majority of the assault rifles in the game deal 40-50 damage per hit. The value was increased a bit compared to earlier CODs, like COD4, where are the typical damage was 30-40. The time to kill was always very short in COD, but toning the damage down a bit won't hurt. In BF4, the max damage most assault rifles can deal is 25. That means at least 4 hits are required to kill your target. Not saying for them to just completely copy BF, but COD4 was much more balanced when it came to that.
Enough about damage though, cause other elements are just as bad. Revenge spawns from MW3 are back. You can view a few examples of those in my MW3 review.
I kind of liked the maps, but here is another problem. You are playing in a 6v6 and the maps are huge. What's worse is, how do you mess up the spawns with maps that big?
Consists of Survival from MW3 and a new mode called Extinction.
Survival was the only fun you could have in MW3, and was a great alternative to Treyarch's Zombies. Unfortunately, it was ruined in COD Ghosts.
You play survival on multiplayer maps, and those huge maps actually fit pretty well. The maps have a lot of buildings, most of which give you the ability to access every floor. There are plenty of very high vantage points.
The new killstreaks fit survival pretty well too, like the one where you fly on a Little Bird as a side gunner. Survival even increased its player cap, allowing 4 players now. Unfortunately, it suffers from being dumbed down.
First of all, the enemies can withstand way too much damage, like it takes 2 headshots with a pistol to kill one. Enemy's health needs to be rebalanced. Just like in Nazi Zombies, enemies get stronger the more waves you finish, but you have to do it gradually, not from the very start.
Second problem is that the mode was removed of its money system. Now you get you killstreaks, perks, weapons randomly. During or after waves your will be sent a few care packages, spread out throughout the map. What's funny is that recently i played Battlefront beta, and it featured a mode just like that. Pretty much the same thing, except with finite amount of waves, and sometimes they will send a package on some random spot on the map.
This is where all the fun of Ghosts comes from.
The concept of it, is that you have a drill, and there are these hives that block the way and they must be drilled. When you start drilling aliens will try to destroy the drill.
Unlike the survival, this one actually has money system, and there are killstreaks, weapons to spend them on. Also it has a separate leveling up system, giving you access to different killstreaks, classes, perks.
Unlike zombies, aliens don't get tougher every wave, they mostly increase in numbers and sometimes new aliens types get introduced.
Also during the drilling, you will be given a challenge, if you complete it, you will be awarded with an upgrade point for you character. You can upgrade your gun, get different types of bullets, maybe increase your health.
This mode even features a health bar. It regenerates, but it's aesthetically nice.
The only drawback is that there is only 1 level in the vanilla game. Meanwhile, in survival you can play a total of 14 maps.
Well, i hope i convinced you to avoid COD Ghosts. The story is complete nonsense. The multiplayer is unbalanced and
dead. The survival mode was ruined, and the only good mode left only features 1 map.

I love the concept for this game but in execution it just doesn't live up to my expectations, but that's not necessarily a deal breaker seeing as the game is currently still in Beta.
If they can shore up the matchmaking, allow you to more easily party up with friends (instead of forcing both to manually join the same server and role the dice that you both get in), and shore up the gameplay I think this game could be very solid.
As it stands right now I'll give it a 4/10, with the potential to get up to a nice 7/10 depending on how the developers progress through beta.
In conclusion: cool concept albeit poorly executed thus far, match finding system is fodder, weapon responsiveness needs tuning. Lot of potential, fate of the game is determined by how hard the developers work to handle everything in Beta.
I do not currently recommend this game, but that could very easily change in the near future.

Short review.
WW2 Arcade game, looks ok empty maps. Fairly meh. Grind.
Longer review- Based mainly on Spaatz build. Action game only played . Cannot comment on the strategic game.
Once upon a time the devs spoke about realism & that it was constant influence in the development. That time has long since past and COD has a bigger influence. Good or bad thing is up to you. Sure some people will cry beta ! but if this game is beta then it's in development hell. At this point in the development tweaks & final polish should be added not still working on getting basic functions up to scratch.
Controls - fairly std shooter layout but no lean function or cover function either. No toggle functions except for prone. Though with crouching barely being faster than prone it's not too often you will use it. Oddly you can pick up more weapons but cannot drop them. Another odd thing, you cannot change your settings unless in a match.
Sound - Pretty poor. It doesnt sound like a battle at all. Weapon sounds are underwhelming, muffled with no real rapport & no where near loud enough.  Added to that sound is patchy, amount of times a tank has sneaked up behind me or have been shot by a rifle 50m & never heard the shot. It also feels very localize, anything more than 100m is not heard.
Interface sounds can get irratating after a while & some maps have music playing from tannoys which can be very loud compared to other sounds, neither can be switch off. Sound options are limted to simply music and sfx.
Graphics - Not too bad stylised rather than realistic things look. Feel as they should but a bit too clean. Optimization could be a lot better & the fog effect could use some rework, some maps give victoriain London a run for its money, on a clear day the fog creeps in at 100m & often everything just feels too muted or too brown because of it. A proper foggy day though does look rather good & adds some atmosphere that is far too often lacking from the game.  Objects do look like they have been plonked on the ground rather than be a part of it & interiors are sterile; shell hole in roof but someone nice enough to clear up after it for instance, more debris & wear is needed to make things feel more like locations rather than a collection of assests. Muzzle flash is a hit & miss affair & dont expect to see it at range with any consistancy, a tank can fire its main gun & you would not know unless you are close to it. Same goes for smoke.
Models themselves are pretty good though with a good amount of detail, the theme is very much historyish than historical.
Fov slider is present huzzah! but the game has a odd fov. I use a widescreen & have mine on Hoz 95 on most games. Do that on here & everything gets stretched & your avatar ends up with 5ft long arms
One thing I must note is there is no over the top bloom. So many modern games use it cheaply, this game does not.
The UI is ok & normally quite clear but can get cluttered on multi objective missions with no way to turn it off.
Infantry animations currently are a mismatch.  Players seem to iceskate areound the place like drunks & the gait does not match the speed. Rather than have a speed up mechanic it has a delayed reaction one instead hence the ice & it does give the feeling you are not fully in control. Added to that the movement bob is rather lewd not side to side as you may expect more forward & back to the degree that if you toggle iron sight and move it looks like you character is having it off with their weapon.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
FTP game so a section on the pricing model.
For me I dont mind games that allow you pay some cash & get things quicker. Games are a business however we feel and their purpose is about earning money but I dont like blatant P2W or gouging in general. Does H&G do this ?
Well apx £15 will get you 90 days veterans (vip) & if you bought the £40 package that would leave you 7700 gold to buy things with. This is not that much if you want to speed ahead . Guns can range from 200 to 2000+ gold  a ranked up soldier can set you back 11546 for a General 2846 for a Major to apx 1300 gold for a private depending on the class.
Now remember this is one soldier, the way the game plays you are likely to have several so costs could easily mount up if you pay to speed ahead.  One aspect I dont like about the veteran pack is the extra badge you can use. In short a veteran will always have an advantage over a non veteran as its the only way to get this.
How bad is the grind without veteran status?  A average player will have to play a lot of games to get into the higher levels. Capping & defending is the highest xp, which in my mind is a good thing. Infantry kills are a low rate , with spotting been the lowest at apx 2-3 xp. One issue with the system is the cap zone is tiny given the size of the maps & getting defense kills is hard for instance as its best to not even let the enemy get in the cap zone to begin with.
Currency comes in two flavours. Gold ; real money and in game money. Credits for action game , warfunds for strategic game. the player is rewarded for getting a higher rank with a salary per match that you play 50% or more of. The issue here is the match maker will often put you in matches where that is not achevable as the match is one that is already started and sometimes due to the way teams are worked out you will have to quit the game without earning a thing as your assigned formation gets wiped out. Even with this quirk a non vet play can earn a fair amount of credits over time so the end items are in reach though it is still a long reach. Buy and customizing 1 gun can set you back 250k and more easlily while earnings can be in the 2-10k mark depending on rank and if salary actually works.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Gameplay-
If you join a non training match , the match can be uneven as it is based on what a general is doing on the campaign map in your selected campaign. Training matches try to balance things out.
You start off only being able to do skimish maps these are smaller maps with up to 3 objectives & a limit to usable items. Once leveled up you move onto the bigger map & able to use more toys.  This really should be an upgrade but often feels hollow as the bigger maps are a good size, which is great , but they really need a large amount of players to make them worthwhile, less than 20 a side on a 1k by 1k map doesnt work too well.
The matches work by capturing points but you need to cap them along the supply line shown or you cannot cap them. Some maps have multiple supply lines.
The maps are pretty open & even in the built up areas there is not a lot of cover, windows are either fully open or shut & cover is often at heights so you cannot crouch properly to minimize exposure. They don't feel designed to be fought over more like markers than anything.
Infantry play is run & gun. They move too fast & the penatlies for moving are minor. Auto weapons easily dominate. Sniping does work however but more for scope users.  LMG's can be hipfired without much trouble. There is a jump in the game & it gets all the typical abuse you would expect cue bunny hops to avoid been shot & skyrim horse physics.
Damage model is off- shoot a guy in the chest with a panzerfaust & wonder why it only wounded him as you bleed out.                            Get run over by a jeep, nothing happens to jeep despite it hitting the building you were using as cover.Grenades have very small radius & dont do much. You can also customize you weapon greatly changing it & adding to the power diff between new players & older. Need to be toned down along with the effect of badges.
A lot of work is needed to stop it been COD WW2 on big maps.

After a few years I have finally decided to share my opinion of this game and its development as a play tester (I'm the cop in the first screenshot ;) ).
This was my second early access purchase and the game started off promising. I was interested in because the same person behind Zombie panic! Source mod was behind this (although don't think this is ZPS 2) and in not much time found myself on the play testers team for Monochrome ltd. There were at least a dozen of us and we were all unpaid volunteers.
My experience with the game and as a play tester was going well. It was very enjoyable working with the developers and other play testers and the game appeared to be coming along smoothly.
Not a lot was happening in my life at that time so I spent a lot of time play testing contagion; logging bugs to be fixed and what have you. We would also attend skype meetings which were 3am my time and I even upgraded to a gaming desktop (although needed) bought on credit to continue to help play test when my laptop could no longer handle the game as it was in development and constantly being updated. Of course no one asked this of me, I am just trying to say that I really wanted to help this game and being the first time I playtested anything found it quite fun seeing behind the scenes of a game being made.
After a few months I started to notice bugs I had logged were being reported as fixed when they hadn't been and trying to talk to the CEO in skype meetings fell on deaf ears.
My final experience as a play tester was on one of our skype meetings (at 3am) in where the CEO joins and instantly starts slamming the staff and volunteer play testers for not promoting the game enough and in two weaks his new PR guy (that is paid) has done more work promoting the game than all of us put together.
I was shocked, first, the other play testers and I were volunteers and were meant to play test, Second, it wasn't in the other staff members job description, Third, we were never asked to promote the game and Fourth, I felt I had been putting in a lot of free work for this guy and he didn't show any appreciation, like a decent person would when you help them.
I stopped play testing immediately after that skype meeting but I did go back to the game when it was released and came out of early access just to see the result only to be met with disapointment and see that some bugs I had logged still remained. I believe it was released too soon.
The game soon after slowly died and the review section was met with a lot of unhappy customers, new, people who played throughout the early access period and even an ex employee, no doubt becuase of the actions of the CEO; which talking of reviews, for about a year he appeared to have a bit of a breakdown and was flagging and responding to nearly all negative reviews of the game. That now appears to have stopped. It is a shame as the game could have been great like ZPS was in its prime. I feel the developers did a good job with the game but ultimately it was let down by bad management and a the whole attacking negative reviewers fiasco didn't help his or the game's image. Maybe he should of kept that PR guy around a bit longer.
If you don't have any one to play with it probably isn't worth your time as multiplayer no consists of a few hundred people if you are lucky and single player is not so hot. I would say if you want to play something similar to this that was better recieved then go grab the free Zombie Panic Source mod.
PS. As I mentioned earlier, there were at least a dozen play testers however the CEO only felt the need to mention 2 of them in the credits... showing that appreciation again.

Gameplay dynamics in hunted is very interesting. Early on, emphasis is on getting supplies and staying alive, whereas the late game when most players are dead it turns into a multiplayer stealth game with the zombies hunting the humans. It can get tedious if you're a zombie, but that's the point - it's more fun to stay alive and is more rewarding for being so. The noise mechanic adds a layer of strategy with the phone. Using it to vibrate another player's phone will give their presence away, but by doing so will give away your proximity. Then again, if it happens to you - do you whip out your phone for a split second to hear where it came from, or do you keep your gun out so you're not vulnerable?

Far Cry 3 is one of the few big titles that has a decidedly adult taste to it right from the get-go, and manages to maintain a true action feel throughout the entire game. I'm a big proponent of using stealth if I ever have the choice, and Far Cry 3 delivers in spades with it's takedown mechanic and classic HUD. I did change the key bindings to suit how I like to play, however, and the only problem that seemed to result from this was unwanted grenade switching when using the mouse wheel to change guns.
The environments are varied and colourful (I'd say, similar to Dead Island but with slightly better textures), and I really enjoyed the positive boost to stealth provided by doing things at night. The explosions (of which there are many) were great, the voice acting was good for the key characters (not so much for the natives), and there are plenty of minigames to suit all the basic tastes. What I liked most about FC3 though, was that my stealth approach was broken up during the missions by plenty of "blow♥♥♥♥♥♥up", "torch that", "and kill them all with 50cal" moments, which is exactly what you would expect from a good action title.
My critiscisms are in no way game-breaking, and for the most part are just 1%'ers that would have made this game unforgettable for me. I don't know whethers it's because I got DLC with the pack I bought, but the pacing of difficulty with animals in the environment could probably have used a bit of work, as I was basically a God who Crocodiles could barely scratch by about half way through the game. There is basically no incentive to use guns without silencers, unless you're the kind of person who just really digs pressing the "r" button, as silenced weapons were no less powerful or accurate and in almost all cases were more effective that LMG's. It was too easy to unlock new areas and therefore new guns, which had the flow-on effect of my wallet constantly being full, and making looting redundant. I think FC2 was much more on the money (forgive me) when it came to the amount of cash that was floating around, and what you had to do to get it.
All-in-all though, an very enjoyable game that gave me 50+ hrs of gameplay for $5. Can't really argue with that can you?

Want to know how to win any game?  P2win to get a sniper rifle, then just harass bases to move forward.  That's it, any skills level, any map, just like that ^.
Tanks and planes don't do a thing as far as I can tell, as long as you have the all powerful sniper rifle you can make your team win any map, which gets you more in game cash to upgrade your stuff, to win more maps, etc, etc.
If you don't p2win, you're stuck at the other end of the sniper rifle.
Of course the game is too painfully unpolished to give a decent kill cam (a la TF2), so you can hunt down the sniper who got you.  Nope just got to hope you can make him out against muddy textures and contant lag.
As is the pattern with these sorts of games, a LOT of work has been put into the first few levels to sucker you in.  They're not too big, they have reasonable objects and they're actually fun.  But if you hit above T2 expect to get farmed by people who paid more than you; Because you know, God forbid you want to play the game.
It's not even if the enemies are just better.  I would routinely kill 4-5 in a group - as long as they weren't spaced a mile apart all sniping at me - and I'm not even that good.  Just skills left over from TF2 and the like; A real Free 2 Play game, that's actually worth your time.
On the rare occasion when I would die in a straight up fight with someone, it would usually be becuase they had a better gun.  That's right, just buy a better gun than what you start with and you're automatically better.  The Thompson (the first T3 gun you get, for a large invesment in time and in game currency) snipes better than a rifle and hits harder than other machines guns of its type.  I would routinely see anyone wielding a Thompson clean up with kills comparable to mine, when I would use an inferior machine gun.

Sense a theme?

This game provoked quite the reaction in me. And not because I couldn't do it (like that Slenderman thing I got hosed on) - I could do it all too easily - that was the problem...
...I hated this game. I marvelled at the graphics and the scenery and I was so excited to play it after Far Cry 2, which I had on the PS3 and loved. But Far Cry 3 was such a massive letdown for me. Why is my character smart enough to use sophisitcated assault weapons with all sorts of moving parts with no training, but so dumb he needs specific things to make a bag, instead of just equipping the awesome power of any old bit of cloth? Why can my character, still as aforementioned, untrained, hide in the long grass and ambush a ute full of armed-to-the-teeth baddies after only a few minutes game play, and confidently come out the winner after having slaughtered the lot of them? Why can my untrained character storm a compound full of said baddies and make it look like an angry Space Marine swept through by the time you're done picking over the multiple victims of this latest Ramboesque assault? Why, why, why? The crafting system annoyed me, the tourist-turned-Rambo thing annoyed me, the having to look for difficult to find things annoyed me. It was like the unnecessarily slow dipping mechanism in Austin Powers - what was the point of most of it? I got annoyed at this game quite easily, it seems.
I quit playing it and my enjoyment of it went through the roof. Suddenly, I found I was no longer annoyed at the game's poor design choices and woeful character dynamic. I'm only writing this because part of me is still irritated by it.
I just read on the WIkia about this that Jason Brody is naturally good with firearms. Riiight. Then I'm going to make a character naturally better with swords than the Kurgan. Just because. It's just so lazy and childish. Oh, and the Tatau. Let's not forget magic now. After Far Cry 2. Magic. Maybe magic is part of the Far Cry thing, but since I only played Far Cry 2 before this, I don't know, and perhaps I'm being unfair. But anyway, I hated it. And it's not often that I will actually come out and say that about anything, because I appreciate the sheer amount of work that went into making the finished product. Lots of people really loved this game, so it could just be me.
If you like having your character spend time on finding a specific type of animal to hunt, kill, then use its untanned skin to lovingly handcraft a POUCH (or small bag, as it's also called) while dodging myopic and suicidal enemies on a tropical island, while supposedly nursing yourself through riproaring psychological trauma at what happened to you in the game's intro, then this is the game for you. If you've got better things to do, like play Peggle, do them instead.

Heroes and Generals brings back alot of the magic that battlefield 1942 had back in the day, and alot of the problems as well.
The heroes part of the game is a fun fps reminiscent of much older fps titles. Anyone who played Battlefield 1942 or Battlefield 2, and to a lesser extent the newer battlefield series will reckognize how this game works pretty fast. Hit detection is solid with bullets having travel times and bullet drop, no windage which is good. Melee combat is in the game but is rather buggy (aim for their belts, not their torso!). The biggest draw back is there is not a very diverse maps list. While the game is fun to play in short bursts, playing on the same 7 maps gets boring.
Vehicles are ok, with shells needing to "penetrate" to deal damage. Sadly this penetration is solely based on angle of impact and will not travel past the first piece of armor hit. This means that occasionally shells will bounce for seemingly no reason when it looked like you had a very solid hit. The damage dealt is also not location dependent, rather a simple health bar which makes combat more aggrevating.
The last part of the Heroes component I will remark on is the progression. This game IS free to play, and you can unlock all weapons in the game for free. Items can be purchased with in game currency after you unlock them by progressing your soldier and unlocking achievements. These are all rather straight forward, get X kills with a rifle to unlock the next progression. Most of the primary weapons can further be upgraded with things like adjusted triggers, new barrels and sights, better springs and bolts and ammunition. I was able to purchase 2 soldiers, an smg, anti tank rocket launcher, anti tank mines and a tank within the first 20 hours of playing. With a single round lasting about half an hour that comes out to 40-50 games, which is abit slower than I would have liked.
The biggest downside to the progression is it is slow. I imagine if I had focused on a single soldier rather than 4 unique soldiers I would be about 1/2 to 3/4 of the way to unlocking the Generals component by now. That's 60 hours to unlock 1/2 of the game, abit extreme to be honest. Instead I focused on 4 soldiers so I could tailor them for different situations, standard infantry, cqb, anti tank and a tank driver. After 60 hours my highest ranking soldier is about 1/8th of the way to unlocking Generals, that is a very long time and deserves to be mentioned for anyone unsure if they wanna give this a try.
Final Verdict: It's a fun game, could use more variety but for being free I'd say worth it. While you can absolutely play for free, I'd sudgest spending $5-$10 to unlock a heavy machine gun or a decent tank which will make game to game abit less frustrating. If you want to play for free be prepared for a grind.

Wether you are looking for COOP Escape maps similar to left for dead/zombie mod HL2 or PvP with a zombie menace in map, this is a great game.
One common issue found with many mods to game zombie shooters is the poor hit box vs accurate aim functions... Contagion however has pulled it off with style. Though certain weapons tend to be slightly overpowered, there is a distinct satisafaction of holding your nerve and racking off a string of well placed melon poppers.
The espace maps are not just a run and gun play through but require team mates to drop life saving weapons in order to collect gears, bolt cutters, fire extinguishers and the like.
The use of the smart phone text update for mission logs is a novel additition to the genre but can be nerve racking when you have to holster your phone (and undermounter light) to read the text.
The addition of crawlers really but a stress on the average zombie fps veteran as the whole aiming dynamic and target tracking shifts 90 degrees.
Overall, i prefer the team coop especially when your dead teammates reanimate against you.
The pvp servers can be fun for a short while but loose playability after you spend 15 minutes for a round to end.
Overall i would recomend the game and give it a 7.5/10 for an fps with an 8/10 for coop survival horror.

I don't know how I got into this game. To be honest, I can't even remember going in. All I can remember is my character waking up on the second floor of an abandoned house just outside the town where I lived and that I was wearing some soldier's clothes. The name of the soldier was Karl Muller. I know this because I could read the name tag on the jacket. All this seemed very weird to me, but I decided to just go back home and figure out everything there. I needed to get out of those clothes; I didn’t want to be confused with someone else.
Just as I was walking down, I heard someone's whistle and an engine running outside the house. When I stepped outside, I saw a man wearing some weird looking green uniform running towards a funny looking green small vehicle and leaving. I decided to steal a bicycle that was sitting right in front of the house and went for a ride through the fields. I figured it was the shortest way home. As I was making my way along the river, I heard a loud noise in the woods and then a clicking noise (metal on metal) right afterwards. I got off the bike and took protection behind a tall tree and all I remember is that I was very scared. I took a minute to look around and see where that noise was coming from. Then, I saw it. It was that man wearing the green uniform. He was lying on the floor, had a really long rifle and he was looking down to a wooden barn across the field. It was a long way, but I saw some men running in and out of that barn. They were wearing a dark grey uniform (much like the one I was wearing) and looked desperate. It was almost as if they were running for their lives. Then the man shot another bullet with his rifle. It was so loud that I had to cover my ears. Then I looked towards the barn and saw one of those soldiers lying on the floor, motionless. The other soldiers were nowhere to be found and I remember feeling sorry for that guy. I asked myself- Why did this happened? Why? That sadness I felt for the guy quickly turned into anger, but to myself. I felt rage and resentment to my cowardly actions. This anger took control over myself and made me grab a shovel I had in my procession (don't know where it came from) and smashed it into that man's head. There was nothing he could do. I think it took one or two hits, but by the time I was done he was no longer part of this world. I grabbed his rifle and saw a complete different world through that scope. I saw tanks and loud fighter airplanes. I saw men in dark gray and green uniforms running everywhere. I saw them fighting over abandoned houses, bridges, and other sectors. I saw dead bodies flying several hundred meters up in the air. I saw a man on a motor bike running over three young soldiers and then exploding after hitting a tree. I saw smoke and heard loud explosions. All the things I saw, I saw them through the scope of this rifle. A rifle I DIDN'T pay for. Then I quickly realized that I was a real soldier and that I was sent to this Free to Play war to see all this epic things and to recommend this game to you.
There is a Free to Play soldier in all of us.

I highly recommend this game!
It is extremely addictive, the combat is fun and innovative, there are consequences for failure (more than simply loading the last saved game,) and with all the time I've spent on this game, I still haven't done all there is to do here.
It takes place it a fictional medieval land, but is a little more realistic in the combat and leveling sense.  There are no "rogues" and "mages," and it's not one of those RPGs where you stack one stat depending on your class.  You might focus on one, but for example, both strength and agility benefit both melee and ranged combat in different ways, and while physical attributes are important to survival in single combat, intelligence and charisma govern things like scouting and leadership which allows you to handle yourself bewtter in the world map (managing larger armies, moving across the map more quickly to catch up to or outrun other armies.) Armour and weopons feel like armor and weapons; they do not boost your strength or other stats like that, rather they are judged by their power and their weight.  You can be an archer character who wears plate armor, but every item has a weight which encumbers you and also decreases your accuracy with a bow, so choose your gear wisely.
Anyway, other posters have said a lot of what I'd like to say, so I'll just say I bought this game cheap and have had more fun with it than many 60 dollar games that I've played.  Yes there are some flaws, like the "dialogue" in the game isn't great, the graphics look pretty old school (but in exchange for having large armies in the battlefield that can run well on even older computers), and the quest variety isn't much, but there's a lot of fun stuff to do in this game, and I haven't even brushed on multiplayer.
Bottom line, you'll have fun playing this game.

I have played more than 500 hours at this game, I am participating to the clan wars, and I still play a lot with friends. But I do not recommend this game to those who don't have it yet.
Paradoxal, isn't it ? Let me explain why :
I was a fan of MW3 and, of course, I decided to buy this game, specially for clan wars. Now that I have it, I play it. It would be a waste of money not to play and I want to achieve all the goals in clan war before i quit playing this game. But for those who don't have it yet, I want to inform them about all the things that could disapoint them.
1) You need a very good PC to run it : I mean, even Battlefield 4 runs better than Ghosts ! And... it is not more beautiful than other COD games. Battlefield 3 or Crysis 1 's graphics are still better ! This is not my own opinion, this is the opinion of many players. So, if you want to play this game, prepare yourself to pay a lot for a new graphic card, etc.
2) map packs are not worth it : they are expensive and nobody plays it. Specially because new maps are not mixed with old ones. Because everyone is playing the old ones, it's getting harder and harder to find people to play on the new maps. For example : the free fall map was exclusively reserved for players who pre-ordered the game. "They" finally had to make it free and playable for everyone because ABSOLUTELY NOBODY was playing it ! Season pass is not worth it too, because it does not even include coolest stuffs (and sometimes very useful ones) such as extra slots for loadouts, wolf skin for the dog, or captain price skin.
3) because fewer and fewer players are playing it, it is already more and more difficult to find players to play with. Only TDM and Domination are still played enough. Specially for clan wars, this lack of players will be a big problem.
4) clan war is a total failure. Because I was getting bored shooting on noobs when I was playing MW3, I got very excited when I heard about clan wars coming on Ghosts. I thought it would be a good occasion to meet and fight against best players, to participate to some kind of online competition. Good thing when you don't have the occasion to play in LAN or in real LAN tournaments. But Clan war is nothing like that. You don't fight other clans, you play as usual and the competition only counts the number of victories. The clan that gets the most victories during a certain time wins. So, clan war is just a "who will kill the most noobs" competition. Except for diamond division, it is even a " who will not sleep " competition (because clans who sleep the less will, of course, play more and get more victories. Clan war is the most disapointing part of this game.
5) Hackers were a big problem. Every day, every night, there was at least one hacker every 4 or 5 matches. "They" finally reacted and banned tons of them. But it was too late. Now, because of those massive bans, it's even more difficult to find players to play with. They should have made a system like : warnings first, then punitions like stats reset, and then Ban.
Morality : For those who have this game already, let's continue to enjoy playing it. The community is small on Steam, but we can still have fun. But for those who don't have it yet, please think twice. specially about the cost of this game, because it will include the upgrade of your PC (if you don't have a decent and very recent one). And, as mentionned above, the second biggest problem is the fact that less and less players are playing it, for all the reasons I explained : tons of good players who quit playing because of the cheaters, then, tons of cheaters who got banned, technical needs : not everyone can afford a so good PC for the moment, map packs that are dividing the community even more, and, last but not least : many players who leave for other good games such as BF4, Titan Fall,... and even old cod like MW3 (many of my friends went back to mw3) etc.
Best regards.
(Post Scriptum : I had a GTX 580, and I had to upgrado to GTX 780 to run it fully)

ah yes Heroes & Generals. This game is just plain awful, granted I've only played for 3 days (take that as you will). The game is a WW2 shooter game. The devs got the WW2 part right, but as to a game or any sorta fun to be have is out the window. Most of the time games are unbalanced (mainly when I played on the germans side) and you will find it very discouraging. When i say unbalanced i mean like all infantry (mostly noobies) against 6 tanks (cant be hurt by normal nades like most new players would think). Most of the capture points are very far apart, so you will find urself running alot in this game, which will usually end with a enemy sniper taking ur face off once u get close to any sort of action. Also you have a sprint meter which doesnt last long or make a huge difference between walking. The WW2 sniper rifles act like modern rifles with their 2 mile long range, and also most of the maps are feilds so dont expect much cover, unless your keen on camping. As with alot of free games theres always hacking, which wasnt terrible in this game but stacked on top of the other problems it was harder to ignore (reporting it didnt work). You cant talk to the other team, even though the option is there. At some points people were so annoyed they restorted to trolling and team killing. Another fun element i suppose. Now on to money. In game money seemed very balanced, for a time. I unlocked a smg and started leveling it to the point i could unlock the thompson smg (the very reason i wanted to play a ww2 game in the first place). So i grind and grind for kills. till I finally unlock the gun, but then i have to buy the gun. Which is fine but then the price is 135000. After all that grinding to unlocked the gun I had about 11000. the m1 grand was 21000 which was resonable. but 135000 just to own a 3rd gun is ridiculous. If you get the crazy idea to actually pay real money its very easy of course. So it may not be paytowin, but its not too far from it. The community wasnt very helpful also (either because they wondered the same thing or felt like noobs should just figure it out). As for the Generals side the only thing i heard about them was how they were idiots and didnt send the right supplies (sounds like real ww2). I highly recommend this game!
It is extremely addictive, the combat is fun and innovative, there are consequences for failure (more than simply loading the last saved game,) and with all the time I've spent on this game, I still haven't done all there is to do here.
It takes place it a fictional medieval land, but is a little more realistic in the combat and leveling sense.  There are no "rogues" and "mages," and it's not one of those RPGs where you stack one stat depending on your class.  You might focus on one, but for example, both strength and agility benefit both melee and ranged combat in different ways, and while physical attributes are important to survival in single combat, intelligence and charisma govern things like scouting and leadership which allows you to handle yourself bewtter in the world map (managing larger armies, moving across the map more quickly to catch up to or outrun other armies.) Armour and weopons feel like armor and weapons; they do not boost your strength or other stats like that, rather they are judged by their power and their weight.  You can be an archer character who wears plate armor, but every item has a weight which encumbers you and also decreases your accuracy with a bow, so choose your gear wisely.
Anyway, other posters have said a lot of what I'd like to say, so I'll just say I bought this game cheap and have had more fun with it than many 60 dollar games that I've played.  Yes there are some flaws, like the "dialogue" in the game isn't great, the graphics look pretty old school (but in exchange for having large armies in the battlefield that can run well on even older computers), and the quest variety isn't much, but there's a lot of fun stuff to do in this game, and I haven't even brushed on multiplayer.
Bottom line, you'll have fun playing this game.

I bought this game with the belief that it has the foundation to be one of the greatest Zombie-shooter (miminal survival) game of our time. I know I have my own expectations of what would make a good Zombie game, and to be quite frank, only a few have been met. I still strongly believe in this game, being one of the many that got into Early Access. With the updates so far, it makes me feel a lot more comfortable with my decision to stick with this Zombie game. They have been working hard to bring to light their roadmap of ideas, as well has simultaneously bring us fixes that make the game what it was supposed to be at release. The game doesn't come without bugs might I add! There are only few now, but those few are very noticeable! Doorway-Snags, falling through floors, and what might not be a bug but bothers me is that you can avoid Zombies by just standing on an elevated furniture.
What I want for the next big update would be:
1. New maps and possibly new modes. As fun as it is, I feel that 3 maps, and 3 modes are what would deter people from jumping into the game or even noticing it as it passes by on Steam.
2. Zombie models. It's a general fantasy of any player to have more diversity of mobs in-game. The add-on to playable characters was fantastic though!
3. Hack-patches. This is very important as more and more hackers are finding their way to delighting themselves by ruining people's fun. I've seen many speed-hacks and even wall-hacks. Note that you'll see this maybe once out of every ten or so games. It's not that often, but definitely something to look into. I know that hackers will appear in every game or so, but I just want to state something that's been happening in-game.
Should you buy this game?
Hell yeah! I firmly believe that this game will STILL be one of the very best Zombie games of this next coming year. The work put into pleasing the fans, the ideas, and the support for the game are all very strong.
If you want some quick action jsut before bed? This is the game.
If you want a game you can put effort, time, and skill into, this is the game.
8/10 and as this game matures and the player-base continues to grow, it's soon to be a 10/10!

A good game that's a bit rough around the edges but is still enjoyable at it's core. Assembling your party from a ragtag group of mercenaries to a full-fledged army fighting for the throne is a long but fulfilling task that's quite unlike anything else offered in this genre.
It's not pretty but it's got by far the best melee combat in any game I've played to date. The ability to attack and defend in four directions adds skill to combat and makes for tense 1v1 battles. It's a system that's been taken and implemented in other games that followed it and it for good reason, you won't want to go back to anything else.
I've dropped over 100 hours into this game and I've yet to experience everything. It's a difficult climb to the top filled with tales of victory and defeat alike. You'll have a lot of stories to tell about that battle you lost in Suno that scattered your forces and separated you from your companions. There are a lot of possibilities for emergent storylines with your party as people come and go, it's really well done.
There are many paths to glory, whether you're a merchant or a bandit or a mercenary you'll find plenty to do. If that's not enough there's a big modding community that have added a ton of items and features to the game. I only play modded now and that's because it's really easy to get into, even allowing you to have multiple modules installed at once and pick which one you want to load at startup.
There aren't a lot of games like Mount and Blade, I'd recommend picking it up and giving it a try.

The sheer amount of single player replayability alone makes this game worth its full price, let alone the summer sale reduction it's got now. Then add the modability of the multiplayer/vanilla multiplayer is pretty great on top of that. Don't get me wrong, though; the best experience here is the open campaign single player, which is the main reason this game shines as brightly as it does.

Playing Mount & Blade is much like the experience of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ youself, sure from the outside you cannot notice the benefits but once you discover the inside, a warm pleasant feeling washes over your body providing a sense of joy and achievement. Mount & Blade might not have the best visuals but it gets the aesthetic right, everything from the weapons to the clothing all have a prescence and significance assisting the core mechanics of the game which are VERY solid. Innovative combat mechanics and a festering community with♥♥♥♥♥♥filled pants is alive and well. All in all this game acted as a laxative to my very constipated attitude toward multiplayer games and rekindled my love for the 'experience'.

As of 12/15/2013 - This is still an early bird of this game, but that doesn't keep folks from having fun with it.
This is a team-based FPS game with Zombies.  Even in the alpha build I had a pretty good time.  Put in about 5-6 hours offline and online.  It has a decent bundle of weapons and still adding more.  Only a few maps released so far but the detail in those maps are really well done!  The zombies are fun to kill as they really only die from a headshot... I've seen some die without one but what a waste of bullets.
The RPD escape map is fairly easy with a decent team but once some of your team becomes zombies, it gets really difficult.  The extraction map in the city is very fun with a good team (you find NPC's, protect them, and then get them to the exit point), but it can also suck really bad if your team has no idea what to do or doesn't communicate.
The survival horror is pretty good but randomized ammo can make you godlike one game and dead in short order another game.  I can totally see this game getting a good sized niche crowd with fun servers once it is a finished game.
However being an alpha build - the zombie animations look silly when they attack and the movement/objects feel bigger than they really are.  The scope of balance isn't quite there since randomized stuff can ruin a good game in one way or another.
Still - I had a good time for what it is.  The PVP could be a hot ticket as you try to keep quiet and avoid zombies so that you don't alert other humans who want to kill you.
I'd recommend it, but those looking for a polished game should wait a bit for it to be complete.

The slow pacing adds to the sense of dread and paranoia that will hit you while you scavange for a few more bullets and try to find the way out. This game is well worth the price of entry and a steal if you can get it on sale.

You can play a gamemode where you just have to kill other survivors throughout the map. The building side of the game is enjoyable and thrilling, all you need is a nailgun and just some wood planks, then you can border up a house from the zombies outside to keep the other AI survivors safe.
Overall this game is great fun for people who are into horror games, FPS games and creativity games. This game is extremely fun with your friends and great fun to go solo.
