It's not pretty but it's got by far the best melee combat in any game I've played to date. The ability to attack and defend in four directions adds skill to combat and makes for tense 1v1 battles. It's a system that's been taken and implemented in other games that followed it and it for good reason, you won't want to go back to anything else.
I've dropped over 100 hours into this game and I've yet to experience everything. It's a difficult climb to the top filled with tales of victory and defeat alike. You'll have a lot of stories to tell about that battle you lost in Suno that scattered your forces and separated you from your companions. There are a lot of possibilities for emergent storylines with your party as people come and go, it's really well done.
There are many paths to glory, whether you're a merchant or a bandit or a mercenary you'll find plenty to do. If that's not enough there's a big modding community that have added a ton of items and features to the game. I only play modded now and that's because it's really easy to get into, even allowing you to have multiple modules installed at once and pick which one you want to load at startup.
There aren't a lot of games like Mount and Blade, I'd recommend picking it up and giving it a try.

The sheer amount of single player replayability alone makes this game worth its full price, let alone the summer sale reduction it's got now. Then add the modability of the multiplayer/vanilla multiplayer is pretty great on top of that. Don't get me wrong, though; the best experience here is the open campaign single player, which is the main reason this game shines as brightly as it does.

So I think for me, like alot of people, although I knew about the Far Cry franchise beforehand, Far Cry 3 was my introduction   to it. As I came to expect from everything I had heard about it prior to me playing it, the Island setting of the game is absolutely beautiful. One of the highlights of the game is easily either finding a really high mountain or radio tower, or riding a hang glider, and looking off into the distance and seeing the full majesty of the game world, and also realizing that, for the most part, every place you can see is a palce you can go. The gun play, I will admit, is not the most satisfying, but it gets the job done (Although I loved the ripper LMG and the grenade launcher). I did have an awful lot of fun using the bow though, seeing just how far I could get a headshot from, and it was especially fun when you get fire and explosive arrows.
This next paragraph WILL contain spoilers so skip to the next one if you dont want them. Now on the note of the story and characters, the story is pretty much what it seems. You're a group of college students visiting a remote tropical Island which, SURPRISE, is teeming with drug dealing, slave trading, Pirates. In terms of the characters, I found it to be 50/50. Half of the character's SUCK. The main protagonist and his friends are barely tolerable at times with how generic they are. On the other hand, the characters on the Islands themselves, are actually pretty well done. You can tell they put alot of effort into the villains, and holy crap, Vaas is probably one of the best villains ever. He balances both humor and sadism perfectly, and I think it's kind of lame he wasn't really the main villain of the game. Now one HUGE gripe I have with the game is the ending (or endings). Basically in a sense, the game really tries to make you pick a certain choice. If you choose to stay on the Island with Citra, the game punishes you for it in several ways, and that just sort of kills it for me and makes me wonder why they even bothered giving you the option.
The game does actually do a reasonably good job of making you feel like you're out of your element, trying to survive on this remote Island........for awhile at least. Early on, the practice of hunting, gathering, exploring and activating radio towers to reveal the island and gain new supplies and weapons, the bounty and hunting misslons, searching for relics, and taking pirate outposts really to feeling of trying to survive....but once you get past a certain point, it starts to feel like busy work. Once you have all the weapons, activating all the towers, and taken all the out posts, there isn't much of a point to doing anything else and not finishing the game.
Ultimately, I did enjoy my time with Far Cry 3, and although it certainly isn't one of my favorite FPSs ever, I think anyone who enjoys open world games will find something to enjoy here. Get it when it's on sale.

Far Cry 3 is without a doubt one of the best open world games ever. The story, character, and gameplay make it extremely addicting and hard to ignore. While taking place on the same island as Far Cry 1, Far Cry 3 has nothing to do with the original game. You play as a guy called Jason Brody who get's trapped on an island with some friends who get captured by pirates and slave traders, and you must rescue them. While the story may seem basic at first, we start to see Jason's decent into insanity.

Far Cry 3 is an open world first person shooter that follows the story of Jason Brody, a man alone at the edge of the world, stranded on a mysterious tropical island as he embarks on a desperate quest to rescue his friends.
The game features weapon and skill customization, a good cooperative experience, allowing up to 4 players to play the campaign simultaneously and a immersive and engaging adventure.
The gameplay is great, the graphics and environments are absolutely gorgeous and the story is engaging and surrounded by mystery.
I highly recommend Far Cry 3.

Despite all the rage for Uplay ruining this game, I bought it anyway... AND I ENJOYED THE HECK OUT OF IT! Uplay only caused me one tiny problem when launching but easily fixed by uninstalling and reinstalling the Uplay launcher (can be downloaded from the official Uplay website).
So back on track... I'm only just gone over 10 hrs of gameplay and probably not even scratched the surface yet. The world is VAST. There is tons of stuff to explore, hidden locations you can discover, side quests to complete, animals to hunt, outposts to be taken down... that's probably not even half of them. But I immensely enjoy this game despite being an FPS noob. The exploration part of the game reminds me of when I first played Skyrim so that is part of why this is such a great game so far.
I cannot say much yet about the story but it seems interesting so far. I'm not too bothered with the main missions and wanting to get it down as quickly as possible. But the gameplay itself is very fun to get into. Using the sniper rifle and the bow and arrow is very satisfying. Gathering plants and hunting animals actually matter! So do it!
The details of this game is also what makes this game so great. From the music that automatically plays when I get into a car to using a hang glider to move around the island!
So you are still hesitating to buy this game on Steam because of Uplay? JUST BUY IT! You won't regret it.

First things first - H&G is extremely P2W. There's both the overt perks - an extra ribbon slot if you pay for membership, which equals things like taking 15% less damage, and the subtler ones, like skipping the incredible grind. Every non-basic weapon in this game is paid for - if you want to kill a tank, you'll pay more for the rockets than you'll be awarded for the kill, even if you perform perfectly. If you make your SMG shoot fast or if you make your sniper kill in one shot, you'll have to spend most of your paycheck buying the bullets back. If you want to move to a weapon that's better than the starting one, you'll have to win 30+ battles until you have the credits...of course, assuming you only use basic gear. Upgrade, start using novelties like grenades or vehicles, and it's gonna take a lot longer.
Overall, it's the worst kind of F2P. I wondered a bit whether to hit "recommend" or not, but in the end, I do have to recommend the game. It's fun. The terrible model is not getting fixed, and is likely to become even worse. The game itself however is fun, even if you're limited to forking over $100 or playing with only a basic semi-automatic rifle. Running around with  thirty other guys, relying on only your eyesight to spot enemies - it's surprisingly hard - ambushing people in the tall grass, stealing weapons from dead foes and supply stashes..it's great. It gets old after a while unless you pay up, but the first few hours are a lot of fun!

An almost perfect Open World FPS with crafting and RPG elements. The story is amazing and the acting/voiceover work is probably the best I've ever seen in a game (the guy who plays Vaas is incredible. Best villain EVER). The thing that impressed me most about this game is, you don't have to spend hours of your time crafting an sorting through piles of junk, trying to determine what to keep and what to sell or discard. Junk is easily "quick sold" and is explicitly marked as junk so there's no need to feel like you should hold onto it until later in the game when it may come in handy. The only real items of importance when it comes to crafting are animal skins for capacity upgrades (i.e., how much stuff you can carry) and plants for crafting medicines and buffs.
Leveling and stat trees are balanced and easily managed. It's possible to gain every skill in the game in a single run through so you don't have to feel like you missed out or ruined your game by taking one skill point over another. Just simply farm up some more XP and get that skill as well.
Finally, the graphics are beautiful, even if a bit aged. It's very easy to get totally submersed in the game with the wonderful graphics and beautiful locations, especially considering how great the story is and how amazing the voice and acting talent are (did I mention that Vaas is incredible? Because if there were ever Oscars given to video game actors, he should be the first to receive one). The options menu is deep and extremely configurable, from key layouts to graphics and sound settings. I have a pretty basic bargain-bin laptop (Acer Aspire E 15) with no modifications running the integrated intel HD 4400 with 1792 VM and can get the game to run with a bit of lag at full settings. I run mostly on medium with a few settings set to high, however, and get a constant frame rate of ~30fps (which is great for my non-gaming computer).
My only gripe with this game is the soundtrack. It's pretty bland and bear-bones and neither adds nor subtracts from the game. It's just kind of "there". It doesn't hinder the experience in any way but I feel with a stronger score or maybe even the addition of some licensed music added during key scenes, it could have added that much more to the submersive experience.
Overall, this game is a 9.5 out of 10 which by my grading standards, is practically a 10. I save 10s for the absolute best of the best. Games that not only are damn near perfectly designed and executed and fun to play, but which have also changed the landscape of gaming in general and paved the way for others to follow. The only "10"s I've played I can count on 2 hands (Super Mario 3 and Super Mario World, The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past and Ocarina of Time, Half-Life II, Tetris, Mrs. Pac-Man and maybe a few more I'm forgetting). Far Cry 3 is almost there but, there isn't much here that hasn't already been done before. That said, everything about the game that came from other games, Far Cry 3 put it all together and made it better as a whole than anyone else in it's genre. They took the best parts of games like Borderlands and Fallout and improved upon them in a way that's damn near perfect.

What started out years ago as potentially the fastest and most popular FPS on the market has dwindled down to a Lag Compensated, Frustrating, Unsupported, Cheat fest. Every game I get into, if I can get into a game, takes a long time to load and is ridiculously unplayable. The PC community months after the game launched has less than a few players evidenced by the "number of players" info when perusing the game types, only a few people playing on only a couple of game modes, most game modes have zero (0) players so you cant play them at all, this doesnt change - ever, everytime you look, it's the same story, only the punished few. The PC community is being ignored by Activision. We dont have the simplest of options in the game, there are no separate controls for volume, no options to pick a server with a good "ping". We have no dedicated servers (if there were, why does the server freeze then toss you mid-game when a player quits?), we have to join, if we can at all, whatever map / server the system picks for you. There are no options for map type, ping, number of players, etc ...  most of the convenient choices in previous versions of this game are gone. If the system puts you in a map you dont want to play or its so laggy you cant play, you can not get out right away, you have to wait and wait and wait, then when you finally have the chance to go back to the main menu and try a different "map/server "  you find yourself waiting in que for the same map you just left, then you have to waste your time trying to get out all over again! This process of trying to find a mediocre at best map to play can waste up to 5 minutes or more of your time. Lately (Feb 2014) even though there seems to be players (1000) in a couple game modes, I can't join at all even though I honestly waited 20-30 minutes, just to see how long it would take. GAMEPLAY (when you are fortunite enough to get into a game) -  When I die the killcam shows something completely different than what I experienced while dying. Its as if the player that killed me and I are a second or two apart in the timing of the game. This is not an isolated event, it happens everytime I play. I hear other players complaining about the same experience, constantly, every game! Players accusing other of cheating when its the game  programmers code that must be allowing this strange behavior, I hear accusations between players constantly. There always seems to be one player without the problem, he's usually top of the leader board. This phenomenom nessesitates the need to play only the servers/games that you dont crash/freeze/lag immediatly until the game picks you as host, then you can improve your K/D ratio, until then you have to get out quick because it's impossible to play. I have read countless reviews, seen countless YouTube videos, and talked with other players who have relentlously reported these problems to Activision. These problems are global and have been proclamed by all who play whether its Xbox, or PC (PC wholly the worst). The support from Activision or Infinity Ward whomever handles problems reported by players, is unresponsive. They already made their money, they're probably laughing all the way to the bank. I have a 75M up/ 35M down fiber connection and an Alienware "built for speed, I7 6860HQ 3.6Ghz., 8 gig Ram, Nvidea GTX 780, etc... computer. I feel like I am being punished for investing in equipment for gaming. I dont nessesarily want an advantage (of course I do) over others just a fair gaming experience. I die in the game from players that arent on my screen yet, nobody is there, in an empty room, but the killcam showed him shooting me for seconds right in front of me, or I shoot him first, empty my gun into him, before he even sees me, then I die, the killcam shows him shooting me for 2 sec and my back was turned because he was 2 sec ahead in the game and I hadnt turned to shoot him yet, we were not even in the same game. I don't have this problem with other FPS games such as BattleField 4, Titan Fall (new) or Crysis. I also turn all the video options to their lowest settings but it doesnt matter even with a $600 GTX 780 card. I also see cheaters running rampant in way too many games, I finally found out that leaving the game an using "F1" to look at "friends" allows you to report the person, most people like me, for months, dont know how to report anyone. The cheats know this so they feel free. If you report them either nothing is done or the guy gets his Steam account reset then he goes back into the game and resumes cheating, these guys laugh at Activision and are open about the fact that they cant be stopped. You see people at presique 1 level 30 with a "custom name" mopping everyone, obviously a reset player. Over and Over! How much can even a dedicated COD player endure? It's ridiculous. I hear many players talking about leaving COD for good and I am probably going to join them. This is what happens when a Company like Activision allows players to believe they don't care, maybe they became corrupt and greedy and started publishing unfinished games to the public. You cant convince me Activision couldnt fix these problems if they wanted to invest the time, they are capable, the answer must be they just don't care about us! The game is sold, it's over, time to move on and make more money. Don't get me wrong I like money too, Problem is.... I really loved this game! Perfect in fit for the player that wants a challenge. But not anymore! What a waste of a formerly capable game concept.

Now, going into this game, I had many misconceptions about the Far Cry series in general, and to be honest I didn't expect too much from this game. Well, as it turns out, I was quite mistaken. Sure, the main character sucks, and sure pretty much everybody on Rook Island (Including him) are villanous to some capacity, but the game is fantastic. The setting is a small set of islands in the South Pacific, where you, and your brothers and friends, are taken captive by Vaas Montenegro, an unhinged pirate who revels in his insanity. In fact, it could be argued that he's the most sane of the villans since he acknowedges his mental state. But I digress. So, you're lucky enough to escape the slave trade, and declare a one-man war against Vaas and his pirates. The environment is not exactly varied, mostly what one would expect in an equitorial climate. Beach and jungle, with some mountains and old temple ruins thrown in for variety. The gameplay is fantastic. There is nothing as thrilling as mowing down pirates responding to an SOS call because you failed stealth to the tune of some odd dubstep/drums and bass track. The soundtrack is fantastic. It alternates between the former, and a quiet, pounding stealth track that plays whenever you silently dispatch pirates to gain access to their base. In this game, stealth is as much of an option as loud, and in fact I feel it is as fun, but have no fear. There are plenty of weapons to suit your needs should things not go as planned. Between the heart-pounding soundtrack, the variety of guns (go with the AK) and the option to do pretty much anything you want, any way you want, and the villan to end all villans, and I cannot see why you shouldn't play this game. Even if you like more futuristic FPS games (Like me) and you don't like the idea of slicing some pirate up with a machete in a hot, sweaty jungle, trust me; You'll be glad you did. In all honesty, I want Far cry 4 to be as good as Far Cry 3, but I don't know; the bar's been set almost impossibly high.
Overall Score: 10/10

Not exactly the prettiest game there ever was, but in terms of gameplay it still stands strong. The quests can get a little repetitive and/or annoying, especially when you waste a month running all over the map looking for one enemy bandit party that is required for a quest, but otherwise this is a very, very good game.
One of the main selling points here is that it is incredibly open-ended. There is no main quest, no main storyline, its all just you and how you want to play it. Roving mercenary captain relying on his sword and armor? Sure. Archer, possibly of the horse variety? Why not. And then you can be a merchant, pure and simple, amassing unparalleled wealth. Or perhaps utilising your sheer amounts of cash to just buy an army and take over everything. Really, the possibilities are, if not limitless, then pretty close.
And when you tire of the base game, there are always mods. Like, a ton. No seriously, the amount of full-conversion mods that take you to a completely different world/setting are staggering. Be an Uruk raider in Middle-Earth, or a Stark bannerman in Westeros, or even a bounty hunter in the Outer Rim, and these are just the tip of the iceberg.
Buy this game if you want something with great replayability, something that is completely open-ended, something that puts gameplay over graphics.

The multiplayer portion of the game is what really ruins the game, in my opinion, however.  It's buggy as hell, for starters, and lag seems to be an issue no matter how decent a connection every player in a given lobby has.  To boot, as with every CoD game in the last decade, hackers make their appearances in droves.  The difference with Ghosts, however, is that no one is doing a damn thing about it.  Within the first three months of Ghosts, it's already as shabby and hacked-apart as MW3 was in it's last months.  Steam doesn't do anything about it (and why should they, it's not their game), and Activision has, once again, put aside the pleas of its fans and left out any sort of hacker control.  No votekick, no PunkBuster, nothing.  For any legitimate players, your choices soon dwindle down to playing against Bots, which have neither skill nor allows for any real EXP gain.
The most frustrating factor to me, however, is how terribly the servers are.  First, we never really got those dedicated servers that were promised before launch, did we? No, all we got was this terrible hybrid system that disallows for any control over who and where you play.  Even worse, though, is that, because you have no way to look for servers, you're stuck, just as in MW3, waiting for a lobby to find enough players to launch.  For sometimes as much as half an hour at a time.
Ultimately, Ghosts is a tired and vain game, with nothing new or fun to offer its players.  Don't make the mistake that I made: don't buy Ghosts.

Not exactly the prettiest game there ever was, but in terms of gameplay it still stands strong. The quests can get a little repetitive and/or annoying, especially when you waste a month running all over the map looking for one enemy bandit party that is required for a quest, but otherwise this is a very, very good game.
One of the main selling points here is that it is incredibly open-ended. There is no main quest, no main storyline, its all just you and how you want to play it. Roving mercenary captain relying on his sword and armor? Sure. Archer, possibly of the horse variety? Why not. And then you can be a merchant, pure and simple, amassing unparalleled wealth. Or perhaps utilising your sheer amounts of cash to just buy an army and take over everything. Really, the possibilities are, if not limitless, then pretty close.
And when you tire of the base game, there are always mods. Like, a ton. No seriously, the amount of full-conversion mods that take you to a completely different world/setting are staggering. Be an Uruk raider in Middle-Earth, or a Stark bannerman in Westeros, or even a bounty hunter in the Outer Rim, and these are just the tip of the iceberg.
Buy this game if you want something with great replayability, something that is completely open-ended, something that puts gameplay over graphics.

This game was very close to awesome, but the developers ruined it with poor choices that ruined gameplay.
-pay to win

-worst hit detection I've ever seen in an online shooter game

As I was writing my review of this game, I realized the entire series of flaws can be summarized in one very easy statement: YOU HAVE TO BUY GRENADES.
As you play the game, you earn silver currency.  That silver currency can be spent to upgrade weapons, or buy new weapons, vehicles, etc.  Saving up enough currency to buy a "good" weapon requires you to grind at least 300+ hours.  Meanwhile, as you use grenades or anything with ammunition, you have to spend your currency to replenish your grenade supply.  The entire system is designed to make sure a casual player NEVER EVER EVER accomplishes anything in this game.  It's a dirty, money-grubbing scheme to wear casual players down and finally push them to the point at which they reluctantly break out their wallets.  As a non-paying casual player: you will never get a "good" gun.  You will never level up. You will never be anything but fodder waiting to be slaughtered by the pay-to-win players  ...and yes, this game absolutely groups beginners, pay-to-winners, and 500+ hour players into the same exact battles.  Again, it's a scheme designed to frustrate non-paying casual players into taking out their wallets to overcome the disadvantage.
One gun:  Yeah, this is self explanatory.  Guns have weight, and the game designers intentionally designed the weight of the guns in such a way to prevent you from carrying more than one.  Unless of course you pay to play, in which case you can pay for light-weight guns that enable you to carry two.  This limitation is exacerbated by the fact that each type of gun is strictly limited to valued use in very specific circumstances.  For example, machine guns are great inside of houses, but are completely useless at long range.  The horrible single-gun system also contributes to the ill-effects of the hero swapping feature.
Hero swapping:  In mid-battle, players can change their participating "hero." The game is designed in such a way that each "hero" becomes specialized.  There are tank drivers, pilots, paratroopers, snipers, machine gunners, etc.  Each has a specific role.  Some battle maps cater to specific types.  For example, some maps have wide rivers that must be crossed on foot.  Obviously these maps cater to sniper-rifles.  It's important to stress the point that you CAN NOT change weapons once you've joined a game.  As soldiers trudge across the open water, snipers pick them off.  Machine gunners, whom lack range effectiveness are basically worthless on these types of maps, as there is little to no close-quarters combat.  Here's the trick:  the game allows players to switch between heroes. Thus, if you happen to have played 1000+ hours, you will have the ability to swap out your useless machine-gunner for a more useful sniper.  It's very strange.  Rather than simply switching guns - which would make much more sense, you have to actually switch heroes.  Unfortunately, leveling up those heroes takes hundreds of hours each.  Like other strange mechanics in this game, the hero-swap mechanic was clearly implemented to encourage people to pay-to-win.  IE: pay $50 and you can have both a great machine-gunner hero and a great sniper hero without having to invest 1000+ hours like everyone else.  Why not just allow people to carry 2 guns, or even allow them to swap guns during battle?  Because that wouldn't encourage people to pay money!
Hit detection:  When I first started playing this game, this was the very first thing I noticed.  I would run up to an enemy with my trusty machine-gun and start blasting.  As I filled the stationary target with lead, my screen displayed spurts of blood - indicating that my shots were definitely hitting the target.  Bullet after bullet slammed into the enemy's body.  Then, slowly, as I continued to blast away, the target would turn towards me.  Then the bullet-riddled enemy would fire one shot, and BOOM.  I died.  Yep, I shot him half-a-dozen times, and he one-shot-killed me and walked away.  This same, frustrating scenario has happened to me literally hundreds of times.  Check out the forums, and you will see that I am certainly not an isolated case.  It happens to everyone.  It's the most frustrating thing I have ever experienced in a multiplayer shooting game.
Hacks:  While you may not necessarily consider this the fault of the game developers at first, you have to consider the entire pay-to-win scheme to fully understand the problem.  This game is free to play.  Anyone with a computer and an email address can play.  If a player cheats and gets banned, then that player can simply register a new email address and cheat again.  They don't lose anything, because they didn't pay anything.  If a player had to pay $40 for a new account every time they got banned from cheating, they would quickly change their cheating ways as their bank accounts were drained from buying more and more new copies of the game to cheat with.  However, since this is free-to-play, the cheaters don't care.  They come in and have their fun ruining a game and getting 30-2 on the killboards.  Then they get banned in a week and create a new account.. rinse-and-repeat.  Believe me, the cheating is prevalent.  As you play you will be saying "gee, I just saw a guy outrun a jeep, shoot me through a wall with a magical bullet from 500 meters away, and absorb 20 shots from a machine gun.  this seems strange."
Overall, I am disappointed by the choices developers made with H&G.  It could have been a unique and fun game, but unfortunately the greedy pay-to-win mechanics sabotaged what otherwise would have been a great experience.

The quests can get a little repetitive and/or annoying, especially when you waste a month running all over the map looking for one enemy bandit party that is required for a quest, but otherwise this is a very, very good game.

Roving mercenary captain relying on his sword and armor? Sure. Archer, possibly of the horse variety? Why not. And then you can be a merchant, pure and simple, amassing unparalleled wealth. Be an Uruk raider in Middle-Earth, or a Stark bannerman in Westeros, or even a bounty hunter in the Outer Rim, and these are just the tip of the iceberg.
Buy this game if you want something with great replayability, something that is completely open-ended, something that puts gameplay over graphics.

I cannot recommend this game at this point in development.  While it has a lot of potential, the game is simply too incomplete to give any kind of recommendation to purchase it.
While I am happy to contribute to the team's ongoing efforts to create a more realistic, survival-based zombie game that isn't so "arcadey" as L4D series, there's really nothing worth noting that sets this title apart to make it worth playing at the moment.
There's Bugs.  Lots of Bugs.
I realize that an early access game is subject to bugs, and I expect to encounter them.  It's not that I'd berate a game for it's incomplete state in a beta-stage, however, some core, fundamental issues simply make this a game not worth playing.  For example, this game emphasizes the headshot to conserve ammo, and yet, the hit detection is just wrong.  You can literally empty a magazine at a zombie's face and never hit their head.  The zombie AI is so lacking, they get stuck on double doors, when the other door is broken open.  The get stuck within map objects and cannot move.  Sometimes they just freeze in place and stare at you.  This wouldn't be so glaring if it weren't exacerbated by the fact that zombies actually aren't even scary in this game.  More than half the time you can walk right past them, and they don't even acknowledge you.
Gameplay
The co-op modes are pretty much impossible, which is probably why everyone just plays hunted.  I've had the game a week and never found any servers on anything but PD or aurora estates.  If you're unfortunate and join the co-op games after they start, you get spawned as a zombie in locations that are completely remote, or blocked off, from where the survivor players actually are located.  This is worse in a closed map like RPD, and somewhat livable in Estates (an open map).  However, so many times I just sit as a as a Zombie wishing the "zombie-vision" worked, so I could go do something rather than hopelessly waiting for the survivors to die so I can partake in the fun.
This game desperately needs a lobby system a-la L4D, so you can all join and then start together.  Or, it's Zombie mode needs to be addressed so those waiting to play can have fun too.  And I admit, zombie mode IS fun.  It's just so difficult to find survivors and harass them, after 20 minutes of wandering around, you really just want to find fire and watch your corpse burn.
The video makes the game seem way better than it is, sadly.  And I loathe over-hyped games.  At this point, it is a broken, watered down, feature deprived version of L4D.  While I completely expected that for an early-access game, the video was misleading.
I will say, however, that once polished and completed, Contagion will most likely be a far more enjoyable and frightening experience than Left 4 Dead.  Time will tell.

Before you take my recommendation against this game too seriously, you should understand that H&G is a relatively enjoyable experience for some time. Sniping is way too easy, to put it simply.  With almost no recoil and insane damage, anyone can buy one of these killing machines after a few hours of playing and turn into an instant pro.  Range could literally be from halfway across the map, so don't even think of getting revenge.
2. Camping
At least 90% of every match turns into some guy pulling out a tank, sitting across from you on a bridge, and smoking literally everything that comes even close to it.  I mean, come on, they even made the tank shots look like a laser beam.  If, at some point 30 min in when a plane finally blows this insufferable piece of♥♥♥♥♥♥up, it takes them about 20s to be back in the same spot blowing everyone to hell.  Anti vehicle weapons help slightly, but unless you have a degree in rocket curvature, chances are you wont hit anything either coming straight at you or completely halted.
3.  Starting Weapons

To be fair, as much as the Gewehr and Garand are completely incomparable (Gewehr couldn't hit the side of a barn), they are both typically worthless weapons.  It would be more effective to give each player a melee weapon and tell them to charge the enemy line then to give them these annoying contraptions.  Recoil is insane, and you're lucky to even shoot in the right direction after 3 shots.
This game is a constant grind, but to be fair, the maps and graphics are superb.

Contagion delivers a bit of a different and interesting exprience to the co-op zombie survival genre, it is fun and worth checking out for co-oping with friends or jumping on a server solo! thumbs up from me.
here is a rundown of the currently available game modes:
Deathmatch (The Hunt) - depending on which map you are playing the gameplay varies. its basically last one alive wins the round and the dead become zombie which speeds things up and makes it harder to survive. There are smaller more fast paced maps (the park map) or the suburb map which is much more suspenseful and involves a bit of hide and seek (you can board up a house and hide in the garage like a little girl). it never gets too boring cause you can always check your mobile phone which will tell you if people are around you and will give you audio clues about their location.
Escape - an objective based mode which takes place in a prison. the objectives are generated randomly and item placements change so in one play through you might be escaping from the garage and the other might get you up to the roof to a chopper. it is very suspensful and revolves around ammo conservation and team work. the diffculty level could be higher but maybe that's a setting I haven't found yet.
Extraction - revolves around helping NPCs escaping, haven't played it much so i can't really speak about it
If you like first person multiplayer games and enjoyed old school hl2/hl mods that experiment in gameplay this is for you.

Welcome to the Steam Summer Sale.
Another chance to buy crap over priced games.
This time it's Mount & Blade.
There's an almost playable game hidden in here, but it's very very well hidden.
Tournaments - You ride around in circles forever. Or stop so you can be hit and have a chance of lining up.
The world map - You click where you want to go, random enemies attack you, sometimes you win, sometimes you have to surrender, you can't play it on the mode where you can't go back a save because it's that random how lucky you'll be.
Woah now. So the game is balanced same as a FPS? You dive back to the last save point? Well that sounds ok.
Yeah if the game is interesting, that sounds ok. If the game involves reasonably brain dead combat, pixel thin graphics and long dialogue blurbs that essentially say "Go hire 5 men" in 60 words ... then no .. it's not ok.
The graphics and environment are *that* great, that even the designers let you tab out of anywhere, avoid the 3D world entirely and just dive straight to the stores / castle.
NPC characters? 90% all exactly the same, not sure why they bothered making it so you could talk to them.
I'm not sure who'll like this game. It fails as an FPS, fails as strategy, fails as an RPG. About the only fun part is the battles and they aren't that great.
Yet another waste of cash in the Summer Sale.
Don't buy it.
EDIT: I think people that get in to this, just manage to ignore the rest and play it for the battles. So I guess it's your call. I recently picked up the now in early beta, Contagion by Monochrome. Contagion is a co-op survival horror game, much like the Valve Left 4 Dead series, but with stark differences. Monochrome is doing a lot of things right. Very right. Polish the game up and give it a tweak or two, and we may just have a game that tops the legend that is Valve.
In Contagion there are currently 3 game modes on 3 maps (you can learn more about the maps on the contagion wiki), with my favorite being the Roanoke prison escape level. On this level you’re trapped in a prison over run by zombies, the power is out and all you have to light the way are the few candles, trash can fires and your ever trusty flashlight. The atmosphere built on this level is what I imagine a true zombie apocalypse to be like.  Mass panic as humanity scraped to survive and the chaos this calamity brought, leaving the world in a state of brokenness. This is the world that is built in this game, it truly makes you feel the weight of every choice you make and the consequences that any wrong step can bring.
The prison is deathly quiet, you hear the sparks of cables, torn from the walls, the soft hum of the vending machine, the flicker of florescent lights as they struggle to stay lit in the darkness. Or the grunts of a horde of zombies on the other side of a thin plywood, polyester coated door. Panicked, praying to a god you might or might not even believe in that they didn’t hear the sound of you reloading your gun, because you know more zombies stand on the other side of that door than you have bullets left.
Each shot in this game is a game altering choice. One shot too many and you’ve alerted the horde, and one shot too few that you couldn’t kill that zombie before it ate your face. The eeriness of the silence in this game makes that choice even harder with each shot. As you progress through the level, you wind up in the cell blocks, made of cinder block. Each time your finger pulls that trigger the walls shake with the sound of your bullet. Did you wake the beast? Were you sure the path behind you was clear in the need of a retreat? Are you sure about that?
The atmosphere of this game is perfect for the genre. Ammo is scarce, guns are hard to find, you’re lucky if you can find a healing gun more than once a level with levels being up to 40 minutes long with no check point. All of these factors add up to what a horror game is about. Especially one with zombies, which is so overdone now a days that it takes a truly exceptional game to stand out. Levels in this game can and are long, and if you die, that’s it (unless on multiplayer in which you become a zombie and attack the remaining survivors. More later). Veto. You’re done. This enhances the weight on each choice you make because you’ve already sunk 30 minutes of your time into this one level and if you die you go right back to square one.  A developer not making a game that holds your hand the entire way through is such a breath of fresh air. Too often mainstream games place the player in a god type character with little to no real challenge. I’m thankful for the fact that Monochrome took the risk and kicked the players♥♥♥♥♥ Now I think the zombie AI needs some improvement and the difficultly could be higher, but it is only in beta and these are all things that can and will be improved. What brings relief to me is that I see the framework and from what I can tell the developers are headed in the direction that I believe is going to make a great game. A game that if given the right community and mod support, will be played for years with user created maps and new weapons, enemy types, ect. Monochrome, you have a great thing going here don’t screw it up.
Since the game is only just now in an open public beta, I don’t expect it to be anywhere near perfect, but I do have some flaws that I would like to point out that I believe are very correctable and would take this game from great concept to a truly timeless game. I believe in you Monochrome!
First is the level of difficulty involved with the Zombie AI. The traditional approach to difficultly in zombie games is “make em take more bullets and make more of em”. While there is nothing necessarily wrong with this approach, it leads to stagnate game play with no real sense of horror because after a few play throughs you know what comes from where and how many it will be. Make the zombies more than mindless brain eating drones. If I walk into a room that has multiple entrances, have the zombies move around to flank me and trap me in the room. Have one go to block the only exit on the stairwell while the other tries to pin me in a corner. If the threat of the unknown is there every time you play, the game will always feels new to you and you won’t grow tired of the same set pieces playing out on each level. If you never really know what to expect with a game you’ve logged 50+ hours into, then you have found yourself a truly exceptional game.
Second is more of a mechanical issue with the way the game handles, if you will. The controls can be a bit clunky at times, and while this can add to the excitement of the game, they feel a bit too clunky to the point of mild frustration. This is even more so in the multiplayer when playing as a zombie. This is the most dreadful part of the game, and maybe they designed it that way as an extra incentive to not die, but damn is it not fun. Zombie die easily, move slow, do little damage, and are very limited in their options. Breaking down a plywood office door takes well over two minutes and 40+ attacks, even longer with metal doors. Well just go around them? Often times you can’t as you are spawned into a room with only a single exit and are forced to break down multiple doors to be able to get to the remaining players. Now the zombies do have some cool features such as the ability to see in the dark, call a mini horde and then blend into that horde, but the pure lack of fun playing a zombie trumps all these and tends to lend to many players simply leaving a game upon death. Not a good design feature. Address these issues and make the zombie mode fun to play and you’ve got a good multiplayer mode in the works.
My last little nit pick about the game, besides the obvious issues that are just because a game is in beta is how hard it is to get a private match going. Setting up a server is impossible without the prior knowledge of port forwarding and server hosting. I’d love to be able to set up a small private match for my friends and I through in game means, and I hope the final version has some form of this. Even better if we get it in beta.
Monochrome, you’ve got a diamond in the rough here, please for my selfish pleasures get this right. Because if you do, I and many, many others will surely be sinking hundreds of hours into it. I highly recommend grabbing this game, I have a gut feeling its going to be a good one.

Far Cry 3 ist schon toll, wunderschöne Grafik, riesige Spielwelt und allerhand was ich alles machen kann. Allerdings halte ich die sehr aggressive Tierwelt für übertrieben. Und auch wenn man so veranlagt ist wie ich, das ich wirklich jeden Stein und jeden Quadratnanometer der Insel vollständig erkundigt haben möchte, wird es irgendwann recht langweilig.
Sobald nämlich alle Posten eingenommen wurden, sind kaum noch Gegner da, denn die Gegner respawnen nicht. Und einmal abgesehen von den Tieren, vor denen ich mich echt in acht nehmen muss, droht mir sonst keine Gefahr mehr.
Gibt zwar noch allerhand an Nebenmissionen die ich erledigen kann aber die fühlen sich eher leer und steril an. Richtig Spannung kommt da bei mir nicht auf.
Was ich auch ziemlich nervig finde, das die gegnerischen Soldaten immer von dem selben Synchronsprecher gesprochen werden. Das ist zwar im Prinzip nicht schlimm, aber im zweiten Teil waren es 2 Sprecher die immer sehr schöne Dialoge gehalten haben. Gerade wenn ich mich in ein Lager anschleichen will, war das in Far Cry 2 immer sehr schön diesen Dialogen zuzuhören.
Die NPCs scheinen meiner Meinung nach auch voll einen an der Waffel zu haben. Zumindest bekomme ich den Eindruck wenn man diesen Kommentaren eine Weile zuhört.
Ziemlich bescheuert sind auch die Speicherpunkte. Es ist mehr als ärgerlich, wenn ich mich gerade in einem Gefecht mit Gegnern befinde, dann noch ein wildes Tier anfängt mich zu attackieren ich das Zeitliche segne und nachdem Neustart ganz woanders wieder anfangen muss.
Das Dumme ist nämllich, das sich gerne es aus einem oder 2 Jeeps, die ich attackiert habe, 2 -3 weitere dazu gesellen und mir die Hölle ordentlich einheizen. Richtig kompliziert wird es dann, wenn noch ein Bär oder ein daher gelaufener Tiger mich von hinten anfällt.
Die Story hätte ich anders umgesetzt, beziehungsweise anders geschrieben. Schließlich liegt hier der Augenmerk aufs erkunden, jemanden retten zu müssen ist auf so einem riesigen Terrain nicht so gut gewählt.
Ein ganz großes Plus ist natürlich Vaas Montenegro. Der hat zwar ganz ordentlich ein Dachschaden, aber die Art und Weise wie er dargestellt wird ist überragend. Schade das die anderen gegnerischen Soldaten nicht in ähnlicherweise vertont wurden.
FarCry 3 macht Spass, ich habe mich sehr gut unterhalten gefühlt, hat für mich aber leider keinen hohen Wiederspielwert.
Unnötigerweise wird ein uPlay-Account benötigt, sodaß ich beide Accounts parallel laufen lassen muss um Far Cry 3 zu spielen.

I bought Far Cry 3, whilst looking for a new shooter, and while it does fulfill that category, it's so much more. Far Cry is easily the most thought provoking and interesting game that I've ever played. While the combat is a bit average (excluding those knife skills!), the perk system is fairly good. Contagion is an above average zombie survival FPS game that provides some unique gameplay elements.  I enjoyed playing this game during the beta and release and especially liked the route changes as you replay levels and the emphasis on teamwork.
But I feel the full release is still in late beta because of these things:
1) Game breaking bugs like zombies getting stuck, zombie players spawning in locations where they are trapped, zombie players can’t climb certain walls that the A.I. can, and a path in Barlowe Square that sometimes doesn’t open and the game is ruined.
2) The overly difficult gameplay which seems to lack testing before implementation.  You probably have a 5% chance at most of winning on a public server in the PVE game modes on normal difficulty.  This is due to a lack of ammo, lack of melee weapons, easy player infection, and overpowered player zombies.  Pretty much the only way to win in PVE is to play solo or with a close group of friends.  I would strongly recommend kiting large zombie hordes, especially in Barlowe Square, kiting is an almost essential playing style and can be a huge turnoff for some players.
3) There is a lack of content to justify the $20 price, although the developer has promised more free content is on the way.  I picked up the game for cheap so I can’t complain, but I feel there is not enough maps or replayability for a new buyer.
4) The Hunted mode (PVP) feels ‘arcadey’ to me because points are awarded for killing zombies.  Players are encouraged to shoot zombies for points which helps move the game along at a faster pace to get to the next round.  But I feel when someone is hunting they are generally trying to be stealthy when searching for prey.  The Battle Royale mode in ARMA 3 is a similar game mode, but slower paced and a good example of how this mode should play IMO.
I think this game has the potential to be great someday, especially after bug fixes, new content, and the release of the SDK.  But Contagion currently lacks polish and I can’t recommend the game for now.
***The August 2014 update has made the difficulty more reasonable with more ammo and stronger melee attacks.  There is also a new map.  Game is starting to look a lot better.

Heroes and Generals takes me back about 10 years and invokes memories of Battlefield 1942. It has the control points, vehicles, and the same overcast dreary feel that BF1942 had. The devlopers have added some modern features such as a leveling system, perks, weapon modification, iron sights, squads and a stategy meta game that make it a modern WWII themed shooter. Unlike BF1942 Heroes and Generals lacks the balance, mods and fun that got me into PC gaming back in 2003.
Running around in a vehicle with friends on teamspeak is a hell of alot of fun. The weapon are very accurate and will kill players in 2-3 shots in the chest. Bullets have travel time and drop over distance. Landing a headshot on a jeep driver who is trying to run you over is satisifing experience. Grenades are deadly in buildings, but are a limited use item. The control point based gameplay keeps players from both sides engaged in combat throughout the game.
The games loses all the fun if you play with randoms. There is no good way to coordinate in game with members of your team or squad, and the free to play nature of the game attracts less serious players. Outside of a limited number of single use anti-tank rockets on select points there is no way for low level players to effectivity fight tanks. Those who spent real money on unlocks like tanks and the sniper rifle(which costs $10 in gold) have an unfair advantage over new players which leads to immense frustration. While the small arms are balanced between the US and German factions, the tanks are not blanced. The US get a light tank that can kill other tanks with a powerful cannon that can damage any german tank. The german's light tank is only equipped with 2 machine guns that cannot penetrate any US tank. The lack of anti-tank weapons and outclassed german tanks leads to spawn camping.
I understand this is a free to play game and the developers need microtransactions to keep funding further development of the game. However they throw balance out the window and push people towards buying weapon and vehicle unlocks. Outside of cosmetic items anything can be earned by playing enough. After 33 hours on a single solder and placing consistently in the top quarter of players in the matches I had purchased an sub machine gun, a rocket launcher, and a more powerful rifle. The all mighty sniper rifle and lightweight anti-tank grenades were still 30 to 40 hours of gameplay away for me.
For a game that has been in development for 3 years I expected a much more refined product. Thankfully I did not spend a cent on this game.

I thought this game had a ton of potential but I was quite disappointed. Basically it plays like every other coop zombie shooter out there. They aimed to make aspsects of it more realistic which is only really evident with how hard it is to find ammo and health. This wouldn't be nearly as obnoxious if the melee mechanics were a bit more polished. You would think whacking on a zombie's face with a sledgehammer would produce a kill in a few hits but this is not the case, it takes just as much effort with a sledgehammer as it does with a dinky knife. The melee system is also pretty clunky and there doesn't seem to be a variation on attack speed based on what weapons you have.
I also only ever played this with one other person and we both agreed that a lot of the maps would be easier if there three or more people. This obviously isn't the developer's fault but it's something to keep in mind when you purchase it. Its definitely a challenge, which is fun but, we found some of the maps were too much for just a duo to take on. The zombie mode is another aspect that has potential but, at the moment, doesn't really deliver, this plays into my biggest complaint about this game. The spawn points are not very kind to you. Contagion is a fun objective based zombie survival game. Minus some initial issues with crashing to the desktop before getting into the game, I'd recommend it heartily. The game rewards good observation skills and keen awareness of your surroundings. There are a couple issues with odd animations when the zombies get in close to attack or when they go to climb over something, but the sound quality is very good including some background noise such as far off gunshots, which is hard to mistake for gunshots within the map that you're playing. Good job on the sounds. The zombies sound eerie and when they spot you, you'll know it. Ammo is spread around the maps, and is sparse, but luckily, there are some decent melee weapons.
For people who want to compare this to Left 4 Dead, I'd say it's a bit more easy going, but just as scary even without "special" infected. The maps objectives and loot is randomized throughout the map, so check your corners and behind desks because there are some surprises occasionally in the form of ammo and weapons.
Multiplayer requires cooperation. Those people who run and gun getting all the loot will find themselves alone soon with the players that die taking over spots as zombies. More than a few times I was surprised by a zombie while I was going to check a dark room and it turned out a player who had died was waiting for someone.
It's worth the full price of the game, although I got it at the steam sale for half off. I'd recommend it as a well thought out zombie survival game.

So…Though my profile shows me at 19 hours on this game, I started playing well before it hit Steam.
With that said. If you are reading these reviews before you decide to test a FREE TO PLAY, pay no head to these 4-5 hour playtime reviews… They know not of what they speak.
I love the game for what it is and what it used to be. The game is so smooth these days however; I do wish there were more readily available low-ping matches (USA West). I don’t know exactly how the server location is decided but before I complain any more, you used to NEVER find a single USA server. So I am ok where it stands at this point. (But would still like it either explained or fixed)
I DO NOT use the automatic matchmaking. I go through the list and find the first server that gives me the option to join.  There were 4 matches I could join in the browser but the MM system still gave me a 5 estimated wait period. Again, I don’t know how this system is set up but it could use a looking at.
Back in the day it was SO easy and cheap (game currency) to hop into a tank or a plane and get started. If infantry was your thing, you could get AT grenades in just a few matches and with the limited FoV the tank drivers have, it was easy to sneak up and get two grenades on. There are free AAA emplacements on nearly every map… use them. It’s not as easy today, but not hard enough to rate down. Back then you also had a ton of kids buying pilots, jumping into your assault squad, and JUMPING OUT of your fighter planes to cap points… The price raise and the time it takes to get promoted to pilot DEFINITELY reduced these lil prick’s population in the skies.
I DO NOT agree with how long it takes to grind out General….I understand this was to prevent flooding of the map, and inexperienced players on the strategic side of things, BUT those of us who know what the hell we are doing, should not have to put that many hours in to get there. I’d much rather farm IN GAME CURRENCY to buy straight general than the XP. (If you can buy with in game already, ignore this)
I DO NOT agree with the maintenance upkeep costs. It is nearly more expensive to repair my gun mods after ONE match than it is to buy a new gun or car….wtf. I DO think you SHOULD pay to refill specialty ammo. This makes sense and ammo lasts for some damn time on your rifles (pending trigger happiness). But the cost of keeping your weapon at 100% is way too much to justify to us players… I’d like to see either lower costs or removal of upkeep. (Ammo excluded) I haven’t read anything stating that the condition of our weapon affects the efficiency of said weapon. If it doesn’t affect how your gun operates than take it out… if it does, lower the damn cost….please.
Vehicle maintenance is fine with me… This also makes it an investment if you want to pilot a tank or fighter, thus making the vehicle presence manageable. I MISS HAVING TO LAND AT HOME BASE TO RELOAD MY AIRCRAFT! (Where applicable) This was a great mechanic and took the planes out of the sky for some time. The reload time in air isn’t bad at all, but I’d prefer to land to refuel, repair, and rearm.
THIS GAME IS NOT A PAY TO WIN GAME! It’s a pay because I-don’t-want-to-put-any-hours-into-getting-what-I-want game. You can buy a plane and load out your pilot with more badass equipment than any para, a fresh player can hope into an AAA and blow you out of the sky/ parachute. You can go buy a tank… a low rank can grab 2-3 AT grenades and you are dead before you know he’s behind you. You can buy the biggest baddest LMG, you can be killed by any semi decent player with a primary. Some guns are better than others in certain situations… No one can argue that. But the guns are well balanced, If you stack damage on your sniper rifle, you lose stability, fire rate, range. It’s a give and take. And using a weapon for two to three matches in a row will unlock and allow you to start upgrading components. I felt like I unlocked every option on my Gweh before I even hit rank 2. (I couldn’t afford it because I died a lot but it was an option.)
Overall there are some things we had back pre steam that I’d like to see return, and others that the team has done a great job optimizing.  There is no reason and no cost not to try it out for yourselves. If you are going to try it, give yourself some time to get used to the guns, maps, and mechanics of the game.

I have always enjoyed Call of Duty. I know most people won't agree with me, but I really like the previous ones. Easy, fast-paced action that were fun and addictive. However, the latest installment, Ghost, is a disaster.
The "new engine" is actually just a modded version of the old quake engine, and that is far from next gen. Ghost is laggy in multiplayer, even though I have strong internet connection (100mbit/s) and a computer that can handle most new games on high/ultra settings. You can't change your FOV (field of view), which is stupid. Audio settings is also very poor and I can't mix them as I want. Ghost required a stupid amount (6gb) of RAM at lanch to even run the game, for no apparent reason. That has however been reduced to 4gb now.The game looks awful and still doesn't run well, which is a serious problem.
The new maps in multiplayer are a lot bigger then usual. It seems like they have stolen a lot of ideas from Battlefield 3 here. However, the engine isn't made for these big maps, so It runs with quite poor FPS. The bigger maps is also boring, and it's not what Call of Duty is suppose to be. It should be close combat fights, with fun weapons and killstreaks. It's suppose to be a unrealistic but funny shooter. The opposite of Battlefield.
The game is laggy even in the main menu. It's like they haven't even tested the PC version before lanch. Lazy, greedy, moneygrabbing developers, fake advertising and promises is why this game deserves my fail of the year-award.
They haven't put much time into optimizing the game properly for PC, and that is not acceptable for a big studio like Infinity Ward. Instead of buying this buggy,boring and unfinished mess, go pick up Battlefield, CS:GO, or Call of Duty-Black Ops Instead.

I strongly believe that Far Cry 3 is one of the greatest games of all time. This is means of both story and gameplay.
For this review, I will mainly be focusing on story, so there will be spoilers.
Here we go.

Far Cry 3 this huge, very broad statement about the definition of insanity and the true motives of a man isolated from all that he loves, being forced to fight back against the terrorist government to rescue his friends and family before they're sold to slavery. His brother has already been killed by Vaas, the first real villian you hear of. He is a madman, addicted to drugs and torturing others, but he has a terrible past. He started because his boss (the main villian) killed his entire family, but his sister, to which he dearly cared for, leading him to the brink of meltdown. He is now forced to work for the lead villian, of which I have not found the name of, or be sentenced to death. His sister however is now the leader of the rebels, who fights against Vaas to reclaim the island and restore it back to it's peaceful state.
I find this to be a great story, a very simple concept of corruption in the government done by many other great games, (Just Cause 2, Infamous, Bioshock Infinite, etc.), branched out into things like insanity. This just blows my mind, and I can't imagine what it was like to write the script for Vaas.
There had been only one problem with the game that I have found. (Yes, this is my favorite game of all time, having at least 300 hours on PS3). There is a severe disconnect between story and gameplay. In the game, there are outposts that you need to capture to make Vass' army weaker and gain territory, of which I did a lot of them before the main story to make it a bit easier. In the outposts, you need to kill at least 5 people to gain control of it, not to mention guard dogs, caged animals, and other things. In the beginning of the story however, the main character, Jason Brody, is completely innocent, or acts this way. He is a wimp who hates killing or even hurting others but must do so to gain his friends back. This is seen in the first mission, when he freaks out about stabbing a man that is trying to kill him. So in one mission, Jason has a clear chance to kill the main villian, Hoyt Volker, but refuses because of the mission at hand. Surely in this scenario, the average revenge driven person would have killed Hoyt. Jason does not go for the shot, and I think you even fail the mission if you shoot him. This is even at this point, where I am essentially rambo jesus with an Assaut Rifle, Portable Artillery, a Bow and Arrow that silently one hit kills almost anything, and a sniper rifle.
Do you see the disconnection?
But now I'm starting to think this isn't a problem, and rather adds to the story. Jason slowly progresses in the story to being able to kill, eventually enjoying it and taking pride in killing, (especially when he gets to use the grenade launcher), which I think is brilliant. As when taking outposts, this is not to directly help your friends, but to weaken Vaas. When faced with the concept of his friends in danger, he becomes weak. So I think the disconnection really just adds to the main idea of insanity and true motive.
Overall an astounding storyline that has been analyzed by me a bit too much in my free time. I have played this game far too much but I still love it and continue to play it.

BEFORE YOU GUYS READ ANYTHING. I give this game a 7/10 in its current "beta" phase.
Lets begin.
Firstly, this game is great for people that want to escape the norms of COD or Battlefield to some degree. You have Tanks, Planes, Paratroopers, Infantry, and Recon. Each one is designed to preform a certain task (usually... Some people like to do things that shouldn't be done). You have perfect counters to everything... usually... if you can think for f*** sake.
Plane? use an aa gun
Tank? Find a Panzerfaust somewhere.
Infantry, Paratrooper, or Recon? Man up, grab a rifle, and go hunting.
Need I say more?
Secondly, there is a RTS aspect to the game. Each side (now) has a set stockpile of equipment for disposale (income rates, amounts of vehicles, stockpiling... get it?) Once you get to the Officer ranks you can send out division to fight in the war ( don't be that guy that sends a guard squad up against a Light Armor.. ffs) This opens up new possibilities due to the fact that the players control where the battle is going.
Thirdly, this game is in BETA. Yeah so its been in BETA a long time. It is however adding a bunch of new things to the game that make sense (usually) and help the players. Used to only get SMGs through capping points. Now you get SMGS through killing people w/ your smg (eh). Tanks are being added, and so are more planes (hopefully soon)
Lastly, Its a good World War 2 FPS game. Does that needed to be added upon?? Go sniper jackson in that damn tower.
Some cons.
FPS issues: the Reto team made this software so its going to have a lot of fps issues for now.
Not-Realistic: Yeah the bullet damage is not so keen on being realistic, but the community is pushing for this.
Not much customization (for now): You can't customize your soldiers.. yet. The community is also pushing for this.
You have infantry with sniper rifles: WHY RETO WHY!?!?!
Issues with Teamwork: Yeah its a real good game for teamwork.. when people decide they want to actually work together. The community wants this stuff to be defined a lot more.
1 Person per Tank: not a real big issue, just wish it was better. Ya know?
Plane bombs op af: Yeah, you don't want to be caught outside a whole lot.
Cheers. I guess.

I have nothing but praise for this game.  For a beta game it is FANTASTIC.  Far above COD and the Battlefield franchise in my opinion.  The game is very immersive and intense at times. The game does have some issues, but what Beta game doesn't?  If you're looking for some negatives, the hit detection is not always spot on (this has become very rare), sometimes you will be completely outnumbered, which isn't the developer't fault, it is the generals'.  As any game, it has things that you will love and you will hate.  Overall, this is probably the best FPS I have ever played.  I rank it right up in my books with COD 4.
People keep calling this game a "Pay to Win" game.  It is not.  You can purchase anything from weapons to tanks, and with the tanks, sure, you can pay to get a better tank.  But as far as an form of ground troop, the weapon only means so much.  It would be the equivalent of you being able to buy the highest level assault rifle in Call of Duty.  It really comes down to skill, as the rifle is not going to make that much of a difference to be game changing.  I would NOT call this game "Pay to Win", if anything I would call it "Pay to Avoid Grinding".

A good game. I can feel the terror as I'm searching through a house and i hear a fist pounding on the doors or hear a window shatter as the living dead shamble in after me. The atmosphere is tense and thrilling and this game delivers of the feeling of a zombie apocalpyse. However, to give it an honest review. The game has its share of bugs. Teleporting Zombies, Living Dead not dying after multiple head shots, falling through the ground are one of the many bugs that plague the game (no pun intended). It is also extremely boring to be a zombie, which takes away from the games immersion. Hitting doors is strange given that it gives off a fleshy sound after each impact, infecting players isnt working (at least not on any of the servers I've played). To go back to the light side, Hunt is the shining star of the game, as it adds the HUMAN element to the game that you'd find in AMCS The Walking Dead or Day Z. I'd be searching for weapons with a friend of mine whom I teamed up with and were looking around in an attic when one of the windows shattered and a hail of bullets sprayed into the room, forcing us to duck and work tactically to return fire. Moments like this make the game feel amazing. However, there is a lot in the game that makes me rip my hair out or makes me exit and play Total War instead. The game just doesnt feel worth the $20, instead more like the $4 that i paid for during the thanksgiving sale. I however, cannot be to hard with the game, as it is in its adolescene and if what ive seen so far is only the beta. I cannot wait for what is coming when it is finished. The Game earns a 7/10 with an amazing atmosphere, tense emotions, terrifying living dead and human factor, hunt game mode and a lot of other cool things. only set back is boring as being a zombie and some bugs. I reccomend buying it now as the price is low so you get your moneys worth.

This game is jacked full of bugs and problems. Among those are glitchy character movement, unrealistic physics, terrible exp system ( difficult when there is BARELY a "contribution factor" when it comes to shooting players or HELPING capture a point then die, but still do-able ) , lag ( expected from time to time ) and key mechanics.
I know I know I did not put much time into this game; I did not need to. 13-14 hours is plenty of time (more than I would have liked to spend) to know if you like a game or not. I hated ground wars, since you get very little reward for killing and a LOT for capturing, making the game more or less focused on point control. This was fine but it meant less killing more running. You will get your fair share of kills and deaths, though. It can still be very fun but most of the time fustratingly so.
Every new player must start as an infantryman and work their way to fighter pilot or tank crewman unless you spend money on the game, which I found cool but taxing as I had to fight a very one-sided war since Germany was winning at the time. ( Player-based real-time resources I am sure ).
I become a pilot only to find that Germany had better planes ( mainly because they only have one bomb as opposed to Allies 2 ) which were much more agile. I could not find resupply depots or hangars or ANYTHING of the sort, and I was not sure how to see all points on the map so I could strategically bomb or defend a position from the air, and it takes roughly 100 seconds for your bombs/ammo to be resupplied, then they have to reload.
This last thing was it for me. Any aircraft with HE ( High Explosive ) shells could kill your pilot with only a few shots no matter where it hit your aircraft. My more heavily-armored dive bomber would be shot at and would take minimal damage while my pilot just fell out of the still closed cockpit because of the "impact from the HE shells". Apparently this is how the hosts WANT it to be and is completely unrealistic and nerve racking.
Just to lay that out for you future pilots of H&G that means your slow dive bomber that CANNOT out maneuver a decent German aircraft will be shot down within seconds of being spotted, make this one giant cat and mouse game of getting off a couple of bombs, then running until you die. You may kill some of them or even a few but if they have one pilot with HE who can fly a plane on average you will die in the first couple to few rounds that touch the TAIL END OF YOUR AIRCRAFT.
All of this and apparently things have been this way for a long time, seeing as the game has been in BETA for years now. To me, this whole thing is just one giant joke.
Welp that is my 2 cents, you get what you pay for in this game. Feel free to comment/debate let me know your thoughts.
P.S. there is no defending the aircraft mechanics that is just ♥♥♥♥♥♥, unrealistic, and lazy.

That variety of weapons, array of vehicles and grand strategy you were promised in the teaser? Hope you like spending weeks upon weeks grinding for it, because that's what you're going to do if you want that content.
But wait! You can unlock game content that you want right away without grinding it out! If you want to play some grand strategy, a general is going to set you back $60USD. In real-world money. Pilot? $8 for an entry-level pilot. $24 if you don't want to grind the pilot once you get him. Same for every other class.
Now, this just unlocks the class. If you want those fancy tanks and guns, you've gotta (you guessed it) spend weeks more grinding them or pay for them.
This game is a "free" to play of the worst kind. $60 for the strategy portion could net you Hearts of Iron and all of its DLC, which is a much more thought out grand-strategy than this one. The $24 from the pilot would give you a couple games in the Il-2 series or DCS, which offers significantly more content (you're either flying the P-38 or BF-109) and a better flight model (this game makes Ace Combat's flight and damage model look realistic). For tanks, the combat is unrealistic and other games such as Red Orchestra offer a better (and cheaper) tank damage system. Speaking of red orchestra, you could purchase that game and the Ostefront expansion and have everything this game has to offer without having to do ridiculous things like purchase your own weapons, ammo, and fuel.
Honestly, it's the best war-based first person shooter I've ever played, and it's free!

Far Cry 3 is an awesome game. If you like open world first person shooter games this belongs in your collection.  The game is better balanced than previous Far Cry titles.  I really did not enjoy FC1 or FC2, but I happily recommend FC3.

Let's just look at some of the pros and cons.
___________________________________________________________________________________________________________
GOOD:
- Beautiful. A Lot of Green. Just Beautiful. (Graphically)
- Excellent Gunplay, complete with decent gun sounds, and gun models. Overall a fun shooter.
~ Also decent customisation.
~ Really good animations.
~ Also Healing animations are nice.
- Rewarding stealth system.
- Far Cry 3 Map Editor. Even though almost no one uses it THAT much. The game's map editor is, as far as I can tell, as good as a game engine, most notably CryEngine SDK. (Cause Dunia is a variant of Cryengine)
- Great story. Please don't ask me to write a review on the story.
~ Essentially; believable characters, the villians, especially Vaas, were awesome.
~ Good acting, and VAs.
- Music! Brian Tyler really done the soundtrack really well.
- (Partially) Moddable. Mostly able to change stats and audio.
- Good Variety of wildlife. Mostly belivable too.
- Decent Multiplayer.
- Takedowns are awesome.
~ The Takedown system has good flow. Though I have problems with the Death From Above (OP), and the Gunslinger Takedown.
- You can liberate any outpost how ever you like: Stealth, Long Range, Assault.
- Good variety of side activities, even unique side missions that are similar to the main story missions.
- Climbing Radio Towers is fun. It's also rewarding.
- Wingsuit and parachute are fun to use. Easy to control too.
etc.
___________________________________________________________________________________________________________
CONS
- UPlay
~ Achievements are locked to UPlay instead of Steam.
~ Lost your UPlay account? You can't use the Steam Key again!
- Graphics. Some settings are bundled to certain options. Mostly on Post Processing.

I came to this title in reverse order - that is, I played "Far Cry 4" before getting my hands on "Far Cry 3."
This game is better(!) than its successor.
"4" was bigger, and had a bit more context for some of the knick-knack hunting, but "3" has a much better narrative and is far more focused overall.
The better focus and overall flow of "3" is evident because "3" isn't simply LIKE the next title in the series...it IS "Far Cry 4," but without the sprawl. All the mechanics are the same, or so close that you can't tell the difference without a side-by-side comparison. There's less land-area in this game, but there's still plenty of space to go off the beaten path without facing down an overly long walk to the next landmark. Also, the compactness of the terrain seems to have disincentivized the developers from doing the weird things that "4" did with the wildlife. Sure, predators do attack, but their aggression seems reasonable and well timed in this game. In "4," the constant tripping over♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off creatures with teeth and talons was alternately comical and exasperating.
Also, "3" doesn't always give you a convenient sniping spot for everything. There are times when you're going to have to get in a little closer than you might be comfortable with. This fits with the environment, so it's not a case of being arbitrarily forced out of your preferred playstyle.
Regarding the narrative, Jason Brody is a far more interesting character (and undergoes far more development) than AJ Ghale. The stakes for Brody are very real at all times, whereas AJ's involvement felt weirdly rareified. Jason, like AJ, is an outsider, but he has a group of insiders to relate to and fret over. AJ, on the other hand, had no concrete connections to anybody in the game world.
And Vaas and Volker are far more effective (and interesting) villains than Pagan Min was.
The one thing that was a little strange was how Jason would seem to break character during setpiece missions. He's very serious almost all of the time, yet becomes something of a "snarky bro" when in a pressure situation with one of his friends. It's weird and forced - but also brief enough to be forgiven.
If you crave "Far Cry 4, but better," you just have to take one step BACK in the series.

A lot of new players believe that there is a lot of hacking in this game. I did too actually, and initially gave this game a poor review. Now that I have played a lot more, I realize that what originally appears to be hacking is actually:
Ping (you move out of the way behind a wall but game says you got hit)
Teamwork (I spotted you as a recon from far far away and thus all my team knows exactly where you are for a few seconds. Someone comes round a corner already pointing and firing at your exact location, thus appears to be using a wallhack)
Better mods and badges (as an mmo, you are up against people with "maxed out" characters. Of course you will not do well at first!)
Pure damn luck (I often shoot guys far away as I am moving forwards. 1 in 100 gets a headshot! Or someone shoots you, fails to kill you, you turn around and headshot them! Again, I do this 1 in 100 times but in both cases the victim (understandably) calls hacks!)
Teamspeak etc. (Of course, experienced clans playing together with coms are likely to destroy your team. But games last about 20 minutes, and your next game is just as likely to be against a disorganized rabble!)
And at the end of the day it is Free To Play. Of course there are reasonable advantages to paying (like most games, faster progression) but you get 100% of the game for free!
