Im just gonna leave it there and address the issues people have with this game as and give some tips.
Dont go into this game if you are expecting instant gratification and pop up well dont messages evey ten secounds. Expect to have to put in time to unlock stuff.
I would say take your time and learn to play, as it does not play like CODFIELD games. Learn the games features before ♥♥♥♥♥ing, learn the menus, learn the features or ask on the steam forum. Watch what your team is doing, pay attention. Most in importantly, take a deep breath and slow down, sprinting around in the open and trying to 360 noscope you will fail and fail badly. Learn your weapon; is it effective at short/med/long range, whats the damage like, what do you like/not like about it, what situations is it good in. Early on you will be vulnerable to armour but just avoid it, spot it for people who can kill it or looks for a panzerfaust dotted around the maps. This game is really role based, but if you wish to level quickly unlock the sub machine gun and cap/defend points, then buy the first car to get around and stick to training missions till you know the game better. Maybe look into getting another character as that way you can have various loadouts and dont switch your first character to tanker you will regret it.
The unlocks take time and involve various trees so it is better to think about it as a RPG style progression rather than cod/bf style.  You can pay not to grind if you prefer, its up to you, either way you get the same stuff eventually. Dont think though every other player has payed for their gear (because most havent) and thats why you suck and its so unfair cry cry cry sob sob sob.  The grind can be tedious at points and certain things are very expensive in points, such as the mp40 and thompson, probably one of the worst aspects of the game, but those things are worth it and will slay once earned. Dont just buy things as soon as you unlock them, you may not want/need them. If you put in the time you will be rewarded.

Summing up M&B:W is a rather difficult affair.
The single-player is a fantastic open-world sandbox medieval RPG and the choices you can make are vast. It is a true-to-form sandbox, meaning there is nothing that says you HAVE to do anything.
Raise an army, become a mercenary general, fight for kings in their wars, become a lord, usurp the throne of a kingdom and become the king, start your own kingdom, rule the world... these are all very real possibilities in the single-player mode.
The combat system is fantastic, if a little tricky. It definitely takes a bit of getting used to before you can flawlessly execute the attacks you want and defend yourself, but once you master it, it's incredibly gratifying and it just feels good.
The modding community for this game is fantastic. In my opinion, the single-player side is where the mods stand out, including a couple off the top of my head that change the setting into Westeros or Middle-Earth.
Fantastic game, can't recommend it enough, and it's down to $4 during Summer Sale 2014... you really can't afford not to pick this one up.

My two cents:
First off I just want to say I never had a problem with Uplay. Yes it sucks that the you have to create an account and plug in the key, and use their service but I personally haven't ran into a problem besides them saying, "Hey check this game out" or "buy this" for 49.99 when steam has it for 19.99.
I'm not big on FPS unless they fall into the realm of fallout, where you have looting and you can upgrade. This game is nothing like fallout but I enjoy how it's open word and you can upgrade.
However finding the first animal skins to upgrade your ammo pouch is hard, I had every other skin it seems like besides the bore skins.  When I finally got the bore skins I was able to upgrade and max out my ammo.
The start of the game is rough, your life bar is way too low and even when you heal by injecting yourself with meds you make, you are still taking damage. I think late in the game there is a perk that makes the process go faster but too many times I was destroyed with at least one bar of health while trying to heal.
I wasn't looking for a stealth game but the preview videos and even a tag for this game is stealth.  The stealth elements bearly work. I will say early on in the game they work and will say as far as maybe 5 baddies, but some of these outposts have 15 baddies.  In part it's due to the fact and SHOCKINGLY enough that the A.I. is actually very competent. They react fast, they take cover, heck they even flake you and regroup.
I think in farcry 2, where you could shoot someone in the leg and his friends would come to help would have been a gem in this game. It's like oh, okay "Billy" is dead set off the alarm...Pretty much anything with set off the alarm which basically throws the stealth element out of the game.
I enjoyed the money aspect of the game. Too many times money and loot sort of become useless, all loot in this game is useless mind you, it's just stuff you can sell but the balance between money and buying ammo and bullet proof vests is somewhat balanced. You need to keep looting, you need to do side jobs because we you go after an outpost you are going to have to restock. It can be upwards of a grand to restock everything.
The map and pathfinding is like Assassin's Creed but doesn't work, Since AC is such a hit I think they wanted to put the stealth element in, and this is why the game sort of fails for me. Yes the driving sucks, and the crafting system can be annoying, but when stealth is suppose to be one of your biggest options on how to complete a taste, you feel like this option is just so unreleastic that it takes some time to realize it's broken and they are just using the stealth Tag to get AC players to give it a go... If you shoot someone with high powered rifle, wither or not they are wearing body armor, they are going down, but not in this game.  Maybe if the sniper rifle worked a bit better sealth word, but still wouldnt be enough to complete the stealth element.
As I said, I liked the looting, the perks, and the AI I think is shockngly good but for me, being on my high horse and not a fan of FPS or even steath games I got to go negative because they are trying to make the game something it's not and are trying to make you play in a way that I don't think is really possible. Heck they even Pull out the lame follow this guy and don't get caught from AC, but you can be right on top of the guy.  It sort of feels like they just threw in AC stuff without any focus on it.
In the end the game is worth playing, I will note voice acting is good besides your main character. For whatever reason, and it's not like the actor did a bad job, his voice just doesn't mesh well with your character.

As an early beta, this quite an exceptionally well-crafted multiplayer experience.  Animations are fluid and tactful, movement has weight but takes some time to get used to, the weapon mechanics for guns work as they should and leaves only a little room for improvement, though melee weapons seem to be needing some fine-tuning.
In terms of content, the map variety is limited, weapon variety is also somewhat bare bones as of now with only 2 pistol types, 2 automatic rifles, a grenade, what seemed like only 1 variant of shotgun, 2 SMG's, a rifle, and only a handful of melee weapons, and there is only one enemy type as of yet.  In terms of the games mechanics, it works mostly as it should, some minor updates would make it fully playable in the state it is in, but the content is severely lacking and should become somewhat of a priority.
In terms of recommending it for early beta access, no, I can't say I can recommend it at the pricetag it's at for what you get as of now, but I can recommend it based on the potential that I see for it and what the developers promise to continue offering much later on, and for what the product will be when it is finished.

One day I found this little gem of a series on sale. 3 games for about $7, I said "eh, why not."
I did not expect to find myself playing for days. In fact, I'm still just playing the original, haven't even delved into the two later titles in the series, and it's been over a year. I find myself forcing myself to put it down for periods of time, because whenever I pick it back up I'm hooked for that week.
You start off as a lone adventurer, defending yourself from bandits. You pick fellow travelers along the way, and soon enough you have your own army of mercenaries. You can hire yourself out to one of the warring factions and become force to be feared by all, eventually working your way up the ranks.
It's a sandbox game, you don't have to follow any path but your own. You choose if you want to be a lone wolf or a terrifying general on the battlefield. Numbers play a role in battles, but also your own personal skill, making it oh so gratifying when your group of 50 decimates a challenging army of 200. Even more so when you capture cities with hundreds of enemies in garrison and use it for yourself.
You will have to work for your gains and wealth, but you will so endulged in the game that it never feels like BS grinding or wasted time. The time you put it lends itself to how much accomplishment you feel.
Trust me, it may not have fancy graphics or the prettiest shine, but I've had more fun with it than any big name title in a long while and the replayability is limitless.
Plus just get it on sale when the whole package is under 10 bucks. Think about it, people spend more than that on fastfood for just one meal.

While this is probably one of the most polished Call of Duty games, honestly.... I'm burnt out on them. This one included. The Campaign mode is just like every other CoD since the first one. It just feels like a expansion for Black Ops though. Yes there are some space and underwater battle scenes, building rappelling, tank, helicopter, a remote-control dog scene, and a monorail scene complete with shaky ground that breaks up the typical formula's poke-your-head-out-and-get-shot-dead-from-out-of-nowhere monotony that you've all come to know. I just don't think the mixed gameplay is enough to save it however. Graphically, the game looks amazing... but it's the SAME GAME and with the gaming graphics plateauing across the industry, this is just not good enough any more. I'm just too old for this now.
The campaign plot itself is a new low for incredibly B-movie styled hokey, with no self-effacing gag to at least give a knowing wink to the silliness. The plot only feels tacked on to give some measure of weak cohesion with all the set-pieces. I have to wonder with the billions in sales why Activision can't afford to bother some best-selling military fiction writers to pen something with some more thematic substance and maturity... something that gets me thinking about things more than "war is bad". At least with the early Call of Duty games, I got to learn about the battles of WW2. Now? ...I just learn about some futuristic wank.
However, we all know that most CoD players come for the multiplayer, right? Well, this is always the game's saving grace because it's pretty much the only thing people buy the game for. There are some interesting modes here. Extinction is a kind of mash up of what make CoD Zombies good, except that the aliens are not scary and just annoying. For more 4 player fun, try the squads Safeguard mode. This proves to be similar to MW2's enjoyable survival modes, and is a lot of fun, with my only complaint that you can't play solo with AI like you can with extinction.
In short... Activition is just going to keep making these games because they make a boatload of money with each generation of new players. I waited until I got this on steam discount because I no longer believe that it's worth the silly dollars they're asking at launch.... but having said that, if you're a CoD junkie it's pretty much an essential purchase. You'll buy it anyway... just like the next installment, and even if they replace all the guns with poo-flingers for the inevitable sequel.

I would, honestly, recommend spending your money on something else.  As a gamer, and avid fan of the franchise, I was VERY disappointed.

Summing up M&B:W is a rather difficult affair.
The single-player is a fantastic open-world sandbox medieval RPG and the choices you can make are vast. It is a true-to-form sandbox, meaning there is nothing that says you HAVE to do anything.
Raise an army, become a mercenary general, fight for kings in their wars, become a lord, usurp the throne of a kingdom and become the king, start your own kingdom, rule the world... these are all very real possibilities in the single-player mode.
The combat system is fantastic, if a little tricky. It definitely takes a bit of getting used to before you can flawlessly execute the attacks you want and defend yourself, but once you master it, it's incredibly gratifying and it just feels good.
The modding community for this game is fantastic. In my opinion, the single-player side is where the mods stand out, including a couple off the top of my head that change the setting into Westeros or Middle-Earth.
Fantastic game, can't recommend it enough, and it's down to $4 during Summer Sale 2014... you really can't afford not to pick this one up.

+ It's free and it takes only 1 GB free space, so try it out if you're at all interested.
+ The heroes/generals concept seems to be good (although you will have to pay/grind a lot to find out)
+ It's quite fun as a new experience. You will get some good action in the very first minutes of gameplay.
- Poor weapon physics. Free and unupgraded weapons feel more like bows and arrows.
- Casual health/damage balance. Remember trying to kill somebody with a machine gun in Quake?
- Heavy grind to unlock new content. The purpose of that grinding is not to prolong your fun, but to make your life miserable enough for you to be willing to pay.
- Unrealistic feel. There's a lack of feedback all around: when you get hit, you don't feel it. When you hit an enemy, there's no visible reaction except for damage texts. There's always some intefrace sounds - some drums and fanfares that don't let you concentrate on your surroundings.
- Some premium features are overpowered. For example, you can get an APC for your team on a map where nobody have even AT grenades, blow up all their jeeps and camp the respawn with that heavy MG.
To sum up, it seems like a game about happy carefree people having fun in the woods shooting each other with fake weapons, riding bikes and jeeps, and spending dough on attractions. It doesn't feel like war.

So I was in a skype call riding on the back of a bike with a friend through an airfield, we were getting shot at, and I was screaming that we were gonna die, my friend calmly says "It's okay, they cant hurt us if we're going at a constant speed of fifteen miles..." BOOM!!! A tank managed to hit us dead on as he said that. but in all honesty, a pretty solid BETA, my only complaint is that it's a p2w game.

Was good for a bit... Grind got to be hilariously bad (and made worse with an economy 'rebalance'), P2W-lite in that keeping up with the whales requires thousands of hours of grinding, and constant worrying about whether or not you'll be able to renew your veteran status to keep two badges equipped.
Weapons and vehicles are about as balanced as a drunk, epileptic, one-legged unicyclist on a tightrope at a rave. Nerfs are handed out primarily to whichever faction wins the most, and buffs (to the point that you question why people even play the other factions) are handed out almost entirely to America. Ever wanted to drive a Sherman, survive 6 tank shells dead-on from the side and kill a Panzer III through its front armor at a 45 degree angle in two shells? Well now you can! Want to fire a carbine that fires faster (okay, so it's tied for fastest fire rate) than any other gun in the game with the same accuracy afforded to a bolt-action rifle? Well... Now you can! Enlist for the US Army today!
Don't even get me started on the hit detection. When you have a rocket decide to hit the ground BEHIND the STATIONARY tank TEN FEET IN FRONT OF YOU, you know something's just a bit off.
Hackers were some-what common last I played, it got to the point where my group would stop trying if we saw certain names on the enemy team because they were so obvious, and were around for so long (even after multiple reports), more so than a lot of other F2P games with any reasonable cheating countermeasures.
I'll let the devs and community literally speak for themselves. They'll probably not have very many nice things to say if you don't blindly praise how amazing the game, its community, and its developers are.
1/2/2017
A new year... Not quite a new game. Still pretty much the same, it's actually possible to earn credits using a modded StG-44 now so there's that. EXP grinding is still painfully slow, newer players that haven't thrown literally hundreds of dollars, or 500+ hours at the game are still going to get wrecked by fully automatic anything with their wimpy unmodded peashooters, to say nothing of the snipers and tanks. Haven't noticed any hackers though I'm sure I've been accused of it after going 23/4 with a DP-27. On a German. Point-blank. Against SMGs.
Haven't quite gotten around to seeing how broken the balancing is these days, but I suspect it hasn't changed much since the StG-44 and DP-27 seem to handle exactly the same as they always have.

Grabbed the game recently. As a player who has spent maybe thousands of hours in DoD, DoD:Source, and many other WWII themed games, this one feels great. Characters have a weight to them, and it is slow paced to most of the games that you see nowadays. Animations are smooth, and the game is trying to be authentic; what I mean by that is, you can see your legs and feet for example, when you take cover your character holds the weapon differently, etc... I mean those stuff which you don't see much nowadays.
Graphics are fine. Sounds can use a lot of work though. WWII themed games, I care about sounds by a great deal. UI can also use some work too, especially the "launcher"; it is sometimes unresponsive, and the weapon upgrade screen can sometimes lead you to wrong directions.
Now, maybe the one thing most of you are wondering. Is the game P2W? I haven't invested much time, but so far apart from one thing, I don't think so. The thing that bothers me is, 2nd Badge being available if you are a VIP member. A badge is basically sort of an achievement, and each badge grants you a different kind of bonus. A VIP member will have a badge advantage, and of course, time advantage.
I said time advantage, let me elaborate on that a little bit. Currently, I get around 3-4k points from a match. I recently unlocked a new weapon (unlocking doesn't mean you can use it instantly; it just means you can purchase it now). It requires 120k+ points. That is around 20-30 matches for a weapon that I cannot test, and it is a bit too much. I hope they add a trial system, giving you access to a weapon for 2-3 matches, to get a feel for that weapon.
There aren't many weapons in the game yet, and buying a weapon by the hard-earned points you acquire is a big investment. You can also tweak your weapons, but they have not much of a visual/aural effect as far as I can tell. I hope they'll add more weapons soon, I'd like to see British weapons for example.
The vehicle aspect of the game is definitely interesting. As you progress, you have a choice to become a tanker or a pilot for example. And these two roles may have a dramatic impact on the battles; infantry is always the key, but infantry without support is often bound to fail in their duties.
I have a problem with long battles though, you aren't properly rewarded for your commitment in my opinion. And some battles may drag on for very long. And if you are using a modded weapon, the longer the battle is, the higher your repair cost probably would be. I hope they'll take a look at the repair costs, and maybe fix it to a percentage of gains so that it will be balanced for long battles.
Speaking of battles, they are actually somewhat different from other games, and it is very interesting. The battles themselves may not be balanced, but the overall war (generally) is. High ranking players commit units to battles, and battles dynamically change as you are playing it; new fronts can open up, and existing ones can collapse for example. Reinforcements can turn the tide of the battle, and lead up to epic experiences. The same dynamic battle system can also lead to battles where your enemy or you has overwhelming forces, which can also end up in heroic fights for the overwhelmed side.
Now, before a conclusion, here is a dynamic battle example. Our side just had a small guard unit (only 3 infantry players), while the enemy had a motorized infantry unit (5 infantry players, with armored transport). Against the odds, we successfully held the enemy for a long while, and our Generals send us reinforcements. As we were about to crush the enemy, their generals send them reinforcements too, as well as opening up new fronts, dragging the battle even further. In the end, we were victorious, and I felt great about that, as I was one of three infantry that held the line for a long time.
Overall, I recommend this game to anyone who are interested in the FPS genre in general. If you like WWII theme, definitely give it a try. From F2P aspect, weapon costs could get a tweak, and 2nd badge could be made available to everyone at a certain rank, but nothing major aside from that.

Alright, where to begin...
The game is completed, story wise. I would say i haven't enjoyed a game that much for quite some time.
Story was great, although would have prefered the villain be  done little better. The main villain of the game was little unneccesary. Not complaining, i had fun either way. Vaas was definitely the most well made character in that game by far, they completely nailed it.
This game has a lot of side activities to do, i mostly did story, which was around 20 hours. I did play on the master difficulty, which was even more fun and quite challenging at the same time. I liked moments where i had to think throughout my actions to make sure i succeed.
Animal hunting is also interesting addition to the game, i actually liked hunting animals. The purpose of hunting animals is for the hide you use to craft from additional weapon slots (up to 4) to inventory slots. You can craft medicine, boosters etc by cutting different plants. Also getting better upgrades require  better quality hides from animals.
I absolutely loved the driving mechanics in this game. It really feels like driving a real car, with a little extreme aspect added to it. Very responsive steering and accelerating in general, even handbrake was useful. Crashing was quite realistic.
I am not sure about the AI behaviour since i played on the highest difficulty, but from what i experienced- AI is quite active, compared to some games. Even though i used stealth in most cases, they still discovered dead bodies of their comrades and were alerted right away which made it more challenging to do stealth, i liked that a lot too.
Not only crafting, but skills were interesting too. There were basically 3 types of styles you could end up doing- I picked stealth. You can acquire skills by getting XP from stuff you do. When you lvl up you can pick a skill, every skill adds a part to your tattoo on your left hand. I really liked how it transformed into a pretty cool tattoo in the end.
World is quite huge and environment is really gorgeous. I loved gliding over huge mountains and just looking at the nature.
There are also collectables... 4 types i think-> chests, relics, memory cards and lost messages.
There were minor things that bothered me a little. For example quite annoying was when after a cutscene you had to do something and you failed- you had to watch the cutscene all over again. Made me rage few times :D I wish there was an option to skip the cutscene after you've seen it already once.
For now that's all i can remember about the game, still going to do all the side missions and get all the collectables some time in the future.
To sum up i'd say this is best of Far Cry so far(even better than 4). If you want to play it and enjoy the hell out of it, play on the highest difficulty, makes the game last longer ;) Surprisingly works stealth quite well in this game, which is unusual for such straight-forward games. Make sure you know what style you wanna go and make your skill decisions wisely ;)

I was wondering why I had barely heard of anyone playing this game, or why nobody ever talked about it; it's pretty apparent why now though. It's a wallet warrior's dream, but for those looking for an actual game, look elsewhere.
So I thought this game was really fun at first, gave it a good review and was really enjoying the gameplay. As you get further in, however, the game really begins to lose it's fun, and fast.
You start to see how screwed the ingame economy is. For example, in order to counter enemy tanks, you're going to need the Panzerschreck, which is 35000 silver. That's not bad, if you're a decent teamplayer you get roughly 3000-4000 per match. But when you use it, you're spending thousands to restock it's ammo. Which, if you need to use it a lot in a particular match, often leaves you with a negative balance of silver. In a single match I had to spend over 5000 to replenish it.
Same goes for vehicles, you're going to be spending thousands per match repairing and restocking your vehicles to the point where your meager amounts of silver per match won't cover it, and you'll slowy dwindle your resources until you're forced to use stock gear again. Leaving you ♥♥♥♥ed if the enemy team has a lot of vehicles.
Ontop of that, past the beginner weapons you're going to be expected to spend absurd amounts on new weapons (an MP40 costs 127,000) and that's ontop of grinding ribbons for them to be unlocked, and saving up silver without losing it all from repairs and ammo.
Tired of recieving negative amounts of credits? Want to unlock new weapons and vehicles? Shekel up goyim, and you can have everything instantly :^) you won't even have to level up, paying does that for you!
edit: looks like even the devs acknowledge this. Check out the ultimate packs and the description for them on Steam.
"This pack enables you to get the full Heroes & Generals experience, where you can play all roles as Heroes on the battlefields AND command Assault Teams as a General without first having to spend hours, weeks and even months of playtime to progress your characters and unlock weapons, equipment and vehicles."
They're TELLING US to forget about playing, just fork out money to get the 'full experience', as if having to play is a chore. Shouldn't the entire game be fun, not just when you fork out $110 or spend months grinding? What ever happened to putting time into a game because it's enjoyable? Not because you 'have to' to have fun...

This game is very unique.  It is a really good shooter with unique qualities. So each and every battle is strategically important.  Furthermore, the units you can use on each battle are controlled by an RTS game to which you can contribute.  You can earn or pay for units that if destroyed are removed from the RTS game.  These can be planes, tanks, paratroopers, infantry or recon troops.  And each one of those has specialised troops within with vehicles and what not that you can unlock as you progress in the game.  Overall, it is very enjoyable.  while the mechanics are familiar, the way you play and enjoyment  you get out of the game is better than a standard shooter.

100% Battlefield clone. I don't care for the Battlefield franchise, and I have absolutely no interest in a clone of that franchise.
That aside, there are other reasons not to play the game. Aiming is not smooth to the degree that any modern shooter should be. Matchmaking takes at least 2 minutes to find a game, and then usually puts you in a game that has less than 2 minutes left in the match. Furthermore, even though you have over 10 members on your team, only about 8 can be deployed at once. If your team does a good job of not getting killed, you could wait for a good 5 minutes waiting for someone to die. Also, there apparently are only 3 maps at present, so even if this is a beta, it's not a very entertaining one.
While Battlefield allows you to operate vehicles and choose what loadout you want, you need levels to operate vehicles in this game. Furthremore, you have to spend countless hours leveling your 1 default character build before it gives you any selection as to what class you would like to play. Didn't games use to be about having fun?
The biggest issue, however, is the hit detection. I have never played a multiplayer shooter that has such a problem registering hits as much as this. The game fails to register about 1/2 of the shots fired, that were on target. This is not due to lag (you can shoot a camper that hasen't even moved for the last 5 minutes and it will still not register the first shot sometimes), it's just incredibly bad programming. If you download this game, prepare to be frustrated beyond belief (especially if you are using bolt action rifles). Back in 1998 I played Delta Force 2 on a 28k dial-up modem and had none of these issues that this game has, lag is not even remotely an excuse for their coding issues.
Basically it's Battlefield 1943 all over again with slow matchmaking, heavy restrictions and the same maps over and over and a game-breakingly buggy hit detection system. It's a relatively small download, but there is still no reason to bother.

Essentially a WW1 version of Planetside 2, except you have to unlock even MORE of the game's content. Although a player willing to drop a hefty chunk of change on items, or play a pretty boring bog-standard FPS with needlessly large maps for a while will eventually start to have an interesting multiplayer experience, I can't in good conscience recommend this given the existence of both Planetside 2 and Team Fortress 2.
Item's credit (in-game currency) costs are prohibitively high, which is one thing when one starts with a variety of options to choose from, but entirely another when everyone starts armed with the same rifle and grenade. Furthermore, grenades have a hefty restock cost taken from the credits you have earned.
The tactical side of the gameplay is as tactical as any massively multiplayer FPS, which is to say, not very. Besides this, there is a huge investment needed to access this side of the game, one that I find not worthwhile.
There's the core of a good game here, and to be sure, it IS early access. It could morph into something beatiful. At this time, though, I don't recommend spending much time on it.

This game is like a Micheal Bay movie. It's loud, stupid, silly, full of style but so little substance. Truth be told, the gameplay is fun. It really is. Open world exploration, lots of stuff to do, hunting, taking down objectives with lots of flexibility, yada yada.
PROS:
- Gunplay and combat is fun.
- Minor RPG progression creates some variation in gameplay.
- Very pretty to look at. The islands are gorgeous.
- The wingsuit and vehicles are loads of fun.
CONS:
- Uplay is an idiotic service and needs to die in a hole.
- The story just...sucks. So much. I hated it.
- The characters are bad and just plain unlikable. I hated each and every one of them with a passion. Except Vaas. Vaas was great. I love Vaas.
- Climbing towers to unlock maps got old very, very, very fast. Stop it. It's dumb.
- The map is littered with collectibles that are practically worthless. There's no reason to go look for chests. Literally no reason. It's lame. Also, don't reveal chests on the map. It ruins all the fun of exploration and looking for them. Hell, even when you open a chest it's just filled with items that are just sold for cash.
- The story drags on. For a game with a pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥ story/characters to begin with (IMO), that ain't good.
- The game tries to deal with some pretty dark and ♥♥♥♥ed up stuff (drugs, sexual assault, human trafficking) but it does it so immaturely that it feels dumb and takes away from the experience.
The combat and open-ended gameplay are pretty much the main reasons to play this game. There isn't much beyond there to warrant it. That said, I do feel that there are a lot of other games that can deliver very similar experiences in a much more complete package.
If you see it on sale for cheap, pick it up. Otherwise, you're better off skipping out.

I downloaded this game several weeks ago at the behest of an online gamming buddy of mine. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! Just kidding! I blame him for my new found addiction of Heros & Generals. I have some complaints of course. But all games are going to have their flaws and drawbacks. It IS in Beta...so it's still a work in progress. They're also going to have their good points too.
One main complaint I have is the progress/achievment status update that appears RIGHT IN YOUR SIGHT-LINE during gameplay and blocks your view of WHERE YOU ARE GOING! Very bad design on that part. The makers should place that status update bar either "Center Bottom" or "Center Top" of the game play screen. Everyone I speak with in-game all agree that it needs to be MOVED!
Also, they definitely need to work on the natural movement of characters in-game. Movement isn't human or fluid. You sort of drift and float, rather than stop when you are supposed to be stopping. Example: You are running...you have to turn right or left quickly...but what you really end up doing is skidding, floating or drifing past where you were trying to end up. Humans really don't do that. Transitions into and from vehicles is cumbersome...luggy and very slow.
There should be some options for players as well. Eventually, you can start to purchase personnel vehicles. The American side has a great motorcycle that is almost impossible to crash...that goes for their Jeep as well. But the Germans have a Kubelwagen that skids all over the place, spins out and fish tails constantly. A very unstable vehicle to say the least. The German Motorcycle with Side Car is similar in that it too is very unstable and difficult to control. It would be nice if you had the option to have the side car or not. Even up the balance of play a bit...that's what that would do.
Otherwise...the game is a blast. And there are plenty more things to praise as well as complain about. But since it's the most expensive FREE game I have ever played on Steam (Spent a total of about $133.15) in order to have more options available...for that price, I would hope that the makers of this game take heed of some of the more common sense requests for changes in the game to heart. I'd hate to see this game go the way of the Dodo Bird, just because it's starts to lose popularity. I've invested WAY too much money (REAL MONEY MIND YOU) in their FREE game to see it go away.
They also need to get an in-game communication system up and running for the separate teams. They mention that the "T" key does this...but it does not. Most people...if they either hook up or you have buddies that all join the game, end up using either "Steam Chat" (which is squirly at best) or they use "Mumble" (which I hate...because I lost all in-game sounds...special effects sounds, foot steps, etc. the day I installed it and went through the set-up protocalls) and then there's Ventrillo I guess and some others. So personally, I wish they would just get the Team Voice Chat to work. That's not such a difficult thing to do...is it? I don't know. I'm not a computer programmer.
O.K., well...thank you for the opportunity to allow my input. Fun game!

Fun for the first few hours, but easily sours beyond that.
I understand the game is in beta, but there's mutiple issues with it that must be addressed.
First, the credit system and its way of handling explosives. Many games involving tanks I come off with less credits than I had before; example, I gained 5k credits but to resupply my rocket launcher, grenades, and repair my vehicle costs 9k credits. Not liking that at all. Two way this can be fixed: remove credit consumption upon explosives, or give the panzerfaust (the launcher picked up in the field) more rounds.
Second, the optimization. On any other game I can get a smooth 30-45 FPS when there's 48+ players fighting in an area. This game barely has 10 fighting in an area and my framerate dips down to 10 or 15. Any smoke or explosions whatsoever kill the framerate. Not good at all. As for the rest of the game, a large amount of optimization could be used by allowing shadows to be turned off. Not as good in terms of looks, but an excellent increase in performance.
Third, the extremely heavy weighting towards purchasing weapons with cash instead of credits. I understand that they have to make their money, but the amount of pressure they're putting on you to buy something with real world cash is ridiculous. Example: it takes 75,000 credits to buy the bolt action rifle. If we're not resupplying on any grenades, launcher rounds, or repairing vehicles,  with an average of 3,500 credits per battle, it comes out to 21 battles. Multiply that by the 25 minutes it takes on average to complete a battle, and you get almost 9 hours.
9 hours spent in a game with your basic weapons, no grenades, and nothing to defend against tanks taking you out for... a bolt action rifle. And that's not counting the amount of time spent just getting up to that start point. I just have to say, no. And that's with getting a surefire 3,500 credits per battle. Sometimes I earn even less than that.
I'll keep playing for a little bit longer in hopes that this might improve once I finally get the rifle or maybe something else. After that, if it doesn't, I'm out.
Edit: Two things that could also make it better. Add the option to continue training matches beyond level 3, say up until you get your first unit to command. Second, remove deploy delay penalty for suicides. Its just stupid to be penalized for something that 99.99% of the time was an accident.
Edit 2: Just went through regular random matchmaking, spent 10 min helping neutralize the last two access points for the enemy. Battle ended, got 0 credits and 0 warfunds. Not happy at all.

The most frustrating game I have played in a while.
I am really interested in Heroes & Generals. I love the concept as well as the throw back to old WWII shooters like call of duty and battlefield 1942. There are forever a few major flaws in the game which I cannot stand.
1. The game progression is way too slow. You are barely rewarded for kills so I tried spending most of my time capturing points. But even with a descent KD ratio and number of caps, I only seem to get 200-300 XP out of a game. Since it takes 6000XP to reach level 4 from 3 and the class I am interested in (paratroopers) requires level 7 the grind is just too long.
2. The action moments are few and far between. This game is a lot of fun when you get on a kill streak and you are working as a team. But I spend most of my time respawning, running between shortness of breaths and getting killed almost as soon as I get in the fight. Taking a jeep only makes you a bigger target from what I've experienced.
3. Unbalanced. You cannot have fun when you are up against tanks, snipers, and dive bombers when all you have is an M1.
4. Unintuitive. There are a lot of things that don't make sense. For example why can't you switch loadouts between deaths? If the loadout isn't working in a certain scenario i.e. against tanks, why can't I change my loadout or character?
5. Clunky movement. The movement is not meant to be crisp like bf4 or cod, I get it. But I think ithe responsiveness is excessively slow. slowing down, jumping, even running into a doorway is difficult in this game.
6. Money. Just like the latest episode of South Park on fremium games: this game is barely fun unless you sink money into it to get the good weapons and classes.
The game is still in beta and I hope some of these issues will be addressed. But as it stands now, I find the game rather unenjoyable. Which is a shame because I love the concept.

This game easily used to be my favorite of the free to play games. For as long as this game has been around people have always complained about the way sniper rifles and scopes worked in the game. If you were a sniper, you got a scoped rifle you could mod. If you were infantry you could get a scoped rifle, but it could not be modded. This sytem worked perfectly. Not everyone in the world had a scoped weapon. You had teams of people who actualy made attempts at objectives instead of everyone camping with a scope. Of course a lot of players didnt care for this system. Every one just wants to be a sniper. Somewhere around the walker update is when this game started going down hill. The removal of a 2X base magnification wasnt so much of an issue for me. What this actualy did though was make the sights on the U.S. and Soviet factions rifles perfect, but in turn added what I beleive to be an unintended nerf to the german bolt action rifle. You can hardly see the front sight. Now when asked for an explination as to why the base magnification had been reduced. The reply I received from one of the devs was " The new players coming to the game wont miss anything. It is only the long running and current players that will know they are missing anything" I was taken back by this response. Alienating your current players base in an attempt to bring in more players doesnt seem like a good buisness strat. But its not my company, so I continued to play. Figureing I will just need to adapt to the changes and hope the path Reto-Moto has in mind will keep supplying me with a great game. They hadnt done me to horribley wrong yet and were still supplying me with fun. The patch that had followed however ruined the game for me. A scope could now be mounted to just about everything in the game. It was at this point I realized exactly what had happened. Magnification on the rifles was reduced and then scopes introduced in an attempt to increase in game purchases so a player could remain competative. Not only did they do this with the addition of scopes and reduction of base magnification, but the cost of running the match iron sights on a rifle will end up costing you 4-6k more in repairs then if you run a scope. I can not in good conscience recommend a game that at any point could see a game altering change made in order to harvest funds from the player base. I know from previous experiences with FTP games that once a Dev team does this they will continue do it.

The core game is very great. The combat mechanics are pretty interesting as you can choose which direction you swing your weapon. There are a variety of weapons to use and you acquire greater skill in a weapon by using it in battle.
The 'vanilla' campaign is features a very large map which a variety of kingdoms. You can improve your standing with a kingdom and continue to create more money and create a bigger army. Starting the game is quite hard as you must build up an army that is first high in quanitity and later better in quality of troops. However, this can be easily overcomed by competing in tournaments hosted at random big cities. After getting past the difficulty at the beginning of creating a big army, it does get quite easier.
This game features a ton of mods both to campaign and multiplayer. There are mods that completely overhaul the game, changing the units in each kingdom, changing the entire map, adding new weapons and armours, and/or changing various core mechanics such as creating your own kingdom, becoming a soldier of another lord's army, and such. You can have a hard time trying to pick a mod to use, but when the right one is found, a lot more opportunities not presented in the 'vanilla' game are opened up.
I have not tried multiplayer, as the campaign is fun enough to play.

I'm not one to expect groundbreaking new features in Call of Duty, in fact... I would have been happy if this was just BO2 with different guns and maps.  But it's a step backward in every area.
They are a step back from BO2 for sure.  Graphics wise, it's comparable to MW3 or MW2.  Textures are low-res, models uninspiring, and maps unimpressive.
Usually with games, you have a choice.  The game can look great, but run poorly on most hardware... like BF4.  Or it can look bad, but run great like State of Decay.  But with Ghosts, on the otherhand, you get a game that looks bad and plays terrible.  Turning everything down, I could finally muster out 70-80fps... but zoom in with any scope, and I'm down in the 30s.  I can run Battlefield 4 on higher settings and get more frames.
Want to change your VOIP volume?  Nope.  Want to see your ping?  You don't even get connection bars in Ghosts.  Theater mode, no can do.
There's really nothing here for even the most diehard CoD fans.  People have complained about CoD being a bad console port for some time now, but this is the first one where actually I agree with them.

Contagion is the great successor of Zombie Panic Source, that succesful game that came out years ago.
In this new game, you now have new objectives to accomplish along other survivors, finding weapons and making your way to the exit by either sneaking on zombies or runnning into it with plenty of ammo.

You are able to barricad yourself in houses( the only one opened in the maps are those for objectives, sadly.) and to heal your partners.
For the part about where you die and turn into a zombie, they managed to fix one of the biggest complain of the first game, the zombie gameplay was boring, now fixed by the adding of new options such as grabbing, running and trying to act like a normal zombie, only so a imprudent survivor run right next to you and get bitten.
There is still the infection part, which makes this game unique and nice.

I also have hopes that new maps and custom maps will be added.
I highly advice this game for zombie fans .

There are only 4 maps for now: one is co-op objective and three for Hunted (deathmatch) game mode. Also there is a extraction game mode but it's getting old pretty fast. So does the whole game.
But the problem is not in that there are few maps, rather strange recoil and jittery 3-rd person animations. The major problem is that word 'boring' does not fully describe playing Contagion as a zombie. While some features (like glow and outlines are being added) are being worked on, lack of features like mini-map or zombie shortcuts/paths for faster map navigation making that experience painful. Try playing on objective map as a zombie and you'll want to leave server quite fast because hanging around mindlessly over a huge map is not fun by any means. If you somehow find a way to survivors you have nothing extra that makes player controlled zombie better than a AI zombie. But being a human is no better. Somehow, Monochrome made a co-op game without most co-op related features. Really, all you need your buddies for is to carry a key? In fact, a some kid could get one and do not know it, so co-op progress will halt as other players even do not know who got a valuable co-op items!
Lastly, developers do not fix critical bugs and adjust game play mechanics as fast as I'd like to see in a multiplayer only game. They do regular content updates (like Halloween and X-mas updates) thought.
As for now, it's hardly a game I'd recommend to anyone due to it's gameplay. It's really gets boring after 2-5 hours of play. Pretty picture, neat sounds and randomized fences/ locked doors alone just can't keep the gameplay up.
Zombie Panic: Source is still a much better game. And it's free.
P.S. I've backed Contagion on Kickstarter and played the game before most other players. I will update my review tone if anything will change in a positive way.

Contagion, a game (currently in beta) created by the makers of the incredible mod Zombie Panic: Source, brings you an incredible and unique experience.
The Pros: Unique gameplay brings you a refreshing experience of what it would really be like in a zombie apocalypse. Whether you're fighting other players while avoiding zombies, or working with them to escape or defend locations, it's always a blast.
Random generation makes every playthrough different in some way, guns and ammo spawn in different locations and objective modes can change every time with different paths and areas. The phone with objectives and maps is an awesome concept too.
Play as a zombie and blend into AI hordes or sneak up on humans to snag a bite. With player controlled zombies, it brings a continually terrifying threat that forces you to watch your back constantly.
Cons: While this game is still in beta and can't yet be fully judged, it does lack maps. The random generation helps but there are currently only three maps you can play on. Game is still being optimized, recent patch helped a lot.
TL;DR All in all, a fantastic game that is definitely worth $15 even in beta!

All start as a soilder and you earn the most points by captureing enemy locations, and smaller points for kills, weapon use and whotnot.
You begin with skirmishes that have 3-4 capture locations on a smallish map. When you earn high enough rank you can enter large scale battles with 10 or so captures.
It is a browser based game so most machines should play it.
Anyway, it is your standard WWII fps with the combat and all but at certain ranks you can branch off and permanatly switch your infantry character to a piolet, tank driver, paratrooper ( you actually deploy from planes) recon (snipey Sniperson) and last a General.
Each role has unique missions to perform and are feezably balanced.
Each role has specialty weapons that class spawns with but with XP you can unlock all the weapons, vehicles and upgrades you want.
The game also features a ribbon aspect that work like perks to your character.
After reaching General you can enter a stratagy side of the game I hear plays like Risk that gives your side more resources and helps the war effort. ( I haven't reached General yet, so I really don't know the details.

Boosters for ribbon earning and xp gain can also be bought.
Sure people say pay-to-win but not "really" you just pay to unlock faster.
You can also become subscribers and pay a membership to get extra xp bonuses as well.

An Interesting title i picked up.
Essentially a graphically upgraded version of the ZPS mod, Contagion features serveral gamemodes to amuse yourself with.
Early Access right now, can't say a helluva lot. Will require several coats of polish.
Some things i have to mention.
-There are few weapons as of current... Expect to squabble among your "fellow" Survivors whether who gets to keep what weapons.
-The zombies are apparently allergic to bullets and any kind of damage, as the go into a severe state of anaphylaxis when a bullet strikes them. This makes for a frustrating time aquiring headshots.

The core game is very great. The combat mechanics are pretty interesting as you can choose which direction you swing your weapon. There are a variety of weapons to use and you acquire greater skill in a weapon by using it in battle.
The 'vanilla' campaign is features a very large map which a variety of kingdoms. You can improve your standing with a kingdom and continue to create more money and create a bigger army. Starting the game is quite hard as you must build up an army that is first high in quanitity and later better in quality of troops. However, this can be easily overcomed by competing in tournaments hosted at random big cities. After getting past the difficulty at the beginning of creating a big army, it does get quite easier.
This game features a ton of mods both to campaign and multiplayer. There are mods that completely overhaul the game, changing the units in each kingdom, changing the entire map, adding new weapons and armours, and/or changing various core mechanics such as creating your own kingdom, becoming a soldier of another lord's army, and such. You can have a hard time trying to pick a mod to use, but when the right one is found, a lot more opportunities not presented in the 'vanilla' game are opened up.
I have not tried multiplayer, as the campaign is fun enough to play.

Contagion: a masterpiece thrown into the gutter and smashed right into pieces. My criticisms you ask? I'll give you my criticisms alright! When I initially purchased this game I was under the impression that the game would deliver some challenges with its content by being possibly overrun by tens and thousands of zombies while completing objective based maps that tested the strengths and virtues of my team. Well, I guess the whole being overrun thing didn't happen exactly as I previously thought. I'd say the mere fact I can't even hit the zombies' head due to the lack of an accurate hit box is enough for a gamemode itself. That's right, have fun trying to headshot zombies that squirm out of place everytime you have your ironsight accurately stationed at their forehead, it won't happen -- even if your ping is fantastically at 20 or less! The mobs, zombies, in this game are fantasically bugged beyond all belief with their seizure-like squirms that run in abundance throughout the packs of zombies in the game. As far as spawning new zombies in the game, I don't think there are many spawn points for new zombies, I actually think once you kill one they're dead for good again. I did like the running animation of your character while in first person, why with your arms extended upwards to your right while holding your handgun running like a squad member, who needs quality game mechanics when you can just watch your character run all day long looking cool!
Continuing on, let's talk about the attention to detail needed within this game, especially while playing objective mode. Have fun trying to find your way around the map trying to complete vaguely written objectives that'll surely take you hours to finally find and complete. It literally took my friend and I several hours, about 2 hours in fact, to finally find an important key needed to unlock a door in the first objective based map in the game, especially with little to no clue or even a semblance of a clue as to where to go. Now, I understand the need for a survival oriented sense of dread and hopelessness within a zombie game, but to have players running around the first half of a map endlessly for hours is just plain griefing the player base in general. A sort of indication on where to go, even a tiny general one, goes a long way while still keeping that frightful atmosphere of dread and despair. So besides being clueless in this game, I also noticed that every single zombie resembles a main character within the game, so you won't have to die to see yourself reincarnated as a flesh devouring rot head, you'll shoot a couple of them before you do so, not a unique feature at all. Another issue I had with the game is its lack of administrative features given to its players. There is no voting system in place to vote kick griefers, change maps, or even restart a current level. There's nothing at all besides possibly using console commands.
While I can understand this game is still in its infancy, technically beta/alpha level, the game does currently lack in a lot of content such as the amount of maps within the game, only 4 maps currently, and the MANY bugs that currently plague the game. I've only really mentioned a handful of bugs I've noticed so far but I'm sure you'll find more once you purchase this game. Another thing that really annoyed me after the fact I bought this game was the falsly advertised store page for the game when I first bought it stating that the game is in early access, which would imply it's in beta status not a seemingly preliminary alpha access. On a final note, if you ever get the chance to breeze through the game's forum page, you'll noticed a bunch of self-righteous devs who denounce any little criticised comment about their dear game and instantly shun what fanboys the game does have. I don't recommened this game to anyone, at least at the current moment where the game is stil lacking a stable environment to play in.

Better late than never on a review. FarCry 3 is one of the best games out still, even now after FarCry 4s release. This is a heavy-statement, but the fact still remains that the story, character development, gameplay mechanics and player immersion are well presented, well blanaced and inherently iconic to this game.
As the player, you will either come to like and develop with Jason or not, but as time progresses you become aware that the player, the protagonist Jason Brody, is not the player at all. The jungle, the rocks, trees and shrubbery are on display as the central role in this first-person story, the wildlife are the supporting cast, and the pirates and soldiers simply provide their cameo apperances. This allows the story to hold-up amongst all the sneaking, tagging, crafting and collecting, and allows the player to become fully imersed in the world without having to resort to a WWJD sense of mind. (Jason)
For those who have not played this yet I implore you to buy as you will not be disapointed. However I also feel if you started with FarCry4, not to compare too much as you will want to take on the story and the depth of the enviroment as it's own concept.

Mount and Blade Warband...where you go around slaughtering hordes of people until finally, after many strategic battles and wars, you have conquered all of Calradia. Now, sitting on your throne, you think back to the years you spent taking this throne. You think of all the families you displaced, all the men who fought giving Calradia a greater future. A future under you rule, a future of glory and fame. A future which you have given Calradia, a future which you control. A future, in essence, which ebbs and flows to your command, your power, your armies. And you, the greatest person ever to set forth into the land of Calradia, have created this future. You, not Aiden Pierce. Not the Dragonborn. Not Steve. No. The person behind all of this is you, you as you want to be.
And perhaps, besides the gameplay, this is what makes Mount and Blade Warband simply stunning, a masterpiece of war and games. The fact that there is no hero, no true great king or legend. It is simply what you want to make of your character, all the options are given to you. You may be the low bandit, running in the night and hitting up the caravans and farmers.  You may be the cruel lord, one who will have his men die at his orders and his peasants work to death to pay for the death of those solders, all because of fear. You may be the commoner, rising up and becoming a threat to lords and, maybe one day, to entire kingdoms. You may be the heroic knight, who returns the golden throne to it's rightful owner. You may be the black king, one who destoys life with no hesitation, and locks up all who oppose him in the deepest and darkest dungeons. you may be the white king, who makes sure that every peasant is treated fairly, and even the bandits are given chances at redemption. You may be the hired soldier, who goes around and sells his sword to the highest bidder. You can, if you truly want to be and have hours to waste, the helpless princess. Who gets themselves caught over, and over, and over, and over, and you get the point.
But no matter what you are, it doesn't change the fact that you can go to places other than Calradia. You may enter the land of Game of Thrones, through the Clash of Kings mod, to name one. But even if native ever gets boring, which is unlikely (I'm still not bored yet!), you can get mods. And so, the fight goes on, and on, and on, and on...like Steve Perry has told us.
To tell the truth? I think this game should be priced higher, I feel like I've gotten at least thousands of dollars out of it.

Generally speaking, I don't play a ton of first person shooters. I'm probably dating myself here, but the last shooters I got into were when I was a kid playing the original Doom and Wolfenstein 3D games. That being said, I think the only games that match the amount of hours I've plugged into Far Cry 3 are XCOM and the Civilization franchise.
The reason for this is because Far Cry 3 is chocked full of story.
Mechanically, the game has a lot going for it despite its relative age. I think this is why I keep coming back to it. I still haven't been able to craft every item in the game. Each item requires you to hunt down a specific type of animal and skin them. Once you do, you can use the hides, feathers, etc. to craft different things that will aid you. There are usually four tiers to each type of item, the fourth of which requires you to hunt down a very specific creature and skin it. The hunting mechanics are pretty incredible.
You can use various injections to give yourself a bonus when hunting or in combat, crafted out of specific type of booster syringes made from plants on the island. Some of these allow you to better resist fire, or will give you the ability to sense animals or enemies in your vicinity (displayed on the minimap), or might make you seem undetectable or non-threatening to animals. There are a lot of vehicles lying around on the island. Unlike Far Cry 2, most of these are just regular trucks, cars, or quads with the occasional vehicle set up with a mounted fifty cal on the back. This also applies to boats and jet skis.
As the game progresses, you will gain experience points - this happens through completing various objectives like taking outposts, hunting specific types of animals, completing missions, etc. Once you reach a specific amount of experience, you can advance Jason's skills through a skill tree system. This is represented in-game by a quasi-magical tattoo (called the Tatau in the game). It's a tribal-like tattoo that forms on your arm and gives you specific abilities centered around athletic and combative feats. There are three tiers of advancement: the Shark (direct confrontation), the Spider (stealth skills), and the Heron (movement and athleticism). This is used in a deus ex machina fashion to explain why Jason suddenly has a mastery of physical combat and has such an edge over his opponents. This is less annoying than it sounds, because of the way they incorporate it into the lore of the game.
The game also has a kickin' soundtrack.
In short, with the game's mechanics, the story line, and the commentary on the fragility of one's inherent humanity when forced into Seeing Some Stuff, I will always come back to Far Cry 3. It's probably one of the most well-crafted games in the last decade.

Heroes & Generals -  This game IS still a beta game, so with keeping that in mind, let me tell you a few things about it.    War is hell.   Starting out in this game in the European Theater can be just like the real war - hell.   You hit the ground running in the real time shooter game on either the Allied Side or the Axis side.  Initially, not knowing where to go, you will get blown up, ambushed and sniped, maybe even hit by a jeep.   But persevere and learn the layout of the battlefield and it won't be long before you can survive and progress in this great game.   You start as infantry and gain skills for everything you do which in turn make you better at doing various things, such as driving a jeep, firing a machine gun, throwing grenades, etc.   This makes it possible to unlock more advanced weapons and even change branches of the military to armored division, or become a paratrooper, fighter pilotor, recon member, and ultimately even work your way up to become a general.   Run out of bullets?  Pick up the fallen enemy weapons and use those!   There are so many options in this game that it becomes quickly addicting.   IF you like strategy, you get that on a grand scale as well by earning points not only to improve your skills, but to purchase actual assault teams and then place them on the giant, ever changing war map.   This dynamic map is what ultimately influences your first person battles.   Tired of getting shot at by planes?   Buy an assault team of fighter recon planes and place them in a battle and join it!  Help shape the war, not just the battles.  The war map is even accessible on your mobile phone which allows you the virtual chess board battle anytime, anywhere.   Again, as I said, the game is still in BETA so some changes are for the good, some not so much.   But the game has a huge loyal fanbase and one last thing that makes it so great is that they ban cheaters.   Many frustrations in other games are due to cheaters who can't play a fair match to save their lives, and they only get pleasure by cheating and making everyone else feel bad.  This hurts the community and ultimately harms the game which wants players to play the game.  The folks at Reto have made their own banwave anticheat program and it keeps the battlefield fun most of the time.   So if you want to feel some history in action, and get out some frustration on the enemy, this game is highly, HIGHLY recommended.

Really fun and entertaining zombie game. Unlike many others the zombies actually "feel" real. They shamble through the streets, heads bobbing around like maniacs as they slowly pace toward you, making those headshots more difficult than one would imagine. Completely ignoring bullets as they rip through their arms and legs, as it has no effect other than waying their arm slightly. If you want the kill, you're going to have to get that perfect headshot.
They stupidly wander aimlessly, only beginning the chase once you've alerted them by sprinting through the streets or firing like a maniac. Smashing through doors and barricades with their bleeding arms, lacking the mental capacity to use door knobs. The zombies definitely have a life-like, or rather, un-life-like quality that makes them very appealing.
But the zombies aren't the only threat. Aside from the co-op "Extraction" and "Escape" game modes, "Hunted" brings one of the most exciting and dynamic pvp experiences. Because unlike other games, being shot down doesn't just end your life, it brings on a new one. The hunt continues as you stalk the humans from the shadows as a newly made zombie. As a human you scavenge for weapons and supplies on the spot, compulsively checking your phone for nearby survivors, or player zombies. You can run guns ablaze through the streets, hoping to run into il-prepared survivors, or barricade a house of your own and take your last stand. Shooting through windows at other survivors or battling an onslaught of zombies as they swarm their way up the stairs or bashing down the door to the room you've taken shelter in.
Overall it's a great game and I strongly recommen it. However, a Mic is basically a must. While not so much if you fly solo on Hunted, but the co-op modes desperately require coordination and team work, as a well-crrafted co-op game should. Definitely better with friends. Teaming up with them as securing a house together as you battle off the undead is some of the most fun I've had in a multiplayer game.
The only downside to this game is the lack of content. Which can be expected from an early-access game. There's only 3 maps as of yet, 1 of which is used in 2 of the game modes. But with steam workshop support in the works, user maps and mods, that will soon be a thing of the past. But it doesn't require that. The devs are still very much working on the game and supplying new content.
Well worth the price. I'm already over 30hours of gametime and it has yet to lose it's luster. At $15, this game is a steal.

Mount and Blade Warband...where you go around slaughtering hordes of people until finally, after many strategic battles and wars, you have conquered all of Calradia. Now, sitting on your throne, you think back to the years you spent taking this throne. You think of all the families you displaced, all the men who fought giving Calradia a greater future. A future under you rule, a future of glory and fame. A future which you have given Calradia, a future which you control. A future, in essence, which ebbs and flows to your command, your power, your armies. And you, the greatest person ever to set forth into the land of Calradia, have created this future. You, not Aiden Pierce. Not the Dragonborn. Not Steve. No. The person behind all of this is you, you as you want to be.
And perhaps, besides the gameplay, this is what makes Mount and Blade Warband simply stunning, a masterpiece of war and games. The fact that there is no hero, no true great king or legend. It is simply what you want to make of your character, all the options are given to you. You may be the low bandit, running in the night and hitting up the caravans and farmers.  You may be the cruel lord, one who will have his men die at his orders and his peasants work to death to pay for the death of those solders, all because of fear. You may be the commoner, rising up and becoming a threat to lords and, maybe one day, to entire kingdoms. You may be the heroic knight, who returns the golden throne to it's rightful owner. You may be the black king, one who destoys life with no hesitation, and locks up all who oppose him in the deepest and darkest dungeons. you may be the white king, who makes sure that every peasant is treated fairly, and even the bandits are given chances at redemption. You may be the hired soldier, who goes around and sells his sword to the highest bidder. You can, if you truly want to be and have hours to waste, the helpless princess. Who gets themselves caught over, and over, and over, and over, and you get the point.
But no matter what you are, it doesn't change the fact that you can go to places other than Calradia. You may enter the land of Game of Thrones, through the Clash of Kings mod, to name one. But even if native ever gets boring, which is unlikely (I'm still not bored yet!), you can get mods. And so, the fight goes on, and on, and on, and on...like Steve Perry has told us.
To tell the truth? I think this game should be priced higher, I feel like I've gotten at least thousands of dollars out of it.

Basically all of my experience with this game was on Xbox 360.  Here on PC, I got it for free in a Humble Bundle, so I didn't replay it since I'd already put countless hours into the Xbox 360 version.  I feel comfortable reviewing it anyways though.
The storyline of this game is pretty well done; it sucks you in.  You can tell the developers put a lot of time and effort into it, and I think that's why you find yourself getting so into it.  Every time I played this game, I found myself getting into character and playing the game as if I was that character, rather than myself, playing a video game.
From a gameplay standpoint, it's just plain fun.  There's plenty to explore and discover, lots of things to do, and a ton of enemies that need killing.  On Xbox 360 there weren't many bugs that I found, and from what I've heard, there aren't that many here on the PC version either.  Obviously I can't say for certain though.
Visually and auditorily, the little bit of the game I played here on PC was spectacular.  On full ultra settings, the game looks downright beautiful.  Combine that with the well done sound effects, and you've got an awesome atmosphere!
All in all, although my time with this game was on Xbox 360, I feel comfortable saying that if you're interested in this game, and you think you'd like it; buy it, because you're probably right!

Why this game is one of the best Zombie games out there. I'll run down the pro's and con's of this game. First thing up...
-Pros-
1. The first actual feeling of 'survival' I've ever got from a game. There's no crosshairs. There's no mini-map (unless you call the GPS for a few game modes a mini-map).
2. The game is hard. But then again, surviving millions of walking dead people who are trying to eat you, isn't going to be easy. I like that. The game isn't  a cake walk.
3. The game requires teamwork. If you don't work with the living, you're going to end up dead.
4. No OP special zombies. Once you die, you become a zombie. You don't have any voodoo witchcraft that's going to turn you into a magical flying 500 pound zombie.
5. You actually need the flashlight in this game. I can't tell you how many zombie games I've played where you have a flashlight, but there's reall no need for it.
6. Shoot for the brain, not just the head. This also makes it hard for new players, which I guess could be considered a downfall. Headshots don't do a damn thing. You have to shoot/hit the brain. You shoot the chin? Nothing. You shoot the cheek? Nothing. Hit the brain.
7. The workshop is expanding and it's incredibly easy to submit your own work. I've even done it myself.
8. Detail. The maps are beautiful and complex.
9. Not one game is ever the same. The map will change up between every round. On Escape, if you die one round and try it again, you will have to take a different route. Same with the weapons, they won't be in the same place.
-Cons-
1. There could be more maps. There's only a handfull of maps right now, but the makers of the game did say that they were going to come out with 2 free DLC packs. I would guess this comes with new maps. But what do you expect? Some peope complain that there are not enough maps, ignoring the fact that this is not an AAA title. It's made by a small group of developers.
2. Kinda hard to find some games in some game modes. Hunted is by far the most popular game type. Humans Vs Humans Vs Zombies. It's great. But other game modes usually don't have any players. Really hope the game becomes more popular over time.
3. Not enough servers with custom content.
That's about it! Please, don't only read the bad reviews and Metacritic is notorious for giving great games less than great reviews.

Another game with a great concept ,but nothing more. It's fun at first because everyone is just like you. You guys are all starting out and basically it's fair. But once you hit tier 2 and get to do assault and defend mission, kiss those skirmishes goodbye. I can't even remember going back to a skirmish after I hit tier 2. But it get's better, after you spawn in the middle of no where while trying to re capture your point that is being contested. The tanks roaming around the point, planes vulturing around, and people who have scopes and actual rifles that can shoot across long distances with a high amount of damage, just pick you off one by one as you who have barely just begun learning the game still have no clue hwat is going on. All that happens, is your mowed down one by one like some re enactment of enemy at the gate. But you know what, I let it slide because at the end of the day it is a free game the does not force me to pay anything. I want to be clear about this, I 'm not mad at this game. If anything I am frustrated. I am frustrated because I wanted it to be different. I wanted this game to actually make a difference and make me believe that you don't need to be a multimillion dollar juggernaut of a company to make a good big battle war type game. I figured man this game looks interesting and maybe it's gonna show people that games like battlefield and CoD have lost their way. But I was wrong. The physics are terrible. Sometimes shots have problems registering and what seemed like 3 shots hitting the target might only be one. Simple actions, like jumping across a fence become a micro management endeavor and their is barely any tutorial on the game itself. The tutorial is a joke. I don't know if lazy can even describe this tutorial system. Like I think that part deserve a review of it's own because Jesus Christ man was that honestly the best you could do? Don't worry I 'm not gonna harp on you too much for that part cause I have better things to do and honestly I would be surprise if your game actually made it out of beta, and even actually made a mark on the fps/mmo scene. Moving on, if you don't know already, it's a pay 2 win game. For anyone not sure what that means, it's simple you have to pay more than what a normal game such as battlefield would cost you, which gives you the same opportunity as everyone else to unlock and play the game to it's fullest. Why is this even a business model? Like no really, who in there right mind thinks this is a good business model. War Z did this and it got destroyed by the community. It was a laughing stock. I figure at this point we are all aware that people hate this. But alas if you want to unlock the stuff instead of grinding tediously you got to put down some dough. Hold up, I know what you are thinking, all I got to do is grind out and I will get all the cool stuff, easy. LOL you don't think they thought of that. Here's the funny part that still gets me. You want to know why I wanted to go back to those fair skirmishes, Its because I could make an impact and actually capture points and get experience. If I am getting spawn camped for half the match by a sniper and 2 tanks how much xp and in game income do you think I get? Almost none. You get rewarded based on how well you did in the game. So if you have no clue what's going on (trust me you wont) and if you don't have anti tank weaponry (they don’t ♥♥♥♥ing teach you how to get that either, I had to look up a guide) then your just gonna be confused. That sounds fun right? You know what is worst than losing, not knowing why you lost. That is the number one thing that gets to me. You don't have the simple time to help guide a player to understand the game better so he can be competent enough to play it. Why is this hard? Are the new players like rewards for those who went through your hazing process like some Greek fraternity? Like come on, I can not believe that at all during the development process, you guys weren't like "man maybe we should teach people how to deal with certain situations in the game" Did that thought never cross your mind? Did you just think hey no worries, they'll get it eventually. Graphics are actually decent considering the game is free and a massively multilayer game (it's not btw, It's max I think is 24 v 24 which is just your typical Big team battle esque combat simulator). The only Part that is massive is that you get campaign missions where some idiot who actually had enough time or money made it to general and is spending his money or time to send in troops (you) to certain parts in the war. Then he just has to pray your not morons who suicide and just waste all his resources. That's it. The Air combat is pretty neat but then they made something called HS rounds or something that just pierce through the cockpit like its butter and the pilot hit box is so large that planes just get murdered now. Used to have cool dog fights, from what I have seen and heard from the older versions, but now it's quite underwhelming. I figure that once you suffer enough and get the hang of the game to be able to get a gun with a scope and some actual useful equipment then it becomes manageable. I could even say it would be fun because you are no longer on the receiving end of the spawn camping anymore. Yeah don't think you can just get a sight that's going to help you see someone more than 50 yards away, because that would mean you might have chance in the larger maps.
