Ubisoft's got a bad reputation with PC gamers, much of it well-deserved. They can't optimize for crap (although Rocksteady just beat them on that with Arkham Knight), and go overboard with DRM. Fortunately, Ubisoft seems to have realized that the Far Cry series is deeply rooted in the PC and has given an unusually high amount of love to the PC version. The game still has a few hiccups, and I'd much rather not have uPlay, but it could have been a lot worse. At least Ubisoft bothered to give us a full suite of visual settings to tweak! Also, multiplayer was broken when I tried to play it, so I'm only talking about the single player here.
I first played the game on a 1 GB GTX560 non-Ti, and it would crash on startup if I attempted to play on high settings. I was forced to use the medium presets, which still weren't bad-looking and at least I got 100 fps. I've since switched to a 4 GB GTX760 superclocked, and have nearly all the details cranked up at 1080p and the results are mind-blowing. The open-world jungle island is a sight to behold on high settings. The attention to detail rivals Crysis. Even when I first played using the medium settings, I was very impressed by the visual quality.
But graphics don't make the game. Far Cry 2 looked incredible back in 2008 (and still holds up well today), but was let down by its "realism" features which ended up turning the gameplay into a chore - remember those jamming weapons, that malaria, and the need to keep repairing your vehicle's engine? Not to mention the utterly frustrating infinite-respawning guard checkpoints? Fear not - the most disliked features of Far Cry 2 have been discarded, while the aspects which people liked have been carried over and improved.
The single-player campaign is a blast from the very beginning, and is sufficiently engaging to make you want to play all the way to the end. It opens with you, Jason Brody, being captured with your fellow tourists by a memorable madman named Vaas Montenegro. You escape (but your brother dies in the process) in a high-adrenaline sequence, and slowly but surely begin plotting revenge with the help of the indigenous islanders. One by one, you rescue your other surviving friends, with the ultimate showdowns against Vaas and the ruthless mercenaries he's affiliated with. The story missions are well designed with the appropriate blend of stealth and Rambo-esque action. Jason Brody is a true badass, that's all I can say.
Ah yes, the stealth. Despite the arsenal of awesome weapons, going stealth is where the real fun lies. Outside the story missions, there are numerous guard outposts you can conquer by killing all the mercenaries within (turning the place into a base for indigenous allies in the process). You can dash in guns-a-blazing, but that'll set off an alarm and the baddies will signal for backup, making the fight tougher. You also get less XP. Instead, you should scout the area, using your binoculars to spot and tag the baddies, and then snipe them with a bow (hilariously fun) or silenced sniper rifle, or sneak in like the Predator and use your knife to pick them off one-by-one. You can upgrade your melee abilities with XP which makes things even more varied and fun. Once you've upgraded your abilities enough, you're an unstoppable force cackling as those enemies crap their pants trying to figure out who is reducing their headcount.
To aid yourself in combat, you can inject yourself with syringes, which you create by gathering specific plants (fortunately they are common everywhere on the map and you'll rarely feel that you have a hard time finding a necessary plant). These syringes can boost your health, adrenaline, or allow you to see threat outlines through walls, Detective Mode style. Never have I found myself taking plants so seriously in a shooting game.
As with other open-world games, Far Cry 3 has a few RPG elements which involve a fair bit of grinding. To upgrade your combat abilities, you need to gain XP from killing baddies or wildlife, and thankfully it doesn't take too long to get everything upgraded especially if you stick to stealth. To upgrade your carrying abilities, however, things get strange. You need to slaughter very specific kinds of wildlife and skin them, fashioning the collected skins into ammo bags, wallets (yes, you can't carry too much money without a proper wallet), grenade bags, syringe bags, etc. Some animals are difficult to find, and some are difficult to kill (especially those in the water). I wonder how on earth the animal population didn't go extinct after all the hours I spent hunting for the skins I needed. PETA would certainly go nuts over this game, haha. Anyway, even the finding-skins aspect of the game isn't too much of a chore. Grinding is actually kind of fun!
I wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone looking for an immersive open-world single player game. Well done Ubisoft!

I'd like to open with the fact that this REALLY is a FANTASTIC game.  The maps are really cool, the weapons function and sound awesome, and the class progression is really cool.
The play is mostly fluid, the game is fairly balanced... UNTIL:
Once you hit about Tier 4 or Tier 5.
The game allows you to specialize into Tank Crew very early.
HOWEVER,
the different class specializations are staggered throughout the experience tree.
Tank Crew is allowed a full tier before Fighter pilot.
Fighter pilot and Tank Crew are allowed SEVERAL experience "levels" away from "paratrooper."
So:
If you'd like to play a higher tier like Paratrooper or Recon, you essentially have to level on foot against people who are piloting tanks and airplanes.  There are MANY maps that highly favor tank/plane playing players and it becomes nearly impossible for a player on foot to even compete.  Truthfully, I'm a fairly skilled SMG player that understands how to navigate the map well and infiltrate enemy spawns/basses etc.  I simply could not even APPROACH enemy bases without instantly being killed. I haven't paid any money for the game, so the game held a LOT of value for me until about Tier 6.  After Tier 6, I essentially just spawned and died repeatedly and wasn't even participating in the game.
I would have spent money on the game had I not experienced some of the later level skrimishes.  It just simply wasn't balanced, and it removes the ability of F2P'ers to even participate.
TLDR: DO try the game.  It is a lot of fun.  DO NOT play the game past level 5-6 unless you plan on dropping ~20$ on the game.  Really is and WILL be a very great game.

Well, since this game was free and still in beta, I never expected much. Yes, the engine needs a lot of work, but I'm glad they have their own, instead of using Unreal or Source (I hate Source). The graphics are quite alright. When the settings are all the way up, I still see jagged edges and blurry textures. The gameplay is sort of mudane sometimes, considering  infantry are ill-equiped to fight the numerous tanks. The experience system is just like any other shooter. The money system, of course, has earned currency and "premium" currency (premium being the currency you pay for with real money). The in-game money is based upon your soldier's level, as they have a certain salary they are paid each game. Price levels for guns are really high. Leveling up takes a very long time. HOWEVER, the game has great potential, with its multi-branch and multi-company operations. What do I mean by this? There are tanks/armored personnel carriers, planes, and infantry fighting on the same battlefield. There are different objectives for different companies of soldiers on massive maps. You could be killing Jerries in the factory while your buddy is rolling his tank through the countryside, taking out anti-air nests.
All in all, this game is needy of improvement, but has a ton of potential. It is free, so everyone should give it a try. The World War II setting was definitely a turn-on for me, but the FPS action is intense enough to attract any gamer.

Additionaly, the game has very interesting gunplay, and a huge plethora of weapons, tanks and vehicles, unlike that of any other ww2 game, and the subtle grinding, adds to the experience by constantly having you work towards something. Mount and Blade is a low fantasy (no orcs or elves here) medieval first person RPG with elements of strategy and empire building worked in seamlessly. While that description alone may sound pretty cool, the execution of this game is what makes it truly remarkable. The combat in this game is spectacular and I dare say is the best melee first person combat in gaming right now. The strategy elements of army building, strategic warfare, city management, diplomacy, and the advancement of your status within a country all add a lot of depth and character to this title. The game's only flaws are its lack of polish in some areas. The graphics are not cutting edge, but they get the job done well. Dialogue options and social questing aspects could have been done better in my opinion - I'm a big roleplayer and I wanted to actually communicate with the characters in the game beyond what was offered. While the game lacks a bit of polish in places, the overall experience is tremendously fun. The game is also blessed with an exceptional modding community - so the sky is the limit with this game. Is it worth a buy? Absolutely!

This game came out in 2010 and it looks much older. The graphics (and animations) can suck at times, and at other times are just laughable, and they're a massive improvement on the original M&B. But if you're not scared away by the low-budget graphics, then you're in for an awesome game.
This game is a medeival combat simulator, with elements of Strategy games and RPGs, and a big open sandbox set in a fictional medeival land called Calradia. The combat itself is simple to get the hang of, but truly an art to master, and you'll find that you wont get far spam-clicking through battles. The land is war-torn and splintered on the remains of the fallen Empire of Calradia. It's constantly fought over by several different kings, each leading a unique faction. You can choose to join a faction and help your liege take the throne, or you can start your own kingdom and unify Calradia under your own rule. Or you can stick to banditry and plunder villages or something. There are literally so many ways you can go with this game. It's also got tons of achievements you can earn to show off your mastery! And with Warband, there is also multiplayer mode, which pretty much filled in what the original M&B was missing. There are many servers to play on that can boast up to 200 players. You can also buy the Napoleonic Wars DLC, which (as the name implies) is a multiplayer DLC set in the historical Napoleonic Wars, bringing muskets into the game. And if you find the game getting boring on its own, that is where modding comes in! Because this game was practically made for modding, there is a rather large and active modding community available on the interwebs with many great mods bringing the games setting from the Neolithic Revolution to the far-future and everything in between. Also, there are many resources at your disposal if you're looking to make a mod yourself.
Overall, I'd give this game a maximum rating, in spite of its graphics, because the gameplay is so great and there are so many possibilites with it. My review can't quite do it justice. You should seriously buy this game for yourself and fill in that gaping void in your library.

After a, no doubt, tough start with incapable servers and plentiful issues, the game has developed to a fine indie title.
Contagion belongs into the 'more modern, more realistic' Zombie setting. It emphases the value of ammo, by not giving out too much in first place and as well using a simple, yet effective damage model:
Killing a single zombie may eat up entire mags of your weapon... or just a single shot, if you hit the head. Which isn't easy, because the Zombies sway and being hit will severely cripple your aim for a few seconds. Additionally, every shot will potentially alert a dozen more zombies (and in PvP: other Players), making it a overall bad idea to shoot anything in first place. But melee weapons are tricky to use and require Stamina, meaning you can't just bash your way through hordes.
Combine that with a high zombie damage (10 hits and you're dead) and the fact that a player zombie can potentially oneshot you with an infecting grapple (which doesn't deal damage, but has a high chance of infecting you, turning you into a walking timebomb) and you got a hell of a tough zombie survival game.
Whilst the 'Escape Mode' really didn't appeal me and felt more like a casual 'Escape'-Flashgame with giant levels, tough to find objectives and a few sparse zombies, the other modes are a lot of fun. Exspecially I have found a liking to the Hunt mode, where it's FFA and the last survivor standing wins.  Without any indicator but sounds, sight and a short-ranged cellphone-based 'pinging', keeping a low profile is #1 strategy in PvP. But how are you supposed to kill someone without shooting, if sneaking up and melee'ing isn't an option?
Well, good luck figuring it out for yourself!

just realized I never wrote a recommendation for this game.  I've mentioned it so often, even in a review of FC4.  Yes it has achieved new levels of awesomeness imo.  There are so many aspects that deserve recognition, a real world and open world that allows for linear gameplay without telling you where you must go, a great variety of characters, some creepy that keep the story line, which is really well written and preformed, interesting, and, finally a set of friends and comrades you go around a rescue, sometimes they participate in your quest.
There are certainly areas to improve, like I wish your friends were feeding you fresh ammo or upgrades they found, or, a better collection system that FC4 addresses that makes collecting a faster process allowing you to upgrade without the dredgery of cycling through a menu to figure out what you need to collect.  I also wish the side missions had an impact on the game, that civilians really start to appreciate you more as more of their island is freed, and a larger port city to bring in more characters.  Perhaps at the end, not having your GF abonden you and having the island build you a dream resort villa as a reward for freeing them of decades of oppression.  But that reflects the point of the game as it really does keep itself in the plausible yet thrilling action of a world controled by psychopaths.
The characters are awesome, and the world which you explore is amazing too.  "I wonder if I can get on top of that mountain..." and then you do, then "I wonder how far I can fly from this point..."
The surrounding and inaccessible islands are way out of scale and personally I wish they were just little uninhabitted islands surrounded by water to keep everything in the plausible world.
When I finished one island I was shocked to find that I would have to concur another island just as large with a whole new set of circumstances and foe to defeat.  This game provides plenty to do and I easily spent 5 full days to complete everything.  It is well worth the price, $29.99, even if you, like myself, don't play the multiplayer portion.

Mount and Blade is a low fantasy (no orcs or elves here) medieval first person RPG with elements of strategy and empire building worked in seamlessly. While that description alone may sound pretty cool, the execution of this game is what makes it truly remarkable. The combat in this game is spectacular and I dare say is the best melee first person combat in gaming right now. The strategy elements of army building, strategic warfare, city management, diplomacy, and the advancement of your status within a country all add a lot of depth and character to this title. The game's only flaws are its lack of polish in some areas. The graphics are not cutting edge, but they get the job done well. Dialogue options and social questing aspects could have been done better in my opinion - I'm a big roleplayer and I wanted to actually communicate with the characters in the game beyond what was offered. While the game lacks a bit of polish in places, the overall experience is tremendously fun. The game is also blessed with an exceptional modding community - so the sky is the limit with this game. Is it worth a buy? Absolutely!

This game came out in 2010 and it looks much older. The graphics (and animations) can suck at times, and at other times are just laughable, and they're a massive improvement on the original M&B. But if you're not scared away by the low-budget graphics, then you're in for an awesome game.
This game is a medeival combat simulator, with elements of Strategy games and RPGs, and a big open sandbox set in a fictional medeival land called Calradia. The combat itself is simple to get the hang of, but truly an art to master, and you'll find that you wont get far spam-clicking through battles. The land is war-torn and splintered on the remains of the fallen Empire of Calradia. It's constantly fought over by several different kings, each leading a unique faction. You can choose to join a faction and help your liege take the throne, or you can start your own kingdom and unify Calradia under your own rule. Or you can stick to banditry and plunder villages or something. There are literally so many ways you can go with this game. It's also got tons of achievements you can earn to show off your mastery! And with Warband, there is also multiplayer mode, which pretty much filled in what the original M&B was missing. There are many servers to play on that can boast up to 200 players. You can also buy the Napoleonic Wars DLC, which (as the name implies) is a multiplayer DLC set in the historical Napoleonic Wars, bringing muskets into the game. And if you find the game getting boring on its own, that is where modding comes in! Because this game was practically made for modding, there is a rather large and active modding community available on the interwebs with many great mods bringing the games setting from the Neolithic Revolution to the far-future and everything in between. Also, there are many resources at your disposal if you're looking to make a mod yourself.
Overall, I'd give this game a maximum rating, in spite of its graphics, because the gameplay is so great and there are so many possibilites with it. My review can't quite do it justice. You should seriously buy this game for yourself and fill in that gaping void in your library.

Heroes and Generals has all the ingredients needed to become THE number one game to go to for any World War 2 enthousiast out there. It has planes, cars, tanks, a very  decent arsenal of weapons, modifications for almost everything you can obtain, a brilliant fully customizable class system, big maps, nice graphics and in the 'near' future a pile of extra content. Complete new theatres of war such as Russia, Africa, The Pacific and more.. are confirmed by the devs to be release at some point in the future.
If team Reto keeps the updates at a steady flow and manages to maintain it's current fragile balance between PAY and FREE this game can become the new standard for all future online World War 2 simulators.
If you enjoy watching World War 2 movies and games, I HIGHLY recommend this game! But even if you don't, it's definitely worth trying out, there's a very real chance you will like it a lot.

One "man" stuck on an island, hell-bent on rescuing his friends from slave-trading pirates. Except this "man", Jason Brody, is a whiny brat who is slowly deluded into fancying himself a god-king amongst peasants. Sound stupid? Yeah, I thought so too. This is like "Lord of the Flies" with machine guns. Other than the somewhat lame story, I thought this game was quite good. The characters were rather varied, and quite charming in their unique own ways. Citra was completely insane (but incredibly HOT!!!), Hoyt Volker was similarly off his rocker (not to mention having an annoying accent), and Dennis reveals himself to be a cultist psycho at the very end of the game. There are only two characters that I actually LIKED: Dr. Earnhardt, the kind-hearted drug addict "botanist", and Vaas Montenegro, the main antagonist of Far Cry 3. At this point, one should see that most if not all these characters are insane. Part of the whole story is Jason's descent into insanity, as power and the sway of the untamed jungle go to his head. His foil is Vaas, whose memorable "Definition of Insanity" monologue leaves the player wondering if Jason and all the others are not at least as insane; in my view, Vaas is the only one who has the courage to admit that he is insane. One almost feels sorry for him. The combat was great; a nice variety of weapons at the players' disposal. I also liked the animal hunts, which changed the pace of the game somewhat (bear hunting, komodo dragon-skinning, and alligator-pulverizing are just some of the adventures that await) and the missions which gave the player a greater sense of the Imperial Japanese military's historical presence on these islands (ie the "Lost" missions). I also enjoyed the storyline that dealt with Zheng He's diplomatic mission; it gave one a sense of the history behind this grand Ming venture, which was somewhat soured by the fact that the in-game history lesson was delivered by a♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥psychopath. Eventually, looting the island got a little tedious; at that point, progressing with the story is all one can do. Good game overall.
9.3/10

The balance of this game is a great thing to question.  Infantry and air are the dominating factor to this game, armor is just useless unless you some how convice other infantry to stay with you, which will never happen.  The amount of anti-tank equipment in this game is way way out there, ranging from mines, grenades, and rockects (you can carry up to 90 gernades and mines at any one given time).  Apperently all the infantry are super soldiers that can carry a large amount of ordinance to combat armor vehicles.  I wish I could carry a bazooka with 12 rockects (12.75 lbs not counting ammo), 90 high explosive anti-tank grenades (3 lbs each), 90 high explosive anti-tank mines (9lbs Germany and 2lbs US), and a sub-machine gun with a full combat load.
Air is good to have, because if you have the better air you do control the battlefield.  The developers put in AA guns to kind of equalize this factor, however the AA guns do far to little damage and are inaccurate as all can be.  Your only hope is to shoot the pilot out of his aircraft.  Also the extra "sandbag" walls around the AA gun serve no purpose other than blocking the line of fire of the gun since the majority of pilots fly extremely low to the ground.
Starting out as a new player will be the most boring and lamest grind fest of your life.  Everybody quickly switches to the SMG once its unlocked, but the amount of ingame currancy you need to get is a bit high priced to even be effective.  For the amount of 1 upgrade to a gun, you can buy a vehicle or aircraft, at which point the gun is a secondary and not really needed unless you plan to dismount.  Also the likely hood of you running into a player with a fully upgraded SMG or Assault rifle is almost garrented and you will be just a smear on the ground, with maybe only one round fired out of your rifle.
Until some type of balance is met, i would not recommend this game to any new players unless you like getting an amazing negative K/D.  You might take a gamble and roll armor and hope you get a match with no AT weapons on any infantry, but that is one in a million chance.
IF you some how manage to get down all the ranks that are in this game, you can then put resources in for a fight that other people will play.  Thats right, once you get high enough you can no longer take place in actual battles with that character any more, and you will have to create a new character and start all over again.  On a high note, the developers saw how this would be annoying to the players, so they let the players transfer equipment from there "commanding" characters to ones they could actually play.

I was hoping for a better implementation of WW2 Online, but this isn't it. Medal progression is glacial (making equipment unlocks few and far between), there's no useful means of communication other than whistles/horns, unless you set it up yourself outside the game... maybe with a group of friends over TS/vent/mumble/whatever, it might be tolerable, but probably not, because you'd still get lumped in with the rest of the zergs.

Heroes & Generals is personally one of my new favorites. You're probably wondering, "Why do we need ANOTHER WWII first person shooter? There are hundreds to choose from already!" Yes, while many WWII shooter games are available, this one brings some new aspects to the table. The first thing I praise the game for is its historical accuracy. The guns, the soldier design, the buildings, the battle areas, all of it is so realistic I sometimes forget I'm even playing a game. The graphics are beautiful, but on the downside, the game is poorly optimised as it is still in beta stages. The way you unlock and get new weapons isn't anything unique, a level up and gain experience to unlock weapons system, but I feel the system is very well balanced, unlike many other games. Recently, there has been a lot of conflict about if this game is pay to win, or P2W. My personal opinion on this is that it's more pay to PROGRESS not pay to WIN. A player who earned their weapons and earned the upgrades will still do better than a person who just joined and poured money into getting the perfect weapon. Even though weapon stats help, the game is still more about skill than the right gun. Everybody has their own play style and their own favorite guns and favorite upgrades, there really is no meta. Paying to unlock items in the game is more of saving yourself the grinding. In the game, you can fight for the Axis or the Allies on the western front. The soldiers you can choose from are infantry, tanker, figher pilot, paratrooper, and recon. All the types of soldiers support eachother and play a major roll in the victory. If you play for a while, you can move your soldier up to a general, and command armies to different cities on the map to help lead your side to victory over Europe. Other than minor optimisation issues, I have no problems with this game. It is one of the better WWII first person shooters I've seen out there. The game is free while in beta, so go download it and join the fight!

Far Cry games alwasy elicit a mixed feeling from me. On the one hand, the physics and "virtual realism" of the game makes it one of the best at balancing exploration with tension to prevent any kind of boredom. The enemy AI is not bad, and once they spot you, you had better be good at whatever range of combat you choose to take them on. I do enjoy the sniper action in this game... However, even as a sniper, you better change your location frequently or they may just circle around and get you. The enemy classes advance as  you advance through the game to keep things interesting.
I really appreciate the wildlife. Both for all the extra animals that provide craftable items, and also for all those animals that are neither food nor craft, but still add to the overall realism of the game environment. I mean, crabs on the beach and Portuguese Man O' War in the sea! Need I say more?
The predatory creatures in this game will make sure you stay on your toes. There is nothing like standing on a road, thinking you are alone, then having a tiger leap out of the bush to rip your face off! So, find a safe house if you are going to park your character, because things can happen if you do not.
Even when you have cleared all the enemy strongholds, you can explore the island pursuing secondary objective for hours and hours and even more hours. The artwork is so freaking beautiful, I would enjoy exploring these islands even if they were empty.

Heroes and Generals is one of those interesting games that combines a great overall shooter feel to a terrible leveling system, poor maps, and a non-existant balancing system. Overall, the weapons from the start feel pretty balanced, but later you will realize that snipers are overpowered. This has to do very little to do with the weapon itself, and is more along the lines of a map design flaw. See, most maps are long range maps with few cover. This is perfect for snipers, as they tend to stick in the forests away from the battle and pick off people. For the people being sniped, they have little chance of being aware of a sniper until they get shot. Even when they DO know where the sniper is, there is almost no cover at all. Tanks in this game are actually pretty balanced. Nuff said(Its also very fun).Flying in this game is ATROCIOUS. I almost could not figure out what was going on. I, coming from games like war thunder, believe that the devs should work on this aspect more. One last note- NERF THE PARATROOPERS. Paratroopers are absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. They have the option to drop where ever they please, unload a clip into every soldier around, and run about with no real concern. I understand that the tactic of paratroopers are to surprise the enemy, but having them run around with no real concern is far from their intended purpose. Overall, I think that Heroes and generals is a great game, but some of its aspects are still far from balanced, and need more work. Lastly, the only reason I'm recommending it is because it is f2p. I still believe that freemium games should die in a fire, and this is no exception. If the devs plan to release the game in this state, I am going to be VERY♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off. The only way the devs can resurrect this game is if they add a tiering system, so newbies dont have to deal with the♥♥♥♥♥♥that I went through. Luckily, you can get it for free, so i feel that you should try it to see if you woul like it.

So, this game has been up for a few years now. Still, I decided to buy it on the Summer Sale this year. If I were to know what this game would be like, before buying it, I'd pay the full price - here's why.
Starting off with the design, graphical things; it's beautiful, even today, this game has lovely graphics compared to new (FPS) games. Secondly, there's the Singleplayer story; I have never played a game with a story so well-written before. It's weird and the characters are really obscure, but that's what keeps you thinking, throughout the entire story. At moments I should have been sleeping, I found myself wondering what would be the next objective or mission, and why Vaas was such a cold-blooded f♥♥♥. Especially for those who are looking for a challenging (you can choose your own difficulty so do not worry) story-based FPS, buy it. It is never to late to say you love a game released back in the days when there were no iPhone 6, PS4 and Far Cry 4 yet (must have been a terrible time to live in, except for the FC4 thing.)
All together, this is far from all of the positive and good things I can tell you about this game, it's wonderful.
About UPlay, don't worry too much, it's worth it and it kind of makes up the lack of achievements on Steam, because you can get achievements on UPLay and buy in-game things with the credits you get. Also, I've never ever had connection problems with UPlay, so: it's really not that bad!
Hope this helped you out with making your choice (BUY IT :D),

In my honest opinion, Far Cry 3 is an excellent evolution from Far Cry 2 and if you liked its predessecor, you will absolutely adore this game. It makes so many things better than FC2. But I am, again, getting ahead of myself. For all you lazy ones, pros and cons are listed below as always.
So, the story: You are a man named Jason Brody and you, your two brothers and some other friends are making a vacation on Rook island under the assumption it's all wildlife in celebration of your little Brother's pilot license. What you didn't know is that on Rook Island there are pirates who capture people and sell them on the slave market. And that's what happens to you and your friends. The intro sequence shows you celebrating and in the next moment, the first main villain by the name of Vaas Montenegro stands before the cage you are held captive in and talks to you and your older brother. You two manage to escape that cage and then your main objective becomes abundantly clear: Escape the slave camp and rescue your friends with the ultimate goal of getting everyone out alive and escape the island.
Of course, objectives will be shifting heavily throughout the story and they almost all involve a large amount of murder and violence. Which takes me to the gameplay mechanics. And to be honest, there is nothing we haven't seen in the previous games - but it's executed much better. You get your standard FPS controls and you will be able to drive cars and boats as well as use hang gliders which are distributed frequently on positions and vantage points that are pretty high up. But you can also traverse the whole island (with a couple of exceptions) on foot. It's slower but in terms of navigating much easier for the most part.
All the vehicles you get to drive have their own handling and weight behind them. And the driving part of the game is executed really well in my opinion, as you can feel the weight behind each vehicle and it is not all that easy to get the hang of it and drive moderately decent to not crash into a bunch of trees, rocks or fall off cliffs which more often than not will kill you. The flying with the hang glider is also well executed and works as you would expect.
The gunplay isn't as well executed as the driving aspect of the game as all the weapons you get feel kinda... light weight. You would expect a .50 caliber sniper rifle to look heavy and sound heavier when fired but that isn't the case. Sure, it's loud and enemies get alerted but firing a big weapon in this game isn't nearly as satisfying as it could have been. Another example would be the Desert Eagle or the Magnum revolver you can acquire. These guns look heavy and awesome but the way they sound is underwhelming at best. Other than that what works really well are the silencer attachments for most of the weapons. It sounds just as it should and you really feel like a spec ops dude when firing those weapons from the shadows. Also, stealth works well in this game too.
In terms of weapon variety you got a lot of weapons to choose from. There are some shotguns, SMGs, MGs, pistols, assault rifles, sniper rifles, a bow, explosives and some special weapons. Enough to cover up all your needs without making the weapon variety feel over-the-top for such a relatively small island. It's good.
Also there's melee combat. The knives you get to choose are purely cosmetic. Melee comes into play mostly when using stealth takedowns.
So, what else? Far Cry 3 features an open world and you've got a lot of♥♥♥♥♥♥to do if you're going for it. Since it's a Ubisoft game you can expect a reasonable amount of collectibles which get you XP for finding these things. And luckily, if you are going for a 100% save game (which I accomplished) you can buy treasure maps with all the locations of the collectibles and even all the loot chests on the whole island. Besides collecting stuff there are a lot of side objectives.
Remember the guard posts from Far Cry 2? Well... On the map there are a lot of outposts of your opposing factions (which there are two of) and you can liberate them, earning you XP and a fast travel point as well as some side quests which are called "Wanted Dead" and "Path of the Hunter". In WD you have to go to the indicated location and kill the target with your knife, in PotH you go to the indicated location, take the weapon that is dropped off there for you and hunt a specific type of animal with said weapon. Then there are some sidequests which involve talking with villagers and, of course, the main story questline. Also, the lookouts in Assassin's Creed make their return here as you have to climb radio towers to unlock obscured parts of the map to be able to navigate the terrain more effectively, find collectibles and side objectives.
Also, FC3 features a crafting aspect. This involves hunting down and skinning specific animals to craft weapon holsters, ammo pouches and all kinds of bags to carry your belongings around as well as use specific types of flora around the island to craft potent injections to help you progress, get an edge over your enemies or heal you.
And the game features skills. Pretty much at the beginning after the intro mission you get introduced to the faction you will be fighting for most of the time and they give you the Tatau. It's a tattoo on your left arm that will progress and get more complicated the more skills you unlock. As far as I'm concerned, unlocking all 54 skills is relatively easy since every collectible you find and side activity you participate in rewards you with XP. The thing is: you can not unlock all skills before having done a considerable amount of the story quests. Before doing some of that you can only unlock about 10 or 12 if I recall correctly. This is a good way of managing things as to not overpower the main character you play as early on in the game.
In terms of enemy variety you got a bunch of endangered animal species and enemy soldiers which range from assaulters to snipers over to RPGs, heavy gatling units and flamethrower units as well as close combat units or molotov units. Nothing too fancy but you should approach each enemy type differently.
Let's talk about the people and the voice acting for a bit. Because it is, in my opinion, the game's strongest point. All of the characters are so well designed, from their looks to their behaviour and voice acting that they are truly believable and in no way flat. When talking to them you just feel that there's a story behind all of it, you feel their character. They are unique people you're going to remember even after finishing the game. Save for your friends you're trying to save. Which is weird but I can overlook that. The well designed characters make the story feel important, unique and worth going through.
The gripes I got with the game?
Fire effects work not nearly as cool as they did in FC2. Also there are some very minor bugs where you could get stuck in a sprint animation if you happened to sprint-slide down one specific hill. And yes, I've found that hill. Other than that it rarely freezes and crashes and runs fine on modern-day systems. Of course you will get the occasional FPS drop on an average gaming PC but if you set up things right you can still achieve a constant 60 FPS. If you have a high-end PC you will get constant 60 FPS regardless. Also the aforementioned gunplay with heavy weapons doesn't feel too impressive.
Pros and cons:
+ Engaging story
+ Strong characters
+ Good vehicle handling
+ Decent gunplay
+ Neat graphics
+ Stable gaming experience
+ Believalbe world
- Meager fire effects
- Heavy weapons feel like aluminum toys
- Occasional FPS drop
- Occasional freezing and crashing (rarely for me)
Would I recommend this game? Hell yes!
At the current price? 20€ is a reasonable price for around 40 hours of playtime.
The DLC's not worth it though. Save for Blood Dragon but that's a standalone DLC.
So yeah. Get it. It's good.

The game is still in developpement, it can be buggy sometime, but it will not stop the fun, sometime bugs could help in a weird way, but it helped a bit!
Heroes & Generals is Free to play, and a in-game money system is in it, it will serve you to buy weapons and upgrade, nut you can also pay them with real money. This game is not a pay to win type, even if you have bought weapons with real money, it will change nothing against everyone.
The sound of the game are extremely impressive, really great quality, you can almost feel the bullet flying near you or the shoot of a sherman tank.
This game is actually two game in one, one part is the hero part(the FPS part), and the second part is the general one(RTS style).I never actually tried the general part, but I have seen what I can give to the heroe part since both of them are connected. The hero part is the one that you will feel the action and the general one is the one that will send troop for the hero part.
For the people who think that this is Call Of Duty style of game, step back since trying to make the most kills during the hero part will become boring and will make you die so many times (death after death), the hero part is cooperative, work always with your teammates to accomplish nearly impossible challenges during a game.
I fully reccommend that you try this game! It free and really fun.

Great game!
Its like battlefield but it has huge amount of fun things and attention to details. (you can ride bicycle and another player can sit behind you, so you carry both)
The progression system keeps you playing for months! Its like little WW2 mmorpg. (i'm still playing it)
Lots of things to unlock and it feels awesome when you buy etc. Light Machine Gun and everyone has only Rifles.
Its a 18 vs 18 battlefield match with Tanks, Planes, Paratroopers, Snipers and Infantry. Its not just a deathmatch but you need to capture objectives to advance and win the match.
I personally got captured by such fun infantry gameplay, where you can actually hide in bushes or behind trees because there is no marker over your head, and surprise the enemy. Or if you like fast-paced gameplay then in objectives or close quarters. You can even beat enemy with a shovel.
Also blowing a tank as infantry feels very satisfying.
P2W: No. I donated some $ to this game and bought only weapon skins. There is nothing that would give you advantage over non paying players.
CONS:
Its very open game, so sometimes people spawnkill (very frustrating), or your team is sitting in the wood instead of capturing objectives (also very frustrating). Bugs here and there can be annoying too but they get squashed over time.
Not everything is perfect and game can get frustrating at the times. Luckily its only a minority of times.
If you are fan of battlefield type games, stop staring at this review and download it already!
Last note to players who tried this game long ago: Game got alot more balanced with recent updates.  All factions are now equal. And lots of bad stuff and bugs are fixed.

A solid, simple fps game marred by the console generation and rushed production. The game has great map design for the most part, and a michael bay movie single player story. This is the stupidist plot in the series yet, but most people don't play for single player alone.
The multiplayer is where the game shines, but falls short of excellence by using console monetasation stragities such as dlc maps, weapons, and cosmetic skins. Gunplay feels well and weapons are mostly balanced, while still being unique. The game was clearly rushed and isn't optimised for the pc yet. The biggest letdown is the lack of dedicated servers. With the current and flawed match making only 2 of the many game modes have enough players to start and even those are plagued with cheaters. Vac anti-cheat is a good addition, but it doesn't work fast enough or effective enough. Finding a game on off hours is nearly impossible. usually 1.5k to 6k players worldwide but the flawed match making struggles to find a game or enough players to start a new one.
This game does have the most robust experence with custom games such as modes and bots compared to the any other game in the series. This game could have been the best in the series, but suffers too much from a money hungry company.

Heroes and Generals is by far the game with the most potential at this moment. The idea of several different campaigns in several theaters in certain years is a riveting idea. Sadly, at the moment the game is only in beta and only has 1 campaign with 2 nations. The gameplay itself is quite interesting as well. The Heroes part is when you start out and command actual soldiers. As you get more xp, you unlock more soldeir careers. You start out as your common but versitile infantryman. After a few mroe levels of xp you unlock the tankman, who, as you may have already guessed, drives tanks. Next you get a pilot, then paratrooper, then recon, and then a commander. These upgrades can take a while, unless you buy, with real money, in game coins. All the careers are very well thought out and balanced. The common inantryman can beat all of he other classes in certain circumstances and with certain weapons, but the other classes are far mroe specialiazed and will slaughter other classes but get wrecked by others. Fortunately, you can have many soldiers, so you can have Bob as a pilot and Pablo as a tankman, etc.  The general commands 1 or several assault teams, which determine where the Heroes are fighting in the overall war. In battle each assault team only has a liimited number of respawns and can only spawn certain troops. The battles are for control of several objectives on the map. There are several different maps, each one better suited for some troops than others. The weapons that the Heroes wield all cost money and you have to have ribbons to unlock certain guns. You get ribbons by kills with a type of weapon, driving around in a tank, blowing up people, etc. All of these contribute to a sense of progress and realism. Those are all the things that make me love the game, however there are a few minor things I should warn a person considering getting the game about.
1. The game is still in beta and there are a few bugs that can happen.
2. Some people (although not all) get annoyed by the need to shoot a person 2-3 times to get a kill. However, I will defend the game developers by saying that their reasoning makes senese, as shooting a person with a pistol at 500 yards should not come even close to killing them. Also shots to the head are 1 hit kills, unless you there is an extreme distance between you and the target. Also, the ranges make complete sense, as a rifle should shoot farther than a sub machine gun.
3. Tanks seem overpowered, especially if your team has none and no one thought to bring anti tank weapons.
4. Snipers are a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ 1 shot to the head from a position 500 yards away where you can't see them killing you may make you rage quite.
5. Loading screens take a while.
6. Your team is stupid.

I might be one of the few who do this, but I play most Call of Duty games for the campaign. Much like reading a "fluff" filled action book, the story is usually ridiculous and highly entertaining. Is it extremely thoughtful? No. In fact, it takes itself far too seriously, all of the time. Most play for the Multiplayer (which I found dated and poor for this title, compared to Black Ops II). I will say that I did enjoy the Campaign, it was very entertaining to play though, although as a game it fell short regarding having any "new" elements.
Infinity Ward (what is left of them) should focus their next efforts, if they can pull their attention from the CoD Cash-grab Fountain, to a stellar Action/Adventure title, that doesn't rely on empty feeling shooter mechanics, or over the top B-grade action movie dialogue. The team at Raven and Infinity Ward are EXTREMELY capable of creating beautiful, well thought out environments, and yet it is possible just to breeze through them, with no discovery encouraged. Give me a game to discover within, try to rival Uncharted, Tomb Raider, the Arkham series games.
Overall, the game is not terribly impressive in terms of Graphics, Gameplay, or Story, so I would recommend holding out until this is on sale, unless you just CAN'T play the previous titles for the Multiplayer.

The other pros include nice graphics, great sounds and so on...
Now for the part you WANT to hear :) Why is it bad then?
It's not the grind... The game basically forces you to pick a class and stick with it, wich in my opinion is a good thing, since it doesnt make you an all-rounder or a jack of trades Rambo. Also it's not a grind, if the battles are fun (if sometimes unbalanced). Some stuff is really exoensive though, so a bit of tweaking is in order there.
What DOES bug me, is that once you unlock a class, YOU CANNOT SWITCH BACK TO THE PREVIOUS ONE, WITHOUT PAYING COINS! How the f...ck does that work??? I already had the class unlocked, for christs sake!
My advice: Give it a go! If you want to personally live through war, or get a feeling, that you are in a WWII movie, then this is a gem for you! Just don't expect, that you will have tons of weapons/tanks/planes/etc...

To sum this up: I have played this game a long before it ever came out on steam. A way back when germans started with K98 bolt action rifle. I had big high hopes for this.
Game has moved quite a bit in more casualish way, I'm not saying it's necessarily a bad thing - but for me personally I would prefer more realistic style of game.
Now this review more in depth... bear with me.
Game used to be a whole lot interesting back when germans started with bolt action rifle faced with american semi-automatic one. This created more diversity between factions making germans lurking from the distance and sniping rushing americans who would attempt to get into close range fights.
Red Orchestra + real-time strategy would make an excellent, if not perfect, game in my mind. That's how I imagined over an year or two ago when I first played the game. I imagined that they would add more factions as priority, russians and brits, to give an example. More factions would add more depth to the RTS side of game and also more interesting battles for FPS players where you wouldn't face always the same weapons.
Then I imagined they would make damage model more realistic. To make semi-automatic rifles as useful as they were back in the day. All bullethits should have an permanent effect on the character in my opinion. And to make movement and shooting more smooth - to make game more realistic and immersive, you should make movement feel like you are in control of the character.
I would also thought that they would make games much bigger, increasing the player count per match. Again, to make game feel more immersive and actionpacked. 64 player games would be great I thought. The sight of over 20 germans climbing from trench shouting furiously and charging towards you - epic.
They did not do any of this, instead the game nowadays is just like very simple RTS combined with worse version of battlefield 1942 to me. Remainder of very promising and interesting consept it once was. They also made content much harder to reach by playing for free- luckily I had all my snipers and tank drivers still available, which would nowadays require hundreds or thousands of hours of gaming to unlock. So I don't feel the passion of the developers in this, not when I did when I first played this. Instead I feel like they are developing this just for the audience / money. Not that there is nothing wrong with money. I might be wrong and this certainly is just an opinion.
I do understand that they listened to their players, being quiet all the time just happily and ignorantly awaiting for my dream game to complete. So they went with the loud majority band wagon. So I'm writing this review here, just to hope that a member of Reto-Moto happens to see this, goes to game designer and reminds him that there is also a group of players like me: who respect passion and innovation in games.
What can I say? I do know it's in development. But I greatly dislike the course of development, the route it's taking. Therefore I think giving this project thumps down is fairly reasonable. Thank you for reading this trough.

Forget the anti-COD circlejerk.  This is a polished game with very few bugs, one of the best CoD games they've put together.  The multiplayer is just what CoD is known for, smaller maps with consistant action and good objective based team play on game modes like Blitz and Domination.  There's some great new game modes like Search and Rescue (think of Search and Destroy only you can revive your teammates), Bliz (which is like a CTF mode but you only need to make it to the enemy base), and they've added all the old favorites like TDM and even Gun game.  There's also a few squad based co-op modes worth checking out, and a pretty decent singleplayer, with over the top Michael Bay explosions, overly dramatic world ending storyline, and playable dogs!
It's worth checking out.  To be completely objective, the one problem the game has it that it does suffer from hackers, there' quite a few in multiplayer.  While outright hacking like aimbots and shooting through walls is exceedingly rare, wall hacking is pretty common.  Fortunately most of these people are terrible even if they're wall hacking and you can frag them all the same, so it's typically not completely gamebreaking, but can be frustrating.

Mount & Blade: Warband is simply one of the best games of all-time and one of those few rare gems that always remains on my hard drive. I play awhile, leave for other games, come back and play another round, leave.... Wash and repeat.
Gameplay can be difficult in the beginning, as your character will start with very low-end equipment and no army to speak of.  Stick with it, improve your skills and stats, and Warband will be a very rewarding experience.
+ Open ended sandbox
+ Weapon dynamics (although polearms can certainly use improved modeling)
+ Many variations of soldier classes and weapons
+ Fantastic combat
+ Excellent combat
+ Combat is spot on
+ Did I mention combat?
- Graphics (gameplay more than makes up for mediocre graphics).
- Limited storyline and script
Although the vanilla version is excellent with endless replayability, the perfection is in the many different free mods available.  Many are very professional with incredible story depth and gameplay such as "Prophesy of Pendor" (my personal favorite) and "Brytenwalda".  Play these for a very challenging experience far and beyond the standard game.
In summary, M & B Warband is highly recommended for players who enjoy 1st person medieval combat.

A few minor annoyance issues with game play tend to bother you after about 40 hours of game play.  Apparently players agree that the game needs "fine tuning" or more of a story line.  There are now a ton of MODs out there to download for free.  Each seeks to expand on a great sandbox game and offers great variety for replay value.  The only negative is the origional game, and the numerous mods, all have very limited RPG elements.  I don't want the game "scripting me" or "forcing me" to  play a certain way.. but I'd love to have a few plot lines thrown in.  Voice acting would be nice as well.
Mount and Blade 2 has been promised for some time now but does not have a release date.  This is a great series and I devotely HOPE that the next installement drops soon.

I bought the game, went on multiplayer and was almost immediately killed by someone who flew through a building, throwing insults at me and my mother.
Well here we are again. The latest CoD installment. At the time of writing this, I have invested over 80 hours into this game, about 10 for the campaign and 70 for multiplayer. I wish with all my heart that I could say this game "breaks the mould" or as the product description says, is "an extraordinary step forward". But I can't.
The developers have grown too accustomed to their huge sales and are terrified of changing the format in case they lose money. Sure, the graphics have been improved, there are new multiplayer tweaks to make the matches somewhat more interesting. Sure, things have changed, but nothing has CHANGED.
The game still employs the most basic point-and-fire system imaginable, so no matter how fluid it is, your mind is never challenged. You could play tense, lightning fast matches all night, but you would still have the brain of a potato. It's not stimulating at all. I found myself on the verge of dribbling once or twice.
CAMPAIGN: The campaign has fallen into the trap of "bigger is better" but unfortunately, more explosions and more chaos do not make a better game. No matter how many satellites explode, however many dams burst and however many invasions are repelled, the campaign is not memorable. You never think "Wow." afterwards. It sort of fades from your memory even as you play. Maybe that's a good thing. At best, the storyline seems to be some very weak narrative linked by lots of shooting. The characters have no depth so you care little for them when they inevitably die in horrific circumstances. Masterful characters are written so well that you put your character in harm's way to save them. I cried like a child at the ending to Mass Effect 2 but the GHOSTS characters could be tortured to death with a brick and I wouldn't bat an eye.
MULTIPLAYER: Where can I start with the multiplayer? I think will start with the weapons. I don't know how many millions they had at their disposal but to present us with 8 assault rifles and 4 sniper rifles? That is pitiful. It's like booking a table at a fancy restaurant, ordering the "lightly chargrilled buffalo rump steak with creamy cheddar slices on organic, wholewheat farmhouse bread". And they give you a cheeseburger. It's almost insulting.
Also, the stats for each weapon are nearly pointless. The damage of any automatic weapon is irrelevant because your opponent will be dead before they have time to react even if you have the weakest assault rifle available. It's literally a case of "who shoots first, wins". And despite many experiments I did on how accuracy affects bullet spread, I cannot see the link. Precision marksman rifles and tiny submachine guns both appear to fire with near-perfect accuracy, with spreads of about 30cm across 100m distances. It's so hard to miss, that I sneezed whilst looking at an opponent, accidentally clicked, and killed them with a headshot.
I have not experienced one single occasion where 2 accurate shooters fire automatics at each other and the last to pull the trigger survived.
The feature of the sprint vault (jump low obstacles while sprinting and carry on sprinting) is a nice touch, but it's affect on the gameplay is miniscule. Also, the slide feature was raved about, as though people have forgotten the identical purpose dolphin dive in Black Ops, which came out 4 years ago.  It too, makes little difference in moving about the map.
MAPS: The maps have pros and cons, some major, some minor. The maps are all far too small to bother with the need for sniper rifles. With the ridiculous precision of the assault rifles and LMGs, sniper rifles are useless. The developers need to either degrade other weapons' accuracy accordingly, or make the maps at least twice as big. Don't believe me? Try the map Whiteout or Stonehaven which both have extremely long sightlines and I almost guarantee that you will be killed by someone who is likely using an assault rifle, often without the scope, from the other side of the map.
Some maps have dynamic qualities, such as shootable ladders or trees to make new routes (only 1 or 2 on each map) buttons which move some part of the map (eg a door) and in Tremor, guess what happens? Exactly right! Every few minutes, the screen shakes predictably.
As I mentioned in the first section, there are FAR too many hackers in this game. Perhaps in every 10-15 matches, you will encounter somebody aimbotting, wallhacking etc, which makes the game impossible for legit players.
CONCLUSION: The bottom line then. Ghosts is a great game, but it has made no attempt to improve on the previous installments. Call of Duty is a series with so much promise and so much potential, but they have been squandering it for half a decade. They are slaves to the customer demand, churning out a game every year or so to keep us happy, and refusing to change anything major, just in case they lose a scrap of their precious profits (insert Gollum joke here).
And the thing is, it's OUR fault. We eat it up. Every poor game, every failure to take a step forward and we buy millions of copies to make them think that it's okay. They have worked out that they don't NEED to make big changes to keep us on a leash.
If you sent back a meal at a restaurant because it was cold, and they replaced with another, slightly less cold meal, would you eat it? You'd send it back again and ask why they haven't improved it. That is what we need to do with Call of Duty, and video  games as a whole. Improvement makes things better.
If cavemen had never tried anything new, we'd still be sitting in caves, banging rocks together. Looking at people playing CoD, I wonder if we still are.

I want this game to be good.  I really do.  But the devs need to change things a lot before it can be good.  This game is a mix between pay to win and pay to not grind.  Most F2P games are P2W (which is why I truly think that F2P models are a rip-off, but that's another discussion entirely), but this game in particular is bad.  Guns that you would get automatically in any other WWII game (MP-40, K98, Thompson, 1911, Luger, etc) you have to buy (starter weapons are the G43 for the Germans - which was not the standard issue rifle for German infantry - and M1 Garand for the US) with in game credits or VIP gold (stuff you pay real US dollars for).  However, it is expensive as hell to buy these things.  The MP-40 costs over 100K credits, and you get maybe 3k credits a game if you're good.
There are different classes: pilot, tank crewman, paratrooper and sniper.  The flying is awful in this game and each side only has one plane.  The tanks are the most developed thus far, but they're very imbalanced.  The starter tanks are basically metal M34s with no stopping power whatsoever.  It takes forever to unlock better tanks, so you're forced to either die continually in your garbage starter tank until you can unlock a tank worth using, or you have to buy better tanks with real money.
This game has great graphics, but the infantry combat is kind of bad (you slide around a bit, intead of stopping when you stop pressing W, S, A, or D), the sounds are bad, the visual effects aren't great and the hit registration is terrible.
I have heard that the dev team is small on this game.  But I think the real issue is that they're too focused on their store side of this F2P game, instead of making the game actually better.  If this game became a modern day Battlefield 1942, I would pay $60 upfront for it.  Instead, it's botched.
I'm going to continue to play this on and off as the game progresses, but as of right now the game is not terribly fun to play.  Again, I want this game to be good, but the devs need to put their backs into it.

Far Cry 3 tells you the story of Jason Brody and his friends, who travel to an island to celebrate Jason's little brother's pilot license. But Jason's friends (not all) disappear within the time....
Jason meets a guy, called Denis. Denis helps Jason not only to save his frirends, but to join Citra and her alliance. After what Jason finishes his job with Denis, he travells to Vaas' boss' island, to gather more information on his friends.
On that island, all the action beggins. Jason becomes an undercover agent for Hoyt (Vaas' boss) and in a mission, Jason is sent to Hoyt's jail to torture Jason's brother (Hoyt knew that Jason was working for Citra). His brother takes the pain given by Jason, and then Jason kills Hoyt and gets with his brother to Citra's castle (Citra is actually Vaas' sister).

You will choose what your soul wants.

Far Cry 3 is one of those open-world games that actually makes you FEEL you'd WANT to explore the Rook Islands with its varied wild flora AND fauna (hostile or indifferent), as well as the various enemies (pirates or privateers) and with the Rakyat assisting at times. The story missions are quite a lot of fun, and if you level up properly none of them are very difficult (i.e. do the stealth kills and try to take down outposts undetected to get extra XP for the skills).
You started out as a party guy Jason Brody, who can't do anything. Your brother Grant was the ex-Army, and somehow you ended up captured on this island held by pirates and right in the INTRO sequence your brother got killed and your mad dash to freedom ended up with you diving over a waterfall, but you lived, and you woke up in a village, and handed your first mission... and a wimply pistol... get up this tower on top of the hill, and activate it.
From there on, you steadily progress from a wimpy adrenaline junky to a fearsome killing machine capable of mowing down squads of professional mercenaries with LMG or assault rifle, hit wings off a fly at 100 yards with a sniper rifle, blade dance with professional knife fighters, stealth kill like a ninja, as you liberate the Rook Islands from two megalomaniacs, Vaas, and his boss, Hoyt, while recovering your friends one by one.
The islands are beautiful, and the animals behave independently of you. Goats and Buffalos and pigs and more wander the landscape, and predators like bears, leopards, even tigers wander the wild hunting them, and if you get in the way, you as well. In the ocean there are bull sharks and regular fish, and in the swamps there are crocodiles. Yes, it's a ton of fun exploring the place. There are small villages, pirate and merc outposts (that you can liberate... by killing everybody), unoccupied villages that were sites of atrocities, more radio towers you can deactivate, plus for the obssessive collectors, various artifacts to collect, such as 120 relics from the past cultures (including one from Chinese history!) letters from the Japanese WW2 occupation (plenty of bodies left around), memory cards left in outposts detailing the sordid narc industry links of Rook Island, as well as different animals and plants (they go in the survival handbook).
There are also untold number of caves, underground passages, leading to totally unknown areas deep within the bowels of the island that makes you wonder if you're playing Tomb Raider. :D  Indeed, the radio towers and many other sequences do require a bit of jumping and climbing to accomplish.
Even on the surface, there are random things happening. Friendly and enemy jeeps patrol the routes. Enemy soldiers will patrol, and sometimes, force march prisoners / slaves on the road. You may engage, or not as you see fit, but they are excellent source of XPs, as valid as any one. And animals do roam the island, as it is wild out there.
There are plenty of side missions, some of which are handed out by locals, like "help find my daughter, who ran away with boyfriend!"  in addition to the story missions. Furthermore, conquered outposts often have bounty missions (kill a pirate or a merc and his minions) as well as "path of the hunter" missions (hunt down X animals using provided weapons). (HINT: you only have to use the same CLASS of weapon, not the specific weapon. If they provide a regular .45ACP, bring your customized .44 Magnum or .50AE Desert Eagle)
Ah, speaking of weapons... lots and lots of weapons. Pistols, sniper rifles, shotguns, assault rifiles, grenade launchers, light machine guns, special weapons (including recurve bow), and signature weapons. Some weapons can be customized with different type of sights, extended magazines, even a suppressor. And there are different paintjobs available too. Add the oddballs, like repair tool (welding torch), flamethrower, and even a flare gun... and things can get interesting indeed. Did I mention that many vehicles have mounted weapons, like a HMG that you can wield?
How you tackle mission (usually involving killing everybody at a certain place) is entirely up to you. Run and gun? Snipe and hide? Silent and deadly? Lure and ambush? It is all up to you. When you have the best sniper rifle (.50 cal with suppressor two-stage zoom scope) you can kill even a heavy with a single shot to the head from afar. There are also sometimes captured predators that you can "liberate" with a shot to the cage, thus letting it attack the enemies in the camp for you! Remember, bonus points if you were never detected (1500 xp instead of 500 xp).
I have tried many open-world games before, from Far Cry 2 to Mercenaries 2, from GTA 3 (and sequels) to many others. Far Cry 3 stands above the rest because it is so well balanced. it doesn't unlock too many skills (some require you to unlock via story missions) at once, no matter how much XP you accumulated. it also doesn't unlock the 2nd island until well past 75% point. At each point you are reminded of the stakes you're playing with... the lives of your friends that may still be in pirate's hands, and each and every one will be scarred for life. The villians are psychopaths, but interesting psychopaths. And the other characters that you meet? They all have their own motivations, which may or may not match your own.
Somehow, FC3 just struck the right balance between too "scattered brained", i.e. "Too many choices! What do I do now?" vs. "where's the freedom? I am bored, I want to do something ELSE"...  And there are plenty of variety in the missions as well as outposts. On the hunt missions, you have to use the specified weapon class/type., which can be challenging, such as hunting tigers with a pistol, or bears with a shotgun. On the bounty missions, you are to kill the one or two "leaders" with your blade. The rest are up to you with no restrictions. Just keep in mind in late game there can be two leaders with a dozen minions around them, and killing them all can be a difficult endeavor, esp. if you can only knife the leaders.
The skills you learn are divided into three categories: crane, shark, and spider, which of which has a different "tree". As mentioned before, they are unlocked by progressing in the story missions and can be learned by spending "skill points" which are earned by every few thousand XP. And they add a lot of fun abilities, such as chain takedowns, knife throw take down, grenade takedown, double take down, death from above, death from below, and so on.
There are bazillion crates scattered on the island, each containing some artifacts and/or money. You can further loot the bodies (enemy or friendly) for more artifacts, many of which can be sold for $$$. If you have killed some fauna, you cna often skin them for making containers / slings for ammo, wallet, and so on, and it's the only way you can carry more weapons, more ammo, even more money. In fact, you can also craft herbal medicine from the plants you gathered (which are generically divided into "colored leaves", and you need X of Red and Y of yellow and so on. As you progress you'll learn other formulas, like animal repellant, hunting instinct (lets you see animals, even behind hills), as well as herbal medicine that just heals you, deep dive potion that lets you go below 60 meters deep, and more.
All in all, Far Cry 3 is a ton of fun with variety of missions, side mission, as well as plenty of freeform encounter play. The story of growth and one man's journey from wimp to hero is the story of the player. And THAT ultimately, is why it's so much fun.

I'm a big fan of Red Orchestra so I thought I'd give this game a try. First thing I noticed when I jumped into battle were the bad combat mechanics. Torso shots don't kill, you need at least 3-4 of them with the Gewehr 43, like 7 with the MP34 and 2 of them with the slow Kar-98 (I obviously didn't try any other weapons thanks to the blatant pay2win that this game is, the devs genuinely expect you to spend hours playing their badly made game grinding XP to buy guns OR pay 20 USD to buy a virtual rifle, yeah that makes sense) In a fast paced game this wouldn't be a problem, but Heroes and Generals isn't exactly fast paced, on the contrary, so when you shoot at an enemy running towards a building, 90% of the time you won't kill him because it takes so many hits to kill him, unless you get a headshot. It is pretty offputting to hit someone 3 times and just watch them run into the building, perfectly alive. It is also great to shoot an enemy running at you with a shovel and getting killed instead of him, because you are apparently shooting him with a bb gun but his shovel is like a lightsaber.
The prices to buy items are just insulting. 10 EUR (12.53 USD) will get you 2200 gold, which will ALMOST get you a scoped Kar-98, but not quite, you are still short 99 gold. So 12.53 of your hard earned dollars won't get you a scoped rifle in an early access game.There are some good free2play games out there, with a good business model and this game, at the moment, is not one of them, not even close. This game contains the bad aspects of free2play games, which makes it feel like a cashgrab. Reminds me of WarZ (currently known as "Infestation: Survivor Stories) in that sense.
I don't wanna get too much into the rest of the game mechanics. I understand it is an early access game and all that is subject to change, but it is hard not to get a little critical of an early access game, not even close to finished, practicing such blatant money whoring. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

Some of the mechanics are okay, some aren't; shooting is decent, hit detection is atrocious, and the sheer number of hits some people can survive is bizarre. Are people paying real money for armour that lets them become bullet tanks? I hate this game.
Red Orchestra 2 is better in just about every way; better shooting mechanics, hit detection, graphics, ambiance, gritty warzone feeling, spawning, capturing, everything. Red Orchestra 2 is the game to play if you're looking for WW2 combat. Everything you do in that game is a struggle for control of the battlefield and every kill, suppressing fire, and advance is satisfying and helpful for the entire team. Heroes and Generals completely fails to have that in-depth feel.
Strangely enough, I was excited that this game would be MMO and you could traverse the Western Front and choose where to battle, but you can't, it's not an MMO, it's just done in map instances. Even Red Orchestra 2 has more players per match. Way more. Play Red Orchestra 2 instead of this, you won't be let down.
Oh and, Heroes and Generals is pay-to-win. Enough said.

Okay so my #1 Rule when reviewing a game is that I must at least play 100 hours so that I can get a real feel for the game, but for Heroes & Generals I had to make an exception... For starters it's a free to play MMOFPS set in WWII. Unlike traditional lobby based shooters, Battles fought within Heroes and Generals contribute towards a continuously changing world based on the battles that are fought and won by the players in this war-torn European country side. High ranking players acting as “Generals” command various assault teams towards key objective locations within the world. Once an assault team has been moved into play it is up to the "Heroes" to determine what happens, with the help of there commanding general giving them there orders.
Now he's why I am posting this review so early compared to usual. On my first ever game of Heroes & Generals I was given the oppitunity to feel like a total badass... Here's the senario, there was an abandoned farmhouse deep within German lines with a group of four germans guarding the area that we had been told to take out. Me and my squad of 2 other were coming down the hill towards the farmhouse, the Pvt. to my left gets sniped from the vantage point positioned within the first of the two barns. The rest of the team and I take cover before running inside, taking out the guy up in the vantage point before we get flanked from behind and as he gets a few shots off, two hit my team-mate killing him, I dash behind some barrel and taking two pot-shots at him hitting him twise, once in the chest and the second in the heard landing him in the cart behind him. I run into the other barn taking out the other two guys swiftly then I go to check outside for re-enforcements. Indeed there was, a jeep carrying four men was heading towards the farm, so i get behind cover and get ready for an ambush in the time I have. As the jeep pulls up i roll a grenade under the chassy. The explosion took out two of the guys, the other two, shell shocked stumble into the barn seeking cover, I manage to shoot one in the back then flank around then assassinate the other with my knife...
So for Heroes & Generals im giving the game a 6/10 because of its well thought out battles but there are quite a few bugs, but it is still in early access
