I hate/love this game... mostly hate.
This game still has load of work to do. Leveling your soldier is arduous and making it something other than basic infantry costs a lot of your hard earned grind money. If you don't like your option, it costs even to go back to infantry.
With my first soldier I tried tank crew. Guess was first tank squishy carbage without even real cannon, that can't even pierce most of the enemy armor? yes. And I had to learn through hard way that you need to pay more that grind money to buy special AP ammo to even bite enemy tanks.
Ok, I suffer to real tank, classic Stuart. Guess what I learn then? This game has HORRIBLE hit detection. Even your HE ammo that has 10 meter blast radius needs to hit within 1m of enemy infantry foot for hit to register, and then you need to be lucky even for that. Only way you can tackle enemy infantry 100% certainty is either hit them spot on or switch to machine gun on your turret, which you need to switch on every damn time, and it most often ends up you losing the sight of infantry, and 20 seconds later you find that infantry sneaking outside your tank, waiting for you to pop up and look around. Yeah, for you to see clearly to your surroundings, you need to peek from your tank.
Stuart experience was bad, I am already wondering should I quit. Then I think that in other hand, there's promise in this game, and buy pilot with a plane. Does this pilot have a mustang? spitfire? No. It has some weird bigass lightning plane, and guess what? You get your♥♥♥♥♥absolutely beaten by germany planes.
Honestly, this game has burned me. I keep seeing something good in this game, but three out of five times, it just makes me absolutely mad because of constant BS moments it keeps throwing at you. Even if you are winning match, if you've had been facing BS like being pitted against 2 enemy planes that are faster and more agile than your mammoth lightning, you do not feel good.
Let's say that 1/2 matches you lose. Those feel really bad, because most of the time there are no good losses that make you feel like it's *your* fault. It's either that nobody on your team plays objective (reminds me bit of like having bad team at LoL or Dota2) or that you have been pitted in absolutely horrid matchmake, I've had many matches where I am alone against 3-4 enemy tanks, and I've been been many times 2v1 with my ♥♥♥♥♥♥ lightning plane against better german fighters, once even 3v1. and generally I am already knee deep in♥♥♥♥♥♥if it's 1v1, because german planes are simply better. Sure, they might not have as much bombs as USA planes, but that does not count here, because most times you'll get shot before you get to aim and drop your bombs.
Sometimes the matches begin even if you don't have enough infantry, and you are just left to watch as enemy infantry caps your assault teams spawnpoints from air or from tank. You can try, but good luck hitting them.
Then there are the won matches. 3/5 you do not feel like you have won. Because of all the hit detection BS and overpowered enemies.
I am absolutely done with this game. It does have lot of promise, but this game should not have this pricy transaction system for game that is clearly in early Beta.
I might check it after 1.0, and see if I change my mind. I will admit however that it does have promise and it tries some new interesting things such as RTS mixed with FPS matches... but that content is only to those that have played unhealthy amount of this game grinding their soldiers or straight out bought a general rank soldier... so I cannot comment on how good that part of the game is.
... At this game's current state, I do NOT recommend it.

[EDIT for new developments]
Another year, another CoD.
I find this one of the "better" CoD's in terms of customization and visual appeal, but that is heavily overshadowed by its glaring flaws.
(This applies only for the MP portions, not the SP or Extinction)
For one, there is no form of built in anti-cheat, not even VAC, so hackers are more commonplace than they have been in previous iterations on the PC, which quickly makes for a unpleasant experience.
[EDIT: Their is now a anti-cheat, and it does work, to a degree]
Second, the hitreg is at its all-time low, with being shot around corners and bullets disappearing into nothingness commonplace, even at seemingly low pings, which you cannot even tell since the game no longer displays that for you.
Thirdly, the map designs in this game are absolutely terrible, with them ether being too big (Stonehaven), or too small (Strikezone), with only 2-3 maps being a reasonable size for the average 6v6 TDM match.
For the fourth point, gun and equipment balance is out of whack in this iteration, with Assault rifles essentially beating every other weapon type in all situations, even snipers and SMG's, and explosives like IED's (the new Bouncing Betty/Claymore) being nigh impossible to see without a specific perk, which really drags down the experience when you just randomly die due to a IED placed somewhere you cant even see.
For the final nail in the coffin, the game has horrendous performance issues, even on beefy computers. With framerates dropping below 60 even on the smaller levels, it disrupts gameplay quite a bit when your framerate drops in the middle of a gunfight, causing you to die when you should have lived.
+ Character Customization
+/- Updated engine adds prettiness
- Hitreg
- Lack of Anti-cheat [EDIT: Their is a anti-cheat in place, it works to a degree]
- Poor map design
- Poor weapon and equipment balance
- Poor optimization
Overall, If I didnt get this game as a gift, I would not be buying it, but if you got it for free, its a good bout of fun. Just be prepared to scream bloody murder at disappearing bullets.

Far Cry 3 is an open world first person shooter with some RPG and Stealth elements. But there's so much more to it than that. Being a very cynical and critical person that, despite being an avid "gamer" pretty much my whole life, doesn't like video games that much, I'm shocked to say that this game is a valid contender to my favorite game ever. This does not mean I consider it the best game ever, I mean that out of every game in my life I've ever played, this is what I might have gotten the most enjoyment and fun out of. The game that I've liked the most. Now, without further ado, my full, unbiased assessment of the game.
The gameplay consists of exploration, combat and side activities. In Far Cry 3, you explore a large, colorful and lively island called "Rook Island", filled with settlements, caves, small islands, mountains, lakes, and so much more. There are plenty of collectibles and loot out there waiting to be found, as well as lots of other cool secrets and easter eggs I won't spoil. You can get around by foot, car, boat, hanglider and even a
later in the game.
The combat has you fighting both humans and animals that you find around the island. There are mainly two ways of dealing with threats: The shooty explody messy loud way using firearms, grenades and other fun stuff, and the sneaky stealthy stabby way, using your knife, rocks to distract enemies, and other stuff. Both are fun and have their advantages and disadvantages. I did, though, find stealth as the way to go in most cases, since you die quickly in firefights since Jason isn't a superhero that can just shrug off bullets by biting them out of- oh, wait, nevermind.
The game has a diverse selection of weapons, in the categories as what you would expect (Assault Rifle, pistol, machine gun, sniper rifle, grenade launcher, shotgun, etc.), but also has some more unique items if you're not a whiny ♥♥♥♥♥ (Recurve bow with explosive arrows, flare gun, a mother♥♥♥♥ing flamethrower, etc.).
If you're like most people, you'll try to stealth it up most of the time, but inevitably slip up, get caught, go rambo style and blow everything up.
The story might just be one of the best parts of this game. I'm not going to spoil too much of it, but I'll give the basic outline.
You are Jason Brody, an annoying rich spoiled white kid who has come to an island with his friends, who are also rich white kids. Before long they are all captured by pirates, and Jason ends up in the camp of Vaas. the insane main antagonist of the game. He manages to barely escape, where upon he is rescued by the Rakyat, a tribe fighting the pirates and struggling to regain freedom. You become a beacon of hope for their movement, being the only person to ever escape Vaas's camp alive. Throughout the game you will help their movement, adapt to your new environment and attempt to rescue your friends. But the journey will change you drastically, for better or worse.
The game features a large cast of diverse, believable characters, the voice acting is superb, and the story is overall absorbing and very well written, with some of the most fantastic dialogue I've ever seen in a video game.
9/10. Has some very minor flaws, but overall a nearly perfect game.

Farcry 3 is truly an outstanding game.
Story:
The story is emotional and original. The game starts off with you, Jason Brody, a young man with his friends trying to have the best vacation ever. To finish off their journey, they decide to make a blind jump onto Rook Island (A fictional island) However, everything changes when you, your brothers and your friends are captured by terrorists and held for ransom on the island. Jason Brody soon gets free from captivity and starts his quest on finding and rescuing his friends. Throughout his quest, you see Brody go through emotional changes that effect him. For example, Jason begins with not wanting to kill anybody. Towards the end of the game, he kills more and more and he doesn't think twice about it. When he first kills he believes it's necessary to save his friends but it soon becomes a part of him, takes over him, changes him. It is very interesting to see the transition as he goes.
Gameplay:
The gameplay is solid and unique to that of other games in it's genre. There's plenty of shooting, explosions, and stabbing for you action fans out there. However, there is also a crafting system in which you can craft packs for more ammunition, health packs (medial syringes), even drugs that inhance your abilities greatly for a short amount of time.
Pros
-solid gameplay
-great story
-best villian
-a lot of fun
-plenty to do in the world. Many side quests help you get to know the people and the interesting history of the island.
-Weapons feel smooth, look great, and are fun to use whether it be a rocket launcher, bow, or even a standard pistol. They are so much fun!
-100+ hours of gameplay
-two endings
-plays with your emotions
-well constructed world
-no more weapon jams
-fun addicting multiplayer
Cons
-The co-op mode is very much lacking. Very linear, the story is linear, and stealth is very difficult to do which is a bit upsetting. Still fun, just don't expect anything as awesome as the single player
-When you start off, you get very little ammunition and it does take a while to craft to be able to hold more ammunition
The single player in general deserves a 96/100

It's great if you want a Pay-2-Win WWII themed Airsoft Reenactment simulator. The infantry combat is blocky. Blockier than even Red Orchestra 1's combat. It's also down-right miserable. The bullet velocity is like a snail. Every bullet seems to have a 200fps velocity which makes fighting someone up-close a bit frustrating. Anti-tank weapons are near useless. The damage, even for an arcade shooter with a health bar, is ridiculously low... even on high powered rifles such as a K98k.
It takes two-three shots to kill someone with an M1, and that's fine since it's semi-auto. However, it takes 2-3 shots to kill the same guy with a K98k... the K98k is bolt action.
Why didn't they do what Valve did with DOD:S? Meaning, M1 Garand is 2 shot kill, unless headshot. K98k is one shot kill on torso or above. That kind of balance was just fine. One had rate of fire, while the other had stopping power.
NOTE: I'm not saying they need to make bullet travel instant. I'm saying they need to make it realistic. It shouldn't take 5 seconds for a bullet to travel 300 feet.
Being a paratrooper is even more miserable than being just regular infantry. That's due to the fact that seemingly everyone who plays H&G are 12 year olds whose silhouette identifcation does not extend past "it's a plane." You'll find yourself constantly getting murdered by your own team whether you stay in the plane or jump out.
What makes it even worse is, they make it EXTREMELY EASY to tell if it's a C-47 or a Ju-57. Ju 57 is made out of corrugated steel, has GIANT IRON CROSSES ON IT, is shaped like a brick, and has THREE ENGINES. A C-47 is shaped like a bullet, has wider wings, only TWO ENGINES, and MASSIVE INVASION STRIPES PAINTED ON THEM.
On top of all that, there's blue markers over the friendly planes, I believe.
They got tank combat right(ish), though. Think of it as a mix of Red Orchestra tanks and World of Tanks.... except it's everything bad about World of Tanks mixed in with everything good about Red Orchestra tanks. Basically, it's a first person perspective of inside a tank, unless you have your commander popped out of his cupola.
The tank movement is arcadey, which is okay. I don't mind that.The shell velocity when you shoot is as correct as it can be.
So what's my issue? Health bars on vehicles. They should not happen. What happens to a tank should depend on where it's hit, and what it's hit with. It should also depend on the amount of armor. The only thing armor does is "If the shot's gonna bounce, it's gonna bounce. If it's gonna go through, it's gonna go through and take away half of it's health."
That's not how it should be. It should be more like this, "If the shot goes through, it's going to slow down substantially and do stuff to the stuff and people inside." Also, "what angle is the tank facing me from?" should be a factor.
However... be warned... pilots are seemingly unable to tell what team you're on. Be prepared to die to your own team even more.... even though there are blue markers for those who can't identify friendlies from the sky...
My worst issue with it, though? From level 0-3 (or however it works), you play on a fun small-scale Domination type mode on a small map that is good for the amount of players in a match. After you get to level 3, you're forced to play this "Defender/Attacker" game mode. The maps are just too large for how few people are in a given match. The maps are also just far too open for it to be fun as infantry.... especially when the biggest vehicle anyone on your team has is a Kubelwagen or a Jeep, and the enemy has tanks.
My second worst issue is it's a terrible grind-fest. You earn money slowly. You level up your ribbons slowly. You level your character up slowly. You can alleviate the money and character levelling issue by a VERY SLIGHT margin. However, if you want to make your ribbons (how you ACTUALLY unlock new stuff) level up more quickly, you have to PAY EVEN MORE money for individual boosts for the specific ribbon you want.
Alternatively, you can just drop $15 to buy the gun/item/vehicle you want immediately without doing anything to obtain it before-hand.
All-in-all, Heroes & Generals is a massive money grabbing Pay-2-Win, grind, teamkill-fest.
If I were you, I wouldn't fall for the "Free-2-Play" in the title. If I were you, I'd move along and have a look at Red Orchestra (both of them).
You only have to pay for them once, and then you have literally everything the game offers (it offers fun, is what it does). No paid DLC. No Paying to Win. Nothing like that. It does everything H&G WANTS to do, but is so much better at doing it.
I do not recommend this game, and I would not recommend it to even my worst enemy.

World War 2, a war to end all wars. The era has been put in many video games most commonly Call of duty and Battefield. This game introduces a interesting RTS and Fps style of play. There are Heroes which are represented by the playable classes and the Generals who command the Assault teams that are bascailly the points of Heroes. However, Even in Early access there are still some problems.
To begin with, i would like to start with the pros of the game. It has a great element of teamwork, making it impossible to win the round without having any support. This game has gone through many updates each introducing a new piece of gameplay making the action game (Fps) part even more interesting. The wide collection of weapons and tanks help add to the World War era. Each side has it own strength and weakness with the introduction of the new update. This game is easily one of the (if not THE) greatest single-player FPSes I've ever played. (There is multiplayer, but you don't need to know that. Seriously, don't bother.)
Everything falls just right in this game; hunting animals to craft larger rucksacks, wallets and ammo pouches is fun (complete with certain equipment that can't be crafted without sidequest-specific animal hides), shooting feels just inaccurate enough with assault rifles, explosions feel explosiony, fire is gorgeous, water is gorgeous, and there are SO MANY WAYS to take on enemy outposts (from brute force, to range, to stealth, and even sneaky trap-setting).
However, one detail sets this game apart for me:
The sound.
I don't mean the music, or the way footsteps fall, or any bitrate magic; I mean a very specific thing:
Echoes.
You see, when a gun fires, someone shouts, a car accelerates, or an animal roars and you are at a distance, a magical echoing effect is applied to the sounds, and there's something whimsical to hearing it. Allow an example:
You're bearing down on your targets, safe in a cliffside. They have no clue a sniper is looking down on them. You shoot, and one falls without notice. Another. Another. But maybe you miss, or shoot the fourth guy in the leg, or someone turns around and sees his body fall down. Suddenly the outpost is in panic, men scream and shout, firing their guns at things that aren't there. Then one spots you, and you hear his call of "I SEE ONE!" ring out across the air. All this sounds cool, but as I said before, hearing it with echoes is truly something
.

As a general gamer, I usually like to enjoy my games as soon as I pick them up. If a game doesn't really catch my eye or I try it and find out that it infuriates me, I will know then that it's not the game for me. Heroes & Generals seemed like a good game, until I tried it out myself to find out what it was really like. Only then did I realize there were problems with the game that affected my enjoyability. Keep in mind my review does not go in-depth as much as people who have played for hours on end, this is from the perspective of guy who wanted to try the game out.
Pros: - WW2 Esque Setting (Of Course)
- Graphics Look Decent if not Good!
- Map is Huge
Cons: - This Game is Buggy (Of course I understand it's still in Beta though)
- This Game Can Become Very One-Sided
- Movement Feels Sluggish/Not Responsive Enough
- Driving Feels Akward
- Map is Too Big For On Foot Soldiers
Now it is time to tell my first encounter.
So after telling my friend to download the game and launch we hop on to the main screen, and I'll be honest the UI confused me a bit. The layout didn't quite point out what it needed to and I felt as though I was poking around stuff on my own, no help whatsoever. After finally figuring out how to use the UI and figuring out how to join a squad with my friend we decided to group up. Only problem was that his game was bugged, and for some reason listed him as a higher tier. The only reason we found this out was after he restarted his game and it set him back to Tier 1. Ok, that was weird but it still didn't affect my gameplay, I was excited to see the actual gameplay. Now we finally got in a group and finally got into a match. We were thrown right in and we both had a general sense of what to do, so that wasn't a problem. One thing became very clear very quick though. The match we joined was a one-sided war. While our side would spawn with a bike, the enemy side was spawning with vehicles with mounted guns. By the time we had biked our way over to a waypoint, we were gunned down immediatley. Afterwards it began the vicious cycle of running out under-geared and dieing constantly. Then once our original spawn point was beginning to be captured, the game would decide to spawn us further back on foot. This caused our original point to almost be captured,and  the only way we saved it was to storm the place with grenades. After a while the game began to frustrate me and I ended up just quitting and deleting the game from my library. I know that it's in beta, but a beta is still a good indicator as to if you'll like the game or not.
Overall I Did Not Enjoy This Game, It Could Be Expanded Upon But I Think I Will Wait To See What Happens. 3.5/10

TL;DR: The gameplay is really fun, but the writing is so bad. SO BAD. The characters are generic, unlikable and uninteresting. The only two good characters in the game are antagonists so you don't even want to kill them. The writing is also very off with the very silly tone the game and the series itself) had always had. But it is still a really good game overall.
Far Cry 3 is an open world FPS. Wow. Not many of those around. Far Cry 3 has been critically acclaimed, and loved by many users. So, the game must be really good, right? Yes, it is. But it isn't the 'ONE ADVENTURE YOU WON’T WANT TO MISS'. God, no. Far Cry 3 has fantastic gameplay, while the writing resembles a box filled with bad sweets with layers and layers of cream and other goods so you don't know that it's basically poisoned. It looks like something really good and deep, but the reality is that it's a piece of♥♥♥♥♥♥
Our game starts off with the most unlikable protagonists in video gaming history: Jason Brody(from California), his older and younger brother, girlfriend and a bunch of his friends decides to go out in a trip to Bangkok that may or may not be very dangerous. But they're rich bro ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s and they don't really give a♥♥♥♥♥♥ Speaking of danger, turns out they get captured by pirates while sky-diving in an isolated island. Way to go, dumbasses.
Jason somehow escapes because these pirates are near-deaf/blind throughout the entire game, and meets the local tribe, the Rakyat, whom tells Jason of the 'Tatau'. So if you get ♥♥♥♥ing tattoos, you get super-human powers. ...okay, not exactly, but Jason, with the help of the Tatau, becomes a rich Californian ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to the hero of the Rakyat by receiving the generic and unexplained protagonist powers(seriously, how does he even ♥♥♥♥ing know how to reload a gun?).
The gameplay of Far Cry 3 involves shooting things, or stealth, both of which are well done. It also involves the islands(two) that you're in, the Rook Islands. They were used by the Japanese as an outpost during World War II, but is now abandoned. The Rook Islands are filled with wild life, which you can hunt down and use their skins to craft new bags so you can carry more things, weapons and ammo(never explained why you need specific animal skins to make specific bags- just roll with it).
Back to the shooting and stealth- the shooting as you may have guessed it- is about gunning down pirates and animals. The weapons feel smooth and while some don't resemble their real-life counterparts, overall they feel very good. The stealth is not very complicated, and a bit basic. You can throw rocks to distract enemies, use silenced weapons to take them out from afar, use melee takedowns for more XP(leveling up with gives you more
tattoos), or even use the wild-life against them by releasing locked cages. The stealth is much more fun then you would expect.
The world of Rook Islands is not filled with many colourful characters, and the jungle setting has been used for the Far Cry franchise before. ...did I mention that this game is a sequel to Far Cry 2? Yeah, it kinda is. Nearly everything has been remade, but supposedly it's all in the same world according to the developers.
Back to Rook Islands, while I didn't enjoy exploring it because personally, I didn't have much motivation to, but if you want all of the collectibles, or really like jungles, I guess you'll really like it.
Now, why is the writing so ♥♥♥♥♥♥? ...because they had money to actually make a great game, but couldn't hire a writer who could write a good story. Seriously, throughout the game, there are only two interesting characters, and they are all antagonists! It seems like that the writer didn't understand one fundamental thing about characters: if they're interesting, you don't want to kill them because you want to learn more about them! Why do I want to kill this guy when I really like him?
Oh, he's toying me around, he killed my brother- it doesn't look like he's toying me around(there's this one guy who doesn't tell you where you're supposed to go even though the minimap tells you, and if you go there Jason gets mad at him because he was lost even though the ♥♥♥♥ing minimap, AKA the game, told him. You lose all immersion at that point), and why should I give any ♥♥♥♥s about my brother? I only saw him for like 5 minutes, he killed a guy(he served in the military, so at least it makes sense that HE knows how to load a gun), and bam, shot in the neck. Not very impressive, eh?
One other thing about the goddamn game is that not only these characters are generic and uninteresting, they don't feel like real ♥♥♥♥ing people. If I don't care about them, AND they don't feel like humans in the first place, why do I have any incentive to go out and save them from the pirates? Seriously.
But of course, I HAVE to mention about Vass, the main protagonist, the guy with the Mohawk that's everywhere on the box art and everything. He's the only one that actually says cool, interesting and funny lines, but he wasn't even written by the writer. The voice actor for Vass, Michael Mando(not sure if it was his actor or someone else), came up with the character and the writers liked him so much that they just wrote him into the game. Wow. Just, wow.
And speaking of writers, the interviews with the lead writer, Jeffrey Yohalem, is pretty entertaining. Everytime he gets questioned by his writing, all he says is that they 'don't understand' it, and that it's supposed to be a satire about violence in video games. I can't help but laugh at that- just play the game and see if the game is a satire about ANYTHING.
Oh yeah, speaking of playing the game, despite I'm ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on the plot so much, Far Cry 3 is still a really great game and that's why I recommend it. But let's get back to the story, shall we? I'm not done yet. The plot is about you rescuing your friends, but you get jacked up on drugs and tattoos. The development is very similar to Alice in Wonderland(god, they even have quotes from it. I hate games with Alice in Wonderland quotes). Of course, unlike Alice in Wonderland, the writing is♥♥♥♥♥♥
Okay... I think that's enough for the story. What about the miscellaneous stuff? The graphics are great, and the soundtrack is... well... above average. Let's just leave it at that. There are vehicles in this game, and even though I hate first-person driving, it's actually pretty well done. The weapon customization is very disappointing, and the weapons are not that different from each other in the first place.
Oh, and UPlay. It's Ubisoft's version of Steam, but it glitches out so much, and it's inferior to Steam in every way. That alone might put you off actually.
So, is Far Cry 3 any good? Yes it is! It's really really good! I'll give Far Cry 3 a 7.5/10; it's a really good game. But the fact is, the Far Cry franchise has always been about being silly. Far Cry 1 and 2 was very, very silly(and also badly written, but also silly), but the fact that Far Cry 3 tried to be something more than blowing things up really hurt it. It basically shot itself in the head by trying to be so deep, while having♥♥♥♥♥♥writers and a game about killing a bunch of pirates.
The writing is SO MUCH BETTER in the DLC, Far Cry 3: Blood Dragon. It's a whole new story set in a different retro 80's movie type world. The reason why it's so good is because it doesn't take itself seriously. Far Cry is really about doing silly things, and in Far Cry 4, they extend upon that by making you ride ♥♥♥♥ing elephants. But the writing in Far Cry 3(and in 4 as well actually) is so much different than the tone of the gameplay and the overall game, that it was really bad, and that's why I cared so much about the writing in this review.

Truly a masterpiece in the world of PC gaming.  Mount and Blade: Warband is an interesting combination of strategy and boots on the ground combat in its single-player campaign. The game was not properly configurated for computers. Cutscenes lag constantly and the the sound cuts in and out, so I am unable to listen to the story. I am running the game on a MSI G Series GT60 2OC-022US laptop, which exceeds the minimal and recommend requirements by a lot. I run the video settings on the highest setting and it tends to lag frequently. I switch all the video settings to low and the gameplay runs smoothly with some lag from time to time, but the cutscenes still lag terribly and the sound cuts in and out! The gameplay itself has a lot of problems as well, during an extinction match I planted the drill on the designated area and it would not allow me to switch back to my gun no matter what I tried to do and it showed I was still holding the drill. When I started playing the multiplayer it had problems connecting to the servers and I was at my friend house using his comcast internet, it would take forever to connect to the server. The story, I think is just terrible, my expectations were that it would be better than the Call of Duty Modern Warfare series, boy was I wrong, (SPOILER ALERT!), the story was about how the confederation takes over most of the world and hijacks a giant space cannon that could obliterate the earth, then the confederation reverse engineers many of their own and you go and stop them in space. :
Campaign:
I played the campaign on it's hardest difficulty and it took me somewhere around 15 hours. The story is about Jason Brody having a vacation on an island. And wakes up in a cage realising that his vacation is over and he has to save all his friends so they can get back home. This sounds and also felt generic. But as you continue through the game the story gets more and more interesting, due to well voiced characters and the inspiring monologues. The game also felt like some kind of total recall to me, because the character has many drug trips. So even when I was playing the normal sp missions I was asking myself if it wasn't just a drug trip. Because if the bulk of the story was a drug trip the story would make a lot more sense. The campaign story was mostly the reason that kept me playing.
Gameplay:
The gameplay other hand was good and entertaining, but nothing special for me. Some early missions could be annoying, because you were forced to play stealthily. Also the sp missions can sometimes feel as a narrow route.  The power of the gameplay itself is that you can choose how you want to play. stealthily or guns blazing. Both can be fun but both also have some issues. The stealth problem is that the ai can be annoying. And for guns blazing you can easily run out of ammo and have to break your arm to revive yourself many times if you play guns blazing.(Atleast on my difficulty. I would maybe recommend to play 1 difficulty below or first do a lot of side missions to unlock more health, weapons etc.) Also if you have no ammo you mostly have to camp until you can easily knife someone, without getting hit. Sadly every endboss fight from the game showed the definition of insanity in gameplay. The game was also a bit overwhelming in the beginning because of the many menus with upgrades. At first I ignored them, but later I really saw the benefit of it. Otherwise you will easily die.  The graphics of the game still look nice, I especially liked the lighting. And how much effort there had been put into the building.
Open World:
I have to be honest I haven't done that much in it. Because I wasn't really interested in it. Still I can say if you are interested in exploring the world there is alot to do! There are enough side-missions, which is mostly killing enemies/animals in a certain way, missions where you have to go from A to B as fast as you can etc and, of course, collecting stuff. Really the only thing that made me stop fast-traveling from mission to missions was the tower climbing and the animal/flower hunt to unlock stuff. They were more rewarding to me than the side missions that just give you money and xp that I already had enough of.
:
Multiplayer:
In my opinion the mp isn't that special. It has 4 standard game modes. Of course they are varied with some nice ideas. But to me it just feels like a cod-clone. The multiplayer also has a strong map editor. Probably at the time there were many great mods made. (I found some interesting ones on youtube. ) But now that the game isn't as active anymore, I couldn't find a modded map to play.
-Co-op:
I played the co-op with someone many months before continuing my singleplayer campaign. It was pretty long at 6-8 hours. But still the co-op was pretty generic and forgetable. The only thing that I liked were the mini-games. What is strange is that the multiplayer and the co-op leveling system are combined. So if I had only played Co-Op, I would have all the unlocked loadouts for the multiplayer.
:
I can say Farcry 3 is a great game, but you can ignore the multiplayer and co-op, because they aren't that special and that active anymore. I think for the people who only own FarCry 4, FarCry 3 is still a great game to play, especially for the campaign, that makes it something special.

I like the game and its concept. H&G is a defacto strategy game played through an FPShooter/Driver/Flyer(Also third person driving and flying). For people who only want to shoot, drive or fly it is fine. You dont see the strategy element if you dont want to. However you will participate in the ultimate outcome of the strategy game.
The shooting and moving feels pretty good. Getting used to each weapons ironsights takes a few games.
It is fast-paced, but also suited for patient defenders.
There are only a few maps at the moment, but I think they are all well made.
The matches are based on what is happening on the strategic map. Skirmishes consist of three capture points and a team score based on holding said points. Skirmishes are usually quick games ~5-15 minutes. Strategically skirmishes occur at the many supply points surrounding an objective point(like a city, factory or airfield).
Assault/Defend are typically longer battles than skirmishes. They consist of one to three main capture/hold points with several others forming a line to a supply points at the edge of the map. Depending on the strategic situation that means attackers may be assaulting a city from several locations. So when you play on the same map, there is some variety. Also the battles are not linear, as a team may have to divide to cover flank or rear.
You may run into aimbotters and or people who can make repeated rediculously awesome shots from anywhere.
The dev team has done a significant amount of work just during the short time I have been playing. Kudos to them.

Fun game with beautiful scenery and interesting story.  Like most Ubisoft games though, the majority of the games content involves repetative grinding that amounts to doing the same thing over and over, which is necessary if you want to unlock more weapons or abilities.  Free outposts from bad guys to get fast travel checkpoints, hunt animals to upgrade your equipment, do the same bounties for money/exp, or explore for lost treasure.  After awhile, I got bored quickly and decided to just move on with the main storyline.  The game seems more challenging with less items unlocked and less locations to go to quickly.  It's fun to just drive around and get attacked by pirates while offroading to your next checkpoint.
The audio for the game is pretty bad- the majority of the voice acting that doesn't involve major NPCs is incredibly muffled- Ubisoft has a tendency to outsource this kind of thing to some other company/branch, since Assassin's Creed has the exact identical issue with voices having terrible sound quality.  The music is pretty good- especially during points in the main storyline.
The story itself isn't too bad, although a bit predictable.  Makes you wonder if you're completely insane and everyone around you doesn't exist considering all the major NPCs disappear from sight, right as they finish talking to you.
Overall, it's a fun experience though the completionist in me hates it for its repetative nature.

I almost hate to say it, especially with the story's uneven pacing and tone, but this game is really freaking fun. Gunplay is a blast, there is satisfying weapon diversity, it has beautiful in-game world with just the right amount of sandbox and over-the-top ridiculousness, with everything like living through an enjoyably-bad 80s action movie. In fact, this is almost akin to the bromance version of Commando, with a bit of Apocalypse Now and (hopefully) self-aware commentary thrown in for good measure.
The only major downsides for me were the weak QTE-esque "boss fights" and the mostly-stupid hallucinatory parts, which really killed momentum for me and made me just want to get back to stealthily liberating outposts.
I've read a lot of commentary about the ending, as well as some of the broader meanings and supposed point of the story, and I'm officially half-convinced: Jason is clearly an unreliable narrator, and it always felt like the entire experience was a bit too self-aware to be taken at face value, especially considering all the hallucinogens and fourth-wall violations sprinkled throughout. However, even if the main goal was to encourage analysis and, on some level, critique the tropes of the "hero" archetype and videogames at large, the delivery still felt weirdly clumsy and disjointed, and maybe even a little pretentious. It may be art, but that doesn't necessarily mean it's *good* art.

I'm going to admit that my kneejerk reaction to this game when it first came out was something less than positive. That being said, I gave it a few months, and I sat down and digested what occurred in the single player game itself. In addition, I took a closer look at how the game engine performs, and reached a few conclusions that weren't immediately apparent or obvious.
I'll start with the game engine and the graphics overhaul that Ghosts brought to the CoD franchise. A lot of people are complaining that the game doesn't run that well in terms of frame rate. The reason for this is because they've set their graphics settings way too high. The console version certainly doesn't run the game in 1080p at max settings. Personally, I set the resolution lower (1440x900) and the graphics settings to "high" and the game runs a lot smoother (and looks much better) than it did at 1920x1200 with graphics at "normal". I'll post my PC build at the end of the review. Long story short, this game looks absolutely stunning at max graphics, but you need a top of the line video card with a lot of built-in RAM to run it well.
And now for the single player campaign. At first, like many other people, I was disappointed in how generic the story seemed, and with how absurd the plot was at times. Then I actually started looking into all of the cute things IW put into the game, and I came to the conclusion that IW actually did their homework. Without spoiling anything, those crazy satellites in the game actually exist, along with a majority of the hardware presented in the game, heartbeat monitor notwithstanding. The story, on the other hand... at first glance, it seems like IW just threw something together with no idea where it was heading. Looking back on it, after having seen the extra cutscene you get after you beat the game on veteran, and taking it into context with the backstory we were presented with.... all I can say is, "Wow." Assuming IW doesn't chicken out of the next logical step in terms of plot, the next installment in the series is going to *completely* change the way you look at games. Allow me to explain:
No, the game didn't add anything really substantial as far as innovation goes, but the graphics overhaul does make the game look very pretty. If you enjoyed the Modern Warfare series and its gameplay, you'll enjoy this game. Is it a cinematic masterpiece? No. Is it entertaining? Yes. All in all, I feel that this game was deliberately generic because IW needed filler to properly setup the next game, which, if my guess is correct, should be
entertaining. Do I recommend this game? Yes, but only if you've already played Modern Warfare 1, 2, and 3 and enjoyed them. If you haven't played those, go buy Modern Warfare and see what you think. If you enjoy it, move on up the ladder.

Heroes and Generals is a fast-paced first person shooter game based around the World War 2 era.  If you are looking for a game that is more arcade-like than realistic, this is definitely the game for you.  While this game is based around a career driven progression system with one or multiple characters, the bulk of the game revolves around grinding specific ribbons, which in turn, unlocks badges used as
.  It does not take much effort or time before you earn most of the equipment you desire credit-wise, even without paying real money.
Leveling in this game can be quite slow post Rommel build.  The amount of time per character to reach the higher ranks which yield the
portion of the game will indeed take you some serious time investment without using real money.  It is very much doable though.  The amount of experience you earn in a match is only slightly proportional to your efforts in each match, so there isn't much to distinguish a player who does nothing all match to the guy that does everything.  Paying for veteran greatly reduces the grind however, by adding 100% xp boost.
There is a variety of weapons the game has to offer, however, these weapons follow the same progression as the character and generally there are top tier weapons.  This limits the majority of end game weapons vastly, so you will see most players running around with similar weapons on each side.  The weapon mod system is a neat idea, but at a very primitive stage in development, not offering much in terms of detail other then visual reference (bars) of what they do.  You won't get to see detailed numbers (damage/range/etc).  The weapon skins are a very neat idea to add some uniqueness to the game, however these are only store bought features.  It would have been nice to see some skins available for purchase via game earned credits, whilst leaving some as exclusive to store bought.
The are many vehicles in the game currently but these are very limited in each sub category.  This can make playing with vehicles seem stale, but all characters have some kind of options in terms of different types of vehicles that can be earned via the character progression system (ribbons).  It will take some time playing each character to unlock the higher tier vehicles (motorcycles/apcs).  Tankers will find progressing to the next tier tanks a very long and unrewarding grind.  Currently the game does not reward very much experience to tankers and pilots, most of the experience in the game is earned via capturing or defending control points.  You can have plenty of fun playing with the tanks (allied side) and planes (axis side) in matches, learning how to appropriately use them is a steep learning curve though.
There are not many maps in the game currently, so after about two weeks of playing the game, you will come to know all the maps very well.  What the game does to try to make the maps have some variation is a good idea, but doesn't change the map modes (defend/assault) up enough to provide longevity to the game.  The developers would be wise to add some more variation to the maps based on the supply lines that are open in the maps.
Overall, the game is very fun when playing with friends.  Playing this game alone can be stressful.  Heroes and Generals is a team game, best played with a team on external voice communications.  The game has a steep learning curve, mechanics, campaign map, modifications, progression system, but once learned can be quite enjoyable experience.  The game has major potential and I have been content with the updates so far!

A frenetic, fast-paced shooter with a cheap blockbuster, explosion-filled singleplayer campaign and long-lasting multiplayer. This formula hasn't been changed in 6 years. If you were buying Ghosts hoping for a revolution, like I did, you will be dissapointed like no Asian dad ever was, when their son brought Fs home.  If you came expecting something quick that would keep you occupied and like all the millitary stuff, you shall enjoy this game. The multiplayer hasn't changed as well. The enemy will still spawn on you from time to time. You will still get shot in the back and from the side for no reason. And you will get yelled on by a tween, stating he had intercourse with your dear mother. Gameplay flaws aside, there are the TECHNICAL ones. The ridiculous RAM requirement (was fixed from 6 GB down to 4), the occasional LAGS (if you look from side to side you get tearing), especially on startup of a match. And it doesn't even look that good to have the right to drop framerates. It's seriously not optimized for PCs. Checked on both a fairly low-end notebook and a mainstream, capable gaming desktop. It's the kind of port-it-from-the-xbox-and-slap-it-on-windows port. I realized I made a mistake AFTER purchasing this game. Have I tried it before, I would go with Treyarch's installment, Call of Duty: Black Ops 2. Overall, the game is enjoyable and the campaign is truly epic, but the technical problems and the slowly-getting-old gameplay mechanics are something that will probably bug the most of players, who are familiar with the CoD franchise or FPS in general. For your first Call of Duty, this is not a bad pick, however.

I will base this review on 2 different sections: Single Player and Multi-player.
SP: It is absolutely amazing. With the introduction to Riley (THE DOG!!) and many other new aspects it brings a whole new experience when compared to previous Call of Duty titles. Throughout the campaign you experience new, creative objectives such as travelling through space, or even walking down a skyscraper. I have never enjoyed a campaign as much as this one in a long time!
M-P: I feel in a way a little disappointed in the way MP is laid out this year. It has a slower pace when compared to previous Call of Duty's and feels in a way like one of it's main rivals, Battlefield 4.. Although the Prestige system is still in place, it is brought to you by buying and playing as individual squad members, meaning that you go through ranks 1-60 on one character then buy the next one and do this so on and fourth until reaching the maximum rank. This is completely different as to what it is usually like and I feel that it hasn't got the same appeal to stay hooked to proceed through the ranks.. Squad points (the currency) are used to buy these squad members and within each individual you need to buy the weapons, perks, attachments etc. Everything bought only sticks to one member so playing within 2 or more members can be difficult as you are always short for points. I think that this system is poor and does not have any advantages over the previous ways of unlocking unlocks.

One of the greatest games I've ever played. If you love history, ancient warriors, medievial times, aspiring to be a king or heroic knight, then this game is for you. You will love it.
The native game is not so great, definitely find better mods, you'll enjoy it far more.
Pros: The hand-to-hand combat action, character development (as in leveling, but you don't gain charater traits), becoming a king (can take awhile), conquering kingdoms, riding into battle as the commanding general, huge map, mods that drastically improve the overall gaming experience, and doing other side quests. Battles are the most fun. One of the best things about the game is the challenge involved early on. The game has a steep learning curve or can be quite difficult in the beginning i.e., gaining money, leveling, gaining better equipment, doing quests to earn favor with princes, generals, kings, or when romancing women.
Good Mods: Brytenwalda. (If I had a better pc I would have conquered all of the British Isles.)
Cons: You can't completely destroy other kingdoms although that might have changed in this game (haven't played it in a while), can become addicting (too much fun), the gaming experience is 100x better with an excellent gaming computer better graphics, you can add more soldiers on the battle field at once if you have a higher ghz, etc. As a king you don't have too many functions/options, and city development is pretty simplistic and boring. In that respect it's not like playing Total War or some strategy game. However, city development can be upgraded if you search for good mods that have it such as The Wedding Dance or  Sword of Damocles mods. Another con is that it can be more developed when concerning characters, quests, storyline (the game does not have one); it's all really in your imagination.
The game is a lot more fun if you have a good pc with good graphics and your computer can add more soldiers on the field at once without crashing. It does crash if you overload the number of people of the battlefield.
Overall I rate this game 10/10. One of the top 3 games of all-time in my opinion.

Call of Duty has been one of, if not the most well known franchise in gaming this past generation and last. The franchise has been in decline quality wise after the release of Modern Warfare - excluding maybe Black Ops 2 - which leads to the release of one of the weakest entries (Both Single Player and Multi Player) in the franchise yet. From the get go, you'll notice this game was built by Infinity Ward on the grounds of pure arrogance. This game is the very definition of "Bare minimum".
Call of Duty: Ghosts stars a few protagonists, main one being Logan Walker - and the world they live in after a devastating Orbital Strike after a space station was hijacked. The story follows a special assault squad that go by the name of "Ghosts" and the brother's entry to said Squad as they fight to take control of the US again.
Safe to say that while I did enjoy the campaign, the game is still very, very bare bones in EVERY area possible. The campaign will run you up to around 4 hours - maybe less if you're more skilled. There is much less variation in this game than in previous Call of Duty titles and the story is kind of... silly.
The visuals are pretty standard Call of Duty, looks worse in some areas than other games - namely environments. Ground and wall textures often look very muddy and really contrast against the character models. There is a large degree of inconsistency with textures all across the game which makes the game look visibly worse than even Black Ops 2 - arguably though, it has better effects, like smoke particles and such. One thing I also have to mention is how lazy the character models are. I've noticed certain colors in textures, or maybe the meshes themselves maybe (?) that are "invisible" [Note: This is a detail that only those with knowledge with how 3D modeling/texturing work will notice and know what it means.] and you can see the background through the meshes, this is pretty common on the hands or in certain cutscenes on their faces.
Sound is pretty decent though. There are a few decent tracks across the game that are pretty good, but are all ultimately forgetable. Guns sound pretty good too, at the very least. Weapons in Call of Duty titles have always had pretty good soundwork dedicated to them and this game is no exception, even if the soundwork is definately re used from previous games. The menu sounds are also recycled STILL from the older Modern Warfare titles, and this is pretty displeasing by now, it feels lazy. Voice acting is generally pretty decent all around as well, as far as military speak goes I suppose.
Gameplay is still the exact same old Call of Duty you've been sick of for years now. It has the exact same controls, the exact same annoying Sprint cuts (Lets you run for a second until it cuts, then forces you to repeatedly hit the Sprint key for short bursts), the exact same annoying grenade mechanics (Still has the "Run until the market on the screen diseappears or throwback) , the exact same stupid recoil inconsistency on weapons, the exact same scripted campaign sections (Press "Key" to do this or that instead of doing it yourself) and the exact same plot twists to boot. You can play as the dog, Riley - whom your control in First Person view as you go sneaking about in tall grass, you then hit a key and Riley will instantly kill an enemy.   You also play as an Attack Chopper later on in the game, but it feels like you're controling a dude on a jetpack because it handles pretty linearly and you pretty much just hold down a key to get lock ons and release to kill them on sight, or shoot em all up - occasionally use Flares to divert missiles from hitting you and that's about it and then later on in the game, you get to control a tank, which feels like a very lightweight version of the same Tank mechanics you can find in Battlefield 3, you hit a button to shoot a missile (lock on as well) and another to use the rail gun. Other than these, the gameplay is still pretty much just run down a corridor shooting every guy on sight so you can advance to the next - it's enjoyable, but ultimately nothing worth replaying. There ARE Intel collectibles - same as past Modern Warfare titles that go by the name of Rorke Files, but they really aren't worth going after.
An extra mode they made - called Extinction - is ultimately one of the silliest things they have done to date. It's a less glorified version of Black Ops' Zombie mode sporting only 1 stage and being reduced to a wave based shooter as you destroy alien stuff across the map. It's a fun mode the first two or three times you play it, but because it's only 1 map (yes just 1 map)  there's not much to do after you beat it once. You basically have one player carry a drill around and work with it (it breaks down at times) while they fend off a horde of incoming aliens, as you progress further in the map the aliens start getting bigger and badder. It's pretty much a glorified horde mode, except it only has 1 map.
All in all though, this is - by far the WEAKEST modern Call of Duty title they have ever released. Previously, I would have said Modern Warfare 3 was the most laughable title they had released, until I played this one. Sporting a very short campaign, highly inconsistant texture work, re used assets down the toilet, a laughable story, a 1-map extra mode (Seriously??), and NOTHING new added to the base game mechanics - this ends up being the most obvious of all lazy works and servers at pure arrogance by part of Activision at chiming in a once great franchise.
NOTE: This review only covers Single Player and Extinction mode.
Pros
+ Great smoke and particle effects
+ Good Voice Acting
Cons
- Re-Used Gameplay Mechanics
- Re-Used Sound Effects
- Texture Inconsistency
- Very scripted and linear campaign
- Next to no variation
- Short Campaign with a laughable story
- Collectibles serve little purpose
- Mediocre not fleshed out characters
- Extinction mode only has 1 Goddamn map
PC Port Notes: To get the best visual quality on this game - be sure to have Screen Quality on Extra - anything below looks like it's rendered in sub 720p and be sure to do this BEFORE you actually start the game as ANYTIME you change ANY setting in game - it will force you to watch that stage's LOOONG intro video again everytime you want to change any setting in the Video Options.

Calradia; a land of war split into several factions in which you become a part of. You may do whatever you would assume you could do in a Medieval Fantasy world and more. You can become a vassal, siege castles, raid villages, build an army, attack others, etc.. but the main premise: Conquer Calradia as your own sole kingdom. This is a daunting task and will take you many 100s, maybe thousands of hours of work to finish entirely. You must conquer every single castle, town, and village of all the other factions under your own name, uniting Calradia once and for all, so eternal peace is restored. This can technically be considered beating the game, even though there is not an official end screen. However, this is an extremely difficult thing to do, and if you do want to do this, it takes a lot of patience, skill, and ambition. It is truly an amazing feat.
However, there is one minor thing that makes the game a bit less polished, and that is the graphics. To be quite honest, the graphics really are not very good. They are decent, it doesn't look like a NES game, but they aren't great. The thing is though, every Warband player can easily ignore this fact because the gameplay is so amazing.
To show you even more good things about this game...It's value. This game is only 20 dollars and is constantly on sale for extremely cheap- only about 5 dollars. This game is so worth the price because of the sheer amount of modifications you can apply to the game and the insanely huge amount of activities you can do. 1000s of hours can be spent in this game and you will still have fun with it. It is just one of the best games ever created. No other game is like Warband, no other game can rival Warband, and no game will ever be able to take the place of Warband. This game is incredibly amazing and words cannot describe how good it is.

Call of Duty has been one of, if not the most well known franchise in gaming this past generation and last. The franchise has been in decline quality wise after the release of Modern Warfare - excluding maybe Black Ops 2 - which leads to the release of one of the weakest entries (Both Single Player and Multi Player) in the franchise yet. From the get go, you'll notice this game was built by Infinity Ward on the grounds of pure arrogance. This game is the very definition of "Bare minimum".
Call of Duty: Ghosts stars a few protagonists, main one being Logan Walker - and the world they live in after a devastating Orbital Strike after a space station was hijacked. The story follows a special assault squad that go by the name of "Ghosts" and the brother's entry to said Squad as they fight to take control of the US again.
Safe to say that while I did enjoy the campaign, the game is still very, very bare bones in EVERY area possible. The campaign will run you up to around 4 hours - maybe less if you're more skilled. There is much less variation in this game than in previous Call of Duty titles and the story is kind of... silly.
The visuals are pretty standard Call of Duty, looks worse in some areas than other games - namely environments. Ground and wall textures often look very muddy and really contrast against the character models. There is a large degree of inconsistency with textures all across the game which makes the game look visibly worse than even Black Ops 2 - arguably though, it has better effects, like smoke particles and such. One thing I also have to mention is how lazy the character models are. I've noticed certain colors in textures, or maybe the meshes themselves maybe (?) that are "invisible" [Note: This is a detail that only those with knowledge with how 3D modeling/texturing work will notice and know what it means.] and you can see the background through the meshes, this is pretty common on the hands or in certain cutscenes on their faces.
Sound is pretty decent though. There are a few decent tracks across the game that are pretty good, but are all ultimately forgetable. Guns sound pretty good too, at the very least. Weapons in Call of Duty titles have always had pretty good soundwork dedicated to them and this game is no exception, even if the soundwork is definately re used from previous games. The menu sounds are also recycled STILL from the older Modern Warfare titles, and this is pretty displeasing by now, it feels lazy. Voice acting is generally pretty decent all around as well, as far as military speak goes I suppose.
Gameplay is still the exact same old Call of Duty you've been sick of for years now. It has the exact same controls, the exact same annoying Sprint cuts (Lets you run for a second until it cuts, then forces you to repeatedly hit the Sprint key for short bursts), the exact same annoying grenade mechanics (Still has the "Run until the market on the screen diseappears or throwback) , the exact same stupid recoil inconsistency on weapons, the exact same scripted campaign sections (Press "Key" to do this or that instead of doing it yourself) and the exact same plot twists to boot. You can play as the dog, Riley - whom your control in First Person view as you go sneaking about in tall grass, you then hit a key and Riley will instantly kill an enemy.   You also play as an Attack Chopper later on in the game, but it feels like you're controling a dude on a jetpack because it handles pretty linearly and you pretty much just hold down a key to get lock ons and release to kill them on sight, or shoot em all up - occasionally use Flares to divert missiles from hitting you and that's about it and then later on in the game, you get to control a tank, which feels like a very lightweight version of the same Tank mechanics you can find in Battlefield 3, you hit a button to shoot a missile (lock on as well) and another to use the rail gun. Other than these, the gameplay is still pretty much just run down a corridor shooting every guy on sight so you can advance to the next - it's enjoyable, but ultimately nothing worth replaying. There ARE Intel collectibles - same as past Modern Warfare titles that go by the name of Rorke Files, but they really aren't worth going after.
An extra mode they made - called Extinction - is ultimately one of the silliest things they have done to date. It's a less glorified version of Black Ops' Zombie mode sporting only 1 stage and being reduced to a wave based shooter as you destroy alien stuff across the map. It's a fun mode the first two or three times you play it, but because it's only 1 map (yes just 1 map)  there's not much to do after you beat it once. You basically have one player carry a drill around and work with it (it breaks down at times) while they fend off a horde of incoming aliens, as you progress further in the map the aliens start getting bigger and badder. It's pretty much a glorified horde mode, except it only has 1 map.
All in all though, this is - by far the WEAKEST modern Call of Duty title they have ever released. Previously, I would have said Modern Warfare 3 was the most laughable title they had released, until I played this one. Sporting a very short campaign, highly inconsistant texture work, re used assets down the toilet, a laughable story, a 1-map extra mode (Seriously??), and NOTHING new added to the base game mechanics - this ends up being the most obvious of all lazy works and servers at pure arrogance by part of Activision at chiming in a once great franchise.
NOTE: This review only covers Single Player and Extinction mode.
Pros
+ Great smoke and particle effects
+ Good Voice Acting
Cons
- Re-Used Gameplay Mechanics
- Re-Used Sound Effects
- Texture Inconsistency
- Very scripted and linear campaign
- Next to no variation
- Short Campaign with a laughable story
- Collectibles serve little purpose
- Mediocre not fleshed out characters
- Extinction mode only has 1 Goddamn map
PC Port Notes: To get the best visual quality on this game - be sure to have Screen Quality on Extra - anything below looks like it's rendered in sub 720p and be sure to do this BEFORE you actually start the game as ANYTIME you change ANY setting in game - it will force you to watch that stage's LOOONG intro video again everytime you want to change any setting in the Video Options.

If you are keen on a specific type of gameplay, even 12-20 player infantry-focused competitve FPS, I am not sure Ghosts is the best choice. It is, however, a well-rounded package for the casual FPS player. There are four main game modes; their specific details can be found on Wikia and elsewhere, so I'll only share my impressions.
Campaign: mediocre
It's also short, only around 5 hours on Regular difficulty. Ironically this works to the game's favor because it doesn't drag. When I think of Black Ops, I think of "Step One...!" When I think of CoD 4, I think of Prypiat and "Crew Expendable." There is no Reznov or Price in Ghosts. It's just a group of forgettable characters on a conventional military quest against a bad guy I fought pathetic. Even the few references to other media aren't done that well. On the other hand, in that short 5 hours, you get to play missions from under the sea to outside the atmosphere. You get to drive a tank like a bumper car and pilot a chopper like an arcade game. Most missions feel like deja vu if you've played MW or Black Ops before, and the few novel ones don't stand out. If the campaign were 10 hour and I had to play each type of mission twice as much, I'd probably complain. Fortunately, the 5 hours are a rush, even if a forgettable one.
Actually I do have one complaint about the campaign. The mission briefings are narrated like a story. Terrible choice for a video game, where if something is not experienced, it should at least be like a movie. Then again, all that has been done by other CoD games.
Multiplayer: I think it stays true to CoD, but I know little about that.
Unlockable weapons/equipment, perks, kill streaks, operations (challenges) are all present. There are plenty of better reviews on how the multiplayer stack up against other CoD and non-CoD games.
For a casual gamer new to CoD, the best I can say is that CoD multiplayer is kinda like CS, but fancier. For the same casual players, Private Match is a godsend. You can set up a Private Match to play with friends (or just by yourself); you have instant access to all weapons/perks/kill streaks/maps/most if not all game modes + full bot support. If you don't care to go through persistent growth experience, Ghosts remains perfectly playable. The only downside is you can't just open your game for any stranger to find and join.
Squads: The opposite of Private Match
If you instead want to experience the persistent growth of competitive multiplayer without the actual competition, Squads mode is for you. Here is a collection of 4 game modes focused on AI, co-op, and 1-on-1 competition. The popular Survival mode from MW3 makes a return, with 4 instead of 2 max players now. There is, however, no objective based Spec Ops missions. Unlike Private Match, Squads mode has match making to help you join up with strangers. Squads is the opposite of Multiplayer and is made possible by the game's AI, which is better than any other AI of this type that I've seen.
Extinction: Ah, I actually don't like it that much.
It's the equivalent of Zombies from Black Ops with aliens instead. I can't think of another analogy so just go watch a gameplay video. My problem with Extinction is that it's both short and objective based, thus reducing its replayability compared to other co-op modes in Ghosts. You have a separate progression track specific to this mode, and you can always try different play styles. But for me, if I can complete the mission with one setup, I don't see why i should bother with another. I also find the aliens lame compared to zombies. That's just me; many critics like this mode.
Performance:
There is no shortage of complaints against Ghosts' performance on the PC, especially for multiplayer. They are legit. In its defense though, I am able to play Ghosts on a system below its minimum requirement (Core Duo Quad 3.0, 4GB RAM, HD 4770 1GB) pretty smoothly. In single player, I could set most video options to normal, with a few high and few low and still play at a decent frame rate most of the time (below 60 for sure but I haven't checked fps). With most settings tuned to low, I can also play co-op and Extinction with the only serious slowdowns occuring at the beginning of a match and, surprisingly, at the menu screen both post-match and each time I start Ghost Multiplayer. If you have a good system, Ghost may not live up to your expectations, but if you have a crappy one, you may still be able to play, at least non-competitively.
Bottomline:
Ghosts is like one of the starter weapons in its multiplayer. It has a good collection of decent game modes. If you want a FPS with variety that you can enjoy casually, Ghosts is for you; it's perhaps better at this than any other FPS game out there. If you are a conniseur, every one of those modes may fall short. If you are a conniseur, this review isn't for you. If someday you evolve from casual to a specific taste, you can always get a more appropriate game.

So. Far Cry 3. The predecessor to Far Cry 4, an amazing game which I have already played and completed. So you might be wondering - is there any point getting this game? Yes.
Pros:
- Beautiful graphics (even though it's a few years old)
- Amazing storyline - you are kidnapped by a psychopatic pirate called Vaas while on a holiday with your two brothers and friends. You then set out to find them and save them using the jungle and cool weapons to help you.
- Weapons - yep, this game might not have such an extensive arsenal of things such as GTA V, but there is enough to keep you happy (especially the special ones such as flamethrowers, and RPG's).
- Free Roam/Open World
This is one of the best open world games ever. Minimal amounts of people. Lots of nature and wildlife to explore. This makes Far Cry 3 one of the best games ever to just explore.
Cons:
Even though this game is simply brilliant, there are still some drawbacks.
- This game does require a good GPU to run it. You will need at least a £130 GPU to play on medium/low settings. So far though with my GTX 770 I have not noticed any frame drops.
- Controls
This game is best enjoyed with a gamepad which means either getting used to the keyboard or buying a cheap one from ebay or your local dodgy shop. Luckily I have a gamepad.
Also, sometimes you will not know which control is which since this is different than a standard FPS.
And that's about it for the cons. All in all, if you bought this at the sales for peanuts, don't be disappointed because this game is truly fantastic - and even if you didn't, it's still worth the £15 price tag. So I hoped this helped :)
P.S I have played this game before, so don't question me playing only 2hrs of it here.

Warband is awesome. I guess I should start with the combat system:
The sword combat system is great, you move the mouse in the direction you want to block, and the direction you want to attack, then press the block button (RMB by default) or the attack buttom (LMB by default). However, many little details are added to this IE the concept of chamber blocking, where you can actually attack to block a sword if you time it right.
There are also axes in the game, though I haven't used them much, I prefer my lance, sword, and bow.
As for polearms, a few can be swung like swords,  but for most you are better off thrusting with. Speed and distance help a ton (Dont try to stab someone right next to you while backing up, you really aren't doing much). There isn't much else to them, though they are still very fun.
Overall, a good melee system.
For ranged weapons, you have bows, crossbows, and throwing weapons.
I haven't used throwing weapons much yet, but they aren't too bad from what ive seen.
Crossbows have a ton of stopping power, and i suggest one for anyone planning on being infantry. They can hit at quite the range and are powerful enough to shut down a charging horse.
Bows are what I use most. I've found them most effective on horseback, as with a few points in horse archery, the accuracy penalty isn't too bad. Its great for stopping a knight that is chasing you. Infantry equipped with this are really going to miss out.
Overall, a good ranged weapon system, though I feel like they can be a bit overpowered on horseback, as the ai sucks with all things ranged, and you can just run circles around them and land every shot.
Warband isn't just about the battles though (although that is definitely my favorite part). There is a lot to do when it comes to diplomacy, or generally just running your warband. You could form a group of elite mercenaries and just take up quests. Or you could build up favor with a king and earn yourself a fief. You could go from town to town buying low and selling high, or you could be a bandit and ambush any nearby caravans.
If you want a game you will get a lot of fun out of, I can't suggest this game any more. The base game is great, and the massive collection of mods for it keep you busy for ages.
Note on the Napoleonic Wars DLC though, it feels like a slightly more polished up mod, so I don't suggest it unless you really like that era or want to try a mod that requires it.
