I rate the game Far Cry 3 (PC version) 4.5/5. Very Good.
A great action/adventure game with some nice exploration interesting, somewhat experimental music and some of the most beautiful graphics (almost as beautiful as Skyrim but not quite due to the lack of great variety of graphics in one location versus another) I have ever seen (this game does have the best looking plant life I have ever seen in any game). This game's graphics were so excellent in fact that it often reminded me of tropical places I have been (Hawaii mostly) and the bright warm colors throughout were great to see this winter. The game's environments do have some variety but there aren't enough different types of plants and flowers and so forth (but there is just enough variety to the plant life that it's generally believable looking enough...barely), The controls and AI are good and the sounds (especially the sounds of gunfire) are particularly excellent. There are a few bugs but none of them are major and this game also has some of the most impressively realistic animations I have ever seen (people and animals are great and this game also wins my award for the most realistic looking videogame chickens I have ever seen.
Also, unlike in the Fallout games which often had me fighting the same battles over and over again whenever I came back to a previously discovered location, this game has an inventive (and yet simple) method of discovering new areas and permanently clearing each area of enemies (which are then replaced with your own allies) so that the battles seldom seem repetitive and at once your actions seem to matter (I would like to see this game mechanic used in other action adventure open-world games as well). Enemies are cleared out by raiding strongholds scattered throughout the geographic areas. Once a stronghold is taken, the enemies in the vicinity of the stronghold vanish (when you're not looking) and are replaced by your own forces. Simple but excellent and something which was not done in any Bethesda game (Morrowind, Oblivion, Skyrim, Fallout 3, Fallout: New Vegas) but is a great improvement over the repetitive fights of those games. Wonderful game overall!
This game has two potential endings...but unfortunately, yet again (this game being no exception to the general rule of multiple-choice game endings) it comes down to a final, spur of the moment choice to decide which ending happens rather than having each of your actions throughout the game lead up to one ending or the other (and this situation would have been a bit of a let down were it not for the excellent presentation of the choice of endings and the ending itself (I chose the good ending of course, to rescue my friends).
The kind of gritty plot this game has may not be for everyone and many may find that they are unsympathetic with the main character (he's a thrill seeker) but...this game has some good messages to present...the idea of power potentially (but not necessarily) being a corrupting influence foremost among them as well as the idea that being exposed to violence can make one much more callous and comfortable about dispensing it and thus added to that the idea that a monstrous social environment can help to create monstrous people if they lack the integrity to prevent their own corruption...coupled to this the concept that a life lived governed the rules of survival of the fittest is a nearly worthless life to lead (and will lead to a short life regardless of how strong you think you are)....and so on and so forth. The potential meanings and messages of this game can be debated at length. Overall though, this is a beautiful, fun, though often brutal interesting action game set in an open-world environment. This game has been called "Skyrim with guns" but this is not quite correct. This game sometimes reminded me of Fallout: New Vegas and Skyrim true, but this game is also very different from both of those, being even more action oriented (comparatively little dialogue in this game when compared with those) and having a much more consistently faster, often frantic pace. This game really has its own unique style.
This is a relatively minor problem but...After the main plot is done, this game lets you wander around and do anything you didn't do before the game's main plot ended (if you chose the good ending that is) but I wish that, over time, more positive benefit and changes could be seen occurring on the island as a result of your actions. After you defeat all the enemies and take over all of the enemy outposts there's really not much left to do but explore a little bit and then end the game. Beyond the main plot and little sub-missions in the game (which are few and far between), other characters on the island can't be "interacted" with to a great extent. You can play poker with some of them in various bars but that's about it. Though the island is always inviting and beautiful (the weather patterns were a bit overly simplistic though), once the main plot is done and the enemies are defeated there isn't much to do. I wish the game's inhabitants would throw you some sort of celebration for saving them but that doesn't happen and for a game with so much polish and excellence, the ending (if you choose to stay on the island after the main plot is over)...well, the game doesn't give you anything else as a major award or accolade. Like in Skyrim, you just go to your favorite place (or wherever else you want to go) and quit the game. With all the bad guys gone (for the most part) the characters should be celebrating and throwing parties for you and stuff but no, they just act normal and it feels odd that that's all they do.
Other relatively minor problems I should mention: The game map of the islands is too almost too easy to access. You should be required to go somewhere or other that has an actual map in order to see where you are and what's going on and so forth. There were times when the lack of having a clear direction or knowledge of where I was was exciting and added to the interesting experience but too often, once I had secured a radio tower the presence of the map alleviated this sense of exciting confusion...however, more importantly, the map screen makes an awfully loud, obnoxious humming sound. Really unnecessary and it became pretty irritating by the end of the game.

NOTE: I write this review while having played relatively little vanilla, rather ive been using this mod:
I really suggest you do too if you want a little more to the vanilla experience without changing anything too drastically.
Warband is awesome. I guess I should start with the combat system:
The sword combat system is great, you move the mouse in the direction you want to block, and the direction you want to attack, then press the block button (RMB by default) or the attack buttom (LMB by default). However, many little details are added to this IE the concept of chamber blocking, where you can actually attack to block a sword if you time it right.
There are also axes in the game, though I haven't used them much, I prefer my lance, sword, and bow.
As for polearms, a few can be swung like swords,  but for most you are better off thrusting with. Speed and distance help a ton (Dont try to stab someone right next to you while backing up, you really aren't doing much). There isn't much else to them, though they are still very fun.
Overall, a good melee system.
For ranged weapons, you have bows, crossbows, and throwing weapons.
I haven't used throwing weapons much yet, but they aren't too bad from what ive seen.
Crossbows have a ton of stopping power, and i suggest one for anyone planning on being infantry. They can hit at quite the range and are powerful enough to shut down a charging horse.
Bows are what I use most. I've found them most effective on horseback, as with a few points in horse archery, the accuracy penalty isn't too bad. Its great for stopping a knight that is chasing you. Infantry equipped with this are really going to miss out.
Overall, a good ranged weapon system, though I feel like they can be a bit overpowered on horseback, as the ai sucks with all things ranged, and you can just run circles around them and land every shot.
Warband isn't just about the battles though (although that is definitely my favorite part). There is a lot to do when it comes to diplomacy, or generally just running your warband. You could form a group of elite mercenaries and just take up quests. Or you could build up favor with a king and earn yourself a fief. You could go from town to town buying low and selling high, or you could be a bandit and ambush any nearby caravans.
If you want a game you will get a lot of fun out of, I can't suggest this game any more. The base game is great, and the massive collection of mods for it keep you busy for ages.
Note on the Napoleonic Wars DLC though, it feels like a slightly more polished up mod, so I don't suggest it unless you really like that era or want to try a mod that requires it.

The learning curve is incredibly steep, but this is about as good of a Medieval action/RPG/simulation game that you are ever going to find. You start out as a nobody, thrust into the middle of the vicious world that is Europe during the Middle Ages. From there, you have the freedom to become a mighty warrior, a duplicitous nobleman, a skilled trader, a battle-hardened mercenary, a respected general, or really any other role you can think of.
This is one of those games where the story and gameplay are what you make of them. The game is almost completely open, and certainly doesn't hold your hand at all or ever put you on rails. If you like openness in your game world and don't mind playing a game that is incredibly harsh, unforgiving, and downright out-to-get-you, give this one a shot.

Immensely frustrating, but fair. It's free, so try it for yourself.
TL;DR: When you're getting rolled by some paid tankers and a match takes 1 hour, you want to ragequit. Then you remember you didn't pay anything for the game, and even though it's in beta, it's a pretty damn realistic WW2 shooter. The "veteran membership" system is a bit shady, though, and should only consist of XP boost.
--
I started playing the game, and I was hooked. It was so great to play a WW2 shooter that had a lot of really cool mechanics from FPS' over the last two decades: the gunplay of first few call of duty games, the vehicular combat of BF1942, and a nice little roleplay xp mechanism of the modern genre. However, the moment I left the beginner's tier into the second, my experience immediately became frustrating. Once you reach the mid-ranks, people can start buying things like tanks, new guns, weapon upgrades, etc. It throws the game out of whack, where you feel you don't have a chance unless you are really teaming up with friends over skype. But as a lone soldier without the time or money to improve your situation, it is really impossible, and you sort of reach an experience stalemate where you rely on camping to farm points.
However with that said, it was free to play, and I felt like if I would spend 20 EUR I might not feel like the scales were so out of my favour. Testing that, I bought 7 euros worth of gold, but sadly, this didn't really do much. I bought a kar98, hoping that I could upgrade it with a scope. Unfortunately, I found that the scoped rile is a seperate weapon. Even when I upgraded the sights, hoping that this would improve the 1px tick at the end of my gun, nothing changed in the gun model itself. This made me really irritated, as I felt like I was misled by the in-game store to believe that the gun would actually look different. Also, I found issues with the melee system - my hits never register. Not to mention when you jump, you kind of feel like you are on the moon.
In all, the game was fun, but it really punished me for being impatient and trying to play it like the early CoD or BF1942 games. It may feel like those games, but it sure as hell isn't. People complain about the "Pay-to-Win" system, but honestly, I think it is quite reasonable. Some people, like teenagers or those who have more spare time, can afford to grind the coins to get better stuff; however, working people typically cannot, and I can see that it would be nice to skip that timesink to get to the end when you have the fun toys. That said, I do feel like this game walks the line.

This Review is of Napoleonic Wars only. Mount and Blade warband is however an amazing game and you should get it. This contains all events that I have experienced in my time playing this game and I may update it to add new events as I see fit.
Day 1
I begin my first day of service in a Prussian castle. The Austrians have come to take our castle and it is up to my team and I to stop them. There is seventy of us charging out to the front lines and over 100 Austrian bots controlled by five player commanders.The Austrians prepare to fire and take around thirteen of us down right away. My friends and I quickly scuttle behind a hill with some other team mates. We get ready to fire and climb the hill slowly. As our upper torsos peak over the hill three of us go down as the remaining two fire and both miss. Damn.
Day 2
My friends and I walk out of the castle once again and see the right flank being overrun and our artillery being charged. We instantly run to the rescue, sucessfully pushing back the Austrian ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s in a bloody massacre. Planting the Prussian flag we show the Austrians that this is our land and we will fight to our last breaths for it.
Day 3
It is the dead of night. My division has been moved to defend a small fort across a river from a small village. We hear the Austrians begin their march and the battle begins. My friends and I take to horses, slashing down Austrians as we ride through the field, dodging musket fire. The battle rages through the night and in the morning we come out victorious.
Day 4
My division has been ordered to fight and finish the last of the Austrian army. My friend and I march in line behind our comrades following our commander. As we march I am shot down but not killed. My friend continues marching as our numbers continuously fall. Eventually Austrian cavalry charge our remaining forces and my friend suffers a panic attack and is one of the first to fall. We both now have PTSD and he has developped a fear of horses.

This game is not a masterpiece, yet it is incredibly addictive.

This game doesn't hold your hand, it shoves you out into the world after a couple of starting quests and tells you: "Do what you like, we won't restrain you. It's up to you to make your own story".
You can be a tradesman, a vassal or even forge your own empire, taking down those filthy Sarranids and claim victory for yourself. Don't think it will be easy though, once you get enough castles, it becomes a juggling act of resources such as food and troops, and of course, money. It can be easily made through pillaging villages, but at some point, you will face some angry enemy Lords who won't find you burning their villages quite so funny as you may.
Don't get put off by this games graphics. And sure, it may not be the most in depth RPG of its kind, but it's enough to make you want to experience your own adventures, as if you were really there. And isn't that what fantasy gaming is about?

Each Faction gets 6 different branches of the army you can choose from as you progress, Infantry, Tank Crewman, Fighter Pilot, Paratrooper, Recon(Sniper), and General. One of my favorite games, period. That said, it's not a game everyone will enjoy.
Initial Description:
This game is a mix of RTS, RPG, and hack/slash. The combat isn't quite fast-paced, but quick enough that it is rare that you feel like nothing is going on. The game is very much a sandbox, with no driven storyline/plot to it. The quest system is very bare-bones, with little variety, but is still good for a while.
Gameplay:
The meat of the gameplay is in building an army, and then either taking over Calradia or simply being a jerk to the different kingdoms to see how long you last. The game uses an instance-based system for battles, where you wander on the map screen, traveling around until you run into someone you want to fight/talk to, then you click on them and depending on who it is, it will pop up with different dialogue boxes, giving a variety of options in some cases. Once in a battle, you can use a limited command interface to direct your troops, so as to get the highest chances of winning. From there the battle plays out, with the two (or more) armies colliding in the middle and having it out. You always have the option of charging into the fray yourself, but that has consequences of it's own, more on that in another section.
The political system is both basic and very complex, it is very odd because it seems arbitrary and to be utterly random at first,  but as you play more and more, you start to see how it fits together, and can take advantage of different nobles' rivalries for your own gain.
Graphics:
The graphics are pretty bad, from a visual fidelity standpoint, but that's kind of to be expected given that it was developed by a fairly small group, initially being just a guy and his wife in their basement, IIRC. They may not be the prettiest, but they work well for the game and have a sort of style to them.
Animations vary from good to wonky, but that is a fairly minor complaint.
Length:
I've put over 100 hours in, and am still playing it. There is a very wide variety of mods available to expand the life of the game.
Balance & AI:
This is a tricky one, because the AI doesn't handle mounted archery or pikemen very well,  it is ridiculously easy to just walk over the entire game if you get a group of about 50 elite units, especially if horsemen are involved.
Realism:
The game is actually fairly realistic, as to the weapons and armors contained in it, as well as how the nobles react to the player and their accomplishments. There are no fantasy weapons or skimpy armors here, and weapons perform generally how they would in real life against the various armours. The game isn't set during a specific time period, so you end up with a bit of weirdness as some nations have crossbows while others are still using bows. Even the difficulty of use on weapons scales realistically. Crossbows can be used relatively well from the start, but bows take a lot of use for the character to get good with them, and throwing weapons, while very powerful, have extremely limited ammunition amounts and are very inaccurate, even at less than 10 meters it is possible to miss. By the same token, it is also possible to plant a Javelin in a charging horseman's face, for ridiculous damage.
Combat:
A very good system, with momentum being the main factor in damage. A point blank thrust with a spear for example, will do nothing because you don't have the room to actually build up enough force to do damage. This creates some very interesting dynamics between the different weapon types, with each type of weapon having a use in at least 2-3 situations.
Major issues:
Castle sieges are very haphazard, with as many as 50 units trying to go up a single ladder, which is barely wide enough for going up two by two. If the player character is incapacitated during a fight, it results in the entire battle stopping, and then you have to use the auto-resolve function. The auto resolve function puts way too much emphasis on numbers, with a group of 75 peasants capable of defeating 25 Knight Cavalry, which is a situation where if the battle were to actually play out, the peasants would lose without the knights taking a single loss.
Difficulty: This is highly customizable, ranging from Skyrim on easy mode, to Dark souls levels of difficulty, and because of this, pretty much anyone can get good at the game.
Reccomendations:
I would reccomend the game, but with the caveat that if you can't make your own goals, you won't have much fun. The biggest reccomendation I can make for this game is to NEVER play the unmodded game. I would highly reccomend obtaining the Diplomacy mod, as it expands the political system quite a bit, and adds a ton of anti-frustration features. I would actually go so far as to call it the 'community patch' for mount and blade, and I myself consider it essential. Another thing to keep in mind, is that a large chunk of the modding community for this game are masochists. I'm not kidding here, the vast majority of major mods for this game, especially the total conversions, have a focus on making it more difficult. The only overhauls that I can reccomend to players who haven't beaten native/diplomacy mod are Floris modpack and surprisingly Prophecy of Pendor, which is more difficult than native, but this is more due to larger numbers of units all around, and said units being much more powerful than vanilla units. In native, the Elite troops top out at about level 30 at highest, while in Prophecy of Pendor there are units that go clear up to level 70.  The other difficulty tweaks that prophecy of pendor adds are easy to disable/reduce.

Far Cry 3 is probably one of the first real open world games I have played.  It is also probably one of the most enjoyable for me.  I enjoy the plot of the game greatly and the design in extremely detailed.  I love the multiple activities one can do on the island and I think it makes for a great open world game.  While there are multiple endings, your freedom doesn't really come into play with those endings until the very end of the game.  None of the things you do throughout the game affect the final scenario.  It is only in that scenario alone that you can choose your ending.  Also, while the new skills you learn throughout the game are very helpful, they don't always add up to being unique.  By the end of the game, you usually have almost every skill unlocked and available to use.  So, it's not like that's something that affects the game too much.  Far Cry 3 is definitely a game that you make for yourself.  While the plot is somewhat linear until the very end, you choose how hard to make it for yourself.  You can run and gun your way through an enemy base or you can try to stealthily take out enemies from afar.  The ability to customize your weapons is also very beneficial.  After a while, you realize your best weapons and can use that to your advantage after crafting enough weapon holsters and ammunition pouches.  Is the game fun?  Totally.  I have enjoyed it a lot.  Is there some replay value in the game?  Eh, there is some I guess.  You can't really change up the plot itself until the very end and that doesn't even really affect the game at all because you end up being able to explore the island afterwards no matter what you choose.  However, there is some fun to be had with changing up your tactics and such.  Is the game worth it?  I would say that it is worth the price, but being the person I am, I would totally recommend getting it on sale because that's where you get the most bang for your buck.  I've spent hours playing this game and I've really enjoyed it.  While I have discussed the single player, there is not much to be said for the multiplayer.  It's alright I guess.  The setup for leveling up and unlocking items is pretty cool.  The special perks you can get are nice.  It's not really anything new though compared to your average FPS multiplayer game.  I have yet to put too much time into the co-op, but it is still decent I guess.  I feel like the main source of entertainment in this game, though, is in the singleplayer.

Heroes & Generals is personally one of my new favorites. You're probably wondering, "Why do we need ANOTHER WWII first person shooter? There are hundreds to choose from already!" Yes, while many WWII shooter games are available, this one brings some new aspects to the table. The first thing I praise the game for is its historical accuracy. The guns, the soldier design, the buildings, the battle areas, all of it is so realistic I sometimes forget I'm even playing a game. The graphics are beautiful, but on the downside, the game is poorly optimised as it is still in beta stages. The way you unlock and get new weapons isn't anything unique, a level up and gain experience to unlock weapons system, but I feel the system is very well balanced, unlike many other games. Recently, there has been a lot of conflict about if this game is pay to win, or P2W. My personal opinion on this is that it's more pay to PROGRESS not pay to WIN. A player who earned their weapons and earned the upgrades will still do better than a person who just joined and poured money into getting the perfect weapon. Even though weapon stats help, the game is still more about skill than the right gun. Everybody has their own play style and their own favorite guns and favorite upgrades, there really is no meta. Paying to unlock items in the game is more of saving yourself the grinding. In the game, you can fight for the Axis or the Allies on the western front. The soldiers you can choose from are infantry, tanker, figher pilot, paratrooper, and recon. All the types of soldiers support eachother and play a major roll in the victory. If you play for a while, you can move your soldier up to a general, and command armies to different cities on the map to help lead your side to victory over Europe. Other than minor optimisation issues, I have no problems with this game. It is one of the better WWII first person shooters I've seen out there. The game is free while in beta, so go download it and join the fight!

This indie game may not look like much, and in truth it isn't. It is rather simple. But there's just something about roaming the lands, building an army, killing your enemies and conquering the world that has me hooked. I suppose it doesn't help my addiciton that the creators encourage modding, and there's a huge community for it. One particular mod - A Clash of Kings which is, you may have guessed, based off the Game of Thrones/A Song of Ice and Fire series - has me playing endlessly. The sheer amount to do and the dozens of ways to play more than make up for its few shortcomings, like the poor graphics.
The combat, though simple, is extremely fun. Whether it's the challenging difficulty of your weak character struggling to take down some bandits, or the ease with which your level 30 "Destroyer of Worlds" mows down your enemies, it never gets old. Both archery and melee are well-thoughtout and easily learned. One of the best mechanics which I find reminiscent of Minecraft is that there is no real objective in M&B: Warband. You're not trying to gain revenge on someone who wronged you or rescue a relative. You can be an outaw, raiding villages and♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off the nobles, a mercenary, leading your small but fairly skilled band of men against the enemies of the men paying you, a lord, fighting for your king to crush his enemies, or even, perhaps, becoming a king yourself. Hell, you can even become a trader, travelling from city to city, buying and selling while you fend off the bandits who wish to rob you.
P.S. There's a free demo to try that lasts for 40 in-game days, so you don't have to take my word that M&B is an amazing game. Find out it yourself.

This indie game may not look like much, and in truth it isn't. It is rather simple. But there's just something about roaming the lands, building an army, killing your enemies and conquering the world that has me hooked. I suppose it doesn't help my addiciton that the creators encourage modding, and there's a huge community for it. One particular mod - A Clash of Kings which is, you may have guessed, based off the Game of Thrones/A Song of Ice and Fire series - has me playing endlessly. The sheer amount to do and the dozens of ways to play more than make up for its few shortcomings, like the poor graphics.
The combat, though simple, is extremely fun. Whether it's the challenging difficulty of your weak character struggling to take down some bandits, or the ease with which your level 30 "Destroyer of Worlds" mows down your enemies, it never gets old. Both archery and melee are well-thoughtout and easily learned. One of the best mechanics which I find reminiscent of Minecraft is that there is no real objective in M&B: Warband. You're not trying to gain revenge on someone who wronged you or rescue a relative. You can be an outaw, raiding villages and♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off the nobles, a mercenary, leading your small but fairly skilled band of men against the enemies of the men paying you, a lord, fighting for your king to crush his enemies, or even, perhaps, becoming a king yourself. Hell, you can even become a trader, travelling from city to city, buying and selling while you fend off the bandits who wish to rob you.
P.S. There's a free demo to try that lasts for 40 in-game days, so you don't have to take my word that M&B is an amazing game. Find out it yourself.

Enemies still spawn way too often, there is a lot of exploring and walking (not that it's bad, but nowdays, me personally don't have much time for gaming like I used to).
Graphics are okay. My PC can max them out easily, but framerate is locked below 60. You can tell. I don't know if this is how the game is, or if it can be fixed but playing a shooter below 60fps is not good. As far of game design, everything looks pretty colorful, smooth and full of life.
Gamplay is good. There are a lot of special moves, weapons and ways to move around the islands. Cars in my opinion are a bit irrelevant in this game. With being able to hide and cut through the jungle stealthly, driving a car is just asking to get in a shootout with pirates (which takes me back to how frustrating FC2 was. Drive a couple of feet, get into a fight. It took hours to reach your destination). Sure, shootouts are fun, but in a game like this they get old pretty quick. However, eventhough pirates apear way too often and randomly, it is very easy to avoid them.
I'm not much into the idea of killing animals, but given the nature of the game and the setting, it is somewhat justifiable. Then again, you have your trusty repelant to avoid confrontation.

Graphics: 8/10 (choppy framerate on above recommended system)

Like many people here I have been with the franchise since it began in 2003 but now I feel that the once great developer Infinity Ward (more like Infinitely Wasted) has let down the dedicated fan following with this iteration of the series if it can be called that.
When I started playing the game it had horrible fps drops which still exist and that's not acceptable for a PC port from such a developer. Not only are there frequent fps drops but they happen in the same places and this started to stink of poor optimization by the developers. Besides that, the texture quality is totally overrated for a 2013 game: it's nowhere near on par with the likes of Battlefield 4 (all problems with that game aside) where the graphics warranted the beefy system requirements, this game has high specifications but the graphics don't justify having them to begin with which I think is a waste and outright false advertising.
That being said I can't even find a way to display the game's fps...like as if the developers intentionally blocked it because they know their game is terrible.
What has annoyed me about this game the most is the story: while previous games have had some pretty outlandlish plot lines, the story in this game's singleplayer campaign is so stupid that it really didn't provide anything exciting...the Michael Bay explosion-fests are getting boring. What put the cherry on top was the ending - it was such a cheap move that it was practically screaming "sequel". Considering this story was written by a Hollywood screenwriter you'd think it would be something decent...but no, it's just dumbed down to allow for the stupid explosion-fests.
Is it worth getting this game? I don't think so. You may as well get Battlefield 4 or wait for Titanfall and have fun in those games than in COD: Ghosts.

The magic in this game is that your experience will depend hugely on your playstyle. It can be played like 90% of shooters out there, killing everything you see with an assult rifle, but it can also be played completely stealthily, or psychotically loud using equipment, explosions, fire, wildlife, and vehicles to your advantage, and the game does a good job of making you feel like a badass no matter which you choose. It's nice that you're never pinned into a certain style so you can always try new things. The open world nature of the game ensures it will always be different and dynamic, and you will find yourself improvising as a result.
It does have some flaws though. Jason, the player character made me facepalm on multiple occasions. Alternately coming across as cowardly, then all of a sudden cocky and brash. All while tying his damnedest to fit into a "D-bag fratboy" stereotype. Most of his friends weren't much better either. It seems a lot of game developpers believe having generic, stereotypical characters as the main protagonists will make their game more relatable, but in reality it just comes across as boring and cliched. The few helpful characters you meet on the island are more interesting but the star of the show is definitely the antagonists. They forced me hate them, which I wish I could say about more games.
It does suffer from some console-itis, using an (optional) weapon wheel, and has some bearable mouse acceleration and menu issues. Also, why mousewheel to change from grenades to molotovs? Performance isn't great either, I think because it wasn't optimally ported. Still very playable and nowhere near as bad as a lot of other games out there, but just sad to see the Far Cry franchise drifting away from the PC.
I felt sad when I finished Far Cry 3 because there wasn't more to play, which is a lot higher praise than I thought I'd be giving it when I started.

This game already came out September 13th, 2011. It's called Red Orchestra 2: Heroes of Stalingrad.
To be fair, that may be tarnishing RO2's name a bit, because there wasn't any money grabbing upgrading to be done. Especially in a Beta. Betas are for testing and fixing things, not trying to squeeze every dime out of a players wallet.
The only thing that I see this game attempting to do (other than air combat, which from what I've played, is terrible) that RO2 didn't do is have a persistent on going war. That's it. RO2 does everything else this game is trying to do only about 10,000x better.
My only other comment that could be considered helpful is this - the M1 is more or less what won the war. The ability to throw down accurate fire at a higher rate of fire than the K-98. So why in the world do you allow the German players to pretty much skip over the K-98 and all buy Gewer 43s? It wasn't even in production until, you guessed it, 1943, and even then it was a rarity. Only 400k of them were made, compared to the millions of K-98s that were floating around. Giving pretty much all the German players access to this rifle negates any advantage the US has in terms of firepower, which is unbelievable to me.
WWII Nazi war doctrine revolved around MGs, not semi auto rifles that, oh, by the way, aren't actually semi auto. The rate of fire of a M1 should be "as fast as you can reacquire a target and click the mouse" not "until the timer we built into the game lapses."
It irks me that this game has any kind of following while a superior game (RO2) sits with empty servers.
I'd honestly like to hear from a Dev what differences there is supposed to be between this an RO2. Because honestly I feel like they're just trying to grab some money from WWII fans.

That would be suprising, if you didn't knew this one, but anyway.
Far Cry 3 is FPS Sandbox. After first couple of taks you are free to explore halt of the game world (second one comes somewhere after half of the storyline). So, you went skydiving with your friends, and ended up in pirates captivity. Your brother was in military, but he dies pretty quicly, so you - never held a gun, never killed anybody - have to save your friends and destroy drug cartel. Seems like fun, eh?
Of course you are not alone. You got saved by some guy named Denis, and he introduces you to faction fighting with pirates. So you join them, and do jobs for them, complete their trials ect. In return, you get to follow the path of the warrior - basicly you can get new skills each time you level up, like ability to drag enemy you killed with a knife, more HP, faster reloading, ect. You level up by doing missions (story and side), killing enemies and finding collectibles. Easy to guess, story missions make you free your friends. Side missions make you an errand boy for Rakyat and islands' inhabitats. So you walt the Path of the Hunter (hunt animals for skins), Path of Warrior (have a bunch of enemies, with special one that needs to be killed with a knife), or help villagers. Big plus for one of the missions that gave me schivers.
There are of course more side jobs, like turning on Radio towers (results in free weapons from the stores), or freeing outposts (unlocking quicktravel locations and gun stores). And finally, trials of Rakyat. Basicly you get a vechicle, or a gun with unlimited ammo, and enemies rushing to kill you. The higher the score, the more XP and money you get.
Game offers yoy plenty of guns - you have couple of Assault Rifles, SMGs, Shotguns, Sniper Rifles, Launchers and so on. You can carry up to 4 customised guns (sights, suppressors, mags, your call. Sometimes more than one per gun). Why up to? Here comes crafting. In order to have more (guns, ammo, syringes, money...) you need to craft specific items. Need more money? Craft bigger wallet! In order to craft items you need some skins, so you have to hunt plenty of animals. Quite good conception if you ask me. If you are looking for buffs, you can harvest plants. They are used to craft syringes, which can give you varius boosts, like imediate healing a couple of health bars, seeing animals for a while, or breathing underwater.
If you like to collect items, there are plenty of collectibles here. You can look for relics (120), lost letters (20) and memory cards (20). Apart of additional XP and money, only thing they give you is possibility to score 100% of the game. Worth it? Well, 100% is goddamn satisfying.
I had fun playing FC3. Sence of freedom caused by open world mixed with awesome graphics was enough for me to stick to this game for a long, long time. There was plenty things to kill, and what else do you need? Only minus? Fully upgraded wallet could only carry 10000$. I think that removing this restriction wouldn't be a bad idea. Besides, I have no objections. Great game

Please note that this review is in its early access phase.
The game is pretty straight forward as you start up you choose the faction you want to be in.
>Germany (Master Race)
>USA
>RUSSIA JOINS THE WAR (March 2015)
>Other factions coming soon (Russia, Japan, British, etc)
After choosing your faction you then are given a basic infantry unit. This unit can select from a small variety of customizable weapons from the selected faction (note that guns can be purchased from across factions; EX Germany buys Russian guns: PPSH).
You then can A) Select the training method in the upper right hand corner and quickly take a crash course in H&G or B) Dive right into the action and learn on the fly. If you select option B you are put in Tier 1 classification matches which pits you against other Tier 1 players with similar experience levels.
Once you get to level 3 on one character every single game you place from there on out will be Tier 2 or higher as this is where Tanks/Planes/ and Specialty classes are available to be used in combat.
Specializations: NOTE: Once an infantry unit is made into a specialization they cannot be put back into another branch of the army they will forever stay in the specialization.
Tanker: Level 4
Piolet: Level 5
Recon: Level 9
I overall enjoy this game as it played in the FPS genre like CoD and Battlefield and it kind of has a mixed styling of both.

Well I now have over 300 hours into this game so I think its safe to say I like it. They are essentially trying to create a full WW2 combat experience while maintaining easy to play mechanics. Dammage models are pretty simple yet effective. Get shot in the head and you are dead in one shot, otherwise you can usually take 2 or 3 shots to the torso before dying. Tanks are much stronger in the front and weaker in the rear and shots that impact on an angle are usually deflected. They have planes as well but I have not played as a pilot yet so I can not provide much info.
You get 2 game modes, Skirmish and Assualt. Skirmishes are the starting battles and also serve for quick in and out battles. Basically you have 3 objectives (A, B, and C) on a small map that you must hold the majority of the time to win the match. Assualts are much larger maps with many secondary objectives (A1, A2, B1, B2) and objective lines that lead up to the main objectives (01, 02, 03) that you are either defending or attacking. Each different assult map is different enough to keep them interesting but I do wish there were a few more available.
As far as the multiplayer aspect goes this game suffers like most others from the typical MMO pit falls. If you start a match with people who dont know what they are doing or decide they want to run off into the woods and fight alone you dont have much chance of winning and you basically are forced to just get what kills and captures you can for points. Sometimes you get a great group and dominate and are freindly and actually stop their jeep to pick up fellow players to get to the objectives. Other times you get loners who just speed off alone, rush in to a heavily enemy ocupied buidling and gets killed over and over again wasting spawns. And then ofcourse their are the ragers who start ♥♥♥♥♥ing as soon as they relize they are going to lose (yet half the time these same people have a K/D ratio of 1/10). I would say its fairly even between good groups and bad, but the Germans do seem to usually have the most wins.
So far this game is still not P2W. The only things that you can only get by spending real money are cosmetic options (like camo color scheme) all the equipment and vehicles can be bought with in game currency. Sure they make you grind for it if you dont want to shell out some money but so far I havent dropped a dime and have lots of fun playing and have a few very decently equiped units including a high level US infantryman with a fully decked out tommy gun and a German tanker with light, medium and heavy tanks. But expect to grind to get the equipment you want if you dont spend money.
Over all if you want a fun and fairly simple WW2 MMO with ground units, tanks, and planes thats free to play this is a great choice. Its not perfect, but it is fun.
The best bit of advice I can give to new players is figure what you want that specific guy to be (Infantry, Tanker, Pilot, or recon) before spending currency because thats a very easy way to waste a lot of in game currency. In th egame you start out as Infantry and through experience and medals you unlock new branches like tanker and so on at different levels. If you want to be infantry start buying equipment for your guy as soon as you can. If you want to be something else grind using only the basic equipment and only start spending once you unlock your chosen branch.
UPDATE: Since the Xylander update they fixed the issues with the pay system and repair system. They upped the credits you earn and how you earn them so its much better. Deffinately not P2W currently.
However I do agree that the frame rate issue is really bad, unless you have a beast of a machine you will have to lower settings to get decent frame rates and even then you migh tnot get great FR.

Mount & Blade: Warband is an unique medieval fighting game presented primarily in third person. Warband has impressively combined major RTS elements with immersive third person fighting gameplay, allowing the player to not only command their own army, but fight alongside it as well.
Single player features a real time ‘click-to-move’ overworld where you traverse the lands with your warband party, fighting enemy parties, visiting castles and villages for trading or recruitment and waging war on the enemy faction’s settlements. The actual fighting is done in a similar style to the Total War games, only you get to participate in the battle yourself. Once you engaged in a fight, you play as your personal character in the field of battle alongside your entire warband to fight the enemy, at this point you can give specific commands to your soldiers as you charge in  on a somewhat-valiant steed and roll some heads for yourself.
Single player Warband is basically a large sandbox RPG. You don’t have any real objective or direction when you start the game, but you will generally work your way into becoming a mercenary for one of the 5 factions and help them destroy the enemy and take their castles in the name of your King. Eventually you will work your way up the ranks, swearing an oath to the King and making friends and enemies with the other vassals in your kingdom.
This is when you can start to influence the actions of the kingdom. You can work together with other lords to accuse others of treason or marry into one of the many nobles of the realm which provides different benefits to male and female player characters.
Sick of capturing castles for your King only to have them bestowed upon another vassal? Well you can start your own faction! Provided you are strong enough and you can support a war effort on your own, you are free to capture castles in your own name and take over Calradia for yourself! With a little convincing, those Lords you spent all that time sucking up to might even decide to renounce their oath to their King and join you…
Multiplayer Warband has a rather competitive community, most servers run Battle mode which is round based combat, once you die you spectate until one team wins. Since there are 4 directions to block and attack when fighting with melee weapons, the game is quite hard to master, becoming a pro in multiplayer takes a lot of practice. You can’t just hack and slash and hope for the best, you need to pay attention to what your opponent/s are doing and act accordingly.
There is also huge potential for modding, there are already loads of popular total conversion mods for Warband including 13th Century Europe mods, Musket era mods, Cowboy era mods and some fantasy style mods.
Controls and player movement are very clunky, but they work exactly like they should. The game provides skill-based multiplayer and a fun single player that will give you hours upon hours of play before you get bored (I’ve played 700~ hours of Warband and have yet to ‘finish’ a single player game as my own faction). Moreover, there aren’t many games like this out there. Sure there are medieval RPGs and RTSs, but none that combine both into a fun little package that offers such freedom, not to mention the modding potential.
The game universe goes far deeper than the average player might consider. The Kings and Lords and Ladies of the realm all have a relationship with one another and an attitude towards war which determines who they will pledge their allegiance too, who they will quarrel with and how they will act. Even the minor act of raiding and burning a village can have huge impacts in the game in many ways, the village will hate you (obviously), the Lord reigning over it will dislike you, the city it belongs to will suffer in terms of economy and produce less income, this could cause even more backlash to the player who may one day own these fiefs their selves. With all these variables things can become a little buggy at times, but it mostly works.
There is a very intricate system at play here and the developers have really tried to capture the political and economical systems that went on in medieval Europe on a grand scale.
While the graphics are a small upgrade from the original Mount & Blade, they still aren’t exactly up to scratch with the high standards of 2010 (the game's release year).
The sounds of battle (weapons, war cries and death) are moderately satisfying, but there are barely any voices in the game. However there is a nice soundtrack to both the battles and while traversing across the land.
There are many people out there who would find a game like this totally boring, with no given objective to complete it can be easy to get bored... Then there are people like me who come across a game like this and see the potential for adventure in a huge medieval sandbox where you can command an army, fight with your army and ultimately coordinate a war on a large scale. And for others it’s all about the multiplayer.
Whether you are a fan of competitive medieval combat games, or a fan of medieval RPGs and large battles, this is definitely one to try.

It's a game you wish you could enjoy, but it seems more like a boat simulator than a war simulator. Player characters struggle to build momentum, light weapons swing at almost the same rate as heavier and longer blades, yet yield no where near the same distance advantage, nor arc of attack advantage (sweep a 2-Handed blade and you can cover over 180 degrees, vs a mere ~35 with a dagger).
It has many options for weapons, stats, and skills to make a build of your choice, but speed will not help you evade, as it takes moments to build your speed and going up an incline produces no advantage. Daggers cannot swing as fast as two-handed weapons, no reach their length to hit, nor sweep their arc of attack.
The only options to enjoy this game is to pick a cookie-cutter build (slow, armored, 2-handed blade), or to group with other people using a 'trash' build in an attempt to humiliate the cookie-cutters.
The latter is fun for quite a while; the former is if you play solo.
Summary:
This game favors 2-Handed blades; blades sweep a wide area, recover as quickly as a dagger, and due to 'blade parry' they can stop an attack easily because of the sweep, and distance, and are ready to strike as quickly as any other weapon.
Player characters/controllers suffer from some bizarre physics which don't affect those who choose not to spec. in running speed. Running feels more like riding a moped with engine problems and a passenger (fyi, there is no '♥♥♥♥♥-seat' on a moped for a reason). Keep in mind, this is on flat terrain, spec. in speed does no good on an incline.
It's the "counter-strike; with less opportunity for enjoyment" melee game.

I have spent the most hours on this game, out of any of my other games on steam, and for good reason. Originally, I only cared for the custom battle mode, but that was when I played the demo. When I finally got the full game, I found that the campaign and multiplayer vastly over shadow this game mode. The campaign was one of the most addicting campaigns I have played in a while, and at times it forced me to be strategic, whether in the overhead map, or on the battlefield leading my warband or my military when I became a vasalage, or a king. This was one of my favorite parts of the campaign, being able to conquer the main nations of the game, and becoming the ruler of your own dominion, and it was so engrossing doing so. However, I wish for there to be more in terms of diplomatic actions, available when leading your own nation. Another thing I enjoyed about the campaign was managing my warband, recruiting new people, watching it grow in size and experience, and I couldnt help smiling later in the game, when I'd see one of my units from the start of the game, had become a unit of battle hardened veterans that have survived to that point in the game. Though, admitably, it was irritating when you recruit so many people, and their wages go up, so more money out of the protagonist's pocket, but it is negligeable when you participate in battles, or in the many tournaments and stadium games around Calradia.
The battles of the game require the player to postition troops, and use them effectively against the enemy. All battles are fought from the field, it is not an RTS, but it seems to mix this with a third person action game, as the player gives orders, and moves troops, and fights the enemy from the field, in a third person mode, or switching to first person. Next to the battles, there are also melee fights and tournaments. Melee fights are essentially fights between the player and 20 ai opponents, and your job is to defeat as many as possible, until you reach 20 or you are KOed. You can earn plenty of cash from this, and they are always going on, but the tournaments are where it's at. They are essentially larger melee fights, but allow the use of horses, and lances, there is even some jousting, but it's a bit odd seeing how there isn't a border between the two participants, but it is still alot of fun, and you can earn alot of money from tournaments, by placing bets on yourself, and of course winning.
And lastly for campaign, the quests, and at times, I feel as though this is the campaign's weakpoint. The quests are really repetative, unless you are a vassalage for a King, or you are a king yourself. Other than that, the quests seem to cycle between the same few things between different people.
Moving on from the campaign, we go to the multiplayer, the aspect that set this game apart from its predecessor. The multiplayer has quite a large community, and it provides plenty of entertainment and challenge. However, a portion of the challenge simply comes from the control of the weapons and blocking. In the single player, you could simply edit the control of blocking and stricking in the options, such as blocking automatically in the direction of the opponent's strike. On multiplayer, you control your strikes and blocks (with the exception of the shield) with the direction of the mouse, which can be irritating. However, this means that the ability to land hits and block successfully requires some skill, and it feels satisfying when you block your opponent successfully, then defeat them with several precise strikes.
The game modes seem pretty self explainatory, deathmatch, TDM, siege, and then battle. Battle is a unique game mode, in the fact that you only have one life per round, you die, that's it, you aren't coming back until the next round. This adds tension, and drives players to work cooperatively, especially in alot of the mods for the game.
This brings us to the final stop, the mod community. Oh my god, the mod community is huge, so many mods for this game. One is available on steam, the Napoleonic wars mod, which allows players to fight in the boots of 19th century European forces, with authentic weaponry, and equipment. Mods like this are all over the internet, Rome at war, North and south, mods based on World War 2, World War 1, and several other eras. Naturally, not all these mods are good, but most of them are worth the download, especially if you are in a clan or regiment for the game. I believe my stance on this game is pretty obvious, this game is worth the money, and it is worth the time you invest into it.

You can play this game un-modded, and love the crap out of it) to the point where it's rather surprising. NPCs have a relation bar with you that is fairly linear. Negative, means they resent you. In the + zone, they are either indifferent or favorable of you. This is changed through simple actions, such as talking with them, being at a party they attend, aiding them in battle, being in the same battle (war campagin ect. ect.) as them, supporting them for towns/castles/settlements/forts, supporting them to rise higher in the kingdom's social structure, and so on. It is impacted negatively by personally K.O.ing them in combat, fighting with them, raiding their lands, insulting them, crippling their efforts in your kingdom, suggesting they will turn on the kingdom, so on and so forth. You can also marry in this game, which can help support your own claim to the throne down the line, if you so wish to establish your own kingdom, and unite the land (instead of serving a king or queen, and helping them unite it).
Combat is tricky to learn. It is as realistic as can be with the game's engine, which is pretty damn close to being real. You will have a lot of fun fighting, be it 1v1, on the field of war, in the games, and so on. My suggestion, is PRACTICE, PRACTICE, PRACTICE! Turn the difficultly ALL the way up, go into the training fields, and get to learning. It is all muscle memory, attention to detail, and understanding the mechanics. You have to read your opponent and know what they will do before they do, and know what they will do to counter or react to your actions. The A.I. is very adapative at higher levels, and can even cause you to contemplate your life choices up to this point (such as, WHY DIDN'T YOU TRAIN, DUDE!)
The econonmy can be a cluster♥♥♥♥ of confusion if you don't take the time to sit down, compare prices, level your economic and social skills up, and realize that if you plan to live off the game as a merchant with powerful mercenaries, you'll need to take your time and be careful of the risks. The markets can rise and fall just as swiftly as they do in reality, if not even quicker. From being an honest merchant, bartering low and selling high (trust me, doing that is a feat of strength in this game...) to being the corrupt A-hole who raids, pillage, and steals all he can from weaker foes to selling them as soon as he can (yo, that's me) or the middle-guy. Only fight bandits, deserters, outlaws, and so on... and only plunder your enemy 's towns! (Guess what, plundering them reduces the kingdoms economy. So if you take over your enemies by forcing their econonmy low, you'll have to either live with the fact it'll be a S**t-stain on you kingdom's economny, or spend the time and effort rebuilding it and protecting it!) The eco' game is just as ruthless as the war game. You can literally find yourself cornered to your last fort, no supplies, troops with low morale, and questionably crappy gear and low stats because you didn't  control your own wealth, and failed to protect your kingdom's own economic growth.
There's a multiplayer system, which is just pure combat. No land control, no bartering, just kill, kill, kill, KILL! Or at least that's all I've seen... I am sure someone has plenty of moded servers out there that let you do more than just that, but I haven't explored for it.
Overall, I would give this game a 4/5. You'll sink a lot of hours into it, you will love it, you will hate it, you will cry like a baby when you lose if you don't practice and learn. You will rise to the top, standing on the pillar of success built upon THOUSANDS of dead bodies (you just had to kill all those poor peasants who couldn't defend their selves, didn't you?) and HUNDREDS of THOUSANDS of tears born from everyone just wanting to give you a big ol' hug -- with their sword. No, not their♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Their actual sword.
Oh, before I forget. Diplomacy is a big part in this game. If you're at war with EVERY kingdom at the same time, you might find yourself ♥♥♥♥ed very quickly, especially if they have trade agreements, non-aggression pacts, or even peace treaties with each other. Trust me, the A.I. is very quick to gang up on a weak kingdom in hopes of getting more land, more nobles, and more soldiers. You have to recruit your own heroes into your party, and focus on what they level up as. Diveristy is the only way you can win this, without cheating. Leave the heroic combatants to you, and your fellow knightly heroes. Roguish/hunters/ect are best left to the exploration skills that help you navigative the land and track your prey quickly. Your fallen nobles, your merchants, and housewives are best left to the social and diplomatic field. These are the one's who'll help you get more loot, or sell at a better price, or if you're out and on your own as a indepedent kingdom... your life-lines. Gold and diplomacy is the biggest factor when you're trying to take over the land for your self. It is the only way you can get a foot-hold. Even then, if you haven't played the game correctly and you have a very small claim to the throne, or none... you'll end up losing the kingdom.
FINALLY! You cannot actually lose the game, at least I don't -believe- you can. I never have, and I've lost a lot of fights before I learned what I was doing. It's just going to be a very long grind for you, my dear friends. You will learn like many of us have; the hard way. The true way. Blood and guts, tears and sweat. (Just so you know, you can tweak the difficulty settings. It can range from very easy to OMFG, HALO ON LEGENDARY WITH ALL SKULLS ON WASN'T THIS BAD. Trust me, Halo ain't got S**T on this game's hardest settings.)
I hope anyone who reads this, gets a general idea of it. It's a very well-developed game, with a lot of means to play it. You can focus on one aspect individually, or try to play them all at once. This is NOT meant to be a short game AT ALL. You will be putting in A LOT OF HOURS. A LOT OF THEM. OH MY GOD I AM STILL HERE, SOMEONE SEND HELP. I AM TRAPPED.
Seriously. This game is not for the impatient.

Grabbed the game recently. As a player who has spent maybe thousands of hours in DoD, DoD:Source, and many other WWII themed games, this one feels great. Characters have a weight to them, and it is slow paced to most of the games that you see nowadays. Animations are smooth, and the game is trying to be authentic; what I mean by that is, you can see your legs and feet for example, when you take cover your character holds the weapon differently, etc... I mean those stuff which you don't see much nowadays.
Graphics are fine. Sounds can use a lot of work though. WWII themed games, I care about sounds by a great deal. UI can also use some work too, especially the "launcher"; it is sometimes unresponsive, and the weapon upgrade screen can sometimes lead you to wrong directions.
Now, maybe the one thing most of you are wondering. Is the game P2W? I haven't invested much time, but so far apart from one thing, I don't think so. The thing that bothers me is, 2nd Badge being available if you are a VIP member. A badge is basically sort of an achievement, and each badge grants you a different kind of bonus. A VIP member will have a badge advantage, and of course, time advantage.
I said time advantage, let me elaborate on that a little bit. Currently, I get around 3-4k points from a match. I recently unlocked a new weapon (unlocking doesn't mean you can use it instantly; it just means you can purchase it now). It requires 120k+ points. That is around 20-30 matches for a weapon that I cannot test, and it is a bit too much. I hope they add a trial system, giving you access to a weapon for 2-3 matches, to get a feel for that weapon.
There aren't many weapons in the game yet, and buying a weapon by the hard-earned points you acquire is a big investment. You can also tweak your weapons, but they have not much of a visual/aural effect as far as I can tell. I hope they'll add more weapons soon, I'd like to see British weapons for example.
The vehicle aspect of the game is definitely interesting. As you progress, you have a choice to become a tanker or a pilot for example. And these two roles may have a dramatic impact on the battles; infantry is always the key, but infantry without support is often bound to fail in their duties.
I have a problem with long battles though, you aren't properly rewarded for your commitment in my opinion. And some battles may drag on for very long. And if you are using a modded weapon, the longer the battle is, the higher your repair cost probably would be. I hope they'll take a look at the repair costs, and maybe fix it to a percentage of gains so that it will be balanced for long battles.
Speaking of battles, they are actually somewhat different from other games, and it is very interesting. The battles themselves may not be balanced, but the overall war (generally) is. High ranking players commit units to battles, and battles dynamically change as you are playing it; new fronts can open up, and existing ones can collapse for example. Reinforcements can turn the tide of the battle, and lead up to epic experiences. The same dynamic battle system can also lead to battles where your enemy or you has overwhelming forces, which can also end up in heroic fights for the overwhelmed side.
Now, before a conclusion, here is a dynamic battle example. Our side just had a small guard unit (only 3 infantry players), while the enemy had a motorized infantry unit (5 infantry players, with armored transport). Against the odds, we successfully held the enemy for a long while, and our Generals send us reinforcements. As we were about to crush the enemy, their generals send them reinforcements too, as well as opening up new fronts, dragging the battle even further. In the end, we were victorious, and I felt great about that, as I was one of three infantry that held the line for a long time.
Overall, I recommend this game to anyone who are interested in the FPS genre in general. If you like WWII theme, definitely give it a try. From F2P aspect, weapon costs could get a tweak, and 2nd badge could be made available to everyone at a certain rank, but nothing major aside from that.

Addicting.  So much potential here for what could someday be my favorite franchise.  Sandbox with elements of RPG with live combat.  The combat is fun with a plethora of dark-age-death-dealing-devices to blugeon your foes to a pulp.  Be a free rider slaughtering bandits or be a scoundrel yourself.  Serve a king or plot/battle your way to starting your own kindom.  As I said, there is enough here to make the game worth the money if you're a fan of the genre, but the game needs work to be perfect.  The game offers many choices but I would love to see more depth in all areas.
Now I'll tear it down a bit. NEEDS: Better NPC interaction with more story depth.  Maybe a better questing system for NPCs.  You can talk to anyone, but there just isn't enough going on in the game to make it anything more than a chore after awhile.
I would also like the ability to closely control my kingdom's finances.  It sucks to grant a noble a fiefdom just to have him send poorly and be unable to maintain garrisons.  There should be a way to closely regulate these properties, maybe give your nobles help and cash so their castles aren't a hinderence. It also wouldn't hurt to have a better interface for defending your fiefdoms.  Bandits spawn like rats at an annoyingly unbelievable rate(especially vikings and tundra bandits) and as you are always a day's ride or more from your holdings,  they are constantly ransacked, making it near impossible to build improvements.  You should be able to garrison even small villages to at least fend of ruffians, if not enemy armies.  Maybe order appointed NPCs to gaurd your/their holds.(Playing recently and it seemed as if my NPCs had better AI and were actually doing a better job of managing their affairs.)
You should also have some way of spending for faster build times on improvements or a work-allocation system to allow for faster construction.  Feeling like you are improving your holds is a big part of the game's reward.
Another idea is to add a way to train/hire troops at held cities.  Riding from village to village for one or two guys at a time is fun at first.
If your a 'Dev' reading this, the character interaction and story depth is priority one.  The rest would be nice too.  All that out of the way and I can honestly say, I am addicted to this game and recommended it.  I know I will be giving this studio plenty of 'Denars' in the future.

Majority of the the game is from a "birds eye view" perspective of the game world with groups of bandits, armies of the different kingdoms, and of course your army, marching around and occasionationally facing off in the various landscapes found in the different regions. OH! and another thing! Tired of playing these fantasy games and constantly being attacked from creatures that dont exist? like dragons? *cough cough* Well have no fear! Those beasts do not exist in this realm. Thank god.

-if you want a game that allows you to ravage the landscapes towns and cities with your very own army, get this game
-if you want a game that allows you to experience the chaos that is medivel warfare, get this game
-if you want to lose friends and family due to you never leaving your computer screen, get this game
-if you want... wait why are you still reading this?? GET THIS GAME!

Through long consideration, I decided to recommend this game unlike my earlier review (which I obviously deleted prior to posting this) but it has been a tough decision.
The bad:
This game is a horrible console port and clearly suffers from poor optimization. I wasn't particularly impressed with the first person shooter aspect of the game, it lacked a certain sharpness to it which made playing these action scenes either ridiculously linear and dull or extremely crowded and confusing. I really don't think much of the alternative endings gimmick, even though both endings are narratively good, because you don't get to make choices that really make any difference anywhere else.
Back to the technical aspects, in game morphological AA (it also has the option of classical Multisampling on top of that) is tied to a graphical setting vaguely referred to as PostFX and if you want to disable the ridiculous motion blur you also have to disable this which means horribly jagged edges in many objects, unfortunately distracting you from gameplay and your immersive open world surroundings. If you're using DX11, forget about implementing more efficient algorithms through your gpu control panel because you can't force them so the performance is also borderline abysmal, even with a 4690K and a R9 290, my framerate constantly dropped below 60fps using ultra settings with 4xMSAA. Bad for fast paced action scenes and bad for creating a distraction. Finally, the draw distance is not good and huge rocks and trees form in front of your eyes with a ludicrous pixelated fade-in effect as you glide over them in the skies.
The good:
While the overarching story is very strong and the subjects it dances around are complex, the same can't be said about some of the side quests which seem forced and makes for a repetitive gameplay. It's nuanced and the the main characters have some depth to them and a lot of the game borders on grey moral areas but takes an understandable step in not overstepping that line. There are plenty of breathers from the first person shooter monotony either via the hunting/crafting mechanics or the car/jeep/helicopter action scenes. Open world is always nice and refreshing such as when you come across a tiger attacking its prey in the jungle etc.
The protagonist's dilemmas add a layer of depth to the already intriguing story line. Is his quest just about revenge or protecting loved ones or is he going after an itch he has never been able to scratch? Unfortunately, much of this is left unexplored and we just have to guess his motives and his true desires. Artistic direction is fantastic, the architecture of the ruins, the towns, caves, the island... all of it is a thing of beauty and all come together to create a unique and  captivating atmosphere.
It's a memorable game for the characters , the story and the settings, environment. Much of the game mechanics (radio towers, crafting etc.) integrate well with the story but some of it (really, hunting two sharks for a wallet?) just seems patched on, for the sake of having "moar stuff" I guess. All in all, recommended despite the many annoyances.

In praise of the undying bear
I really liked Far Cry but really didn’t like Far Cry 2, so I was hoping that FAR CRY 3  would put the franchise back on track. Thankfully it did. The Rook Islands are beautifully realised and provide some of the most impressive and realistic graphics I’ve encountered to date. The islands are lush and colourful and teeming with wildlife, all of which makes for a deeply immersive environment. Even if you ignored all the missions there’s a lot of fun to be had just exploring and hunting. But there are plenty of missions (almost 40 main story missions, a dozen or so side missions, plus a bunch of hunting and supply missions) to be completed. The main story is pretty good for an open world game. It’s not outstanding by any means but it provides sufficient momentum for your stay on the island and includes some pretty cool trippy experiences. Alongside the missions there are numerous items to collect, if you feel so inclined, and there are radio towers to activate and outposts to liberate. I had as much fun completing these tasks as I did completing the missions (although I didn’t track down all the collectibles -- there are just too many of them). It’s not all good however. The game has an incomprehensibly stupid save system. There is only one save slot and you can’t save at all during a mission. So if you have to leave the game mid-mission you have to start right back at the beginning next time you play. I know other games have employed similar systems but I just don’t understand why. The option to save should always be there -- you don’t have to use it if you don’t want to. I also found the looting mechanics to be annoying. Although you don’t have to wait for the prompt to activate the process it’s still too easy to accidentally swap weapons rather than collect loot. And finally, not enough dialogue was recorded for the minor NPCs, and consequently you here them repeating the same statements over and over again. These gripes aside, however, there’s little to detract from what is a great gaming experience. I haven’t tried the multiplayer options yet so I can’t comment on them. I plan on giving them a try later and will update this review if necessary. 4/5

Absolute perfection. OK, so maybe not "perfection", but close enough for me. Have you ever been playing a game like Skyrim and thought "Boy I wish I could raise an army of about 50 or so Viking-like warriors and then pillage the village and slaughter the villagers!" Well if you're like me, you have. And also if you're like me, you're gonna love this game.
Graphics aren't exactly anything to write home about but hey, that means even non-gaming machines can easily run it on the highest graphical settings, plus this means absolutely NO lag (yes, really) when your army of about 75 clashes with an army of about 100. It's style of play is somewhat similar to that of The Witcher series. Majority of the the game is from a "birds eye view" perspective of the game world with groups of bandits, armies of the different kingdoms, and of course your army, marching around and occasionationally facing off in the various landscapes found in the different regions. Once in battle, the game becomes a 3rd (or 1st) person perspective of your character (fully customizable with tons of armor, clothes, and weapons) as he/she valiently leads his/her army of honor (or band of misfits) to battle against various forces. OH! and another thing! Tired of playing these fantasy games and constantly being attacked from creatures that dont exist? like dragons? *cough cough* Well have no fear! Those beasts do not exist in this realm. Thank god.
Bottom line:
-if you want a game that is VERY open ended and has plenty of replayability, get this game
-if you want a game that allows you to ravage the landscapes towns and cities with your very own army, get this game
-if you want a game that allows you to experience the chaos that is medivel warfare, get this game
-if you want to lose friends and family due to you never leaving your computer screen, get this game
-if you want... wait why are you still reading this?? GET THIS GAME!

Heroes and Generals... Where to begin? This Free-to-play game has had me addicted since the first day I downloaded it. I can see quite a few games within the game. How I would describe the game is this: Call of Duty, Battlefield, Company of Heroes, and ARMA put together in an MMO. The graphics are spectacular, the game runs smooth with hardly any lag on my end, and you don't die every two seconds (mostly!) One of the cool things is you start out in training maps that will match you with other players with your similar ability. That way you can ease yourself into the actual campaign battles and get familiar with the maps.
One of the best things about H&G is the leveling system. You have the option to buy upgrades and new items with credits, which you earn through playing the game, or with gold, which you acquire by paying real money. There is a vast amount of ribbons (achievements) you can achieve which will allow you to upgrade your character's inventory accordingly. Or, where gold comes in, you can simply breeze through the game and buy the items, but where's the fun in that?
Another cool thing, is you can have multiple characters that have different parts on the battlefield. For example, you can have an infantryman, tank crew, paratrooper, etc., whom you can switch to during respawn should you choose. Of course it takes time to train everybody! Note, if you have friends who play H&G, you can also invite them to a squad so you can play together. This is easy through a sub-menu under the main character screen.
Altogether, this game is a win! I haven't played something so beautiful in years! Now, I must get back to the war!

This game is broken, plain and simple.
Pros:
-Decent map design in multiplayer.
-Extinction is a worthy successor to Zombies.
Cons:
-Poor optimization. Even if your rig meets (or exceeds) the recommended system requirements, you will experience FPS drops and will not not be able to play the game on decent settings.
-No anti-cheat in multiplayer. Roughly 30% of the games I've played online have been totally unplayable due to hackers. Wallhacks, aimbots, hacked prestige lobbies, you name it. Infinity Ward has remained silent on this issue, so it's likely they have no plans to implement any sort of anti-cheat.
-The single player is awful. I mean, I wasn't expecting Schindler's List out of a Call of Duty game, but if you actually care about that kind of thing, the plot is nonsensical and the gameplay is boring from beginning to end.
-Poor balance in multiplayer. IEDs, Attack Dogs, and the Bulldog shotgun are clearly better than any other lethal/killstreak/weapon. This leads to a rather predictable and frustrating multiplayer experience.
Do not purchase this game. You deserve better, and Infinity Ward does not deserve your $60.
