“Let me tell you 'bout a story 'bout a man named Miles, on a tragic and fateful tour,
He had no cash to spare, just an M1 Garand, went to play a World War II game!
But did he ever return, no he never returned, and his rank is now unknown! (Poor old Miles)
He may never again fight in those same three maps; He’s the man who never returned!”
This game is a perfect example of everything that is wrong with gaming today. “Pay to Win” is the name of the game here. Everything has a price, and trying to play without paying is an exercise in futility. Now, payment for in-game items with actual currency isn’t inherently bad, but when you make the in-game methods for acquisition so difficult, in a game that is so horribly unbalanced in some areas, while absurdly over-balanced in others, it becomes clear that the game is broken.
Of course, to implement payment options for items in a game that is still in development is just absurd, and borders on fraud. ‘Pay for these items to get the upper hand!’ ‘With this new update, those items you bought are worthless/inaccessible until you get this other thing!’ This is not how a game developer is supposed to make a game; this is a ‘Spanish Prisoner’ scenario, with a Skinner box attached!
Now, personally, I was willing to play the game regardless; it was fun… until the Rommel Update, when the game became balanced to the point where what was supposed to be WWII started to look like WWI: I quit playing after I sat through a 3 Hour match on an Assault/Defense map which used to take an hour at most before the update. I refuse to play any longer; I refuse to waste my time with a game which doesn’t look like it’ll ever leave Beta. Do not spend money on this game. Do not play this game.
“Now, citizens of the world, don’t you think it’s a scandal, how the people have to pay and pay?
Fight this Fee to Play; don’t spend cash on this game! Recommend a different vidya game!”

I have typically preferred the Infinity Ward versions of COD and Ghosts is no exception. After only recording 8/9 hours on Black Ops 2 I have fallen in love with Ghosts and COD multiplayer again. However it is not without its criticisms - mainly the poor optimisation; the games runs heavy and suffers FPS issues causing me for the first time to drop down to 720 resolution. Not even Crysis 3 made me do that!
However this is my sole criticism and if I focus on gameplay I would go as far as to say this is the best COD (certainly for multiplayer) since MW2. The class building system has been substantially revamped and to a COD veteran, like myself, it was actually a bit confusing to start with but once I understood it I appreciated the greater flexibility on offer. Class building is much less limited and you can really build a class to your strengths whether that be a speed running hip firing class or a full on stealthy slow class.
The maps are a bit inconsistent. Some maps are a bit large and overly complicated with the action being focussed in only a small section of the map but some maps are fantastically layered providing interesting horizontal and vertical sight lines. Not to mention destroyable scenery (e.g. on Octane blowing holes you can aim through on the roof of one building) and interactive objects. All in all the ratio of good maps to bad maps is weighted towards more good maps - another plus!
Extinction too is a nice addition. Its something fresh (sort of BO Zombie style) for the COD franchise and is actually really done well. Makes for a fun break from standard multiplayer.
Overall if you can deal with playing at lower settings and care more about gameplay then Ghosts:Multiplayer is definitely the best COD for a long time and is worth the time and money.

The great:  The pure sense of freedom.  Other open-world games plop in what they call a "sandbox", only to do what a parent would do to a kid in an actual sandbox, which is hold their hand and forcefully steer them to where they need to go and to what tools they need to use.  Far Cry 3 pushes the parent away, shoots them a few times, and spits on their remains.  When liberating an outpost, do you get points off for doing it stealthily?  Nope.  Do you get points off if you then get noticed and proceed to rocket-launch the place to smithereens?  Nope.  Do you get points off when you then throw a molotov at the empty shacks and burn it all to the ground?  Nope once again.  This game knows how to do things;  gives you a toolbox, and sets you at a task.  You can get anywhere on the map any way you want, you can kill animals any way you want, you can desecrate ancient tombs any way you want!  This leads to a ton of replayibility, natural variety, and emergent gameplay.
The good:  The world.  While some areas can feel samey, (it's a lot of jungle), this in no way takes from the beautiful and artfully crafted environments.  The map is enormous, pocketed with hidden tombs and abandoned army bases, the lore is rich, as seen in carvings, scrolls, etc., and the forest around you feels alive and evolving.  While driving around, you could see a pack of wild dogs attacking enemies, or a jaguar hunting some wild pigs.  If you're sniping from a hill in the distance, it's entirely possible you will get mauled by a nearby tiger.  Additionally, the fast-travel system is not too intrusive and makes you work for it, as you must first liberate strongholds at varying difficulties.  All-in-all, the whole thing feels real.
The bad:  Uplay and PC optimization.  Blah blah, Ubisoft sucks, blah blah.  Moving on from that, the only hang-up I have with this game is how it performs.  I can run a modern game like Dying LIght or Shadow of Mordor at about 45-55 FPS easily.  I cannot, however, manage to keep a steady 35 FPS in this game with a mid-range GPU.  I feel like there could have definitely been more optimization in regards to this platform, and as a result, my fan chugging away takes me right out of the experience.
Other notable things:  The story/characters.  While the story isn't a twisty-turny masterpiece of fiction, it is written and acted out well.  The villains are charismatic and memorable (especially Vaas), the voice acting is pleasant, and the progression of events moves along briskly and with some intense set pieces.  I haven't yet played a mission where I felt bored, it's genuinely surprising.
Result:  Buy it at no less than 25% off.

Far Cry 3 is a game where you take a break from ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on Ubisoft constantly and instead give money to Ubisoft and then♥♥♥♥♥♥on them.  In Far Cry 3, you play as Jason Brody, probably one of the worst protagonists of all time.  He's a whiny douchey dudebro who spends days, maybe even weeks, risking his life and killing countless people in order to save his friends, only to basically abandon them three seconds later.  On top of that, half the things he says are ♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and he's constantly an♥♥♥♥♥to his girlfriend who is one of the few characters in this game you don't want to murder in some way.  After awhile you'll probably start killing yourself in game because you can't stand who you're playing as and you want him to suffer.
Most of this is made marginally better by the supporting cast of characters, which includes two White Snoop Doggs, some creepy Island guy named Dennis who constantly sounds like he's on the verge of sexually assaulting someone, Citra who's basically just a perpetually stoned genderbent Dennis, some guy named Keith who's barely in the game, your girlfriend who Jason will give zero ♥♥♥♥s about, some tough blonde chick named Daisy who doesn't get enough screentime, your brother Riley who Jason cares about but you won't, two Real American Heroes, and all the islanders you'll waste time killing because you're a sadistic ♥♥♥♥.  And yes, surprisingly all these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s are still more likeable than the protagonist.
The villains in this story are perplexingly the most likeable characters.  Buck is a horrible♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥but hell at least he's amusing at times and a bit more three dimensional.  Same goes for Hoyt, a horrible person but ♥♥♥♥ at least he's entertaining.  But the one that takes the cake is Vaas.  I could not bring myself to really care about anyone else except Vaas.  Dude barely gets any characterization, tortures and murders people, but he's still the most likeable person in this game.  Each of these villains you get to face off against in ♥♥♥♥♥♥ QTE battles that will make you want to actually stab yourself in the eyes. The gameplay isn't that bad.  Gunplay is...well gunplay.  Nothing spectacular about it.  You can carry up to four weapons if you're patient with hunting.  If you're not a patient person then hunting can be a bit frustrating, which sucks because you're forced to hunt in order to craft larger ammo pouches, weapon holsters etc.  Also scattered around the world are plants, which you can use to make drugs that assist you in hunting, combat, or exploration.  It's pretty interesting and plants are incredibly abundant, so it's not as tedious as hunting.  Scattered throughout the world are enemy outposts, which you can take over by killing everyone there.  There's numerous ways to go about taking over an outpost, but it gets pretty repetitive after awhile.  Taking over an outpost gives you access to a weapon store, respawn point, and quicktravel point.  It also gives you some side missions which also grow repetitive.  There's also radio towers.  Climbing them and rewiring stuff unlocks new areas of the map and gives free weapons.  There are some collectibles but I'm not that big on those so yeah.  Doing stuff gives you XP which you can then spend on a variety of skills, most of which are either completely useless or so situational that you'll never use them.  There's also a variety of GTA style minigames which give you cash and XP.  There's some vehicles which handle largely the same and are a bit difficult to drive since driving is done in first person.

Mount & Blade: Warband is the second installment in the Mount & Blade franchise.
-You may find a simple review below the main review with the pros and cons of the game.
Warband added many new features from the original, and one of the largest was multiplayer. Multiplayer is in my opinion Warband's strongest attribute. The PvP combat is excellent, the maps are well made, and the experience overall is superb. Battles are large and epic, ranging from perhaps 10 people on each side to over 100. The vast array of weapons to use assures a new experience every time you play - everything from One Handed Swords, One Handed Axes, Spears, Bows, Crossbows, Javelins, and huge War Cleavers. Each faction (six in all) has a unique loadout, which adds a unique flavour aswell. Sieges are also quite ferocious and time consuming, some taking almost an hour or more. Combat involves a four-directional combat system, and a simple but practical approach to projectile drop. The community for this game is amazing, although players in Asia and North America may find slight problems finding populated servers due to the majority of players being centered in the EU. The Singleplayer is fun, but very repetitive. Your objective is to have the entire map controlled by one faction or your own. You can do a variety of quests for lords, kings, and villages - but are all repetitive. The character levelling is good, with a good array of choices to make your character how you like. A variety of different mods that are available for this game adds to the replay value of both the Multiplayer and Singleplayer aspects.
Pros
+Intuitive Combat
+Great Mounted Combat
+Sounds and Soundtrack are superb
+Singleplayer has wonderful RPG elements
+Many mods and additions to add hours of fun to the game
Cons
-Aging Graphics
-Hit Detection can be a bit sloppy
-Does not have DirectX 11 support (DirectX 7 & 9 only)
-Smaller community than most games
-Singleplayer has many repetitive aspects and quests (which can sometimes be snuffed with mods)
Overall Rating: 8.5/10 (Good game, has a few flaws)

Update: Well the new patch is here and planes are still awful. Apparently of all the things to fix being repeatedly bombed upon spawning is bottom of the developers list. If you enjoy unending frustration, a lack of common sense in game design philosophy, and general annoyance you should definitely download Heroes and Generals. Otherwise I would suggest giving this one a pass.
For a free game Heroes and Generals is pretty polished however the balancing and gameplay issues will fairly well ensure that your enjoyment of the game is crippled almost immediately. The developers seem to have a fierce love of placing spawn points in open fields with little to no cover. When you spawn you have approximately four seconds of invulnerability (coupled with no sprint) after which you will be fair game for the snipers or tanks that park around these kill farms.
If you play the game you will need to join Germany as they seem to have the largest bank roll which allows them to steamroll the US in each 'war' which always last about three days. More funds mean more tanks and planes for the German side. The German plane is especially frustrating as their initial fighter is both smaller and more manueverable than the American fighter. In theory this is made up for by the fact that the German plane carries only a single bomb compared to the American's two however there are medals in the game which will allow a plane to carry up to three additional bombs. Couple this with the fact that the bombs are on a cooldown rather than being limited availability and the Germans rapidly deplete the American plane reserves and then begin bombing everything into dust.
The game tried to put some clever ideas into play by letting the highest level players (Generals) retire to command battles. They have warfunds which can be used to purchase assault teams, vehicles, and reinforce battles that are occurings. This seems like it would be entertaining but unfortunately you run into a lot of matches where one side is completely outgunned. Matches with all infantry versus a well-supplied armor or fighter group end in tears rather wiftly and brutally. Balancing the forces fighting comes second to the 'strategy' of swarming your opponents with more vehicles.
Mysteriously the developers refuse to patch obvious imbalances and instead concern themselves with fixing game types that aren't broken. The typical game mode involves one side needing to hold a series of control points for 30 minutes. Previously once the 30 minute window ended the game was over and the successful defenders could claim victory. Now, however, even if the defenders hold out they must still reclaim all of the original command points before they can secure victory. The attackers in the mean time do not suffer any noticeable downside to failing in their objective.
All in all there is fun to be had in H&G but it is a fun you will have to fight tooth and nail for against a tide of poor balancing and questionable design philosophy.

While this game is well ported with a natural control scheme and graphics that run smoothly the game it's self is lacking. Sure on the surface there is plenty to do. In fact in order to "level" your character you actually have to do a variety of different open world missions in order to earn xp, and more importantly upgrade your weapon and ammo capacity. That's a great way to make the players engage the open world that you have created. From that perspective alone the game is fun. Though there are some annoyances with scripted events spawning guys after you shot everyone else in that area which is annoying cause you think you've cleared it out already. The driving controls are bad. I'd rather just walk everywhere then use a vehicle if I can. Being able to sneak around the jungle is cool. Where the game really falls apart is the "good guy" side of the character cast. How you ask? Let's meet the characters. *SOME SPOILERS AHEAD*
First up is token black guy with generic foreign accent. Could be Islander, Jamaican, African or Finnish, who knows, it's terrible. Then he wears a US Marine button down because he was in America and/or in the US military but had to leave because he was a bad cab driver or something? I don't know. He is such an odd character that by the time he opens up about his “mysterious past” in the story I'm at the point where I don't care, just tell me what I have to do for the quest. He teaches you the whole time about the power of the tattoo/tat-tau and being a warrior and how it saved him from being a lost soul. Except he never does anything warrior like and is a total train wreck emotionally the entire game. He's like Lord Friend Zone from Game of Thrones except LFZ has his stuff together and actually does stuff. This guy just mopes around his hut all day trying to give you tattoos and ♥♥♥♥♥es at you on the radio because you aren't saving the entire island single handily fast enough.
Then comes the generic cast of native islander people. Who are covered from taint to septum in tattoo which are suppose to be earned and represent bad-assery except that these guys literally help you do nothing. They can't even take a single out post by themselves nor seem to do anything other then occasionally get into horrible car accidents while driving around for no reason instead of helping you fight the pirate occupiers. Thank God Chad, the generic frat bro comes along to rescue them from their own inept misery. Doing so by learning about their bad♥♥♥♥♥warrior culture which they themselves can't seem to harness for their own good.
Finally you meet the warrior-goddess-priestess chick who leads the physical and spiritual rebellion against the pirate/slaver MNC? She happens of course to be the one hot chick on the entire island chain who advances your warrior training by swinging her hips around seductively. Gets you broodingly to do rando missions that finally result in her roofieing you and♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥you. But you don't seem to mind cause she's hot, even though you have a girlfriend? And because you finally sleep with her she and because of her major cracker-jack fever, she goes all psyco-girlfriend on you and forces you to choose between her and your actual girlfriend. One of which will be your sex toy war prize for winning the other will be brutalized and killed. Wonderful.
Finally there is the cast of generic frat bros and sorority sis's who you came to the island with. Regardless of relationship to you they all are at times incredible weak (this is understandable they are very traumatized from being captured by human slavers) to incredibly strong like killing people and flying helicopters. Then snap back to being really weak again, brooding and definitely on their moral high horse because you're "questionably" killing people while being a bad♥♥♥♥♥and saving them from being sex slaves. On top of all the whinny-ness the one who is your girlfriend, once saved, gets all weird because you're showing strength and resolve by saving a repressed island from the sex trafficking trade and from a life of slavery at the hands of pirates. She seems to prefer and does her best to push you back from warrior crusader, who is fighting for good, to Chad who lives off daddy's allowance while drinking bud light on the couch of the families third vacation home all day. Also she immediately starts planning your life for you again after you rescue her? Super annoying.
Now the story is saved by two incredibly well written bad guys whose monologues and character interactions are amazingly entertaining and you truly feel a sense of both anger at them for their actions, but a sense of justification in their own actions in their insanity and evilness. They see what they are doing as both bettering the economy of the island and bringing a better life along with all the corruption. They make naturally unlikable bad guys with out being too cliche.
The CIA officer and his German mercenary friend are also both very entertaining and lend well to the story.
The game is worth it on sale. But the weak female characters, whose soul purpose in the story is to be prize objects annoyed me. Especially since one is suppose to be a warrior priestess who like voodoo-tattoo lord friend zone really never does anything worthy of the title warrior. I don't think either of them can even actually use a weapon. They could have done so much more with the story. Either by simply leaving some of these characters out, or by making their contributions to the story more meaningful and less weak. In the end it feels like we are just left with a tale where white frat boy Chad comes and saves his weak bros and some brown people by becoming a brooding emotionally scarred PTSD Rambo who machine guns his way through an entire Black Water battalion of pirate slavers. And it could have been more of that as an action style movie/game with less weak characters, or less of that with more of a cast of strong supporting characters who support the main character's growth as a warrior and as a person.

With the 130 hours in mind, I can safely say this game is absolutely amazing. Far Cry 3 was a major development from the first 2 games, and has become without question, my most favourite game of all time. Far Cry 3 explores various themes, and carries quite an incredible storyline that is deceptively dark and powerful, even if the initial plot is very simple. I've played through Far Cry 3 at least 4 times, on every difficulty and tried different endings and choices. The first time I finished the game was by far, the most moving ending I've experienced in any game. It has great replayability, even after finishing Far Cry 4 I come back to this for the memories and unique gameplay. With amazing graphics, a gripping storyline, and such realistic gameplay, I still recommend Far Cry 3 today. I will never forget my time with Far Cry 3, it was the best experience I've ever had the pleasure to be part in. The map editor probably kept me entertained for months, and while I never played much co-op, what I did play was pretty fun. I personally prefer Far Cry 3 over 4, as it just feels more magical and special. I only hope that Far Cry 5 will return to the brutal and beautiful atmosphere that Far Cry 3 had, without completely redoing it (cough cough Far Cry 4).
So yes, Far Cry 3 is still worth every cent (and probably more to be honest). It still remains my most favourite game ever, and will for a very long time. Don't hold back on getting it, It's an unforgettable journey.

Personally, I've never had the pleasure of interacting with the forums or the Reto-Moto staff, but I've still had plenty of problems of my own.
First off, infantry and armor combat is completely unbalanced. One tank is able to lock down the entire area it can see, and infantry can't do jack about it. But wait, you might say. This is why rocket launchers were invented, so that infantry can take on tanks! Indeed, they are in the game, but you can't have on in your starter loadout. To get it, you must first grind a ribbon (read the other reviews if you want to know how fun that is), and then put up 40k credits. I averaged about 1000 credits in a good game, and that was before I got put in matches with tanks.
The second problem adds to the problem of getting enough credits to pay for anything. After getting blown out by people rolling around in inpenetrable steel monsters or with super-modified weapons (likely bought with real currency), I come back bruised and battered to the main menu, only to find that the quartermaster wants me to pay for the ammunition I used, and for the repairs to my weapons. The same quartermaster I'm trying to save up money to buy the bazooka from. The silver lining to this is that it's not suprising to go a round firing less than a handful of shots, since I get turned into dust before I can even see the enemy.
"But wait", the fanboy who's spent thousands on the game says. "You can still kill people perfeclty fine with the default weapon. You're just crying because you're bad at this game." Well, ignoring everything I've said about tanks, the game is still broken. Not broken as in unbalanced (though it most definitely is that too), but broken as in unoptimized. The connection to the server is often unstable, which makes close quarter combat a matter of luck. The engine is also terrible, running at maybe 18 fps even on 800x600 resolution with the lowest graphics. Good luck hitting anything that moves.
tl;dr Unoptimized, unbalanced, unfair, unfun.

Far Cry 3 is a first person shooter in an open world environment.
After the successful Far Cry game which came out in 2004 ( and being one of the best shooters in gaming )
and to its downfall disappointment of Far Cry 2 which came out in 2008 ( personally my favorite FPS game in 2008 ).
In 2012 we get the return of the Far Cry franchise which was believed to be dead after the criticism of Far Cry 2.
The question is will Far Cry 3 bring its previous glory ?
The story :
Is mainly focused on Jason Brody and his friends which they went on a tropical island for their vacation ( awesome idea really ) but things went bad when they land on the island and got caught by pirates and their leader Vass.
From that point things get from bad to worse and Jason has to learn how to survive and adept to the jungle in order to save his friends and himself from Vass and the pirates, unfortunately for Jason not everyone will survive and choices must be made by him, and there will be consequences for every thing Jason will do.
Gameplay :
As said before Far Cry 3 is a first person shooter in an open world game, but there is more than that.
Far Cry 3 is more complicated in the gameplay content  and is much more exciting.
Far Cry 3 lets you explore the world like never before !
Do you want to hunt animals in order to improve you kit ?
go ahead nothing will stop you unless the wild animals will get you first.
Want to go gun blazing with flamethrower and bomb everything with rocket launcher ?
You can do that if you get the weapons first,
want to be the silent assassin and kill everyone in the camp without anyone noticing you ?
Well you can do that if you are good enough.
and there are more stuff to do like hunting for treasures or making syringes from plants that you pick up
also you can race through out the world, beating you friends score on some side mission.
Far Cry 3 is one of those games which can be called "it has everything to offer"
and every part of it is just overwhelming and thrilling to experience.
Bugs :
thanks to the so called "Uplay" there might be some problems with the game.
I have been experienced an unwelcome problem which crashed the game every time I tired to play
but luckily the problem was solved after the next update of my GPU hardware.
Sound :
Oh boy the sound, its been awhile since I last got soundtracks from a game to my cellphone to hear it
from how beautifully they have done the soundtracks.
every part of the game was really well done and with the amazing soundtracks\music it was perfectly executed.
There is no question that Far Cry 3 has one of the best music\soundtracks in gaming.
Graphics :
Far Cry 3 is just beautiful and the game itself is a demanding one for a reason
while you can run Far Cry 3 on lower graphic options on most PC system hardware now days,
the fact is that the game is astonishing from its water,tress,mountains,grass,villages, and the whole world
and it will be very unfortunate if you won't experience the beauty that Far Cry 3 world is delivering.
AI\Difficulty :
While the AI isn't the smartest one ( especially the pirates ) it seems like the developers have done a great job
at making the wild animals dangerous and threatening ( damn you lizard and sharks ).
The game itself have four different difficulty levels ( easy,normal,hard,hardcore ) and believe me the "hard" and "hardcore" part is ain't a joke like most of the games today and you will be having a hard time at beating the game
on the hardest difficulty. ( like it should be )
Summary :
Far Cry 3 is considered by many to be the best game of 2012 and the best Far Cry game of its franchise,
and you know what ? they are right.
Far Cry 3 delivers an amazing singleplayer experience and an outright enjoyable coop mode
and a nice mutliplayer mode. While you can ignore from the coop and multiplayer ( which I suggest you do not cause both of them are fun and enjoyable ) the singleplay is the main attraction and the real treasure in this tropical island.
I recommend this game to everyone !!! and overall I give this game a 9\10
Simply amazing game which everyone should get and enjoy.

I originally reviewed this game and gave it a negative rating.  Why? Becasue I must've been doing something wrong and I kept losing my army. The AI was terrible and I didn't like micromanaging all my units.  Well, after play more and learning the game, I can say this game is fairly addictive.
Doing research on where to start is a must. The frozen area gives the most loot and better chance of encountering roving mobs.  They are harder however so learning how to kite with a long weapon is necessary.
The combat is pretty difficult.  If you hire a bunch of grunts and slowly upgrade them, you dont have to do a thing in a skirmish. You can literally sit back and maybe lose 1 or 2 guys.  The surgery skill is a pretty nice skill to have in this regard.
In conclusion, this game is worth a buy.  You may thing $20 is a bit steep for an old game with terrible graphics but you will get plenty of hours out of it. Just look at all the hours most of these other reviewers have.

I want to like it, honestly I do. It is much better than Far Cry 2 which I never finished cause it bored the heck out of me and was beyond repetitive. This returns somewhat to the roots of the series. Big tropical island with all sorts of adventure to be had. That is good, the Africa plot in FC2 was just dull. There is a repetitive style with the world however unlike FC2 it doesn't feel like you are traveling from dull sandbox to dull sandbox but literally playing in one giant sandbox. Which is similar to the original Far Cry.
Visuals are of course much better. They remind me of the first time I played the original Far Cry and was blown away.
The story...well literally I think the character Oliver wrote the story because it just is a narcotic filled mess. There is a constant assault to question sanity mixed up with rich California style brats who behave in incredibly cliche manners. Jason the "hero" then gets a magical tattoo, goes into rambo mode, and would be a decent protagonist if he actually lost his California kid voice.
I get it, he's not a badass and he's still human inside. But as the story goes, I just found myself disliking his character more and more. He gets an Anakin Skywalker vibe going, "I will be the most powerful!!", which gets very so-so. Vass on the otherhand, while certainly an in your face antagonist, is a complete and utter idiot. He's like a really crappy Bond villain who has numerous attempts to kill Bond but keeps trying to do things over the top instead of just blowing Bond's head off.
Characters and writing aside, it's an overall decent island romp. If you liked the original FC and hated FC2, you'll like FC3. Which is why I recommend it. However, if you have any sense of taste, you'll turn your brain off for the story and characters. Or just root for the bad guys. You know they'll lose but its better than rooting for these brat protagonists.

Probably in my top 5 games of all time. The story, atmosphere, and gameplay are over-the-top fun. The best part about this game is that it will probably take around 100 hours to fully complete. So many memorable and intense moments not only with the story, but the RP elements that you do on your own. For example, being attacked by a shark or that time that you took over an outpost only using a flamethrower. I definitely recommend getting this game if you are a fan of roleplay games such as Skyrim or Fallout or fans of just general first person shooters. Probably the only cons of this game would have to be the bland multiplayer which is just your typical team deathmatch. My other con of the game is when I first loaded it up it lagged immensely running an average of 15 FPS in cutscenes even on the lowest settings. After looking up how to solve my problem I eventually got my game to run a smooth 45 FPS on high settings which is probably the highest I can get on my setup. All in all a 10/10 game that I definitely recommend getting

In Warband you can join a lord, start your own kingdom, pick up jobs, or just terrorize everyone.

The ways you build your character are also very noteable, it is very debatable if being a commander (HIgh leadership, prisoner, trading, persuasion) or Front line (High irnoskin, power strike, combat related skills) is more effective.

If you like FPS games and open world games then Far Cry 3 is well worth your time.  The game gives you lots of fun toys & lots of fun situations to try them out in, with all the polish you expect of a AAA title.  What this means in gameplay terms is lots of freedom to solve problems your own way, so much so that this game should have been called 'Far Cry 3 - There's more than one way to skin a cat'.
Find yourself staking out a mercenary stronghold only to hear the distinctive growl of a tiger in the foliage behind you?  Don't worry, just slap on some animal repellent and chase the beast into the enemy camp.  See a platoon of enemy soldiers patrolling the long grass?  Set fire to it with a burning arrow and watch a swathe of tropical paradise burn.  This playfulness is considerably enlivened by the dynamic nature of the world and it is not at all uncommon to find third parties, human or animal, getting involved in fights.
If there's one drawback with this game it's the writing.  Like a lot of video games is aspires to cinema but only to the level of a B-movie.  Still, when you're having a blast, siccing tigers and rpgs on bad guys, you don't mind so much.  So to conclude, unless you place stern literary requirements on your open world shooters - get this game, it's lots of fun.

An excellent game by the very talented guys at Taleworlds Studios. Mount and Blade Warband is a sandbox RPG combined with a 3rd/1st person swordfighting game. Lead your warband up to glory on an overland map , interacting with dozens of other characters to build up your renown and standing with the other nobles in the wartorn land of Calradia. The second element to the game is 3rd person view  medieval combat, with one of the best attack systems for this kind of game. The fighting mechanisms in Mount and Blade are easy to lean, but incredibly dificult to master. Once you've perfected your swordfighting techniques, try fighting massive battles with hundreds of troops, or , even better, check out Mount and Blade Warband's multiplayer gamemode fighting other real players !
Mount and Blade Warband also features an amazing multiplayer-only expansion : Napoleonic Wars, that pits you in 19th Century Europe. Immensely frustrating at first, but an incredibly rewarding game experience with an amazing community !
Mount and Blade Warband is a must-have in your gaming collection!

(Note: Since posting, I've updated this review. See the lower paragraph.) This game is a worthless and unsupported pile of crap. Let me just say that I can run Black Ops II at maximum settings with absolutely no FPS dips or issues whatsoever. Ghosts, on the other hand, is a different story. Even on the lowest possible settings (where the game looks beyond awful, as if I had Vaseline smeared across my screen), I can barely keep it above 20 FPS, and sporadic dipping freqently pushes the FPS down into the single digits. Even tweaking the settings to the best you can for your system (which, even after being done, the game will probably still look terrible) is a nightmare. Every time you save a change in the graphics setting menu, even something as basic as switching between fullscreen and windowed mode, the game will have to reload the entire level. There is simply no excuse for such poor PC optimization. This game is an absolute insult to customers. Avoid at all costs. I bought this game on disc at BestBuy for $40, which is $20 less than the normal price as of now, and I paid about $39 too much. Do not waste your money on this.

I got around to playing this game again today, and I noticed that the framerate issues have been far improved (nowhere near perfect, but much, much, better). I still wouldn't recommend paying the full price for it, but it might be worth picking up when/if it goes on super-sale.

The game is great fun when you get past the beginning levels, to a certain extent. At first, it is a very unique and exiciting shooter, having everyone roll out into an objective with a jeep, is pretty cool. After a couple of games, this starts to become repetitive and a bit tedious. The charge across road, hide in forest, capture objective, is a fairly solid idea however it quickly bores, in my opinion. Even when this is fun, which is 50% of the time, when you have an epic firefight across the forests and storm objectives, it does feel a bit tedious at times, you die drive another jeep in die, again and again and again. Despite this, it is great fun when everything in the game comes together, the tank crews rolling in, parachuters dropping down and airplanes bombing you this way and that. When all of these things occur at the same time it is great, and this happens quite often. However, there are a variety of factors that drag this down, not just because of game mechanics, but perhaps also because of the community and players. It gets annoying when you charge into an objective, get sniped, do it again, get sniped, do it again, get sniped and so on. Plenty of people are going to say, "That's your own fault for being stupid HERDURR," the problem is,  there's not much else I can do as an infantry man. I can sit back and try and snipe people? But this isn't really a factor in this game. There's not much you can do but charge, machine gun and die, the marksman factor of this game exsists but it's not very effective, and there's no other gameplay mechanics that change this. An example I can use is Planetside 2 or Arma, where it is a perfectly reasonable option to just surround the objective and starve out your enemies, something that doesn't happen in this game. That might just be the way I feel about this game, but it is my review. Finally, in my big rant, there are times when I just want to smash my pc to pieces. There is nothing more annoying than a tank destroyer creeping around into the rear and blowing up every tank that spawns because the turrets are too slow to turn, and no one can blow up the enemy tank because anti tank items are too 'pay to win' and most people don't seem to even know about them.
The game has got a very large and annoying pay to win system, don't get me wrong it's a great game, graphics are great, gameplay is great, but pay to win and annoying tactics and repetition lets this game down, so overall I'd give it a 7.5/10. This is just what I've seen from the game, people may disagree but that's what I think.

An excellent game by the very talented guys at Taleworlds Studios. Mount and Blade Warband is a sandbox RPG combined with a 3rd/1st person swordfighting game. Lead your warband up to glory on an overland map , interacting with dozens of other characters to build up your renown and standing with the other nobles in the wartorn land of Calradia. The second element to the game is 3rd person view  medieval combat, with one of the best attack systems for this kind of game. The fighting mechanisms in Mount and Blade are easy to lean, but incredibly dificult to master. Once you've perfected your swordfighting techniques, try fighting massive battles with hundreds of troops, or , even better, check out Mount and Blade Warband's multiplayer gamemode fighting other real players !
Mount and Blade Warband also features an amazing multiplayer-only expansion : Napoleonic Wars, that pits you in 19th Century Europe. Immensely frustrating at first, but an incredibly rewarding game experience with an amazing community !
Mount and Blade Warband is a must-have in your gaming collection!

This game has a deep 3rd person medieval battle simulator at its core, with strong RPG-style leveling, map conquest, and some simple questing to build relationship with NPCs. To explain how GREAT this game is, let me tell you the story of a character I just retired. I started as a no-name who got mugged in a big town, and ended as the emperor of the known world. I was a level 1 son of a ruined nobleman with a rusty sword, a hunting crossbow, and a lame horse. I ended as a level 43 king warrior with a coat of plates armor, riding a heavily armored horse, and I could swing my masterwork sword twice per second. Did I mention I was carrying around 2.5 million gold coins and ruled over 22 towns, including the one where I got mugged? My first company had seven peasants with pitchforks and butcher knives. A few months I had leveled up my peasant and had a decent infantry squad supported by deadly but weak archery squad. The battle system is well fleshed out and you can command separately each type of unit and issue them about 25 different commands. When I retired I ran a company of 150 elite cavalry units, the famous swadian knights. I could literally take on companies almost thrice my size with favorable terrain (armored horses with armored warriors on them don't do so well in mountainous terrain you see.) When I retired I had leveled 4 NPC heroes in my company to level 35+. I had made them all cavalry, but I could have made them archers or infantry, it was up to me to choose their skills. One of them was a good engineer to build siege towers promptly, another one had great spotting so that my map vision was extended. I also ruled over 25-ish lords to whom I had given countless villages and castles as fiefs so that they could run large companies, some of them larger than mine. When I retired I was the most famous man in the land. I was also known as a man of honor since I avoided looting villages, freed allied lords and let rival lords go when I captured them on the battlefield. I had won hundreds of battles, some against rival kings and their gigantic companies, and had killed 15,000 foes out in the open battlefield or during sieges. If anything I said here appeals to you, do yourself a favor and pick up this game. Yes the graphics are not that great, but I was having so much fun that I did not notice.

Mostly like every other COD game, but it’s a good game to have and enjoy for what it is....
Multiplayer has some issues with hacking, but otherwise works fine. In regards to the multiplayer maps, some of the maps are classic COD fashion, meaning that they are small and gun fights breakout almost immediately after spawning, but Infinity Ward seems to be pushing larger maps as well. In my opinion, these larger maps are annoying (camping heaven) and as a result take a while to get kills on modes like Team Death Match. On a plus note, the new game modes are enjoyable, my favorite being Crank. Also the perk system has been changed, in some ways for the better and in others for the worse, but this is ultimately a user based decision.
Ghosts campaign is exciting  and pretty on max settings, aside from the classic COD mentality of stealing material from action films, the campaign is has awesome set pieces, but fails to make any of them wow moments (except for the intro, that was badass on all accounts). The campaign is different compared to the other CODs, which gives the Ghost unit some legitimacy. The story is mainly given to you by narration while you wait for the next mission to load. In typical fashion, the main character never speaks, but at least Infinity Ward gave you an adorable dog. However, this game is not the benchmark of graphics. Even on the highest settings, certain textures looked as if they belonged to games from 8 years ago; perhaps this is acceptable on consoles, but surely not on PC. Though this isn’t new and I highly doubt any one actually buys COD for the graphics or technical breakthroughs, for this one should consider Battle Field. I have played both Battle Field 4 and Ghost, and I have to say that I actually think the Ghost story line is much better than Battle Field's story line, however, this is opinion based once again.
I never experienced any fps drops or stutters on campaign, squad, or multiplayer (all running at the highest settings). I did not buy the game on launch, so perhaps it’s been patched and dealt with, I don’t honestly know.

I love this game! I bought it on a sale, played it, got addicted.
Graphics: everything is so beautiful and interesting to look at. Beaches, animals, camps, forests, mountains, people.
Sound: the soundtrack is quite decent and fitting to the situations (like if♥♥♥♥♥♥is going down it heats up).
Gameplay: the best feature! Jason (you) controls very well, gun play is perfect, the cars handle well, interacting with your environment is easy and smooth. There's a lot you can do in this game. You're really left to decide how to go ahead with things.
Story: the story is a little crazy; Vaas is the lead villain even if there is another antagonist in the story and really fleshed out though it would have been cool if he was more involved in the story. There are some really trippy parts in this game, times when you're on drugs or in trances. I really liked that aspect, it added a lot to the theme of a "mystical tropical island". Citra is a very interesting character too. But the others, not really. You have your friends but they're pretty blank.  There are some "moral choices" to make here and there, speficially in the end (giving the game two endings). However I felt it was a bit obvious what would happen.
So the game in general is perfect but for a few things that I think should have been tweaked (such as the ending/s). There is high replay value, an interesting DLC game, and some very cool mods to make the game fresh for a 2nd play through.

Wow this is a difficult game to describe. A sandbox action RPG set in a medieval land (fantasy, but realistic- no dragons, elves etc). After creating a character and completing a couple of short quests, the world is basically yours to explore and you can play as you please. You get money and/or xp by hunting bandits, pillaging, trading, selling prisoners, fighting tournaments, completing quests... and much more besides.
There are 6 factions all competing for control of the realm. You may decided to ally yourself with one of them, serving the King as a vassal, fighting his wars and seizing towns and castles. You may decided to assist a claimant to the throne, creating a rebel faction to usurp the current King, or you may proclaim youself King and create your own faction. Be aware that this is a dynamic and ever changing world- relations rise and fall, lands are conquered or pillaged, and lords may betray their King and defect. Every action has a consequence.
The game world is presented in a basic overworld map, switching to 3rd person upon entering a town, castle or village, or when in combat. The combat itself is the real meat of the game, allowing the player to swing, thrust or chop depending on the movement of the mouse. Riding on horseback also adds to the fun factor, and learning to time your strike as you gallop towards the enemy is key.
You may also recruit militia and companions into your party, and they will join you on the battlefield. They can be given commands (such as follow, hold and charge) and will also earn xp and level up. The command system is simple, but works well. If you don't want to get blood on your shiny new armour then sending your troops ahead to fight without you is often a legitimate option.
The game does have a few quirks that will annoy some people (such as companions bickering, complaining and abandoning you). Fortunately there is a program available to download (TweakMB) that allows you to easily tailor the gameplay mechanics to better suit you.
Buy this game if you enjoy solid combat, open-ended gameplay and epic battles.

As small as the PC COD community is, we do have high expectations, just as our console friends of this yearly series. So, it came as a huge shock when I discovered how limiting the PC Ghosts experience was. The core game is Call of Duty with all of it's usual bells and whistles such as a set-peice filled campaign, class driven multiplayer, and the new co-op extinction mode. To put it as simply as possible, if you came for COD, you get COD, but that's just about it. Also, if you have a beast rig that makes titles like Battlefield 4 glow with realism, expect COD Ghosts to look like a muddy and uninspired mess. With the budget Infinity Ward has, and after boasting about their new game-engine, you will be suprised to see just how last gen this title is. To be honest, this is by no means the worst looking COD title out, but for next-gen, and also being compared to their competition Battlefield 4 you might not want to account visuals as a game changer for your purchasing descision. The online is addictive (and frustrating) like previous titles which alone does make the game worth a whirl, but with horrible clan support, no real compelling or inspired weapon upgrades, and with horrible FPS drops the online will get tedious and make you question why you're not on Battlefield at times. For 60$ game is a no-go in my humble opinion. I'd wait for the bargain bin sale before picking this COD title up.

Ok, so legit review time. I have put quite a bit of time into this game.
There are some problems at the moment, but it'll be fixed in the next update. You can go on the forums and see what the problems are (mainly do to with the RTS/Campaign part of the game), since they don't censor the forums like many other gaming companies. I've seen people saying this game is pay to win, and I'd say otherwise. Pay for convenience, yes, but you can unlock anything that someone with money can. So it's more pay to progress faster, if you wish. Either way, the game is pretty balanced inside of the actual FPS and the better player will come out on top.
If you're looking for something close to battlefield 2, this is definitely it. The best part is it's free to play, and you can earn anything. It might take a little while to progress to the very top, but it's definitely worth it and the community can be pretty helpful when you ask for some help.
The game definitely needs better tutorials, but other than that I'd definitely recommend playing this game and at the very least giving it a good try (around 40-50 hours) to see if you enjoy it.

I am a banana. I say that partly because I like taking all my clothes off and hiding in bowls of muesli and partly because like a banana I feel I’m going soft as I get older. I’ve been liking more games lately, and I know saying that has just made someone who likes modern warfare shooters spit-take a mouthful of inexpensive supermarket whisky, but the games that exist outside that particular♥♥♥♥♥bubble have been going from strength to strength. That could just be because absolutely ♥♥♥♥ing anything looks good alongside a♥♥♥♥♥bubble, or perhaps it means I actually do have the power to make things improve as long as I unceasingly bully and insult it for half a decade. Although that seems unlikely because as has already been established, I am a banana, and the only influence I have is over one’s potassium intake.
But whatever the case a few years ago I did Far Cry 2 and though it would have been alright if it weren’t for a couple of rather glaring issues, and now Far Cry 3 has pretty much sorted out those glaring issues and therefore is alright. It’s fine. It fills the space; what do you want from me, I am a banana.
The glaringist of the glaring issues in Far Cry 2 was characters as in there didn’t seem to be any. Just a whole load of people doing stuff. Far Cry 3 meanwhile has a strong character focus, meaning there are still a load of people doing stuff, but now they wonder aloud if the stuff they’re doing is the right stuff after all. You are Jason Brody, an American tourist and a member of small group of preening self-centered rich gobshites, who to the immense relief of the entire known universe, fall foul of a slavery ring on a tropical island, run by a psychopath named Vaas, who’s name one can remember with a simple mnemonic: “Watch out for Vaas, he’ll enslave your♥♥♥♥♥♥” Over the course of rescuing his surviving friends, Jason must shed his idle doughy Wonder Bread carapace and build himself anew from the steel and the bear-skins of the jungle. But by the time he’s reunited with his friends, and they’re all sitting around winging about torture, enslavement, and the lack of mobile reception, Jason must face the fact that he probably doesn’t have much to talk about with them anymore since none of them like Belgian takedowns or flamethrower bear hunting.
It is nice to see a shooter protagonist who doesn’t start out with years of off-camera special forces training and instead must gradually grow into that role through nonstop violence and taking massive amounts of drugs, to the point that his toenail clippings alert sniffer dogs. It’s a character arc: the character has to change and adapt rather than start out as a big meathead in power armor and end as the exact same meathead in power armor with maybe a slightly sorer throat. And I’m fond of how the game retains its focus on Jason’s internal journey by never leaving his first-person perspective, which is great for dream sequences but not so much for vehicle sections. I kept sliding off the roads because the cars are always a few feet wider than you think they are. It’s a lot like online dating.
But I digress. The character arc brings to mind the one in Spec Ops: The Line, as in both cases a hostile environment strips the comfortable hypocrisies of civilization from an everyman protagonist, until only a monster remains. Except in Far Cry 3’s case, you start thinking that he actually quite likes being a monster. And while you can never go back to your old life now that you have an itch that can only be scratched by adding to your necklace of testicles, at least you don’t have to queue up at the DMV now.
So what we have here is a truly organic sandbox shooter. It’s a free-trade parsnip while something like BLOPS 2 is a discarded KFC chicken wing on a dog turd. A typical combat mission involves scouting the area from a vantage point, marking targets, picking the optimal angle of approach, and taking down the baddies one by one. It’s quite relaxing really, like pruning a rosebush where the roses can get freaked out and call another rosebush to come and back it up. And it’s always very satisfying to pull it off without being spotted, although the nature of an organic sandbox can lead to some odd results.
One time I was carefully scouting an enemy base and just about decided on the best angle of attack when a ♥♥♥♥ing tiger lolloped into the base and ♥♥♥♥ing cleared it out with strategic maulings. What a right wally Mister ♥♥♥♥♥cat has made me look like, but it’s the sort of thing that’d never ♥♥♥♥ing happen in Call of Duty, isn’t it? Not unless Mister ♥♥♥♥♥cat was a programmed setpiece with ties to Al Qaeda. Anyway animal hunting is a big part of upgrading your equipment so after that I resolved to up my tiger quota in case the rebel army started thinking tigers might make better insurgents than random pasty holiday makers.
The funny thing was: after I’d murdered enough the animals to craft all the inventory upgrades and earn the title of parallel universe Noah, as well as gotten most of the upgrades I needed from the experience track, there was still about half the game to go. And this is without obsessive side questing. I did a few, but I spent more time flying randomly around on the hang glider imagining that I was pooing on enemy installations. It’s like the first half of the game is for upgrading into a badass mofo, and the second half is for pootiling around being a badass mofo, which I actually kinda like if that was intended. There are too many games where you only get the ultra-♥♥♥♥♥cat death beam surprise that rips off the enemies♥♥♥♥♥♥and writes their obituary with it right at the end of the game so you only get to use it on the end boss and maybe his goldfish. Giving us plenty of time to make the most of all the best toys is remaining true to the sandbox; no joining the dots from checkpoint to checkpoint, just set of tools and a target. You want to hang glide over an assassination mission and jump on the dude like he’s a ♥♥♥♥ing Koopa Troopa, then godspeed, you mad ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.
Having said that though, the story mission can be a bit more checkpoint Charley and a bit less roaming Rambo. What’s most disappointing is that the major villains are all defeated with horrible quick-time-event cutscenes that aren’t so much boss fights as middle management disagreements. I appreciate that given the setting you can’t exactly have them piloting giant robots but still. Come to think of it, the story aspect is generally weaker in the second half, especially after Vaas the♥♥♥♥♥♥ the character who is the ♥♥♥♥ing face of the game mind you, disappears and is replaced by someone less interesting, and now that I’m on the complain train, stealthing it is fun, but intense firefighting gets annoying ‘cause your health drops like a fat dog from a hot air balloon and wresting with the weapons selector and health syringes under pressure is like rearranging the HDMI cables at gunpoint.
But this is nitpicking. As we established at the start, I am a banana and Far Cry 3 is fine. It’s alright. There is one last disappointment in the story ending though. I opted to stay on the island rather than go home but without wishing to spoil, that ending is♥♥♥♥♥♥ Don’t tell me the good ending entails a guy who machetes bears while high going back to civilization, ‘cause I’d give him a week before he’s making bootleg wallets out of fat people's ears. - Yahtzee

Now I am the kind of person who loves a sandbox FPS and should have given this game a perfect score but it has some problems with it.  One, it commits a grevious sin when takedowns are contextual and otherwise melee requires multiple hits to kill.  Second, QTEs or quick time events, essentially a cop out for games and they are more an irritant than a solid gameplay mechanic.  Third, cut scenes, a good story should be able to be told without having to have this five minute interruption to continue the story.  Plus, they're not skippable so when I've played through the game already and just want to replay it for the sandbox and to complete missions, I want to skip them to get the missions and go.  Fourth, this may seem nit picky but for me it drove me nuts, I could not map crouch to ctrl, which it is in every other game.  I found myself trying to crouch in TF2 but because I had started to intregrate "C" as my crouch, I was shot in the face because I then had to exit a chat menu.
So those are my issues with the game, however, I found a lot of fun with Far Cry as well.  First, the world is massive allowing for lots of exploration and giving the sense of accomplishment when you finally beat the sandbox.  Two, the weapons unlocking system in interesting but money becomes arbitrary and useless later in the game but the weapons themselves are fun to customize and offer a lot of versatility with missions.  Third, the vehicles are a tremendous amount of fun to drive as they control well even with a keyboard, and give a sense of weight as they take time to respond and brake but also make going across the map without using the fast travel fun and fast.  Fourth, the first time you play through the game the story is engaging and worth it because it does have a good central antagonist and a solid plot.  Fifth, the wildlife is a lot of fun to engage with, especially when you can break open a cage and set a bear rampaging through a group of badies as you then send their hopes and dreams splattering across a nearby wall as you snipe them, distracted by the bear.
Above all, it is a good game and one that has a lot of replay value if only for the sandbox and fun driving mechanics. BUT, I MUST make one final criticism; a fatal sin that prevents me from recommending the game fully, is the fact that Ubisoft makes you install UPlay first and that right there requires me to have to exorcise my computer.  But, if you're someone who has no problem with that then go nuts.  Ignoring the UPlay sin, I recommend it so that will be my final verdict, a recommendation* and a score of 85/100.

This is a really awesome game! I played it at a friend's house years before buying it myself and was hooked from the first second, when I personally slew almost 200 peasants.
The game has a great fighting mechanic and the startegy improves as you progress. You start of a warrior with a small band of followers who need to be fed and looked after while you start all the little quests while hiding from the dangerous armies roaming the land.
When you get a bit of a reputation you will be allowed to do jobs for a king as the leader of a mercenary gang. With the number of followers increasing you need that extra cash to feed them and get better armour. Then you just hope you aren't called to war. Those battles are insane. With 800 men on a side. An entire nation's soldiers and you just sit there with your 25 men trying not to die, but if you enhance you reputation even more you can become a vassal and lord of a king. Then it starts getting complicated. You are given some villages and/or a castle to manage. Training soldiers and protecting your villages from bandits while saving money for the future. I was once forced to defend my first castle on the front lines against an army of 700 people. I refused to give up and managed to kill 550 of them before I was knocked unconscious and my men finished the battle successfully.
You need to start thinking about the future. Will you be satisfied to be ruled by a king? That's when the alliances start. You must court a lady and get married to solidify your position. When you've saved up all you can and built a decent army you have a chat to your king and ask to leave his service. (Best done on good terms)
You are now a free man and you have to take your army and capture your first castle to begin your great empire.
The game allowes many play styles. You might be an archer, lancer, knight, crossbowman, or swordsman.
You don't have to do what I did. You can be a bandit lord, feared by all. Or remain as you are doing what you want but be ambitious and the world will be yours! The hardest part however is balancing your lords so they all like you a difficult thing to do. I once read that Kingship was won by feasts not fiefs!
With this award system implemented by Steam, I would nominate this game for about 3 of them but only one is allowed. Still, this game is 100% worth the money and it goes on sale often.
Also mod it to be whatever you want it to be, it has plenty of options.

I have enjoyed my time playing H&G, while there are twerks and annoyances that exist within almost most FPS style games it has been mostly positive expirence for me.
The variety of play styles are good your tried and true infantry which is pretty much all around capable of killing everything in game without much assistance provided you are equipped to do so.
Recon, what you expect of a sniper however the scope only gives you so much of an edge over your iron sights counter parts but you are limited with weaponry and primarly should rely on keeping 100m or more between you and your target.
Pilots- First and foremost I can not fly a plane very well at all, so I recommed watching others and practicing a lot but a good pilot is the scariest thing in game.
Paratrooper- If you enjoy the ambush and appearing where you are least expected this is your class. Equipped with a good sub machine gun they can pop up anywhere and pretty much be a terror anywhere on the map.
Tanks/Panzers- This is a grind, I can't beat around the bush it will take you a month of solid grinding to work your way through the tanks but the tanks are at least fun. Wonky veichle mechanics will hinder you and the armor models will frustrate you but if you enjoy it and are able to work through the starter tanks you will find joy in driving these metal beasts.
General- I have no opinion not my style.
The Good: Various loadouts and perks which change the way you play, while yes People who have veteran status will have a slight edge over you do not let that discourage you. Playing better doesnt mean a guy with a gold bought weapon will be able to use it. Playing infantry while difficult at times is varried and does not have be the same thing. YOu can be an anti tank monster and have the enemy team scared everything they hear you drive up with your car behind them. A machine gunner carrying hundreds of rounds and hold a position with ease. Or the tried and true rifleman with grenades which can kill at medium/short/long range.
The Bad: A grind, to get what you want at a reasonable pace without paying for veterancy will take you a week or more depending on your profession. Infantry/para will not be a problem, Tanker or recon will take time but if you like it slow and steady this wont be a major con.
Wonky veichles, sometimes they behave sometimes they dont. Flipping a car or motorcycle is easy getting stuck is a constant problem and working out what to do is not easy while being shot at.
Teammates: its everywhere, LoL,WoW,Dota and here people will be people online however the developers are serious and punish bad behavior so a quick screenshot and submit and they will take action, two trolls were banned for a while after I submitted my ticket.
Recommedation:  If you enjoy FPS with a tact of veichles and planes this will be fun I have enjoyed over 200 hours and nearly done it all except general. However if you cant get over the pay for upgrades then dont bother because people will just spend money to get a leg up in a competitive game. However solid playing beats out people screaming out P2W, it isnt. (Using a russian weapon doesnt make you a god, kill him and steal it. That money is now in your hands)  You support the game you get a small buff its standard in most games, my 2nd perk doesnt prevent me from doing something stupid or someone being smarter than me and killing me.
I hope this was helpful in making a decision, give it a shot its free to play for a reason. Stick around and support or just play more at your own pace.

Quite possibly the worst Call of Duty to ever be released and does it surprise us that it's an Infinity Ward production? It might be time we apologized to all those IW employees who were sacked after Modern Warfare 2 because what is clear now is that the fault lay with the management. And, sorry to say, most of them are still here.
Much like MW3, gamers were promised servers and bought the game with that in mind only to find out that that was not the case. Then, some time later, they tried to backpedal and suggest that the system that runs matchmaking was actually what they were talking about when they said "server". This, of course, entirely ignores the fact that one of their executive producers had already claimed that servers would be rolling out over time.
Short version: they lied. Again. Just like they did with MW3 which they claimed would have servers and then flat out told us that we weren't going to get them, regardless of what they had previously said. There are no servers and there never will be.
The resulting game (which another of their employees intimated was only crap because it was never designed to matchmaker based - guess IW don't care who knows they're talking crap) is baaaaaaad to the very nth degree. Lag is a HUGE decider in this game. Have a slow or outdated machine, then the game will either pick you to host or favour your data over that of people who were foolish enough to put their hard-earned cash into their PCs. So it doesn't matter how fast or skilled you are, you will lose to an outdated machine.
Snipers: the vast majority of the time, your shots, whether on target or not, will not register. You WILL get angry when you shoot someone several times and they still have time to have coffee, get their nails done and light a cigarette before turning around to shoot you. You're also only given semi-auto pistols as a backup weapon so get used to dying in close quarters. You will have no decent defense.
The alternative -> Marksman Rifles (where they have dumped anything that resembles a useful semi-auto rifle): here you will discover a new type of crap, something we haven't seen since the sniper-hating exec that was in charge of Black Ops 1 and openly admitted to nerfing and hindering their capabilities. In short: You can use red-dot sights and the like on them or acog and thermals. The thermals (more accurate here and on assault rifles than on snipers) kick like crazy, so landing more than one shot is time-consuming. The red-dots are good, but reek of an effort to hinder you from a decent magnification with something that would actually snipe well. There IS a sight in game that bridges that gap - the VMR sight - but, of course, they don't let you have that on Marksman Rifles.
VAC is almost as non-existent here as in MW2, prepare to see hacker after hacker after hacker. And thanks to lag, that can make killcams appear as if something turned and shot you with unnatural agility, you will be freaking out over who is actually hacking and who isn't.
If a match is running slowly and you wanna know who has the bad ping that's dragging you down? Tough crap, they removed ping meters so you couldn't see how badly everyone is running.

As a long time fan of FPS games, nothing is better than seeing the words "Free To Play" or F2P.  However, it's not without feeling vain at some point.  This is with all F2P games.  After having played several "Free To Play" games, I've decided this was the most well rounded.  At very few points in the game, do you feel belittled due to weapons, equiptment, or people that pay for in-game items and/or ranks.  If you do, play more, play smarter, play better.  You can eventually get everything, in time.  You play, you earn unlocks.  You level guns, ranks, ribbons, etc.  These give you upgrades, perks, and the option to purchase guns and modifications with in-game currency.  In no way, shape, or form, do paying people have any upper hand, when it comes to weapons and skills.  Paying people, only get items/ranks instantly.  Personally, I think it takes away from the game if you don't level your character.  Who's going to be better, a person that bought his sniper with little gameplay time?  Or a sniper whom had to level his Bolt Action Rifle to Rank 11 to unlock and earn his sniper?  I have my personal answer, but it's your call.
This also is nothing like Tom Clancey Ghost Recon Phantoms.  In that game, you can spend forever earning decent guns, and withing 3 weeks, almost everything has a gun 3 times better.  You can buy guns in that game, and in 3 weeks, they'll have better ones, forcing you to spend more money.  I became ranked in the top 3000 players, and quit, because almost all players after that rank level have holes burning in their pockets.  In Heroes and Generals, they aren't adding guns every 3 weeks, and if they do, they're not unrealistically reachable.  Sure you have to put in the time and complete objectives.  But a person couldn't possibly be that utterly lazy to think things are just handed to you.  It's kind of like any MMORPG, you have to level your character.  Play it!  Enjoy it!  Spend money if you want for cool different paint patterns on weapons that are a complete waste of funds.  It's your game.  It's your life.  I'm just hear to say, that it's not a bad "Free To Play - Pay To Win" type game.  Any free player with any decent amount of skill, should love this game.  The grind may suck at times, but totally worth it when you earn what you've been working towards.
As a sidenote: Once you've reached a weapon you like, or happen to be stuck with for quite a few ranks until what you're seeking, modify the gun.  A lot of people say not to modify, but screw it.  I'm working towards Recon/Sniper because I always snipe in games, and pretty damn good at it.  So I modified my Bolt Action, and now have max damage, and more than halfway range, and good precision.  I one shot kill almost every time with my BA Rifle.  With good aim, and figuring speed-to-target ratio (running/biking targets), I can shoot a moving target better than most snipers, with scopes.

In interesting game that still needs some work.
H&G cuts a good line between straight up FPS and more tactical gameplay, being able to push and take objectives however you can (although most can only be captured directly by infantry) with ample opportunities to flank, lay traps for an assault or fight in a more attritional style using infantry, jeeps, planes, tanks, APCs and a sound you will soon find familiar if you start playing, the bicycle.
The biggest drawbacks currently are the poor hit detection, which is all done server side rather than client side like most FPS games. Server side hit detection makes shooting accurately a real headache due to the way the server reads player locations and then displays them client side.
The second drawback is the huge imbalance in player counts and the balance of weaponry for each side. The Axis (German) side is vastly more popular and so the Allies (US) are left wanting. The equipment, especially the light arms, is rather unbalanced too, I don't want to see mirror images of different weapons for each team but to have some weapons actually be effective, currently the Axis MGs, the MG32 and MG42, are very accurate, high RoF, shoulder fired, low recoil, death spewing machines, the American counterparts, the BAR and M1919, are horribly weak in comparison, lower RoF, higher recoil, rather terrible iron sights and just feel very poorly implemented.
Despite those criticisms, the game good, if you don't start playing now then at least keep an eye on it, there are regular updates and I expect the most glaring issues to be fixed soon.

Mount & Blade: Warband is a pretty great game! It can get annoying at times like, when you try to make a big army and they abandon one by one you for no reason. :( But that's also because some of my soldiers think that I am lousy at paying them. (That's because I am). The multiplayer is so fickin fun and the combat is very good! Also, unicorn horses! Just stick an arrow in their skull! (They'll be fine... I thnk!) The AI and single player is awesome and you have so many things to do. You can run a kingdom or be a mercenary. It all depends on what you want to do. I rate this game a: 5 out of 5!

Graphics: For an Indie Title the Graphics are fine. Don't expect to see anything Amazing though.
Story: There isn't really an actual story to the game. You make a character, decide their background, and then your thrown into this Medievel envirement to do whatever you please. There are quests, but nothing too epic.
Gameplay: This is one of the best open world games (and one of the best games) I've ever played. You can command up to hundreds of troops (1000's in mods) and do whatever you want. Want to be a Bandit. Go right ahead. Want to be a vassel to a King? Go right ahead. Want to take over the world as an evil warlord. Go right ahead! The possibilities are endless. The game has a unique and very good melee weapon system, that is a change to just click to attack and click to block. And the loots and monys are ripe for the taking in this game.
Sound: There isn't much voice acting but the Music is excellent.
Replayability: With 6 factions there are a ton of troop types, weapons, armors, ways to fight(greatswords, lances, spears, sword 'n' shield, etc.) And the ability to make your own Kingdom or join one and just do whatever. Not-to mention the HUGE mod community which is one of the main reasons to buy this game. There is alot of replay value.
Last thoughts: This is a fantastic open world game. Both a 3rd/1st person action and strategy combined. You tell your HUNDREDS of troops how to fight, where to be positioned, and give them tacticts while on the battle field in real time. There hundred's of weapons and armors, many troop types, 6 different factions with strengths and weaknesses, companions, cities and castles to conquer and more. After you've done your fighting and castle/city capturing you can manage the court and your people, install upgrades to your towns/cities/castles, hire or persuad lords to join you, and truly become a King. The MOD community for this game is fantastic. There are tons of mods that add in overhauls to the game(different time periods, more gameplay options, fantasy settings, modern settings, and much more) Just sealing the deal for this gem of a game.
