This is a brilliant, addicting game that you MUST buy! It is a Medieval Sandbox game which involves you recruiting people from Villages and going all Hero Mode and fighting Bandits, helping Villagers and doing jobs for towns.
Or, go all Evil and raid Villages, attack innocent Farmers, harass Merchant Carvans and being a total Jerk.
You can also sell your sword (or whatever weapon you wish to use) to one of the many factions in the game, 6 in total, who are all competing for complete dominance in the land of Calradia.
Firstly, we have the Kingdom of Nords. The Nords are Vikingish people who majorly rely on their Heavy Infantry, the Nordic Huscarls. In my opinion, thease are the BEST (and I mean the BEST) infantry units that you could possibly get. Their position in Calradia, is in the North West. A word of warning, even though this faction is pretty much the faction that all beginners will join, the game is made to have this faction ALWAYS, ALWAYS, trying to be at war with any faction. One time when I was playing with them, they were at war with EVERY SINGLE OTHER FACTION in the game! I couldn't even leave a city without being attacked by another faction.
Secondly, we have the Kingdom of Vaegirs. Russiany Axe Wielding, Bow using merry men who live in the Snowy areas of Calradia. Along with a few villages and a city of the Nords, they are terrorised by Sea Raiders, who plague the Coasts. Becareful when fighting them, as they are the strongest, and most dangerous bandits you can run into in this game, but also carry some AMAZING start loot, and can be used to XP farm for your men. The Vaegirs also boast the Best Archers in the game, the Vaegir Marksman, who's only possible equals are the Sarranid Bow Masters, who we will get to later. This factions position, is in the North East.
Thirdly, the Kingdom of Swadia. A mix between English and possible French, who are in the very middle of Calradia. In my opinion, they are a faction I would not choose to join, because due to the fact that they are at war, any faction they go to war with, will be right next to them, meaning you would not get a break, unlike the Nords, who if they were at war with the Rhodoks, would get some breathing room, as they would be a kingdom away from them. The Swadians also have the Best, but most expensive, Cavalry in the game. The powerful Swadian Knights! The Sarranid Mamlukes (who we will get to later) can also possibly give the Knights a good challenge.
Fourthly, the Kingdom of Rhodoks. They have the same origins as the Swadians. They rebelled against the Swads and founded their own Kingdom in the mountains. They are a nice beginner starting area, and possibly a very nice faction to join, as long as they are fighting in their own land. Their position is in the South West of Calradia, in the Mountains. They have the strongest crossbowmen, and have some very decent infantry, who mainly carry Spears. The Rhodok Seargent (Sorry if that is spelt incorrectly) may be the Second best Infantry, if not the third. Their Crossbowmen, the Rhodok Sharpshooter, is the best Crossbowmen in the game, beating the Swadian Crossbowmen. A mix with their Crossbowmen, along with some Vaegir Marksman and Nordic Huscarls, could become the strongest force in Calradia, especially if mixed with some Swadian Knights and a few Sarranid And Khergit Cavalry. Also, like the Nords and Vaegirs, are under siege by some powerful Bandits, the Mountain Bandits, who do have some annoying units, but also have some nice loot and can be used to get some early starting XP.
Now to the Sarranid Sultanate. Deserty people who have some very nice Cavalry and Archers. They are in the South East part of Calradia. Just look at the Deserts and you will see them. You could say that their Mamlukes are equal with the Swadian Knights, and are better than those knights, as the Mamlukes cost less to pay for. The Sarranid Master Archers are also the second best Archers in the game, with the Vaegir Marksman being the first. Their special bandits are the Desert Bandits. Horse Riding, Lance wielding people who are very annoying, especially when you have a poorly equipped and upgraded bunch of soldiers. They can be used to get a nice bit of XP, but their loot in not impressive.
Finally, we come to the Khergit Khanate. People who possibly take after the likes of Ghenghis Khan (I think so, and no racism is meant). Mostly all their units are horse riders, so getting across Calradia, and the battlefield, will be no problem. They mainly rely on their Bows and Lances, and are horrible when attacking a Castle or Town, so becareful when using them when on the attacking side of a siege. They are also in the middle of Calradia, but just a little to the right. Honestly, I would not join them, because if you are attacking a well equipped army of Rhodoks (which most games I have had, the Khergs and Rhods are at war) your Lancers could be decimated by their Spears, and any remaining units would be shot down by their Crossbowmen. The game is simply fun and addicting. It CAN become repetitive if you do the same things over and over again (Same goes with any other game). The gameplay itself is smooth and polished for the most part. There's sometimes a hit detection lag. Probably one of the best Beta's I've played in a long time. The game never crashes or bugs out.  Going prone could use some work as it's a little buggy at times when your on an incline. The weapons themselves are decent, not really accurate to the historical values in the ratings department, but they seem to be adjusted to provide fair gameplay on both factions. Same goes with the vehicles. The upgrades are an awesome feature. It's also nice that mods require repairs and ammo/grenades require purchasing. Keeps the currency flowing. Too many kids are complaining about the cost of buying weapons and mods. Personally I think it's near perfect. I like how you have to continually spend earned currency to keep your modified stuff. Gives a reason to keep playing. If they unlocked all guns and mods from the beginning, it would simply be another game where 5 hours of gameplay gets you everything and the currency is no longer a part of the game.
There is sort of a Pay-To-Win portion of the game, however the gameplay is really about SKILL and not so much about your loadout. Using real money can get you anything you want, but it isn't cheap and good! This game is about teamwork and using your army to push and defend objectives. This isn't a lone wolf kinda game. You can be successful once in a while capturing objectives on your own, but you really need the help of your team to hold down a position and bulldoze to the next. If you're expecting a COD/Battlefield game, don't bother.
The game really needs a proximity voip system to bring it to the next level. As I said above, you need a team at your back moving and working together. I feel like this could be accomplished with a voip system. Proximity makes sense because not all soldiers had radios in ww2.  The voip thing is probably the biggest thing on my wishlist for this game.
Other than that, keep adding new content, maybe update textures/sounds and that's really about it. OH and the squad system (playing with friends) is barebones and could use a little work. You shouldn't have to bail out of your squad to make changes to your loadout. That's it. Play the game and once you get passed the learning curve, you'll have fun.

Okay, so I thought I'd wait a while before writing a review on this game, purely because I really really wanted to like it, and for a while I did, but to me, the 3 major things that spoil this game are as follows.
1. The feature of being able to pay for weapons instead of purchasing them, meaning you can buy higher tier guns and♥♥♥♥♥♥on your enemies before they've had the chance to grind the hundreds of hours needed in order to earn them through gameplay alone.
2. As mentioned above, the insane amount of grinding to get experience points, as well as in game currency, which you will burn through rediculously fast, having to PAY TO REFILL HALF YOUR WEAPONS AT THE END OF EVERY GAME. If the xp/currency to hours of gameplay ratio was just a little more balanced, this would not be an issue, and would just solve so many of this games problems.
3. (And this may not apply to everyone, but I know quite a few players who have this problem) Serious FPS issues. Maybe it's the optimization of the game, maybe it's my computer (although I doubt it), or maybe it's something else, who knows. All I know is that the game fluctuates from a playable 20-30fps, to a completely unplayable and game breaking 7-10 fps, seemingly at random. This has happened to me on every game I've played in my 24 hours of gameplay, and it's the reason I won't be playing the game again for a while. I haven't been able to find any fix for this, and anyone who has the same problem and asks about it gets ignored.
There are many other issues that bother me about this game, but I think the above 3 sum up my major gripes with it. I do, however, still recomend this game. Why? Because it's a free to play, and all you have to lose is some gigs of storage space and a few hours. Maybe you'll have a better time than me, maybe you like hours of hard grinding gameplay, maybe that's your thing. But of course, you might not enjoy it, but it's worth a try. The playerbase in this game (for the most part) is really great, with everyone I've come across being friendly, mature, and really getting into the game, making it that much more immersive. Regardless, I think it's a game with great potential, I just wouldn't put money into at this stage. Worth a few hours of play at least.

Do not let the somewhat outdated graphics fool you, this is one of my favorite games. Ever. Now the game by itself, Native is good on its own. You can play it differently every time you play with whole diffrent outcomes. Become a king in one and become a bandit in the other! Singleplayer was good, but multiplayer is great. Multiplayer quickly became the default way to play M&B, battles of up to 200 people fighting eachother, ducking at the sound of arrows, charges on horseback, steam groups that have made their own group FOR M&B command battles with their comrades. These huge battles put M&B on the map.
The Native Moudle is great by itself, but the folks at Tale Worlds took it a step further and added a huge mod system to it! The reason why I said moudle is that once you start the game you have a range of moudles/mods to choose from. The default is Native (duh) but you can download mods from the site or other sources on the internet that can either change the game completly where it seems it could be a stand alone game by itself or simple additions to Native that add on to it.
These mods can offer hundreds of hours of play time to the game, great modifications like PW (Persistent World) change the whole focus of the game into being sorta a MMO. In this you start of a commenor in a huge Persistent World, as the title says. There you build yourself up or don't, it is all up to you, into becoming a Knight or a Lord for some faction that other players has created. Or become a Preist or a simple farmer and live peacefully and hope that other players who are bandits do not rob you or a battle between two factions emerges on your crops. Various other modifications such as Iron Europe which changes the Native medieval setting to the trenches of WW1, where you have your bolt action and machine guns where you fire at eachother in the trenches Another multiplayer game mind you. I can go on and on but I am not exactly here to tell you about other peoples work, you can take a look at that yourself but you see what I mean. Here is the good the bad and ugly.
___________________________________________________________________________________
THE GOOD-
.Easy to learn but difficult to master combat system, this gives you plenty of play time to try and master your concept. Also combat is very fun, you watch for your enemies moves as you block with your sword by moving your mouse in the direction of the combatant is thrusting or slicing.
.The Mod System. As I said before, this literaly gives the game thousands of hours of gameplay and entierly different ways of playing the game. Remember this is one of the biggest ones.
.Customization and RPG Elements. The RPG elements come from singeplayer which are a simple but effective system but the customization in armour, uniforms, facial features, etc... really gives you a wide varitey of options into making what your character wants to be like, in singleplayer or multiplayer. Speaking of which...
Multiplayer. This is another big one, multiplayer opens a huge community of players who create entire regiments and clans which are organized who have their own formations, command structure, etc... This alone can offer hundreds of hours of gameplay. Multiplayer is the DEFAULT mode to play M&B in my opinion and one of the most important features of the game.
___________________________________________________________________________________
THE BAD-
.The outdated graphics. The graphics in the game can be considered a bit dated by todays standereds, but it is not really that big of a deal in my opinion. As long as you are having fun graphics are not a priority.
.Minor Bugs/Gliches. Yes there may be a couple bugs and gliches here and there, like there may be some lag here and there in massive multiplayer game sessions but cant that be said for all? Also there is some gliches where you may jump on a cart and might get stuck, but this is pretty unlikely. Also small gliches here and there but nothing game breaking.
.Maps Boundries. The points of maps can be somewhat... choppy? It is a little hard to explain, it is sorta untextured and if you get to the back it can be somewhat untextured. But this is not that big of a deal again, as long as you are having fun.
___________________________________________________________________________________
THE UGLY-
SINGLEPLAYER. Building up a "huge" army and then have it all obliterated by an enemy on campaign.
MULTIPLAYER. PW MOD- Start from a peasent and then litearly work your way up to a knight or lord and then have your faction destroyed by a much larger faction and then you become a farmer or preist and live a queit and peaceful life...
___________________________________________________________________________________
So in my opinion the game gets a 10/10, there is so many great mods to chose from and overall is is perfect, and I know there is people out there who would say, "Ohhhhh, the ground looks sorta untextured and not photorealstic! Blah, blah, BLAH! For those people out there, get over it! Enjoy a game with great gameplay and mechanics. And if a game has photorealstic graphics but the gameplay is crap, then it is just a boring chore. And this games all around gameplay is perfect! Some mods feel like they can be stand alone games by themselves. A great game and I reccomend it to everybody.

A great game, filled with tactics and corruption, as you fight your way through a land known as Calradia. The combat system is fantastic, Cavalry charge into battle with deadly Crossbow Bolts flying overhead. Sieges are difficult, time consuming, and expensive in troop casualties, and even then there is no garuntee you will recieve the castle. The skill system is one of the best I have experienced, the army system is fantastic. The economy is well thought out, with each event influencing a towns wealth. You could become a merceny, and fight for a pretender to a throne and become his most valuable vassal, or you could be a loyal member of a royal family, earning wealth through taxes and wars. You could be a man of the arena, travelling the land building wealth and experience through hard fought small scale battles.
All in all, a fantastic buy for any strategy gamer out there who wants to lead from the front lines and charge into battle with his soldiers.

A really fun, semi-persistant multiplayer WW2 combined-arms shooter that is buried under an insane level of grind and Pay-to-Win microtransactions, as well as unfortunate balance issues.
If I could buy this game for a flat price and have largely everything avaliable, only behind some reasonable character leveling, I would easily recommend this to everyone interested in a great, solid WW2 shooter. The shooting mechanics feel solid, and the infantry weapons are fun to use. Jumping into a game as a tanker is incredibly fun and tank combat feels interesting and rewarding. And if you join into a game with a couple friends, you can have an awesome multiplayer experience that reminds me of the fun I had with early Call of Duty and Battlefield games.
It all falls apart when you actually try to start unlocking new classes, equipment, weapons, and vehicles. The level of grind required just to level up becomes exceedingly tiresome, and it only gets worse when you look at the costs you're required to pay to then make use of that leveling up. You're expected to save several hundred games worth of credits for a single new item, and that's not considering the maintenance costs you pay for repairs and rearming.
That issue has a rippling effect on the rest of the game, as it is not uncommon to get into games that are quite simply impossible to win. A not-insignificant number of my games have been in situations where my team is a bunch of dudes with rifles against enemy tanks, planes, and soldiers with overpoweringly strong weapons. Since I've played a bit and managed to get a second character that is a tanker things have gotten a bit better, but I will still run into situations where it is hopeless as I'm a light tank against medium and heavy tanks, or the enemy has uncontested air superiority and bomb me whenever I try to push forward.
I sincerely hope the developers pay attention to these reviews, because this game can easily be made into something incredible with some simple changes to the leveling and in-game currency requirements. But as it stands, it's a great shooter ruined by an awful grind and pay-to-win tendencies.

SUMMARY: PRO: Good Campaign/ok graphics  CON: Terrible PC optomization and broken multiplayer
That being said, the campaign is splendid, it's the same action packed campaign we have come to expect year after year from both developers. Despite the campaign though, it has little else to praise for however. Multiplayers matches are hard to join despite showing thousands of players at the moment. Frame rate drops constantly and is quite inconsistent a majority of the time. Menus and interface strongly made for console, not PC. Extinction isalright, however, gets quite tedious if playing alone with no real objective other than to plant drills and run trying to exterminate alien hives, and with only one map, it really isn't special compared to zombies from Treyarch. Multiplayer also seems to be broken with NO dedicated servers, poor matchmaking, and unbalanced teams a fair amount of the time. Graphics are good for a Call of Duty game, however, medioce compared to some other recent releases. It is clear that the game was ported from the xbox 360/PS3 version of the game and not the next gen consoles of the Xbox One which is terrible craftsmanship for the game as a whole. It is clear after Infinity Ward lost most of their original founders and members, the company that was left is trying to rebuild it's once great company, but it isn't fullfiling the hole the orignal infinity ward team made and set the bar for Call of Duty games.  In the end, if you have any thought of purchasing "Call of Duty: Ghosts" you should buy it only and ONLY with the campaign in mind. Mutliplayer is broken beyond reason and the game in general is terribly optomized for PC, even "Call of Duty Black Ops 2" had a better optomized por than this. However, for the price you pay, it is hard justifying the $60 dollar price tag.
Pros:
-Great Campaign and ends with set up to the next Infinity Ward Game
-Action sequences plentiful
Cons:
-Broken Multiplayer
-Mediocre "Next gen" graphics compared to more recent releases
-Terrible PC optomization
-Extremely limited graphic settings
-No dedicated graphics
-Poor matchmaking system
-Frame rate inconsistency often\

Having played a few hours of Heroes and Generals once the servers had come back online after repeated DDOS attacks follwoing a ban wave for those found to be cheating, i could do little more then wonder why clocked up as much time as i did.
Right now the game is still in BETA, so some of these misgivings might be corrected in the future.
The game as it stands at the moment tries desperately to become a good shoot/strategy game, however despite it's efforts it falls sadly short.
There are 2 paths to take in H&G you can either be a hero (green coloured machine gun fodder) for which this review is based entirely upon , or a general which adds an RTS element  similar to that found in Natural selection.
As a hero you're expected to march into battle and capture control points for your team which will then in turn give your team resources. When one teams' resources reach the limit that team wins. This gives the game conflict zones which attract players from each team creating some interesting battle scenarios.
there are a few maps out there with a few types of weather thrown in for good measure, and the design from this point of view isnt bad at all.
The game play at times feels little slow and clunky, something that might improve with age. none the less it seemed too obvious and too frequent to constantly forgive. All too often you would move your soldier near a bicycle or jeep and by the time you have the ability to operate the vehicle you've been murdered by a sniper. Control responsiveness also felt distant at times, but then also good at other times.
The game operates a 3 currency system.
hero points - the ones you earn for playing as a hero.
general points - the ones you earn for playing as a general
gold points - the ones you buy for real life wonga.
the hero points could be spent on weapons and attachments for your various items when you accumulated enough of them.
The game also hides its best weapons right behind a paywall (where no amount of hero points will buy these weapons). so it could be considered pay to win. That's fine i thought, however it became even more obvious that the game really wanted me to spend money when even some of the more basic weapons or accessories that cost more hero points than can be accumulated in a reasonable time frame. (whats reasonable to you may differ from my expecations), but having played a few hours of it i found my self not really any better off in terms of weaponry. The vehicles out there such as the tanks could be destroyed using equipment bought with hero points but the price was far too high considering the amount of times you would encounter one.
The game also runs an achievement / medal system which in turn improves your soldiers abilities be it running / damage resistance or hula hooping while juggling with knives. This is a good part of the game. However again i didnt think that the time invested equaled the right reward for your effort.
If you have the time or the cash to throw at this game you might well enjoy it, however i found it to be a bit too demanding for time without the reward to back up your efforts.
Not recommended for now.

I have played every single Call of Duty title to date, and there have been some Call of Duty titles that wasn't better than the last or the same could be said in reverse, but, Call of Duty Ghosts is the first Call of Duty title that simply was bad all around to the point that it was unplayable and not even tolerable.  Here is my first and most important dislike with Ghosts, FOV.  Field of View (FOV) in Ghosts is set to 65 and there is not a way to change that.  The problem with the FOV being set to 65 means the game is so narrow that the game feels that it is taped to your head, and after prolong exposure one can start to feel sick.
Second issue with Ghosts is the graphics and the so called "new graphics engine".  The color and graphics seem very outdated.  Some maps are simply grey all over and no life.  Third issue with Ghosts is lack or equal game type amongst server types, hardcore and softcore.  That brings me to number four.  The forth issue is game modes.  Game modes in this game lack in fun and competitiveness.  Instead of making game modes team based like CTF, TKOTH and so on, they made mostly single player style game modes.
Lastly, game performance.  Game performance in the new Call of Duty Ghosts is surprisingly weak considering the game graphics seem so flat.  There seems to be only two graphic settings and everything between does not make an impact.  I find setting the graphics quality to Extra then everything else on low or off gives the best image quality and performance, setting everything to ultra still looks identical but with extreme lag to accompany it.
So, all of those issues listed and described above makes the game unplayable in my opinion.  I am really sadden because now I have to spend the next two years not playing a FPS game.

A really enjoyable WW2 shooter experience that is highly skill based. It is unique in that battles that are played out in the FPS mode are as a result of what has happened on the grander "Generals" scale - what you are given as troops to use in combat (tanks, planes, snipers, AT, ect) are there because real general players recruited those units and sent them to fight or defend a particluar city. The result of each battle has an effect of the war as a whole, as it could mean the capture of a factory to pump out more tanks for your side, or an important strategic location that will enable your team to funnel into the enemy capital and capture it, ending the war and beggining a whole new one.
As far as progression goes, this game also has a lot to offer. You can have multiple soldiers, each with their own loadouts, training, and unlocks, such as a footsoldier with a rifle and a tank driver with a Panzer IV that you were finally able to save up enough money to purchase.

This game isn't too shabby.  It kind of reminds me a lot like Day of Defeat without the linear map designs.  It can be fun but numerous flaws ruins the experience in the long run.
Things I like about this game:
I really like the large non-linear maps because now you aren't forced to run towards defended areas from one direction which really makes it feel more like a real war zone.  Paratroopers can land behind enemy lines or people can use vehicles like jeeps/bicycles/etc to outflank enemy positions or get to contested zones faster.  Planes and tanks can come soften up positions or help infantry advance.  Spawning can only occur in captured zones.  Graphics are okay and sound is good.  Teamwork is key to victory in this game.
Things I don't like about this game:
Problem is, they really need to balance the planes more which are too OP given that if you have no planes on your side...then you're screwed.  AA guns work like crap, doing minimal damage and there are no other real anti air weapons to speak of.  Once they blow up the 2-3 AA guns per map then you lose if you didn't have or ran out of planes.  Allow the planes to get debris on their glass cockpits so they can't see so well and worsen controls so they can't just dive bomb repeatedly.  You will often have dive bombing planes just sniping single soldiers with bombs while they are running through forests.  That's just unrealistic.  Also they never run out of bombs and reload more bombs too quickly.  That's just insane because of the AA gun issues.
Early tanks are also VERY OP too...only for Americans though.  Then apparently German tanks become OP later on.  Like really this is the biggest complaint of a lot of people and I don't like it either.  It's more annoying given that you can definitely Pay2Win during the earlier stages because apparently you can bring seriously OP tanks to lower level matches if you bought them.  That ruins gameplay and balance whenever it happens since there's no way for lower ranked players to have these vehicles in these lower tiered matches.  That creates completely unbalanced gameplay very often.  It also encourages a lot of people to quit because you will play MANY matches where it's just utterly and completely hopeless.  You just stay for the points.  If you even get them...
The points system works but it has many issues.  Apparently you can only earn your salary if you were in at least half of the match and the rest is performance.  There's no way to filter out matches that are past that halfway point(since matches can be short or long depending on the skill of the players involved in the match).  Spending slightly less than half the time in a match will earn you nothing and it will happen frequently if you look to join ongoing battles to skip the insanely slow matchmaking.  I can't even tell you how many matches that I earned nothing because of this, not even performance points either(16 kills 2 deaths 25 minutes 0 points....What!?).  You can be like Rambo and still get nothing. Oh and if they run out of your class during a battle, then you get nothing unless you had another class that still has forces to that battle.  Then you will get your points.  If not, you could literally play almost the entire match and leave with nothing.  WHAT!?  Usually like 20-30 minutes into the match this will occur if one side has a lot of bad tank/pilot/sniper class players who just routinely get killed and you will be forced to quit the match and get nothing no matter how good you personally were.
I believe another issue is that you literally need to repair EVERYTHING!  You must refill ammo supplies for EVERYTHING!  This isn't a bad idea but the costs become way too high once you buy a few things.  I have no problem grinding to get attachments and new guns, vehicles and the rest of the stuff.  It's just that once you grind a ton of hours to get a new gun/vehicle, you shouldn't have to pay steep repair/upkeep bills on all of them.  This was a real dealbreaker for me.  Once I noticed repair/resupply bills reaching close to what I earn...that ruined the game for me.  You would have to frequently camp or use default gear if you want to grind points again.
Tanks will actually hide and blast you from pretty far away on a regular basis to avoid repairs, which means infantry doesn't get much needed support with their own tankers hiding from repair bills.  German tank operators won't even use their tanks often because of how OP early US tanks are and the repair bills, which seriously ruins the balance of the match onc2e more than half your tank squad refuses to drive their tanks into battle.  Lower tank repairs and create a fog of war or scopes that become dirty for tanks.  I find it ridiculous for tanks to be camping and sniping large distances across the map for entire matches.
Because of the repair issue with my tank operator, I made another soldier class to help me earn more points for the tank operator.  I decked out his gear so I could kill more easily when it comes to my playstyle(smg and rifle, extra mags for rifle, no mags for smg to make it fit and attachments).  I kill a lot of people with this combo and just pick up an enemy SMG first chance I get.  In my opinion, attachments only allow you to fine tune weapons to your playstyle.  Attachments will give some improvements, but take away just as much in another area so it's actually well balanced.  The problem is having to repair attachments as well.  This alone caused me to reach a grind wall with my soldier class.  Repairing my attachments was costing me close to 70-90% of my total points earned on a near regular basis.  Basically I needed to unequip all the attachments to make it possible to grind a reasonable amount of points again.  Which makes you think...why buy them at all if you can't use them to grind more points?
I also don't like how a single soldiers can capture zones.  Some maps are more problematic with this but you will frequently find lone soldiers going way around the edges of the map to get to other points, snipe or capture zones by themselves.  Defending points, thats okay but to capture it should require at least 2-3 soldiers.
Damage reduction badge is dumb.  Only 5% increments(up to a 15% badge) but it totally screws up the balance with body shots when you need to take 3-4 rifle or SMG body shots to down a guy.  If you think about it, if they can survive 3-4 bullets, it's likely because they saved themselves from an additional 15%-60% total bullet damage that they should've received.  That's insane and it reduces gameplay balance.
Bugs like dismounting a bike will occasionally send you 20 feet into the air and kill you when you land, you can't lay prone on a lot of slanted terrains which forces you to do a lot of repositioning, hitting people with a shovel doesn't make enough noise(meaning I have no idea if I'm hitting them or not until the 2nd or 3rd swing and they finally go down), headshotting a tanker with his head out doesn't kill him in one shot(for me anyways).
All in all, the game is decent.  Way too many balance issues right now though.  Planes are OP, early US tanks are OP, later German tanks are OP, anti-air weapons are nonexistant, points system is half broken and flawed, weapon attachments and tanks cost too much to repair, historically inaccurate weapons/vehicles and there is a tiered matchmaking system which allows Pay2Win since you can bring OP tanks/planes/weapons to lower tiered matches.  It's a big issue since one decently skilled tank operator with an OP tank can overrun an entire squad of soldiers and smaller tanks way too easily especially if they didn't start with any planes.  This game needs a lot of work.  The only thing that other people complained about that I didn't experience were the bad moderators...I personally didn't experience any issues there.  Then again, I don't think I ran into a single moderator so maybe I lucked out.

Shiny. As with  other bits of the Far Cry series, Crysis, and Crysanthemum, this one is a very pretty game. There's a nice, spacious world to explore, a story that is surreal and/or creepy at times, but overall engaging, and opportunities to jump in to a dune buggy and go run over three pirates and a cassowary.
There are also navigational issues and interface design choices that should have gotten the responsible parties slapped vigorously with a large fish and ordered to do it again, but properly. There are also moments when a player might be inclined to roll their eyes so hard they risk spraining something and muttering about cockeyed video game logic. Video game logic in and of itself is not a bad thing in games, indeed it is basically mandatory, but it should not jerk players out of an otherwise immersive experience like a bungee cord hooked to the belt of a sprinter in someone's attempt to score a win on America's Funniest Home Videos.
The game also suffers from a condition known as Mighty Whitey Syndrome, in which a white guy kind of swoops in on the more melanin-rich locals and out does them at their own thing to save the day.
It does pass the most important test of a game, though. I'm enjoying it, and I feel no regret about the purchase at all.
Oh, it's worth mentioning that it's got Uplay on it. Ubisoft's game management thingy. It's sort of an unsightly but more or less benign tumour, in contrast to the horrific and often inoperable malignant bowel cancer that is Games For Windows Live.

As of right now I would not recommend.  May update later if things are changed.  Everyone loves bullet points.  Even though long, here are my abbreviated thoughts:
Pros:
- The rare balanced fight feels intense and you get a sense of comraderie
- Realistic other then the weapon damage
- Spawning and capturing spawn points is fun.  you can play lone ranger and try and cap a point behind enemy lines, split your forces to capture two full lines and ensure constant re-enforcements, concentrate everything on the major cap points, etc.
- Free to play... (more on this below)
- Deciding your role (tank, plane, etc.) is cool
- Picking up a sweet gun from a player you killed and turning it back on them
Cons:
- Cheating is rampant (even after the bust).  Nazis will be nazis, I guess.
- Germans either have way better equipment or every decent player plays on that side.  Battles and wars are becoming more and more lopsided the more I play
- As mentioned above: weapon damage is too weak to be realistic.  3 point-blank shots from a rifle to the chest shouldn't leave a guy standing
- Things cost way too much, and the grind is too much, imho.  Right now I'm working on getting a BAR and it will probably take ~30 hrs total to scrape the money together to buy it.  Or I could buy gold at obscene prices.  I think $5 would be reasonable for a gun, but when I have to buy $20 of gold to buy a $7-8 gun, I feel gipped.
- Levelling up takes way too long once you reach about level 7.  There could be more sub-ranks in-between so you at least feel like you are accomplishing something
- Dying: i don't mind dying, that's part of the game.  Some deaths are fun as you can go out in a blaze of glory.  For some reason when you die all the sound seems to....i'm not sure the right word...simplify?  You rush into a room shooting at anything that moves and bullets whizzing by, then suddenly there's a nice, quiet out-of-body experience of watching yourself die from a silent bullet.  I would like to have my deaths have more weight to them.  Right now it's like pressing a reset button, my suspension of disbelief violated, and then respawn.  It pulls you out of the game.
- I fully upgraded my Garand rifle in hopes of many kills and many dollars to buy my BAR faster.  After upgrading (this happens with any gun, it seems) the game has a hard time keeping up.  Before combat worked fine, now with a fully-upgraded gun it seems that all of the new math slows down everything.  FPS will run at steady 50-60 until the gun is fired.  Then it drops to about 25-30.  If there is another player in the crosshairs it drops to 10-15.  It works better to just keep the no-frills weapons.  This can be very frustrating in frantic situations.
Some of these things get changed and I'll be happy to update.  Right now I'm holding on but losing interest.

Alive and well, copious amounts of modifcations exist, brining Warband to a galaxy far far away, to Sengoku Japan, and all sorts of insanity in-between. Hours of hotly contested walls and fields await; just don't expect to be enthralled beyond riding down farmers in the singleplayer.

M&B
An utterly fantastic game!
Many games claim to be "realistic" and to "Give the player control", by which they mean "Players in god mode" and "Perform a QTE". M&B however, has no sort of linearity or rules whatsoever. You are left in a new land called "Calradia" and that's the ONLY thing that the game will determine for you. From there on YOU choose what quests to take, what lands to explore and what Paths to follow.
It takes place in a world view similiar to that of the "Total war" series, in which you only have control of yourself, along with whatever band of mercenaries/soldiers you recruit. Here you can choose where, in the map, to travel, and manage your company.
Upon entering battle, it shifts to a third person game (with the ability to use a first person worldview) with what is, without doubt the best fencing system ever created (consisting of four directions to attack and four to block. The direction of the attack or block being the direction in which one moves the mouse). While in battle, is also given control of the band of mercenaries or soldiers following him, which are split into groups that can be set before the battle, and can be commanded in a style similiar to what would be a thrid person total war game (arguably better).
And one mustn't forget the massive multiplayer maps, allowing over 200 people (This number, however, being very rare) in a single server, and a role-playing and competetive community surrounding the game and a few, select modificaions for it.
As a last note, I'd highly recommend installing the "Floris" mod pack, which can be found here:

It is also worth mentioning this game features the simplest way of modding ever implemented.

The short: Heroes & Generals is a game that until recently actually was quite enjoyable because the tactical FPS gameplay was connected to strategic gameplay on a map of western europe. This has unfortunately been changed and you will now need to either pay or grind yourself past a huge XP wall. Also I would not advice that you spend any money on the game, because you cannot expect that anything you buy will remain accessible to you. (longer explanation below)
The long:
Until recently I would have recommended this game. However not any more as the latest update changed things dramatically. The thing that made this game stand out compared to other FPS games was that the FPS action was tied to a strategic game, where players could send assault teams to various hot spots and try to get the upper hand against the enemy. The FPS action would then take place at these hot spots, meaning that in the end battles boiled down to the equipment given by the assault teams, the number of troops (respawns) given by the assault teams, the tactical play on the map and players skill. The result was a unique game where both the tactical and strategic level mattered. So what changed this?
The strategic map is now an "end game" feature and to get to it you have two options: 1) Grind the FPS games for months (maybe years, depending on whether you are a casual player or not). The XP required to get to the point where you can enter the strategic gameplay is insane. 2) Pay to get access. Expect price tags of 13 USD and above to gain access up ranks that will allow you to command assault teams on the strategic map to a whopping 50+ USD to get access to a brigader general. A brigader general allows you to assign all kinds of assault teams to him while cheaper officers can only assign assault units of the same type as their training (for instance an infantry soldier can only get infantry assault teams, a tank commander only tank assault teams etc.).
The result of this change in the game is that you will now have to wait for several minutes before you can get into a FPS match that takes place on the campaign map. The duration of campaigns has been reduced to just a few days where they before could go back and forth for weeks. The fall in duration I think is because if one side has a few more players who are able to control more and stronger assault teams, then they can easily take over the opponent.
The developers did include a "training" game mode where the teams will be balanced. But if you want truly balanced matches then I think you should consider another game as even though the FPS combat is often enjoyable, you can find other titles out there that simply do things better. The great thing about the campaign map is that it can bring you into situations where you are at a disadvantage, but never without a chance. The great moments were those where you won the battle against all odds. That kind of moment will be much more rare now that the developers has made the strategic map an end game feature.
Finally I would like to offer the advice that if you decide to play this game, think carefully before you make an in game purchase. In other titles I have played the developers has often tried to treat players fairly if they opened up for in game purchases before the game was completed. Even though all of them more or less write into their terms & conditions that they reserve the right to manage, regulate, control, modify and/or eliminate the stuff you can purchase, you will in most cases find developers who care enough about keeping their players happy to compensate the players if they make this kind of changes in their games. The developers of -this- game, however, will do exactly as they please. For instance, just prior to the latest update, I had purchased a few assault teams to be able to participate in the strategic gameplay. Now I cannot use these assault teams because my soldiers are not of the correct level. To get to that level will take me several months of grinding. This means that the stuff I purchased is no longer stuff I have access to. I requested reimbursement from the developers, but their reply was that they was in their right to make this change and didn't owe me anything.

Hero's and Generals is not like Battlefield 1942, Red Orchestra or any other WW2 FPS game I have played. You choose a side to fight for, the choices are currently just the USA and Germany, you fight in parts of a full battle for Europe advancing on small sections of the battlefield at a time. To complete the overall goal of winning the war.
The game itself plays alright the weapons feel fantastic and it is extremely satisfying to eliminate the enemy team, the hit detection is above average when you shoot someone at close range you will always hit them, no matter how high your ping is. At long range however this is not the case, as lag does still have an effect and makes the game near unplayable with a ping over 110.
I do unfortunatly have some major issues with H&G; there are no dedicated servers. This is due to the way the game plays, while advancing sections of the war to eventually win and restart is an interesting idea it fails when it comes to connections, it is simply not ideal to have not have dedicated severs, most of the time I am unable to join matches due to my location and have had to wait long periods of time to get to play.
Another of my gripes is that H&G is highly pay to win/pay not to grind. With certain ammunition being only buyable, for instance once you run out of your initial 60 grenades you have purchase more.
You can control a variety of vehicles providing that you have purchased them with in game currency or real world dollars; this is where the pay not to grind comes in.
While all can be brought with in game currency, to get them you would have to play a minimum of 15 hours for the medium tier, providing your score per minute is 3.
15 hours to get an edge? That SPM is not too hard to get but it is still a heavy grind.
The graphics of the game are not the best but are adequate for the type of game it is and are defiantly playable. There are some problems with the clipping of your character model and the environment, and graphical glitches such as texture loss. This detracts quite a bit from gameplay.
Overall the game is fun but with the P2W nature it makes for a less than pleasing experience. However if this can be fixed I would recommend it, and if you’re up for a grind it still  might be worth playing.

M&B
An utterly fantastic game!
Many games claim to be "realistic" and to "Give the player control", by which they mean "Players in god mode" and "Perform a QTE". M&B however, has no sort of linearity or rules whatsoever. You are left in a new land called "Calradia" and that's the ONLY thing that the game will determine for you. From there on YOU choose what quests to take, what lands to explore and what Paths to follow.
It takes place in a world view similiar to that of the "Total war" series, in which you only have control of yourself, along with whatever band of mercenaries/soldiers you recruit. Here you can choose where, in the map, to travel, and manage your company.
Upon entering battle, it shifts to a third person game (with the ability to use a first person worldview) with what is, without doubt the best fencing system ever created (consisting of four directions to attack and four to block. The direction of the attack or block being the direction in which one moves the mouse). While in battle, is also given control of the band of mercenaries or soldiers following him, which are split into groups that can be set before the battle, and can be commanded in a style similiar to what would be a thrid person total war game (arguably better).
And one mustn't forget the massive multiplayer maps, allowing over 200 people (This number, however, being very rare) in a single server, and a role-playing and competetive community surrounding the game and a few, select modificaions for it.
As a last note, I'd highly recommend installing the "Floris" mod pack, which can be found here:

It is also worth mentioning this game features the simplest way of modding ever implemented.

One of the best example of open world game I've seen so far. If you like the X series for its open world aspect, you are likely to enjoy this game too.
Build your own army and conquer the world by either building your own empire or by pledging allegiance to one of the kingdoms. Whatever your choice, you have to develop relationships with the different entities of the world to be able to rely on them when needs be.
The fighting system by itself is very engaging. You have to command your army on the field but you also have to take part of the mess in person.

Imagine Skyrim meets the Legend of Zelda. You move your party around an overhead strategic map, trading, camping, questing and the like. When you cross paths with an enemy, first-person combat is entered.
The control scheme for the combat is very unique and easy to learn, but hard to master.
If you're looking for a new RPG, but aren't interested in the usual suspects at the moment, you will not be sorry for purchasing this game.

This game is fantastic - definitely the best medieval combat in any game I've played. Its quite simple to learn, but difficult to master. It makes you feel like a real swordsman as you develop your skills. You can fight as an archer, calvary, or as a foot soldier.
The singleplayer is an amazing sandbox experience. There isn't any real story here, but that's fine - it means you can make your own. You can be a merchent, a mercenary, a vassal, or even make your own kingdom.
In addition to the hundreds of hours you could put into the singleplayer, the multiplayer offers hundreds more. It offers team deathmatches, free for all deathmatches, battles (where if you die you stay dead), duels, and my personal favorite sieges, where one side tries to capture a flag in the center of their opponents castle. The multiplayer is where the amazing combat of Mount and Blade shines. The best players are amazing and will defeat you nine times out of ten in one on one combat, but don't think its not easy to get into. Everyone is friendly and if you stick by your teammates as you get a feel for it you'll soon be fighting with the best of them. I highly recommend looking up combat guides for the game - there are fantastic ones out there for each of the three general troop types (archer, calvary, footman).
This is one of my favorite games - I've put more hours into it than Skyrim. I can't recommend it highly enough.

As much as I love this game (and the series as a whole) I have to say, simply: DO NOT BUY.
Is the game fun? Absolutely.
Is it gorgeous? Without a doubt.
Is it a diverse and difficult environment? As much as is possible in an FPS, yes.
So what's the issue?
Honestly, I have very little issue with the game itself.  The mechanics are fun, there's a good variety of weapons, and there's a lot of versatility in how you want to handle any given mission.
My problem comes down the the software.
I have played through FC3 at least 3 times now.  I have a rig that was brand-new when Skyrim came out (so you have an idea of how old it is), but she's a stable machine, and I have no issue running games like FC3.  Unfortunately, because of the hate-god that is Ubisoft, FC3 gamers are forced to utilise Ubi's gaming interface, uPlay.  Unlike Steam (and to a lesser degree Origin), uPlay is not user friendly, and doesn't streamline the gaming experience.
To add to this, Ubisoft offers no real support for any issues.  If you're truly interested in playing FC3, let me recommend to you to go onto Ubi's forums and read about the player's complaints.  I'm not pointing out the complaints themselves--I understand every game is going to have flaws that need to be fixed.  No, I want to direct your attention to the amazing degree of customer service you see from Ubi's support staff.
I can some it up in one sentence: "Please support a ticket."
Basically, if you are having ANY problem with the game, and you've already run through all of the general fixes (reinstalling the game, verifying the cache, that sort of thing), you have to turn to Ubisoft's ticket support system, and you have to wait for a reply.  It may be a few days, a few weeks, or in some cases (mine, for instance) you may never a reply.
So if you have a game-breaking issue (such as CTD on load, as I have), you're stuck with a game that you shelled out good money for, and you can't play.  There is very little that is more frustrating to a gamer.  Except maybe an escort mission.  Forget that noise.
Anyway...
TL:DR: Ubisoft can't be bothered to fix their crap, and FC3 is broken beyond repair.  Find something better to spend your money on.

*Short preview without rants*
I recommend giving the game a go for at least 3-5 ranks.   It's free, stable (more than BF4), not Pay2Win (it's the unlock early kind, not too serious), not Sub2Win, not riddled with cheaters (might feel like it with their modified weapons),  can support every playstyle from Hand-to-hand to Anti-Tank.   Give the game a go, but don't expect high polish of BF4 or scale of Planetside 2.
*End Short Part*
Heroes and Generals is like an old speaker set:   Great Sounding and is a blast but has a few loose wires that simply annoy you to death like bad Dell Speakers.
The game is of the few to throw in some 6k-7k players  in a war governed by Generals (other players) to wrestle control over the map using resources to bring the Hero players into battle.   Generals can essentially deploy troops to a battle, what kind how many that sort of stuff   Sounds good in theory and at the least it feels like it works well ( Not a General) but there are slight annoyances.   As a Hero jumping into a random game, you could end up in what a General might consider " not worth it" or simply didn't fully consider what type of units to send to a battle.   Or you might  end up in a battle without the ability to use your car, too low amount of players ( 18vs18 is the common if not limit).
Worse case scenario is ending up ina  battle where you have only 1 access line to work with and your entire team is stuck behind a river with a blown up bridge ( can't shoot in river, snipers and riflemen constantly shooting, enemy tanks too far to use AT on your equipment, and if oyu had any tanks they would have to take a LONG way around.)
Thats just part of the issues with this game.   Often times you will feel like weapons are unbalanced even though only few are.   Some can be modified to be one-hit-kill weapons.   And don't get me started with the unbalanced tanks...You'll be expected to fully take on Shermans and Easy 8s with a Pz3 that can BARELY pen their sides (makes sense in history, not so much in this game).   Your best bet is to go with others to engage them or flank them.
However despite what some people might have an issue with, the game has several good sides.
Infantry come in an array weaponry and equipment that can be customized to suit your playstyle.
Infantry can also have their own vehicles from a car to motorbike w/ sidecar machine gun and even an IFV that can spawn other infantry.   Also a lovely thing is you can modify the vehicles to include support crates filled with medical supplies, ammo and single-use anti-tank weaponry.
Some people may think the game is too Grindy but I feel like it's near the mid-zone.  It doesn't feel liek it takes forever but you're not gonna unlock every item as fast as others.
There's probably tons of more to say but I don't ahev the time right now.  Give the game a Shot.

*Short preview without rants*
I recommend giving the game a go for at least 3-5 ranks.   It's free, stable (more than BF4), not Pay2Win (it's the unlock early kind, not too serious), not Sub2Win, not riddled with cheaters (might feel like it with their modified weapons),  can support every playstyle from Hand-to-hand to Anti-Tank.   Give the game a go, but don't expect high polish of BF4 or scale of Planetside 2.
*End Short Part*
Heroes and Generals is like an old speaker set:   Great Sounding and is a blast but has a few loose wires that simply annoy you to death like bad Dell Speakers.
The game is of the few to throw in some 6k-7k players  in a war governed by Generals (other players) to wrestle control over the map using resources to bring the Hero players into battle.   Generals can essentially deploy troops to a battle, what kind how many that sort of stuff   Sounds good in theory and at the least it feels like it works well ( Not a General) but there are slight annoyances.   As a Hero jumping into a random game, you could end up in what a General might consider " not worth it" or simply didn't fully consider what type of units to send to a battle.   Or you might  end up in a battle without the ability to use your car, too low amount of players ( 18vs18 is the common if not limit).
Worse case scenario is ending up ina  battle where you have only 1 access line to work with and your entire team is stuck behind a river with a blown up bridge ( can't shoot in river, snipers and riflemen constantly shooting, enemy tanks too far to use AT on your equipment, and if oyu had any tanks they would have to take a LONG way around.)
Thats just part of the issues with this game.   Often times you will feel like weapons are unbalanced even though only few are.   Some can be modified to be one-hit-kill weapons.   And don't get me started with the unbalanced tanks...You'll be expected to fully take on Shermans and Easy 8s with a Pz3 that can BARELY pen their sides (makes sense in history, not so much in this game).   Your best bet is to go with others to engage them or flank them.
However despite what some people might have an issue with, the game has several good sides.
Infantry come in an array weaponry and equipment that can be customized to suit your playstyle.
Infantry can also have their own vehicles from a car to motorbike w/ sidecar machine gun and even an IFV that can spawn other infantry.   Also a lovely thing is you can modify the vehicles to include support crates filled with medical supplies, ammo and single-use anti-tank weaponry.
Some people may think the game is too Grindy but I feel like it's near the mid-zone.  It doesn't feel liek it takes forever but you're not gonna unlock every item as fast as others.
There's probably tons of more to say but I don't ahev the time right now.  Give the game a Shot.

Good game not just another fps shooter.

PROS:
in a new update they have added a higher earning in-game money system. this allows you to buy things a WHOLE lot quicker than before. Also, you can now put  low power scopes on your infantry rifles, giving new player hope against enemy snipers.
New charcter movement making the Game less clunky and more realistic.
New on screen effects like camera shakes from explosions and dirt kicked up from bullet impacts
Realistic balistics (Not sniper elite style but ok) and bullet damage is realistic.
Beautiful overall graphics quality and light settings, soldiers and vehicle models are realisticand game has more color now and the maps have been updated and look way better
Character Progression has been tweak to be shorter allowing characters to reach higher levels faster
A new system has been added to ensure players understand the game before battling tanks and planes
Medics have been added to the game
New flight mechanics improved the game making planes easier to fly.
CONS:
Horrible weapon sounds for: Mosin nagant, SVT-40, Kar 98k, New M1917 and P08 sounds are crap (Plz bring back old P08 and M1917 sounds) other sounds are ok
Many health crates were removed from the game, so you will need to rely on medical equipment on vehicles or medics.
The tanking in the game is basically broken. Tanks are not "rare beasts" that send infantry running. They are either annoyences or free money. A king tiger can be easily taken out by infantry as long as they have a motorcycle and 3 grenades with glue on them. This gives infantry a payday and drains the pockets of tankers.
Same gamemode all the time. Capture the objective or defend the objective, no stealth gamemode or bridge destruction, face off, etc.
All maps are EXACTLY THE SAME 8 total maps. same building textures, same models, same terrain, no destroyed city setting, no Winter maps no Stalingrad, no desert, no urban city, same hollow French buildings over and over again.
Overall detail is non existant (Street signs, ruble, train cars, left behind helmets and gear, burning cars, oil lamps, beds, etc.) NONE of that
Different classes must now be purchased by ingame money or premium currency. You can no longer switch a soldier to a class (such as recon, tanker, pilot, etc.) you must buy the seperate character.
FINAL THOUGHTS:

I must say one of the most complexicating games I have ever played. The game can throw you down into the dirt and it can simultaneously beckon you to ride onto it again. Some aspects of it include the fact that the singleplayer mode is only grea when you apply cheats as when you intially start, it is all interesting and great. You get some basic essentials and enough money to get a handful of peasants. Then you finish the starter game and you realise you are able to take on some bandits and robbers and other riff raff. Then you become richer and realise you can acquire more troops upgrade them to be quite decent and added to your skills such as surgery which help to reduce losses of troops you can have a hefty crew. Add to the fact that you can also decently outfit yourself to take on a few robbers too. But then the wall appears - You are so strong, taking on robbers all the time is just a waste and the only real way to progress is to start provoking some silly Lords. But then doing that can actively put yourself at war with a whole faction which is just great when you have about 50 soldiers and each lord can potential have about 200 or so soldiers and that is just one Lord!!!! This is when you either pack it in and leave, commit yourself to slowly and painstakingly gaining more ground on the faction by resorting to one of few options, following an allegiance. It will work but the politics and minute details in joining a faction is so complicated that it has made myself come to the conclusion of just pressing alt + F4, turning off my computer and just joining some Gym or group to get the same enjoyment. I mean seriously who would spend their time trying to persuade and get on good terms with certain lords and then spend hours and hours leeching power from the faction, marrying the General's daughter so that he can do whatever you want, just to get a measly foot hold on some castles and villages to make your own faction. You would definetly do this otherwise you would get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥by ten lords having 200 - 300 soldiers in approximately three to four days of being able to capture a castle. Yeah capturing a castle is a diffcultly and a half. Try getting some soldiers that don't even know which end of a sword is pointy up against one hundred archers and crossbows that will just waste the lot of them before they run up that single ladder, I mean seriously ONE LADDER to attack. Why didn't the developers think of having multiple ladders? It's just so much easier to defend and seriously if you were the one defending that castle you would get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥by 100 archers anyway, and then get wiped by 50 heavy soldiers if you were just lucky enough to stay alive. Also without any extra mods if you fall in combat the match automatically ends. It can be really upsetting when you are about even - even with the enemy and you just casually take a javalin to the face and you're like... Crap I just lost the match now I have to either run away or load to a previous save and re match. Seriously if anyone is willing to spend some time reading my crap they can learn a whole lot more of what a typical experienced warbander like myself puts up with, enjoys and dedicates their time to. There is also the fact that you need to really practice practice practice practice before you can even THINK about blocking with just a weapon. It's just too fastpaced to do it as a noob. Everyone has to always use shields, but over time you get used to dying every time and you practice and practice and you get it like second nature. By then I ask myself again, why do I dedicate all this time, it's like a skill I have to learn! Neverthless I am not finished moping about the game yet. Once you get over the fact of trying to get one castle you really have to learn how to protect that castle. You need to be some kind of wizard, which I suppose you can be once you level up quite nicely with some faction which you have dedicated so much time leveling up with to rake in hundreds of fresh recruits, taking them to a training place, spending hours to make them from recruit to seasoned knight or foot guard or expert archer or crossbowman, then to go right back to the castle, drop them off so that when some stuckup bigoted lord decides to park his horse right up your castle, you can have a chance to keep the castle you so miraclously and painstakingly won. Politics and domination aside, the actual fighting of Mount and blade can be quite great and boring. Never have I ever felt so much fun trying to master blocking an up hit when I always go sideways block. Quite frustrating at first but then I just laugh it off. It is also a bit annoying when playing singleplayer matches with other lords when you really need a horse to actually survive the match. You can risk getting your head severed by some big burly knight that ravishes you like last night's dinner if you are on foot. If you use your head you can go behind  some of your troops, pick up a bow or crossbow or a pike and fend them off a bit. The mods really make the difference to the game. Having mods such as Diplomacy really make the game interesting, as you can actually have some Automated micromanagement of your Kingdom. It's really great for singleplayer! I never had so much enjoyment sending my Recruitment officer out to get 100 fresh recruits from any faction you want and they come back in about a week and then spend each day recruiting some recruits up to some seasoned warriors, and plus without you doing anything. It's great really to do that. It's also great if you prefer the poltical side of things, such as buying out kings or using other kinds of diplomacy to pave your way. I also found that once you become a king of some scrapple of a kingdom you own, It is highly difficult to get recognised as a king if you attempt to become one early on in the game. You really need to depend on royals and other npc follower characters which can spread some word about deeds you will do so you can gain more right to rule. If you don't have enough right to rule Kings will just laugh at your face if you send them a messenger asking for peace when they are busting your back side with 300 soldiers that are pillaging your poor poor villages. It is quite demoralising when you ask the King for peace and he just casually says, " You want peace? Then trip on your sword." Oh thanks king you just really made my day haven't you? You just promoted healthy living and state of mind for myself. I have a million things to do as King and you are not helping! Essentially, the game becomes your life. You spend most your free days just playing, becoming one with Mount and Blade. Eventually you just get sucked into this Warband Complex and you become that random charcter you been playing all this time. Now, after a brief overview of the Singleplayer side of things, Mutliplayer is really really great if you have a very good patience. Sometimes it just might be that guy everyone calls the "Xbow" who just sits on that corner of the map and has a chip on his shoulder and decides to let out steam by shooting you in the head all the time. Why he always picks on one target I do not know. Or the fact that all the major clans in the game are dead is also another matter to note. Despite that if you are Australian there is always a server up with under 100 ping to play on which the map is primarily set on the "Arena". It's a really small map but that is so great imagine spending five minutes trying to find some guy that ends up killing you with a two handed weapon anyway. This leads me to come onto weapons. They can be unbalanced sometimes, most of the times. Maybe it's the fact that a two handed sword can be nearly as quick swinging as a one hander sword but that's another problem. There is another problem that really annoys me is the lack of experience a whole lot of players have. The players that usually have experience are people in clans. Others just spam you with bows or two handers.

I'm not really sure how to begin this review so allow me to simply summarize my first match- the one where the game thrusts a rifle into your hands and hastily shoves you into combat without even a mention of the controls (it took me 3 matches to figure out how to whistle).
I spawned at the rear-most (and only remaninng) position of a US Motorized Battalion that was assaulting a town. Checking my rifle, I steeled myself for combat.
And was promptly blow to pieces by one of three Bf 109s hitting the spawn with bombs.
These three fighters were continually swooping down to about 10 - 15 feet of the ground and straffing or bombing the hapless infantry below with impunity. I fired a few rounds from my rifle at one and was informed that they 'Penetrated Armor'. Slightly encouraged, I clambered into the gunner's seat of a parked jeep and opened up with the .30 cal machine gun (which fires an identical round) only to be informed that none of the rounds could pierce the aircraft's 'armor' (I'll get back to this later).
In the end, the threat only ended after I took one out with a panzerfaust as it flew--quite literally--three feet off the ground through our spawn area. The other two disposed of themselves by hitting a cluster of trees and the ground, respectively.
My second round was much better--an extended skirimish between German and American platoons equipped only with infantry and a spattering of jeeps with lmgs on them on either side. Perhaps the first round had just been a fluke, thought I.
And then came the third match.
My 'motorized' battalion (the only 'motor' *I* saw was a single motorcycle) spawned without a sizeable town with a river between us and the enemy. There was a stone bridge and a ford to cross with.
And then from the enemy spawn--an enemy armored column.
Two King Tigers and a Panther appeared on the opposite bank of the river and proceeded to shell the living hell out of anything with a pulse and an M1 rifle.
We returned fire with what we could muster--a handful a panzerfausts and a few sticky bombs.
While I can appreciate that not every match is going to be a fair fight, or even winnable for one side sometimes, but this battle highlighted some major balancing issues with the vehicles:
The tanks were such invincible death machines that there was nothing to encourage them to play tactically. In reality, tank require infantry to protect them lest they victim to enemy anti-tank teams and infantry--in urban environments especially.
Here however, tanks merrily parade into enemy held towns, and there's exceedingly little that the typical rifleman can do about it. We can't scamper onto it and drop a grenade down the hatch à la Saving Private Ryan and thought there's mention of 'anti-tank grenades' and 'sticky bombs' I saw only a single person with one. Besides that, there's no way to change equipment during matches, so if you left your anti-tank gear at home, you'd better pray you can find something laying around.
In short, despite the potential for some lethal air-infantry-armor combined arms tactics, most all vehicles aside from bikes and jeeps are so powerful that there's no encouragement to do so, which seems like a shame to me.
In addition, the lethality of the weapons is almost entirely arbitrary. The M1 Garand, firing a sizeable .30-06 round, takes 5 - 7 rounds to the chest to kill someone. However, picking up a bolt-action Springfield rifle (firing the same round, but a weapon you can buy in the shop rather than just recieving as the starter) will take down someone in only 1 - 2 shots.
The bullet drop on all the weapons are ridiculous, and this is especially pronounced on the SMGs. According to the UI, they're zeroed for '50 meters' but seem to putter-out at what seems to be closer to 25 or 30, and they take almost an entire magazine of 30 to kill.
The art style is a bit cartoonish, and exceedingly gloomy. There is nothing shiny, reflective, or even colorful to be found--everything is painted in drab colors, and beyond about 30 yards or so, it's impossible to identify a person. Frankly, the graphics (even on Medium or High) seem akin to the first Star Wars: Battlefront, though not nearly as crisp or with as good of lighting.
I'll continue to play in the hopes of finding the tactical gameplay I'm looking for, but thus far, things have been disappointing. A strong premise, but even in Beta, there are some glaring shortcomings.

As of right now, I can't recommend this game. I expect this will change. There are two major issues currently. 1) Pay to win model that, while totally optional and avoidable does much to destroy a match. I can't prove who is paying to win and who isn't, but there always those suspect players that have superior fully-modded weapons and vehicles and seem downright impossible to live long enough to even find. That's really just a gripe about P2W more than it is about this game, but I feel it's more obvious here than in some other F2P games. 2) The German side is heavily overpowered. I have never played a single game in which players weren't pointing this out. Conveniently there is no "all" chat and my theory is that they don't want teams to chat as it would inevitably be a flame war about OP weapons. However I've seen the imbalance enough in my own gameplay to disregard anyone else's opinion. The German machine guns are wildly overpowered and it seems every german player has them. How do I know they're OP? You can pick them up from a fallen enemy. Typically the only kill streaks I've ever gotten have been with picked up German weapons. The difference is overwhelming. I spend most games as an American desparately trying to snag German guns. Once I find an M42 I can do fairly well for myself.
I like the concept and generally get at least a few minutes of fun out of every match, but when some of those matches can last an incredibly long time being spawn camped by German armor and aircraft, overall it is currently not a game I'd recommend. I will not recommend any of you to buy this game but as you know due to Human rights it’s your choice to either buy this game or not But if you are buying this game on the computer then don't, Seriously DONT!! It’s very buggy and broken and yet infinity ward haven't bothered to really fix the game except lower the minimum ram limiter which previously made it impossible for people with less than 6 GB of ram to run the game. It is also very buggy and I believe that it has more bugs and optimization problems on pc than Battlefield 4(I am using a 680 sli to run this game and yet I am having problems with texture flickering and fps drops for example: from 60 to 20 fps, While on the other side I am running Battlefield 4 fine with at constant 120 fps on a 64 player server). I would never say it but it but it performs much better on consoles but still it’s not worth any of your money in my opinion. After playing the single player with fps drops (and also some texture flickering if you have sli on). I didn’t find it very interesting or engaging like the previous COD and it looked like some parts were a bit copied and pasted from the previous call of duty series which was rather disappointing. I also found it very confusing that I was having problems running this game as my specification can run battlefield 4 on constant 120 fps while I was having problems running this game at 60 fps because as you know this game doesn’t really look anything pretty and complex to run than battlefield 4 ( Nor as Fun), The textures still on areas look poor and also I fail to notice anything that is next generation about this game  except I do notice a very well modelled dog but I am pretty sure that the dog isn’t the cause of this fps drop, To be honest I think it looks worse than the Black Ops 2 which actually had a better art style and actually was fun to play. And there are also problems with the multiplayer component as it seems like the net code of the multiplayer seems broken and also the ranking system seems to be broken. Also another criticism with the multiplayer is that there are a lot of campers and the spawn system seems to be broken, one obvious reason why there are a lot of campers is that the maps are much bigger and contains many places to hide in  than the previous call of duties which kind is on the one hand good but mostly on the other hand BAD. The good that comes out of the big maps could be that there is more challenge finding the players and might feel more rewarding killing them but on the other hand that is bad as this doesn't feel like a call of duty game anymore where it used to be a easy pick up and go shooter in a small map (Which I am not really a big fan of but at least i used to have a fun when I get bored of other games) but now by making bigger maps they seem to destroy the "FUN" factor of the entire multiplayer segment of the game as now nearly every game you join you will find yourself in a big map plagued with campers who don’t even use snipers which is pretty acceptable but with assault weapons and LMG's which seems ridiculous. I also find the “Dynamic Map” pathetic and also a very misleading term as only a few parts of the maps are destructible and also it is also very scripted and linear as the same thing happens every time you perform on of these events. I might as well call it “scripted destruction”. This may not be true but after playing games like “Crysis and Battlefield Bad Company,3 and 4, I am pretty sure that the destruction on COD isn’t “Dynamic” as it feels and looks heavily scripted and also not everything is destructible thus not really dynamic.  The only game mode that I found that was kind of fun was the extinction mode but I didn’t think it was worth the money which I spent to get this, I think this moped would be better if it was a dlc for Black Ops 2 as out of the £39.99 I spent, I am only finding one mode out of the three actually fun and engaging for a while. In conclusion I think Call of Duty Ghosts is just a recycled Call of Duty Game that isn’t really worth any of your money.
