I must say one of the most complexicating games I have ever played. The game can throw you down into the dirt and it can simultaneously beckon you to ride onto it again. Some aspects of it include the fact that the singleplayer mode is only grea when you apply cheats as when you intially start, it is all interesting and great. You get some basic essentials and enough money to get a handful of peasants. Then you finish the starter game and you realise you are able to take on some bandits and robbers and other riff raff. Then you become richer and realise you can acquire more troops upgrade them to be quite decent and added to your skills such as surgery which help to reduce losses of troops you can have a hefty crew. Add to the fact that you can also decently outfit yourself to take on a few robbers too. But then the wall appears - You are so strong, taking on robbers all the time is just a waste and the only real way to progress is to start provoking some silly Lords. But then doing that can actively put yourself at war with a whole faction which is just great when you have about 50 soldiers and each lord can potential have about 200 or so soldiers and that is just one Lord!!!! This is when you either pack it in and leave, commit yourself to slowly and painstakingly gaining more ground on the faction by resorting to one of few options, following an allegiance. It will work but the politics and minute details in joining a faction is so complicated that it has made myself come to the conclusion of just pressing alt + F4, turning off my computer and just joining some Gym or group to get the same enjoyment. I mean seriously who would spend their time trying to persuade and get on good terms with certain lords and then spend hours and hours leeching power from the faction, marrying the General's daughter so that he can do whatever you want, just to get a measly foot hold on some castles and villages to make your own faction. You would definetly do this otherwise you would get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥by ten lords having 200 - 300 soldiers in approximately three to four days of being able to capture a castle. Yeah capturing a castle is a diffcultly and a half. Try getting some soldiers that don't even know which end of a sword is pointy up against one hundred archers and crossbows that will just waste the lot of them before they run up that single ladder, I mean seriously ONE LADDER to attack. Why didn't the developers think of having multiple ladders? It's just so much easier to defend and seriously if you were the one defending that castle you would get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥by 100 archers anyway, and then get wiped by 50 heavy soldiers if you were just lucky enough to stay alive. Also without any extra mods if you fall in combat the match automatically ends. It can be really upsetting when you are about even - even with the enemy and you just casually take a javalin to the face and you're like... Crap I just lost the match now I have to either run away or load to a previous save and re match. Seriously if anyone is willing to spend some time reading my crap they can learn a whole lot more of what a typical experienced warbander like myself puts up with, enjoys and dedicates their time to. There is also the fact that you need to really practice practice practice practice before you can even THINK about blocking with just a weapon. It's just too fastpaced to do it as a noob. Everyone has to always use shields, but over time you get used to dying every time and you practice and practice and you get it like second nature. By then I ask myself again, why do I dedicate all this time, it's like a skill I have to learn! Neverthless I am not finished moping about the game yet. Once you get over the fact of trying to get one castle you really have to learn how to protect that castle. You need to be some kind of wizard, which I suppose you can be once you level up quite nicely with some faction which you have dedicated so much time leveling up with to rake in hundreds of fresh recruits, taking them to a training place, spending hours to make them from recruit to seasoned knight or foot guard or expert archer or crossbowman, then to go right back to the castle, drop them off so that when some stuckup bigoted lord decides to park his horse right up your castle, you can have a chance to keep the castle you so miraclously and painstakingly won. Politics and domination aside, the actual fighting of Mount and blade can be quite great and boring. Never have I ever felt so much fun trying to master blocking an up hit when I always go sideways block. Quite frustrating at first but then I just laugh it off. It is also a bit annoying when playing singleplayer matches with other lords when you really need a horse to actually survive the match. You can risk getting your head severed by some big burly knight that ravishes you like last night's dinner if you are on foot. If you use your head you can go behind  some of your troops, pick up a bow or crossbow or a pike and fend them off a bit. The mods really make the difference to the game. Having mods such as Diplomacy really make the game interesting, as you can actually have some Automated micromanagement of your Kingdom. It's really great for singleplayer! I never had so much enjoyment sending my Recruitment officer out to get 100 fresh recruits from any faction you want and they come back in about a week and then spend each day recruiting some recruits up to some seasoned warriors, and plus without you doing anything. It's great really to do that. It's also great if you prefer the poltical side of things, such as buying out kings or using other kinds of diplomacy to pave your way. I also found that once you become a king of some scrapple of a kingdom you own, It is highly difficult to get recognised as a king if you attempt to become one early on in the game. You really need to depend on royals and other npc follower characters which can spread some word about deeds you will do so you can gain more right to rule. If you don't have enough right to rule Kings will just laugh at your face if you send them a messenger asking for peace when they are busting your back side with 300 soldiers that are pillaging your poor poor villages. It is quite demoralising when you ask the King for peace and he just casually says, " You want peace? Then trip on your sword." Oh thanks king you just really made my day haven't you? You just promoted healthy living and state of mind for myself. I have a million things to do as King and you are not helping! Essentially, the game becomes your life. You spend most your free days just playing, becoming one with Mount and Blade. Eventually you just get sucked into this Warband Complex and you become that random charcter you been playing all this time. Now, after a brief overview of the Singleplayer side of things, Mutliplayer is really really great if you have a very good patience. Sometimes it just might be that guy everyone calls the "Xbow" who just sits on that corner of the map and has a chip on his shoulder and decides to let out steam by shooting you in the head all the time. Why he always picks on one target I do not know. Or the fact that all the major clans in the game are dead is also another matter to note. Despite that if you are Australian there is always a server up with under 100 ping to play on which the map is primarily set on the "Arena". It's a really small map but that is so great imagine spending five minutes trying to find some guy that ends up killing you with a two handed weapon anyway. This leads me to come onto weapons. They can be unbalanced sometimes, most of the times. Maybe it's the fact that a two handed sword can be nearly as quick swinging as a one hander sword but that's another problem. There is another problem that really annoys me is the lack of experience a whole lot of players have. The players that usually have experience are people in clans. Others just spam you with bows or two handers.

The newest entry in the Infinity Ward Call of Duty series takes a big step forward from their last entry, MW3. The single player campaign is one of the best in recent memory, telling a brand-new, interesting story about a outnumbered, outgunned, and invaded America. It also shows of some epic setpiece moments. Plus, you get to play as a dog! How awesome is that?

I don't know why this game got such a low user score on Metacritic because I really enjoyed it.  Sure, it's classic CoD and the gameplay feels much the same as previous CoD games, but that doesn't mean it isn't a fun experience.  Yes, it's mostly linear, but it wasn't advertised as anything else, so it's not like I didn't know that was coming.  My only issue is that it sucks up 30GB of HDD space!
There are complaints about the graphics, but that must be the console people because it looks
on my PC, and I play pretty much every new shooter or action game that comes out.  CoD: Ghosts easily ranks up there with any other current or next-gen graphics engine, with realistic shaders and lighting, and there's an underwater sequence that is nothing short of breathtaking.  There are complaints about stuttering framerates, but I didn't see
of that, so I really don't know where that's coming from, even with nearly all details cranked to maximum at 1920x1080.  There are a few options that I don't have set to max because they don't really make much difference that you can see.  I also never experienced any lockups or crashes, period.  The game runs flawlessly every time.  No drops in framerate at any time either, so again... no idea what people are talking about.  I guess there are still quite a few people out there that just don't know how to set up a gaming PC?  (Not that it's difficult, of course.)
I can't rate the multiplayer because I didn't try it, simply because online shooters like this have become boring the point of being a crime, so I already know what to expect, not to mention that they are flooded with cheaters and hackers only days after release, so there's really no point.  So if the MP component is unbalanced, or has lame maps... okay, fine, whatever.  Let the multiplayer "child minds" rub thier va-jay-jays with glee as they "own" people online with headshots, and complain about whatever they want, but I don't give a crap.  It's also really sad when someone gives a game a poor review based entirely off the multiplayer and never even tried the single-player campaign.
I liked the single-player part, and if you want a good single-player shooter experience, CoD: Ghosts is a fine addition to the franchise.

Now, where should I start.
Firstly I will show you the good sides of MBW (Mount&Blade Warband).
Secondly I will show you the bad sides of MBW.
Thirdly I will tell you my own opinion about MBW.
The good things about MBW:
+ very good combat system (not only hit and block. You can parry, too)
+ very nice community
+ it is very easy to create mods for MBW
+ it is easy to learn the gameplay
+ there are very much (good) mods
+ you can do whatever you want. Be a trader, a robber, a knight or even a king.
The negative things about MBW:
- poor graphics (there are mods to increase it)
- sometimes you glitch through a ladder or something else
- the hitboxes are not 100% done (nearly 90% - 95% I think).
- the shield skill increases the shield size. it is annoying to see how you arrows get blocked by an invisible part of a shield.
My own opinion:
MBW was my first game on Steam and I really love it.
I highly recommend to start playing in the singleplayer mode. As starter you will feel pain at the multiplayer, because the (most) players in Multiplayer are way better then the bots in singleplayer. Find your favorite waepon, train with it and then join the Multiplayer. i needed around 100 hours before I was good enough to survive the multiplayer without getting angry all time. :)
Don't you think that all this "hit, block, parry" could be borring after 100 hours?
If so, you are wrong. MBW never becomes borring. There are so many mods you can try. For example the multiplayer mods Mercenaries (you earn gold for every fight and use this gold to buy better equipment. In addition you can skill in every direction you want and all players have the same level.) or Persistant World (a multiplayer roleplay mod). You don't like the multiplayer? No problem! There are many singleplayer mods like Freelancer or Vikingr.
Finally I only have to say one thing. Buy it! This money is not wasted!

Out of every game I have ever played. This is what I can rate as my #1 favorite game of all time. An amazing medieval sandbox, where you can be a bandit robbing from villages and caravans. All the way to being a great king unifying the land of Calradia.
There are so many types of weapons to use, bows, crossbows, javelins, swords, hammers, axes, spears, they're all viable weapons. And you can use all the different weapons on foot or from horseback. There are so many possible choices to make, not just for your character, but also for your companions. You can customise your warband aswell with the varying army compositions from 6 different factions.
Now, what makes this game so very awesome is just how moddable it is. It adds nearly endless replayability with all of the total conversion mods. Like Prophesy of Pendor, Bryttenwalda, order of the radiant cross. There are mods putting you in Lord of the Rings, China in WW2, the American civil war, Europe during the rise of Rome. Japan during their internal wars. But, if you miss that calradic feel, there are also lesser conversion mods that take Calradia, and just make it more. Like Diplomacy, adding many new features that make the game far more interesting and enjoyable. And if you dislike anything about the game, odds are you could mod it to what you'd prefer it to be yourself.
Oh and another thing. The multiplayer is still very well alive, particularly in the Napoleonic wars DLC. With many clans regularly fighting eachother multiple times a week.
Buy it. Now. And Napoleonic Wars. Just do it.

Far cry 3 is surprisigly the 3rd installment from Ubisofts Far Cry series. This, like the rest of the Far cry games, has nothing to do with the other ones and is totally independent. Now the story is about a bunch of♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥bag young adults who are basically "swag ♥♥♥♥" that go on vacation to the Rook Islands. Once there they get captured by Vaas (guy on cover) and his group of pirates. From there our protagonist Jason Brody, must escape from the pirates and not only survive, but thrive in the islands and rescue his friends. The gameplay is pretty similar to most FPS's but adds a special bend of natural guerilla warfare to the gameplay as youre in an eotic islands with many sharks, rhinos, and other wild animals. There are many collectibles and stuff to collecta long the wide open world and its super fun to scout out the enemy bases and occasionally have animals do your work for you. As the story progresses you meet more characters and get to understand more of their past. As the game progresses Jason gets more distant from his friends as he has become a badass who kills others like they were flies and even says that he happens to LIKE killing because it feels like everytime he kills someone her has a satisfying feeling of "winning" The game features 3 "boss" enemies which you fight during QTE's but its not enough to deter enjoyment from the game. The ending to this game will also give you some feeling on what it must be like to fight to survive, but then have to go back to normal life. The final decission is difficult to choose depending on if you believe a person that has grown accustomed to killing can go back to society. I feel very confident in saying that for me this game is a 10/10. The story, characters, soundtrack, enviorment, and weapons all just stuc with me to give me an experience I wont soon forget. I HIGHLY recommend this game as the story and gameplay are amazing and this game has definately earned a spot on my top 5 favorite games of all time.

They got off with a bad start, but the game is turning into something half decent now. Can't really say, I had alot of the issues other people had, myself. Purchasing this game is a very personal decision and you've got to ask yourself if you're willing to pay for more of the same, just slightly new/changed features. I did and I have quite some fun with it. Extended thoughts below!
The CoD series will never return to their full glory. CoD 2 MP was incredibly well done and the game offered a nice single player campaign back then. When Modern Warfare came out, it boosted the series and it became even more popular due to the modern combat, at least it was more appealing to me after all the years of WW2 shooters. MW2 slightly topped it's predecessor, as it added more to the already awesome game that was Modern Warfare. It went downhill from there..
BlackOps was okay but didn't nearly excite me as much as the MW did, MW3 was just a moneygrab and it all became more of the same.
I was skeptical about the CoD:Ghosts release, expecting more of the same and even though this is probably also true, one way or another this games makes me feel alot like back when I played MW and MW2. What I like about Ghosts is the customization, the way it's done with the perks and attachments being unlocked with squadpoints regardless of your level, enables you to play with your favorite weapons, perks and attachments right from the start (pretty much). Operations and Clanwars are things that keep you playing, given you are in a clan (of at least 3 people) and actively participate in the weekly clan wars. Group up with some people if you want to get more satisfaction out of playing the game.
What's a bit crappy about Ghosts is the optimization, even though I didn't have alot of the issues people encountered, I still feel the game doesn't run smooth, 60fps, but with occasional stutters or a screenfreeze, usually right at the moment you are trying to kill someone. Could get annoying and might get under your skin but it's just a minor annoyance, at least on my part. The hackers on the other hand (that recently started coming in) are quite annoying and reporting them is/feels useless.
If you've been a fan of the CoD series in the past this game is certainly one to pick up (during a sale). Singleplayer is fastpaced and quite short, but that doesn't matter, it's really actionpacked and keeps you entertained the entire way. Multiplayer feels like MW2 to me but alot of 'new' or rather changed features make it a better version of MW2. The addition of integrated clans and clanwars makes the replayvalue slightly higher.

Where do I begin to describe a gem such as Mount and Blade: Warband.
As you might imagine, I am in love with this game, it's the game I always turn to when I'm bored and the game I can never get enough of. (Even if I happen to still be aweful at it).
In Singleplayer you start of as a lonely wanderer, with a personal background that you customise as you enter the game, but I wouldn't bother to much with that, story isn't barely present in the game, it's basically an all out war between 6 factions who all want to rule the land with you in the middle. After a few moments you'll attract your first followers, most likely villagers from some village that urges to join you in your journey, and that's where the game takes off. Wether you swear yourself to one of the lords of the realm or decide to start your own faction by throwing caution to the wind and attack without any other lords to back you up, Mount and Blade will swallow your time.
The first time I actually sat down to play the campaign, I stayed up for 3 days straight, with only brief pauses from the game, they were meant as more permanent pauses, but the urge to do just a few more actions kept creeping up on me. To make it even worse, I listened to The Sultans of Swing - Dire Straits for almost the entire time, as it felt incredibly fitting for mounted warfare as I swung my sabres.
And if singleplayer sandbox combat isn't your thing the game comes with a fantastic multiplayer scene, where there almost always is atleast one server with plenty of people playing the various multiplayer modes. The amount of players have taken its toll a bit recently, but there's still enough players around to get a few good games out. There's, as I said, many different modes, but the one I prefer most is Siege, which puts you in the role of either an attacker or defender of a castle (I know, who would've thought?) and it's really enjoyable.
All in all, this game is a fantastic time sink, especially if you're as easily impressed by swords and bows as I am. Allthough the graphics may be a bit on the bad side if you're some sort of graphical mastermind, but in that case you're missing out.
Tl;dr : You ride horses and hit people with swords in an open world, I like it a lot, so much so I wrote way to many words to describe it.

I've dedicated many hours on yet another Call of Duty game and Ghosts will probably be the last one as it is clear that the franchise has gone as far as it can.  The annual release roll-out has finally taken its toll on a very tired concept and my interest in this game and the series as a whole has diminished entirely.
There is nothing really new or innovative here and many key features such as the theater mode and detailed combat record have been omitted which is a ludicrous step backwards only toppled by Infinity Ward's sheer ignorance towards the dedicated PC community. Everything that is alleged 'new' is actually an existing spin on the current format disguised as something fresh and intriguing.  The maps are very unbalanced and messy and the new modes just mix already seen playlists with tweaks and gameplay changes.  The Create a Soldier function is just the class system rebranded with poxy soldier customisation option that doesn't wash with me.  Console gamers may find it overwhelming but I will not be schmoozed by minor additions dressed up as new and exciting levels of depth.
The game essentially looks and feels exactly what it is; a tiring FPS title. The engine feels a tad better particularly with the slide mechanic but the graphics are dreadful and it is clear this game is still tied to the last generation of dated consoles.
The single player is absolutely pathetic and I don't know why they bother to include a hyped up story that lasts barely four hours.  It's a typical campaign with linear gameplay, bad AI and a cheesy story.  Extinction is IW's laughable take on zombies and it's very tedious and dull even with friends.
The new look Infinity Ward have failed once again to deliver a satisfactory experience with innovation and originality. It's the same old Call of Duty but in now what is a very ambitious gaming market. This aside with the likes of Destiny and The Division just shows how dated and uninspiring this series has become.  Thank god Treyarch are returning for the next game but they will have their work cut out to rejuvinate and reinvigorate the declining franchise. Call of Duty will need a massive leap in all aspects to maintain its popularity for years to come. Ghosts is a new game that was old before it was released.
Activision wins once again.

This is among the worst "polished" games I can imagine, not even fit for the hormone-filled teenagers I suspect it's geared toward, and here's plenty of reasons why:
> Plot - The setup stretches reality from the start, with "complementary" canned, poorly-scripted action and terrible dialog, with few exceptions.  Like me, you might want to stick it out in hopes it gets better, yet it turns into a cheesy shoot-fest and rapidly degrades through poorly-thought-out-and-executed plot twists, pathetic drug-induced scenes, and mystic mumbo-jumbo to match the very worst/unbelievable of any religion humans have derived (and every bit as inconsistent).  Anyone used to a certain standard of storytelling in their entertainment will quickly find themselves annoyed at the game designers--they pull story developments out of their arses, and the smell is vile.
> Gameplay - Whoever stated this game was like "Skyrim with guns" should be ashamed, for that was either a bribed lie or an inability to logically compare two products.  There is no roleplaying in Far Cry--you are conflicted/confused Jason, whether you like it or not, and you cannot alter your fate in any way except the path I chose (to stop playing).  There is only a minor illusion of choice.  Both skills and side quests become pointless, and though I consider myself more easily amused and less perceptive than many gamers, it took me less than 10 hours of playing around with the game to see its transparency.  Choice and exploration only matter if they are amusing and make a perceptible difference.  Even if you manage to finish the game through practiced stubborness, it's clear that playing again with a different style would be even less rewarding.
When the game tries to imitate a Tomb Raider vibe, it fails to present any interesting challenge--much like expecting a biker to be happy with training wheels.  This reminds me of a great example of forced choice: in a side quest where you agree to help preserve the heritage and rebuild the beauty of the temples by collecting tablets, you have no choice but to -blow up an ancient door/wall- to get one of the tablets, even though there should/could have been plenty of other ways to climb the ruin.  Good job preserving heritage!
So many gamers raged against the terrible cutscenes/forced plot in Mass Effect 3, but they were nothing compared to this game's transgressions.  After the 3rd time your character gets sucker-punched by the main antagonist (even if you are a cautious ninja who can't be killed by 100s of lackies) and try to fight him in a drug-trip scene that would have Alice (from Wonderland) yawning in boredom, I knew the game could not possibly redeem itself, and that I did not even care to see the inevitable revenge finish.
It will not take more than a couple camp captures to learn the poor AI and basically be done with that important part of the game (even though they allow you the chance to repeat yourself 30 or more times just in case you're into that kind of thing).
> Bugs - If you like things appearing out of thin air, disconnecting you from any "reality" you're trying to build/enjoy, or mechanics that work fine one time but not the next, then the remaining bugs might not bother you.
Gamers will most likely begin to feel like a rat running through a poorly-designed maze, despite the graphical variety (the environmental design and animation were great, holding promise that the rest of the game could not match).  I wasted yet more time writing this in the vain hope that no one else would be tempted by the reduced price, and can only hope the designers learned that it's better not to make a game at all than make one this terrible (though it will take far more than a cheap price to get me to take another chance on this series).  If you end up learning all this the hard way, then I feel for you.

Animals are far more dangerous than human beings. You have a far better chance going up against four or six baddies arned with AK47 and shotguns than a couple of dogs. The island looks nice but isn't breathtaking - the graphics work well and so does the control system - as long as you don't go into the menus; they are horrible.

Great game! Enough said. But because this is a review i spose i have to talk about the game a bit.
There is an endless world of things  to do everything from traid to training your troops building an empire or just being a bandit.
You can fight for one of five factions all have there perks and downsides, or you can make your own kingdom and become king  of the land with your own faction but be carfull not to make enimies early if you choose to do so unless you fell you are strong enough to take on all the other factions on your own. In my opinion it s best to become freinds with the other factions before you make your own kingdom as to avoid early violence. If you never played the game or seen it played there are "special" people that you can have join your party to fight with youlater on you can make them cammanders in your army by making them vassals you will need to give them lands and a title in your kingdom, but be carfull if they do not like you they may turn on you so fight with them for a time and be freindly. Vassals from other kingdoms may want to join you as well  , you may want to get to know some of the lower or less prestigious members of the other factions as they will be the most likely to defect to your kindom and if they like you more well then they are less likely to leave you as well. When you are a lower level taking castles will be a pain in the butt, but if you have good troops and good tactical skill you can easily take them. Cities are the most dificult to take but are the best as they offer the most land for your kindom. When you take a place over remember that you will need to leave troops there to defend it from the other factions. For castles i only leave about 10-20 guys at first if i have no vassal for it and for cities i leave 40+ depending on who owns the land around me and who i am at war with at the time. To become king of all of Calradia you will need right to rule to get this you can send the "Special" people from your party to pread the word that you will be a great king or by sending vassals to let the other kings know you will be taking over for this to for you need a high renown and honor, to get renown you have to fight in battles with odds not in your favor or against other vassals for one of the five factions, to get honor you must be an honorable gent. When you defeat vassals for other kingdoms you will be given a choice you can take them as your prizoner or you can let them go, taking them prizoner will get you a pay day but it will paint a target on your back for the other vassals to try and rescue there fellow, but it can be very profitable if you can hold onto him. If you let him go you will get honor and he will like you a bit more. If you were to capture the leader of the country you are at war with and let him go you will get more honor and he may even call a truece between your countries, and he will accept you as king later on.
If you just want to be a bandit well that is not as honorable and if you have "special" people in your party most of them dont like to fight villagers and caravans for various reassons, you will also lose honor and the faction or factons that you are raiding will not like it so remember the golden rule in my book the goods you steal need to be sold so dont attack all the factions leave 2 or 3 to sell to.
Well that is my review it turned into more of a "how to" than a review but thats ok. I love this game and plan to log more hours in time. I hope this helps new and old players to becoming king of Calradria.
Ps. if you want to get in good with a faction marry the kings daughter or son depending on Male/Female.
Thanks for reading.

Before we start, I should say that 99% of my experience playing M&B Warband is in the singleplayer campaign, and therefore I am not necessarily the best person to comment on the multiplayer.
This is probably one of the most unassuming games you'll find on Steam. The lack of graphical fidelity and the clunkiness of the menus are immediately apparent, but you won't know just how well this game "feels" to play until you experience it for yourself. Charging an enemy line on horseback at full tilt and precisely angling your spear so it lands right in the skull of a foe is incredibly satisfying, and almost every aspect of the combat is tight, exhilerating, and highly enjoyable. Not sold? Download the demo and try for yourself. Even the somewhat janky siege battles can be a lot of fun.
Mount&Blade: Warband is a crazy deep game, and it can be pretty intimidating at the beginning, especially since many of the systems are not fully explained. But once you get used to the combat, get a handle for how this game thinks, and start making a name for yourself in the fantasy-medieval realm of Calradria, you'll see just how deep, how crazy, and how incredibly fun and absorbing this game is. It is entirely possible to lose whole weekends, or even weeks, to this behemoth of a game, and despite my 500+ hours played I still haven't done everything there is to do.
This is one of those games that you need to put some time and effort into, but it'll reward you in a huge way. There is no narrative or story; you make your own way in this world, and decide your own course of action. And that's a beautiful thing, as it makes M&B:W a great game for role players and game diary writers. You start off in command of a few troops, but before too long you might be a king's favourite general, and be granted land and titles of your own - or better still, you might just be a king yourself! A lot will change as your life in Calradria progresses, but the battles are the constant, the glue that holds this awesome game together.
In short, this is one of the deepest, most absorbing, most satisfying and most memorable games of the past 5 years, or maybe more, and it really is a total package, given the crazy deep singleplayer and the robust multiplayer options. Not bad for a game made by a small independent development team in Ankara, Turkey.

Far Cry 3 is a great game, which is shocking since the first game was absolutely terrible and the second one was less than mediocre. They really fixed all the problems 2 had and improved in almost every way.
Sneaking around is a ton of fun and clearing out outposts without ever being detected is some of the most satisfying stuff I've ever experienced in a game. The enemy AI is a bit overly oblivious at times while still having remnants of 2's superhuman instincts, such as everyone in the vicinity knowing your exact location even if a dog sees you for half a second. On the other hand, stealth is almost the only way to play this game in many scenarios, as you can't really take a bullet that well, meaning going crazy with loud guns, explosives and knives is usually going to end up with you respawning at the nearest radio tower or safehouse.
There are so many guns in this game that I don't think I used them all even though I tried to. Most of them even have their own customizations for further diversity, and that's fantastic. The game did away with 2's gun durability so you don't have to constantly run up to gun shops to get a new one after each firefight.
Exploring the jungle is a bunch of fun with all the delicious collectables, loot chests and animals of many species. I found myself exploring the entire area, clearing outposts and collecting things before I was pretty much forced to do main quests, both due to lack of other stuff and the fact that I had like 15 skill points I couldn't use.
The story I've heard some people say good things about, but it was kind of so-so for me. It was all pretty basic stuff with the exception of EVERYONE on the island being completely demented. I just couldn't get into it.
As of this writing, I haven't beaten the co-op storyline, but I can already say that it's easily one of the game's weakest points, if not THE weakest point.
Overall, you should really consider getting this game if you feel like playing a fun sandbox game about stealth, guns, collectables and scary scary crocodiles.

Great game! Enough said. But because this is a review i spose i have to talk about the game a bit.
There is an endless world of things  to do everything from traid to training your troops building an empire or just being a bandit.
You can fight for one of five factions all have there perks and downsides, or you can make your own kingdom and become king  of the land with your own faction but be carfull not to make enimies early if you choose to do so unless you fell you are strong enough to take on all the other factions on your own. In my opinion it s best to become freinds with the other factions before you make your own kingdom as to avoid early violence. If you never played the game or seen it played there are "special" people that you can have join your party to fight with youlater on you can make them cammanders in your army by making them vassals you will need to give them lands and a title in your kingdom, but be carfull if they do not like you they may turn on you so fight with them for a time and be freindly. Vassals from other kingdoms may want to join you as well  , you may want to get to know some of the lower or less prestigious members of the other factions as they will be the most likely to defect to your kindom and if they like you more well then they are less likely to leave you as well. When you are a lower level taking castles will be a pain in the butt, but if you have good troops and good tactical skill you can easily take them. Cities are the most dificult to take but are the best as they offer the most land for your kindom. When you take a place over remember that you will need to leave troops there to defend it from the other factions. For castles i only leave about 10-20 guys at first if i have no vassal for it and for cities i leave 40+ depending on who owns the land around me and who i am at war with at the time. To become king of all of Calradia you will need right to rule to get this you can send the "Special" people from your party to pread the word that you will be a great king or by sending vassals to let the other kings know you will be taking over for this to for you need a high renown and honor, to get renown you have to fight in battles with odds not in your favor or against other vassals for one of the five factions, to get honor you must be an honorable gent. When you defeat vassals for other kingdoms you will be given a choice you can take them as your prizoner or you can let them go, taking them prizoner will get you a pay day but it will paint a target on your back for the other vassals to try and rescue there fellow, but it can be very profitable if you can hold onto him. If you let him go you will get honor and he will like you a bit more. If you were to capture the leader of the country you are at war with and let him go you will get more honor and he may even call a truece between your countries, and he will accept you as king later on.
If you just want to be a bandit well that is not as honorable and if you have "special" people in your party most of them dont like to fight villagers and caravans for various reassons, you will also lose honor and the faction or factons that you are raiding will not like it so remember the golden rule in my book the goods you steal need to be sold so dont attack all the factions leave 2 or 3 to sell to.
Well that is my review it turned into more of a "how to" than a review but thats ok. I love this game and plan to log more hours in time. I hope this helps new and old players to becoming king of Calradria.
Ps. if you want to get in good with a faction marry the kings daughter or son depending on Male/Female.
Thanks for reading.

The Graphics are nice but of course a little dated now and with my settup appeared very cartoony.. the people that is had thick black borders around them.. the world however was beautiful!
Now the story.. jeeze.. it was amazing BUT.. I found a lot of flaws with it.. to start with the story restarts 3 times.. 3 times you complete it and it takes everything away from you and sends you back to the start only this time something is a little different... I also hated the weird magical mystical scenes.. granted when I'd smoked some weed or had hallucigenic powder blown in my face? great! but then you reach say a boss battle and your transported to some made up magical place where the fight consists of button bashing (really.. you have to mash keys when it tells you to win) at first I did not even know I had killed the first boss.. I thought I was somehow on drugs in fact I still believe I was on drugs.. I swear I killed him while on drugs and he never actually died but after i came around apparently I killed him so you know? ok?

Now I had great fun with this game but I don't know I'm sort of half for recommending it and half for not... right now it feels a cross between original farcry but done as a point and click adventure game..
I've decided after a small break to decide that I'm NOT going to OFFICIALLY recommend this game however I'd like you to be well aware that this is a magnificent game even though there was to many flaws for me to recommend it.. you should buy it if it's affordable to you.. I picked up this game after playing Far Cry 4 on the PS4. I was impressed with that game and wanted to see what else the series had to offer. I was very very surprised because in my opinion - Far Cry 3 blows Far Cry 4 out of the water. Since I've purchased Far Cry 3, I haven't played 4 at all because 3 just...feels better.
The game does a great job of setting up the story in the opening, and I became invested in the characters very quickly. The main character, Jason Brody, is on a mission to rescue his captive friends after they became stranded on a jungle island following a skydiving accident. This is a really compelling mission, and I, as the player, felt really motivated to save them.
I'm not good at starting and finishing Single-Player campaigns (the last one I finished was The Last Of Us Remastered over the summer), but I was hooked into this one from beginning to end.
The gameplay is very fun and feels very responsive. Seeing how many guards you can silenty snipe before they alert the rest of the outpost is intense and rewards smart playing. There are plenty of customizable weapons and I always felt like I had options. There are many fun weapons as well (namely the Flamethrower).
Gunfights are fun and feel fair. I was rarely frustrated (except for the damn heavy soldiers).
Anyone who is worried about missing elephants and other improvements from FC4, don't be. I didn't miss them at all.
The ONLY negative thing I have to say about this game is the occasional overuse of "trippy" drugs. The island natives occasionally give drugs to Jason to make him realize things from their perspective, and they lead to many many cool hallucination sequences. However they end up using this effect in a boss encounter or two and it takes away from the satisfaction of the fight. I would have preferred if they stuck to the realism a bit more in the boss sequences.
I highly recommend this game if you like FPS games, games with a good storyline, or wanna see what the Far Cry franchise is all about for a good price.

There are some things they need to sort out with this game, but I like it.  The bad is, if you want to play with a friend you have to level the same way.  You cannot always play in the same game if they are recon and you are a pilot for example.  So if you follow a different leveling branch you cannot create a squad and play together consistently.  Currently there are only 2 factions to play (American & German), but I hope they will add more.  That's not a big deterrant, but it just gives you less options.  Players who pay for weapons can have a huge advantage off of a newcomer to the game.  After you level up that difference can be negated, but it's just something of which you should be aware.  The games you join are random for the most part.  So you can join a game and can be completely over matched, but you cannot leave and join another match.  So I like the fact that people cannot game hop.  It's annoying when you are winning, and everyone leaves.  My issues with this is if you drop into a game where they have planes and heavy ground support and you have neither, you will not win.  So you may spend 30 minutes of your life in a game that is incredibley lobsided.  Speaking of lobsided, I don't know what the difference is, but the Germans win probably 80% of the matches I've played.  I've played some on both sides and it holds true no matter what team I'm on. You can upgrade your weapons, but most of the upgrades have as big of a downside as they do an upside.  So it almost pays to leave your weapon as is and not modify it.
I like the maps, the guns, and the idea.  More things need to be added to make ist a really good game.  Hopefully when it's ready for release they will have addressed all those items.  There is nothing like hiding behind a rock you can clearly see over, but cannot shoot over.  Little things like that I'm hoping they clean up for us.

was developed by Ubisoft Montréal & Shanghai and published late 2012 to great ciritcal acclaim. I played it only recently (early 2015), but even though some years old, this game feels like it was made recently. As the third installment in the famous
franchise, it continues upon the open-world orientated gameplay establised by
, while fixing almost all of the problems that game had and offering a feel and way of playing all of its own.
The game makes one identify to a degree with Jason Brody, the playable protagonist who is taken captive together with his friends on a tropical island by a gang of pirates lead by someone called Vaas. The opening sequence of the game, from the initial cutscene with the rather vainly partying friends up to the first encounter with Vaas and the escape from his claws, stands out as a classic way of making clear what a game is all about. Vaas is a sinister character, as dark and evil as one could imagine, and more. His fascination with utter violence and the madness of the human mind offers some memorable gaming moments, that made me stare at my screen in utter disbelief and will stay with me for a long time.
Jason Brody starts out as a rather unsure would-be-hero, who is shocked whenever he sees someone killed, and who is very reluctant to kill himself. But his encounter with the sheer evil of Vaas and his fellow criminals, gradually turns him into a killing machine, with only one goal: to free his friends, and ultimately seek revenge. The game cleverly underscores this development by offering some role-playing element: finishing missions or killing enemies grants experience points and levels you up so that you can acquire several abilities which help to overcome obstacles more easily. While the game is rather challenging during its first hours, with raising in level and acquiting more special abilities and better weapons it gets easier, which helps to get the idea of turning into a mean killing machine rather well.
Apart from Jason Brody and Vaas,
contains several interesting and even unique characters along with three "factions" spread out on two distinct islands. There are too many characters to mention them all, but standing out apart from Vaas is Citra, the priestess of the natives who introduces an almost palpable sexual, brooding tension into the game. One of the best parts of the game is the excellent voice-acting: every charachter, how odd or sinister, is made completely believable through his or her voice.
The world itself is huge: longer journeys can take up to ten minutes, even by car, jeep or boat (of which there are several types). All in all, the story is not only gripping and very well told, it is combined with the freedom of an open world in a very convincing way. You can play this game in several different ways, the options being almost limitless. Following the main story is a valid possibility, but I found it more interesting to divert from this quite often, roaming around in the astoundingly beautiful world in order to capture an enemy outpost (either by force, stealth or cunning, the choice is once more yours!), gather some useful plants or just hunt for animals (who offer several rewards as well).
Apart from the 38 missions in the main storyline, there are over two hundred (!!) side-missions, ranging from stealth kills to hunting specific animals with a specific weapon, trying one's driving skills in a race, climbing communication towers in order to reveal parts of the map or even playing some poker. The amount of gaming hours to be got in singleplayer alone runs into several dozens or more, comparable to a game in that other famous open-world franchise,
. I tried the multiplayer as well, but the servers are almost empty by now, alone the rather bland co-op still offers some possibilities.
Apart from the amazing game- and gunplay, the game is a prime example of state-of-the-art graphics and sound, excellently optimized and hardly showing that it was primarily aimed at consoles. It runs flawlessly on my 7-year old pc with a 2,66 Ghz cpu, 4 GB ram and a GeForce GTX 650 ti. All the expected options and tweaks for optimal performance are there, but it has to be said: the game does look much better on the highest settings (very high or ultra), so even if it costs you some fps, do try those. The one thing that could offset several players is the mandatory use of the "infamous" Uplay, a platform that gets huge criticism more often than not. However, for me Uplay just works fine, not only in this but in every other game I played on it. Granted, the achievements are a bit pointless since they don't show on Steam, but the possibility of unlocking extra content by gaining U-points in quite nice. Apart from that, the few dlc packets for the game are completely superfluous, but that's a very, very minor criticism.
Anyone interested in the recent developments of first-person shooters or in the way a modern game can tell a story in combination with an open gaming world, should buy and play this game.

Now that I have finished the game. I stand by my original opinion. The single player feels like it was stiched together from cutting room floor cast offs from previous titles and glued together with a weak story. By this I mean, you are supposed to be playing as a Ghost, a stealthy, covert, deadly force, for 3/4 of the game you aren't even a Ghost, nothing is stealthy nor are you a force to be reckoned with. After you do become a Ghost you are slapped around like a little ♥♥♥♥♥, the missions are all about running and hiding and don't fit with the Ghost story told at the beginning. Further there is far too many resources squandered on the dog, Riley, whom you can control through a computer system (but only when scripted) somehow this huge German Shephard is so stealthy he can crawl right past enemies unseen, he is taken from you on the beach mission and then randomly reappears near the end of the game *spoilers* when you have to carry the poor pup to safety. This part feels like it was tacked on when they realised the game was far too short. (As it was, on hard I finished in 7 hours, this is with all the dying I was doing due to the sudden and random frame drops, had I not had to redo so many sections I am confident I could have finished in under 6 hours) Even without Riley on screen if you've turned the dog effects up, you will have random and sudden framedrops. While playing you are so forced where to go, the game may as well have been on rails. You cannot even choose a path through a fountain, you have to go around it, funnelled down a road where the crappy enemy AI can shoot you. They do not aim, the bullets just magically find you if you are to the remotely in front of the enemy. I had one facing almost totally away from me, only to have him suddenly facing me as I crept closer, I am not saying he turned, or moved to be facing me... he was just suddenly facing me gun up and firing as if he had been the whole time. Rarely do you actually get to make a choice or go off on your own and when you do it is all too brief. Your teammates take priority forcing you out of the way through doors, or pushing you out of cover if they are scripted to be there. But all for not as they couldn't hit the broadside of a barn. Back to the performance issues from my original post, with third party hacks and some doctoring of the game I was able to get a playable (solid) framerate, decent FOV and proper multi monitor support, however I CANNOT use this in multiplayer, so the game is still broken. PC Gamer reports having it run great (100fps) on dual TITANS (single monitor), however, this is stupid for this engine, dual 650's or dual 6850's should run this engine that fast. Dual Titans, 780ti, 290X's etc should run this game well over 100fps solid on nVidia Surround or AMD Eyefinity, dual 7950 should be able to get a solid 60fps. As I said in my original post, this game bites... CoD is all but dead and hopefully it finds its way to the grave soon. I will no longer be purchasing any CoD title (on PC or Consoles) even if this was in the bargin bin I would tell you to steer clear.

PROS:
Concept: Pretty nice concept for an older version war game.
Maps: You get to travel around the maps in Tanks, Planes, Jeeps, Bikes, Run and or Swim.
Teams: You can create characters either on the US or German side and build them up the more you play.
CONS:
P2W (Play2Win): You can continue playing the game and eventually get the Tanks, Guns, Planes and other equipment but it takes a very  long time to get there. Expect to invest 100+ hours. Or, you can just purchase the items with real money and buy what you want. And trust me when I say you will be spending a hell of a lot of money to do it. This is a very expensive P2W system.
Enemy hit box: The enemy and vehicle hit boxes needs work.
Match Making System: The Match Making System needs  a lot of work as it feels unbalanced.
1 Shot Wonder: Expect to be 1 shotted a lot in this game. (1 Shotted, re-spawn, go into battle and engage enemy, 1 shotted again, re-spawn, go into battle and engage enemy again. Over & over & over).
Hackers: There are hackers in this game but not as prevalent as some other games out there.
So a good rule of thumb. If you're interested in an Early Access game, regardless if it's Free2Play or not, you should go in expecting the worst. Normally, these Early Access games are usually just trying to get your money and there are many out there. In the future just *YouTube* and watch the game play of whichever game you are interested in then read the reviews to make a logical decision.
As for this game, it needs a lot of work to get it where it needs to be.

The best word I can use to describe Far Cry 3 is "shallow" -- shallow mechanics, shallow world, and an extremely shallow story.  The game is, at its heart, an FPS, yet it tries so desperately to reach out of that genre (for whatever reason), that it attempts too much and accomplishes little.
The crafting system consists nothing more of harvesting 1 of 5 plants, or killing an animal, and potentially combining it with another one.  Non-plant crafting can be maxed within the first half of the game, and the plant crafting gets pretty annoying.  I do not want to go to a menu and craft a "run faster" syringe -- it would be faster for me to just ignore it altogether and keep running.
The world is massive, yet there is not much to do other than shoot at things.  This is fine -- like I said, the game is an FPS -- but the reviews and commentary on this game led me to high expectations.  The radio tower "puzzles" are more annoying than thought-provoking, and are often only failed because you overjumped a ledge or missed some dangling rope.
That said, the graphics are absolutely stunning.  The island is a paradise that begs for you to immerse yourself in it.  There are caves to swim in, hills to climb, and jungles to explore.  There are animals, plant life, and people (both friendly and otherwise) populating the island... which just makes you realize how little you can actually do to interact with them.
The story is predictable and unimaginitive, and doesn't contribute anything to the genre.  This may have even been the first game where I really took issue with the voice acting.  The lead character sounds like he hasn't quite left puberty, which makes all his "heroics" all the more lackluster.
I can't help but compare this game to Fallout, and perhaps that's what led to my disappointment.  Far Cry 3 reaches for the stars and falls short, wandering around an island no one wants to be on.

Bits and pieces are true form most other posts. After playing for 9 hours I can tell you a few things.
1 You will spend a long time grinding for most things in the game.
While some people will not mind most will. You will need to spend at least 6-8 hours to unlock the bazooka. There will be maps where you are still new and you will have to fight the other team who has tanks. The funny thing is first you have to unlock it and you think, great now I can kill the damn things. Yes and no. now you have to pay 28500 in game credits to buy it. It gets better, now you have to pay for any ammo you use (same for grenades). The ammo is not cheap.
2 If you buy anything for one soldier you cannot use it for any other soldier.
The thought behind this is they want you to make a soldier that is for one thing. I.e. one for just troops(rife man), one for just fighting tanks (AT), and one for support (MG). It’s a nice thought, but as it stands you have to buy each soldier slot (7100) then you need to use that soldier to unlock everything again. (Like I said you will spend a long time grinding.)
3 They will even tell you that some or most battles will be lopsided.
As I said before you will be put into games where you are new (just a rifle and a grenade) have to fight tanks. The only way you can kill them is with a bazooka. (Remember you are new and haven’t unlocked tanks or airplanes yet.) It will be a test of patience to get through the match, as they will just steamroll you from the start. The sad part is even in the small domination style games you can have a jeep with a mounted gun on it. While it won’t dominate the game it makes it that much less fun dying to it and not really having a chance. Mind you this in all in the random game choice. I did figure the other find mission choice out but you spend all your time in queue or there was no one in the games. Most people have higher level guns and equipment in most matches.
4 If you want to unlock anything faster than a snail you will spend real money.
Kind of like I said in the first part you will have to grind like hell for anything. It’s not like I’m a bad player or I’m butt hurt case people can kill me. In most games I played I was 10-4, in some really lopsided game I was 21-1. I only got around 3-4k points each match. Also like I said you first have to unlock the item you want then you have to pay for it. Also remember what I said in point 2 you can’t use the gun for any other solder just the one you bought it for. Your rife ammo is free but everything else you have to pay for.
5 Most servers are not In the US
I had a ping of 120 in most cases. It was not my internet, I get 100 Mbs download. Although I didn't see much in the way of lag. (Just thought you might like to know.)
All I can say in the end is you can have fun with this game IF you want to put many hours into it. I will never pay for anything a free game (my choice) and you will never have to for this game. (Other than some camos for your guns.) The VERY clear option is to pay real money if you want to start doing well without 20+ hours for just two or three soldiers with enough firepower to kill more than just infantry with a starting gun. I can’t say anything for tanks, airplanes, recon or generals I got close to unlocking tank crew (2478-3000) but I don’t want to spend that much time in this game. The gun play is similar to red orchestra but better in my opinion. It’s a slower pace than BF4 but faster than Arma 3. Did I have fun with this game? YES. Although with as much time as you have to put in before you can play all aspects of the game it’s not worth it to me. If you don’t mind putting hundreds of hours into a game before you can play all of it this is the game for you. I will more then happly come back and play when I don't have to put so many hours in to just unlocking the gme before I can start playing the game. Also for people who are looking for answer to the question "Is it pay to win". No. But I like the way one You Tuber put it its pay to advance.

You can read any number of other reviews that are going to discuss gameplay, and the story, and the crafting system, and all other aspects of this game.  I've got what comes down to one very simple reason for loving this game, and that's the towers.  Spread through Rook Island are eighteen radio towers.  Each time you climb a tower you unlock the map of the surrounding area and get some free weapons and such.  So, what is it about the towers that makes FC3 such a joy?  Although identical in structure, each tower has been damaged to some degree, making each tower a unique mini puzzle, figuring out where you have to jump and climb to get to the top.  It would have been so simple to make each climb identical, just a simple cookie-cutter pattern, and 99 games out of 100 would have done just that.  FC3 went that extra mile, put in that added touch.  That's what makes this such a great game.  They thought about it, thought about what we'd like, what they'd like as gamers, and implemented it.  I don't say this often, but good going on this one, Ubisoft.

First-person medieval combat done right is a wonderful thing. I've played a couple of titles like that at this point, and this is easily one of the better ones. The strategy overlay, while oppressively simple, still does well enough at fleshing the game out in between moments of fighting. The difficulty, when set high enough, can be pleasantly relentless even for someone with snap reflexes.
It is far from perfect, of course, and the textures tear and go haywire regularly. The AI is abysmally stupid and simple-minded even on the higher settings, leaving you feeling a little out of place from their utter lack of reaction or real tactics at all.
To keep it simple, if the idea of mixing part RPG and strategy with great medieval combat sounds good (you can play with a decent assortment of weapons and armor) the game is enough to warrant trying.

After playing Far Cry 2 a few years back, I almost expected this game to be exactly the same. This game surprised me by managing to feel fresh, even though it is similar to Far Cry 2. The first thing I noticed is that the game is much easier than the previous title. It is rare to encounter enemies outside of their designated bases. I played the game for the first time on hard mode, and it was mostly a breeze. The only parts that were challenging were some of the scripted missions, but even those were easy because of the combination of skills and equipment that I unlocked. I was stealthy for the first half of the game, but after a while, I didn't even bother any more because I was powerful enough to casually destroy enemy bases.
The story is another thing that surprised me. I felt that it was lightyears ahead of Far Cry 2. The acting was good, and unlike other FPS stories, I always understood what was happening and I did not just have rely on the waypoint markers to figure out where to go next. My only complaint is the Batman Arkham style dream sequences that happen. I just did not find them to be believable. Also, I have almost no respect for the main character because he is clearly in the middle of an identity crisis. He thinks that he "found his calling." Well, you'll see.
I got this game for about $7 on a sale a while back and I feel that it was worth every penny. It took me nearly 20 hours to complete, with most missions complete and all skills unlocked. I do recommend this game if you are looking for a different kind of FPS game.

If you are a real fan of CoD this game is pretty much a progression of the series, in other words, you'll like it as much as any other CoD
The game is not very optimized, true, but compared to so many other so called "next-gen" games around it runs pretty damn well on my 3 year old PC and my 2 year old stock AMD 6970. And I mean 50 FPS stable, 30 in huge vistas, after just a few minutes of tweaking the many options in the graphics menu and shutting down the physics-heavy fur, you would need some serious power to run that just like anything with nVidia Phsyx or anything similar. The new graphics are very well implemented IMHO, they don't block at any time your ability to see your target with flashy cinema-camera-like features that don't even seem like a soldier's eye at all, all the while being pretty nice to your human, real world eyes.
When I bought Black Ops 1 some years ago my processor didn't run it, but I stayed shut and bought a newer one instead of complaining to the devs about their attempt to improve the game. The game even had a graphical glitch that used to crash the game once every while, but I just waited and after a month they fixed that. People just need to get used to tweaking the options in the menus to fit your machine. You can't max everything forever.
People say they have no creativity, but I disagree. They are being very creative with what they have and they have to remain true to what their game is, otherwise it's not going to be CoD any longer. They don't have to and shouldn't be trying to be like any other game. There are so many cool games out there, each one has their own approach to FPS. This is CoD's. If you don't like it, good (or bad) for you, go play some other game, nobody is forcing you, dear example of hater, to stay here, even less to complain about it.
From what I saw, the whole campaign and a bit of MP, the game is sweet.
Epic, unrealistic, Hollywood-like scenes just as every CoD since the fourth. I never before had paused a game because of a para-drop, but for heaven sakes I was not expecting that! It does not try to say at any time it's being realistic, and it's great that way. You embrace the epicness just like you would embrace Halo's sci-fi epicness or any Hollywood action movie's epicness. And yes, it is the same on-the-rails shooter just like most others around. If you don't like this kind of SP gaming, go search something else in the not-so-long list of (mostly great as well) open-worlders.
Since i've been bogged into finals and stuff, I couldn't play MP properly, against players. But the AI MP I tried was great. The bots are smart, much better than the CSS stuff I've got used to. I was actually surprised when one of them jumped to dodge my rounds. All other MP features felt like improvements over the last few games, such as cool maps that embrace the best of CoD's frantic CQB combat, an easily accessible scoreboard that doesn't crash my keyboard for pressing too many buttons, cool new balance/usefulness-focused weapons (rather than a huge rooster of rifles of which only 2 are good due to little care for balancing), interesting point reward system, and, for me, the list goes on and on.
People that compare this game to BF4 are crazy IMO. They are different games with different ideas and very different graphical engines. You can't just create an BF4 engine in the span of a year to add to your game. They needed at least 3 years of work together with several studious to make the first frostbite in 2008, more five years of improvements and investment got them their engine's third iteration, which is great. Yet, their engine is carefully tailored not to require any graphical options that might be too heavy on any machine, they save on textures and occlusion and exaggerate the lightning to mask  that. In a certain way, Ghosts' engine is technically heavier than BF4's. Just look at the requirements: CoD's minimal asks for double (1024 Mb)the VRAM and 6 Gbs of RAM next to BF4's 512 Mb VRAM-4Gb Ram minimum. People often don't understand that kind of thing and start jumping to conclusions.
Every game comes out with a few bugs. If the guys from other companies had the idea of making open-betas, great. But if there where none, for whichever reasons, don't expect a perfect game right off the bat.
From what I could see, this game is a logical improvement over the last. When you go to the cinema to see LOTR 2 some years after you saw the first, you have to expect what's obvious: the continuation of what they promised you with some Visual FX improvements. The game delivers much more than a disguised launcher update and a map pack, it's a whole new piece of juicy shoot-em-up impressiveness. I don't know what all those hater-commenters where expecting when they bought the game, but it delivered just what I've got used to expect from a CoD, and it was GREAT!

A visually stimulating world packed full of jaw dropping moments thanks to the incredible character acting and voice acting. You’ll never be left wanting from the moment you watch the first cut scene to the explosive final moments of your journey. The islands are teeming with enemy bases to commandeer, rare animals to hunt down and sights that will keep you enthralled for hours on end.
You are tasked with playing the role of a young, extremely energetic man named Jason Brody. You find yourself and 6 of your family members/pals trapped on a fictional island called Rook Island which is situated near Papua New Guinea. The island is chock full of wild life, pirates, exotic plants, hidden caves, waterfalls and small villages to name just a few attractions. Rook Island is completely at your disposal pretty much from the get-go. It’s up to you to decide how you utilise it.
Far Cry 3 begins with you and your friends having an awesome holiday together, frequenting bars, beaches, getting into fights and eventually being convinced to undertake the bright idea of skydiving. Accompanied by M.I.A.’s Paper Planes, you are shown a montage of the Brody Bunch & co. having fun and then hurtling through the skies in skydiving gear. Just as you think you’re about to see your group land, the footage you have just been watching is revealed to have been playing on a phone in front of your face. A young, sunken eyed, scar-faced man with a mohawk and red clothing is shown to be the one who has been dangling the video through the bars of your cage for your viewing. As Jason Brody, you look around the cage you have been confined to and see your older brother Grant tied up to one of the pieces of bamboo which structure the cage.
He wears a nice smile, but deep down he’s twisted beyond repair.
The foul mouthed pirate then goes on to give one of the best acted scenes in computer game history, forcefully instructing you and Grant that he’s the one in charge and that he’s planning on ransoming you for a handsome profit. After being called away by another pirate, you learn that your captor is named Vaas (superbly acted and voiced by Michael Mando). Vaas leaves you and Grant in your cage but Grant, having been in the US Army Reserves, proves his resourcefulness by escaping from his bonds and moving over to free your own hands.
From here you both go on to make a daring escape through the pirate village and at the same time become acquainted with the controls of the game. Having reviewed Far Cry 3 on a PC I can say that the controls are as intuitive as you could hope.
I won’t go on to reveal anything else that transpires during this introduction to one of the most awe-inspiring games you’ll have played, but I will go on to detail the features of Far Cry 3 that make it such an excellent experience.
Far Cry 3 is littered with gun fights, vehicle races, treasure hunts and a plethora of other fun features that will keep you occupied for hours. To progress through the story line, you are presented with a yellow exclamation mark on your map indicating where to go or who to talk to in order to move on to the next part of the game’s wild adventure.
For those who prefer to whiz through the game without looking back, you could easily finish Far Cry 3 in around 15 hours. For completionists you’ll be pleased to hear that there’s a generous provision of side missions to extend the game’s value past 30 hours. I personally took my time by enjoying every single moment and finished the game in 49 hours. It could easily have been more if I decided to collect every treasure, relic and get a high score in every trial.
Speaking of side missions, you have many options to choose from…
Radio towers scatter the map that, when climbed and activated, reveal a section of the island on your in-game map. These towers can prove quite challenging to traverse and if you slip and fall, you will most likely die. But don’t worry, you just have to start again from the bottom of the tower. Treasure chests can often be found along your climb that award you with money, items and ammunition so keep your eyes peeled. Once you reach the top, the camera display will zoom out and show you places of interest that surround the towers and also unlock a section of your map to display the land and it’s secrets. You’ll also unlock certain weapons that can be freely acquired from vending machines when you scout the towers.
Pirate camps are also littered around Rook Island, and as the name suggests are controlled by pirates. To appropriate these camps, you can go in guns ablaze or prefer to take a stealthy approach. The main goal is to leave no pirates standing. If you are seen, the pirates will become alert and can activate alarms which summon extra squadrons of pirates in vehicles to your location. You will need to eradicate every pirate in order to raise the flag of the native people to this land and wipe out the pirate presence. Rewards come in the form of extra XP by appropriating a camp without being seen, so stay out of sight of those pirates and keep it quiet.
If you were to unlock the entire map without picking up any treasures, you will see just how many relics, chests and the like are waiting for your discovery. Treasures can be found around buildings, in amongst trees and rocks, underwater or in hidden caves to name just a few locations. They act as a way to earn extra XP, money or items to sell for monetary gains. Going on treasure hunts can be incredibly fun, especially if you have to dive down a great big hole in the earth into deep, dark waters. Climbing back out is the tricky part.
All sorts of challenges await you on your travels throughout Rook Island. Courier missions will have you pilot a selected vehicle and pass through certain check points to reach the recipient in a set amount of time; Time Trials allow you to drive yet another selected vehicle and follow a path laid before you until you reach the finish line; mini-games such as darts, poker or shooting ranges and more. The massive amount of gameplay hidden throughout Far Cry 3 is astonishing and manages to keep you interested for a long time.
Trials of the Rakyat take the form of a small ‘instanced’ area where you are tasked with getting a high score by killing enemies with a provided weapon in a set amount of time. Large red rocks can be found throughout Rook Island that transport you to these trial areas. By activating these rocks, you will be shown the requirements of the specific trial and the points you need to get to attain a high score. Some of these are great fun, especially the one which gives you a car to squish pirate after pirate with.
After taking control of a pirate camp, a job board will become available. You can pick up hunting or assassination jobs from these boards. Hunting will task you with seeking out a particular animal and disposing of it using a certain weapon. Assassination jobs will require you to find a specific pirate and kill him with your knife. However you’ll need to stay hidden if you don’t want a fire-fight to erupt. Each side-mission will award you with XP and money, so make sure you get out there and earn that moolah!

While I am not one of the guys with several hundred hours worth of gameplay, I can reasonably say that this game got me hooked.
Yes... While my best unit is only at the sixth rank... I've had my fair share of weapons that are too expensive to buy when you unlock them, but hey... This isn't Your everyday Call of Duty where you play for two hours and unlock and use 15 different guns, and it sure as h3ll ain't another Alliance of valliant arms to dump your life's savings into just to have a chance at living past the first encounter... You have to be in it for the long-haul in order to be that guy with the Tiger tank and it's 88mm cannon... While yes, the is the option to buy things with gold(Real money)... They have made it deciently fair on the pricing of said amount's of gold to buy this item... and to buy a weapon using gold without unlocking it is significantly more expensive than waiting to unlock it.

A massive step up from Far Cry 2, yet very remeniscent of Far Cry 1 in many ways, Far Cry 3 was very entertaining. It's characters were varied and unpredictable, the setting was gorgeous, and the action was never lacking. Good gun and weapon variety/customization was a strongsuit of the title, as was it's complex set of factions and plot events. The fast travel feature was perfect: It had just enough locations to render the large map managaeble, but they were sparse enough to justify hopping into a vehicle rather than sprinting a kilometer. After a certain point, some of the game's features became obsolete or pointless, such as after getting all upgraded wallets, pouches, etc., going on animal hunts was relatively useless. The voice acting was pretty good, but it was overdone at times when a calmer tone would have suited the in-game context much better. Overall though, a fantastic title. I could see how some might find the title a bit repetetive or a tad boring at times due to the fact that it was so utterly open and free at times, but I think it's a fun game worth at least trying out.
I was going to end this review with a quote about the definition of insanity, but I think that would be a bit cliche at this point.

Being the only worthwhile multi-player FPS set in WWII at this time (sorry WWII Online... bring those graphics up from 1999), it's definitely worth checking out. Plus, you know, free-to-play. As far as graphics are concerned, it's quite pretty. Especially so if you have a pc that can handle 'High' settings.
Unfortunately, the game has a micro-transaction system, so there is an element of pay-to-win, also. You can buy gold from the company and use it to upgrade to a premium account for a period of time (ala World of Tanks), fast-track experience to level your character's abilites with weapons, etc. You can also use the credits to unlock things immediately, rather than earning them.
So, I could download the game, pay $99 or so, and enter my first battle as a proud owner of a scoped Kar98, Anti-tank/anti-infantry mines, an ME-109, a Pz.38T, Pz.IV, StuG.III, a King Tiger, an numerous other things before I even learn what the controls do.
To be fair, it is in early release beta... since May 2012...
Somehow, you can fly a P-38 Lightning or ME-109 close enough to the ground to kill an infantryman with your wing.
Somehow, you can shoot down a plane with an AP shell from a light tank (yes, you read that correctly).
You have no free-look key, so you are stuck looking in the direction you're facing. Easy for enemy to blindside you.
You can't toggle crouching. You can only crouch while holding the key.
Bazookas and Panzerschreks do exactly the same damage, same accuracy and range (all 3 unrealistic).
They are both completely OP.
You have to look up to throw your grenade farther... only you cant see how far you're throwing it because you're looking up at the sky (no free-look, remember).
BUT!!!
Despite the poor mechanics and early-release state, the micro-transaction feature works FLAWLESSLY. You do not have to worry that you won't be able to spend your money with this game. You spend it perfectly.
I still play it, though. lulz
