I'm having a fun time exploring the islands and soaking up the beautiful scenery.  The combat is satisfying for the most part.  I enjoy the takedowns; they can be more exciting than the traditional way of killing enemies,  however, I feel like the advanced ones are not made available to the player much at all.  For example, I have yet to find an instance where I can kill an enemy above me from a cliff.  I do wish there were more of these opportunities.
The storyline so far isn't anything special and that's okay FOR ME, but I do like reading some of the lore regarding the islands and of the people who've lived there.  I also must give praise to the diversity of animals and their overall design including animation and sound effects.  The crafting system is simple and feels realistic.  The fact that I have to hunt for skins where I can easily be killed, say, by a tiger (Damn, they're strong lol) makes everything considerably more realistic.  There are also a plethora of vehicles across the map of which you can use to navigate the terrain.  Seriously, there are like a dozen.  Nice job there.
I only have a few pesky complaints with the game.  It requires a UPLAY account in order to actually play the game.  I did not know this until I finished downloading it.  Took me about 20 minutes to actually get the game to run for the first time but after that it was smooth sailing.  A lot of reviewers gripe about UPLAY not cooperating with them leading to their inability to actually play the game, but I haven't come across anything so serious that I woudn't buy a Ubisoft game ever again.  Still, though, I really, really can't stand being forced to create a third-party account to play a game.  Just make it playable through Steam and that's it.
Traversing the island I did find myself desiring a radio to listen to music.  Yeah, you can listen to it driving a vehicle but you can't really hear the music over the engines.  Since radio towers are a big factor in Far Cry 3, I kind of expected to have a radio on hand especially since I prefer walking around as opposed to driving.
Lastly I would have liked a little more diversity in side quests. You have either killing commander enemies with a knife which is the only way to complete the mission or hunting down certain animals, like a pest control sort of mission.  These are so far what I've encountered.
Overall, this is a must have.  You will easily put in over 20 hours into this if you take your time collecting the relics, loot boxes, completing side quests, liberating outposts, etc.  8/10

To sum it up: pay to win.
You start off playing training missions, and for the most part is is quite fun. The game's mechanics are not on par with other WW2 shooters out there such as DoD: Source or more importantly Red Orchestra 2, but you're willing to look past that because of the overarching goal to 'win the war' and the fact that the game's progression gives you incentives to keep playing.
Unfortunately it's when you rank up and step out of training missions into the campaign missions where the game comes undone. Whilst it is refreshing to finally see the game as it was meant to be played, that is with multiple goals and not just the domination gametype in the training missions, you'll often be outnumbered or outnumber the enemy team and crush them. Not only that but you'll start playing against people who have spent inordinate amounts of money on ridiculous weapon mods that will one shot you and they'll also take 3x the amount of damage of a normal person due to some insane perk they unlocked via money. Yes you can grind to attain some of these advantages but it is a long and arduous grind, not something the average person could hope to attain. I'm willing to have some iffy balance in a WW2 game seeing as in real life battles are not always fair, but when you get the drop on a guy who is peddling a bike, you put 6 rounds into him and then he jumps off his bike only to one shot kill you it is incredibly frustrating.
Something that I very much get in a RO2 match is the feel of war; bullets whizzing over my head, soldiers writhing in pain, artillery raining down close to me. All these things are just non existent in H&G, half the time you won't even hear the shot that killed you, the audio in general is awful.
Pros:
Progression is definitely there.
You feel like there is an overarching goal to 'win the war'.
Cons:
Wonky mechanics, not as good as other current WW2 shooters on the market.
Pay to win or if you are not fond of that term, pay to advance.
Awful balancing.
No visceral 'war' feeling.
Recommendation: Go buy Red Orchestra 2.

This game is more than meets the eye. First glance, I will admit. I hated this game entirely.
However, after around, 3 hours of playtime, I fell in complete love. This is by far the most immersive WWII game out there.
I expected very little from the F2P game, Horrible graphics, slow gameplay, things like that.
But what I realized is that this game doesnt use any gags to "Trick" your brain into loving it.
What some games do is that they restrict your ability to play, I.e only letting you play 3 matches a day.
Some games also allow you to win very quickly, "tricking" your brain making you think "I'm amazing and this game is fun" because. winning makes everyone happy, right?
This game followed NONE of those little gags. Its entirely based on your ABILITY to play the game.
The more you play, the more you earn.
The game also features a unique system for unlocking items.
To unlock new weapons and equipment you must fill a form of Pre-requisite such as killing enemies with grenades or riding a bicycle insted of riding in a car. (Yes, there is a physical training badge)
Also, BICYCLES! Who wouldnt love riding into battle with a trusty Bicycle Brigade by your side?
Some people may argue that this is a pay to win game, which is not true at all. Paying money only speeds up your characters progress via unlocking things early. You are able to unlock everything in the game with just a little effort on your part.
This game has many flaws, however, many perfections also. Its also being continualy updated, so you can expect new things almost every month, wonderful.
The last thing I'll cover is the unique system of "Wars".
In these "Wars" a simple game of domination could turn the tide for whether Germany or Allied forces win the war.
I love this game, if I could, i would give it a hug. But alas, I cant, do to it being a download.

I wasn't going to review this game until it was fixed, but seeing as it's on sale and many might want to buy it, as well as the fact that it's been almost two months and the game shows no signs of improving, I made an exception. Long story short, Do not buy this. The game is terribly optimized, I only get around 30-40 on my rig and it even drop to 20 in some areas. Extra is unplayable for most people. Crashes for NVIDIA users are constant, for example, whenever I play whiteout for about 5 minutes it immediately crashes the display driver, and with AMD, it's nothing but corrupted textures on things like tractors, trucks and even some guns, making it unplayable for them.
As for the gameplay, it's shockingly bad, balance is horrible with Assault Rifles and SMG's being the only practical weapons with all others only useful for playing around. The MSBS kills in 0.056 seconds while most other weapons need 0.140, weapons with built in attachments like the Honey Badger invalidate any other weapon not doing the same. The Riot Shield is completely broken with users being able to shoot through your shield completely or just shooting the bottom of the shield and the hit detection thinking they shot your foot, and on top of that, weapons actually do more damage when shooting someone's feet, the same as the Headshot multiplier.
If you think you can get past all of that for some CoD action, proceed with caution. Probably the biggest reason not to buy this is the lack of any anti-cheat, be it VAC or Punkbuster. Hackers and cheaters are abundant. In almost every lobby I have joined, my first or second one has always had at least one. This is literally killing the game, and it's numbers show, If you don't like team deathmatch or domination you're♥♥♥♥♥♥out of luck, because there are no players in any other playlist, and dom is only even populated during the US daytime.
In my opinion, Call of Duty Ghosts is this year's Blunder Of The Year. Some will point and say, "What about Colonial Marines, what about Ride to Hell?" Now let me ask you, did anyone ever expect those to be good? Colonial marines was in development hell for at least 6 years, and Ride to Hell was made by the guys who make Nascar games. This was a major AAA release with a development cost of several hundred millions of dollars, and this isn't even playable, not even 2 months after release. Avoid at all costs.

I've owned the game since release day and have yet to experience a single crash or bug. The game runs smoothly at 60 FPS with all settings at high / ultra in both single player and multiplayer.
The single player campaign, though short, goes a long way towards putting you into the feel of a special operations team member with missions ranging from underwater combat to base infiltration to space combat. While the story itself is fairly straightfoward and reminiscint of a hollywood summer action flick, it's still enjoyable.
The multiplayer is where the game stands out compared to previous call of duty titles. The level designs are larger and much more complete in terms of accessibility and realism of buildings as well as other objects. Firing through cracks in objects will not cause bullet collision with invisible walls which is quite nice. Another major bonus is the removal of a large portion of the aerial kill streak rewards, bringing the fight back down to a groundwar rather than constant map bombardments by overpowered rewards.
The people who are complaining about the performance of this game are putting on display a fault of their own machine hardware rather than a fault with the game itself. Because this game was designed for so-called "next generation" hardware, it is odd to expect it to still run smoothly on outdated setups.
While the game is not extreme in it's innovations within multiplayer, the addition of more movement possibilities such as sliding and vaulting allows for a deeper level of immersion as the usual bunny hop and run and gun mentality which is too often seen in CoD titles has been all but eliminated. In it's place are players willing to take a more serious tactical approach to gun combat. While this does lead to a slower pace in matches, it also adds a better sense of realism and immersion which is seriously lacking in previous Call of Duty titles.
Nothing more to say.  Bad FPS, takes too long to find lobbies, overall failure for PC.

Good game, executed wrongly. The commitment of Infinity Ward and Activision have been questionable with the latest installment in the CoD series. On release day there was of course the 6gb of RAM requirement which there was no explanation for (now lowered to 4gb RAM requirement which is standard for a game now a days). It seems although the heads of the developers have been elsewhere with the "Next Gen" consoles coming out and have still failed to fully optimise multiplayer (Every other call of duty you could get 80+ FPS on a nvidia GTX650Ti on high-ultra settings) let alone rid the game of hackers with what feels like a non existent anti-cheat system. I put plenty of hours into this on release weekend and have never really touched it since. I'm curious to see what the DLC will bring although i must say i'm not to keen on spending more money on a game that i might never touch again. Anyway with that being said here is some of my thoughts
The positives :
- Infinity Ward/Activision did release a further optimised patch to show they care but the game is still poorly optimised compared to others. Saying that, campaign is way better optimised than Multiplayer and is actually playable.
- Controlling riley is a nice feature (Just not worth 32.4gb of my hard drive.)
- Extinction was a nice attempt to make something of this game. (I enjoyed this game mode. Just gets very repetitive.)
- Squads/Spec Ops is in this game. (Although i feel it has been kind of neglected.)
The negatives
- Bad optimisation. Possibly the worst port to date?
- The number of hackers online is unbelievable
- Campaign missions are really lacking that something, i was kind of lost and struggling to connect what i done in missions had to do with the actual story.
- Player base has already dropped so much be it down to hackers, bad optimisation or the repetitive gameplay mechanics.
- "Next Gen" game made on the ancient call of duty engine with a couple of tweaks here and there.
I would not recommend buying this game unless there is some significant changes and finally some attention paid to the PC Port for once by Infinity Ward.
Overall Score: 5/10

This review is primarily negative. I only recommend this game because I feel everyone should try it and form their own opinion.
This game has a lot of potential, but that Potential is over shadowed by the lack of balance in this game. The health and damage system in this game is complete bull, its the type of game where you can sneak up on someone, unload 5-10 bullets into their back, just to have  them turn around and one shot you. Bolt action rifles are insta kill weapons and if you dont have one of these then you better hope your gun has a fast rate of fire, and even then theres no garanty you will be able to kill some one before they shoot you dead, because the game has no form of suppression. Thats right, you can unload a light machine gun clip at an enemy and they will get no penalty towards aiming/shooting you while your bullets fly by their head. The firs weapons you get are Advanced rifles( M1 Garand US, Gewehr43 Germany)  but these weapons might as well be BBguns  because they are completely useless.
Feel like playing as Germany? well have fun!!! Because this is  an America ♥♥♥♥ YEAH! game. American Weapons= Win, German weapons= Frustration.  Ever play a ww2 game in which the BAR and M1919 Browning have absolutely no rocoil? well look no further, The BAR is probably the smoothest firing weapon in this game, its as if the developers decided that the phisics of this gun should be thrown out the window. German light machine guns have massive recoil while the American M1919 Browning fires as smooth as a submachine gun. If you wanna play as a tank driver, Germany has a slightly larger selection of tanks which is nice  except that you have to go threw two different tanks before you can unlock a tank that can actually fight other tanks, unless you pay $10. The starter tank for germany has a light machine gun that can bearly penetrate the armor of the of the American starter tank which also only has a machine gun except it can tear to shreds pretty much all of the german light tanks. the First tank Americans can unlock is a Stuart which is basically the best tank in the game,  Dont even bother trying to fight one  as a German tank driver unless you have a medium/heavy tank or you get flank on it with an Ausf E.
these are only a few of the Issues  this game has, not to mention the fact that Knives  have about a 20% chance of actually hitting your enemy when you go to stab them, if they move ever so slightly, when you start you stab, you might as well just pull out your gun and hope they dont shoot you first. The game only has five maps at the moment three large maps which seem like they can hold  about 60 players in them, except only 18 players  on each side can join a game at once,  and two smalls maps. the maps limit you to how many vehicles  your squad can have  on the field at once, so if your a tank driver theres a chance that you will spawn without a tank and you will have to wait until you die and until an allied tank get destroyed before you can spawn with a tank, and if your not fast enough some one else will spawn a tank and you will have to wait all over again before you can try to spawn one.
For all the Flaws that the game has, it does have its upsides, your characters are relatively customizable and each class you choose can be pretty unique. Also you can have as many characters on your account as you want, just dont bother naming them because no one else will see their name. if you like paratroopers, this game has probably the most authentic paratroopers in a game i have ever seen, just dont hide with your back to the wall  because your parashoot back pack will be visible on the other side of the wall and will give you away.
Even though i mainly have complaints about this game  i do enjoy it, although a lot of thing need to be changed  in my opinion if this game wants to be truly successful. Until then, i still prefer Red Orchestra/Rising Storm. Partly because im tiered of ww2 games that only feature America and German, its as if Game companies forget that other countries fought in the war, i would love to play a game like this that was based In North Africa between UK and Italy or just some thing else other then Germany VS America.

I have never played a game quite like Mount and Blade. It's an action strategy sandbox game that allows the player to lay siege to castles, build up relationships and deal in politics for the sake of raising one of the five kings of the fictional land of Calradia to power, insighting a rebellion in the name of a claimant to the throne, or even one day make yourself ruler of the entire land.
The combat system is entirely unique, using multi directional attacks and blocks that require the player to outsmart, as well as outplay their adversaries. The player uses the comabt system in organised tournaments, in the siege of castles or open combat across a variety of battlefields. Although I thoroughly enjoy the combat system of this game, it took some time to fully grasp and understand, as the learning curve can be quite treacherous, but well worth it in the end.
The game makes use of an overworld map in which all the various parties, such as lords, kings, caravans, farmers, bandits and the player character's party go about their business in real time. This works very well and gives the player the feeling that they have been dropped into the middle of a real, active world full of conflict, although due to the fact that this has not been done before in this way, some players may feel alienated by how different the game looks and feels.
In the corner of the screen a chat log is constantly in use, telling the player when lords have been captured, castles or cities have been besieged, kingdoms have formed alliances or someone has been indicted for treason, the first indication that there is more to this game than meets the eye!
On the battlefield, the armies you command consist of troops that you yourself trained, hired, met in the evening with inside a lonely tavern, or saved from the grasp of a cruel lord. They can be commanded in any manner the player wishes, similar to games such as Rome: Total War, only instead of being a supreme commander in the sky, you are one of the men on the field marching into battle with tension forever rising as the enemy makes their presence known on the horizon.
Although it may not be for everyone due to the steep learning curve, as well as the entirely unique and perhaps daunting combat system, I cannot do this game enough justice with mere words. Regardless of whether you like it or not, Mount and Blade: Warband is certainly unique and I can gaurantee that your time traversing the treacherous land of Calradia will not soon be forgotten.

Overall not a stunning game, but certainly a very good game as well as unique.

I have never played a game quite like Mount and Blade. It's an action strategy sandbox game that allows the player to lay siege to castles, build up relationships and deal in politics for the sake of raising one of the five kings of the fictional land of Calradia to power, insighting a rebellion in the name of a claimant to the throne, or even one day make yourself ruler of the entire land.
The combat system is entirely unique, using multi directional attacks and blocks that require the player to outsmart, as well as outplay their adversaries. The player uses the comabt system in organised tournaments, in the siege of castles or open combat across a variety of battlefields. Although I thoroughly enjoy the combat system of this game, it took some time to fully grasp and understand, as the learning curve can be quite treacherous, but well worth it in the end.
The game makes use of an overworld map in which all the various parties, such as lords, kings, caravans, farmers, bandits and the player character's party go about their business in real time. This works very well and gives the player the feeling that they have been dropped into the middle of a real, active world full of conflict, although due to the fact that this has not been done before in this way, some players may feel alienated by how different the game looks and feels.
In the corner of the screen a chat log is constantly in use, telling the player when lords have been captured, castles or cities have been besieged, kingdoms have formed alliances or someone has been indicted for treason, the first indication that there is more to this game than meets the eye!
On the battlefield, the armies you command consist of troops that you yourself trained, hired, met in the evening with inside a lonely tavern, or saved from the grasp of a cruel lord. They can be commanded in any manner the player wishes, similar to games such as Rome: Total War, only instead of being a supreme commander in the sky, you are one of the men on the field marching into battle with tension forever rising as the enemy makes their presence known on the horizon.
Although it may not be for everyone due to the steep learning curve, as well as the entirely unique and perhaps daunting combat system, I cannot do this game enough justice with mere words. Regardless of whether you like it or not, Mount and Blade: Warband is certainly unique and I can gaurantee that your time traversing the treacherous land of Calradia will not soon be forgotten.

Would I reccomend this game to others?  Do you enjoy Call of Duty games?  Then yes I would reccomend it.  Do you enjoy military FPS with an action bent to them?  Then I would reccomend it.  Are you looking for a reimagining of the Call of Duty franchise?  Are you wanting a military simulator?  A deep moving story?  Then I would not reccomend because what you're looking for is no Call of Duty.  The game is big, dumb, fun, just like every CoD before it. No better. No worse.  For some the bloom is off the rose, but for my money I enjoy these every year.  This is the first one I picked up on PC and haven't had the frame rate problems that a lot of folks seem to have.  The main campaign is a fairly straightforward story.  Some fun set-pieces with flooding cities, collapsing buildlings and more explosions that you can shake a stick at.  Kick it up to Vetran and it at least offers a little bit of resistance to running through it.
Multiplayer isn't too bad except that I haven't been able to get many games in.  Pretty unpopulated on the PC.  But there are bot matches, which is my prefernce anyway.  The Sqauds system is fun, giving you multiple characters to level and build out your AI team the way you want.  Nothing much new from MW3 or BlopsII, although there seems to be less emphasis on crazy kill streak rewards.  The new Cranked mode is a fun twist as well with a kill giving you a 30 second time to get another kill (as well as a speed boost).  If you hate campers that should be your jam.  If you like camping you might want to find another mode.  The maps are varied, although some seem a bit big for the number of players.
I didn't get a chance to play Extinction yet, but it seems to be a mash-up of the suvival mode from MW3 and the Zombies mode from Treyarchs games.  Not a bad combo.
Overall, it's Call of Duty.  If you already hate the series, it's not going to change that.  If you like the series it also probably won't change that.  It can look quite good at times (I got a pretty steady 40ish FPS on mid-level settings with mid-level gaming laptop) and has some different level designs that offer a slight change of pace, but mostly it's the same shooting and moving they've been offering for 10+ games now.  If you're not burned out on the concept of cinematic/action/military FPS, give it a try.

Short Version: A Truly epic game filled with something for everyone... once you get past the UI issues.
Long Version: I have spent so much time (230+ hours) on this game that is has truly one of the highest entertainment/cost ratios of anything.  You start off as a small pudly guy with barely a coin to your name and you end being Emperor of all Existence.  You swing swords and level up your character, run trade caravans, manage cities, politick with your fellow Lords, then eventually try to keep your vassals from rebelling or breaking off as you manage a farflung kindom.  There's exploration, economy, town building, politics and relationships (even a small marriage game), but mostly you will be slaughtering fools that stand in the way of your ascension.  Jousting, sneaking into sieged castles, being the first out of a siege tower onto the walls, running down fleeing infantry with horses and long lances.  And that's just the vanilla game.  There are hordes of high quality mods that fix up the crappy UI as best as can be, streamline the more annoying parts, and add swathes of new content (troops, weapons, you name it).
The only real downside is the UI.  It is crap.  Commands you want to use all the time are buried under multiple menus, the leadership interface during battles is awful, and hunting down specific NPCs requires you to memorize every possible town/castle layout.  Luckily there are mods that simplify a lot of this.  I highly recommend the Diplomacy Mod (for UI) at the very least, and if you want to get really epic there is Prophecy of Pendor or the Floris Mod.  Both those mods do some serious heavy rework.
This game is well worth buying and I can't wait for Mount and Blade 2 to come out!

Where FC2 makes you feel like a terrible person through amplifying gameplay, FC3 tries to do this through the narrative. Most of the complaints I've heard about this game come to this exact aspect (the aspect that makes the game for me): even when taking missions, you're not a good person. Your character is a massive♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥living out his action movie dreams, "saving" the natives from their oppressor. You're not supposed to feel good after completing the narrative, you're supposed to be left troubled and wondering. That being said, a couple of missions (mainly involving Buck) take this a little too far for me. There's a fine line between forcing players to question themselves about what they are willing to do to progress the game (a question asked many times throughout the story), and trivializing certain actions. FC3 doesn't always walk on the right side of that line, but for the most part it shows a good effort.
My main complaints with this game revolve around the huge power creep. Whereas in FC2 at the end of the game you'll have better weapons but still need to play smart, by FC3's midpoint your protagonist has turned into God. You'll have access to items that literally make your character invincible, and while that's convenient for some of the more obnoxious quicktime boss fights, that's a cover for poor game design.
There also is a good amount of extraneous features and systems. Hunting, crafting, WWII letters, Relics, plant gathering, radio tower, drug notes, etc. all seem fresh at first but quickly become tiring.  It's a troubling turn when the gamer views a "secret" marker on the map as another objective to be ticked off rather than a secret to discover, and FC3 goes far beyond that point. Some of the systems seem to have beem put together by dfiferent teams who never spoke with each other. After hunting an animal you can skin it and craft items with its skin. However, the animation for skinning is actually the protagonist pulling out the animal's internal organs and putting them in a bag. At first I thought this might be commentary on Brody's action hero fantasies, but after watching the animation for the 200th time I didn't care anymore.
Coop is present but takes out all that makes FC3 different and fun. Whereas attacking a point in the Singleplayer game would allow a great deal of creativity. Coop is a linear shooter. Most levels have one specific "best weapon" and punish you tremendously for not using it. This is unfortunate, because between levels you use your experience to upgrade certain skills and weapons. If you specialize yourself in the sniper class and weapons, then you'll be entirely out of luck when you run into a level set in a cave or bunker. It can be fun to play with a friend or two, but Coop's definitely not the strong point of FC3.

When I first played "Mount & Blade" back in 2009, I had absolutely no idea what I was getting myself into. The game enraptured me as soon as I started playing, and I quickly logged over 100 hours into the game before I even started delving into the mods, which increased the games playability even further. Unfortunately, when my old computer died, I lost all of that old progress, but when I get back to Steam recently and saw "Mount & Blade: Warband" for sale, it was something I barely had to think about, I bought it as soon as I possibly could.
Obviously there were many differences in this version, and there's always something that a game loses in a sequel. For some, it's a less enthralling plot, for others, it's a weak combat system, but I have to say, with Warband, they improved on everything from the previous game, and lost nothing in return. I was absolutely blown away at the highly improved combat system, as well as the relationship system that you can have with the other lords of the realm. For instance, in the original "Mount & Blade", your relationship with the other lords was very superficial. You could ask them to follow you, and carry out simple tasks, but this time around, you could do many more things with a lord who you had the favor of. One of my favorite aspects that they added was that you could convince a rival lord whom you were well aquainted with to defect from their nation and join with yours, and although it is extremely dificult to do so, it's still fun to try, nonetheless.
Another thing that this game had improved from the original was the way that nations interracted, as well as being able to create a nation yourself. There were mods from the original that improved on these, one that comes to mind was the "Lords and Realms" mod that allowed you to create your own nation, and from what I've seen it looks like the team that created "Warband" took a lot of inspiration from the mod and added it into the game, which is by no means a bad thing. The nations themselves are less prone to throwing out random declarations of war, and instead run on a trust based system. If one nations soldiers are attacking peasents and caravans, then they are more likely to be declared an enemy, and thus a war will start. But if you do good things for another nation, then they will be less inclined to attack yours. It's a much better mechanic than having the rulers randomly declare war for little to no reason.
The replayability of this game, though, is what truly makes it worth every penny. Just as the last game had me logging many, many hours, this game has me coming back for more and more. Every time you play, there will be different things for you to do, different units for you to train, different ways for you to play and different nations for you to fight for. I highly recommend this game to anyone who has a love of all things medieval, especially the combat aspect, as the battles in this game have you using various tactics to defeat an enemy force.
There are of course a few minor issues with this game, one of which is that it can, and will, take you quite a while to build up a large enough army to contend with some of the other nations. It can take anywhere from 10 - 30 hours of gameplay to build up the resources to amass a small army, and even then you have to micromanage your men to make sure that they're happy, and that you have enough money to pay them all, lest you wish for your men to desert. One easy way of making money is the tournaments, with are incredibly fun, and don't take long to complete, but give you vast amounts of coin that you will desparately need. So if you are the impatient type, be aware that this game takes a bit of patience if you truly wish to get the full experience.
The others are the graphics, as well as the music. The graphics are the most glaring issue, as most of the time, the people look either disfigured or horrible mangy, even some of the Kings. The game itself doesn't have the best polygon count, and often things will seem very rigid and pointy, especially some of the more hilly and mountainous regions. The people often move around in a strange, and perhaps even creepy maner, with many townsfolk walking into walls for minutes on end. The music for the game isn't exactly bad, so much as annoying when it plays over and over again, especially the battle music. The overall music that plays in the overworld isn't so bad, however, and I have had no issue listening to it for many, many hours. However, neither of these problems really felt all that bad to me, as I could always mute the music if I wanted, and most of the time you aren't really going to be focusing on the graphics when you have so much else to be doing. The disfigured faces are strange at first, but you get used to it as you start accepting that this is the way the people of Calradia look. Most of the soldiers go into battle with helmets on anyway, so it's not a huge issue.
Overall, this is a fantastic game with great fighting mechanics, interesting strategies for battles, a fun land to explore and many people to impress. I haven't even delved into the multiplayer aspect, but without it, it's still an incredible experience. Even if it may take a while to get into, I highly recommend it to anyone with enough money to buy it. It's kept me entertained for a long time, and it will no doubt continue to entertain me for long after I write this review.

An interesting strategy/action game to say the least with a thriving modding community (Confusingly lacking the Steam Foundry as the developers themselves nod to modding the game giving out an achievement for it) that allows you to take a wildly varied approach to medieval combat. The main sticking point of this game is conflict whether it be large and bloody wars or small and...well equally bloody skirmishes and it gives you plenty of tools for the deed in the form of axes, lances, crossbows and more. The choice of how you play this game has many answers ranging from being the ever loyal vassal letting your chosen liege rule the continent or backstabbing them after a protracted war against a rival and taking over the weaker side's holdings for your own bid for dominion. The answer of how you fund your murder spree can be just as varied from mapping out the supply and demand of the cities for trade, collecting taxes from your fiefs or your enemies fiefs down to simply cleaning up bandits and cleaning up their hoards.
The battlefields are varied based on the geographic location you are at in the world which will make you plan what battles you participate in. For example taking your cavalry into the mountains is not the brightest idea but by the same token having your archers on flat plains can be just as murderous for either party. Sieges can be handled traditionally by starving them out or if you trust in your sword swinging you can just knock out those weaklings and possibly earn yourself the honor of a new castle.
Combat is split into two very different methods which will be up to you as you can set up groups to the traditional 1-9 hotkeys (0 being the Everyone command) and you can be as hands on or hands off with your approach to troop management as you wish. Setting up how close they stand together, what weapons they should focus on using and if they should use ranged weapons or hold fire are some options along with formations if the units you have 'selected' are eligible. Your warband will typically be made up of your chosen nation's troops but the exception to this would be the Companions you meet in the taverns across the continent who have their own personalities, preferences and nationalities of troops if you raise them to command in your own kingdom. This can be a pain for some but well worth it as they can progress and be outfitted just like the player character giving you excellent control over a number of truly Elite troops.
Pros
Excellent modding community that can transport you to anywhere from Westeros to The Empire from Warhammer Fantasy or even the British Isles.
The size of conflicts can become truly massive when armies engage as opposed to the PC versus Bandits or one lord versus another pushing your combat and troop skills to the limit. (Small Con - This can lead to long dragged out battles once the numbers get into the 1000+ range)
The number of skills available to you and companions can give useful boosts ranging from training up weaker units to turning deaths into simple wounds saving your hard earned troops.
A relationship building aspect with the lords of the land allowing you to tempt them to defect or swap your constantly raided village for their cozy collection of hovels next to the capital.
Cons
Play can take quite a bit of trial and error to gauge what you should do and when you should do it as the Warband 'expansion' adds on regional bandits with wildly varying equipment, tactics and power levels.
Running your own kingdom can be a pain between the infighting of lords and the bitterness of former employers leading to unrelenting wars.

Alright, I've been playing this for a bit now, and I have a general idea of how this game works.
For a game that's only in beta, it's impressive. The gameplay is decent (really clunky in terms of pretty much any modern FPS, but it's in beta, so it SHOULD improve). It's kind of a bit less-hardcore Red Orchestra 2, and I do like the idea of being able to modify the weapons to match your play style. The graphics aren't great, but the gameplay is really fun. I do really like this game.
I do have a few gripes though.
1. Level-up WAY TOO DANG SLOWLY. You know how I was talking about matching your play style? Well, it's too..."grindy" for lack of a better term. Yes, I know this a free-to-play game and they want people to try and pay to get the better stuff, but this is kind of ridiculous. Also, I think you should be able to have a basic SMG, Assault Rifle, Sniper Rifle, Shotgun, and Pistol right from the get-go so you can gain skills with each specific type of gun rather than beign forced to use the bad rifle or SMG you get early-game until you can finally buy the gun you actually want.
2. Melee sucks. You buy the base melee weapon...it's a freaking shovel. If you want to get a better weapon, you either need to shell out some money to just buy a weapon you will only use as absolutely necessary or grind like 5 levels before you actually get a knife. And oh, wait. You only level it up if you manage to get melee kills. Which absolutely sucks considering the hit register is terrible when it comes to trying to melee someone. Yes, I realize this game is a FPS, but if you are going to include a melee system, make sure that it works.
3. The prices for buying gold are just strange. I mean, I was about to go buy some gold because I thought "hey, this game is pretty fun, I wouldn't mind paying $5 to get a nice loadout for some fun. NOPE. The minimum price is $9.01. Then $12.89. Then $25.85. Then $64.72. Then $129.51. First of all, did the devs have a monkey with a number pad punch in the numbers for the prices? Randomest numbers possible, I swear. And seriously, let's be realistic. Nobody with any sense should be shelling out more than $25 for this game. Not when it's in early access, and especially not when it's an online-only FPS. TF2 is a much more polished FPS, and it's free to play. CS:GO and Insurgency are $15 not on sale. Red Orchestra 2 is $10, and it's a WWII FPS. I do realize the devs should get some money, but by opening this game to be free to play and including such a ridiculous money system, you're really going to PREVENT people from paying money. You need to keep the competition in mind. Also, with some of the "veteran" stuff, this is dancing on the edge of "pay to win," which is something that really will be seen negatively.
4. How do you kill someone by HITTING THEM WITH A BIKE?
But all in all, this is a fun game. I've enjoyed playing it, and I've told several of my friends to play it. Keep up the great work!
...But seriously, change the pay-to-win crap or I'm done.

Before rating down my review just because it has a 'pros' section on a game that has bad reputation and you completely disagree with me & hate this game, read the reason on part 4 first. I am criticizing this game objectively without bias, so don't expect me to only bash the game with bad reviews like other popular reviews to satisfy your hatred of the game. I am completely aware this game has a bad reputation on the community due various reasons. So please, read first, rate later. My review consists of:
1. Pros
2. Cons
3. TL;DR
4. Pay to Win explanation; why so many negative reviews, including mine?
+ Gameplay is fun. It's the only good WW2 MMOFPS out there with large player base and this kind of gameplay. Would've been better if they are using PlanetSide 2's style, though. But maybe it's protected with copyright.
+ Moderate scale of battle. Unlike most other 5v5 MMOFPS, Heroes and Generals has a 18v18 map
+ Good graphics, but not great.
+ Good shooting system. Snipers will be affected by gravity (but not wind) and they will have to adjust their scope accordingly. Weapons that appears to be blocked by certain object won't be able to hit the target just because the crosshair is on the target. And last but not least, unlike CoD, recoil exists here. In general, shooting system is challenging (especially long range shooting), but the difficulty does not overwhelm the fun.
+ Various tanks & other land vehicles, planes, even bicycles
+ Haven't tried the 'Generals' side where you get to deploy troops to win the war, but I heard people said it's pretty good
+ Weapon choice is limited, but adequate. You won't easily purchase any good weapons without using the bad ones first since there are prerequisite to fulfill before purchasing one. So progress is needed to achieve good weaponry.
+ Soldier classes, ranks, and other visual progress bar technique to keep you addicted
+ Three out of 5 WW2 major military power is here (Russia, US, Nazi)
+ Teamwork heavily determine the outcome of the battle. Individual skills only affect snipers.
+ Game is being updated frequently with the devs actively streaming on twitch.
- Reloading animation doesn't make sense. After 2 shots with my Kar98k, the reloading animation shows me putting in 5 bullets. Bullet count always resets to zero when you reload.
- Clunky & crude animations, makes close quarter combat very awkward
- One type of plane. No bombers, which is weird. Dive bombers played a big role in WW2.
- Game stays in Early Alpha for a very long time. Showing that the updates are quite insignificant and devs are only trying to increase the pay-to-win range.
- No Japanese & British? All major military powers in WW2 would be complete if they add the Japs & the British, maybe they're still working on it (French was also a major one in Allied Forces but they surrendered early)
- Pay to Win system is very blatant and annoying, complete expalantion on part 4
- Terrain texture is crude, trees and grass are like from the early 2000s games.
- Lack of objects on open areas to provide cover and realistic combat, buildings and ruins provides the only covers, which makes it very obvious. Rocks and trees can also be used but it's usually not really effective and not well placed.
- Despite the fact that teamwork is very important to win the game, majority part of the community are not cooperative nor communicative. But this is not completely their fault, the devs are guilty too, here. More about this will be written on part 4.
Great gameplay, pay to win is annoying, challenging shooting system, one of the best WW2 MMOFPS out there with large player base, land vehicles, planes & infantry battle, grinding is almost pointless due to expensive weapons, imperious & immature moderators that are capable to ban you (rare occurance). Point is, if you're not ready to spend money on this game, don't waste your time grinding. If you are really into WW2 MMOFPS, this game is worth trying.
This is the main reason the community keep bashing Heroes & Generals with bad reviews, completely ignoring the good side of the game and creating a negative-only review, reinforced by the infamous dev's incapability to take criticisms and the squad of immature & imperious mods that bans players who killed them in-game. On the other hand, I am used to these kind of games. I am originally from Indonesia, and Steam wasn't very popular there. I spent years playing crappy online games which is much worse than Heroes and Generals and has worse Pay to Win system before I knew about Steam. And believe me, gaming devs that implement this kind of Pay to Win system will grow in an extremely slow rate, with most of them ending up in bankruptcy. Their revenue might be large but the volume of the financial flow will grow too slow, not growing at all, or even starts dropping where they'll have to cut down the pay to win system, leading to low or even negative profit.
Their main income sources are rich kids, new gamers, impulsive people, WW2 history nerd gamer, and pardon my language, complete idiots. They are the only ones who will spend money on this game and their population is decreasing rapidly with gamers' adaptation to the pay to win system. Gamers can't be so easily fooled to spend money on a pay-to-win game like those early online gamers back in 2000s. Their money-grabbing behavior just won't work in today's gaming community. The biggest flaw of Heroes & Generals' Pay to Win system is their limitation of the main gameplay itself, which is their main power. It is the only WW2 MMOFPS out there that has a large player base and they failed to use that advantage properly.
Creating a pay wall in front of soldier classes, nickname change, weapon mods, land vehicles, and planes is an unbelievably imbecile pay-to-win implementation. Those things are the primary features that builds the main gameplay. Giving massively underpowered tanks to people who doesn't spend money is also a very foolish step. This pay wall prevent the teamwork element from running properly since the core of the game is guarded by a massive pay wall.
If they ever want to repair the reputation and ensure their companies' future, I suggest they completely remove the pay wall that limits the gameplay, lower all prices/increase income from each game to make it worthwile to play, remove durability system/lower the price to repair stuff, and remove the game from Free to Play section. People's price range varies but I personally willing to pay maximum $20 for this quality of game with no pay-to-win system as a prerequisite. If they remove the alpha and make the graphics, animations & textures better, plus adding more new significant features (new nations? new weapons? new planes? new vehicles?), I would definitely willing to pay up to $35 for a copy. Balance the guns and vehicles to prevent frustration on new players. Create a workshop and sell skins on community market just like CS:GO's strategy as an extra income that won't interfere with the gameplay. Add more guns to increase income from skins. Hire mature and professional mods. And many other stuff they could improve. They need to learn that this kind of behavior belongs to developing countries that is still new to online gaming compared to US and EU. For example, they would do well in Indonesia (not for long). Their current course is without question outdated and leads to failure.

The laziest cat in America swaps places with the richest feline in England in director Tim Hill's lasagna-laden sequel to the 2004 theatrical hit Garfield. Jon Arbuckle (Breckin Meyer) is on his way to London to propose to his veterinarian girlfriend, Liz Wilson (Jennifer Love Hewitt), and his unflappable cat, Garfield, is determined to be there when Jon pops the big question. Of course, Garfield wouldn't go anywhere without his old pal Odie, and soon after arriving in the land of Big Ben, the clueless tomcat inadvertently changes places with royal look-a-like Prince. It seems that Prince's owner, Lady Eleanor, has recently passed away, leaving the care of her sprawling estate Castle Carlyle in the capable paws of her devoted kitty companion. The trouble is, Prince has decided it's due time for a vacation, and with Garfield in charge there's no telling what kind of trouble will befall Castle Carlyle. Despite having a devoted butler named Smithee (Ian Abercrombie) to cater to his every whim and a whole host of fun-loving critters with whom to pass the lazy days spent lounging in the sun, this crowned head begins to feel the sting of deceit as the envious Lord Dargis (Billy Connolly) hatches a dastardly plan to do away with the whiskered heir and claim Castle Carlyle all to himself. Meanwhile, as Garfield attempts to hold his ground against his greedy would-be nemesis, the fun-loving Prince is living it up with Jon and Odie by taking a trip to some of London's most popular pubs. ~ Jason Buchanan, Rovi

- You can be a mercenary selling your sword and company of soldiers to different masters

The list could go on but the point is theres LOTS to do in this game. Buy it and you wont regret it.

I love this game.
I started it Holiday 2012, probably just after Christmas, along with the Steam versions of Max Payne 3 and Dark Souls. Over the next few months, I sunk dozens upon dozens of hours into Dark Souls and more (when you include Wiki time and Xbox 360 horseplay), and horsed around in Max Payne 3, but of the three games I got two years ago, THIS is the one I felt most compelled to finish. (Still haven't -- and I only finished Dark Souls because I could, I was content to just pvp all the time). Alas, life gets in the way and after months of on-and-off play, I didn't really play FC3 again until a week ago.
I am plowing through FC3 now, because on my birthday, my sister got me FC4 for my Xbox One. Before I have yet another addition to my pileup of unfinished/unstarted games, I wanted to give the earlier installment all my attention. All the praise it got in fall 2012 is much deserved.
The story is great, the characters are a little flat but energetic enough to make believe in their fictional lives and personalities. I am given direction and guidance in an open-world game while being encouraged to go my own way. The gunplay and stylistic elements of combat are as good as any great shooter and the depth of the loot just enough to keep me interested in changing it up and getting new gear as I plunder Rook Island.
As for the islands themselves, they are a blast to explore. I never finished the original Far Cry when I played it on my PC about 9 years ago, but I remember that game and Crysis (which was also from Crytek, the original makers of FarCry) having some of the most immersive and interesting envrionments to explore in most of the first-person games I have EVER played (in FarCry I would go crouch/prone somewhere and just spy on the enemy camps, listening to their banter and figuring out ways to mess with them. Because of all the dicking around I'm not really sure how the game started or where it was taking me to, lol. I have a similar case with Borderlands 1 and 2). This game accomplishes the same feat of wonder, danger and personality. The blood of adventure runs through its veins.
My only gripe is that Far Cry 3 reuses too many assets (NPC voices, filler dialogue, etc.) and that the enemy groups don't adapt to you so much as you makeing them dance like puppets. The multiplayer has some balance/depth issues as well but it works for what it is, and is fun and fast while being tactical to a degree.
For the record, I've never finished a Bethesda game either, so Far Cry 3 will get special honours as the first open-world immersive experience I've finished in the current modern era of gaming. Kudos, Ubisoft.

Just putting my opinion into this for people who're looking into this game. My evaluation of this game would put it at a 6.5/10. I suppose all the hype and positive comments people had for this game raised had me expecting a crazy great game.
The story wasn't all that great, despite people claiming it to be. The gameplay was alright, gunplay was solid as well as driving the vehicles which was probably the funnest part of the game for me.
The enemy marker you have in game makes it really easy and takes the fun out of guessing where the enemies are. By spotting the enemies, they're highlighted orange and will highlight through every object that stands between you and them, meaning you basically have X-Ray vision. It takes almost no skill to kill enemies since you can always track them.
The animations of looting and healing got tiresome pretty quickly.
The side quests didn't really have any worthwhile incentives and taking into account that the game length was pretty long, there was quite a limited selection of weapons, not enough to satisfy my thirst for explosions and crazy spraying and praying. The selection of weapons was decent, but a lot of them I didn't bother using since I easily unlocked a higher tier weapon immediately after unlocking the lower tier ones.
The crafting system is a joke, it works, but it's not really worth filling up your inventory space for.
The leveling system is an even bigger joke, I don't even want to talk about it.
You can go and attack enemy outposts to liberate the area which in turn allows you to do side missions that will unlock attachments for your weapons to be purchasable. Sounds great at first, but then you realize once a outpost is liberated the enemies disappear from that area immediately. No more encounters on the road, or in the jungle. All enemy activities cease from that area. And if you liberate all the outposts... Well, you no longer have anyone to fight.
Once you beat the game you can go back to the island to continue exploring, however at this point there's not really anything worthwhile to do unless you want to convert this shooting game into a treasure hunting game, in which you look for the little totems of the indigenous people there and letters from Japanese soldiers of WW2. It's not worth the time, because you don't get anything out of it really.
My biggest gripe about this game is that you never get to just outright kill the important foes. That and you wonder about how you got out of the precarious situations the villain puts you in, that would normally seal a mortal man's fate, (**SPOILER**-ish) only to get straight into a hallucinogenic knife fighting scene.
You obviously have to win the fight to proceed through the game, but when you've killed the foe you wonder:
"How the HELL did I get out of that situation!?".
(**SPOILER**) For example, getting stabbed squarely in the chest, (pretty sure to the heart), with a approximate 8" blade, falling to the ground, blacking out, hallucinating a debate against yourself while walking down a magically appearing stone path, villain appearing at the end of the path and then knife fighting him, only to wake up in the tribal woman's lap who then declares you victorious for having killed the foe. You might, like I did, go on and say: "What the F*ck!?" ...
For me the game was ruined by those strange inconsistencies and not being able to freely and outrightly killing my main antagonists. The exploration of the island was dull due to the fact that after clearing outposts no enemies were existent in the area, leaving my weapon almost useless aside from killing predators and critters.
I wouldn't recommend this game unless it goes on a big discount or you have a lot of time to kill and excessive cash to discard, otherwise, not worth.

Heroes and Generals is a free to play 3D MMOFPS developed by Roto-Moto and set in WWII . Unlike traditional lobby based shooters, Battles fought within Heroes and Generals contribute towards a persistent overworld based on real areas of Europe during WWII. High ranking players acting as “generals” command various assault teams towards key objective locations within the overworld. Once an assault team has been moved into place a mission is spawned allowing players to join that mission.
Depending on what type of assault team was sent into a mission, players of each faction will have varied amounts of respawns, class types and vehicles available to them. As the battle progresses both factions respective generals can command more teams to reinforce those currently engaged in the mission, giving them extra respawns access to vehicles and more. This allows a battle to wage back in forth on both the strategic and ground level.
Players will have the ability to create their own character and progress towards a specialization including Rifleman, Sniper, Tank Commander, Fighter Pilot and more. Players can also outfit their character with new clothing as they gain experience, allowing them to show off their rank.

I was huge fan of the original Far Cry, but when the developer switched I followed CryTek to Crysis instead of continuing the series. I played Far Cry 2 yeras late and didn't enjoy it. It was so different from what I expected given the original that I couldn't be anything but disappointed.
Far Cry 3 nails the formula though. What they tried to do with 2 in regards to the open world and quests and forts that need to be taken over finally evolved into something fun and engaging. I found myself trying to do everything possible in Far Cry 3. All the side activities, like activating radar towers or racing on a supply drop are just fun. They're all different enough to make exploring and completing these quests as you find them a worthy goal in its own. And the light RPG elements with the skill tree added an extra layer of depth sorely needed to the FPS genre.
On top of that, I also really liked the story, which was another complaint of mine about 2. I'm really happy that they were able to create something interesting and compelling to move the action along, from the first moment to the last. Some of the trippy scenes are incredibly original and they make for a really memerable experience.
The final bonus from this game is casting Michael Mando as Vaas. He gives an incredible performance as one my favorite villians in recent memory.

I fervently REGRET purchasing this game, and DO NOT recommend it to anyone who is looking for fair, legitimate, and competitive online gameplay.
I have been an avid COD fan over the years, starting all the way back with COD 2. I have purchased virtually every new release--whether from Treyarch or IW--with the almost sole intention of playing multiplayer. Sadly, Ghosts is where I stop; this is indisputably the last COD I will ever purchase.
Why? It's simple: the developers' blatant disregard for online playability, neglect (or perhaps unwillingess) to ramp up anti-hack measures/ban cheaters, and complete inability to optimize the game for computers of varying capabilities all serve to undermine the integrity of the entire COD franchise.
First, in online multiplayer on PC, there are hardly ANY players online. The only two game modes you're guaranteed to find matches in are TDM and Domination. What's the point in having all the cool niche game modes if there aren't enough players online using them?
Okay, so let's look at the cause-effect: why aren't there any players online? It really comes down to two main reasons. The first is that the game is poorly optimized, and is consequently only playable by those with top-tier PCs. "Just decrease the visual settings", you suggest? Ah, if we purchase a game for $60, should we really have to downgrade the quality settings to play it? No. The developers are generating millions of profit at significant margins; why should WE have to compromise game quality when they have the means and resources to optimize the game to ensure playability for a diversity of consumers?
Fortunately, I have a high-performing PC and do not experience (the majority) of the lag/fps issues that most complain about. Instead, my biggest issue and disappointment is the ridiculous prevalance of hackers. There are AT LEAST 2-3 hackers in almost every single online match. If you take the time to watch killcams of many top-scoring players, a pathetically high number of them are, quite conspicuously, aiming at you through walls/map barriers. Some are even stupid enough to SHOOT you through walls, even regardless of whether you have all stealth perks active or not (i.e. blind eye, incog, off the grid).
I understand COD is a franchise especially prone to hacking--that's fine, that's to be expected. However, the sheer influx of hackers in COD: Ghosts is just completely sad. Of the 5-6 different COD chapters I've played, this is bar-none the worst for hacking. It is quite evident that Activision/IW/whoever's responsible for anti-hack measures have completely floundered. Until cheaters begin to get caught and banned (which likely won't be for a LONG while), I assuredly will not be playing much. In its current state, the quality of online gameplay is shameful, and yields a considerably frustrating experience for those who want to play fairly and legitimately.

Far Cry 3 has often been said to be Skyrim with guns, I don’t agree.
The game itself is not actually bad, you start as an over privileged rich kid who is taking a holiday break with a bunch of knuckleheaded friends and you have to grow into the role of a survivor after being captured by some slave selling pirates from the local islands. The story throws you into a kind of civil war between the pirates and the local tribe the Rakayat who are trying to loosen their hold over the islands. The story is pretty entertaining, with a few minor branching paths, and some wonderful drug induced symbology hallucination sections that really play with reality, and outpost liberation missions that open up fast travel points in the open world for you to get around more easily.
Some of the other main things to do include a crafting system that is pretty much compulsory as you need certain upgrades that you craft to help you carry more weapons etc., syringe crafting that give you healing, underwater breathing, fire resistance and hunting instinct that lets you see enemies and animals in the area as a white shadow through the terrain and of course radio towers that point out points of interest on the map.
The skill progression is ok, it has some nice skills that help out however more of the skills feel like they are just passive things that kind of enhance the game rather than giving you cool skills that you strive to get.
The crafting is a nice touch but honestly you cannot get certain upgrades until later because certain areas are not available easily, meaning you are left wandering about being only able to carry so much loot or weapons until you can find where the hell to get the last holsters required animal skins from, which in my opinion really holds you back unnecessarily.
The weapons are pretty stock for the best part, I honestly found myself choosing certain weapons then sticking with them for the rest of the game, certain missions try to encourage the use of other weapons however it felt more like an annoyance when I was forced to use a particular weapon for a mission, then having to backtrack to a safe house to reequip what I usually use.
The enemies nearly all look the same which after a bit seems a bit lazy and boring. Apart from the wonderfully charismatic Vaas, as you may have heard who plays a wonderful part and is both insane and wonderfully written.
Although I played around 10-15 hours on this title, I often found myself just sticking to clearing outposts and the main story mission as much of the side missions were very repetitive and once I had completed them a number of times, I just had little interest in every trying them again.
To people who say this is like Skyrim with guns, the only comparisons here as far as I am concerned is that they are both open world, both fun and both first person with a sense of skill progression, that’s about it. The characters here all look the same, in Skyrim more or less all characters have their own looks, the map here feels limited and the outposts look the same, in Skyrim you can tell a city clearly from other cities, with different architecture etc. The list goes on.
This may not be Skyrim but as far as I am concerned it is defiantly worth taking a look at, you won’t regret it if you can get it on sale, even better!!

This game is really underrated. Even though it's graphics is slighlty outdated, it's upsides more than outweigh it's downsides. If you're looking for a good medieval RPG, with huge, epic battles and tons of hours filled with questing and fun, this is the game for you!

What exactly is Mount & Blade? Partly it is a medieval fighting simulator, partly role playing game and partly a strategy game. All of this is present in this huge chunk of buggy code wrapped in mediocre graphics. But that is little too harsh, because this game has something to overcome all of this. Flawless gameplay.
You start by creating your character in not too deep creator. There is couple of background choices which will determine your stats. Stats are the RPG part of the game, you get all the basics like strenght, agility and intelligence, followed by skills that determine your abiliy to hold shields, ride a horse or get better prices from traders. At the very last there are the weapon stats, those are here to tell you how well you will fare with different kind of weapons. You can choose between bows, crossbows, short or long swords, spears and polearms.
After you are done spending your points, you get a piece of the fighting simulator. You get thrown into an one on one fight without any sort of tutorial, this game is expansion after all, so you should already know everything right? Well, in case you did not play the original... Generally you use left mouse button for attacking and right mouse button for defending. That's pretty common right? But that is obviously not everything. By moving the mouse to either of four directions (right, left, up, down) prior to the swing you determine the manner of the attack. To add more fun to this, you can do the same while defending, so basically you have to check your opponent's movement and react fast enough to block. However if you are not up to the challenge you can use automatic blocking, in this case you will only need to time the block and the direction will be automatically chosen by computer. So that's it, quite simple is it not? Other weapons are similar with small differences mostly in possible manners of attacking. Ranged weapons are even more challenging. There is no aim indicator and arrows, bolts or javelins respect the laws of gravity, so it will take a while to get used to it.
Well, that was quite elaborate description of fighting system, I hope I did not bore you. This leaves us with strategy part of the game. So yeah, after you finish your first fight you get your first quest (yep, another sign of rpg) and end up on a huge map, not too unlike Total War world maps, but way uglier, and move your character around. Everything is in real time, but since the time stops everytime your character stops, in principle the game is more similar to turnbased games. So there you are on a huge map, large groups of enemies moving around you. You may try to challenge one of the groups yourself and find out, that you are no hero, just another warrior who gets butchered when facing more than 2 or 3 enemies at once. At this point you get to one of the villages and recruit yourself a bunch of peasants. Soon enough you will find that peasants are more like meat shields and die a lot, but with a piece of luck and good commander (you) they can make it as far as to knighthood. This all sounds more like tactics than strategy right (wink)? Well, to be honest I am not sure how it works in vanilla (unmodded) game, since after original Mount & Blade, in Warband I started with mods right away.
Yes, mods are the greatest thing that could have happened to this game. The basics are great but the game itself needed helluva lot of polishing to become a legend. There are tons of mods ready to be tried and some of them are really robust. I myself am using Floris mod pack (to be find on
which combines many different mods improving graphics and gameplay alike. And the strategy part I was talking about is part of this mod, since in here, before the fight starts you get to strain your mind by choosing how will your units behave during the battle. You had probably already guessed that I think that Mount & Blade: Warband is a good game, well you are right, but with mods, it becomes a GREAT game.

For those that played Battlefield 1942, this game will bring back memories and seem very familiar.  First thing is that this game is in Beta and has a lot of work left to it.  However, it is playable.  This game is a set on a large scale warfront between Germans and the US in WWII.  The battles are part of campaigns in which wins, losses, deaths, and kills are added up over a period of time to determine the campaign winner.  Recently, a new non-campaign mode has been added to provide a more balanced game, but the battles do not count towards the current war.
The game is multi-platform and has three different gametype options; Action, Strategic, and Causual (hand held devices).  You play as a soldier that you can either specialize into a career path such as para trooper, recon, tank crew, or pilot.  Once you promote to an officer rank, you can command assault teams into battle.  As a general you strategically command the battlefield. Providing different gamemode elements on multiple platforms allows H&G to break away from the standard military FPS game mode.
The game is a free-to-play (ftp) and has a market place/store that is used in the business model (BM).  The game gives a strong sense of a pay-to-win (PTW) in early gameplay because people can pay to unlock better weapons. As players advance and unlock items through gameplay, this argument becomes more of a pay-to-advance (PTA) scenario, however the PTW feature still exists hidden in the form of subscription plans.
Subscription plans ($12 US) cost nearly as much as you will find for a Giant MMO like WoW but offer no where near the content, support, or updates you will find in an MMO.  Why then would you buy a subscription plan?  Simple, to get an extra passive perk and a weapon slot. The extra passive perk and extra eqipment slot is a minimal bonus as you are still locked at 10 slots for carrying equipment.  However, if you plan correctly, it will let you equip things like binoculars.  This my friends is PTW feature however little it benefits you.  This is the sinlge game killing factor for me.  As much as I love to play this game, I find the subscription plan ruins competitive gameplay giving people the extra edge in combat. That is not to say the game isn't fun.
The PTW/PTA BM is not nearly as bad as other games like Infestation.  In H&G, the PTW/PTA feature can easily be countered by skill. The game is unbalanced by design which makes it very difficult to point at a PTW/PTA feature as the cause of a lose, but rather the number of planes and tanks on a team vs the other.
Graphically this game needs a lot of work.  The textures and animations need improvement, especially the character models.  The environment can use some touch ups and improvement as well but overall not too bad given the size of the maps.  The game design resembles BF1942 while graphically it looks very similar to Battlefield Play4Free (2011) which is designed on the BF2 engine (2005) with some HD improvements.
The gameplay is smooth for the most part with some glitches, one of the most irritating is typing in chat.  The chat glitches could be related to key remapping but none the less, they are present.  Bullet trajectory is decent implementing elevation and speed.  Hitting a target requires compensation for target movement and hit point dmg so hitting someone in the head will increase the damage done compared to a leg hit. Vehicle handling is good but sensitive so changes in terrain or hitting objects can cause a loss of control.
The biggest issue with gameplay is the very design of the game to be unbalanced. A team may have multiple advanced classes against an infantry based team whereby the infantry based team will more than likely lose without teamwork and advanced unlocks like anit-tank mines and granades. Simply put, it is had to fight a tank or a plan with a rifle.  The battles can be major disappointments and one sided.
I have mixed feelings about recommending this game.  Yes this game is fun and worth a try but the aggressive PTW/PTA business model is disappointing. And what is worse is that since I intially wrote this review in September of 2014, the developers have continued to alter the game patch after patch expanding the grind to unlock items as well as raising the cost of items which makes it harder to play and not pay any money to unlock items. The game is still fun and the PTA/PTW BM can be overcome by skill, but expect a heavy and lenghty grind that lessens the value of playing this game.

"Mount & Blade: Warband"
What a great game this is. There is just so much to do. So far I have put around 100 hours in to it and I still have yet to see the end game. And that is not a bad thing at all. There is so much to do!
You start off by creating your character and his/her story. His/her background, professions, reason for adventuring and even gender decide how good you are with a bow, sword, polearm, horseriding, trade and much more. Of course you can just random the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of it, but if you are like me and like to optimise your character, there will go quite a bit of thinking in to this.
You get to pick one of the major cities where you start off. Regardless of how you optimise (even if you come from a noble family) you are still nobody and will have to prove yourself in this world. You can do this by visiting the Inn in various main cities and trying to recruit fellow 'Hero' characters that will join your party and level up with you. These characters vary from a former Slave Trader to a Miller that is on the run from the army that already killed his wife and child or a mysterious woman that was captured by bandits as a child and raised by them, only to take revenge on them now... and many many more!
Of course you can go around the lads with just these heroes. But since there are many kingdoms at war, deserters making big groups and killing everyone they see, large groups of bandits that try to rob or kill you... you might want to get a few more to make your own little army. You can do this by visiting various villages and try to recruit some former farmers to join your ranks. Slowly as you battle your way around the land these will level up and you get to choose what they become depending on what kingdom they come from. With your party growing and growing you might want to join one of the kingdoms to help them on their quest to dominate all, by plundering enemy villages, sieging castles and towns, destroying enemy parties and capturing their Lord (or setting them free to receive some honor and perhaps make a useful friend along the way).
Apart from all the murder and mayham there is also a bit of politics in the game. Decide who you want to befriend (this could even be the enemy), marry into a wealthy and powerful family.
If you join one of the kingdoms and get enough renown, you might even receive one of the villages, towns or castles that you helped conquer. This opens up a whole new game for you as you now are no longer a roaming freeman, but a proper Lord that will need to defend his holdings. Build reinforncements for your town such as Barracks, a Watchtower and more. Station a few of your troops or even one of your heroes/friends there to defend it.
Ugh, I could keep talking about this game for ever... but all I can suggest is: Try it!
This is such an amazing game, so do not let the graphics fool you. I know they are not on par with say, Skyrim. But in certain ways it will be one of the most amazing games you ever played. Be ready to waste quite some hours away.
Check out some Youtube videos, screenshots or whatever if you're not convinced. Or give me a PM!
PS: They are now busy on creating Mount & Blade: Bannerlord. The next M&B game!

I do not understand why everybody hates Ghosts. It is by far my most favourite COD game:
Singleplayer has many fun elements to it - Multiplayer is amazing: Some maps like Strikezone are really fun to play in and customisation has reached a new level, with the new ability to also change your squad's looks. It is annoying how you have to 'activate' challenges to complete them (to unlock customisation and stuff). Titles and emblems have now been converted into patches and backgrounds, which is nice. I also love how some guns have integrated attachments - and it is so satisfying to be rid of overpowered machine pistols. There are now Marksman and Sniper Rifles: Marksman rifles are basically semi automatic, while Sniper rifles are the hardcore bolt-action types. This is nice, for people who aren't that good with sniping, while the hardcore snipers can still bust their moves (personally, I prefer the bolt action Sniper Rifles).
However, if everyone is put off by the other reviews, then I would advise one to wait for a sale, or at least try to find a way to try it out, but trust me, if you have a deep wallet - like me ;) - then it is a great game.
P.S. the playtime is for singleplayer only, I've played multiplayer a lot more ;)
